data.name: Physical Sciences
data.description: The physical science is a branch of science that explore the fundamental principles and natural laws governing the non-living world. They encompass several key disciplines that study the properties and behavior of matter, energy, and the interactions between them.

data.name: Life Sciences
data.description: Life sciences encompass a broad field of scientific study that focuses on living organisms, including plants, animals, and humans. It involves the exploration and understanding of various aspects of life, ranging from the structure and function of cells and organisms to their interactions within ecosystems.

data.name: Humanities and Social Sciences
data.description: Social sciences focuses on subjects like economics, psychology, and history, while the humanities explore philosophy, languages and literature, and the arts.

subjects.term: History of scholarship and learning. The humanities

data.name: Technology and Engineering
data.description: Engineering is the design and construction of systems and structures for influencing the world around us and enhancing our experience within it. Engineers use the fundamental principles of mathematics, physics and chemistry to create machines that enable us to travel faster, provide improved medical care, and process more complicated information.

data.name: Mathematics and Computing
data.description: Mathematics and computing is the study and analysis of abstract concepts, such as numbers and patterns. Mathematics is the language of choice for scientifically describing and modelling the universe and everything that happens within it. Computing enables these mathematical problems to be solved in an efficient and automated way.

data.name: Materials Science
data.description: Materials science is an interdisciplinary field involving the properties of matter and its applications to various areas of science and engineering. It includes elements of applied physics and chemistry, as well as chemical, mechanical, civil and electrical engineering.

data.name: Chemistry
data.description: Chemistry is a branch of science that involves the study of the composition, structure and properties of matter. Often known as the central science, it is a creative discipline chiefly concerned with atomic and molecular structure and its change, for instance through chemical reactions.

data.name: Biological Sciences
data.description: Biological sciences encompasses all the divisions of natural sciences examining various aspects of vital processes. The concept includes anatomy, physiology, cell biology, biochemistry and biophysics, and covers all organisms from microorganisms, animals to plants.

data.name: Health Sciences
data.description: The health sciences study all aspects of health, disease and healthcare. This field of study aims to develop knowledge, interventions and technology for use in healthcare to improve the treatment of patients.

data.name: Politics and International Studies
data.description: The study and practice of international relations is interdisciplinary in nature, blending the fields of economics, history, and political science to examine topics such as human rights, global poverty, the environment, economics, globalization, security, global ethics, and the political environment.

data.name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
data.description: Electrical and electronic engineering is the branch of engineering that makes use of electricity. Electrical engineering concentrates on systems for generating and transmitting large electrical currents and converting them into other forms of energy, such as mechanical motion. Electronic engineering focusses on lower energy currents for processing and communicating information.

subjects.term: Electrical, magnetic, optical, communications, computer engineering; electronics, lighting

data.name: Social Sciences
data.description: A collectivity of people sharing interactions, relations and networks, usually in a geographical or physical space and with similarity of purpose or life aims.

data.name: Mathematics
data.description: Pure mathematics uses mathematics to explore abstract ideas, mathematics that does not necessarily describe a real physical system. This can include developing the fundamental tools used by mathematicians, such as algebra and calculus, describing multi-dimensional space, or better understanding the philosophical meaning of mathematics and numbers themselves.

data.name: Physics and Astronomy
data.description: Physics is the search for and application of rules that can help us understand and predict the world around us. Central to physics are ideas such as energy, mass, particles and waves. Physics attempts to both answer philosophical questions about the nature of the universe and provide solutions to technological problems.

data.name: Religion
data.description: Religion is a range of social-cultural systems, including designated behaviors and practices, morals, beliefs, worldviews, texts, sanctified places, prophecies, ethics, or organizations, that generally relate humanity to supernatural, transcendental, and spiritual elements —although there is no scholarly consensus over what precisely constitutes a religion.

data.name: History
data.description: History studies the past, including events occurring after the invention of writing systems (dist. 'prehistory'). History relates to past events as well as the memory, discovery, collection, organization, presentation, and interpretation of information about these events.

data.name: Statistics
data.description: Statistics is the application of mathematical concepts to understanding and analysing large collections of data. A central tenet of statistics is to describe the variations in a data set or population using probability distributions. This analysis aids understanding of what underlies these variations and enables predictions of future changes.

data.name: Computer Science
data.description: Computer science is the study and development of the protocols required for automated processing and manipulation of data. This includes, for example, creating algorithms for efficiently searching large volumes of information or encrypting data so that it can be stored and transmitted securely..Computational science is a discipline concerned with the design, implementation and use of mathematical models to analyse and solve scientific problems. Typically, the term refers to the use of computers to perform simulations or numerical analysis of a scientific system or process..Information theory and computation is the study and development of protocols and algorithms for solving problems and analysing information. This discipline usually breaks information down into individual bits, and then determines the optimum logical operation required to efficiently process this data in any required way..Information technology is the design and implementation of computer networks for data processing and communication. This includes designing the hardware for processing information and connecting separate components, and developing software that can efficiently and faultlessly analyse and distribute this data.

data.name: Behavioral Sciences and Psychology
data.description: Psychology is a scientific discipline that focuses on understanding mental functions and the behaviour of individuals and groups.

data.name: Arts
data.description: Art is a diverse range of human activity, and resulting product, that involves creative or imaginative talent expressive of technical proficiency, beauty, emotional power, or conceptual ideas.

data.name: Economics
data.description: Economics is the study of how people allocate scarce resources for production, distribution, and consumption, both individually and collectively. The two branches of economics are microeconomics and macroeconomics. Economics focuses on efficiency in production and exchange.

data.name: Earth and Environmental Sciences
data.description: Earth and environmental sciences cover all aspects of Earth and planetary sciences, and broadly encompasses solid Earth processes, surface and atmospheric dynamics, Earth system history, climate and climate change, marine and freshwater systems, and ecology. It also considers the interactions between humans and these systems.

data.name: Literature
data.description: Literature is any collection of written work, but it is also used more narrowly for writings specifically considered to be an art form, especially prose fiction, drama, and poetry.

data.name: Media and Communication
data.description: Media and communication are closely interconnected fields that involve the creation, transmission, and exchange of information, ideas, and messages. some key aspects of media and communication: Mass Media, Journalism, Digital Media, Advertising and Marketing, Public Relations

data.name: Mechanical Engineering
data.description: Mechanical engineering is the branch of engineering that deals with moving machines and their components. A central principle of mechanical engineering is the control of energy: transferring it from one form to another to suit a specific demand. Car engines, for example, convert chemical energy into kinetic energy. Sub-areas such as Process (Chemical) or Industrial Engineering have their roots in Mechanical Engineering.

data.name: Business and Management
data.description: Management (or managing) is the administration of an organization, whether it is a business, a nonprofit organization, or a government body. It is the art and science of managing the resources of the business. Management includes the activities of setting the strategy of an organization and coordinating the efforts of its employees (or of volunteers) to accomplish its objectives through the application of available resources, such as financial, natural, technological, and human resources.

data.name: Archaeology
data.description: Archaeology is the study of the artefacts and other physical evidence left by past societies of humans and closely related species. It uses scientific analysis of field samples to inform historical understanding.

data.name: Philosophy
data.description: Philosophy is a branch of knowledge and an academic discipline that explores fundamental questions about existence, knowledge, ethics, logic, and the nature of reality. It involves rational inquiry, critical thinking, and systematic analysis to examine and understand concepts and ideas about the world and human experience.

data.name: Cultural Studies
data.description: Cultural studies, also called the cultural sciences, is an interdisciplinary field or scientific branch that examines the dynamics of contemporary culture (including its politics and popular culture) and its historical foundations.

subjects.term: Study and teaching. Research. Cultural studies

data.name: Linguistics
data.description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language including the study of grammar, syntax, and phonetics. Specific branches of linguistics include sociolinguistics, dialectology, psycholinguistics, computational linguistics, comparative linguistics, and structural linguistics.

data.name: Law
data.description: Law is a set of rules that are created and are enforceable by social or governmental institutions to regulate behavior, with its precise definition a matter of longstanding debate. It has been variously described as a science and as the art of justice.

data.name: Biological and Physical Engineering
data.description: 1. Application of technology to biological systems 2. Creating technologies from biological methods

data.name: Education
data.description: Education is an act or process of imparting or acquiring general knowledge, developing the powers of reasoning and judgment, and generally of preparing oneself or others intellectually for mature life. OR The act or process of imparting or acquiring particular knowledge or skills, as for a profession.

data.name: Civil Engineering
data.description: Civil engineering is a professional engineering discipline that deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of the physical and naturally built environment, including works such as roads, bridges, canals, dams, airports, sewerage systems, pipelines, and railways

data.name: Mathematical and Computational Engineering Applications
data.description: Mathematical and Computational Engineering Applications refers to the use of mathematical modeling, analysis, and computational techniques to solve engineering problems and develop innovative solutions. It involves the application of mathematical methods, algorithms, and computer simulations to various branches of engineering, such as mechanical, civil, electrical, chemical, and aerospace engineering, among others.

data.name: Biomaterials
data.description: Biomaterials are those materials — be it natural or synthetic, alive or lifeless, and usually made of multiple components — that interact with biological systems. Biomaterials are often used in medical applications to augment or replace a natural function.

data.name: Materials Chemistry
data.description: Materials chemistry involves the use of chemistry for the design and synthesis of materials with interesting or potentially useful physical characteristics, such as magnetic, optical, structural or catalytic properties. It also involves the characterization, processing and molecular-level understanding of these substances.

subjects.term: Solids. Solid state chemistry (Inorganic and organic)

data.name: Agriculture
data.description: Agriculture is the cultivation of plants, animals, and some other organisms, such as fungi, for the production of food, fibre, fuel, and medicines used by society. Agricultural science is a broad multidisciplinary field of biology that encompasses the parts of exact, natural, economic and social sciences that are used in the practice and understanding of agriculture.

data.name: Clinical Medicine
data.description: Clinical medicine is the branch of medical science that focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases and disorders in individual patients. It involves the application of medical knowledge and skills in a clinical setting, where healthcare professionals interact directly with patients. Clinical medicine integrates various disciplines, including anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, and medical ethics.

data.name: International Relations
data.description: International Relations is the study of relations across boundaries of (nation) states including international political economy, foreign policy analysis, diplomacy, peace and conflict studies, development studies, international security studies, migration studies and more. (Sarah Roughley)

data.name: Anthropology
data.description: Anthropology is the study of humans, their close relatives and their cultural environment. Subfields of anthropology deal with hominin evolution and the comparative study of extant and past cultures.

data.name: Genetics and Genomics
data.description: Genetics and genomics both play roles in health and disease. Genetics refers to the study of genes and the way that certain traits or conditions are passed down from one generation to another. Genomics describes the study of all of a person's genes (the genome).

data.name: Physical Chemistry
data.description: Physical chemistry is one of the traditional sub-disciplines of chemistry and is concerned with the application of the concepts and theories of physics to the analysis of the chemical properties and reactive behaviour of matter. While also at the interface between physics and chemistry, it is distinct from chemical physics. [chemical physics is distinct from physical chemistry in that it focuses more on the characteristic elements and theories of physics. Meanwhile, physical chemistry studies the physical nature of chemistry.]

data.name: Inorganic Chemistry
data.description: Inorganic chemistry is the study of the structure, properties and reactions of all chemical elements and compounds except for organic compounds (hydrocarbons and their derivatives).

data.name: Theoretical Chemistry
data.description: Theoretical chemistry seeks to provide theories and explanations for chemical observations whilst also posing questions to be answered by future experiments. Playing a key role in physical chemistry, it uses the laws of physics to predict molecular structure, dynamics, bonding, reactivity, physical properties and spectroscopic response.

data.name: Organic Chemistry
data.description: Organic chemistry is the study of the synthesis, structure, reactivity and properties of the diverse group of chemical compounds primarily constructed of carbon. All life on earth is carbon-based, thus organic chemistry is also the basis of biochemistry. The ability to form compounds containing long chains of carbon atoms is the basis of polymer chemistry.

data.name: Sociology
data.description: Sociology is the study of social life, change, social hierarchies and divisions, organizations, networks, and social causes and consequences of human behavior. Sociology studies social statics and dynamics at the level of the family as well as at global levels.

data.name: Molecular Biology
data.description: Molecular Biology is the field of biology that studies the composition, structure and interactions of cellular molecules – such as nucleic acids and proteins – that carry out the biological processes essential for the cell’s functions and maintenance.

data.name: Biological Techniques
data.description: Biological techniques are methods or procedures that are used to study living things. They include experimental and computational methods, approaches, protocols and tools for biological research.

subjects.term: Auxiliary techniques and procedures; apparatus, equipment, procedures
Methods of research. Technique. Experimental biology

data.name: Plant Science
data.description: Plant Science is the study of plants, including how they grow, function, reproduce, and interact with their environment. It also covers related fields such as botany, plant physiology, genetics, ecology, and agriculture.

data.name: Microbiology
data.description: Microbiology is the study of microscopic organisms, such as bacteria, viruses, archaea, fungi and protozoa. This discipline includes fundamental research on the biochemistry, physiology, cell biology, ecology, evolution and clinical aspects of microorganisms, including the host response to these agents.

subjects.term: Natural history of microorganisms, fungi, algae

data.name: Probability Theory
data.description: Probability theory is the branch of mathematics concerned with probability. It treats the concept in a rigorous mathematical manner by expressing it through a set of axioms. Typically these axioms formalise probability in terms of a probability space, which assigns a measure taking values between 0 and 1, termed the probability measure, to a set of outcomes called the sample space. Any specified subset of these outcomes is called an event.In probability theory a stochastic or random process is a mathematical object usually defined as a collection of random variables. Historically the random variables were associated with or indexed by a set of numbers, usually viewed as points in time, giving the interpretation of a stochastic process representing numerical values of some system randomly changing over time. Stochastic processes are widely used as mathematical models of systems and phenomena that appear to vary in a random manner. They have applications in many disciplines

data.name: Biophysics
data.description: Biological physics or Biophysics is a branch of physics that deals with systems of a biological nature, from the scale of biological molecules to whole organisms and ecosystems. Biological physics typically uses quantitative physical approaches to address biological questions similar to those studied in biochemistry and molecular biology..Biophysics is the study of physical phenomena and physical processes in living things, on scales spanning molecules, cells, tissues and organisms. Biophysicists use the principles and methods of physics to understand biological systems. It is an interdisciplinary science, closely related to quantitative and systems biology.

data.name: Nanoengineering
data.description: Nanoengineering is a discipline that focuses on the design, synthesis, manipulation, and application of materials and devices at the nanoscale level. It involves the use of nanotechnology principles to create functional structures and systems with unique properties and functionalities. Nanoengineering encompasses a wide range of scientific and engineering fields, including physics, chemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, and biomedical engineering.

data.name: Neuroscience
data.description: Neuroscience is a multidisciplinary science that is concerned with the study of the structure and function of the nervous system. It encompasses the evolution, development, cellular and molecular biology, physiology, anatomy and pharmacology of the nervous system, as well as computational, behavioural and cognitive neuroscience. As a branch of biology it deals with the anatomy, biochemistry, molecular biology, and physiology of neurons and neural circuits.

data.name: Criminology
data.description: Criminology is a multidisciplinary field of study that focuses on the scientific examination of crime, criminal behavior, and the societal response to crime. It encompasses the analysis of the causes and consequences of crime, the study of criminal justice systems, and the development of strategies for crime prevention and control. Criminologists draw upon various disciplines such as sociology, psychology, law, economics, and statistics to gain a comprehensive understanding of crime and its impact on individuals and society.

data.name: Biological Chemistry
data.description: Biological Chemistry is the branch of chemistry that seeks to elucidate the molecular basis of biological processes as well as to develop bio-inspired solutions for chemical challenges. Biological Chemistry covers biochemistry, bioorganic, bioinorganic and biophysical chemistry.

data.name: Chemical Biology
data.description: Chemical biology is a scientific discipline spanning the fields of chemistry and biology. The discipline involves the application of chemical techniques, analysis, and often small molecules produced through synthetic chemistry, to the study and manipulation of biological systems. In contrast to biochemistry, which involves the study of the chemistry of biomolecules and regulation of biochemical pathways within and between cells, chemical biology deals with chemistry applied to biology (synthesis of biomolecules, simulation of biological systems etc.).

subjects.term: General biochemistry of plants and animals

data.name: Analytical Chemistry
data.description: Analytical chemistry is a branch of chemistry that deals with the separation, identification and quantification of chemical compounds. Chemical analyses can be qualitative, as in the identification of the chemical components in a sample, or quantitative, as in the determination of the amount of a certain component in the sample.

data.name: Historiography and Method
data.description: Historiography and Method involve the study of historical writing and methodologies, exploring how historians construct narratives, use sources, and interpret past events.

data.name: Anatomy
data.description: Anatomy is the field of biology that studies the structure of living things. Anatomy focuses on the composition, structure and location of the parts of organisms (tissues, organs and systems) as well as the relationships between different parts.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Life Sciences / Anatomy & Physiology (see also Life Sciences / Human Anatomy & Physiology)

data.name: Radiology
data.description: Radiology, Medical Imaging or Diagnostic Radiology: comprises different imaging modalities and processes to image human body for diagnostic and treatment purposes. It is also used to follow the course of a disease already diagnosed and/or treated.

subjects.term: Medical physics. Medical radiology. Nuclear medicine

data.name: Statistics and Computing
data.description: Statistics and Computing are two interconnected fields that work together to analyze and interpret data using computational techniques and statistical methodologies.

data.name: Science and Technology Studies
data.description: Science and technology studies, or science, technology and society studies (both abbreviated STS) is the study of how society, politics, and culture affect scientific research and technological innovation, and how these, in turn, affect society, politics and culture.

data.name: Artificial Intelligence
data.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is intelligence demonstrated by machines, unlike the natural intelligence displayed by humans and animals, which involves consciousness and emotionality. The distinction between the former and the latter categories is often revealed by the acronym chosen. 'Strong' AI is usually labeled as AGI (Artificial General Intelligence) while attempts to emulate 'natural' intelligence have been called ABI (Artificial Biological Intelligence). Leading AI textbooks define the field as the study of "intelligent agents": any device that perceives its environment and takes actions that maximize its chance of successfully achieving its goals. Colloquially, the term "artificial intelligence" is often used to describe machines (or computers) that mimic "cognitive" functions that humans associate with the human mind, such as "learning" and "problem-solving".

data.name: Data Structures and Information Theory
data.description: Data Structures and Information Theory are two fundamental concepts in computer science and information theory that deal with the representation, organization, and manipulation of data and information. Data structures refer to the way data is organized and stored in a computer's memory or storage to facilitate efficient access, modification, and retrieval of information. while Information theory is a branch of applied mathematics and computer science that studies the quantification, storage, transmission, and processing of information.

data.name: Computational Mathematics and Numerical Analysis
data.description: Computational mathematics and numerical analysis are branches of mathematics that focus on developing and implementing algorithms and numerical methods to solve mathematical problems using computers. These fields play a crucial role in scientific and engineering applications where analytical solutions may be difficult or impossible to obtain.

subjects.term: Instruments and machines (Including practical mathematics, graphical and numerical calculating)

data.name: Public Health
data.description: Public health is the medical discipline concerned with the prevention and control of disease through population surveillance and the promotion of healthy behaviours. Strategies used to promote public health include patient education, the administration of vaccines, and other components of preventive medicine.

subjects.term: Forensic medicine; incidence of injuries, wounds, disease; public preventive medicine

data.name: Evolutionary Biology
data.description: Evolutionary biology is a subdiscipline of the biological sciences concerned with the origin of life and the diversification and adaptation of life forms over time..Evolution is the process of heritable change in populations of organisms over multiple generations. Evolutionary biology is the study of this process, which can occur through mechanisms including natural selection, sexual selection and genetic drift..Evolutionary developmental biology is the comparative study of organismal development and how it has evolved. There is a particular focus on the genetic basis of phenotypic structures, how they change during evolution, and how novel structures arise.

data.name: Theory of Computation
data.description: Theory of computation (TOC) is concerned with how problems can be solved using algorithms and how efficiently they can be solved.

data.name: Immunology
data.description: Immunology is the branch of biomedical sciences concerned with all aspects of the immune system in all multicellular organisms.

data.name: Theoretical Physics
data.description: Theoretical physics is the development of mathematical formalisms and computational protocols for describing all aspects of objects found in the world around us and their interaction. This can involve both providing models for understanding empirical results or constructing self-logical theories for explain phenomena beyond current experiments.

data.name: Cognitive Psychology
data.description: Cognitive psychology is a subfield of psychology that focuses on the study of mental processes, including how people perceive, think, remember, and problem-solve. It examines the internal processes and structures that underlie human cognition and the ways in which individuals acquire, process, store, and use information.

data.name: Clinical Psychology
data.description: Clinical psychology is a specialized field within psychology that focuses on the assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental disorders and psychological distress. Clinical psychologists are trained to work with individuals of all ages, from children to older adults, and they often work in various settings such as clinics, hospitals, private practices, and academic institutions.

data.name: Photonics and Optical Engineering
data.description: study, manipulation, and application of light and its properties. Photonics involves the generation, transmission, detection, and utilization of photons, while Optical Engineering encompasses the design, development, and optimization of optical systems and devices.

data.name: Theatre and Performance Arts
data.description: Theatre is the branch of performing arts concerned with acting out stories in front of an audience, using a combination of speech, gesture, music, dance, sound, and spectacle. Any one or more of these elements is considered performing arts.

data.name: Biomedical Research
data.description: Medical research involves research in a wide range of fields, such as biology, chemistry, pharmacology and toxicology with the goal of developing new medicines or medical procedures or improving the application of those already available. It can be viewed as encompassing preclinical research (for example, in cellular systems and animal models) and clinical research (for example, clinical trials).

data.name: Cell Biology
data.description: Cell biology is the discipline of biological sciences that studies the structure, physiology, growth, reproduction and death of cells. Research in cell biology uses microscopic and molecular tools and examines all cell types, from unicellular organisms such as protozoa to the specialised cells that consitutute multicellular organisms.

data.name: Applications of Mathematics
data.description: practical utilization of mathematical concepts, techniques, and tools to solve real-world problems and address various fields of study. Mathematics has wide-ranging applications in numerous disciplines, including science, engineering, finance, computer science, economics, statistics, and many others

data.name: Industrial Chemistry
data.description: Industrial chemistry is the manufacturing art concerned with the transformation of matter into useful materials in useful amounts. This transformation of available materials into more desirable ones involves processes following recipes, which as a practice often long preceded the development and understanding of the chemical science which supports it.

data.name: Environmental Sciences
data.description: Environmental science is the multidisciplinary study of all aspects of the Earth’s physical and biological environments. It encompasses environmental chemistry, soil science, ecology, climatology, vegetation cover, marine and freshwater systems, as well as environmental remediation and preservation, and agriculture and land use.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Environmental Science (see also Chemistry / Environmental)
Land, recreational and wilderness areas, energy

data.name: Industrial and Production Engineering
data.description: optimization of complex systems, processes, and operations within industries and manufacturing settings

data.name: European History
data.description: European History encompasses the study of the historical development of Europe, including its diverse cultures, political systems, and social transformations from ancient times to the present.

data.name: Literary History
data.description: Literary history is the development of writings in prose, poetry and drama over time. It focuses on specific literary movements and trends that characterized particular periods of literature.

subjects.term: History, description, critical appraisal of more than two literatures

data.name: Social Psychology
data.description: Social psychology is a field of psychology that focuses on how individuals' thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are influenced by the presence of others and the social context in which they exist. It explores various aspects of human social interaction, including social perception, attitudes, conformity, group dynamics, and interpersonal relationships.

data.name: Surgery
data.description: Surgery is a procedure in which incision and physical manipulation are used to treat a patient with an injury or a disease. The patient's tissues are cut during this technique to permit the manipulation of tissues that are otherwise inaccessible.

subjects.term: Surgery, regional medicine, dentistry, ophthalmology, otology, audiology

data.name: Biological Psychology
data.description: Biological psychology, also known as biopsychology or psychobiology, is a field of study within psychology that examines the biological processes and physiological mechanisms underlying behavior and mental processes. It explores the complex relationship between the brain, the body, and behavior.  It explores how biological factors, such as the structure and functioning of the nervous system, genetics, and hormones, influence human behavior and cognitive processes.

subjects.term: Sensory perception, movement, emotions, physiological drives

data.name: Analysis
data.description: Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics dealing with limits and related theories, such as differentiation, integration, measure, infinite series, and analytic functions.

data.name: Theoretical Computer Science
data.description: Theoretical computer science or TCS studies the fundamental mathematical principles of computation, the .mathematical principles, theories, and techniques. It encompasses the mathematical foundations of algorithms, data structures, computational models, and computational complexity.

data.name: Comparative Psychology
data.description: Comparative psychology refers to the scientific study of the behavior and mental processes of non-human animals, especially as these relate to the phylogenetic history, adaptive significance, and development of behavior. Research in this area addresses many different issues, uses many different methods and explores the behavior of many different species from insects to primates

subjects.term: Comparative psychology. Animal and human psychology

data.name: Political Science
data.description: Political science is the study of the theory and practice of politics at the local, national, and global level. It asks fundamental questions about the nature of power, and analyses political activities, thoughts, and behaviours, as well as systems and processes of governance.

data.name: Industries
data.description: Industry studies in the field of business and management refer to the examination and analysis of specific industries, such as healthcare, finance, or retail. It involves studying the economic, social, and technological trends, as well as the regulatory environment and competitive landscape of an industry to understand its performance and growth potential. Industry studies can be conducted by both academic researchers and practitioners, including business analysts, consultants, and policymakers. The aim of industry studies is to provide insights into how businesses can operate more efficiently and effectively within a given industry, as well as to inform policy decisions that may affect the industry as a whole. The topics within industry studies may include market structure, supply chains, innovation, pricing strategies, consumer behavior, and corporate social responsibility, among others.

data.name: Computer and Information Systems Applications
data.description: Computer and Information Systems Applications refer to the practical use and application of computer technology and information systems in various domains. It involves utilizing computer software, hardware, networks, and databases to solve problems, streamline processes, and support decision-making.

data.name: Earth Sciences
data.description: Earth sciences include all fields of natural science related to the planet Earth. It covers the main areas of geology, mineralogy and petrology, geochemistry, geophysics, hydrogeology, oceanography, and atmospheric sciences. It also includes interdisciplinary sciences (earth system sciences) that deal with the interplay of the different earth spheres; lithosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, cryosphere, and atmosphere.

data.name: Optics and Photonics
data.description: Optical physics is the study of the fundamental properties of light and its interaction with matter. This includes classical optical phenomena such as reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference, and also studying the quantum mechanical properties of individual packets of lights known as photons..Optics and photonics is the study of the fundamental properties of light and harnessing them in practical applications. Optics and photonics covers the entire electromagnetic spectrum from high-energy gamma rays and X-rays, through the optical regime of ultraviolet, visible, and infrared light, to long-wavelength microwave and radio waves.

data.name: Archaeology in Society
data.description: Archaeology is a discipline that interacts with and impacts society in various ways. It extends beyond academic research and engages with different stakeholders to contribute to the understanding, preservation, interpretation, and enjoyment of the past.

data.name: Optical Materials
data.description: Optical materials are substances used to manipulate the flow of light. This can include reflecting, absorbing, focusing or splitting an optical beam. The efficiency of a specific material at each task is strongly wavelength dependent, thus a full understanding of the interaction between light and matter is vital.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials
Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Optimization
data.description: Optimization is a mathematical and computational process of finding the best solution to a problem within a given set of constraints. It involves maximizing or minimizing an objective function, subject to certain constraints, in order to achieve the optimal outcome

data.name: Health Care
data.description: Health care is the discipline concerned with the provision and delivery of health services to a patient population by personnel in professional and allied health occupations.

subjects.term: Nursing and services of allied health personnel

data.name: Control, Robotics, Automation
data.description: Automation is the technology by which a process or procedure is performed with minimum human assistance

subjects.term: Mechanical devices and figures. Automata. Ingenious mechanisms. Robots (General)

data.name: Intercultural Philosophy and Religious Traditions
data.description: It refer to the study and exploration of philosophical and religious ideas across different cultures and traditions. It is an interdisciplinary field that seeks to foster dialogue, understanding, and appreciation of diverse philosophical and religious perspectives from around the world. Religious traditions play a significant role in shaping the philosophical outlook of cultures around the world. In the context of intercultural philosophy, religious traditions are seen as important sources of philosophical ideas, ethical principles, and metaphysical beliefs.

subjects.term: Philosophical traditions and schools of thought

data.name: Popular Culture
data.description: The academic study of popular culture encompassing diverse media such as film, television, and comic books, combining communication and cultural studies.

data.name: Christianity
data.description: Christianity is an Abrahamic monotheistic religion based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth.

data.name: IT in Business
data.description: IT (Information Technology) in business refers to the use of computer-based technologies to store, process, and transmit information in various forms. ICT (Information and Communication Technology) is a broader term that encompasses both the hardware and software tools used for communication, collaboration, and information management.  As a field of business and management research and practice, IT and ICT cover a wide range of topics, including:  Information systems: This includes the design, development, implementation, and management of information systems such as databases, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, and other business intelligence tools.  E-commerce: The use of technology to conduct business transactions over the internet, including online shopping, electronic payments, and digital marketing.  Cybersecurity: The protection of computer systems and networks from theft, damage, or unauthorized access, including topics such as risk management, data privacy, and compliance with regulations.  Digital transformation: The integration of digital technology into all areas of a business, including business processes, customer experience, and organizational culture.  Cloud computing: The use of remote servers to store, manage, and process data, which can provide benefits such as scalability, flexibility, and cost savings.  Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning: The use of algorithms and statistical models to analyze and make predictions based on large data sets.  Mobile computing: The use of mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets to access and share information.  Social media: The use of social networking sites, blogs, and other online platforms for marketing, customer engagement, and brand management.  Overall, IT and ICT are critical components of modern business and management, and research in this field continues to explore new ways to leverage technology to improve organizational performance, enhance customer experience, and drive innovation. This topic deals with all aspects of information technology in business and management processes, including strategy development, digitalization, digital transformation. Business IT infrastructure, information systems, process management, e-business, enterprise architecture and software management are the core sub-topics.

data.name: Database Management System
data.description: A Database Management System (DBMS) is software that enables the creation, organization, management, and retrieval of data from a database.

data.name: Structural Biology
data.description: Structural biology is the study of the molecular structure and dynamics of biological macromolecules, particularly proteins and nucleic acids, and how alterations in their structures affect their function. Structural biology incorporates the principles of molecular biology, biochemistry and biophysics.

data.name: Materials Characterization Technique
data.description: Techniques and instrumentation refers to the development of methods and tools to be used in applied physics, materials science or nanotechnology for design, synthesis, manufacturing, imaging or analytics.

data.name: Developmental Biology and Stem Cells
data.description: Developmental biology is the field of biology that studies the processes by which multicellular organisms grow and develop, controlled by their genes. Knowledge of normal developmental processes can aid in the understanding of developmental abnormalities and other conditions such as cancer..Development is the process of growth of the individual from zygote to adult. It includes the coordinated processes of cell proliferation, motility and differentiation, the patterning of organs, regeneration and gametogenesis. Central concepts are the progressive commitment and restriction of cell fate by expression of a genetic program, and the subsequent patterned signalling of future fates to uncommitted cells. // Development is the process of growth of the individual from zygote to adult. data.name: Soft Materials
data.description: Soft materials are materials that can be easily deformed by thermal stresses or thermal fluctuations at about room temperature. Soft materials include liquids, polymers, foams, gels, colloids, granular materials, as well as most soft biological materials.

subjects.term: Materials of special composition or structure, A-Z

data.name: Biotechnology
data.description: Biotechnology is a broad discipline in which biological processes, organisms, cells or cellular components are exploited to develop new technologies. New tools and products developed by biotechnologists are useful in research, agriculture, industry and the clinic.

data.name: Management
data.description: Define General Management as a field of management research General management is a field of management research that focuses on the overall administration and coordination of all the activities within an organization. It involves the use of various management techniques, principles, and strategies to achieve organizational goals and objectives.  General management encompasses various functions, including planning, organizing, staffing, directing, and controlling. These functions are performed at different levels of the organization, ranging from top-level executives to front-line supervisors. General management also involves decision-making, problem-solving, and effective communication to ensure the smooth functioning of the organization.  The field of general management research also encompasses various topics, including organizational behavior, leadership, strategic management, entrepreneurship, and innovation. It aims to develop and apply theories, models, and frameworks to improve organizational performance and achieve sustainable competitive advantage.  In summary, general management is a crucial field of management research that focuses on managing all aspects of an organization to achieve its goals and objectives. It plays a vital role in ensuring organizational success and sustainability in a dynamic and ever-changing business environment.

data.name: Topology
data.description: In mathematics, topology is concerned with the properties of space that are preserved under continuous deformations, such as stretching, twisting, crumpling and bending, but not tearing or gluing.

data.name: Condensed Matter Physics
data.description: Condensed Matter Physics refers to the branch of physics that studies the physical properties and behavior of materials in their solid and liquid states. It focuses on understanding the collective behavior and interactions of large numbers of particles, such as atoms, molecules, or electrons, within condensed phases.

subjects.term: Condensed matter physics (liquid state & solid state physics)
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Applied Linguistics
data.description: Applied linguistics is an interdisciplinary field which identifies, investigates, and offers solutions to language-related real-life problems. It the branch of linguistics concerned with practical applications of language studies, for example language teaching, translation, and speech therapy.

data.name: European Law
data.description: The European Union is based on the rule of law. This means that every action taken by the EU is founded on treaties that have been approved democratically by its members. EU laws help to achieve the objectives of the EU treaties and put EU policies into practice.

data.name: Photography
data.description: Photography plays a crucial role in contemporary art. It encompasses and extends across multiple practices. This disregard for a fixed essence is photography’s strength: no aesthetic purity but a range of rhetorical forms used for the creation of fact, fiction and fantasy. Equally the boundary between the still and the moving image is fluid and porous, enabling new forms of image making to be created and disseminated. An informed practice of photography acknowledges the heterogeneous traditions of fine art and visual culture.

data.name: Literary Region or Country
data.description: In literature regionalism refers to fiction or poetry that focuses on specific features, such as dialect, customs, history, and landscape, of a particular region (also called "local colour"). The setting is particularly important in regional literature and the "locale is likely to be rural and/or provincial.

subjects.term: Literature for and by other groups of people

data.name: Quantum Physics
data.description: Quantum mechanics, including quantum field theory, is a fundamental theory in physics which describes nature at the smallest scales of energy levels of atoms and subatomic particles..Quantum mechanics is the study of the dynamics of particles at its most fundamental level. The state of a particle, such as its position or momentum, is described by a statistical distribution given by its wavefunction. As this name suggests, this formalism gives matter many properties that are classically associated with waves.

subjects.term: Quantum physics (quantum mechanics & quantum field theory)
Quantum physics (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory)

data.name: Architecture
data.description: Architecture means the art and practice of designing and making buildings, or the style in which buildings are made.

data.name: Physiology
data.description: Physiology is the branch of the biological sciences that deals with the life-supporting functions and processes of living organisms or their parts. The study of physiology aims to understand how living things work, which can then aid the treatment of diseases.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Life Sciences / Anatomy & Physiology (see also Life Sciences / Human Anatomy & Physiology)

data.name: Marketing
data.description: Marketing research is a crucial component of business and management research that involves the systematic collection and analysis of data related to a company's marketing activities. It is the process of gathering, analyzing, and interpreting data to gain insights into customer behavior, market trends, and competitive landscape to help businesses make informed decisions about their marketing strategies. Marketing research involves various methods and techniques, including surveys, focus groups, interviews, observation, and data analysis tools. The research can be conducted for different purposes such as product development, pricing strategies, customer satisfaction, brand awareness, and market segmentation. Overall, marketing research plays a crucial role in helping companies understand their customers' needs and preferences, identify potential opportunities and challenges in the market, and make informed decisions to achieve their business objectives.

data.name: Biomedical Engineering and Bioengineering
data.description: Application of engineering principles and design concepts to medicine and biology for healthcare purposes

data.name: Inclusive Education
data.description: Inclusive education means all children in the same classrooms, in the same schools. It means real learning opportunities for groups who have traditionally been excluded – not only children with disabilities, but speakers of minority languages too.

data.name: Ecology
data.description: Ecology is the study of how organisms interact with each other and their environment. It considers processes that occur at the population, community and ecosystem levels and has a particular focus on biodiversity.

data.name: Classical and Continuum Physics
data.description: classical physics refers to the branch of physics that describes the motion and behavior of macroscopic objects, continuum physics focuses on the study of continuous matter and the mathematical models that describe its behavior.

data.name: Programming Language
data.description: A programming language is a set of symbols whose strings are governed by rules apt to communicate instructions to a particular machine. Such strings may be concatenated into longer code and implement abstract algorithms in the form of programs specific to actual computing devices.

data.name: Applied and Technical Physics
data.description: Applied physics is the study of physics for a practical purpose, as opposed to physics motived solely for an improved fundamental understanding. This includes technological advances such as the development of electronics, photonics and device physics, or improving practical investigations, such as experimental nuclear physics and experimental particle physics.

data.name: Educational Psychology
data.description: Educational psychology is a branch of psychology that focuses on understanding how people learn and develop in educational settings. It applies psychological principles and theories to improve teaching methods, enhance learning outcomes, and promote optimal educational experiences. Educational psychologists study various aspects of learning and instruction, including cognitive processes, motivation, memory, assessment, classroom management, and individual differences among learners. They collaborate with educators, administrators, and policymakers to design effective educational interventions, create supportive learning environments, and address the diverse needs of learners.

data.name: School and Schooling
data.description: A school is an educational institution designed to provide learning spaces and learning environments for the teaching of students under the direction of teachers. Most countries have systems of formal education, which is sometimes compulsory. In these systems, students progress through a series of schools. Schooling refers to the process of attending school and learning the body of knowledge taught in a curriculum.

subjects.term: Schools and their activities; special education

data.name: Zoology
data.description: Zoology is the scientific study of animals. This discipline can include animal anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, genetics, evolution, ecology, behaviour and conservation.

data.name: Computer Hardware
data.description: Hardware refers to the external and internal devices and equipment that enables to perform major functions such as input, output, storage, communication, processing, and more.

data.name: Literature and Technology
data.description: Literature and technology are two interconnected fields that have influenced and impacted each other throughout history. Literature often reflects the influence of technology on society, exploring its impact on individuals, relationships, and the human experience. Science fiction is a literary genre that often explores the implications of technology on society and imagines future advancements.

data.name: Psychological Methods
data.description: Psychological methods, as a field of study, encompasses the various techniques, tools, and approaches employed in psychological research and investigation. It focuses on the rigorous and systematic methods used to collect, analyze, and interpret data in order to understand human behavior, cognition, emotions, and mental processes.

data.name: International Economics
data.description: International economics is concerned with the effects upon economic activity from international differences in productive resources and consumer preferences and the international institutions that affect them. It seeks to explain the patterns and consequences of transactions and interactions between the inhabitants of different countries, including trade, investment and transaction.

data.name: Media Industries
data.description: Media industries can be defined as a varied collection of organisations that share the production, publication and distribution of media. Industries include but are not limited to: news, publishing, film, music, social media, advertising, radio, games, TV, comics, books.

subjects.term: Media, entertainment, information and communication industries

data.name: Veterinary Science
data.description: Veterinary medicine and sciences comprise medical subsections and accompanying research concerned with the prevention, control, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases, disorders or injuries affecting the health and welfare of domestic and wild animals. The discipline includes monitoring, management and prevention of zoonotic diseases and advances research under the One Health approach. It further covers laboratory animal science and translational research. Veterinarians ensure a safe food supply for people by maintaining the health and welfare of food-producing animals and monitoring product quality. (Adopted and revised from ENCYCLOPÆDIA BRITANNICA)

data.name: Materials for Energy and Catalysis
data.description: Materials for energy and catalysis are materials with electrochemical properties that makes them suitable for use in energy storage applications, such as batteries, and electrocatalysts.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Structural Materials
data.description: Structural materials are materials used or studied primarily for their mechanical properties, as opposed to their electronic, magnetic, chemical or optical characteristics. This can include a materials response to an applied force, whether this response is elastic or plastic, its hardness, and its strength.

data.name: Logic
data.description: Logic is the study of correct reasoning. It includes both formal and informal logic. Formal logic is the science of deductively valid inferences or logical truths.

data.name: Nanotechnology
data.description: Nanotechnology is a field of science and technology that focuses on the manipulation and control of matter at the nanoscale, typically in the range of 1 to 100 nanometers. It involves the design, characterization, and application of materials, structures, and devices with novel properties and functionalities at the nanoscale. Nanotechnology spans multiple scientific disciplines, including physics, chemistry, biology, materials science, and engineering.

data.name: Languages
data.description: Language is a means of communicating complex ideas or feelings. Although human language can be verbal or non-verbal, it is more complex than any form of animal communication and reflects the culture of its speakers.

data.name: Geometry
data.description: Geometry  is a branch of mathematics concerned with questions of shape, size, relative position of figures, and the properties of space

data.name: History of the Americas
data.description: History of the Americas covers the historical development of North, Central, and South America, including indigenous cultures, colonization, independence movements, and contemporary issues.

data.name: Fine Art
data.description: Fine Art is the traditional term used to embrace painting, sculpture and printmaking, produced for its own sake and not concerned with whether it is functional or practical. Recently the term has come to include photography, video and the modern technologies that generate visual imagery.

data.name: Skills
data.description: A skill is the learned ability to act with determined results with good execution often within a given amount of time, energy, or both. Skills can often be divided into domain-general and domain-specific skills.

data.name: Science Communication
data.description: The practice of informing, educating, raising awareness of science-related topics, and increasing the sense of wonder about scientific discoveries and arguments. Science communicators and audiences are ambiguously defined and the expertise and level of science knowledge varies with each group. Two types of science communication are outward-facing or science outreach (typically conducted by professional scientists to non-expert audiences) and inward-facing or science "inreach" (expert to expert communication from similar or different scientific backgrounds). Examples of outreach include science journalism and science museums. Examples of inreach include scholarly communication and publication in scientific journals.

data.name: Process Engineering
data.description: Process engineering focuses on the design, operation, control, optimization and intensification of chemical, physical, and biological processes

data.name: Astronomy, Cosmology and Space Sciences
data.description: Astronomy and space science are the study of objects and phenomena that are found inside and beyond our solar system. This combines theoretical work, numerical simulations and observation with both terrestrial and space-craft-borne instruments of the electromagnetic radiation, high-energy particles, and gravitational radiation emitted by astronomical objects.Cosmology deals with the origin, development and structure of the cosmos at large.

data.name: Surveying
data.description: Surveying or land surveying is the technique, profession, and science of determining the terrestrial or three-dimensional positions of points and the distances and angles between them

data.name: Archaeological Methodology
data.description: Archaeological methodology refers to the approaches, techniques, and procedures employed by archaeologists to investigate and understand the past through the study of material remains. Archaeological methodology involves a systematic and scientific approach to excavating, recording, analyzing, and interpreting artifacts, structures, and other archaeological evidence.

data.name: Journalism
data.description: Journalism is the production and distribution of reports on the interaction of events, facts, ideas, and people that are the "news of the day" and that informs society to at least some degree. The word applies to the occupation (professional or not), the methods of gathering information, and the organizing literary styles. Journalistic media include: print, television, radio, Internet, and, in the past, newsreels.

data.name: Buddhism
