data.name: Chemical Synthesis
data.description: Chemical synthesis is the process by which one or more chemical reactions are performed with the aim of converting a reactant or starting material into a product or multiple products. Chemical synthesis is at the heart of much chemistry research as it is the basis for discovering compounds with new physical or biological properties.

data.name: Data Analysis and Big Data
data.description: Data Analysis and Big Data are related fields that involve the exploration, interpretation, and extraction of insights from large and complex datasets.

data.name: Computational Materials Science
data.description: Computational materials science and engineering uses modeling, simulation, theory, and informatics to understand materials. The main goals include discovering new materials, determining material behavior and mechanisms, explaining experiments, and exploring materials theories.

data.name: Moral Philosophy and Applied Ethics
data.description: Moral philosophy explores questions about the nature of morality and examines how persons should live their lives in relation to others. Applied ethics discusses the practical applications of moral considerations.

data.name: Community Psychology
data.description: Community psychology is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding and promoting the well-being of individuals within their social and cultural contexts. It emphasizes the importance of considering the broader systems and environments in which people live, rather than solely focusing on individual-level factors.

data.name: Educational Philosophy
data.description: An education philosophy is a set of educational beliefs and core values of a person and/or organisation. It directs the purposes and objectives of educational planning, programs and processes. It focuses on what is the purpose of education, what should be taught, and how it should be taught. In contrast, the philosophy of education is the branch of applied philosophy that investigates the nature of education as well as its aims and problems.

subjects.term: Philosophy and theory, education for specific objectives, educational psychology

data.name: Operations Research and Decision Theory
data.description: Operations Research (OR) is a field of management research and practice that uses mathematical modeling, statistical analysis, and optimization techniques to solve complex problems in organizations. The primary objective of OR is to improve decision-making processes and the overall efficiency and effectiveness of organizations. OR involves the application of various techniques such as linear programming, network analysis, queuing theory, simulation, and decision analysis to support decision-making processes.  Decision Theory, on the other hand, is a field of management research and practice that focuses on understanding and improving the decision-making process. Decision theory provides a framework for analyzing and evaluating decisions under conditions of uncertainty and risk. It involves the use of mathematical models and methods to identify the best course of action based on available information, preferences, and outcomes. Decision theory is used in a wide range of applications, including business, economics, psychology, and political science.  Both OR and Decision Theory are interdisciplinary fields that draw on knowledge from mathematics, computer science, economics, psychology, and other disciplines. They are widely used in various domains, including manufacturing, logistics, finance, healthcare, and transportation, to name a few. By providing a scientific approach to decision-making, OR and Decision Theory help organizations make better-informed decisions and achieve their goals more effectively.

data.name: History of Psychology
data.description: The history of psychology is a field of study that examines the development of psychological thought and practices over time. It involves the critical analysis of the intellectual, social, and cultural factors that have shaped the emergence, evolution, and diversification of psychological theories, concepts, and methods from ancient times to the present. The history of psychology seeks to provide a nuanced and contextualized understanding of the origins, influences, and contributions of key figures and movements in psychology, as well as the broader historical and cultural contexts that have influenced their work.

data.name: Public International Law
data.description: Public International Law governs the legal relationships between sovereign states and other international actors, covering areas such as human rights, international treaties, and conflict resolution.

data.name: Materials for Devices
data.description: Materials for devices are materials employed in devices because of their particular properties, such as electrical, thermal, magnetic, mechanical, ferroelectric or piezoelectric properties. Examples of materials for devices are polymers, oxides, semiconductors and liquid crystals.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials

data.name: Atomic, Molecular and Chemical Physics
data.description: Atomic and molecular physics it the study of the properties, dynamics and interactions of the basic (but not fundamental) building blocks of matter. A crucial component of this is understanding the behaviour of the electrons that surround the atomic nucleus; these dynamics dominate the way atoms and molecules interact with their environment.

subjects.term: Atomic physics. Constitution and properties of matter

data.name: Human Resource Management
data.description: Human Resource Management (HRM) is a field of research and practice that focuses on managing people in organizations. It involves the strategic planning, recruitment, selection, development, motivation, and retention of employees to achieve organizational goals and objectives. As a field of research, HRM studies focus on understanding the theoretical and practical aspects of managing people in organizations. Research topics may include recruitment and selection, training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations, and legal compliance. Researchers in HRM aim to provide evidence-based insights that can inform the development of effective HR policies and practices in organizations. As a field of practice, HRM involves designing and implementing strategies, policies, and practices to attract, develop, motivate, and retain employees. HR professionals are responsible for managing a wide range of HR functions, including talent acquisition, performance management, training and development, compensation and benefits, and employee relations. They work closely with other functional areas of the organization to align HR strategies with overall business goals and objectives. Overall, HRM is an important field of research and practice as it contributes to the development of effective and sustainable HR strategies that can enhance organizational performance, employee engagement, and overall well-being.

subjects.term: BUSINESS & ECONOMICS / Human Resources & Personnel Management

data.name: Construction Management
data.description: overseeing and managing all aspects of a construction project, from the initial planning and design phase to the final completion and delivery of the project. It involves coordinating various activities, resources, and stakeholders to ensure the successful execution of a construction project within defined constraints of time, cost, quality, and safety.

subjects.term: Management of the construction site. Superintendence of building construction

data.name: Transportation Technology and Traffic Engineering
data.description: design, operation, and management of transportation systems to facilitate the movement of people and goods efficiently and safely.

data.name: Sector and Industry Studies
data.description: Sector analysis is an assessment of the economic and financial condition and prospects of a given sector of the economy. Sector analysis serves to provide an investor with a judgment about how well companies in the sector are expected to perform. Industry refers to a group of companies that operate in a similar business sphere, and its categorization is narrow. Sector refers to a part of the economy into which various industries consisting of a great number of companies can be fit, and is larger in comparison.

data.name: Science Education
data.description: Science education is the teaching and learning of science to school children, college students, or adults within the general public. The field of science education includes work in science content, science process (the scientific method), some social science, and some teaching pedagogy.

data.name: Population and Demography
data.description: Demography is the scientific study of human populations, focusing on their size, structure, distribution, and characteristics. It involves analyzing statistical data and social factors to understand population dynamics and how they change over time. Demography examines various aspects, including birth rates, death rates, migration patterns, age distribution, gender composition, socioeconomic status, and other demographic variables. The discipline of demography utilizes methods and tools from statistics, sociology, economics, geography, and other related fields to study and interpret population data. It provides valuable insights into population growth, mortality and fertility patterns, population aging, migration trends, and the implications of these factors for societies, economies, and public policy.

data.name: Film and Television Studies
data.description: Film studies is an academic discipline that deals with various theoretical, historical, and critical approaches to cinema as an art form and a medium. Television studies is an academic discipline that deals with critical approaches to television.

data.name: Entrepreneurship
data.description: Entrepreneurship as a field of research refers to the study of the processes, activities, and behaviors that lead to the creation and growth of new ventures. It involves examining the factors that influence the success or failure of entrepreneurial activities and identifying best practices and strategies for starting and growing successful businesses.  In entrepreneurship research, scholars and practitioners study a wide range of topics, including:  Opportunity recognition and evaluation: How do entrepreneurs identify and evaluate business opportunities, and what factors influence their decision-making?  Innovation and creativity: How do entrepreneurs come up with new and innovative ideas for products, services, and business models, and what role does creativity play in the entrepreneurial process?  Entrepreneurial finance: What are the sources of capital for new ventures, and how can entrepreneurs access the funding they need to start and grow their businesses?  Entrepreneurial marketing: How do entrepreneurs market and sell their products and services, and what marketing strategies are most effective for new ventures?  Entrepreneurial leadership: What are the leadership styles and behaviors that are most effective in the context of entrepreneurial activities, and how can entrepreneurs develop these skills?  Overall, entrepreneurship as a field of research seeks to understand the processes, behaviors, and strategies that lead to successful entrepreneurship, and to develop practical recommendations for entrepreneurs and policymakers to support the creation and growth of new ventures.

subjects.term: New business enterprises. Starting a new business. Business incubators

data.name: Social Philosophy
data.description: Social philosophy covers topics related to public life, civic life, and culture.

data.name: Public Law
data.description: Public law is the part of law that governs relations between legal persons and a government, between different institutions within a state, between different branches of governments, as well as relationships between persons that are of direct concern to society.

data.name: Nursing
data.description: Nursing encompasses autonomous and collaborative care of individuals of all ages, families, groups and communities, sick or well, and in all settings. Nursing includes the promotion of health, prevention of illness, and the care of ill, disabled and dying people. Advocacy, promotion of a safe environment, research, participation in shaping health policy and in patient and health systems management, and education are also key nursing roles. Nursing is the most diverse of all health care professions. Nurses practice in a wide range of settings but generally nursing is divided depending on the needs of the person being nursed.  The major populations are:  communities/public family/individual across the lifespan adult-gerontology pediatrics neonatal women's health/gender-related mental health informatics (eHealth) acute care hospitals ambulatory settings (physician offices, urgent care settings, camps, etc) school/college infirmaries

subjects.term: Nursing and services of allied health personnel

data.name: Mathematical Logic and Foundations
data.description: Mathematical logic explores the applications of formal logic to mathematics. It bears close connections to metamathematics, the foundations of mathematics, and theoretical computer science. The unifying themes in mathematical logic include the study of the expressive power of formal systems and the deductive power of formal proof systems. Foundations of Mathematics is the study of the philosophical and logical and/or algorithmic basis of mathematics, or, in a broader sense, the mathematical investigation of what underlies the philosophical theories concerning the nature of mathematics. Foundations of mathematics can be conceived as the study of the basic mathematical concepts (set, function, geometrical figure, number, etc.) and how they form hierarchies of more complex structures and concepts, especially the fundamentally important structures that form the language of mathematics (formulas, theories and their models giving a meaning to formulas, definitions, proofs, algorithms, etc.) also called metamathematical concepts, with an eye to the philosophical aspects and the unity of mathematics.

data.name: Applied Statistics
data.description: Applied statistics is the use of statistical techniques to solve real-world data analysis problems. It is the root of data analysis, and the practice of applied statistics involves analyzing data to help define and determine organizational needs.

data.name: Health Psychology
data.description: Health psychology is the study of psychological and behavioral processes in health, illness, and healthcare. It is concerned with understanding how psychological, behavioral, and cultural factors contribute to physical health and illness

data.name: Geography
data.description: Geography is a branch of academic study broadly concerned with the Earth. Geographers can be roughly divided into those concerned with physical earth processes (physical geography), such as erosion and sedimentation, and those who are more concerned with human activities (human geography).

data.name: Asian History
data.description: Asian History encompasses the study of the historical development of the Asian continent, including its diverse cultures, political systems, and social transformations from ancient times to the present.

data.name: Archaeology and Heritage
data.description: Archaeology and heritage are closely intertwined fields that focus on the study, preservation, and interpretation of the past and cultural heritage. While archaeology primarily deals with the scientific investigation of past human societies through the analysis of material remains, heritage encompasses a broader concept that includes the cultural, historical, and natural aspects of human society and the built environment.

subjects.term: Preservation, restoration, and conservation of antiquities. Antiquities and state

data.name: Post-Processual Archaeology
data.description: Post-processual archaeology, also known as interpretive archaeology or the "New Archaeology," is a theoretical approach that emerged in the 1980s as a reaction against the processual archaeology that dominated the field during the 1960s and 1970s. Post-processual archaeology emphasizes the importance of subjective interpretations, social contexts, and the role of individuals in shaping the archaeological record.

data.name: Indigenous Religion
data.description: Indigenous religions are the ancestral religions of peoples who are native to particular landscapes.

subjects.term: Other indigenous, ethnic and folk religions and spiritual beliefs

data.name: Comparative Religion
data.description: Comparative Religion studies different religious traditions to understand their beliefs, practices, and historical contexts. It compares religions to identify both shared patterns and distinctive features.

subjects.term: Study of comparative religion. Historiography. Methodology

data.name: Public Economics
data.description: Public economics (or economics of the public sector) is the study of government policy through the lens of economic efficiency and equity. Public economics builds on the theory of welfare economics and is ultimately used as a tool to improve social welfare. Welfare can be defined in terms of well-being, prosperity, and overall state of being.

data.name: Philology
data.description: Philology is an interdisciplinary field of study that encompasses the historical, comparative, and critical analysis of languages and literature. It involves the study of texts, their historical context, linguistic evolution, and cultural significance. The term "philology" derives from the Greek words "philos" (love) and "logos" (word, study). Philology traditionally involves the study of ancient and classical languages, such as Latin and Ancient Greek, as well as the analysis of historical texts and their interpretation.

data.name: Statistical Theory and Methods
data.description: Statistical Theory and Methods involve the study and application of mathematical principles and techniques for collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and making inferences from data. It encompasses the development and exploration of statistical models, estimation methods, hypothesis testing, and data analysis techniques.

data.name: Philosophy of the Social Sciences
data.description: Philosophy of the Social Sciences examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of the social sciences, exploring questions about social reality, explanation, and the nature of social phenomena.

subjects.term: Relation to social sciences. Relation to sociology

data.name: New Religious Movements
data.description: New religious movements (NRMs) are groups or organizations that adopt a new or innovative set of religious beliefs and practices.

data.name: Algebra
data.description: one of the broad parts of mathematics, in its most general form, algebra is the study of mathematical symbols and the rules for manipulating these symbols. It includes everything from elementary equation solving to the study of abstractions such as groups, rings, and fields

data.name: Theoretical Linguistics
data.description: Theoretical linguistics is a term in linguistics which, like the related term general linguistics, can be understood in different ways. Both can be taken as a reference to theory of language, or the branch of linguistics which inquires into the nature of language and seeks to answer fundamental questions as to what language is, or what the common ground of all languages is. The goal of theoretical linguistics can also be the construction of a general theoretical framework for the description of language.

data.name: Political Philosophy

It explores the various factors that contribute to the development of personality traits and how these traits shape an individual's behavior in different situations. It also investigates the role of individual differences in areas such as intelligence, creativity, and mental health. Ultimately, the goal of Personality and Differential Psychology is to understand the unique aspects of individuals and how these aspects relate to their experiences and outcomes in life.

subjects.term: Psychology: the self, ego, identity, personality

data.name: Microeconomics
data.description: Microeconomics is a branch of mainstream economics that studies the behavior of individuals and firms in making decisions regarding the allocation of scarce resources and the interactions among these individuals and firms.

data.name: Fundamentals of Law
data.description: Fundamentals of Law is a basic law that is either a codified constitution, or in countries with uncodified constitutions, a law given to have constitution powers and effect.

subjects.term: Jurisprudence. Philosophy and theory of law

data.name: Alternative Education
data.description: Alternative education refers to educational approaches, environments, or programs that diverge from mainstream schooling in terms of curriculum, structure, instructional methods, or underlying values and philosophies, often emphasizing individualized learning, inclusivity, and progressive pedagogy.

data.name: Literary Genre

data.name: Economy-wide Country Studies
data.description: Macroeconomics is a branch of economics that deals with the performance, structure, behavior, and decision-making of an economy as a whole—for example, using interest rates, taxes, and government spending to regulate an economy's growth and stability. This includes regional, national, and global economies.   Macroeconomists study topics such as GDP (Gross Domestic Product), unemployment (including unemployment rates), national income, price indices, output, consumption, inflation, saving, investment, energy, international trade, and international finance.

data.name: Innovation and Technology Management
data.description: Innovation and Technology Management is a field within business and management that focuses on developing, implementing, and managing innovative technologies and processes in organizations. It involves the management of technology, research and development, product development, and commercialization of technology. The core topics within Innovation and Technology Management include: Innovation strategy: This involves the formulation of strategies for the development, acquisition, and commercialization of innovative products and technologies. Technology management: This includes the management of technology resources, technology planning, technology development, and technology transfer. Research and development: This includes the development and management of research and development processes, research and development teams, and research and development budgets. Intellectual property: This includes the identification, protection, and exploitation of intellectual property rights, such as patents, trademarks, and copyrights. Commercialization: This includes the development of strategies and processes for bringing new products and technologies to market, including marketing, sales, and distribution.  Open innovation: This includes the development of partnerships and collaborations with external organizations for the sharing of knowledge, resources, and expertise. Entrepreneurship: This includes the development of new ventures and the management of innovation-based startups. Organizational innovation: This includes the development of innovative processes and practices within organizations, such as new organizational structures, work processes, and communication systems. Digital transformation: This involves the integration of digital technologies into organizational processes and operations to increase efficiency and competitiveness.

data.name: Industrial Organization
data.description: Industrial organization is an analysis of factors, operational or otherwise, that contribute to a firm's overall strategy and product placement. It involves a study of different areas, from market power to product differentiation to industrial policy, that affect a firm's operations.

data.name: Philosophy of Mind
data.description: The philosophy of mind is a branch of philosophy that explores the nature of the mind, consciousness, mental states, and their relationship to the physical world. It investigates fundamental questions about the nature of subjective experience, the mind-body problem, the relationship between the mental and the physical, and the nature of mental phenomena.

data.name: Higher Education
data.description: Higher education is tertiary education leading to the award of an academic degree. Higher education, which makes up a component of post-secondary, third-level, or tertiary education, is an optional final stage of formal learning that occurs after completion of secondary education. It represents levels 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the 2011 version of the International Standard Classification of Education structure. Tertiary education at a nondegree level is sometimes referred to as further education or continuing education as distinct from higher education.

data.name: Particle Physics

data.name: Judaism

data.name: Religion and Sciences
data.description: The relationship between religion and science involves discussions that interconnect the study of the natural world, history, philosophy, and theology. Even though the ancient and medieval worlds did not have conceptions resembling the modern understandings of "science" or of "religion", certain elements of modern ideas on the subject recur throughout history. The pair-structured phrases "religion and science" and "science and religion" first emerged in the literature during the 19th century.

data.name: Offshore Engineering
data.description: design, construction, operation, and maintenance of structures and systems in offshore environments, typically in or near bodies of water. It involves the application of engineering principles to address the unique challenges and conditions presented by the offshore environment, such as strong waves, currents, corrosive seawater, and harsh weather conditions.

data.name: Plasma Physics
data.description: Plasma physics is the study of a state of matter comprising charged particles. Plasmas are usually created by heating a gas until the electrons become detached from their parent atom or molecule.

data.description: Surfaces, Interfaces, and Thin Films are interconnected areas of study that focus on the properties, interactions, and applications of materials at the nanoscale. Profession requires training and qualification whereas vocation is the innate ability in an individual towards a particular occupation. In modern times, a vocation refers to an occupation for which a person has special abilities or is trained to do that job.

data.name: Industrial and Organizational Psychology
data.description: Industrial and Organizational Psychology (also known as Work and Organizational Psychology, Business Psychology, or I/O Psychology) is the scientific study of human behavior in the workplace. It applies psychological theories and research methods to understand and improve how individuals and organizations function. This field addresses topics such as personnel selection, employee training and development, organizational effectiveness, and the design of healthy and motivating work environments. The ultimate goal of I/O Psychology is to enhance employee well-being, job satisfaction, and productivity while supporting organizational performance and efficiency.

data.name: Building Materials
data.description: Building materials are substances or products used in the construction or renovation of structures such as houses, buildings, bridges, roads, and infrastructure projects. data.name: Corporate Finance
data.description: Define "Corporate Finance" as in Research and Practice Corporate finance is a field of finance that deals with the financial and investment decisions of corporations. It involves managing the financial resources of a company to maximize shareholder value, while taking into account factors such as risk, cost of capital, and financial performance.  In research and practice, corporate finance encompasses a wide range of topics, including:  Capital budgeting: The process of making investment decisions that involve long-term assets and projects.  Capital structure: The mix of debt and equity financing used to fund a company's operations and growth.  Risk management: The identification, assessment, and mitigation of risks that may impact a company's financial performance.  Corporate valuation: The process of determining the value of a company, its assets, and its investments.  Financial analysis: The process of analyzing a company's financial statements to evaluate its financial performance and make investment decisions.  Mergers and acquisitions: The process of buying, selling, or combining companies to create synergies and improve financial performance.  Corporate governance: The system of rules, practices, and processes by which a company is directed and controlled, including the roles and responsibilities of board members, management, and shareholders.  Dividend policy: The decision of whether to distribute earnings to shareholders in the form of dividends or retain earnings for future investments.  Financial reporting: The process of preparing and disclosing financial information to stakeholders, including financial statements and other disclosures.  Overall, the goal of corporate finance is to create value for shareholders by making effective financial decisions and managing financial risks.

subjects.term: Financial management. Business finance. Corporation finance

It involves the investigation of how individuals perceive, evaluate, and respond to a wide range of artistic stimuli, including visual, auditory, and other sensory forms of art. The psychology of aesthetics seeks to understand the psychological mechanisms that underlie the creation, production, and consumption of art, as well as the factors that influence individual differences in aesthetic preferences and judgments.

data.description: Hinduism is an Indian religion or dharma, a religious and universal order or way of life by which followers abide. data.description: Discrete mathematics is the study of mathematical structures that are fundamentally discrete rather than continuous. In contrast to real numbers that have the property of varying "smoothly", the objects studied in discrete mathematics – such as integers, graphs, and statements in logic – do not vary smoothly in this way, but have distinct, separated values.

data.name: Media Psychology
data.description: Media psychology is an interdisciplinary subfield of psychology that focuses on the study of the ways in which people interact with and are affected by various forms of media, including television, film, video games, social media, and the internet. It involves the application of psychological theories and methods to the study of media and its impact on individuals, groups, and society as a whole. The field of media psychology aims to understand how people perceive, process, and respond to media messages, how media influences attitudes and behaviors, and how media can be used to promote positive outcomes such as health, education, and social change.

data.name: Psychology of Religion and Spirituality
data.description: The psychology of religion and spirituality is a subfield of psychology that explores the role of religious and spiritual beliefs, practices, and experiences in mental health and well-being. It examines the psychological aspects of religion and spirituality, including how they impact individuals' beliefs, attitudes, behaviors, and relationships. Additionally, it investigates the psychological and emotional effects of religious and spiritual practices, such as prayer, meditation, and mindfulness. The field also examines the cultural and social influences of religion and spirituality, including the role they play in identity formation, socialization, and community building. Finally, the psychology of religion and spirituality examines how religious and spiritual beliefs and practices can be integrated into psychological interventions and therapy.

data.name: Counseling Psychology
data.description: Counseling psychology is a general practice and health service provider specialty in professional psychology. It focuses on how people function both personally and in their relationships at all ages. Counseling psychology addresses the emotional, social, work, school and physical health concerns people may have at different stages in their lives, focusing on typical life stresses and more severe issues with which people may struggle as individuals and as a part of families, groups and organizations. Counseling psychologists help people with physical, emotional and mental health issues improve their sense of well‐being, alleviate feelings of distress and resolve crises. They also provide assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of more severe psychological symptoms.

data.name: Developmental Psychology
data.description: Developmental psychology is a branch of psychology that focuses on understanding how individuals grow, change, and develop across the lifespan. It seeks to study and explain the physical, cognitive, emotional, and social changes that occur from infancy through old age. Developmental psychologists explore various aspects of human development, including motor skills, language acquisition, cognitive abilities, social interactions, emotional development, and the formation of identity. They examine both the typical patterns of development and the individual differences that exist among individuals.

data.name: Cultural History

data.name: Macroeconomics and Monetary Economics
data.description: Monetary economics is the branch of economics that studies the different theories of money: it provides a framework for analyzing money and considers its functions (such as medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account), and it considers how money can gain acceptance purely because of its convenience as a public good. The discipline has historically prefigured, and remains integrally linked to, macroeconomics. This branch also examines the effects of monetary systems, including regulation of money and associated financial institutions and international aspects.  Modern analysis has attempted to provide microfoundations for the demand for money and to distinguish valid nominal and real monetary relationships for micro or macro uses, including their influence on the aggregate demand for output. Its methods include deriving and testing the implications of money as a substitute for other assets and as based on explicit frictions.

data.name: Regional Economics
data.description: Regional Economics refer to the economic advantage of a geographical location and human activities of greatest height to contribute maximally to the general growth and prosperity of the region. Spatial economics is the study of how space (distance) affects economic behavior.

data.name: Heterodox Economics
data.description: Heterodox economics is any economic thought or theory that contrasts with orthodox schools of economic thought, or that may be beyond neoclassical economics.

data.name: Psychotherapy
data.description: Psychotherapy is a form of treatment that aims to improve an individual's mental health and well-being by exploring and addressing their psychological and emotional difficulties. It involves the use of various techniques and approaches, such as talk therapy, cognitive-behavioral therapy, and humanistic therapy, to help individuals overcome their problems and improve their quality of life. Psychotherapy is typically conducted by licensed mental health professionals, such as psychologists, psychiatrists, or licensed clinical social workers.

data.name: Computer Engineering

data.name: Demographic Economics

data.name: Daoism

data.name: Accounting
data.description: Accounting is a field of study and practice that involves the measurement, analysis, and communication of financial information about economic entities. The economic entities can be individuals, businesses, government agencies, or non-profit organizations.  In research, accounting is concerned with developing and testing theories related to accounting information, its measurement, and its use. The field of accounting research covers a wide range of topics, including financial accounting, managerial accounting, auditing, taxation, accounting information systems, and corporate governance. In practice, accounting involves the application of accounting principles and techniques to record, classify, and summarize financial transactions, and the preparation of financial statements and reports. The practice of accounting includes bookkeeping, financial analysis, tax preparation, and audit services.  The scope of accounting is vast and includes a variety of specialties, such as forensic accounting, environmental accounting, and international accounting. Forensic accounting involves the use of accounting principles and techniques to investigate financial fraud and other crimes. Environmental accounting is concerned with the impact of an entity's operations on the environment, while international accounting involves the study of accounting practices and regulations in different countries.

data.name: Operations Management
data.description: Operations management is a branch of management research that focuses on the design, planning, and control of the processes that create goods and services. It involves the systematic management of the entire production or service delivery process, from the acquisition of raw materials to the delivery of finished products to customers.  Operations management includes a range of activities such as production planning, inventory management, quality control, logistics, and supply chain management. It aims to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the production process, reduce costs, and improve customer satisfaction.  Operations management is crucial for organizations in both manufacturing and service sectors. It plays a vital role in ensuring that the products or services produced meet the expectations of customers, while also managing costs and resources effectively. Effective operations management can lead to increased profitability, competitive advantage, and long-term success for an organization.

data.name: Environmental and Sustainability Education
data.description: Environmental education (EE) refers to organized efforts to teach how natural environments function, and particularly, how human beings can manage behavior and ecosystems to live sustainably. It is a multi-disciplinary field integrating disciplines such as biology, chemistry, physics, ecology, earth science, atmospheric science, mathematics, and geography. Education for Sustainable Development means including key sustainable development issues into teaching and learning; for example, climate change, disaster risk reduction, biodiversity, poverty reduction, and sustainable consumption.

subjects.term: Environmental education. Study and teaching. Research

data.name: Behavioral Economics
data.description: Behavioral Economics is the study of psychology as it relates to the economic decision-making processes of individuals and institutions. Behavioral economics is often related with normative economics. It draws on psychology and economics to explore why people sometimes make irrational decisions, and why and how their behavior does not follow the predictions of economic models.

subjects.term: Economics as a science. Relation to other subjects

data.name: Sales and Distribution
data.description: Sales and distribution are two key functions of management that involve getting products and services to customers. Sales refer to the process of identifying potential customers, generating leads, and convincing them to buy a company's products or services. Distribution, on the other hand, involves the movement of goods from the manufacturer to the end consumer.  As a field of management research and practice, sales and distribution focus on developing strategies and tactics for effective customer engagement, lead generation, and customer retention. This involves understanding customer needs, preferences, and behaviors, as well as identifying market trends and competition.  Sales and distribution management also involves developing efficient and effective distribution channels to ensure that products reach customers in a timely and cost-effective manner. This includes managing inventory, transportation, and logistics to ensure that products are delivered to customers at the right time and in the right condition.  Overall, sales and distribution management is a critical component of a company's success, as it helps to generate revenue and maintain customer loyalty. Effective management of these functions requires a deep understanding of customer needs and behaviors, as well as the ability to develop and implement effective marketing and distribution strategies.

A political-economic system can be defined as the relationship between political and economic institutions in a particular country, as well as their policies. data.name: Corporate Environmental Management
data.description: Corporate Environmental Management (CEM) refers to the process by which companies manage their environmental performance and impacts, including the integration of environmental considerations into their business strategy and operations. It involves identifying and assessing environmental risks and opportunities, setting environmental goals and targets, implementing environmental management systems, and reporting on environmental performance.  CEM includes a wide range of topics, including:  Environmental management systems (EMS): EMS provides a systematic approach to manage an organization's environmental performance. It involves identifying and assessing environmental risks, setting environmental objectives and targets, implementing programs to achieve those objectives, and monitoring and reporting on environmental performance.  Environmental policy: It is a statement outlining a company's commitment to environmental sustainability and the actions it will take to achieve its goals. The policy includes the principles, objectives, and strategies that a company will adopt to manage its environmental impacts.  Sustainability reporting: This is the process of measuring, disclosing, and communicating a company's sustainability performance. It includes the reporting of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) metrics to stakeholders, such as investors, customers, and regulators.  Environmental compliance: Environmental compliance refers to a company's adherence to environmental laws and regulations. Companies must comply with a range of environmental regulations, including air and water quality regulations, waste management regulations, and hazardous materials regulations.  Life cycle assessment (LCA): LCA is a tool used to evaluate the environmental impacts of a product or service throughout its entire life cycle, from raw material extraction to disposal. It can be used to identify areas where a company can reduce its environmental impacts and improve its environmental performance.  Environmental auditing: Environmental auditing is the process of assessing a company's environmental performance and compliance with environmental regulations. Audits can be conducted by internal or external auditors and can provide valuable information for improving a company's environmental performance.  Environmental risk assessment: Environmental risk assessment involves identifying and assessing the environmental risks associated with a company's operations. Companies must understand the potential environmental risks associated with their activities and develop plans to mitigate those risks.  Pollution prevention: Pollution prevention involves implementing practices and technologies to reduce or eliminate the generation of pollutants at the source. This approach can help companies reduce their environmental impacts and improve their sustainability performance.

data.name: Business Law
data.description: Business law, also known as commercial law, is a field of study and practice that encompasses the laws and regulations governing businesses and commercial transactions. It includes a wide range of legal topics, such as contracts, torts, intellectual property, employment law, and corporate governance, contracts, the law of Corporations and other Business Organizations, Securities Law, Intellectual Property, Antitrust, Secured Transactions, Commercial Paper, Income Tax, Pensions & Benefits, Trusts & Estates, Immigration Law, Labor Law, Employment Law and Bankruptcy. In research, business law involves the study and development of legal theories and principles to improve the regulation and practice of business activities. The field of business law research covers a wide range of topics, including the impact of legal regulations on business operations, the role of alternative dispute resolution mechanisms, and the development of new legal frameworks for emerging business practices. Contracts refer to legally binding agreements between parties, such as sales contracts, employment contracts, and partnership agreements. Torts refer to civil wrongs, such as negligence or fraud, that can result in legal liability and financial damages. Intellectual property law governs the protection of creative works and inventions, such as patents, trademarks, and copyrights. Employment law involves the legal rights and obligations of employers and employees, such as discrimination, wrongful termination, and workplace safety. Corporate governance refers to the set of processes and principles that govern the way a company is directed, managed, and controlled, as well as the legal and ethical obligations of corporate leaders and stakeholders. In practice, business law involves the application of legal principles and regulations to business activities, such as the formation of companies, the negotiation and execution of contracts, and the resolution of legal disputes. Business law also involves the compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, such as tax laws, environmental regulations, and consumer protection laws. Business law is essential for the proper functioning of businesses and the economy as a whole. By providing a legal framework for business activities, it helps to ensure the fair and ethical conduct of business operations, protect the interests of stakeholders, and promote economic growth and development.

data.name: Gravitational Physics
data.description: Gravitational physics is the study of implications of the general theory of relativity, in which gravitation is a consequence of the curvature of space and time. It involves investigations into the mathematical foundations of the theory, the nature of space and time, and theory's relationship with quantum mechanics.

subjects.term: Theories of gravitation (Including antigravity, quantum gravity)

data.name: Food Science
data.description: Food Science is a multi-disciplinary field involving chemistry, biochemistry, nutrition, microbiology and engineering to give one the scientific knowledge.

data.name: Engineering Mathematics
data.description: Engineering Mathematics is a branch of mathematics that focuses on the application of mathematical principles, methods, and techniques to solve engineering problems. It provides the foundation for understanding and analyzing the mathematical aspects of engineering systems and phenomena.

data.name: Financial Economics
data.description: Financial economics, also known as finance, is the branch of economics characterized by a "concentration on monetary activities", in which "money of one type or another is likely to appear on both sides of a trade". Its concern is thus the interrelation of financial variables, such as share prices, interest rates and exchange rates, as opposed to those concerning the real economy. It has two main areas of focus: asset pricing, commonly known as "Investments", and corporate finance; the first being the perspective of providers of capital, i.e. investors, and the second of users of capital. It thus provides the theoretical underpinning for much of finance.  The subject is concerned with "the allocation and deployment of economic resources, both spatially and across time, in an uncertain environment". It, therefore, centers on decision-making under uncertainty in the context of the financial markets, and the resultant economic and financial models and principles, and is concerned with deriving testable or policy implications from acceptable assumptions. It is built on the foundations of microeconomics and decision theory.  Financial econometrics is the branch of financial economics that uses econometric techniques to parameterize these relationships.

data.name: Resource and Environmental Economics
data.description: Environmental and resource economics, a specialization option in the economic sciences major, applies economic and management decision tools to issues in forest management, water use, pollution, land use, fisheries, recycling, and hazardous wastes.

data.description: Labor economics is the study of the labor force as an element in the process of production. The labor force comprises all those who work for gain within the labor market, whether as employees, employers, or as self-employed, but also the unemployed, who are seeking work.

data.name: Law and Economics
data.description: The law and economics movement applies economic theory and method to the practice of law. It asserts that the tools of economic reasoning offer the best possibility for justified and consistent legal practice. It is arguably one of the dominant theories of jurisprudence.

data.name: Social Work
data.description: Social work is a practice-based profession and an academic discipline that promotes social change and development, social cohesion, and the empowerment and liberation of people.

subjects.term: Social service. Social work. Charity organization and practice

data.name: Creativity Studies

data.name: Educational Leadership

data.name: Diseases

data.name: Terrorism and Political Violence

data.name: Genetics
data.description: Genetics, study of heredity in general and of genes in particular. Genetics forms one of the central pillars of biology and overlaps with many other areas, such as agriculture, medicine, and biotechnology. Genetics is the branch of science concerned with genes, heredity, and variation in living organisms. It seeks to understand the process of trait inheritance from parents to offspring, including the molecular structure and function of genes, gene behaviour in the context of a cell or organism (e.g. dominance and epigenetics), gene distribution, and variation and change in populations.

data.name: Physical-Biological Anthropology
data.description: Deals with human evolution, variability and human adaptation to climatic and habitat changes.

data.name: Organometallic Chemistry
data.description: Organometallic chemistry is the study of the synthesis, structure and reactivity of chemical compounds that contain metal-carbon bonds. The term often also refers to systems with high metal-ligand covalency. These compounds are often used as homogeneous catalysts.

data.name: Human Geography
data.description: Human geography or anthropogeography is the branch of geography that deals with humans and their communities, cultures, economies, and interactions with the environment by studying their relations with and across locations. It analyzes patterns of human social interaction, their interactions with the environment, and their spatial interdependencies by application of qualitative and quantitative research methods.

data.name: Sociology of the Body
data.description: The study of representations and social uses of the human body in modern societies.

data.name: Nuclear Organization
data.description: Nuclear organization refers to the spatial distribution of nuclear contents and components in a way that reflects or facilitates their activities. For example, chromatin or nucleoli may become more condensed or expanded in response to changes in gene expression or cellular growth rate.

data.name: Biological Models
data.description: Biological models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of human tissue function or disease. For example, certain tumour cell lines may serve as cancer models, and transgenic mice that express human beta-amyloid protein may serve as animal models of Alzheimer's disease.

data.name: System Biology
data.description: Bioinformatics is a field of study that uses computation to extract knowledge from biological data. It includes the collection, storage, retrieval, manipulation and modelling of data for analysis, visualization or prediction through the development of algorithms and software..Computational biology and bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary field that develops and applies computational methods to analyse large collections of biological data, such as genetic sequences, cell populations or protein samples, to make new predictions or discover new biology. The computational methods used include analytical methods, mathematical modelling and simulation.

data.name: Plant Pathology
data.description: Plant pathology is the science that studies the causes of plant diseases, the mechanisms by which diseases develop in individual plants and in plant populations, and the ways and means by which plant diseases can be managed or controlled.

data.name: Nanoscale Biophysics
data.description: Nanoscale biophysics is the study of the physical principles governing biological processes occurring on a nanometre scale, typically on an atomic or molecular level. It also encompasses the development of nanotechnologies designed specifically for biophysical investigations.

data.name: Development of the Nervous System
data.description: The development of the nervous system is the ongoing biological process through which nervous tissue is generated and shaped in an embryo and in postnatal and adult organisms. data.name: Molecular Dynamics
data.description: Molecular dynamics is a method that uses Newton’s equations of motion to computationally simulate the time evolution of a set of interacting atoms. Such techniques are dependent on a description of how the molecules will interact – a force field – and are popular in materials chemistry, biochemistry and biophysics.

data.name: Sociology of Religion
data.description: The Sociology of Religion is the study of religious practices, beliefs, and communities using the methods, tools, and analytical frameworks employed in the discipline of sociology.

subjects.term: Social groups: religious groups and communities

data.name: Crime Control and Security
data.description: Crime control and security refers to the field of study within criminology that focuses on preventing and minimizing criminal behavior and ensuring public safety through various strategies, policies, and practices. It encompasses the examination of measures aimed at detecting, deterring, and responding to criminal activities while maintaining social order.

data.name: Lipidology
data.description: Lipidomics is the medical and clinical discipline focused on the biology, metabolism, and disorders of lipids in the human body. data.name: Spectroscopy
data.description: Spectroscopy involves measuring a material's response to a varied stimulus, most commonly radiation. The amount of radiation absorbed or emitted is usually plotted again energy to afford a spectrum that is characteristic for a material and thus is useful in identifying new species.

data.name: Genomics
data.description: Genomics is the study of the full genetic complement of an organism (the genome). It employs recombinant DNA, DNA sequencing methods, and bioinformatics to sequence, assemble, and analyze the structure and function of genomes. The development of the technology to sequence the DNA of whole genomes on a routine basis has given rise to the discipline of genomics, which dominates genetics research today. Genomics is the study of the structure, function, and evolutionary comparison of whole genomes. Genomics has made it possible to study gene function at a broader level, revealing sets of genes that interact to impinge on some biological property of interest to the researcher. Bioinformatics is the computer-based discipline that deals with the analysis of such large sets of biological information, especially as it applies to genomic information.

data.name: Hematolymphoid System

data.description: Sexual selection is an evolutionary process that favours the traits of individuals who compete more successfully for mating opportunities. These traits are not necessarily those favoured by natural selection on survival and can include exaggerated indicators of sexual fitness and increased ability for conflict within or between sexes.

data.name: Clinical Genetics
data.description: Clinical genetics involves the study, counselling and treatment of individuals and families with heritable disorders and disease predisposition. Diagnostic tools include standard ontologies for describing dysmorphology and traits, pedigree analysis, disease locus mapping by linkage or homozygosity, karyotyping, genome sequencing and genotyping.

data.name: Therapeutics
data.description: Therapeutics are treatments used to alleviate or prevent a particular disease. Examples of therapeutics include drug therapy, medical devices, nutrition therapy and stem-cell therapies. Therapeutics can be used in patients with active disease - to treat the disease itself or its signs and symptoms -, in preventive medicine, or as palliative care.

data.name: Genetics Research
data.description: Genetics research is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the role of genes in traits such as the development of disease. It has a key role in identifying potential targets for therapeutic intervention and also in understanding genetically based variations in response to therapeutic interventions.

data.name: Organelles
data.description: Organelles are entities within a eukaryotic cell that have a specialised function. Examples of organelles include the nucleus, the endoplasmic reticulum, the Golgi, mitochondria, vacuoles or lysosomes, and chloroplasts (in plants).

data.name: Cell Death
data.description: Cell death terminates normal cellular functions, including respiration, metabolism, growth and proliferation. Cell death can be non-programmed, for example as the result of accidental injury or trauma, or programmed. Types of programmed cell death include anoikis, apoptosis, autophagy, necrosis, necroptosis and pyroptosis.

data.name: Computational Biology
data.description: Computational biology, which includes many aspects of bioinformatics, is the science of using biological data to develop algorithms or models in order to understand biological systems and relationships.

data.name: Green Chemistry

data.name: Plant Reproduction
data.description: Plant reproduction is the production of new individuals from one or more parent plants. This can be accomplished by sexual or asexual means.

data.name: History of France

data.name: Genotype
data.description: The genotype is the genetic makeup of a cell, organism or individual with reference to a particular characteristic. In diploid or polyploid individuals, it refers to what combination of alleles the individual carries.

data.name: Biological Probes
data.description: Biological probes are molecules that report the presence of specific ions, molecules or molecular events in vitro or in cells by communicating a measurable signal, often a light-based readout. They may function through selective interaction or attachment to a molecule of interest or undergo conformational changes.

data.name: Evolutionary Psychology
data.description: Evolutionary Psychology is a field of study that seeks to understand human behavior and cognition through the lens of evolutionary theory. It explores how evolutionary processes have shaped our psychological mechanisms, adaptive behaviors, and cognitive abilities. This approach posits that many human behaviors and mental processes are the result of natural selection acting on our ancestors' traits, allowing them to survive and reproduce in their environments. By examining the evolutionary roots of various psychological phenomena, Evolutionary Psychology aims to provide insights into the adaptive functions and evolutionary origins of human behavior, cognition, emotions, and social interactions. It draws upon principles from evolutionary biology, psychology, anthropology, and cognitive science to unravel the evolutionary underpinnings of human nature.

data.name: Sequences, Series, Summability
data.description: In mathematics, a series is, roughly speaking, a description of the operation of adding infinitely many quantities, one after the other, to a given starting quantity. Sequences are the basis for series, which are important in differential equations and analysis

data.name: RNA Metabolism
data.description: RNA metabolism refers to any events in the life cycle of ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules, including their synthesis, folding/unfolding, modification, processing and degradation.

data.name: Coding and Information Theory
data.description: Coding and information theory are closely related fields within computer science and mathematics. Coding theory deals with the design and analysis of error-correcting codes, which are used to transmit data reliably over noisy channels. Information theory, on the other hand, focuses on quantifying and measuring information and communication.

data.name: Emerging Technologies
data.description: Emerging technologies are technologies whose development, practical applications, or both are still largely unrealized. These technologies are generally new but also include older technologies finding new applications. Emerging technologies are often perceived as capable of changing the status quo.

data.name: Endocrine System
data.description: The endocrine system refers to the cells, glands and organs that secrete hormones directly into the blood in order to control physiological and behavioural activities. The effects of the endocrine system are slow to initiate and can have long-term effects.

data.name: Actuarial Mathematics
data.description: Actuarial science is the discipline that applies mathematical and statistical methods to assess risk in insurance, finance and other industries and professions. Actuarial Mathematics refers to research for these mathematical methods

data.name: Financial Services
data.description: The financial services industry is a broad field of business and management research that encompasses organizations and institutions involved in the provision of financial products and services to clients. This includes banking, insurance, investment management, and other financial intermediation services. Research in this field may focus on the structure and organization of financial institutions, regulatory frameworks, financial markets and instruments, risk management, and the impact of technology and innovation on the industry. It may also explore the behavior of financial consumers and their decision-making processes, as well as the economic and social implications of financial services for individuals, businesses, and societies.

data.name: Cross-Cultural Psychology
data.description: Cross-cultural psychology is a field of psychology that examines the influence of cultural factors on human behavior, cognition, and development. It explores the similarities and differences in psychological processes across different cultures, aiming to understand the ways in which culture shapes individual and collective behavior.

data.name: Aerospace Technology and Astronautics
data.description: Aerospace engineering is the branch of engineering that designs and builds machines for flight. This includes craft used both inside (aeronautical engineering) and outside (astronautical engineering) the Earth’s atmosphere. Aerospace engineering combines an understanding of fluid dynamics, robust but lightweight materials and the chemistry and thermodynamics of engines.

data.name: Markov Process
data.description: Markov processes are stochastic processes, traditionally in discrete or continuous time, that have the Markov property, which means the next value of the Markov process depends on the current value, but it is conditionally independent of the previous values of the stochastic process. In other words, the behavior of the process in the future is stochastically independent of its behavior in the past, given the current state of the process. Markov processes form an important class of stochastic processes and have applications in many areas

data.name: Sociology of Culture
data.description: Sociology of Culture examines the ways in which culture influences social life, including the production, dissemination, and consumption of cultural goods, as well as the role of cultural norms and values in shaping social behavior.

data.name: Evolutionary Genetics
data.description: Evolutionary genetics is the study of how genetic variation leads to evolutionary change. It includes topics such as the evolution of genome structure, the genetic basis of speciation and adaptation, and genetic change in response to selection within populations.

data.name: Trade and Retail
data.description: The Trade and Retail industry, also known as the Retail sector, is a field within business and management research and practice that focuses on the process of selling consumer goods or services to customers through physical stores or online platforms. The core topics in this field include: Consumer behavior: studying the behavior of consumers in terms of their needs, preferences, and shopping patterns. Marketing and advertising: developing and implementing strategies to promote products and services to target customers, through advertising, branding, and other marketing techniques. Sales management: managing and coordinating sales teams and developing effective sales strategies to drive revenue growth. Supply chain management: managing the flow of goods and services from suppliers to customers, including logistics, inventory management, and distribution. Retail operations: managing the day-to-day operations of retail stores, including staffing, store layout, and inventory management. E-commerce: understanding the online retail environment and developing strategies for online sales, including website design, social media marketing, and search engine optimization. Customer service: developing strategies to provide high-quality customer service, including training staff, developing policies, and measuring customer satisfaction. Store design and visual merchandising: designing store layouts and displays to attract customers and maximize sales. Retail analytics: analyzing data on consumer behavior, sales, and other metrics to inform business decisions and improve performance. Retail innovation: exploring new technologies and trends in the industry, including the use of artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and other digital tools to enhance the retail experience.

data.name: Experimental Organisms

data.name: Topological effects in photonic systems
data.description: Topological effects in photonic systems refer to the emergence of novel optical phenomena and behaviors that are determined by the topological properties of the underlying photonic structures. These effects arise from the interplay between the geometrical arrangement of the photonic materials and the propagation of light waves.

data.name: Mathematics of Planet Earth

data.name: Climate Sciences
data.description: Climate science is the study of relatively long-term weather conditions, typically spanning decades to centuries but extending to geological timescales. The discipline is primarily concerned with atmospheric properties – for example temperature and humidity – and patterns of circulation, as well as interactions with the ocean, the biosphere, and, over longer timescales, the geosphere.

data.name: Earth System Sciences
data.description: Earth System Sciences embrace chemistry, physics, biology, mathematics and applied sciences in transcending disciplinary boundaries to treat the Earth as an integrated system.

data.name: Laser
data.description: Lasers add a mechanism for optical feedback, such as mirrors, that stimulates further emission and generates a high-intensity beam of radiation.

data.name: Cell Types
data.description: Cells are the fundamental, structural, and functional units of living organisms. Cells are composed of cytoplasm containing various organelles, such as the nucleus, in which the DNA is stored, or mitochondria, which participate in energy production. Animal Cells are limited by their plasma membrane while plant and fungi cells have an additional cell wall.

data.name: Computational Chemistry

data.name: Business Consulting
data.description: The consulting industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the study of consulting firms, their operations, and their impact on clients and industries. This research area includes various topics such as the role of consulting firms in strategy development, the impact of consulting services on organizational performance, the management of consulting projects, the effectiveness of consulting interventions, and the evolution of the consulting industry over time. Studies in this field also analyze the structure of consulting firms, the skills and competencies required for consulting, and the dynamics of client-consultant relationships. Overall, the consulting industry is an important area of research for understanding the strategic and operational challenges faced by organizations in various industries and the role of consulting firms in addressing them.

data.name: Agricultural Genetics
data.description: Agricultural genetics is the applied study of the effects of genetic variation and selection used to propagate valuable heritable trait combinations in crop plants and farm animals. The discipline includes use of genetic markers to guide traditional breeding, and introgression and introduction of traits from other species into farmed organisms.

data.name: Black Theology

data.description: Structure determination is a procedure by which the three-dimensional atomic coordinates of a molecule or biomolecule are solved using an analytical technique. data.name: Microscopy
data.description: Microscopy refers to any method used to acquire images of nearby objects at resolutions that greatly exceed the resolving ability of the unaided human eye. Object visualization may be mediated by light or electron beams using optical or magnetic lenses respectively, or through the use of a physical scanning probe that measures one of a wide range of different sample characteristics.

data.name: Archaea
data.description: Archaea are organisms consisting of a single cell without a nucleus and with distinct structural, physiological and evolutionary characteristics. They inhabit a wide range of habitats, including extreme environments. Archaea form one of the three domains of life; the others are bacteria and eukaryotes.

data.name: Organogenesis
data.description: Organogenesis is the process by which the internal organs and specific structures such as the limb are formed during development of an organism. Organogenesis involves the coordination of multiple developmental processes such as embryonic induction, pattern formation, morphogenesis, cell proliferation and differentiation.

data.name: Stem Cell Biology
data.description: Stem-cell research or Stem Cell Biology is the area of research that studies the properties of stem cells and their potential use in regenerative medicine. As stem cells are the source of all tissues and have the potential to develop into different cell types, understanding their properties helps in our understanding of the healthy and diseased body's development and homeostasis.

data.name: Wetting
data.description: Wetting is the ability of a liquid to spread over a solid surface. The degree of wetting is called wettability, and is determined by a force balance between the cohesive forces of the liquid and the adhesive forces between the surface and the liquid.

data.name: Science, Technology and Society
data.description: Science, Technology and Society (STS) is an interdisciplinary field that studies the conditions under which the production, distribution and utilization of scientific knowledge and technological systems occur; the consequences of these activities upon different groups of people.

data.name: Crime and the Media
data.description: The subfield of crime and media within criminology focuses on the intersection of crime and various forms of media, including news reporting, television, film, literature, social media, and the internet. It examines how crime is portrayed, represented, and perceived through these media channels and explores the influence of media on public understanding, attitudes, and responses to crime.

data.name: Energy Grids and Networks
data.description: Energy grids and networks, also known as power grids or electrical grids, refer to the interconnected systems of power generation, transmission, and distribution that deliver electricity from power plants to consumers. These grids and networks enable the efficient and reliable supply of electricity to homes, businesses, and industries

Energy, power generation, distribution and storage

data.description: Neuronal physiology refers to the biology of neuronal function, including an understanding of the molecular and cellular processes that underlie neuronal activity..Neurophysiology is the study of the function of the nervous system. (Ken)

data.name: Biophysical Methods
data.description: Biophysical methods are techniques to study the structure, properties, dynamics or function of biomolecules at an atomic or molecular level. They encompass a range of techniques including microscopy, spectroscopy, electrophysiology, single-molecule methods and molecular modelling.

subjects.term: Auxiliary techniques and procedures; apparatus, equipment, procedures
Methods of research. Technique. Experimental biology

data.description: Potential theory is the study of harmonic functions

data.description: Studies of literary works written in the ancient world. Usually refers to literature from ancient Greece, Rome and other ancient civilizations.
