Literary studies: ancient, classical and medieval

data.name: Biologics
data.description: A biologic is a therapeutic substance that is produced through a biological process (often involving biotechnology methods), rather than chemical synthesis (as for traditional pharmaceuticals). Types of biologic include antibody therapies, vaccines, gene therapies and cell therapies.

data.name: Business Strategy and Leadership
data.description: Business strategy research is a field of management research that focuses on the development, implementation, and evaluation of strategies that organizations use to achieve their objectives. This field of research examines the various elements that contribute to the success of an organization's strategy, including its competitive positioning, industry dynamics, internal resources and capabilities, and external environment. Business strategy research involves analyzing the strategic decisions made by firms, such as mergers and acquisitions, diversification, market entry, and product innovation. It also examines the role of leadership in shaping and executing strategies, as well as the impact of various organizational structures and cultures on strategy implementation. Research in this field employs various methodologies, including quantitative analysis, case studies, and simulation models. Business strategy researchers often collaborate with practitioners in the field, such as executives and consultants, to develop and test new strategies and approaches. The ultimate goal of business strategy research is to provide insights and guidance for organizations as they navigate complex and dynamic business environments. By understanding the factors that drive successful strategy formulation and implementation, businesses can make informed decisions and achieve sustainable competitive advantage. Leadership research is a field of management research that focuses on understanding and analyzing the various aspects of leadership. This field explores the characteristics, behaviors, and skills that make an effective leader and examines how leaders can inspire and motivate others to achieve organizational goals. Leadership research encompasses a wide range of topics, including leadership styles, leadership theories, leadership development, and leadership effectiveness. Researchers in this field use a variety of research methods, such as surveys, case studies, experiments, and interviews, to explore these topics and gain a deeper understanding of leadership and its impact on organizational outcomes. The findings from leadership research have practical implications for organizations, as they provide insight into how to develop effective leaders, create a positive work culture, and enhance organizational performance. As such, leadership research is an important area of study in management research, and it continues to evolve as new trends and challenges emerge in the business world.

data.name: Chemistry in Society
data.description: Chemistry in Society refers to the study and application of chemical principles, processes, and technologies to address various societal issues and challenges. It recognizes that chemistry plays a crucial role in shaping and impacting different aspects of our lives, from environmental concerns to health, energy, technology, and more.

data.name: Mathematical Applications in Environmental Science
data.description: Using a mathematical approach for any issues in the environmental sciences.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Environmental Science (see also Chemistry / Environmental)
Land, recreational and wilderness areas, energy

data.name: Manifolds and Cell Complexes
data.description: including Differential Topology

data.name: Language Policy and Planning
data.description: Language policy and planning refers to the deliberate efforts made by governments, institutions, and communities to manage and regulate the use of languages within a particular jurisdiction or social context. It involves making decisions about language-related issues such as language choice, language education, language rights, language maintenance, and language revitalization. Language policy and planning are crucial for promoting linguistic diversity, ensuring effective communication, and addressing social, cultural, and political concerns related to language use.

data.name: Pathogenesis
data.description: Pathogenesis is the term that is used to describe the origin and development of a disease.

data.name: Otorhinolaryngology
data.description: Otorhinolaryngology is a medical specialty focusing on the diagnosis, evaluation and management of diseases of head and neck and principally the ears, nose and throat.

data.name: Plant Symbiosis
data.description: Plant symbiosis is the close and persistent co-existence of individuals of more than one species, at least one of which is a plant. In most cases both the plant and its symbiont derive an advantage from the interaction.

data.name: Membrane Trafficking
data.description: Membrane trafficking is the process by which proteins and other macromolecules are distributed throughout the cell, and released to or internalised from the extracellular space. Membrane trafficking uses membrane-bound vesicles as transport intermediaries. Cargo molecules are enclosed within or associate with the membrane of these vesicles.

data.name: Computational Physics and Simulations
data.description: Computational physics is the study and implementation of numerical analysis to solve problems in physics for which a quantitative theory already exists.

data.name: Cell Adhesion
data.description: Cell adhesion is the process by which cells form contacts with each other or with their substratum through specialized protein complexes. Intercellular adhesion can be mediated by adherens junctions, tight junctions and desmosomes, whereas cells can interact with extracellular matrix molecules through focal adhesions.

data.name: Nucleic Acid
data.description: Nucleic acids (DNA or RNA) are polymers of nucleotides – each nucleotide consists of a pentose sugar, a phosphate group and one of the nitrogenous bases (purines and pyrimidines). Nucleic acids function in encoding, transmitting and expressing genetic information in either the double-stranded form (mostly for DNA) or in single-stranded form (mostly for RNA).

data.name: Latin American/Caribbean Literature
data.description: Literature from Latin America (South America) and the Caribbean, both oral and written. Includes both literary works written in Spanish, Portuguese, indigenous languages of the Americas, French, English and Dutch.

subjects.term: Literature for and by other groups of people--Latin America

data.name: Immunological Techniques
data.description: Immunological techniques include both experimental methods to study the immune system and methods to generate or use immunological reagents as experimental tools. The most common immunological methods relate to the production and use of antibodies to detect specific proteins in biological samples.

subjects.term: Methods of research. Technique. Experimental biology

data.name: Water
data.description: Hydrology is the study of the cycling of water through different reservoirs on Earth. It also refers to the cycling of liquids such as hydrocarbons on other planets. Hydrology focuses on the distribution of water in the subsurface, surface and atmosphere, the chemistry of that water, and the effects of climate on the water cycle.

data.name: Musculoskeletal System
data.description: The musculoskeletal system is an organ system comprising the bones, muscles and connective tissues (including cartilage, tendons and ligaments) that bind tissues and organs together. The main functions of this system are to provide structure and support to the body, protect vital organs and enable movement.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Life Sciences / Anatomy & Physiology (see also Life Sciences / Human Anatomy & Physiology)

data.name: Lymphoid Tissues
data.description: Lymphoid tissues are organized structures that support immune responses. The bone marrow and thymus are primary lymphoid tissues and the sites of lymphocyte development. The lymph nodes, spleen, tonsils and Peyer’s patches are examples of secondary lymphoid tissue. Chronic inflammation can lead to the development of tertiary lymphoid tissue.

data.name: History of Germany and Central Europe
data.description: History of Germany and Central Europe studies the historical development of Germany and its neighboring Central European countries, focusing on political, social, and cultural transformations.

subjects.term: Germany and neighboring central European countries

data.name: Biomechanics
data.description: Biomechanics is the scientific study of the mechanics of living structures, or of non-living structures such as silk or nacre that are produced by organisms.

subjects.term: Biomechanics and effects of mechanical forces

data.name: Hormone
data.description: Hormones are small molecules or peptides that act in signalling between one cell or cell set and another. They are generally involved in high-level processes of an organism such as growth, reproduction, and digestion; examples include adrenal complex hormones, gonadal hormones and gastrointestinal hormones, respectively. Hormones can be paracrine, endocrine or autocrine factors.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Life Sciences / Anatomy & Physiology (see also Life Sciences / Human Anatomy & Physiology)

data.name: Clinical Research
data.description: Clinical research is the study of health and illness in people. Clinical research is a branch of healthcare science that determines the safety and effectiveness of medications, devices, diagnostic products and treatment regimens intended for human use.

data.name: Pediatrics
data.description: Paediatrics is a medical discipline focused on individuals from birth to the end of adolescence. The care of paediatric patients is different to that of adults, as many drugs are processed differently in these two groups. Growth and development are also more important in paediatric patients than in adults.

data.name: Pharmacology
data.description: Pharmacology is a branch of biomedical science, encompassing clinical pharmacology, that is concerned with the effects of drugs/pharmaceuticals and other xenobiotics on living systems, as well as their development and chemical properties.

data.name: History of Italy
data.description: History of Italy covers the historical development of Italy, including its ancient civilizations, medieval states, Renaissance achievements, and modern political and social changes.

subjects.term: Italy, San Marino, Vatican City, Malta

data.name: Analytical Biochemistry
data.description: Analytical biochemistry is the study of biochemical components found in a cell or other biological sample. This scientific discipline uses a broad range of techniques for separation, identification, quantification and functional characterization of biological molecules.

data.name: Comics Studies
data.description: Comics studies is an academic field that focuses on comics & graphic novels, and sequential art.

subjects.term: Comic books, graphic novels, fotonovelas, cartoons, caricatures, comic strips
Comic books, strips, etc.—Influence on mass media

data.name: Environmental Anthropology
data.description: Environmental anthropology is a sub-discipline of anthropology that examines the complex relationships between humans and the environments which they inhabit.

data.name: Biogeosciences
data.description: An interdisciplinary field of study integrating geoscience and biological sciences.

data.name: Sociocultural Anthropology
data.description: Sociocultural anthropology, also known as cultural anthropology, is one of the four main subfields of anthropology. It is the study of human societies, cultures, and social behaviors, focusing on understanding the diversity of human customs, beliefs, practices, and institutions. Some key aspects of sociocultural anthropology: Participant Observation, Ethnographic Research, Cultural Relativism, Cross-Cultural Comparison

data.name: Nuclear Transport
data.description: While nuclear transport of small molecules happens by diffusion, that of macromolecules carrying specific recognition signals happens through nuclear pore complexes. Nuclear transport is regulated by the availability of these signals to the transport machinery, changes in the levels or modifications of the molecules to be transported.

data.name: Security Science and Technology
data.description: Security science and technology refer to the interdisciplinary field that combines scientific principles, theories, and technologies to address security challenges and enhance security measures in various domains. It involves the application of scientific methods, engineering, and technological advancements to develop innovative solutions for preventing, detecting, mitigating, and responding to security threats and risks.

subjects.term: Protection from burglary, sabotage, etc. Security in buildings

data.name: Liberation Theology
data.description: Liberation theology is a Christian theological approach emphasizing the liberation of the oppressed. It engages in socio-economic analyses, with social concern for the poor and political liberation for oppressed peoples and addresses other forms of inequality, such as race or caste.

data.name: Plant Stress Responses
data.description: Plant stress responses describe the suite of molecular and cellular processes that are triggered by the detection by the plant of some form of stress. Stresses can be abiotic, such as drought or excess light, or biotic, such as herbivores or pathogens.

data.name: Evolutionary Theory
data.description: Evolutionary theory is the area that focuses on further development and refinement of the modern synthesis of evolution and genetics. Notable topics include the appropriate level of selection, the relative importance of natural selection and other mechanisms, and the rate of evolution at genotypic and phenotypic levels.

data.name: Logic Design
data.description: Logic design is a field of engineering that focuses on the design and implementation of digital circuits and systems using logic gates and Boolean algebra. It involves the process of transforming a set of specifications or requirements into a logical representation that can be implemented using digital components and technologies.

data.name: Cell Division
data.description: Cell division is the process by which a parental cell gives rise to two daughter cells. The process involves both nuclear division and cytokinesis and can either produce two equal cells (symmetric cell division) or two cells with different cellular fates (asymmetric cell division).

data.name: Cognitive Neuroscience
data.description: Cognitive neuroscience is the field of study focusing on the neural substrates of mental processes. It is at the intersection of psychology and neuroscience, but also overlaps with physiological psychology, cognitive psychology and neuropsychology. It combines the theories of cognitive psychology and computational modelling with experimental data about the brain. Cognitive neuroscience is concerned with the scientific study of biological substrates underlying cognition, with a focus on the neural substrates of mental processes.

data.name: Net Literature
data.description: Net literature, also known as digital literature or electronic literature, refers to literary works created specifically for digital platforms and the internet. It encompasses literary works that are designed to be experienced through digital media and take advantage of the interactive, multimedia, and hypertextual capabilities offered by digital technologies.

data.name: Molecular Modelling
data.description: Molecular modelling encompasses all theoretical methods and computational techniques used to mimic and study the structure and behaviour of molecules, ranging from small chemical systems to large biological molecules and material assemblies.

subjects.term: Models of atoms, molecules, or chemical compounds

data.name: Mathematics in the Humanities and Social Sciences
data.description: In the social sciences, an abstraction from reality is made in the form of a model that can be expressed in mathematical form.

synonyms: Mathematik in den Geisteswissenschaften und Sozialwissenschaften

data.name: Mathematical Modeling and Industrial Mathematics
data.description: Industrial mathematics is a branch of applied mathematics. It focusses on problems which come from industry and aims for solutions which are relevant to industry, including finding the most efficient (i.e., cost-effective) way to solve the problem. A mathematical model is a description of a system using mathematical concepts and language. The process of developing a mathematical model is termed mathematical modeling. Mathematical models are used in the natural sciences and engineering disciplines

data.name: European Economic Integration
data.description: European integration is the process of industrial, economic, political, legal, social, and cultural integration of states wholly or partially in Europe or nearby. European integration has primarily come about through the European Union and its policies.  In practical terms, EMU means: Coordination of economic policy-making between Member States. Coordination of fiscal policies, notably through limits on government debt and deficit. An independent monetary policy run by the European Central Bank (ECB).

data.name: Experimental Psychology
data.description: Experimental psychology is a branch of psychology that focuses on conducting scientific experiments to study and understand human behavior and mental processes. It involves designing and conducting controlled experiments in order to investigate various psychological phenomena, such as perception, memory, learning, cognition, emotion, and motivation. Experimental psychologists use rigorous research methods and statistical analyses to collect and analyze data, which helps them draw conclusions and make inferences about the underlying mechanisms of human behavior. By manipulating independent variables and measuring dependent variables, experimental psychologists aim to establish cause-and-effect relationships and test hypotheses about psychological processes.

data.name: Transplantation
data.description: Transplantation is the procedure of transferring a tissue or organ from one individual to another or from one site to another within a single individual. The transplanted tissue or organ replaces damaged or absent tissue, and is functional in the recipient.

data.name: Christian Theology
data.description: Christian theology is the theology of Christian belief and practice.[1] Such study concentrates primarily upon the texts of the Old Testament and of the New Testament, as well as on Christian tradition. Christian theologians use biblical exegesis, rational analysis and argument.

data.name: Control Structures and Microprogramming
data.description: Control structures are programming constructs that enable the execution of different sections of code based on certain conditions or criteria. They determine the flow and order of program execution and allow for decision-making and repetition. While Microprogramming is a low-level design technique used in computer architecture to implement complex instructions and control the behavior of a processor. It involves breaking down complex instructions into a sequence of microinstructions that can be executed by the processor's control unit.

data.name: Cytological Techniques
data.description: Cytological techniques are methods used in the study or manipulation of cells. These include methods used in cell biology to culture, track, phenotype, sort and screen cells in populations or tissues, and molecular methods to understand cellular function.

data.name: Structure of Condensed Matter
data.description: The structure of condensed matter refers to the arrangement and organization of particles, atoms, or molecules in materials that exist in solid or liquid states. It encompasses the spatial distribution, bonding patterns, and overall arrangement of constituent particles, which determine the properties and behavior of the material.

subjects.term: Condensed matter physics (liquid state & solid state physics)
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Neurochemistry
data.description: Neurochemistry is the study of the identities, structures and functions of compounds (neurochemicals) that are generated by and that modulate the nervous system. Neurochemicals include oxytocin, serotonin, dopamine and other neurotransmitters and neurotransmitter-regulating substances.

data.name: Electrochemistry
data.description: Electrochemistry involves electron-transfer reactions between electrodes and analytes. These electrochemical events are often accompanied by chemical reactions and allow one to study redox and electrocatalytic properties of species.

data.name: Metals and Alloys
data.description: Metals and alloys are materials that are typically hard, malleable, and have good electrical and thermal conductivity. Alloys are made by melting two or more elements together, at least one of them a metal. They have properties that improve those of the constituent elements, such greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Metals & Alloys

data.name: Energy Harvesting
data.description: Energy harvesting (also known as power harvesting or energy scavenging) is the process in which energy is captured from a system's environment and converted into usable electric power. It is the conversion of ambient energy present in the environment into electrical energy for use in powering autonomous electronic devices or circuits.

subjects.term: Generation, modification, storage, transmission of electric power
Energy, power generation, distribution and storage

data.name: Medical Genetics
data.description: Medical genetics involves the application of genetics to medical care, including research on the causes and inheritance of genetic disorders, and their diagnosis and management.

data.name: Nanomedicine and Nanotoxicology
data.description: Nanomedicine is the medical application of nanotechnology it is defined as the development of nanoscale (1–100nm) or nanostructured objects/nano-robots/skin patches and their use in medicine for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes based on the use of their structure, which has unique medical effects.   Nanotoxicology mainly deals with the toxicity of nanomaterials/nanoparticles. The main aim of nanotoxicological studies is to determine the toxic/hazardous effects of nanoparticles and nanopharmaceuticals on humans and environment.

data.name: Control and Systems Theory
data.description: Control and systems theory is a branch of engineering and mathematics that deals with the analysis, design, and control of dynamic systems. It provides a theoretical framework for understanding the behavior of systems, developing models, and designing control strategies to achieve desired system performance.

data.name: Projective Geometry
data.description: Projective geometry is the study of geometric properties that are invariant with respect to projective transformations. Compared to elementary geometry, projective geometry has a different setting, projective space, and a selective set of basic geometric concepts. The basic intuitions are that projective space has more points than Euclidean space, for a given dimension, and that geometric transformations are permitted that transform the extra points (called "points at infinity") to Euclidean points, and vice versa

data.name: Cell Migration
data.description: Cell migration is the process by which cells move from one location to another by adopting different motility modes, such as mesenchymal, amoeboid or collective migration. Cell motility is observed in unicellular organisms, is essential for the development and maintenance of multicellular organisms, and is also involved in immune responses and pathological conditions.

data.name: Cultural Evolution
data.description: Cultural evolution is the change over time of non-biological aspects of human society. The process is loosely analogous to biological evolution, although does not necessarily involve Darwinian natural selection, and includes changes in language, art and social behaviour and norms.

data.name: African-American History
data.description: African-American History is the history of Black Americans

data.name: Rheology
data.description: Rheology is a branch of physics concerned with the study of the flow and change of shape of soft materials, which when deformed usually exhibit a combination of elastic, viscous and plastic behaviour.

data.name: Plant Molecular Biology
data.description: Plant molecular biology is the study of the molecular basis of plant life. It is particularly concerned with the processes by which the information encoded in the genome is manifested as structures, processes and behaviours.

data.name: Neuropharmacology
data.description: Neuropharmacology is the study of how drugs affect cellular function in the nervous system

subjects.term: Drugs acting on the nervous system. Neuropsychopharmacology

data.name: Plant Materials
data.description: Plant Materials means the Seed, and all vegetative and reproductive material from the Seed, including, without limitation, plants and their progeny, stems, leaves, pollen, roots, embryos, pods, seed and any unplanted Seed.

data.name: Inflammation
data.description: Inflammation is a biological response to harmful stimuli, such as pathogens, damaged cells or irradiation. It is a protective attempt by the organism to remove injurious stimuli and to initiate the healing process. It is characterized by pain, redness, heat, swelling and disturbance of function.

data.name: Expression Systems
data.description: Expression systems are genetic constructs (a gene encoded by DNA) that are designed to produce a protein, or an RNA (ribonucleic acid), either inside or outside a cell. Expression systems are used in research and in the commercial production of enzymes or therapeutics.

data.name: Sociology of Education
data.description: The sociology of education is a field of study that examines the social processes, structures, and dynamics within educational institutions and systems. It explores the interactions between education and society, focusing on how education shapes and is shaped by social factors, such as social class, gender, race, ethnicity, and social inequalities.

data.name: Coagulation System
data.description: The coagulation system is composed of cells, proteins and processes that mediate blood clotting. Damage to a blood vessel wall triggers the system, initiating interactions between platelets and blood coagulation factors. This leads to the formation of a fibrin-containing clot, which stops bleeding and initiates vessel repair.

data.name: International Finance
data.description: International finance is a field of study and practice that focuses on the financial interactions between countries and multinational corporations operating across borders. It involves analyzing the flows of money and capital across international borders, assessing the risks associated with those flows, and devising strategies to manage those risks.  Some major topics in international finance include:  Foreign exchange rates, Transfer pricing: The study of foreign exchange rates is an important part of international finance. This involves understanding the factors that influence exchange rates, such as interest rates, inflation, and political events.  International investment: International investment involves analyzing the risks and opportunities associated with investing in foreign countries. This may include examining the political and economic conditions in a given country, as well as evaluating the legal and regulatory environment.  Capital flows: The movement of capital between countries is a crucial part of international finance. This includes analyzing the flows of foreign direct investment (FDI), portfolio investments, and other forms of capital.  International trade finance: International trade finance involves the financing and management of international trade transactions, including the provision of credit, insurance, and other financial services.  International banking: International banking involves analyzing the operations of multinational banks, as well as examining the regulatory and supervisory frameworks that govern these institutions.  Multinational corporations: Multinational corporations (MNCs) play a major role in international finance. Analyzing the financial strategies of MNCs, as well as the risks associated with their operations in different countries, is an important topic in the field.  International financial markets: The study of international financial markets involves examining the operations of stock, bond, and other financial markets in different countries, as well as evaluating the risks and opportunities associated with investing in these markets.

subjects.term: International finance. International monetary system. International banking

data.name: European Literature
data.description: Literature from Europe, encompassing both Western and Eastern European literary traditions. Includes literary works written in European languages and works in translation.

subjects.term: Literature for and by other groups of people--Europe

data.name: Ceramics
data.description: Ceramics are inorganic, nonmetallic materials (such as carbides, oxides and nitrides) made by shaping at a high temperature. Ceramics are hard, brittle, heat- and corrosion-resistant, and most often have a crystalline structure.

data.name: Thesis and Dissertation
data.description: A thesis, or dissertation is a document submitted in support of candidature for an academic degree or professional qualification presenting the author's research and findings. In some contexts, the word thesis or a cognate is used for part of a bachelor's or master's course, while dissertation is normally applied to a doctorate.

data.name: Research Methods in Criminology
data.description: Research Methods in Criminology involve the techniques and methodologies used to study crime, criminal behavior, and the criminal justice system, including qualitative and quantitative approaches.

data.name: Functional Analysis
data.description: Functional analysis is a branch of mathematical analysis, the core of which is formed by the study of vector spaces endowed with some kind of limit-related structure (e.g. inner product, norm, topology, etc.) and the linear functions defined on these spaces and respecting these structures in a suitable sense.

data.name: Evolutionary Anthropology
data.description: Evolutionary Anthropology is a subfield of anthropology that combines principles from evolutionary biology with the study of human biology, behavior, and culture. It focuses on understanding human evolution and the evolutionary processes that have shaped human traits and behaviors over time. Evolutionary anthropologists use a multidisciplinary approach, integrating data from genetics, paleontology, archaeology, primatology, and other fields to piece together the evolutionary history of our species.

data.name: Environmental Process Engineering
data.description: Environmental process engineering, also known as environmental technology or environmental systems engineering, refers to the application of engineering principles and technologies to address environmental challenges and develop sustainable solutions. It involves the design, implementation, and optimization of processes and systems to manage and mitigate environmental issues, such as pollution control, waste treatment, water and air quality management, and sustainable resource utilization.

data.name: Nutrition
data.description: Nutrition or Dietetics is the organic process of nourishing or being nourished, including the processes by which an organism assimilates food and uses it for growth and maintenance.

data.name: Plant Development
data.description: Plant development is the process by which structures originate and mature as a plant grows. Plants produce new tissues and structures throughout their life from clusters of undifferentiated cells called meristems.

data.name: Economics of Innovation
data.description: Innovation economics is new, and growing field of economic theory and applied/experimental economics that emphasizes innovation and entrepreneurship.

data.name: Cancer Therapy
data.description: Cancer therapy describes the treatment of cancer in a patient, often with surgery, chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy. Targeted therapies are also available for some cancer types. A cancer patient might receive many different types of therapy, including those aimed at relieving the symptoms of cancer, such as pain.

data.name: Environmental Psychology
data.description: Environmental psychology is a branch of psychology that studies the interactions between individuals and their physical and social environments. It examines how the environment affects human behavior, emotions, and well-being, and how individuals perceive, understand, and respond to their surroundings.

data.name: Environmental Social Sciences
data.description: Environmental social science is the application of social science – broadly the study of the relationship between individuals in their context within society – and its application to our understanding of environmental issues.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Environmental Science (see also Chemistry / Environmental)
Philosophy. Relation to other topics. Methodology

data.name: Political Sociology
data.description: Political sociology is the study of power and the relationship between societies, states, and political conflict. It is a broad subfield that straddles political science and sociology, with “macro” and “micro” components.

data.name: Political and Economic Anthropology
data.description: The study of political and economic systems within societies. It examines how political institutions, power dynamics, and economic activities shape social life, organization, and cultural practices. Political and economic anthropologists often conduct ethnographic research to understand the complexities of governance, decision-making processes, resource distribution, trade, and economic exchange in different cultural contexts.

data.name: Crime and Society
data.description: The subfield of crime and society within criminology examines the complex relationship between crime and various social factors, including cultural, economic, political, and demographic influences. It focuses on understanding how crime is shaped by social structures, norms, and inequalities, and how crime, in turn, impacts society. This subfield delves into the social causes and consequences of crime, as well as the social responses to crime, including policies, interventions, and social control mechanisms.

data.name: Quantum Chemistry
data.description: Quantum chemistry applies quantum mechanics to the theoretical study of chemical systems. It aims, in principle, to solve the Schrödinger equation for the system under scrutiny; however, its complexity for all but the simplest of atoms or molecules requires simplifying assumptions and approximations, creating a trade-off between accuracy and computational cost.

data.name: Hydrogen Energy
data.description: Hydrogen energy is a secondary energy source, which can be produced in a variety of ways with little resource restrictions.

data.name: Engineering and Technology Education
data.description: Engineering education is the activity of teaching knowledge and principles to the professional practice of engineering. It includes an initial education (bachelor's and/or master's degree), and any advanced education and specializations that follow. Engineering education is typically accompanied by additional postgraduate examinations and supervised training as the requirements for a professional engineering license. The length of education, and training to qualify as a basic professional engineer, is typically 5 years, with 15–20 years for an engineer who takes responsibility for major projects.  Technology education is the study of technology, in which students "learn about the processes and knowledge related to technology". As a field of study, it covers the human's ability to shape and change the physical world to meet needs, by manipulating materials and tools with techniques. It addresses the disconnect between wide usage and the lack of knowledge about technical components of technologies used and how to fix them.

data.name: Neuroanatomy
data.description: Neuroanatomy is the study of the anatomy of nervous tissue and neural structures of the nervous system

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Life Sciences / Anatomy & Physiology (see also Life Sciences / Human Anatomy & Physiology)

data.name: Development Studies
data.description: Development studies is an interdisciplinary field of study that examines the economic, social, and political processes involved in the transformation of societies and the improvement of human well-being. It explores theories, policies, and practices related to poverty reduction, sustainable development, inequality, governance, and the role of institutions in fostering inclusive and equitable growth.

subjects.term: Economic development. Development economics. Economic growth

data.name: Urban Sociology
data.description: Urban sociology is the sociological study of cities and urban life. One of the field’s oldest sub-disciplines, urban sociology studies and examines the social, historical, political, cultural, economic, and environmental forces that have shaped urban environments.

data.name: Cancer Microenvironment
data.description: The cancer microenvironment, or tumour microenvironment, describes the non-cancerous cells present in the tumour. These include fibroblasts, immune cells and cells that comprise the blood vessels. It also includes the proteins produced by all of the cells present in the tumour that support the growth of the cancer cells.

data.name: Semiconductors
data.description: Semiconductors are materials that have a small electronic bandgap. This bandgap prevents current from flowing at absolute zero, but thermally excited charge carriers can begin to flow at higher temperatures. Semiconductors, notably silicon, are at the heart of the modern microelectronics industry, and also have applications in light sources and detectors.

data.name: Oral Anatomy
data.description: Oral Anatomy is the branch of anatomy that focuses on the structure and organization of the oral cavity, including the teeth, gums, tongue, palate, and associated structures such as the salivary glands and the temporomandibular joint. It encompasses the study of the morphology, histology, and functional aspects of these components, providing insights into their roles in processes such as mastication, speech, and digestion. Understanding oral anatomy is essential for various fields, including dentistry, orthodontics, and oral surgery, as it aids in diagnosing and treating conditions related to the mouth and surrounding areas.

data.name: Geotechnical Engineering
data.description: Geotechnical engineering is an area of civil engineering that focuses on the engineering behaviour of earth materials. Using the principles of soil and rock mechanics, it applies knowledge from geology, geophysics, hydrology, and related fields. Typical projects include embankments, tunnels, levees, wharves, landfills, and other structures that are built in or supported by soil and rock.

data.name: Business IT Infrastructure
data.description: Business IT infrastructure refers to the set of hardware, software, and networking components that support the flow of information within and between organizations. It is a critical component of modern business operations, as it enables organizations to efficiently store, process, and share data, and to communicate with customers, partners, and suppliers. As a field of business and management research and practice, business IT infrastructure encompasses a wide range of topics, including: IT strategy and planning: This involves developing a comprehensive IT strategy and aligning it with the organization's overall business goals and objectives.  Network design and management: This involves designing and managing the organization's computer networks, including local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANs), and virtual private networks (VPNs). Data storage and management: This involves managing the organization's data storage systems, including databases, data warehouses, and data centers. Security and privacy: This involves implementing measures to protect the organization's information assets from unauthorized access, theft, or loss, as well as ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations. Cloud computing: This involves leveraging cloud-based services to reduce IT costs, improve scalability and agility, and enhance collaboration and data sharing. IT governance and compliance: This involves establishing policies and procedures to ensure that IT resources are used in a responsible and ethical manner and comply with relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards. Emerging technologies: This involves monitoring and evaluating new and emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and the Internet of Things (IoT), to identify opportunities for innovation and competitive advantage.

data.name: Cancer Staging

For example, the TNM classification of malignant tumours is a staging system used for describing the size of the primary tumour (T), if regional lymphnodes are involved (N) and the presence of metastasis (M).

Synthesis can also include functionalization by conjugation to bioactive molecules.

data.name: Knowledge Management
data.description: Knowledge Management (KM) is the practice of capturing, creating, sharing, and utilizing knowledge within an organization to achieve its goals and objectives. It is an interdisciplinary field of management research that combines aspects of information technology, organizational theory, psychology, and sociology to develop strategies and tools for managing knowledge effectively.  KM involves the identification, acquisition, creation, distribution, and use of knowledge, as well as the processes and technologies that support these activities. The ultimate goal of KM is to enable an organization to leverage its knowledge assets to improve performance, innovation, and competitiveness.  Some key aspects of KM include knowledge creation, knowledge sharing, and knowledge retention. These activities require a culture that promotes knowledge sharing and collaboration, as well as the use of information technologies that support the management of knowledge.  Overall, KM is a critical field of management research because it enables organizations to leverage their knowledge assets to create value, innovate, and remain competitive in a rapidly changing business environment.

data.name: Measure and Integration
data.description: Measure Theory is the study of measures. Measure on a set is a systematic way to assign a number to each suitable subset of that set, intuitively interpreted as its size. In this sense, a measure is a generalization of the concepts of length, area, and volume. Measure theory was developed during the late 19th and early 20th centuries by Émile Borel, Henri Lebesgue, Johann Radon, and Maurice Fréchet, among others. The main applications of measures are in the foundations of the Lebesgue integral, in Andrey Kolmogorov's axiomatisation of probability theory and in ergodic theory. In integration theory, specifying a measure allows one to define integrals on spaces more general than subsets of Euclidean space

data.name: Start-Ups and Venture Capital
data.description: Start-up, venture capital, and business angel are related terms in the field of entrepreneurship, which involves starting and growing new businesses.  Start-up refers to a newly founded business enterprise that is typically characterized by a high degree of innovation, uncertainty, and risk. Start-ups are often founded by entrepreneurs who have a novel business idea or technology and seek to commercialize it. As a field of research, start-up studies focus on the process of starting and growing new businesses, including issues such as opportunity identification, business planning, funding, team building, and scaling.  Venture capital (VC) is a form of private equity financing that provides funding to start-ups and early-stage companies that have high growth potential. VC investors provide funding to start-ups in exchange for an ownership stake in the company, and they typically take an active role in managing the company's growth and development. As a field of research, venture capital studies focus on the investment process, including issues such as investment criteria, portfolio management, and exit strategies.  Business angel (also known as angel investor) is an individual investor who provides funding to start-ups in exchange for an ownership stake in the company. Business angels are typically high net worth individuals who have industry expertise and are willing to take a high degree of risk in exchange for potentially high returns. As a field of research, business angel studies focus on the characteristics and behaviors of angel investors, as well as the impact of business angel funding on start-up success.  Overall, start-up, venture capital, and business angel are important fields of research and practice in the entrepreneurship ecosystem, as they support the development and growth of new businesses, drive innovation, and contribute to economic development.

data.name: Public Choice and Political Economy
