data.name: Plant Genetics
data.description: Plant genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity specifically in Plants. Plant genetics deals with heredity in plants, specifically mechanisms of hereditary transmission and variation of inherited characteristics. Plant genetics differs from animal genetics in a number of ways: somatic mutations can contribute to the germ line more easily as flowers develop at the end of branches composed of somatic cells; polyploidy is more common; and plants additionally contain chloroplastic DNA.

data.name: Australasian Film and TV
data.description: The study of film and television from Australia and New Zealand

data.name: Mechatronics
data.description: A multidisciplinary field of engineering that includes a combination of mechanical engineering, robotics, electronics, computer engineering, telecommunications engineering, systems engineering and control engineering

data.name: Robotics
data.description: Design of robots and the respective control systems, engineering, programming and teaching-in. study, design, and development of robots and autonomous systems. Robots are machines or mechanical devices that can perform tasks autonomously or semi-autonomously, either by following pre-programmed instructions or through artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms.

subjects.term: Mechanical devices and figures. Automata. Ingenious mechanisms. Robots (General)

data.name: Cultural Psychology
data.description: Cultural psychology is a field of psychology that focuses on how cultural factors shape and influence individual and collective psychological processes. It examines the ways in which culture, including shared beliefs, values, practices, and symbols, influence human cognition, emotion, perception, and behavior.

data.name: Innate Immunity
data.description: Innate immunity is an immunological subsystem that comprises the cells and mechanisms that provide the first line of defence from infection in a non-specific manner. Innate immune responses are rapid and independent of antigen. Innate immune systems are found in all classes of plants and animals.

data.name: Biomimetic Synthesis
data.description: Biomimetic synthesis is a branch of natural product synthesis that aims to synthesize a target molecule through a series of reactions, and passing through intermediate structures, that are closely related to those that occur during biosynthesis in its natural source.

data.name: Symbolic AI
data.description: In symbolic AI (Artificial Intelligence) knowledge is represented in the form of human-readable symbols and rules, and reasoning and problem-solving is performed by manipulating these using logical inference and search. Applications include knowledge-based systems such as expert systems, planning systems, ontologies, and intelligent tutoring systems (ITS).

data.name: Oriental or Semitic Languages
data.description: Oriental Languages are a group of languages primarily spoken in East Asia. This category includes languages such as Chinese (Mandarin, Cantonese, etc.), Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai, Burmese, and many others. These languages are linguistically diverse and have distinct grammatical structures, writing systems, and phonetic features. Semitic languages are a branch of the Afro-Asiatic language family and are primarily spoken in the Middle East and parts of North Africa. languages include Arabic (the most widely spoken Semitic language), Hebrew, Amharic (spoken in Ethiopia), Aramaic, and others.

synonyms: Sprachen des Nahen Ostens und Semitische Sprachen

data.name: Oncology
data.description: Oncology is the branch of medicine that deals with the diagnosis and treatment of cancer. It includes medical oncology (the use of chemotherapy, hormone therapy, and other drugs to treat cancer), radiation oncology (the use of radiation therapy to treat cancer), and surgical oncology (the use of surgery and other procedures to treat cancer).

data.name: DNA Recombination
data.description: DNA recombination is the exchange of DNA strands to produce new nucleotide sequence arrangements. Recombination occurs typically, though not exclusively, between regions of similar sequence by breaking and rejoining DNA segments, and is essential for generating genetic diversity and for maintaining genome integrity.

data.name: Environmental Biotechnology
data.description: Environmental biotechnology is the branch of biotechnology that addresses environmental problems, such as the removal of pollution, renewable energy generation or biomass production, by exploiting biological processes.

data.name: Global Analysis and Analysis on Manifolds
data.description: In mathematics, global analysis, also called analysis on manifolds, is the study of the global and topological properties of differential equations on manifolds and vector bundles. It uses techniques in infinite-dimensional manifold theory and topological spaces of mappings to classify behaviors of differential equations, particularly nonlinear differential equations. These spaces can include singularities and hence catastrophe theory is a part of global analysis. Optimization problems, such as finding geodesics on Riemannian manifolds, can be solved using differential equations so that the calculus of variations overlaps with global analysis.

synonyms: Globale Analysis und Analysis auf Mannigfaltigkeiten

data.name: Surface Chemistry
data.description: Surface chemistry is the study of chemical reactions at surfaces and interfaces. Appreciating how molecules and atoms interact with surfaces and with each other while on surfaces is key to understanding desirable chemical reactions, such as in heterogeneous catalysis, and also those that are undesirable, such as in corrosion chemistry.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Thin Films, Surfaces & Interfaces

data.name: Technology Commercialization
data.description: Technology commercialization is a field within business and management research and practice that focuses on the process of bringing new technological innovations to the market. It involves the transformation of technological inventions into marketable products or services. Core topics within technology commercialization include: Intellectual property protection: This involves protecting the legal rights of the inventor or organization that owns the technology. Market analysis: This involves analyzing the market potential for the new technology and identifying potential customers and competitors. Business models: This involves identifying the most effective business models for commercializing the technology, such as licensing or direct sales. Funding and financing: This involves identifying and securing funding and financing for the commercialization process, including venture capital, grants, and loans. Product development: This involves developing and testing prototypes of the new technology, refining its features, and ensuring that it meets the needs of the market. Marketing and sales: This involves developing a marketing strategy for the new technology and identifying the most effective sales channels. Entrepreneurship and innovation: This involves understanding the entrepreneurial and innovative aspects of the commercialization process, including the role of entrepreneurship in driving technological innovation and the importance of creating a culture of innovation within organizations.

data.name: Critical Criminology
data.description: Critical criminology is a subfield within the broader field of criminology that adopts a critical perspective to examine crime, law, and the criminal justice system. It emerged in the 1960s as a response to traditional criminological approaches that were seen as overly focused on individual pathology and social control. Critical criminologists aim to understand the structural and systemic factors that contribute to crime and deviance, emphasizing the importance of power, inequality, and social justice in shaping criminal behavior and responses to it.

data.name: Social Choice and Welfare
data.description: Social Choice and Welfare studies the methods and principles for aggregating individual preferences and making collective decisions, focusing on issues of fairness, efficiency, and social welfare.

data.name: Forensic Science
data.description: Forensic science is a branch of science that encompasses the application of scientific principles and techniques to investigate crime scenes, analyze evidence, and aid in the resolution of legal matters. It involves the collection, preservation, examination, and interpretation of physical and biological evidence using various scientific disciplines.

subjects.term: Forensic medicine. Medical jurisprudence. Legal medicine

data.name: Writing Skills
data.description: Writing Skills is the study and practice of effective written communication across various formats and contexts, such as academic, professional, and creative writing. This field emphasizes the development of skills in grammar, syntax, organization, style, and argumentation, as well as the ability to critically reflect on one's own writing and the writing of others.

data.name: Web Development
data.description: Web development is the work involved in developing a website for the Internet (World Wide Web) or an intranet (a private network).[1] Web development can range from developing a simple single static page of plain text to complex web applications, electronic businesses, and social network services. A more comprehensive list of tasks to which Web development commonly refers, may include Web engineering, Web design, Web content development, client liaison, client-side/server-side scripting, Web server and network security configuration, and e-commerce development.

data.name: Latin American Film and TV
data.description: The study of the historical and cultural contexts of film and television practices in Latin America, as well as Latin American film and television texts themselves.

data.name: Human Rights Policy
data.description:
Politics and human rights is a subdiscipline that examines how human rights impacts  politics and also studies the role of human rights in relation to the politics of different regions of the world.

Human rights are rights inherent to all human beings, regardless of race, sex, nationality, ethnicity, language, religion, or any other status. Human rights include the right to life and liberty, freedom from slavery and torture, freedom of opinion and expression, the right to work and education, and many more.  

International human rights law lays down the obligations of Governments to act in certain ways or to refrain from certain acts, in order to promote and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms of individuals or groups. International human rights law is the primary framework for specifying exact human rights obligations, especially for State Parties. There is increasing focus on the growing number of responsibilities accruing to non-state actors, particularly private actors.

subjects.term: State and the individual. Human rights. Civil rights

data.name: National and Regional Theatre and Performance
data.description: A regional theater or resident theater in the United States is a professional or semi-professional theater company that produces its own seasons. Forms of theatrical performances Publicistic performance. This stage form is the successor to the action of the once well-known agitribyad. Plastic Choreographic Performance. Dramatic play.  Humorous performance.  Interactive performance.  Performing a forum-theatre. Theatre or theater is a collaborative form of performing art that uses live performers, usually actors or actresses, to present the experience of a real or imagined event before a live audience in a specific place, often a stage.

data.name: Carbon Materials
data.description: Carbon materials are substances that either wholly or primarily are made up of carbon. These materials might be the element's allotropes like graphites, graphenes, fullerenes and diamonds. Alternatively, carbon-rich compounds like polyaromatic hydrocarbons, graphite/graphene oxides and doped diamonds are also considered carbon materials.

subjects.term: Solids. Solid state chemistry (Inorganic and organic)

data.name: Emergency Medicine
data.description: Emergency medicine, also known as accident and emergency medicine, is the medical specialty concerned with the care of illnesses or injuries requiring immediate medical attention.  Emergency physicians’ primary responsibility is to initiate resuscitation and stabilization and to start investigations and interventions to diagnose and treat illnesses in the acute phase; they generally practise in hospital emergency departments, pre-hospital settings via emergency medical services, and intensive care units, but may also work in primary care settings such as urgent care clinics. Sub-specializations of emergency medicine include disaster medicine, medical toxicology, ultrasonography, critical care medicine, hyperbaric medicine, sports medicine, palliative care, or aerospace medicine.

data.name: Cavity QED
data.description: Cavity QED is the study of the interaction between light confined in a reflective cavity and atoms or other particles, under conditions where the quantum nature of light photons is significant.

subjects.term: Quantum physics (quantum mechanics & quantum field theory)
Quantum physics (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory)

data.name: Deconstruction
data.description: Deconstruction doesn't actually mean "demolition;" instead it means "breaking down" or analyzing something (especially the words in a work of fiction or nonfiction) to discover its true significance, which is supposedly almost never exactly what the author intended.

data.name: Physical Geography
data.description: Physical geography is the branch of natural science which deals with the study of processes and patterns in the natural environment such as the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere.

data.name: Moral Psychology
data.description: Moral psychology is a field of study that combines insights from psychology and philosophy to investigate moral development, moral judgment, moral emotions, and moral decision-making. It explores the psychological processes and factors that shape moral beliefs, values, and behavior. Moral psychology seeks to understand how individuals form moral judgments, how moral reasoning occurs, and how moral values are internalized and applied in real-life situations.

data.name: Health Informatics
data.description: Health informatics  is a multidisciplinary field that uses health information technology in delivery, management and planning  of health care services. It deals with the resources, devices, and methods required to optimize the acquisition, storage, retrieval, and use of information in health and bio-medicine.

subjects.term: Computer applications to medicine. Medical informatics. Medical information technology
Computer applications in industry and technology

data.name: Space Physics
data.description: Space physics is the study of the natural phenomenon that occur in our solar system. Specifically, the sun, the particles and radiation it creates and how these affect the planets. This includes the solar wind and its interaction with the Earth and near-Earth space; so-called space weather.

subjects.term: Solar system: the Sun and planets

data.name: Epidemiology
data.description: Epidemiology is a field of medicine that studies the incidence, causes and effects of diseases in populations, and patterns within these. It has a key role in protecting public health and can provide valuable information for developing new medicines, such as revealing risk factors for a particular disease.

data.name: Audio-Visual Culture
data.description: Audio-visual culture means the practices, technologies, and social meanings through which societies produce, circulate, and interpret combined sound‑and‑image media.

data.name: Computational Science and Engineering
data.description: Computational science and engineering (CSE) deals with the development and application of computational models and simulations, often coupled with high-performance computing, to solve complex physical problems arising in engineering analysis and design (computational engineering) as well as natural phenomena (computational science).

subjects.term: Instruments and machines (Including practical mathematics, graphical and numerical calculating)

data.name: Electronic Devices
data.description: Electronic devices are components for controlling the flow of electrical currents for the purpose of information processing and system control. Prominent examples include transistors and diodes. Electronic devices are usually small and can be grouped together into packages called integrated circuits. This miniaturization is central to the modern electronics boom.

subjects.term: Condensed matter physics (liquid state & solid state physics)
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Tumour Biomarkers
data.description: Tumour biomarkers is a term used to describe many different potential markers of cancer development and progression. These markers can come in many forms – for example, proteins, biochemicals, DNA and RNA – and ideally they should be specific to a particular type of cancer and not present in normal tissues or in healthy individuals.

data.name: Lymphocytes
data.description: Lymphocytes are white blood cells that have important immune functions. The main populations of lymphocytes are B cells, T cells and natural killer (NK) cells. They are typically (although not exclusively) associated with adaptive immune responses. Populations of novel innate-like lymphocytes were first described in 2010.

data.name: History of Modern Europe
data.description: History of Modern Europe studies the period from the late 18th century to the present, including significant events such as the Industrial Revolution, world wars, and the European Union's formation.

subjects.term: Modern history to 20th century: c 1700 to c 1900

data.name: Non-coding RNAs
data.description: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules that are not translated into protein products. Different classes of non-coding RNAs participate in different cellular processes; for example, gene expression regulation (miRNAs, piRNAs, lncRNAs), RNA maturation (snRNAs, snoRNAs) and protein synthesis (rRNAs, tRNAs).

data.name: Metabolism
data.description: Metabolism refers to the chemical reactions that occur within an organism to sustain life. The reactions are divided into two categories: catabolism (the breakdown of organic matter to produce energy); and anabolism (the construction of molecules from smaller units).

data.name: Jewish Cultural Studies
data.description: Jewish Cultural Studies refers to the study of Judaism and the Jewish people through the cultural norms of Jews.

data.name: Management Education
data.description: Management education refers to the study of how to educate and develop effective managers, leaders, and executives. It is a subfield of management research that focuses on identifying best practices in teaching, learning, and curriculum design for management students. Major topics in management education include: Curriculum design and development: This involves designing and developing courses and programs that equip students with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed in their careers as managers and leaders. Teaching and learning methods: This includes identifying and evaluating different teaching and learning methods, such as case studies, experiential learning, simulations, and online learning, and determining which methods are most effective for different types of students and learning objectives. Assessment and evaluation: This involves developing and implementing effective methods for assessing student learning and evaluating the effectiveness of management education programs. Faculty development: This includes identifying and providing training and support for faculty members to ensure they have the skills and knowledge needed to deliver effective management education. Diversity and inclusion: This involves promoting diversity and inclusion in management education by ensuring that courses and programs are designed to address the needs of students from diverse backgrounds and by promoting diversity among faculty and staff. Ethics and corporate social responsibility: This includes developing courses and programs that address ethical issues and promote corporate social responsibility in management education.  Internationalization: This involves preparing students to work in a globalized world by incorporating international perspectives into management education and providing opportunities for students to study and work abroad. Career development: This includes providing students with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed in their careers as managers and leaders, including networking, job search strategies, and career planning.

data.name: Bioorganic Chemistry
data.description: Bioorganic chemistry is a field of study that combines principles from both biology and organic chemistry to investigate and understand the chemical processes and structures of biological systems. It focuses on the study of organic compounds and their interactions with biological molecules, such as proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.

data.name: Engine Technology
data.description: An engine is a machine designed to convert one form of energy into mechanical energy, in particular to propel vehicles.

data.name: Automotive Engineering
data.description: Design, manufacture and operation of motorcycles, automobiles, and trucks and their respective engineering subsystems

data.name: Non-Fiction Literature
data.description: Non-fiction (or nonfiction) is any document or media content that attempts, in good faith, to convey information only about the real world, rather than being grounded in imagination. Non-fiction typically aims to present topics objectively based on historical, scientific, and empirical information. However, some non-fiction ranges into more subjective territory, including sincerely held opinions on real-world topics.

subjects.term: Rhetoric and collections of literary texts from more than two literatures

data.name: Gynecology
data.description: Is the branch of medicine that deals with the diseases and routine physical care of the reproductive system of women

data.name: Societal Outreach of Biology
data.description: the efforts and activities within the field of biology that aim to engage with the general public, address societal issues, and communicate the relevance and implications of biological research to the broader community. It involves reaching out to non-scientific audiences, such as students, policymakers, the media, and the general public, to promote understanding, awareness, and ethical considerations related to biology.

data.name: Information Ethics
data.description: Information ethics is the ethics of how information is created, accessed, used, and controlled in society, including issues like privacy, digital divide, intellectual property, and information rights. It involves the analysis and evaluation of the ethical considerations associated with information technologies and the impact of information on individuals and society.

data.name: Tribology
data.description: Tribology is the science and engineering of interacting surfaces in relative motion. It includes the study and application of the principles of friction, lubrication, and wear.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Thin Films, Surfaces & Interfaces

data.name: Structuralism
data.description: It seeks to understand phenomena by analyzing their underlying structures and systems of relationships, emphasizing the importance of organizing principles and structures in shaping human experiences and behaviors. Some key aspects and principles associated with structuralism Structural Analysis, Binary Oppositions, Language and Sign Systems, Saussurean Linguistics.

data.name: Philosophy of Management
data.description: Philosophy of Management is the study of the fundamental principles, values, and ethical considerations that inform and guide managerial decision-making and organizational behavior. This field explores topics such as leadership, accountability, motivation, corporate social responsibility, and the nature of organizations, with an emphasis on critical reflection and practical application.

subjects.term: Theory. Method. Relation to other subjects

data.name: Plant Cell Biology
data.description: Plant cell biology is the study of all aspects of plant cells. It is particularly concerned with structure, growth, division, signalling, differentiation and death of plant cells.

data.name: Ecological Epidemiology
data.description: Ecological epidemiology is the study of the ecology of infectious diseases. It includes population and community level studies of the interactions between hosts and their pathogens and parasites, and covers diseases of both humans and wildlife.

subjects.term: Incidence of and public measures to prevent disease

data.name: Plant Tropism
data.description: Tropism is the directional growth of an organism, typically a plant, in response an external stimulus, such as light or gravity. Growth towards the stimulus is referred to as positive tropism, and away from the stimulus as negative tropism.

data.name: Synthetic Biology
data.description: Synthetic biology is the design and construction of new biological parts, devices, and systems, and the re-design of existing, natural biological systems for useful purposes.

subjects.term: Methods of research. Technique. Experimental biology

data.name: Classical and Quantum Gravity
data.description: Classical Gravity refers to the theories of gravity obtained without the process of quantisation, namely the theory of General Relativity, extension of the Newtonian Gravity. Quantum Gravity is the field of theoretical physics that attempts to describe the gravitational field according to the principles of quantum mechanics.

subjects.term: Theories of gravitation (Including antigravity, quantum gravity)

data.name: Anthropology of the Arts
data.description: Anthropology of art is a sub-field in social anthropology dedicated to the study of art in different cultural contexts. The anthropology of art focuses on historical, economic and aesthetic dimensions in non-Western art forms, including what is known as 'tribal art'

data.name: Environmental Health
data.description: Environmental health studies public health concerned with all aspects of the natural and built environment affecting human health.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Environmental Science (see also Chemistry / Environmental)

data.name: Anesthesiology
data.description: Anesthesiology is the medical speciality concerned with the total perioperative care of patients before, during and after surgery. It encompasses anesthesia, intensive care medicine, critical emergency medicine, and pain medicine.

data.name: Sports Medicine
data.description: Sports Medicine is a subfield of medicine dealing with physical fitness and the treatment and prevention of injuries in sports and exercise. Although its origins lie in the clinical treatment of athletes, Sports Medicine traditionally also encompasses matters of performance physiology and methods of training control.

data.name: Leisure Studies
data.description: Leisure studies is a branch of the social sciences that focuses on understanding and analyzing leisure.

data.name: Computer Memory Structure
data.description: The memory structure of a computer refers to those hardware elements that store the data elements and the related information during program execution

data.name: Concrete
data.description: Concrete is a versatile construction material widely used in building and infrastructure projects. It is a composite material composed of cement, aggregates (such as sand and gravel or crushed stone), and water.

data.name: Meta-Ethics
data.description: Metaethics is a branch of analytic philosophy that explores the status, foundations, and scope of moral values, properties, and words.

data.name: Financial History
data.description: Financial History studies the development of financial systems, institutions, and markets over time, including the evolution of banking, investment, and monetary policies.

data.name: Mathematical Statistics
data.description: Mathematical statistics is the application of probability theory, a branch of mathematics, to statistics, as opposed to techniques for collecting statistical data. Specific mathematical techniques which are used for this include mathematical analysis, linear algebra, stochastic analysis, differential equations, and measure theory

data.name: Pollution
data.description: Pollution is the introduction of harmful materials into the environment (air, water, soil). It can be naturally caused, e.g. through volcanic ash. Pollution can also be created by human activity, such as trash or runoff produced by factories.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Environmental Science (see also Chemistry / Environmental)
Pollution and threats to the environment

data.name: Bioanalysis and Bioimaging
data.description: Bioanalysis and bioimaging are two important fields within the broader field of biomedical research and healthcare. Both disciplines involve the study and visualization of biological samples and processes, but they have distinct focuses and methodologies. Bioanalysis refers to the quantitative measurement and analysis of biological samples to determine the presence, concentration, and behavior of specific molecules. Bioimaging involves the visualization and mapping of biological structures, processes, and functions at various scales, ranging from cellular to whole-body levels.

data.name: Transnational Crime
data.description: Transnational crime refers to criminal activities that transcend national boundaries and involve multiple countries. These crimes often exploit gaps in legal systems, utilize advanced technology, and take advantage of global networks to carry out illegal operations. Examples of transnational crime include human trafficking, drug smuggling, arms trafficking, cybercrime, money laundering, and terrorism.

data.name: Prison and Punishment
data.description: Prison and punishment is a subfield within criminology that focuses on the study of correctional systems, incarceration, and the various methods used by societies to respond to and punish individuals who have been convicted of crimes. It involves examining the theoretical foundations, historical development, and practical implementation of imprisonment and other forms of punishment.

data.name: Common Company Law
data.description: In Common Company Law, whilst a shareholder is often colloquially referred to as the owner of the company - it is clear that the shareholder is not an owner of the company but makes the shareholder a member of the company and entitles them to enforce the provisions of the company's constitution against the company and against other members.

data.name: Urology
data.description: Urology is a part of health care that deals with diseases of the male and female urinary tract (kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra). It also deals with the male organs that are able to make babies (penis, testes, scrotum, prostate, etc.).

subjects.term: Diseases of the genitourinary system. Urology

data.name: Soil Science
data.description: Study of soil as a natural resource on the surface of the Earth including soil formation, classification and mapping; physical, chemical, biological, and fertility properties of soils; and these properties in relation to the use and management of soils

data.name: Metastasis
data.description: Metastasis is the spread of cancer to a part of the body distant from the original primary cancer. This occurs through the transfer of malignant or cancerous cells via lymph or blood. The new occurrences of cancer are called metastases.

data.name: Cardiology
data.description: Cardiology is a medical specialty that is concerned with the structure and function of the heart and vasculature, and the diagnosis and treatment of patients with cardiovascular diseases.

data.name: Media Sociology
data.description: The study of mass media, communication technologies, and their role in shaping and influencing society. It examines how media institutions, content, and communication processes interact with social structures, cultural norms, and individual behaviors. Media sociology explores a wide range of topics, including media effects, media consumption patterns, media representation, media production, media ownership, and the broader social implications of media technologies.

data.name: Mathematical Applications in Computer Science
data.description: Mathematical applications are fundamental to computer science, providing the theoretical foundation and practical tools necessary for various aspects of the discipline such as Algorithms and Data Structures, Cryptography, Logic and Formal Methods.

data.name: Astrochemistry
data.description: Astrochemistry is the study of the abundance and reactions of molecules in the Universe, and their interaction with radiation.

data.name: Protein Synthesis and Translation
data.description: Translation is the process by which a protein is synthesized by the ribosome, using a messenger RNA (mRNA) template.

data.name: Capital Markets
data.description: A capital market is a financial market in which long-term debt (over a year) or equity-backed securities are bought and sold, in contrast to a money market where short-term debt is bought and sold. Capital markets channel the wealth of savers to those who can put it to long-term productive use, such as companies or governments making long-term investments.

data.name: Economic Sociology
data.description: Economic sociology is a subfield of sociology that examines the social foundations and consequences of economic activities, institutions and systems, often exploring issues such as capitalism, markets, globalization, and the role of culture in economic behavior.

data.name: Geographical Information System
data.description: A Geographic Information System (GIS) is a system designed to capture, store, manipulate, analyze, manage, and present spatial or geographic data. GIS applications are tools that allow users to create interactive queries (user-created searches), analyze spatial information, edit data in maps, and present the results of all these operations.

subjects.term: Geographical information systems and remote sensing

data.name: Statistics in Business, Management, Economics, Finance, Insurance
data.description: Statistics in Business, Management, Economics, Finance, Insurance involves the application of statistical methods to analyze data and inform decision-making in these fields, including risk assessment, market analysis, and performance evaluation.

data.name: Superheavy Elements
data.description: Superheavy elements (SHEs) are elements that have an atomic number greater than that of naturally occurring elements. They are extremely heavy, with atomic numbers typically exceeding 104. These elements are highly unstable and usually exist for only a fraction of a second before decaying into lighter elements through radioactive decay

data.name: Sociolinguistics
data.description: It examines the relationship between language and society. It explores how language varies and changes within social groups, communities, and different cultural contexts. Sociolinguistics investigates the social, cultural, and political factors that influence language use, attitudes, and variation.

data.name: Islamic Studies
data.description: Islamic Studies is the academic study of Islam as a religion, a historical tradition, and a set of intellectual and legal systems. It focuses on foundational texts, theology, law, and the historical development of Muslim societies.

data.name: Sociology of Knowledge and Discourse
data.description: Sociology of knowledge and discourse explores the relationship between social structures, power dynamics, and the production and circulation of knowledge. It investigates how knowledge is shaped by and shapes social institutions, norms, and practices.

subjects.term: Epistemology and sociology. Sociology of knowledge

data.name: Speciation
data.description: Speciation is the process by which a single species gives rise to two daughter species, which are genetically distinct and eventually unable to interbreed. Speciation can occur as a result of factors such as geographical isolation, ecological divergence or sexual selection.

data.name: Internet of Things
data.description: The Internet of things (IoT) is the network of physical devices, vehicles, home appliances, and other items embedded with electronics, software, sensors, actuators, and connectivity which enables these things to connect, collect and exchange data

data.name: Supramolecular Chemistry
data.description: Supramolecular chemistry is the study of entities of greater complexity than individual molecules — assemblies of molecules that bond and organize through intermolecular interactions. The design and synthesis of supramolecular systems invokes interactions beyond the covalent bond, using, for example, hydrogen bonding, metal coordination and interactions to bring discrete building blocks together.

data.name: Ethics of Technology
data.description: It is a field of study that examines the ethical implications, moral dilemmas, and social impacts arising from the development, deployment, and use of technology. It involves the analysis and evaluation of the ethical considerations associated with technological advancements and their effects on individuals, society, and the environment.

data.name: Tumour Immunology
data.description: Tumour immunology describes the interaction between cells of the immune system with tumour cells. Understanding these interactions is important for the development of new therapies for cancer treatment.

data.name: Theoretical Particle Physics
data.description: Theoretical particle physics attempts to develop the models, theoretical framework, and mathematical tools involved in particle physics to understand current experiments and make predictions for future experiments.

data.name: Nuclear Chemistry
data.description: Nuclear chemistry is concerned with the properties of and changes to atomic nuclei, as opposed to traditional chemistry, which involves properties and changes related to the electronic structure of atoms and molecules. The topic includes, for example, the study of radioactivity and nuclear reactions.

data.name: Nursing Education
data.description: Formal learning and training in the science of nursing. This includes the functions and duties in the physical care of patients, and a combination of different disciplines that both accelerates the patient's return to health and helps maintain it. License and Certifications Associate degree nursing programs Baccalaureate nursing program Advanced practice nurses: RegisteredNs who specialize in one of several fields, which include nurse practitioner (NP), certified nurse midwife (CNM), certified registered nurse anesthetist (CRNA), and clinical nurse specialist (CNS).

data.name: Comparative Literature
data.description: Comparative Literature is traditionally known as the study of two or more literatures in comparison (English and German, for example) and their multi-dimensional components which may encompass aspects such as the historical, gender, economic, cultural, social, philosophical, religious, and linguistic factors of the distinct cultures being analyzed.

subjects.term: History, description, critical appraisal of more than two literatures

data.name: Enzymology
data.description: Enzymology is the branch of biochemistry aiming to understand how enzymes work through the relationship between structure and function and how they fold into their native state. It is the study of how enzymes catalyze reactions, how such catalysis is regulated, how enzymes evolve and function and how enzymes can be inhibited to develop therapeutics.

data.name: Electron Transfer
data.description: Electron transfer is a process by which an electron moves from one atom or molecule to another. It is a key concept in redox chemistry – the chemistry of reactions where one reaction partner loses electrons (oxidation) while the other gains electrons (reduction).

data.name: Hindu Theology

These aspects of divine worship are known as Shanmatas, or the sixfold religious practice of the Hindus.

data.name: Computer-Aided Engineering (CAD, CAE) and Design
data.description: Computer-aided engineering (CAE) is the broad usage of computer software to aid in engineering analysis tasks. It is often summarized in the collective abbreviation "CAx".

data.name: Models of Computation
data.description: Includes computability, concurrency, hybrid models, abstract machines, quantum computing, abstract machines. These models help computer scientists and mathematicians analyze and understand different computational problems and algorithms in a formal and rigorous manner.

data.name: Cancer Imaging
data.description: Cancer imaging is an umbrella term that covers the many approaches used to research and diagnose cancer. Originally used to diagnose and stage the disease, cancer imaging is now also used to assist with surgery and radiotherapy, to look for early responses to cancer therapies and to identify patients who are not responding to treatment.

data.name: Business Mathematics
data.description: Business mathematics is a field of study and practice that applies mathematical concepts and techniques to solve business problems. It involves the use of quantitative methods to analyze and make decisions related to financial management, investments, accounting, economics, and other business-related fields. In research, business mathematics involves the development and testing of mathematical models and algorithms to solve business problems. The field of business mathematics research covers a wide range of topics, including financial modeling, risk management, optimization, forecasting, and data analysis. In practice, business mathematics involves the application of mathematical concepts and techniques to solve real-world business problems. It includes financial analysis, budgeting, cost analysis, investment analysis, and other quantitative methods used in business decision-making.

data.name: Mathematical Finance
data.description: Mathematical Finance uses mathematical models and techniques to analyze financial markets, instruments, and risks, providing insights into pricing, investment strategies, and financial decision-making.

data.name: Engineering Fluid Dynamics

data.name: Sociological Theory
data.description: Sociological theory is the body of ideas and frameworks that seek to explain the social world and its phenomena, often focusing on the interconnections between individuals, social structures, institutions, and cultural contexts.

data.name: Fourier Analysis
data.description: Is the study of the way general functions may be represented or approximated by sums of simpler trigonometric functions. Fourier analysis grew from the study of Fourier series, and is named after Joseph Fourier, who showed that representing a function as a sum of trigonometric functions greatly simplifies the study of heat transfer.

data.name: Geodynamics
data.description: Geodynamics refers to the processes by which mantle convection shapes and reshapes the Earth and other rocky planets. Its study includes plate tectonics, volcanism, the chemistry of lava and volcanic rocks, gravity and geomagnetic anomalies as well as seismic investigations into the structure of the mantle.

data.name: Philosophy of the Enlightenment
data.description: The philosophy of the Enlightenment refers to the intellectual movement that took place in Europe during the 17th and 18th centuries, known as the Age of Enlightenment. data.description: Biomineralization is the process by which living organisms produce minerals. Biomineralization processes often lead to the hardening or stiffening of the mineralized materials. data.name: Order, Lattices, Ordered Algebraic Structures
data.description: A lattice is an abstract structure studied in the mathematical subdisciplines of order theory and abstract algebra. It consists of a partially ordered set in which every two elements have a unique supremum (also called a least upper bound or join) and a unique infimum (also called a greatest lower bound or meet). Lattices can also be characterized as algebraic structures satisfying certain axiomatic identities

These mathematical objects are usually defined as a sequence of random variables, where the index of the sequence has the interpretation of time or space.

data.name: Organized Crime
data.description: Organized Crime is the study of criminal enterprises that operate in a structured and hierarchical manner to engage in illegal activities for financial gain. Organized crime involves ongoing criminal enterprises with a high degree of organization, coordination, and longevity. These groups often specialize in activities such as drug trafficking, human trafficking, money laundering, extortion, racketeering, and other illicit endeavors.

data.name: Integral Transforms and Operational Calculus
data.description: In mathematics, an integral transform maps an equation from its original domain into another domain where it might be manipulated and solved much more easily than in the original domain. The solution is then mapped back to the original domain using the inverse of the integral transform.Operational calculus, also known as operational analysis, is a technique by which problems in analysis, in particular differential equations, are transformed into algebraic problems, usually the problem of solving a polynomial equation.

data.name: Seventeenth-Century Literature

It explores the interplay between conscious and unconscious aspects of the mind, including childhood experiences, defense mechanisms, and the dynamics of interpersonal relationships. Psychodynamics places emphasis on the role of unconscious motivations, conflicts, and unresolved issues in shaping individuals' thoughts, feelings, and actions.

data.description: Laser-produced plasmas are plasmas produced by firing high-intensity beams of light. Laser-produced plasmas have been used to create short bursts of x-rays and to accelerate particles — so-called plasma-based accelerators. Laser produced plasmas are also useful for recreating astrophysical plasmas in the laboratory.

data.name: Animal Biotechnology
data.description: Animal biotechnology is a branch of biotechnology in which molecular biology techniques are used to genetically engineer (i.e. modify the genome of) animals in order to improve their suitability for pharmaceutical, agricultural or industrial applications. Animal biotechnology has been used to produce genetically modified animals that synthesize therapeutic proteins, have improved growth rates or are resistant to disease.

data.name: Membrane Biophysics

It explores modes of representation that fashion has taken historically, but also considers the cultural contexts for new directions, at a time when the fashioned body is increasingly implicated in the negotiation of individual and collective identities.

data.name: Preclinical Research
data.description: Preclinical research involves the evaluation of potential therapeutic interventions in cells and animals. Candidates for entry into clinical trials can then be selected based on their effectiveness and safety in disease models. All drugs require data from various toxicological preclinical studies to support their potential safety in humans before clinical trials can begin.

data.name: Microwave Chemistry

Learning disability nurses may work in a range of settings, including people's homes, workplaces, hospitals and prisons.

Core topics within the luxury industry field of research may include consumer behavior and preferences, brand management, product design and development, pricing strategies, distribution and retail management, supply chain management, digital marketing and e-commerce, sustainability and social responsibility, and global luxury markets and trends. data.name: Business Ethics
data.description: Business Ethics refers to the study of moral principles and values that guide the behavior of individuals and organizations in the business world. It is a field of management research that examines the ethical dilemmas that arise in the context of business and how they can be resolved in a socially responsible manner.  The field of Business Ethics encompasses a wide range of topics, including corporate social responsibility, environmental sustainability, fair labor practices, responsible marketing, and ethical decision-making. It seeks to promote ethical conduct in the business world by providing guidance and frameworks for managers and organizations to make decisions that are not only legal and profitable but also ethical and socially responsible.  The field of Business Ethics is interdisciplinary in nature, drawing upon insights from philosophy, economics, psychology, sociology, and law. It has become increasingly important in recent years as businesses face growing pressure to operate in a socially responsible and sustainable manner. As a result, many organizations are now incorporating ethical considerations into their decision-making processes and developing codes of conduct and policies to guide their behavior.

data.name: Field Theory and Polynomials

data.name: Psychoanalysis
data.description: Psychoanalysis is a psychological approach and therapeutic method developed by Sigmund Freud that aims to explore and understand unconscious processes, conflicts, and motivations underlying human behavior. The distribution of income among citizens; and 3.	The stability of the economy.

In practice, HRD professionals work with organizations to identify skills gaps and training needs, and develop programs to address them. They may also provide coaching and mentoring services to employees, or work with managers to improve performance management processes. HRD professionals are often involved in talent management initiatives, such as succession planning and leadership development, to ensure that organizations have the skills and capabilities they need to achieve their strategic objectives.

data.description: Lightweight construction, steel construction, and timber construction are three different approaches to building structures that offer specific advantages and considerations. These materials often include lightweight concrete, gypsum boards, and lightweight steel or aluminum framing systems. While Steel construction utilizes structural steel elements as the primary load-bearing components of the building.  It allows for the creation of large open spaces, offers design flexibility, and provides excellent fire resistance. And Timber construction involves the use of wood as the primary material for structural elements, such as beams, columns, and frames. Wood is a renewable resource, and timber construction offers advantages such as environmental sustainability, aesthetic appeal, and good thermal insulation.

data.name: Eschatology

The end of the world or end times is predicted by several world religions (both Abrahamic and non-Abrahamic), which teach that negative world events will reach a climax. Belief that the end of the world is imminent is known as apocalypticism, and over time has been held both by members of mainstream religions and by doomsday cults. In the context of mysticism, the term refers metaphorically to the end of ordinary reality and to reunion with the divine. Various religions treat eschatology as a future event prophesied in sacred texts or in folklore.

data.name: Business Taxation and Tax Law
data.description: Business taxation and tax law refer to the legal framework and regulations that govern the taxation of business activities and transactions. Business taxation is the process of determining, reporting, and paying taxes on business income, profits, and assets. In research, business taxation and tax law involve the study of tax policies and their impact on businesses and the economy. The field of business taxation research covers a wide range of topics, including tax planning, tax compliance, tax incentives, and tax evasion. Tax planning involves the use of legal strategies to minimize the amount of taxes paid by businesses while complying with tax laws and regulations. Tax compliance involves ensuring that businesses accurately report their income, deductions, and other relevant information on tax returns and pay the appropriate amount of taxes owed. Tax incentives are tax breaks provided by governments to encourage businesses to invest in certain activities or locations. Tax evasion involves the illegal avoidance of paying taxes by intentionally failing to report income or claiming false deductions. In practice, business taxation and tax law involve complying with various federal, state, and local tax laws and regulations. Businesses must report their income and expenses accurately, pay the appropriate amount of taxes owed, and maintain proper documentation to support their tax filings. Tax law also involves understanding the tax implications of various business activities, such as mergers and acquisitions, international transactions, and investments. Business taxation professionals, such as tax attorneys, certified public accountants (CPAs), and tax consultants, help businesses navigate the complex tax landscape and ensure compliance with tax laws and regulations.

data.name: Genetic Service
data.description: Genetic services are provisions to diagnose and advise individuals with risk factors for genetic disorders. Individuals with family members who have such disorders are often at risk of developing the disorder themselves. Genetic services include genetic testing and genetic counselling. Patient education often has a prominent role.

data.name: Production
data.description: In management research, "production" typically refers to the process of creating goods or services using various resources such as labor, machinery, and materials. This process often involves multiple steps and stages, such as planning, sourcing raw materials, manufacturing, quality control, and distribution.  Production management is the field of study that focuses on optimizing the production process to ensure that it is efficient, cost-effective, and meets the needs of customers. This involves identifying and eliminating bottlenecks, minimizing waste, and improving productivity through the use of various techniques and tools such as lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and Total Quality Management.  Effective production management is critical for the success of any business that produces goods or services, as it helps to ensure that products are delivered to customers on time, at the desired quality level, and at a reasonable cost.

data.name: Optical Communications
data.description: Optical communication is communication at a distance using light to carry information. An optical communication system uses a transmitter, which encodes a message into an optical signal, a channel, which carries the signal to its destination, and a receiver, which reproduces the message from the received optical signal.

data.name: Automotive Industry
data.description: The automotive industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the design, development, production, marketing, and sale of vehicles, including cars, trucks, buses, motorcycles, and other types of motorized vehicles. It encompasses a wide range of topics, such as supply chain management, manufacturing processes, technology and innovation, marketing strategies, consumer behavior, government regulations and policies, and sustainability. Researchers in this field may examine the performance and competitive strategies of individual companies, the dynamics of industry structure and competition, and the impact of technological advancements on the industry. The automotive industry has a significant economic impact worldwide and is of interest to scholars, policymakers, and practitioners alike.

data.description: Cancer screening describes any procedure that aims to detect precancerous changes, such that cancer can be treated before it becomes malignant. Mammography and cervical smear tests are routine cancer-screening procedures. Ideally, the benefits of any screening procedure should outweigh the risks.

The key constituents of the cytoskeleton are actin filaments, microtubules and intermediate filaments.

data.name: Behavioral Finance
data.description: Define behavioral finance as in research and practice Behavioral finance is an interdisciplinary field of study that combines principles of psychology and economics to understand how human behavior and emotions influence financial decisions and markets. In research and practice, behavioral finance aims to explain why people make irrational financial decisions, and how these decisions impact markets and the economy as a whole.  Behavioral finance researchers study various psychological and cognitive biases that affect financial decision-making, such as overconfidence, loss aversion, and herding behavior. They also examine the role of emotions, social norms, and cultural factors in shaping financial attitudes and behaviors.  In practice, behavioral finance is used to develop strategies and tools for improving financial decision-making and investment outcomes. This may include developing investment products that take into account investors' behavioral tendencies and preferences, or designing financial education programs that aim to overcome common cognitive biases and promote rational decision-making.  Overall, behavioral finance seeks to provide a more complete understanding of financial markets and investor behavior, with the goal of improving investment outcomes and reducing financial risk.

Researchers also examine the business benefits of promoting employee health and wellbeing, such as reduced healthcare costs, increased productivity, and improved employee engagement and retention. In practice, employee health and wellbeing professionals work with employers to develop and implement programs and policies that support employee health and wellbeing. They may also provide individual coaching and counseling services to employees to help them manage stress, improve their mental health, and adopt healthy lifestyle habits.

data.name: Customer Relationship Management
data.description: Consumer Relationship Management (CRM) is a business strategy that focuses on managing interactions and relationships with customers in order to maximize their lifetime value to the company. CRM involves the use of technology and data analysis to identify and target customers, as well as to personalize and enhance their experiences with the company.  At its core, CRM involves building a deep understanding of each customer's needs, preferences, and behaviors, and using this knowledge to tailor the company's products, services, and communications to meet those needs. This involves collecting and analyzing data from multiple sources, including customer interactions, social media, and other sources, to gain insights into customer behavior and preferences.  Effective CRM can lead to increased customer satisfaction, loyalty, and retention, as well as improved sales and revenue growth for the company. It requires a coordinated effort across multiple departments and functions within the organization, including marketing, sales, customer service, and IT.

data.name: Customer Service and Call Center

It is a field of management research and practice that encompasses a range of activities, strategies, and technologies aimed at meeting customers' needs, improving customer satisfaction, and fostering customer loyalty.  The main goal of customer service and call centers is to provide customers with timely and accurate information, resolve their issues and complaints, and ensure a positive experience throughout their interaction with the company. Effective customer service and call centers involve the use of well-trained agents, efficient processes, and advanced technologies that enable companies to optimize their operations and enhance the customer experience.  The field of customer service and call centers encompasses several key areas of research and practice, including customer relationship management, service quality management, workforce management, technology and innovation, and performance measurement and analytics. data.name: African Philosophy
data.description: African philosophy refers to the diverse philosophical traditions and worldviews that have emerged from the African continent. African philosophy has been influenced by indigenous African cultures and belief systems. These include animism, ancestor worship, and communalism, which emphasize the interconnectedness of humans, nature, and the spiritual realm. African philosophical thought also emerged in response to encounters with external influences such as Arab and European philosophies, Christianity, and Islam. African philosophers often emphasize the importance of community, interdependence, and social harmony in their ethical and epistemological frameworks.

data.name: Cartography
data.description: Cartography is the study and practice of making maps. It combines science, aesthtetics and technique in order to model reality and to commicate spatial information effectively.

data.name: Regional Geography
data.description: Geographical studies that specifically cover a certain region of the world.

subjects.term: Physical geography of areas, regions, places in general

data.name: Molecular Evolution
data.description: Molecular evolution is the area of evolutionary biology that studies evolutionary change at the level of the DNA sequence. It includes the study of rates of sequence change, relative importance of adaptive and neutral changes, and changes in genome structure.

data.name: Ecclesiology
data.description: Ecclesiology is the study of the Church, the origins of Christianity, its relationship to Jesus, its role in salvation, its polity, its discipline, its eschatology, and its leadership.  In its early history, one of the Church's primary ecclesiological issues had to do with the status of Gentile members in what had become the New Testament fulfilment of the essentially Jewish Old Testament church. It later contended with such questions as whether it was to be governed by a council of presbyters or a single bishop, how much authority the bishop of Rome had over other major bishops, the role of the Church in the world, whether salvation was possible outside of the institution of the Church, the relationship between the Church and the State, and questions of theology and liturgy and other issues. Ecclesiology may be used in the specific sense of a particular church or denomination's character, self-described or otherwise. This is the sense of the word in such phrases as Catholic ecclesiology, Protestant ecclesiology, and ecumenical ecclesiology.  The word ecclesiology was defined in the 19th century as the science of the building and decoration of church buildings and is still used in that sense in the context of architectural history.

data.name: Molecular Biophysics
data.description: Molecular biophysics is the study of the physical principles governing biomolecular systems. It seeks to explain biological function in terms of molecular structure, dynamics and organization, from single molecules to supramolecular structures.

data.name: Non-associative Rings and Algebras
data.description: A non-associative algebra (or distributive algebra) is an algebra over a field where the binary multiplication operation is not assumed to be associative

data.name: American Philosophy
data.description: American philosophy includes indigenous and settler philosophies in North, Central, and South America.

subjects.term: Philosophy of United States and Canada
Philosophical traditions and schools of thought

data.name: Human Migration
data.description: Human migration is the movement of people from one place to another intending to settle in a new geographic region.

data.name: Analytical Psychology
data.description: Analytical psychology is a field of study within psychology that focuses on the theories and practices developed by Swiss psychiatrist Carl Jung. It explores the deep connections between the conscious and unconscious aspects of the human psyche, emphasizing the role of symbolism, archetypes, and individuation. Analytical psychology places particular emphasis on the exploration of the unconscious mind and the integration of its contents into one's conscious awareness. It seeks to understand the complexities of the human psyche, including personality development, psychological disorders, and the process of self-discovery and personal growth. Analytical psychologists utilize various techniques, including dream analysis, active imagination, and the interpretation of symbols, to facilitate the exploration and understanding of the unconscious aspects of the individual. The goal of analytical psychology is to promote self-awareness, psychological well-being, and the development of a harmonious relationship between the conscious and unconscious aspects of the psyche.

data.name: Optical Metrology
data.description: Optical metrology is using light to set the standards that define units of measurement and for other high-precision research. Optical clocks, for example, have the potential to define the unit of time — the second — to a more precise degree than is possible in the atomic clocks used at present.

data.name: Mathematical Methods in Physics
data.description: This branch refers to the application of mathematics to problems in physics and the development of mathematical methods suitable for such applications and for the formulation of physical theories.

data.name: Anthropological Theory
data.description: Anthropological theory are analytical tools for explaining and making sense of broad and complex anthropological topics. Anthropological theory is used in all four subfields of anthropology. Cultural anthropology focuses on studying cultural diversity amongst human societies.

subjects.term: Philosophy. Relation to other topics. Methodology

data.name: Computer Networks
data.description: A computer network is a set of computers sharing resources located on or provided by network nodes. Computers use common communication protocols over digital interconnections to communicate with each other. These interconnections are made up of telecommunication network technologies based on physically wired, optical, and wireless radio-frequency methods that may be arranged in a variety of network topologies.

data.name: Development Communication
data.description: Development Communication refers to the use of communication to facilitate social development. Development communication techniques include information dissemination and education, behaviour change, social marketing, social mobilization, media advocacy, communication for social change and community participation.

data.name: Origin of Life
data.description: Studies using chemical methodology to understand how life on Earth may have started, or how life might arise under other circumstances, such as on exoplanets or in a laboratory setting.

data.name: Computational Linguistics
data.description: Computational linguistics is an interdisciplinary field concerned with the computational modelling of natural language, as well as the study of appropriate computational approaches to linguistic questions. In general, computational linguistics draws upon linguistics, computer science, artificial intelligence, math, logic, philosophy, cognitive science, cognitive psychology, psycholinguistics, anthropology and neuroscience, among others.

data.name: Middle Eastern Politics
data.description: Middle Eastern Politics studies the political systems, movements, and conflicts in the Middle East, focusing on issues such as governance, regional dynamics, and international relations.

subjects.term: Middle East. Near East. Southwest Asia. Islamic Empire

data.name: Multilingualism
data.description: The ability to speak and understand multiple languages.  Multilingualism can exist at individual, societal, or global levels and offers numerous benefits and opportunities.

data.name: Services
data.description: The services industry, also known as the service sector, encompasses a wide range of businesses that provide intangible products and services such as hospitality, banking, healthcare, education, insurance, and retail. It is a major contributor to many economies, accounting for a significant portion of the GDP in many countries.  As a field within business and management research and practice, the services industry involves studying and analyzing the unique challenges and opportunities faced by service-based businesses. Some core topics within this field include: Service quality and customer satisfaction: Ensuring that services meet or exceed customer expectations and result in high levels of satisfaction. Service innovation: Developing new and improved services to meet changing customer needs and preferences. Service marketing and branding: Promoting and positioning services effectively in the marketplace to attract and retain customers. Service operations management: Managing service delivery processes to ensure efficiency, quality, and customer satisfaction. Service design and delivery: Designing and delivering services that meet customer needs and preferences while optimizing resource utilization. Service personnel management: Managing the recruitment, training, and development of personnel in service organizations to ensure high levels of customer satisfaction. Service strategy and business models: Developing effective strategies and business models for service-based businesses in highly competitive and dynamic markets. Overall, research and practice in the services industry aim to improve the quality of service delivery, enhance customer satisfaction, and drive business growth and profitability in service-based businesses.

data.name: Interventional Radiology
data.description: Interventional radiology (IR) is a medical sub-specialty of radiology utilizing minimally-invasive image-guided procedures to diagnose and treat diseases in nearly every organ system. These procedures have less risk, less pain and less recovery time in comparison to open surgery. IR refers to a range of techniques which rely on the use radiological image guidance (X-ray fluoroscopy, ultrasound, computed tomography [CT] or magnetic resonance imaging [MRI]) to precisely target therapy.

subjects.term: Surgery utilizing specific instruments and techniques or specific groups of instruments and techniques

data.name: Well-Being
data.description: Well-being is the experience of health, happiness and prosperity, a sense of purpose in life, high life satisfaction, and the ability to manage stress.

subjects.term: Statistics. Social indicators. Quality of life

data.name: Philosophy of Medicine
data.description: Philosophy of Medicine explores the conceptual and ethical issues in medical practice and research, including the nature of health and disease, medical knowledge, and healthcare ethics.

data.name: Cancer Nanotechnology
data.description: Cancer nanotechnology is a branch of nanotechnology concerned with the application of both nanomaterials (such as nanoparticles for tumour imaging or drug delivery) and nanotechnology approaches (such as nanoparticle-based theranostics) to the diagnosis and treatment of cancer.

data.name: Distribution Theory
data.description: possible values and probabilities for a random variable within a given range

data.name: Mathematical Models of Cognitive Processes and Neural Networks
data.description: Mathematical models of cognitive processes and neural networks provide a quantitative framework for understanding and simulating the complex behaviors of the brain and the mind. These models aim to capture the underlying mechanisms and dynamics of cognitive processes and neural activity.

synonyms: Mathematische Modelle kognitiver Prozesse und neuraler Netzwerke
Computational Models of Cognition and Neural Networks
