data.name: Middle Eastern Religions
data.description: All three major Abrahamic religions (Judaism, Christianity, and, Islam) originated from the Middle East and are present in the Middle East. Islam is the most prevalent religion in the contemporary Middle East. Smaller minority religions, such as the Baháʼí Faith, Druze, Alawites, Bábism, Yazidism, Mandaeism, Yarsanism, Samaritanism, Ishikism, Ali-Illahism, Yazdânism and Zoroastrianism are also present in the Middle East region.

subjects.term: Study of comparative religion. Historiography. Methodology

data.name: History of Medieval Europe
data.description: History of Medieval Europe studies the period from the fall of the Roman Empire to the beginning of the Renaissance, focusing on the social, political, cultural, and economic developments of the time.

subjects.term: European history: medieval period, middle ages

data.name: Wood, fabric, and textiles
data.description: Wood, fabric, and textiles are materials commonly used in various industries and applications. Each material possesses unique characteristics and properties that make them suitable for specific uses. Wood is a natural material derived from the stems, branches, and roots of trees. Fabric refers to a flexible material made through weaving, knitting, or felting fibers together. Textiles encompass a broad range of materials used for their flexibility and ability to be woven or knitted.

data.name: Theatre History
data.description: The history of theatre is primarily concerned with the origin and subsequent development of the theatre as an autonomous activity. Since classical Athens in the 5th century BC, vibrant traditions of theatre have flourished in cultures across the world.

data.name: Symbolic and Algebraic Manipulation
data.description: The study and development of algorithms and software for manipulating mathematical expressions and other mathematical objects.

data.name: Socio-Economic Policy
data.description: Social policy is concerned with the ways societies across the world meet human needs for security, education, work, health and wellbeing. Social policy addresses how states and societies respond to global challenges of social, demographic and economic change, and of poverty, migration and globalisation. Social policy is a plan or action of government or institutional agencies which aim to improve or reform society. The economy of governments covers the systems for setting levels of taxation, government budgets, the money supply and interest rates as well as the labour market, national ownership, and many other areas of government interventions into the economy.

data.name: Classroom Management
data.description: Classroom management, as a field of study, involves the strategies, techniques, and approaches used by educators to create and maintain an effective learning environment within a classroom setting. It focuses on promoting positive student behavior, engagement, and academic achievement while minimizing disruptions and fostering a supportive and inclusive classroom climate.

data.name: International and Comparative Education
data.description: International and comparative education is a field of study that examines educational systems, policies, practices, and outcomes across different countries and regions. It focuses on understanding the similarities, differences, and interconnections between education systems globally, as well as the factors that shape them.

data.name: Public Sector Studies
data.description: Public sector studies include the studies on public goods and governmental services such as the military, law enforcement, infrastructure, public transit, public education, along with health care and those working for the government itself, such as elected officials.

data.name: Security Services
data.description: A processing or communication service that enhances the security of the data processing systems and the information transfers of an organization. These services are intended to counter security attacks, and they make use of one or more security mechanisms to provide the service.

data.name: Administrative Law
data.description: Administrative law, the legal framework within which public administration is carried out. It derives from the need to create and develop a system of public administration under law, a concept that may be compared with the much older notion of justice under law.

data.name: Japanese Philosophy
data.description: Japanese philosophy has historically been a fusion of both indigenous Shinto and continental religions, such as Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism.

data.name: Office Management
data.description: Office Management is a field within business and management that involves the planning, organizing, and controlling of administrative activities, procedures, and resources to achieve organizational goals. It includes various administrative tasks such as managing office supplies, budgeting, coordinating meetings, managing employee schedules, and providing support to managers. Core topics within Office Management may include: Administrative support: This involves providing administrative support to managers and executives, including managing their schedules, preparing correspondence, and organizing meetings. Facilities management: This includes managing office spaces, ensuring proper maintenance of equipment, and overseeing office security.  Budgeting and financial management: This involves managing budgets, forecasting expenses, and analyzing financial reports. Human resource management: This includes managing employee records, coordinating recruitment and selection processes, and overseeing employee training and development. Project management: This involves managing projects from start to finish, including planning, budgeting, and executing tasks. Information management: This includes managing information systems, including data collection, storage, and analysis. Communication management: This involves managing communication within and outside the organization, including written and oral communication, social media management, and public relations. Overall, the core objective of Office Management is to ensure that all administrative tasks are handled efficiently and effectively, allowing the organization to operate smoothly and achieve its goals.

data.name: Sports Economics
data.description: Sports Economics is the study of issues of sports by means of economics, its methods and theoretical frameworks (heavily based on macroeconomics) as well as the study of economics problems in the context of sports. Sports Economics attempts to describe, explain and prognosticate actions by relevant parties and use the acquired knowledge technologically.

subjects.term: Athletic and outdoor sports and games

data.name: Data Storage Representation
data.description: Data storage representation refers to the way data is organized, stored, and represented in computer systems. It involves the conversion of data from its original form to a format suitable for storage and retrieval in computer memory or secondary storage devices.

data.name: Diversity-oriented Synthesis
data.description: Diversity-oriented synthesis aims to produce chemical libraries that are representative of a large portion of chemical space by applying a variety of reaction conditions to starting materials with multiple different functional groups. Multiple rounds of such reactions result in rapid access to structurally diverse products suitable for screening.

data.name: Entertainment Industry
data.description: The entertainment industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the various sectors involved in the creation, production, and distribution of entertainment products and services. This includes film, television, music, theater, sports, gaming, and digital media. The research within this field aims to understand the unique challenges and opportunities within each sector, including the impact of changing technologies, evolving consumer behaviors, and shifting market trends. Key topics within the entertainment industry as a field of research include audience engagement, content creation and distribution, intellectual property rights, marketing and advertising, and revenue generation.

subjects.term: Media, entertainment, information and communication industries

data.name: Crime and Technology
data.description: This topic focuses on understanding how technological innovations, both positive and negative, impact criminal activities, crime prevention, and the criminal justice system. This subfield explores the use of technology in committing crimes, such as cybercrime and digital fraud, as well as the role of technology in crime detection, surveillance, and forensic analysis.

data.name: Interpersonal Attraction
data.description: Interpersonal attraction in the field of psychology refers to the psychological processes and factors that influence individuals' feelings of liking, interest, or attraction towards others. It encompasses various aspects of human relationships, such as physical attractiveness, similarity, proximity, and social interaction.

data.name: Drugs
data.description: The subfield of drugs within criminology focuses on the study of drug use, drug-related crime, drug policy, and the social and legal responses to drug-related issues. It examines the causes and consequences of drug abuse and addiction, the relationship between drugs and crime, drug markets, drug law enforcement, and the effectiveness of drug prevention and treatment programs.

data.name: Feminist Theology
data.description: Feminist theology is a movement found in several religions, including Buddhism, Hinduism, Sikhism, Neopaganism, Baháʼí Faith, Christianity, Judaism, Islam, and New Thought, to reconsider the traditions, practices, scriptures, and theologies of those religions from a feminist perspective.

data.name: Attitudes
data.description: In the field of psychology, attitudes refer to an individual's evaluations, beliefs, and feelings toward people, objects, or ideas. Attitudes can be positive, negative, or neutral, and they influence our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors.

data.name: Practice-as-Research
data.description: Practice-as-Research (PaR) is an approach to research wherein the main inquiry approach is practice, and the findings of the inquiry are presented through a piece of practice. PaR usually also includes a written outcome, or an archival outcome in other forms (e.g. digital images or lecture recitals), that captures the critical reflection on practice and evidences the new knowledge gained through the process of the practice. PaR is concerned about the nature of practice. It aims to develop knowledge of operational significance and to advance professional work. PaR in a higher education context places emphasis on analysing and theorising practice rather than merely gathering reference materials for the production of an artefact or artwork.

data.name: Surface Patterning
data.description: Surface patterning includes techniques for preparing and patterning surfaces, from the arrangement of single molecules to the macro-scale, for example, through etching, electrochemical patterning and film deposition.

subjects.term: Properties of materials and nondestructive testing

data.name: Weapons
data.description: This subfield focuses on the study of various aspects related to weapons, including their types, characteristics, prevalence, usage patterns, legal regulations, and the implications of their involvement in criminal activities.

data.name: Patient Education
data.description: Patient education is the procedure in which individuals with health occupations impart information to patients about their own health status and needs. Patient education aims to enable patients to improve their own health by changing their health-related behaviours. Education can be therapeutic or used for disease prevention.

data.name: History of Sub-Saharan Africa
data.description: History of Sub-Saharan Africa studies the historical development of the region south of the Sahara Desert, focusing on pre-colonial societies, colonial impact, and post-independence transformations.

data.name: Multimedia Information Systems
data.description: Multimedia Information Systems (MIS) couple data management capabilities (effective and efficient methods for storage, indexing, querying, and retrieval) with media management (media representation, data compression, standardization, and transmission).

data.name: Games Studies
data.description: Games studies is an interdisciplinary field of academic study that focuses on the analysis, interpretation, and understanding of games and gaming culture. It encompasses various aspects of games, including their design, mechanics, aesthetics, social and cultural impact, and player experiences.

data.name: Environmental Monitoring
data.description: Environmental monitoring or analysis describes the processes and activities (e.g. sampling and analyzing soil or water, or using analytical chemistry) that need to take place to characterize and monitor the quality of the environment.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Environmental Science (see also Chemistry / Environmental)

data.name: Youth Culture
data.description: Youth culture refers to the cultural practice of members of this age group by which they express their identities and demonstrate their sense of belonging to a particular group of young people.

data.name: Survey Methodology
data.description: Survey methodology is "the study of survey methods". As a field of applied statistics concentrating on human-research surveys, survey methodology studies the sampling of individual units from a population and associated techniques of survey data collection, such as questionnaire construction and methods for improving the number and accuracy of responses to surveys.

data.name: Maker
data.description: Arduino, Raspberry Pi, sensor networks, sensors, xbee, 3D printing

data.name: Self-efficacy
data.description: Self-efficacy, in the field of psychology, refers to an individual's belief in their own capabilities to successfully execute tasks, achieve goals, and overcome challenges. It is the perception of one's competence and confidence in their abilities to perform specific actions and produce desired outcomes.

data.name: Phenomenology
data.description: Phenomenology is a tradition in European philosophy that emerged from Edmund Husserl's method of "bracketing" everything except present conscious experience and theorizing on the basis of that experience. Prominent figures in phenomenology include Heidegger, Sartre, Beauvoir, and Merleau-Ponty.

data.name: Humanistic Psychology
data.description: Humanistic psychology is a psychological perspective that emphasizes the unique qualities of individuals, their subjective experiences, and their inherent capacity for personal growth and self-fulfillment. It focuses on understanding human behavior in the context of personal meaning, self-actualization, and the pursuit of personal values and goals. Humanistic psychologists emphasize the importance of self-awareness, self-acceptance, and the realization of one's full potential.

data.name: Natural Products
data.description: Natural products are small molecules produced naturally by any organism including primary and secondary metabolites. They include very small molecules, such as urea, and complex structures, such as Taxol. As they may only be isolable in small quantities, have interesting biological activity and chemical structures, natural product synthesis poses an interesting challenge in organic chemistry.

data.name: Behaviorism
data.description: Behaviorism is a school of thought in psychology that emphasizes the study of observable behavior rather than internal mental processes. It focuses on understanding how behavior is shaped by the environment through conditioning and reinforcement.

data.name: Health Administration
data.description: Health administration, healthcare administration, healthcare management or hospital management is the field relating to leadership, management, and administration of public health systems, health care systems, hospitals, and hospital networks in all the primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors.

subjects.term: Departments of public health. Boards of health

data.name: Personal Development
data.description: Personal development focuses on enhancing one's self-awareness, knowledge, skills, and attitudes with the goal of achieving personal fulfillment and reaching one's potential. It involves a conscious effort to develop and refine aspects of oneself, such as emotional intelligence, self-esteem, resilience, goal-setting, and self-motivation.

subjects.term: Development and modification of character and personality

data.name: Algebraic Topology
data.description: Algebraic topology is a branch of mathematics that uses tools from abstract algebra to study topological spaces. The basic goal is to find algebraic invariants that classify topological spaces up to homeomorphism, though usually most classify up to homotopy equivalence

data.name: Chromosomes
data.description: Chromosomes are cellular structures that contain the genetic material. A chromosome is comprised of a single DNA molecule that may be either circular or linear. The full complement of a cell's chromosomes is called the genome.

data.name: Phlebology
data.description: The term phlebology refers to the study of disorders that affect the veins (Greek: phlebos = vein, blood vessel). Based on a survey of the World Health Organization (WHO), vein problems rank among the most common diseases worldwide. Venous leg disorders are some of the earliest documented illnesses suffered by mankind.

subjects.term: Diseases of the veins. Varicose veins

data.name: Identity Politics
data.description: Identity Politics involves the political mobilization and advocacy based on social identities, such as race, gender, sexuality, and ethnicity, aiming to address issues of representation, rights, and social justice.

subjects.term: Civil and political rights of nondominant groups

data.name: Semiotics
data.description: Semiotics (also called semiotic studies) is the systematic study of sign processes (semiosis) and meaning making. Semiosis is any activity, conduct, or process that involves signs, where a sign is defined as anything that communicates something, usually called a meaning, to the sign's interpreter.

subjects.term: Communication; semantics, pragmatics, languages for special purposes

data.name: Political Communication
data.description: Political communication is concerned with the creation, content, exchange, spread and effect of information between the citizenry and the political entities, policy makers, government officials, and other related set-ups, via different kinds of media, and throughout all stages of the political process.

data.name: Asian Business
data.description: Asian Business is a field of management research and practice that focuses on understanding and analyzing business practices, strategies, and cultures in the Asian region. The field examines the unique characteristics and challenges of businesses operating in Asia and seeks to develop insights and solutions that can help organizations succeed in this dynamic and diverse market. Major topics in Asian Business include: Culture and management: Asian cultures have a significant influence on the way businesses are managed and organized. Research in this area explores the impact of cultural values on leadership, decision-making, and communication. Internationalization: Many Asian businesses are expanding their operations globally, and researchers in this area investigate the drivers, challenges, and strategies involved in this process. Innovation and entrepreneurship: Asia is a hotbed of innovation and entrepreneurship, and researchers in this area explore the factors that contribute to the success of start-ups and established businesses in the region. Strategic management: The Asian market is highly competitive, and companies need to develop effective strategies to succeed. Research in this area focuses on topics such as market entry, diversification, and mergers and acquisitions. Corporate social responsibility: Asian businesses are increasingly recognizing the importance of corporate social responsibility, and researchers in this area explore the role of businesses in promoting sustainable development and addressing social and environmental challenges. Technology and digital transformation: Asia is a leader in digital technology and e-commerce, and researchers in this area investigate the impact of digital transformation on businesses and the wider society. Overall, Asian Business is an interdisciplinary field that draws on various theories and methodologies from management, economics, sociology, and other social sciences. It provides valuable insights into the complexities and opportunities of doing business in Asia and is essential for organizations looking to expand their operations in the region.

data.name: Functions of a Complex Variable
data.description: Complex analysis, traditionally known as the theory of functions of a complex variable, is the branch of mathematical analysis that investigates functions of complex numbers. As a differentiable function of a complex variable is equal to the sum of its Taylor series, complex analysis is particularly concerned with analytic functions of a complex variable (that is, holomorphic functions).

data.name: Christian Cultural Studies
data.description: Christian culture generally includes all the cultural practices which have developed around the religion of Christianity. There are variations in the application of Christian beliefs in different cultures and traditions. Although theology can be an aspect of religious studies and religious studies can be an aspect of theology, these college degrees are distinct in important ways.

subjects.term: Social theology and interreligious relations and attitudes

data.name: Language History
data.description: Language history refers to the study of the development and evolution of languages over time. It involves tracing the origins, changes, and relationships between different languages and language families, as well as understanding the socio-cultural and historical contexts in which these languages have emerged and evolved. Language History, has a broader scope and encompasses the historical, cultural, and social aspects of language use and development as compared to Historical Linguistics

subjects.term: LANGUAGE ARTS & DISCIPLINES / Linguistics / Historical & Comparative

data.name: Algebraic Logic
data.description: In mathematical logic, algebraic logic is the reasoning obtained by manipulating equations with free variables

data.name: Evolutionary Studies
data.description: It is also defined as the study of the history of life forms on Earth. Evolution holds that all species are related and gradually change over generations. In a population, the genetic variations affect the phenotypes (physical characteristics) of an organism.

data.name: Integral Equations
data.description: Integral equations are equations in which an unknown function appears under an integral sign.

subjects.term: Difference equations and functional equations. Integral equations. Calculus of differences

data.name: Metamaterials
data.description: Metamaterials are engineered structures designed to interact with electromagnetic radiation in a desired fashion. They usually comprise an array of structures smaller than the wavelength of interest. These so-called meta-atoms can interact with the electric and magnetic components of light in a way that natural atoms do not.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Ultrafast Photonics
data.description: Ultrafast photonics is the study of light and its interaction with matter on short timescales, typically less than a picosecond. This includes investigating processes that occur in atoms and molecules, such as the dynamics and correlations between electrons during ionization, and often employs ultrafast lasers or mode-locked lasers.

data.name: Biomaterials-Vaccines
data.description: A vaccine is a biological preparation that provides active acquired immunity to a particular infectious disease.[1] A vaccine typically contains an agent that resembles a disease-causing microorganism and is often made from weakened or killed forms of the microbe, its toxins, or one of its surface proteins. The agent stimulates the body's immune system to recognize the agent as a threat, destroy it, and to further recognize and destroy any of the microorganisms associated with that agent that it may encounter in the future. Vaccines can be prophylactic (to prevent or ameliorate the effects of a future infection by a natural or "wild" pathogen), or therapeutic (to fight a disease that has already occurred, such as cancer)

data.name: Photonic Devices
data.description: Photonic devices are components for creating, manipulating or detecting light. This can include laser diodes, light-emitting diodes, solar and photovoltaic cells, displays and optical amplifiers. Other examples are devices for modulating a beam of light and for combining and separating beams of light of different wavelength.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials

data.name: Evangelicalism and Pentecostalism
data.description: Pentecostalism and Evangelicalism are traditions within Protestant Christianity. Pentecostalism emphasizes doctrines like baptism in the Holy Spirit, speaking in tongues, and miraculous gifts. Evangelicalism is a gospel-focused movenement. Most Pentecostals are evangelicals, but not all evangelicals are Pentecostals.

subjects.term: Movements transcending geographical and denominational lines and theological disciplines

data.name: Supercapacitors
data.description: A supercapacitor (SC) is a high-capacity capacitor with a capacitance value much higher than other capacitors, but with lower voltage limits, that bridges the gap between electrolytic capacitors and rechargeable batteries. Unlike ordinary capacitors, supercapacitors do not use the conventional solid dielectric, but rather electrostatic double-layer capacitance and electrochemical pseudocapacitance.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials
Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: African Literature
data.description: Literature from Africa, either oral or written. Includes both literary works written in African and Afro-Asiatic languages, as well as literature written in other languages (Anglophone, Francophone) by African writers and works in translation.

subjects.term: Literature for and by other groups of people--Africa

data.name: Cities, Countries, Regions
data.description: Cities, countries, and regions are geographic entities that play important roles in various contexts, including social, political, economic, and cultural spheres. These terms reflect the diversity of geographical divisions and administrative units across the world. Cities serve as centers of commerce, governance, and cultural exchange, while countries and regions encompass broader territorial boundaries and encompass various cities and rural areas. These entities have distinct identities, histories, and characteristics that shape their social, political, and economic dynamics.

subjects.term: Architecture in relation to special subjects
City and town planning: architectural aspects

data.name: Molecular Self-assembly
data.description: Molecular self-assembly is the spontaneous association of molecules, through non covalent bonds and under equilibrium conditions, into stable, structurally well-defined aggregates.

data.name: Abstract Harmonic Analysis
data.description: Harmonic analysis is a branch of mathematics concerned with the representation of functions or signals as the superposition of basic waves, and the study of and generalization of the notions of Fourier series and Fourier transforms.

data.name: Mobile and Network Security
data.description: set of technologies that protects the usability and integrity of a company's infrastructure by preventing the entry or proliferation within a network of a wide variety of potential threats.

data.name: Medical Biochemistry
data.description: Medical Biochemistry is the application of biochemical principles to the understanding, diagnosis, and treatment of human diseases. It focuses on the biochemical basis of pathology, clinical biomarkers, metabolic disorders, molecular diagnostics, and therapeutic interventions relevant to human health. The field supports clinical decision‑making through biochemical diagnostics, laboratory testing, and the interpretation of molecular and metabolic abnormalities in patients.

data.name: Imaging Techniques
data.description: Imaging techniques are used to obtain a two-dimensional depiction of a surface or a three-dimensional reconstruction of a volume.

subjects.term: Properties of materials and nondestructive testing

data.name: Non-parametric Inference
data.description: statistical techniques that use data to infer unknown quantities of interest while making as few assumptions as possible

data.name: Literature and Pedagogy
data.description: A pedagogical literature review is a synthesis of what has been published by scholars and researchers on some aspect of teaching and learning.

data.name: Laser Technology

data.name: Organization

The ultimate goal of organizational research is to identify ways to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of organizations. Some of the major topics in organizational research include: Organizational behavior: This involves the study of how individuals, groups, and structures within an organization interact with each other. Topics in organizational behavior include motivation, communication, power, conflict, and leadership. Organizational culture: This involves the study of the values, beliefs, and norms that shape the behavior of individuals within an organization. Topics in organizational culture include the role of rituals and symbols, cultural diversity, and the impact of culture on organizational performance. Human resource management: This involves the study of how organizations manage their employees, including recruitment, training, performance appraisal, and compensation. Topics in human resource management include diversity, employee engagement, and the impact of HR practices on organizational performance. Organizational structure and design: This involves the study of how organizations are structured and designed to achieve their goals. Topics in organizational structure and design include organizational size and complexity, formalization, centralization, and decentralization. Strategic management: This involves the study of how organizations develop and implement strategies to achieve their goals. Topics in strategic management include competitive advantage, innovation, and corporate social responsibility. Organizational change and development: This involves the study of how organizations adapt to changing environments and improve their performance over time. Topics in organizational change and development include organizational learning, change management, and innovation.

Human resource management: How can small businesses attract and retain talented employees, and build effective teams that support business growth? Small business management refers to the process of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling resources (including people, finances, and operations) in a small business setting to achieve specific goals and objectives. That system includes national governments, their governmental and intergovernmental organizations as well as government-independent elements of global civil society such as international non-governmental organizations and social movement organizations. data.name: Family Business
data.description: Family Business is a field of research that focuses on the unique characteristics and dynamics of businesses that are owned and operated by families. It involves the study of the intersection between family and business systems, and the ways in which these systems influence the performance, management, and governance of family-owned businesses.  In family business research, scholars and practitioners study a wide range of topics, including:  Family dynamics: How do family dynamics, such as family roles, power structures, and communication patterns, affect the performance and management of family-owned businesses?  Succession planning: How do family-owned businesses plan for the transition of leadership and ownership from one generation to the next, and what factors influence the success or failure of these transitions?  Governance and management: What are the best practices for governance and management in family-owned businesses, and how can families balance the needs of the business with the needs of the family?  Inter-generational entrepreneurship: What are the factors that influence the success or failure of inter-generational entrepreneurship within family-owned businesses?  Family business financing: What are the unique financing challenges faced by family-owned businesses, and how can they access the funding they need to grow and succeed?  Overall, family business research seeks to understand the complex interplay between family and business systems in family-owned businesses, and to develop practical recommendations for families and practitioners to improve the performance, management, and governance of these businesses.

data.name: Supply Chain Management
data.description: Supply chain management (SCM) is the strategic coordination of all activities involved in the sourcing, procurement, conversion, and logistics management of goods and services. It encompasses the planning and management of all activities involved in the movement and transformation of raw materials into finished goods and their delivery to the end customer.  SCM involves the integration of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, and retailers, and the coordination of their activities to optimize the overall supply chain performance. The goal of SCM is to maximize customer value while minimizing costs and improving efficiency and effectiveness.  Key activities involved in SCM include inventory management, transportation and logistics management, demand planning and forecasting, supplier management, and order fulfillment. SCM also involves the use of technology and data analytics to streamline processes and improve decision-making.  Effective supply chain management is critical to the success of any organization, as it can lead to increased competitiveness, improved customer satisfaction, and reduced costs. As a result, it is an important area of study within management research, with a focus on developing new strategies, tools, and techniques to improve supply chain performance.

data.name: Quantum Electrodynamics, Relativistic and Many-body Calculations
data.description: In particle physics, quantum electrodynamics (QED) is the relativistic quantum field theory of electrodynamics. In essence, it describes how light and matter interact and is the first theory where full agreement between quantum mechanics and special relativity is achieved. QED mathematically describes all phenomena involving electrically charged particles interacting by means of exchange of photons and represents the quantum counterpart of classical electromagnetism giving a complete account of matter and light interaction.  In technical terms, QED can be described as a perturbation theory of the electromagnetic quantum vacuum. Richard Feynman called it "the jewel of physics" for its extremely accurate predictions of quantities like the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron and the Lamb shift of the energy levels of hydrogen.

data.name: Corporate Governance
data.description: Corporate governance refers to the set of processes, principles, and policies that govern the way a company is directed, managed, and controlled. It involves the relationships between a company's management, its board of directors, shareholders, and other stakeholders. In research, corporate governance involves the study of the structures, mechanisms, and practices that promote transparency, accountability, and ethical behavior in companies. The field of corporate governance research covers a wide range of topics, including board composition, executive compensation, shareholder rights, and corporate social responsibility. Board composition refers to the selection and makeup of a company's board of directors, including the number of independent directors and their qualifications and experience. Executive compensation involves the design and implementation of compensation packages for top executives, including salaries, bonuses, and stock options. Shareholder rights refer to the rights and protections afforded to shareholders, such as the right to vote on corporate decisions and the right to access information about the company. Corporate social responsibility involves a company's ethical and social obligations to its stakeholders, including its employees, customers, and the wider community. In practice, corporate governance involves the implementation of policies and procedures to ensure that a company operates in an ethical and transparent manner, and that its management is held accountable for its actions. This includes establishing clear lines of authority and decision-making, setting appropriate standards for behavior and performance, and ensuring that the company complies with all relevant laws and regulations. Corporate governance is essential for the long-term success and sustainability of a company. By promoting accountability and transparency, it helps to build trust and confidence among stakeholders, which can lead to improved financial performance and reputation. Effective corporate governance also helps to mitigate risks and prevent conflicts of interest, ensuring that the company operates in the best interests of its stakeholders.

data.name: Big Data
data.description: Big Data is a field of business and management research and practice that focuses on the collection, storage, processing, analysis, and interpretation of large and complex data sets generated by organizations, individuals, and machines. It involves the use of advanced technologies, statistical methods, and computational techniques to extract insights and value from these data sets. Some of the major topics in Big Data include: Data management: This includes the storage, retrieval, and processing of large data sets using various technologies such as Hadoop, NoSQL, and cloud computing. Data analytics: This involves the use of statistical methods and machine learning algorithms to analyze and extract insights from large data sets. Data visualization: This includes the creation of graphical representations of data to help users understand and interpret complex data sets. Data privacy and security: This topic deals with the protection of sensitive data from unauthorized access, use, and disclosure. Business intelligence: This involves the use of Big Data to support business decision-making by providing insights into customer behavior, market trends, and other relevant information. Data governance: This includes the development and implementation of policies, procedures, and standards for the management and use of data within organizations. Social media analytics: This involves the analysis of social media data to understand user behavior, preferences, and opinions. Internet of Things (IoT): This topic deals with the collection and analysis of data generated by connected devices and sensors. Predictive modeling: This involves the use of data to create models that can predict future events or behaviors. Data ethics: This topic deals with the ethical and moral considerations surrounding the collection, use, and analysis of data.

data.name: Entrepreneurial Finance
data.description: Entrepreneurial finance refers to the financial activities and decisions involved in starting and growing a new venture. In research and practice, it is a subfield of finance that focuses specifically on the unique challenges and opportunities of financing new businesses. Entrepreneurial finance involves a wide range of activities and decisions, including: Raising capital: Entrepreneurs need to raise capital to start and grow their businesses. This may involve seeking funding from friends and family, angel investors, venture capitalists, or other sources of financing. Financial planning and forecasting: Entrepreneurs must develop financial plans and forecasts that outline their business goals and projections for revenue, expenses, and cash flow. Capital structure decisions: Entrepreneurs must make decisions about the mix of debt and equity financing they will use to fund their businesses, as well as the terms of these financing arrangements. Managing risk: Entrepreneurs face a wide range of financial risks, including market risk, credit risk, and operational risk. They must develop strategies to manage these risks and ensure the financial stability of their businesses. By understanding the unique financial challenges and opportunities of entrepreneurship, entrepreneurs and investors can make informed decisions that increase the chances of success.

data.name: Criminology in the Global South

data.name: Emotional Development

Emotional development encompasses various aspects, including the experience and expression of emotions, the understanding of emotional cues and social context, and the regulation of emotions in adaptive and healthy ways. This process is influenced by a combination of genetic, biological, cognitive, and environmental factors, and it plays a vital role in shaping individuals' emotional well-being, social relationships, and overall psychological functioning.

data.name: Physical Development

It encompasses various aspects, including changes in body size and proportion, motor skills, sensory abilities, and overall physical health. Physical development starts during prenatal development and continues throughout infancy, childhood, adolescence, and into adulthood. It is influenced by a combination of genetic factors, environmental influences, nutrition, physical activity, and overall health status. Physical development involves the maturation and growth of organs, bones, muscles, and the development of coordination, balance, strength, and motor skills. It also includes the development of sensory systems, such as vision, hearing, taste, touch, and smell. Physical development plays a crucial role in shaping an individual's overall well-being, self-concept, and interaction with the surrounding environment.

data.name: Financial Technology and Innovation
data.description: Financial technology, or fintech, refers to the use of technology to improve and automate financial services and transactions. Fintech companies use innovative technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to provide new financial services or improve existing ones. In research and practice, fintech and innovation involve a range of activities and tasks, including:  Development of new financial products and services: Fintech companies are constantly developing new financial products and services, such as mobile payments, robo-advisors, and peer-to-peer lending platforms, that offer more convenience, accessibility, and affordability than traditional financial services.  Improving financial processes: Fintech companies are also focused on improving financial processes such as underwriting, credit scoring, and fraud detection, by leveraging advanced data analytics and machine learning algorithms.  Enhancing customer experience: Fintech companies use digital channels and user-friendly interfaces to provide a seamless and personalized customer experience, which is a key differentiator in the competitive financial services market.  Increasing financial inclusion: Fintech companies are also focused on increasing financial inclusion, by providing financial services to underserved and unbanked populations, and by offering more affordable and accessible financial services to low-income individuals and small businesses.  Overall, the goal of fintech and innovation is to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and affordability of financial services, and to drive innovation and competition in the financial services industry. In practice, fintech and innovation are transforming the financial services industry, by disrupting traditional business models and creating new opportunities for growth and profitability.

data.name: Fibre Optics
data.description: Fibre optics and optical communications is the use of thin strands of glass for sending information encoded into light over long distances. Total internal reflection prevents light inserted into one end of the fibre from escaping through the sides. Transferring information optically in this way enables much higher transmission rates than using an electrical signal..Optical fibres are flexible, transparent fibers made by drawing glass (silica) or plastic. They are used most often as a means to transmit light between the two ends of the fiber and find wide usage in fiber-optic communications, where they permit transmission over longer distances and at higher bandwidths than electrical cables. Fibers are used instead of metal wires because signals travel along them with less loss; in addition, fibers are immune to electromagnetic interference, a problem from which metal wires suffer excessively. Fibers are also used for illumination and imaging, and are often wrapped in bundles so they may be used to carry light into, or images out of confined spaces, as in the case of a fiberscope. Specially designed fibers are also used for a variety of other applications, some of them being fiber optic sensors and fiber lasers.

data.name: Mergers and Acquisitions
data.description: Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) refer to the process of combining two or more companies to form a new entity or to acquire another company, respectively. In research and practice, M&A involves a range of activities and tasks, including:  Strategic planning: This involves identifying potential acquisition targets or merger partners, evaluating the strategic fit, and developing a strategy for the M&A transaction.  Due diligence: This involves conducting a thorough investigation of the target company's financial, legal, operational, and strategic aspects to identify any potential risks, liabilities, or opportunities associated with the transaction.  Valuation: This involves assessing the value of the target company, using various methods such as discounted cash flow analysis, comparable company analysis, or precedent transactions analysis, to determine the purchase price or exchange ratio for the transaction.  Negotiation and structuring: This involves negotiating the terms and conditions of the transaction, such as the purchase price, payment method, and post-merger management structure, and structuring the deal to minimize risks and maximize synergies.  Integration planning and execution: This involves planning and executing the integration of the two companies, including aligning business processes and systems, integrating cultures and management teams, and realizing synergies and cost savings.  Overall, the goal of M&A is to create value for the shareholders of the acquiring company, by expanding the business, entering new markets, or achieving cost savings through economies of scale. In practice, M&A is used by a range of organizations, including corporations, private equity firms, and investment banks, to achieve their strategic objectives and grow their businesses.

data.name: Financial Law
data.description: Financial law is a field of study and practice that encompasses the laws and regulations governing financial transactions and institutions. It includes a wide range of legal topics, such as banking law, securities regulation, insurance law, and tax law. In research, financial law involves the study and development of legal theories and principles to improve the regulation and practice of financial activities. The field of financial law research covers a wide range of topics, including the impact of financial regulations on the stability and efficiency of financial markets, the development of new legal frameworks for emerging financial practices, and the role of international financial law in regulating cross-border transactions. Banking law refers to the laws and regulations governing the operation of banks and other financial institutions, such as deposit insurance, lending practices, and consumer protection. Securities regulation refers to the laws and regulations governing the issuance, trading, and reporting of securities, such as stocks, bonds, and mutual funds. Insurance law governs the regulation and supervision of insurance companies and the protection of policyholders. Tax law refers to the laws and regulations governing the assessment and collection of taxes, such as income tax, corporate tax, and value-added tax (VAT). Financial law also encompasses international financial law, which deals with the regulation of cross-border financial transactions and the resolution of international financial disputes. In practice, financial law involves the application of legal principles and regulations to financial transactions and institutions, such as the formation and operation of banks and financial companies, the issuance and trading of securities, and the taxation of financial transactions. Financial law also involves the compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, such as anti-money laundering laws, securities disclosure requirements, and tax reporting obligations. Financial law is essential for the proper functioning of financial markets and the economy as a whole. By providing a legal framework for financial transactions and institutions, it helps to ensure the stability, efficiency, and integrity of financial systems, protect the interests of investors and consumers, and promote economic growth and development.

data.name: Investment Appraisal
data.description: Investment appraisal, also known as capital budgeting, refers to the process of evaluating and selecting long-term investment projects or proposals, based on their potential to generate returns or create value for the organization. In research and practice, investment appraisal involves a range of techniques and methods for analyzing and evaluating investment opportunities, including: Net present value (NPV) analysis: This involves calculating the present value of the expected cash flows generated by the investment, and subtracting the initial investment cost. If the NPV is positive, the investment is considered viable. Internal rate of return (IRR) analysis: This involves calculating the rate of return that the investment is expected to generate, based on the expected cash flows. If the IRR is higher than the organization's cost of capital, the investment is considered viable. Payback period analysis: This involves calculating the length of time it will take for the investment to generate enough cash flows to recover the initial investment cost. If the payback period is shorter than the organization's investment horizon, the investment is considered viable. Sensitivity analysis: This involves testing the impact of changes in key assumptions, such as sales volumes, costs, or discount rates, on the viability of the investment. Risk analysis: This involves assessing the risk associated with the investment, such as market risk, financial risk, or operational risk, and incorporating this into the investment appraisal. Overall, the goal of investment appraisal is to identify and evaluate long-term investment opportunities that have the potential to create value for the organization, while managing financial risk and ensuring that the investment is aligned with the organization's strategic objectives. In practice, investment appraisal is used by a range of organizations, including corporations, governments, and nonprofit organizations, to allocate their resources and make investment decisions.

These countries are characterized by a rising middle class, a growing consumer market, and increasing foreign investment. In the field of management research and practice, the study of emerging markets focuses on understanding the unique challenges and opportunities of doing business in these countries. Some of the major topics in this field include:  Entry modes: The various ways in which firms can enter and establish themselves in emerging markets, such as through joint ventures, acquisitions, or greenfield investments.  Institutional voids: The absence or inadequacy of formal institutions such as legal systems, property rights, and regulatory frameworks, which can make it difficult for firms to operate effectively in emerging markets.  Cultural differences: The differences in language, norms, values, and beliefs that can affect communication, relationships, and business practices in emerging markets.  Political risk: The risks associated with political instability, corruption, and government intervention in emerging markets.  Innovation: The ways in which firms can innovate and adapt their business models to meet the unique needs and preferences of emerging market consumers.  Globalization:  Globalization refers to the increasing interconnectedness and interdependence of the world's economies, societies, and cultures. In the field of management research and practice, the study of globalization focuses on understanding the challenges and opportunities of managing businesses in a globalized world. Some of the major topics in this field include:  Global strategy: The ways in which firms can create and implement strategies that enable them to compete effectively in global markets.  Global supply chains: The management of global supply chains, which involve the sourcing, production, and distribution of goods and services across multiple countries and regions.  Cultural diversity: The ways in which cultural differences can affect communication, decision-making, and leadership in global organizations.  Ethical issues: The ethical considerations that arise when doing business across different cultures and jurisdictions, such as human rights, environmental sustainability, and corruption.  Technological innovation: The role of technology in facilitating global communication, collaboration, and innovation, as well as the risks and opportunities associated with emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and blockchain. Business, Management and Organizational topics specially in reference to the Emerging Market Group (IMF classification) countries: Argentina, Brazil, Chile, China, Colombia, Egypt, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Iran, Malaysia, Mexico, the Philippines, Poland, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Thailand, Turkey, and the United Arab Emirates.

data.name: Vision and Colour Science
data.description: Vision and color science is a multidisciplinary field that encompasses the study of human vision, the perception of color, and the underlying physiological, psychological, and physical processes involved. It investigates how light interacts with the visual system, how the brain processes visual information, and how colors are perceived and interpreted.

synonyms: Wissenschaft des Sehens und der Farbe

data.name: African Business
data.description: African Business is a field of management research and practice that focuses on understanding the unique challenges and opportunities of doing business in Africa. It involves studying the various economic, social, cultural, and political factors that affect business operations in the continent. Some of the major topics in African Business include: Market entry strategies: exploring the different ways companies can enter the African market and the challenges they may face in doing so.  Political and legal environment: examining the legal and regulatory frameworks of different African countries and how they impact business operations. Entrepreneurship and innovation: exploring the role of entrepreneurship and innovation in driving economic growth and development in Africa. Corporate social responsibility: studying the ways in which businesses can engage with local communities and contribute to social and environmental sustainability. Human resource management: examining the challenges of recruiting, training, and retaining skilled workers in Africa. Infrastructure and logistics: exploring the challenges of managing supply chains, transportation, and infrastructure in the continent. Emerging markets and sectors: examining the opportunities and challenges presented by emerging sectors and markets, such as fintech, e-commerce, and renewable energy. Cross-cultural management: studying the cultural differences that affect business operations in Africa and how companies can effectively manage cultural diversity. International trade and investment: examining the ways in which African countries engage in international trade and investment and how businesses can navigate these relationships. Economic development and growth: exploring the drivers of economic growth and development in Africa and the role of businesses in promoting sustainable development.

data.name: Indian Religions
data.description: Indian religions, sometimes also termed Dharmic religions or Indic religions, are the religions that originated in the Indian subcontinent. These religions, which include Hinduism, Jainism, Buddhism, and Sikhism, are also classified as Eastern religions. Although Indian religions are connected through the history of India, they constitute a wide range of religious communities, and are not confined to the Indian subcontinent.

data.name: Continuous Optimization
data.description: As opposed to discrete optimization, the variables used in the objective function are required to be continuous variables—that is, to be chosen from a set of real values between which there are no gaps (values from intervals of the real line). Because of this continuity assumption, continuous optimization allows the use of calculus techniques.

data.name: Therapeutic Relationship
data.description: A therapeutic relationship is a professional and collaborative relationship between a therapist and a client with the goal of promoting the client's well-being and addressing their psychological concerns. It involves building trust, empathy, and rapport between the therapist and the client, as well as maintaining clear boundaries and mutual respect. The therapeutic relationship is a crucial aspect of therapy, as it provides a safe and supportive environment for the client to explore and work through their issues.

data.name: Financial Reporting
data.description: Define "Financial Reporting" as in research and practice Financial reporting refers to the process of communicating a company's financial information to external users, such as investors, creditors, and regulatory agencies. Financial reporting includes the preparation and presentation of financial statements, such as the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement, as well as other disclosures about a company's financial position, performance, and cash flows.  In research, financial reporting involves the development and testing of accounting theories and principles to improve the accuracy, reliability, and relevance of financial information. The field of financial reporting research covers a wide range of topics, including the impact of accounting standards and regulations, the role of financial analysts, and the use of financial statement analysis in investment decisions.  Accounting standards and regulations refer to the rules and principles that guide the preparation and presentation of financial statements, such as the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) in the United States. Financial reporting research focuses on the impact of these standards on the quality and comparability of financial information.  Financial analysts play a crucial role in the interpretation and analysis of financial information. Financial reporting research examines the role of financial analysts in the financial reporting process, as well as the factors that influence their behavior and decision-making.  In practice, financial reporting involves the preparation and presentation of financial statements and other disclosures in accordance with accounting standards and regulations. Financial reporting is a key part of corporate reporting and is essential for the transparency and accountability of companies. Financial information is used by investors, creditors, and other stakeholders to make informed decisions about investing, lending, and other financial activities.

subjects.term: Balance sheet. Financial statements. Corporation reports

data.name: Eastern Orthodoxy
data.description: Eastern Orthodoxy, also known as Eastern Orthodox Christianity, is one of the three main branches of Chalcedonian Christianity, alongside Catholicism and Protestantism. Like the Pentarchy of the first millennium, the mainstream (or "canonical") Eastern Orthodox Church is organised into autocephalous churches independent from each other. In the 21st century, the number of mainstream autocephalous churches is seventeen; there also exist autocephalous churches unrecognized by those mainstream ones. Autocephalous churches choose their own primate. Autocephalous churches can have jurisdiction (authority) over other churches, some of which have the status of "autonomous" which means they have more autonomy than simple eparchies.

data.name: Project Management
data.description: Project management is the process of planning, executing, monitoring, and controlling the work of a team to achieve specific goals and objectives within a defined timeline and budget. It involves applying knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to manage project activities effectively and efficiently. The major components of project management are: Project Scope: The objectives, deliverables, and requirements that define the project's boundaries. Project Schedule: The timeline for completing the project, including specific deadlines for milestones and deliverables. Project Budget: The estimated cost of resources needed to complete the project, including personnel, equipment, and materials. Project Team: The group of individuals responsible for completing the project. Project Communication: The process of sharing information with stakeholders and team members to ensure everyone is aware of project status, changes, and expectations. Project Risk Management: The process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential risks that could impact the project's success. Major methodologies and standards used in project management include: Agile: An iterative approach to project management that emphasizes flexibility and collaboration among team members. Waterfall: A linear approach to project management that involves completing tasks in a sequential manner, with each phase dependent on the completion of the previous one. Scrum: An Agile framework for managing and completing complex projects by breaking them down into smaller, more manageable tasks. Lean: A methodology that focuses on maximizing value while minimizing waste, by streamlining processes and eliminating unnecessary steps. PRINCE2: A process-based project management methodology that emphasizes control, governance, and risk management. PMBOK: The Project Management Body of Knowledge, developed by the Project Management Institute (PMI), is a collection of best practices and guidelines for project management.

data.name: Peace Psychology
data.description: Peace psychology is a subfield of psychology that focuses on understanding the causes of violence and promoting peaceful conflict resolution. It is concerned with the psychological factors that contribute to peace, such as attitudes, beliefs, emotions, and behaviors, as well as the psychological impact of war, terrorism, and other forms of violence on individuals and societies. Peace psychology seeks to develop theories and interventions to promote peace and prevent violence, and it draws on multiple disciplines such as social psychology, political science, sociology, and anthropology to inform its research and practice.

data.name: Normative Ethics

data.name: Economic Aspects of Globalization
data.description: Economic globalization refers to the increasing interdependence of world economies as a result of the growing scale of cross-border trade of commodities and services, flow of international capital and wide and rapid spread of technologies. In general, globalization decreases the cost of manufacturing. This means that companies can offer goods at a lower price to consumers. The average cost of goods is a key aspect that contributes to increases in the standard of living. Consumers also have access to a wider variety of goods. The characteristic elements that constitute economic globalization are cross-border flows of goods and services, capital, people, data and ideas

data.name: Motor Skills Development
data.description: Motor skills development, in the field of psychology, refers to the progressive acquisition and refinement of physical movements and abilities that involve the coordination of muscles and body parts. It encompasses both gross motor skills, which involve larger muscle groups and whole-body movements, and fine motor skills, which involve precise and coordinated movements of smaller muscle groups, often in the hands and fingers. Motor skills development is a dynamic process that begins in infancy and continues throughout childhood and into adulthood.

data.name: Exotic Atoms
data.description: Exotic atoms and molecules are forms of basic matter in which one subatomic particle is replaced by another with the same charge. data.name: Tourism Management
data.description: Tourism management is a field within business and management that focuses on managing and developing tourism-related businesses, destinations, and activities. It involves studying and applying strategies to enhance the economic, social, and environmental benefits of tourism. Core topics in tourism management include: Destination management: the planning and management of tourism destinations, including marketing, infrastructure development, and environmental sustainability. Tourism marketing: developing and implementing marketing strategies to promote tourism products and destinations. Hospitality management: managing hotels, resorts, and other hospitality businesses, including customer service, operations, and revenue management. Sustainable tourism: promoting tourism that minimizes negative impacts on the environment and local communities and maximizes positive economic and social benefits.  Cultural tourism: developing and promoting tourism that celebrates local culture, traditions, and heiitage. Tourism economics: analyzing the economic impacts of tourism, including job creation, income generation, and regional development. Tourism policy and planning: developing policies and plans to guide tourism development and management at the local, regional, and national levels. Tourist behavior and experience: understanding tourist motivations, preferences, and behaviors to improve the tourism experience and develop more targeted marketing strategies. Tourism innovation and entrepreneurship: developing new tourism products and services and promoting entrepreneurship and innovation within the tourism industry.

data.name: Islamic Cultural Studies

The early forms of Muslim culture, from the Rashidun Caliphate to the early Umayyad period and the early Abbasid period, were predominantly Arab, Byzantine, and Persian. With the rapid expansion of the Islamic empires, Muslim culture has influenced and assimilated much from the Persian, North Caucasian, Turkic, Mongol, Indian, Bangladeshi, Pakistani, Malay, Somali, Berber, Indonesian, and Moro cultures.  Islamic culture generally includes all of the practices which have developed around the religion of Islam. There are variations in the application of Islamic beliefs in different cultures and traditions.

data.name: Matter-Antimatter Interactions
data.description: In modern physics, antimatter is defined as matter that is composed of the antiparticles (or "partners") of the corresponding particles of "ordinary" matter. Theoretically, a particle and its anti-particle (for example, a proton and an antiproton) have the same mass, but opposite electric charge, and other differences in quantum numbers. A collision between any particle and its anti-particle partner leads to their mutual annihilation, giving rise to various proportions of intense photons (gamma rays), neutrinos, and sometimes less-massive particle–antiparticle pairs.

data.name: Plasma Medicine
data.description: Plasma medicine is an emerging field that combines plasma physics, life sciences and clinical medicine. It is being studied in disinfection, healing, and cancer. Most of the research is in vitro and in animal models.It uses ionized gas for medical uses or dental applications. Plasma, often called the fourth state of matter, is an ionized gas containing positive ions and negative ions or electrons, but is approximately charge neutral on the whole. The plasma sources used for plasma medicine are generally low temperature plasmas, and they generate ions, chemically reactive atoms and molecules, and UV-photons. These plasma-generated active species are useful for several bio-medical applications such as sterilization of implants and surgical instruments as well as modifying biomaterial surface properties.

data.name: Cross-Cultural Management
data.description: Cross-cultural management is a field of management research and practice that focuses on managing the differences and similarities between people from different cultural backgrounds in organizations. It involves understanding how culture affects organizational behavior, and how to effectively manage and leverage cultural differences to enhance organizational performance. Some of the major topics in cross-cultural management include: Cultural dimensions and their impact on management: This topic explores the various dimensions of culture, such as individualism vs. collectivism, power distance, and uncertainty avoidance, and how they influence management practices and decision-making in different cultural contexts. Cross-cultural communication: Effective communication is essential for managing cultural diversity in organizations. This topic examines the challenges and strategies for communicating across cultural boundaries, including verbal and non-verbal communication, language barriers, and cultural norms and expectations. Cross-cultural negotiation and conflict resolution: Differences in values, beliefs, and communication styles can lead to misunderstandings and conflicts in cross-cultural contexts. This topic focuses on developing negotiation and conflict resolution skills that are effective in multicultural environments. Cross-cultural leadership: Leadership styles and behaviors that are effective in one cultural context may not be effective in another. This topic explores the different approaches to leadership across cultures and how to adapt leadership styles to effectively manage a culturally diverse workforce. Managing diversity: Diversity in the workplace is an important issue in cross-cultural management. This topic examines the challenges and benefits of managing a diverse workforce, including issues related to recruitment, retention, and promotion of employees from different cultural backgrounds.

data.name: Anthropology of Education
data.description: Educational anthropology, or the anthropology of education, is a sub-field of anthropology and is widely associated with the pioneering work of Margaret Mead and later, George Spindler, Solon Kimball, and Dell Hymes, and Jean Lave. As the name would suggest, the focus of educational anthropology is on education, although an anthropological approach to education tends to focus on the cultural aspects of education, including informal as well as formal education.

data.name: History of Computing
data.description: The History of Computing involves the history of computing hardware technologies and computer software, the history of the ideas that support computational and information science approaches, and the history of the key actors in these developments such as people, organizations, and communities.

data.name: Financial Accounting
data.description: Financial accounting is a field of study and practice that involves the recording, summarizing, and reporting of a company's financial transactions and activities. It provides information about a company's financial position, performance, and cash flows to external users, such as investors, creditors, and regulatory agencies.  In research, financial accounting involves the development and testing of accounting theories and principles to improve the accuracy and relevance of financial reporting. The field of financial accounting research covers a wide range of topics, including financial statement analysis, valuation, accounting standards, and corporate disclosure.  Financial statement analysis involves the use of financial ratios and other tools to analyze a company's financial statements, such as the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement. Valuation involves the use of financial models to estimate the value of a company's assets, liabilities, and equity.  Accounting standards refer to the rules and principles that guide the preparation and presentation of financial statements, such as the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) in the United States. Corporate disclosure involves the communication of financial information to stakeholders, such as through annual reports, earnings releases, and other regulatory filings.  In practice, financial accounting involves the preparation and presentation of financial statements in accordance with accounting standards and regulations. This includes recording and summarizing financial transactions, preparing financial statements, and ensuring that financial information is accurate, complete, and reliable.  Financial accounting is essential for businesses, as it provides information about a company's financial position and performance to external users. This information is used by investors, creditors, and other stakeholders to make informed decisions about investing, lending, and other financial activities. Financial accounting also helps to ensure transparency and accountability in corporate reporting, which can promote trust and confidence among stakeholders.

Eastern philosophy is characterized by its holistic and experiential approach to understanding the nature of reality, the self, and the pursuit of wisdom. It often emphasizes introspection, meditation, mindfulness, and the cultivation of inner awareness as means to gain insight and transcendence.

data.name: Consumer Behavior
data.description: Consumer behavior refers to the study of individuals, groups, or organizations and the processes they use to select, secure, use, and dispose of products, services, experiences, or ideas to satisfy their needs and desires. It is a crucial area of research for management as it helps companies understand their customers better and develop marketing strategies to meet their needs effectively.  Consumer behavior research involves analyzing various factors that influence consumers' buying decisions, including their psychological, social, cultural, and economic factors. It helps companies understand the motivations, attitudes, and preferences of their customers and how these factors influence their buying decisions.  By understanding consumer behavior, companies can create products and services that better meet their customers' needs, develop effective marketing campaigns, and build stronger relationships with their customers. It also helps companies identify potential new markets and opportunities for growth.

The difference in mass between the reactants and products is manifested as either the release or absorption of energy. This difference in mass arises due to the difference in atomic "binding energy" between the atomic nuclei before and after the reaction.

Media planning often involves working with media buyers and vendors to negotiate pricing and placement of advertisements across various media platforms, such as television, radio, print, digital, and social media. The goal of media planning is to develop a comprehensive media strategy that maximizes the impact of advertising and marketing efforts while minimizing costs.  In management research, media planning is often studied as a way to understand how organizations can effectively allocate resources towards advertising and marketing initiatives, and how they can measure the impact of these initiatives on overall business performance. Researchers may investigate the effectiveness of different media channels, the role of audience targeting and segmentation, and the use of metrics to measure advertising effectiveness and return on investment.

data.name: Procurement
data.description: Procurement and purchasing are both important functions in management research related to the acquisition of goods and services needed for a company's operations. However, they are not interchangeable terms, and they have different meanings and scopes of responsibilities.  Procurement refers to the entire process of acquiring goods and services, from identifying the need for them to the final delivery and payment. It includes all the activities involved in selecting suppliers, negotiating contracts, and managing the relationships with them to ensure that the company's needs are met efficiently and effectively. Procurement involves strategic decision-making to optimize the cost, quality, and timeliness of the acquisitions and to ensure compliance with regulations and ethical standards.  Purchasing, on the other hand, is a subset of procurement that focuses on the actual transaction of buying goods and services. It is the act of placing orders, issuing purchase orders, receiving and inspecting the goods or services, and making payment. Purchasing is a more operational and tactical activity that executes the procurement strategy and ensures that the purchases align with the company's needs and policies.  Overall, procurement is a broader term that encompasses purchasing, but also includes many other activities that are essential for effective supply chain management, such as sourcing, supplier evaluation, contract management, risk management, and performance monitoring. In contrast, purchasing is a more specific term that refers to the transactional aspects of acquiring goods and services.

data.name: Microresonators

This creates a series of standing-wave optical modes, or resonances, similar to those that can exist on a vibrating guitar string. Microresonators can provide the optical feedback required in semiconductor lasers.
