data.description: Data processing is a set of methods that are used to input, retrieve, verify, store, organize, analyse or interpret a set of data. Data processing enables information to be automatically extracted from data, and could be used in computational biology and bioinformatics to organise a large set of 'omics data.

data.name: Business Information Systems
data.description: Business Information Systems (BIS) is a field of study that focuses on the effective and efficient use of technology and information systems to support the operations, management, and decision-making processes of businesses. BIS combines elements of computer science, management science, and business administration to develop and implement systems that improve business performance.  Some of the major topics in BIS include:  Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP): ERP systems integrate and automate key business processes, such as accounting, inventory management, and customer relationship management.  Customer Relationship Management (CRM): CRM systems are used to manage customer interactions and improve customer satisfaction and loyalty.  Supply Chain Management (SCM): SCM systems optimize the flow of materials, information, and finances across the supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs.  Business Intelligence and Analytics: BIS helps businesses to collect and analyze data to support decision-making processes.  E-commerce: E-commerce systems enable businesses to conduct transactions online and reach a global audience.  Knowledge Management: Knowledge management systems help businesses to capture, store, and share knowledge and expertise within the organization.  Cybersecurity: BIS focuses on the protection of business information systems from cyber threats, such as hacking and data breaches.  Overall, BIS aims to align technology with business goals and objectives to create a competitive advantage for the organization.

data.name: Archaeal Evolution
data.description: Archaeal evolution is the process by which the domain of organisms called archaea has developed over multiple generations. This process can be studied by phylogenetics and such studies show that Archaea have a distinct evolutionary history from bacteria and eukaryotes.

data.name: Musculoskeletal Development
data.description: Musculoskeletal development refers to the processes by which the skeletal muscles, bone and cartilage of the body form, mainly from the embryonic mesoderm. Understanding musculoskeletal development helps in the understanding of congenital musculoskeletal disorders.

data.name: Literature and Cultural Studies
data.description: Literature and cultural studies are interconnected fields that examine and analyze the relationship between literature and culture. While literature focuses on the study of written works, cultural studies explore broader cultural phenomena and social practices. Literature studies involve the analysis and interpretation of literary texts, including novels, poetry, plays, and essays. Cultural studies analyze and interpret cultural artifacts, practices, and phenomena, such as art, media, film, music, fashion, and popular culture.

data.name: Adult Stem Cells
data.description: Adult stem cells are cells in the adult that can both self-renew by dividing and give rise to more specialised cell types present in the tissue in which they reside. They serve to maintain and repair the tissue.

data.name: Global South and STS
data.description: Global South and STS (Science and Technology Studies) is an interdisciplinary area of study that focuses on the relationships between science, technology, and society in the Global South, which includes developing and emerging countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. It seeks to understand the ways in which science and technology are shaped by and impact socioeconomic, political, and cultural factors in these regions.

synonyms: Science technology and society in the Global South

data.name: Synaptic Transmission
data.description: Synaptic transmission is the biological process by which a neuron communicates with a target cell across a synapse. Chemical synaptic transmission involves the release of a neurotransmitter from the pre-synaptic neuron, and neurotransmitter binding to specific post-synaptic receptors. Electrical synapse transmission involves the transfer of electrical signals through gap junctions.

data.name: Hydrogeology
data.description: Hydrogeology is the study of the movement and storage of water in the crust of Earth and other rocky planetary bodies. It maps and quantifies the water stored in underground aquifers and occasionally surface systems, identifies pathways of flow and recharge, and assesses the chemical composition and quality of the below-ground water.

data.name: Electrophysiology
data.description: Electrophysiology is the measurement and characterization of the electrical properties of cells and tissues, particularly neurons and neuronal tissue.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Life Sciences / Anatomy & Physiology (see also Life Sciences / Human Anatomy & Physiology)

data.name: Biomarkers
data.description: A biomarker is a biological characteristic that is objectively measured and evaluated as an indicator of normal biological or pathological processes, or a response to a therapeutic intervention. Examples include patterns of gene expression, levels of a particular protein in body fluids, or changes in electrical activity in the brain.

data.name: Functional Genomics
data.description: Functional genomics uses genomic data to study gene and protein expression and function on a global scale (genome-wide or system-wide), focusing on gene transcription, translation and protein-protein interactions, and often involving high-throughput methods.

data.name: Transposition
data.description: Transposition is the process by which a DNA segment moves from a donor to a recipient DNA molecule. It occurs by cutting both strands of the donor and target DNA duplexes, followed by covalently joining the ends of the mobile segment to those of the target site.

data.name: Catalysis
data.description: Catalysis is the increase in the rate of a chemical reaction by the addition of a reagent — the catalyst — that is not itself consumed. The catalyst works by opening up a route between starting material and product with a lower activation barrier than the uncatalyzed process.

data.name: Double-strand DNA breaks
data.description: A double-strand DNA break (DSB) occurs or arises when both strands of the DNA duplex are severed, often as the result of ionizing radiation. They are particularly deleterious as the DNA ends can promote potentially lethal chromosomal rearrangements, and can be repaired by homologous recombination (HR) or non-homologous-end joining (NHEJ).

data.name: DNA Damage Response
data.description: The DNA damage response is a network of cellular pathways that sense, signal and repair DNA lesions. Surveillance proteins that monitor DNA integrity can activate cell cycle checkpoints and DNA repair pathways in response to DNA damage, to prevent the generation of potentially deleterious mutations.

data.name: Eye Diseases
data.description: Eye diseases are disorders affecting the structures of the human eye, including the cornea, lens, retina, optic nerve, conjunctiva, sclera, and uveal tract, encompassing infectious, inflammatory, degenerative, congenital, neoplastic, and functional conditions.

data.name: Forensic Psychology
data.description: Psychological processes and aspects of court proceedings such as expert reports in criminal, family and social court.

data.name: Biological Imaging
data.description: Imaging is the visual representation of a subject. Imaging methods may provide a two-dimensional depiction of a surface or a three-dimensional reconstruction, they may use special probes or modalities to track specific molecular features, and they may use invasive or non-invasive means to visualize the internal components of a subject.

subjects.term: Methods of research. Technique. Experimental biology

data.name: Minority Languages
data.description: Minority languages refer to languages that are spoken by a smaller portion of the population within a specific geographical area or social group. These languages are typically not widely spoken or used as official languages in government or educational settings.

data.name: Arbuscular Mycorrhiza
data.description: Arbuscular mycorrhiza is the most common form of symbiotic association between a fungus and the roots of a vascular plant. The fungal hyphae penetrate plant cells and develop branching morphological structures inside the cells, allowing a vast exchange surface between both organisms.

data.name: Synthetic Chemistry Methodology
data.description: Synthetic chemistry methodology refers to the methods used for the synthesis of chemical compounds.

data.name: Social Neuroscience
data.description: Social neuroscience is a research discipline that examines how the brain mediates social processes and behaviour. A wide range of research topics are examined within this discipline, including social interactions, agency, empathy, morality, and social prejudice and affiliations.

data.name: Endosomes
data.description: Endosomes are membrane-delimited intracellular transport carriers. Three main endosome compartments exist: early, late and recycling endosomes. Early endosomes mature into late endosomes that subsequently fuse with lysosomes. Recycling endosomes are a sub-compartment of early endosomes that return material to the plasma membrane. Endosomes form at the plasma membrane or the Golgi.

data.name: Adherens Junctions
data.description: Adherens junctions are cadherin-based adhesive structures that mediate intercellular contacts. They form through the association of cadherins on adjacent cells, which use their intracellular regions to recruit multiprotein complexes that are linked to the actin cytoskeleton. In epithelia they form a continuous adhesion belt, the zonula adherens, which encircles the apicolateral region of interacting cells.

data.name: Biomimetic Engineering
data.description: Biologically inspired engineering.Biomimetics is an interdisciplinary field in which principles from engineering, chemistry and biology are applied to the synthesis of materials, synthetic systems or machines that have functions that mimic biological processes. Biomaterials are any natural or synthetic material that interacts with any part of a biological system. Biomimetic designs could be used in regenerative medicine, tissue engineering and drug delivery.

data.name: Gene Transcription
data.description: Transcription is the process by which an RNA polymerase synthesizes ribonucleic acid (RNA) using deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) as a template. Translation is the process by which a protein is synthesized by the ribosome, using a messenger RNA (mRNA) template.

data.name: Immunohistochemistry
data.description: Immunohistochemistry is a technique for detecting molecules of interest within tissues using antibodies. Probes or enzymes conjugated to primary antibodies that bind the target molecule (or secondary antibodies that recognize the primary antibody) report the location of targets in tissue or cell samples for imaging.

data.name: Protein Analysis
data.description: Protein analysis is the bioinformatic study of protein structure and function using database searches, sequence comparisons, structural and functional predictions.

synonyms: Study of protein structure and function

data.name: Muscle
data.description: Muscle is a soft tissue composed of elongated cells (muscle fibres) that produce force and motion through contraction. Involuntary cardiac and smooth muscles are responsible for contraction of the heart and movement of substances through hollow organ systems, respectively, and voluntary skeletal muscles are primarily responsible for posture and locomotion.

data.name: Atomic Spectroscopy
data.description: Atomic spectroscopy is the study of the electromagnetic radiation absorbed and emitted by atoms.

data.name: Bone Marrow
data.description: Bone marrow is the tissue that fills the cavities of bones. Bone marrow exists in two types: yellow and red. Yellow marrow consists mostly of fat cells whereas red marrow is a haematopoietic tissue involved in producing erythrocytes and leukocytes.

data.name: Electron Microscopy
data.description: Electron microscopy uses a beam of electrons to illuminate a sample and achieve much higher spatial resolution than light microscopy allowing researchers to observe structures at nanometer or even atomic resolution.

data.name: Special Care Dentistry
data.description: Special Care Dentistry is that branch of dentistry that provides oral care services for people with physical, medical, developmental, or cognitive conditions which limit their ability to receive routine dental care.

data.name: Biofluidmechanics
data.description: Biofluid mechanics is a field of study that focuses on the mechanics and flow behavior of fluids within biological systems. It combines principles from fluid mechanics with the understanding of biological structures and functions to analyze and predict the behavior of fluids in living organisms.

data.name: Adrenal Cortex Hormone
data.description: Adrenal complex hormones are lipid hormones, derived from the small molecule cholesterol and generated by enzymes of the cytochrome P450 family in the adrenal gland that sits atop the kidneys. Example adrenal complex hormones are corticosteroids such as immune system hormone glucocorticoid, and androgens such as testosterone.

data.name: Outcomes Research
data.description: Outcomes research evaluates the quality and effectiveness of health care by measuring parameters such as mortality or quality of life. For example, it can provide evidence on the benefits and risks of particular drugs or other medical interventions in a real-world environment that can be used to improve overall treatment strategies.

data.name: Intrauterine Growth
data.description: Intrauterine growth refers to the growth and development of a fetus that occurs inside the uterus during pregnancy. It involves the increase in size and weight of the fetus as it develops and prepares for birth.

data.name: Pharmaceutics
data.description: Pharmaceutics is the scientific discipline concerned with the process of creating the dosage form (such as a pill for oral administration or a powder for intravenous injection) of a therapeutic that is to be used by patients. It encompasses drug formulation and manufacturing.

data.name: Liquid-liquid Extraction
data.description: Liquid-liquid extraction is a technique by which a soluble chemical compound is extracted from one liquid by contact with a second, immiscible liquid, in which it is preferentially soluble.

data.name: Solar Fuels
data.description: Solar fuels, also known as solar-to-fuel technologies, are methods that harness solar energy to produce clean and renewable fuels. These fuels are generated through the conversion of solar energy into chemical energy, typically by using sunlight to drive chemical reactions that produce energy-rich molecules.

data.name: Microbial Ecology
data.description: Microbial ecology is the study of the interactions of microorganisms with their environment, each other, and plant and animal species. It includes the study of symbioses, biogeochemical cycles and the interaction of microbes with anthropogenic effects such as pollution and climate change.

subjects.term: Ecology, organisms characteristic of specific environments

data.name: Community and Population Ecology
data.description: Community ecology is the study of communities formed of populations of different species. It includes the study of the interactions between species, such as mutualism, predation and competition, and the dynamics and structure of the community.

data.name: Protein Transport
data.description: Protein transport involves the movement of a protein from one cellular or extracellular compartment to another. Protein transport can be facilitated by a variety of pathways including membrane trafficking, protein translocation, and endocytosis or exocytosis.

data.name: PML Bodies
data.description: PML (promyelocytic leukaemia) bodies are spherical structures in the nucleus that can measure up to 1 µM in diameter. The principal organizing component of PML bodies is the PML protein. PML bodies vary in composition and have been implicated in cellular processes such as telomere lengthening and the DNA damage response.

data.name: Paediatric Dentistry
data.description: The branch of dentistry concerned with the dental care and treatment of children. Pediatric dentists are dedicated to the oral health of children from infancy through the teen years.

data.name: Wounding
data.description: Wounding refers to the damage inflicted to plants by some external force. Insect herbivory is a particularly common source of injury to plants.

data.name: Golgi
data.description: The Golgi is a cytoplasmic organelle composed of stacks of flat membrane-bound structures called cisternae. Within the Golgi, proteins are modified, sorted and packaged for transport to other cellular destinations.

data.name: Learning and Instruction
data.description: Learning and instruction refers to a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding how individuals acquire knowledge, develop skills, and change their behavior through various instructional methods and techniques. It involves investigating the cognitive, social, and emotional processes involved in learning, as well as the design and implementation of effective instructional strategies. This field examines the interplay between learners, instructors, and educational environments to enhance the learning process and optimize instructional outcomes. It encompasses theoretical frameworks, empirical research, and practical applications aimed at promoting effective teaching and learning in various educational settings.

data.name: Biological Taxonomy
data.description: The discipline of classification and taxonomy involves the grouping of organisms into categories based on different properties including size, shape and gene sequences. Classification can help to identify evolutionary relationships among organisms..Taxonomy is the classification and description of living organisms. It includes the naming and defining of species, and the collation of data about their biology and biogeography.

data.name: DNA Replication
data.description: DNA replication is the biological process by which an exact copy of a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) molecule is created and it is the basis for biological inheritance. Each of the two strands of the DNA molecule acts as a template for the synthesis of a complementary strand.

data.name: Decision Making
data.description: Decision making is the process of choosing among alternatives associated with different outcomes. Deciding among multiple options can take the form of selecting a course of action or judging among ideas.

data.name: Model Fungi
data.description: Model fungi are commonly studied yeasts, moulds, mushrooms, filamentous or other fungal species chosen for the ease of investigating particular biological phenomena. Research on these fungi provide biological insights relevant to other organisms in areas such as genetics, cell biology, meiosis and pathogenesis.

data.name: Mathematical Psychology
data.description: Mathematical psychology is psychological research that is based on mathematical modeling of perceptual, thought, cognitive and motor processes.

data.name: Science and Technology Governance
data.description: Science and Technology Governance explores the policies, regulations, and ethical considerations that guide the development and application of scientific research and technological innovations.

data.name: Organ Transplantation
data.description: Organ transplantation is a procedure in which a functional, intact organ is transferred from one individual to another. The organ is then functional in the recipient. This type of transplantation can occur between individuals of the same species or between individuals of different species.

data.name: Two-hybrid system
data.description: Two-hybrid systems are methods that assay for the interaction between two proteins, or protein and DNA in cells. Physical interaction is detected by the reconstitution of complementary domains of a reporter or transcription factor that activates reporter gene expression.

data.name: Industrial Microbiology
data.description: Industrial and applied microbiology is a branch of applied microbiology in which microorganisms are used in industrial processes; for example, in the production of high-value products such as drugs, chemicals, fuels and electricity.

data.name: Veterinary Microbiology
data.description: Veterinary Microbiology is the study of the agents responsible for causing animal infections: bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites.

data.name: Embryogenesis
data.description: Animal embryogenesis is the process by which the embryo develops from the fertilised egg cell. Important events that occur during embryogenesis are gastrulation, formation of the early nervous system and initiation of organogenesis..Embryology is the discipline concerned with the study of embryogenesis, the development of the embryo from a fertilised egg cell. Findings in embryology have helped in the understanding of congenital abnormalities and developing assisted reproduction procedures.

data.name: Stress Granules
data.description: Stress granules are aggregates composed of proteins and RNA molecules – mostly stalled translation initiation complexes – that usually form in a reversible manner upon cellular stress. Stress granules can also precipitate the formation of toxic protein aggregates such as those seen during the progression of certain types of neurological disease.

data.name: Batteries
data.description: A battery is a device that stores energy in chemical form and can convert it into electric energy through electrochemical reactions.

subjects.term: Devices for production of electricity by direct energy conversion
Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Ecological Modelling
data.description: Ecological modelling is the construction and analysis of mathematical models of ecological processes, including both purely biological and combined biophysical models. Models can be analytic or simulation-based and are used to understand complex ecological processes and predict how real ecosystems might change.

data.name: Drug Therapy
data.description: Drug therapy (or pharmacotherapy) involves the administration of drugs to treat or prevent disease. In some cases - often in the treatment of disease such as cancer, HIV infection and diabetes - multiple drugs with different active ingredients may be administered, which is known as combination therapy.

data.name: Courts
data.description: Courts is the study of the structure, functioning, and development of legal institutions responsible for the administration of justice, including analyses of judicial decision-making, procedural aspects, and the role of courts in shaping social norms and policies.

data.name: Neurogenesis
data.description: Neurogenesis is the formation of neurons from neural stem cells occurring during embryonic development and throughout adult life. During neurogenesis, neural stem cells divide and differentiate to form mature neurons. Mature neurons do not divide and carry extensions such as axons and dendrites, allowing them to send and receive electrical pulses.

data.name: Engineering Economics
data.description: Engineering economics, previously known as engineering economy, is a subset of economics concerned with the use and "...application of economic principles"[1] in the analysis of engineering decisions

data.name: Collective Cell Migration
data.description: Collective cell migration is the process by which a group of cells move in concert, without completely disrupting their cell-cell contacts. Collective migration is important during morphogenesis, and in pathological processes such as wound healing and cancer cell invasion.

data.name: Optical Microscopy
data.description: Optical Microscopy is a surface investigation technique that relies on the use of light in the visible spectrum to image the topography of a sample. It is usable for feature sizes down to the micron range.

data.name: Psychoactive Drug
data.description: Psychoactive drugs, also known as psychotropic drugs, are substances that alter brain function and produce changes in perception, mood, consciousness, cognition, or behavior. These drugs have effects on the central nervous system (CNS) and can be used for therapeutic purposes, as well as for recreational or non-medical purposes.

data.name: Immunopathogenesis
data.description: Immunopathogenesis is the process of disease development involving an immune response or components thereof.

data.name: Triplex-forming Oligonucleotide
data.description: Triplex-forming oligonucleotides bind in the major groove of duplex DNA in a sequence-specific manner through the formation of hydrogen bonds. They can be used to inhibit the expression of particular genes.

data.name: Laboratory Medical Diagnosis
data.description: Laboratory techniques and procedures are performed on patient specimens to detect biomarkers and diagnose diseases. Blood, urine, semen or tissue samples can be analysed using biochemical, microbiological and cytological methods.

data.name: Race and Ethnicity Studies
data.description: Race and Ethnicity Studies is an interdisciplinary academic field that focuses on the study of race, ethnicity, and related issues. It emerged as a response to the civil rights movements in the United States during the mid-20th century. Race and Ethnicity Studies critically analyze the concepts of race and ethnicity as social constructs rather than biological realities. It explores how these categories are shaped by historical contexts, power dynamics, and cultural representations.

data.name: Raman Spectroscopy
data.description: Raman spectroscopy is an optical technique that detects intrinsic vibrational, rotational and other low-frequency modes in molecules upon inelastic scattering of monochromatic light. Because different chemical functional groups scatter light at different frequencies, Raman spectroscopy can be used as a tool for chemical structure analysis, chemical fingerprinting and chemical imaging.

data.name: Scandinavian Literature
data.description: Scandinavian literature refers to the literary works produced in the countries of Scandinavia, which include Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland (including Finnish-speaking areas), and Iceland. Scandinavian literature encompasses a rich literary tradition spanning various genres, themes, and time periods.

data.name: Freshwater and Marine Ecology
data.description: Biolimnology or freshwater ecology is the study of all aspects of the ecology of terrestrial aquatic systems, including rivers, lakes and ponds. It includes the community ecology of these ecosystems, as well as ecosystem processes, interactions with adjacent terrestrial and marine ecosystems, and conservation and restoration..Freshwater ecology is the study of all aspects of the ecology of terrestrial aquatic systems, including rivers, lakes and ponds. It includes the community ecology of these ecosystems, as well as ecosystem processes, interactions with adjacent terrestrial and marine ecosystems, and conservation and restoration.

data.name: Ethnography
data.description: In criminology, ethnography is employed to gain an in-depth understanding of criminal behavior, criminal subcultures, and the lived experiences of individuals involved in criminal activities. Ethnographic research typically involves direct observation, participant observation, interviews, and analysis of cultural artifacts.

data.name: Human Behavioral Ecology
data.description: Human Behavioral Ecology uses the principles of evolutionary theory to study cultural and human behavioral diversity.

data.name: Root Apical Meristem
data.description: Root apical meristem is the region within the growing root containing meristematic cells. At the heart of the root apical meristem are the cells of the quiescent centre.

data.name: Energy and Behaviour
data.description: Studies the way people use domestic and non-domestic energy. It includes studies on how households react to price or infrastructure changes, and how habitual and cultural reasons may affect energy use.

data.name: Cancer Therapeutic Resistance
data.description: Cancer therapeutic resistance occurs as cancers develop resistance to treatments such as chemotherapy, radiotherapy and targeted therapies, through many different mechanisms. These include specific genetic and epigenetic changes in the cancer cell and/or the microenvironment in which the cancer cell resides.

data.name: Germ Cells
data.description: Germ cells are the cells that give rise to the reproductive cells of sexually reproducing organisms, known as gametes, through a process called gametogenesis. In animals, the reproductive male gametes are sperm cells and the female gametes the oocytes.

data.name: Weight Management
data.description: Weight management is the process of adopting long-term lifestyle modification to maintain a healthy body weight on the basis of a person's age, sex and height. Methods of weight management include eating a healthy diet and increasing physical activity levels.

data.name: Hydrogen Fuel
data.description: Hydrogen fuel refers to hydrogen which is burned as fuel with oxygen. It can be a zero-carbon fuel, provided that it is created in a process that does not involve carbon.

data.name: Bioinorganic Chemistry
data.description: Bioinorganic chemistry is the study of metals in biology. The metals may already feature in the body as native protein cofactors or could be used in inorganic drugs to treat diseases.

data.name: Multipotent Stem Cells
data.description: Multipotent stem cells are cells that have the capacity to self-renew by dividing and to develop into multiple specialised cell types present in a specific tissue or organ. Most adult stem cells are multipotent stem cells. Pluripotent stem cells are cells that have the capacity to self-renew by dividing and to develop into the three primary germ cell layers of the early embryo and therefore into all cells of the adult body, but not extra-embryonic tissues such as the placenta. Embryonic stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells are pluripotent stem cells.

data.name: Mitosis
data.description: Mitosis is the complex process in which duplicated chromosomes are condensed, segregated with the help of the mitotic spindle, and packaged in to daughter cell nuclei. Mitosis occurs in five stages: prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase.

data.name: Molecular Engineering
data.description: Molecular engineering includes methods for the design and synthesis of novel molecules with desirable physical properties or functionalities.

data.name: West Nile Virus
data.description: West nile virus is an infectious agent belonging to the virus family Flaviviridae, which are transmitted by arthropod vectors. West nile virus is a neurotropic flavivirus and is a leading cause of mosquito-borne and epidemic encephalitis in humans. The virus can also infect other mammals and vertebrate species.

data.name: Behavioral Genetics
data.description: Behavioural genetics is the interdisciplinary effort to establish causal links between genes and animal (including human) behavioural traits and neural mechanisms. Methods used include twin studies, quantitative trait mapping by linkage to allelic variants, transgenic animals and targeted gene disruption or silencing.

data.name: Antisense Oligonucleotide Therapy
data.description: Antisense Oligonucleotide Therapy is the treatment with antisense oligonucleotides. These are small pieces of DNA or RNA that can bind to specific molecules of RNA. This blocks the cell's ability to use the RNA to make a protein or work in other ways.

data.name: NF-kappaB
data.description: Nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-κB) is a family of transcription factors that regulate diverse processes in immune cells, including cell survival and proliferation, cell differentiation and cytokine production.

data.name: Sensory Transduction
data.description: Transduction is the conversion of an external stimulus into a neural signal and plays a crucial role in shaping behavioural responses to changes in the external environment. For example, photoreceptors in the retina transduce light energy and hair cells in the cochlea transduce sound energy into neural signals.

data.name: Mirror Neuron
data.description: Mirror neurons are a type of brain cells that are active both when an individual performs a particular action and when they observe someone else performing the same action. They were first discovered in the 1990s and have been primarily studied in primates, including humans. Mirror neurons play a significant role in social cognition, empathy, and understanding the actions and intentions of others.

data.name: Atmospheric Science
data.description: Atmospheric science is the study of the dynamics and chemistry of the layers of gas that surround the Earth, other planets and moons. This encompasses the interactions between various parts of the atmosphere as well as interactions with the oceans and freshwater systems, the biosphere and human activities.

data.name: Network Topology
data.description: Network topology is the "shape" of a network of biological interactions and shows how the nodes - the parts of the network where elements interact - are connected to each other. Common topologies that are found in biological networks include the bus network, star network and ring network.

data.name: Gene Regulation
data.description: Gene regulation refers to the mechanisms that act to induce or repress the expression of a gene. These include structural and chemical changes to the genetic material, binding of proteins to specific DNA elements to regulate transcription, or mechanisms that modulate translation of mRNA.

data.name: Gene Expression
data.description: Gene expression is the generation of a functional gene product from the information encoded by a gene, through the processes of transcription and translation. Gene products are often proteins, however non-protein coding genes can encode functional RNA, including ribosomal RNA (rRNA), transfer RNA (tRNA) or small nuclear RNA (snRNA).

data.name: Protein Function Predictions
data.description: Protein function predictions are bioinformatic methods (i.e. involving computation using software) that aim to predict the function of a protein. Protein function analyses use protein sequences and structures as inputs into software that generates experimentally testable predictions of function.

data.name: Surgical Oncology
data.description: Surgical oncology is a subspecialty of oncology focused specifically on the surgical management of cancer, including tumor removal, biopsy procedures, lymph node dissection, and surgical reconstruction related to cancer treatment.

data.name: Synaptic Pruning
data.description: Synaptic pruning, also known as synaptic elimination or synaptic refinement, is a natural process that occurs in the developing brain during early childhood and adolescence. It involves the elimination of some synaptic connections, or synapses, between neurons, leading to a more efficient and refined neural network.

data.name: Microfluidics
data.description: Microfluidics is the engineering or use of devices that apply fluid flow to channels smaller than 1 millimetre in at least one dimension. Microfluidic devices can reduce reagent consumption, allow well controlled mixing and particle manipulation, integrate and automate multiple assays (known as lab-on-a-chip), and facilitate imaging and tracking.

data.name: Sexual Behaviour
data.description: Sexual behaviour is a process by which humans and other animals demonstrate and/or express sexuality.

data.name: Dental Education
data.description: Dental education involves the teaching and learning of the future generations of dentists to prevent, diagnose and treat oral diseases and meet the dental needs and demands of the individual patients and the public.

data.name: Computational Social Science, Social Networks
data.description: Computational social science refers to the academic sub-disciplines concerned with computational approaches used to model, simulate, and analyze social phenomena. It focuses on investigating social and behavioral relationships and interactions through social simulation, modeling, network analysis, and media analysis.Social Networks aim to analyze the structure of whole social entities as well as a variety of theories explaining the patterns observed in these structures. The study of these structures uses social network analysis to identify local and global patterns, locate influential entities, and examine network dynamics.

data.name: Molecular Ecology
data.description: Molecular ecology is the use of molecular genetic tools to study ecological questions. Techniques such as microarrays and DNA markers are used to study the interactions and diversity of natural populations.

data.name: Marine and Freshwater Sciences
data.description: Marine and Freshwater Biology is the study of the organisms including microbes, plants and animals in aquatic ecosystems, as well as the chemical and physical processes in the sediments of these systems and the relationships between them.

data.name: Urban Politics
data.description: Urban politics is politics in and about cities. This term refers to the diverse political structure that occurs in urban areas where there is diversity in both race and socioeconomic status. City governments search for an equilibrium in their relations with the external environment.

data.name: Production Processes
data.description: The production process is a method that makes use of economic inputs or resources (such as workforce, machinery, or land) to provide goods and services to consumers. The production process influences how to efficiently and productively make final products to be sold, ensuring high quality.

data.name: RNA Vaccines
data.description: RNA vaccines are composed of the nucleic acid RNA, which encode antigen genes of an infectious agent. When administered to host cells, the RNA is translated into protein antigens that elicit protective immunity against the infectious agent.

data.name: Chromosome Condensation
data.description: Chromosome condensation is the dramatic reorganisation of the long thin chromatin strands into compact short chromosomes that occurs in mitosis and meiosis. Chromosome condensation is mediated by the condensin complex, among other proteins, and is necessary to prevent chromosomes from being entangled during chromosome segregation.

data.name: Dendritic Excitability
data.description: Dendritic excitability refers to the readiness of synapses and branches in a dendritic tree to depolarize. It is influenced by the resting membrane potential, ion channel and receptor expression, relative intracellular and extracellular ion concentrations, and is altered during synaptic plasticity.

data.name: Cellular Signalling Networks
data.description: Cellular signalling networks are formed when different cell signalling pathways interact and are detected by a combination of experimental and computational methods. Understanding how a biological system responds to a signal can be deduced by analysing how multiple cell signalling pathways affect each other and, in turn, cellular processes within the network.

data.name: Natural Variation in Plants
data.description: Natural variation in plants refers to the genetic diversity of a single plant species in the wild. Natural variation is a valuable source of beneficial traits for plant breeding.

data.name: Circadian Rhythms and Sleep
data.description: Circadian rhythms are the regular, daily cycles of biological processes or activities, including the regular and predictable variation in the levels of many circulating hormones, ions and the control of sleep and wakefulness. Circadian rhythms are controlled centrally by the suprachiasmatic nucleus, and are most strongly infuenced by light.

data.name: Autophagy
data.description: Autophagy is a process by which cellular material is degraded by lysosomes or vacuoles and recycled. Several autophagy pathways operate within a cell, including macroautophagy, microautophagy and chaperone-mediated autophagy.

data.name: Energy Ethics
data.description: Explores the relationship between energy, ethics, and society.

data.name: Oral Microbiology
data.description: Oral microbiology is the study of the microorganisms (microbiota) of the oral cavity and their interactions between oral microorganisms or with the host. The environment present in the human mouth is suited to the growth of characteristic microorganisms found there. It provides a source of water and nutrients, as well as a moderate temperature. Resident microbes of the mouth adhere to the teeth and gums to resist mechanical flushing from the mouth to stomach where acid-sensitive microbes are destroyed by hydrochloric acid.

data.name: Cell-cycle Exit
data.description: Cell cycle exit is when cells stop dividing and enter a quiescent state, also named G0. Cells exit the cell cycle in response to nutrient- or growth factor deprivation or in response to signals that induce differentiation. In the case of nutrient-and growth factor starvation, cell cycle exit is reversible.

data.name: Dental Materials
data.description: Dental materials are specially fabricated materials, designed for use in dentistry. Examples include temporary dressings, dental restorations, endodontic materials, impression materials, prosthetic materials, dental implants, and many others.

data.name: Gene Mutation
data.description: A mutation is any detectable and heritable change in nucleotide sequence that causes a change in genotype and is transmitted to daughter cells and succeeding generations.

data.name: Human Rights
data.description: Human rights are rights inherent to all human beings, regardless of race, sex, nationality, ethnicity, language, religion, or any other status. Human rights include the right to life and liberty, freedom from slavery and torture, freedom of opinion and expression, the right to work and education, and many more.

data.name: Stars and stellar astrophysics
data.description: Stars are luminous celestial bodies composed of hot, glowing plasma held together by their own gravitational attraction. Stellar astrophysics is the branch of astronomy that focuses on the study of stars, their structure, evolution, and the physical processes that govern them.

data.name: Compact Astrophysical Objects
data.description: Compact astrophysical objects are (supermassive-) black holes, neutron stars and white dwarfs, the remnants of massive star evolution. Conditions are extreme in the vicinity of these objects and lead to a variety of unusual phenomena such as high energy X-ray and gamma-ray radiation, high frequency oscillations, and relativistic jets.

data.name: Electrodiagnosis
data.description: Electrodiagnosis refers to a diagnosis that is made based on recording the spontaneous or stimulus-evoked electrical activity of a tissue or organ, such as a nerve or the brain.

data.name: Mesoderm
data.description: The mesoderm is the middle layer of cells in very early vertebrate and insect embryos. It is one of the three primary germ cell layers and gives rise to tissues and organs such as muscle, bone, blood and the heart.

data.name: Sensory Systems
data.description: Sensory systems include the parts of the nervous system responsible for processing sensory information, including the visual system, auditory system, olfactory system, somatosensory system, gustatory system and vestibular system. Sensory systems are composed of receptors that sense the sensory stimuli, brain areas involved in sensory perception and neural pathways that connect them.

data.name: Synchrotron Techniques
data.description: Synchrotron techniques refer to a set of advanced experimental methods and analytical tools that utilize synchrotron radiation, which is intense and highly collimated electromagnetic radiation produced by charged particles accelerated in a synchrotron facility. common synchrotron techniques include: X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), X-ray Fluorescence (XRF), X-ray Microscopy.

data.name: Rhizobial Symbiosis
data.description: Rhizobial symbiosis refers to the mutually beneficial relationship that forms between plants and soil bacteria that fix nitrogen, termed rhizobia.

data.name: Religion and Human Rights
data.description: The relationship between religion and human rights is both complex and inextricable. While most of the world's religions have supported violence, repression, and prejudice, each has also played a crucial role in the modern struggle for universal human rights.

data.name: Multiphoton Microscopy
data.description: Multiphoton microscopy is a general term for a variety of fluorescence and non-fluorescence microscopy techniques that rely on multiple photons interacting with either individual molecules or optical heterogeneities in a sample. These techniques generally rely on pulsed high-intensity lasers and have better sample penetration than single-photon techniques.

data.name: Ritual Studies
data.description: Ritual Studies is an interdisciplinary field that explores the diverse forms, functions, and meanings of rituals in human societies. It aims to understand the role of rituals in social cohesion, cultural expression, and individual and collective identity, drawing on theories and methods from anthropology, sociology, religious studies, and other disciplines.

data.name: Aging Population
data.description: Population aging refers to the process whereby the proportion of older individuals in a population increases over time, typically due to declining birth rates and increasing life expectancy. It is a demographic phenomenon that occurs when a society experiences a significant increase in the number and proportion of older adults relative to younger age groups.

data.name: Renal Replacement Therapy
data.description: Renal replacement therapy describes the range of therapies designed to remove waste products, such as urea and creatinine, from the blood in cases of kidney failure.

data.name: Urological Surgery
data.description: Urology (from Greek οὖρον ouron "urine" and -λογία -logia "study of"), also known as genitourinary surgery, is the branch of medicine that focuses on surgical and medical diseases of the urinary-tract system and the reproductive organs.

data.name: Computational Platforms and Environments
data.description: Computational platforms and environments are platforms of integrated software that have user-friendly interfaces and that can be used by researchers to properly analyse data, such as large datasets, and answer research questions.

data.name: Model Plants
data.description: Model plants are extensively studied plant species chosen for the ease of investigating particular biological phenomena or for their value in biotechnology or agronomy. Research on model plants provides biological insights relevant to other organisms in areas such as biochemistry, genetics, physiology, ecology, evolution and development.

data.name: Thymus
data.description: The thymus is a primary lymphoid organ that is important for T cell development. In the thymus, developing T cells are deleted if they express receptors that could cause dangerous immune attacks against the body’s own proteins. This process is known as central tolerance.

data.name: Polarization Microscopy
data.description: Polarization microscopy is any optical microscopy technique that uses polarization of white-light illumination beams to generate an image with enhanced contrast.

data.name: Ebola Virus
data.description: Ebola virus is an infectious agent and one of the viruses that can cause haemorraghic fever, a severe infectious disease characterized by high fever and bleeding, in humans and some monkeys. The first infections with this viral genus were reported in Zaire, close to the river Ebola.

data.name: Coat Complexes
data.description: Coat complexes are diverse proteins that associate with forming or formed vesicles in secretory and endocytic membrane trafficking pathways. Coat complexes might provide structural stability, assist in cargo selection or vesicle budding, and influence directional transport.

data.name: Romanticism
data.description: Romanticism refers to a cultural and artistic movement that emerged in the late 18th century and flourished throughout the 19th century. It was a reaction against the rationality and restraint of the Enlightenment era and embraced emotion, individualism, imagination, and a fascination with nature and the past.

data.name: Optical Tweezers
data.description: Optical tweezers (or optical traps) are devices that use a laser to trap a nanometre-to-micrometre-sized dielectric object in place. Optical tweezers are used for performing single molecule force and motion measurements and for non-invasively manipulating objects such as a single cell.

data.name: Pluripotency
data.description: Pluripotency describes the ability of a cell to develop into the three primary germ cell layers of the early embryo and therefore into all cells of the adult body, but not extra-embryonic tissues such as the placenta. Embryonic stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells are characterised by their pluripotency.

data.name: Autotransplantation
data.description: Autotransplantation is the transplantation of an organ or tissue from one part of the body to another in the same individual. The transplant is called an autograft. These are generally not immunologically rejected.

data.name: Deviance
data.description: Deviance is a concept within criminology that refers to behavior that deviates from the social norms or expectations of a particular society or group. It involves actions, beliefs, or traits that are perceived as violating the established standards or values of a community. Deviance is a complex phenomenon that can encompass a wide range of behaviors, from minor rule-breaking to serious criminal acts.

data.name: Statistical Physics
data.description: Statistical physics is a branch of physics that uses probability theory and statistics to solve physical problems that usually involve systems composed of a large number of units. Its main purpose is to study the properties of a system from the statistical behaviour of its components.

data.name: Photosynthesis
data.description: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae and certain types of bacteria synthesise carbohydrates from carbon dioxide and typically water, using light as an energy source. The process can be broken down into two stages - the light and dark reactions. NADPH and ATP generated during the light reactions fuel the formation of carbohydrates in the dark reactions.

subjects.term: Photosynthesis. Assimilation and utilization of carbon dioxide

data.name: Hepatology
data.description: Hepatology is a medical specialty focusing on the structure, function, pathology and disorders of the liver, gall bladder and bile ducts.

data.name: Dendrimers
data.description: Dendrimers are polymers with branched, tree-like structures. They are of interest in applications such as drug delivery and catalysis.

data.name: Separation Science
data.description: Separation science comprises the isolation, separation and purification techniques used to isolate, concentrate or purify cells, viruses, cell fractions, organelles or biological macromolecules (e.g. proteins, protein complexes, chromatin, nucleic acids, carbohydrates or lipids) for subsequent analysis.

data.name: Stochastic Systems and Control
data.description: Stochastic control a sub field of control theory that deals with the existence of uncertainty either in observations or in the noise that drives the evolution of the system.

data.name: Diode Lasers
data.description: Diode lasers are electrically driven lasers generally made from semiconducting materials. In addition to the optical considerations common with all semiconductors, diode laser structures must also incorporate a means of injecting an electrical current into the active region. This often involves extra semiconductor layers and metal contacts.

data.name: Textile Engineering
data.description: Textile engineering is a popular field of engineering that deals with materials like cotton, fibers, yarns, and other materials used in clothing products and accessories. It is primarily concerned with the development and manufacture of textile fabric used in the apparel industry.

data.name: Plant Hormones
data.description: Plant hormones, also known as phytohormones, are chemicals that regulate plant cell processes. They are signal molecules produced within the plant functioning in extremely low concentrations.

data.name: Small Molecules
data.description: Chemical tools are small molecules used as probes of a chemical or biological process. Studying the effects of chemical tools on a system can lead to new insight into the molecular target of the small molecule and the pathways it acts in. Chemical probes with defined targets can be attractive as drugs in clinical pharmacology..Small molecules are low molecular weight molecules that include lipids, monosaccharides, second messengers, other natural products and metabolites, as well as drugs and other xenobiotics. They are distinct from macromolecules such as proteins. In chemical biology, this term also covers metal ions and in this discipline small molecules may play the role of a chemical tool.

subjects.term: General biochemistry of plants and animals

data.name: Oogenesis
data.description: Oogenesis is the development of the mature female germ cells called egg cells or ova. Primordial germ cells, the founder cells of the germ line, develop through several immature stages by undergoing mitosis, meiosis and differentiation into the haploid egg cells, which carry only one set of chromosomes.

data.name: Single-strand DNA breaks
data.description: A single-strand DNA break arises when only one strand of the DNA duplex is severed. They are typically corrected by excision repair pathways.

data.name: Dental Equipment
data.description: Instuments and technology used for Dental treatment

data.name: Endodontics
data.description: Endodontics encompasses the study (practice) of the basic and clinical sciences of normal dental pulp, the etiology, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases and injuries of the dental pulp along with associated periradicular conditions.

data.name: Water and Health
data.description: Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H₂O. It is a transparent, tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless chemical substance, and it is the main constituent of Earth's hydrosphere and the fluids of all known living organisms. Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.

data.name: Quantum Field Theory
data.description: Quantum Field Theory (QFT) is a theoretical framework that combines classical field theory, special relativity, and quantum mechanics and is used to construct physical models of elementary and subatomic particles (in particle physics) and quasiparticles (in condensed matter physics).

data.name: Biogeography
data.description: Biogeography is the study of the large-scale distribution of species. It investigates how these distributions change over time and the processes that govern distribution patterns.

data.name: Viral Epidemiology
data.description: Viral epidemiology is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the incidence and spread of viruses in populations over time. Host, virus and environmental factors are monitored to determine the dynamics of viral infections, the ultimate goal of which is to devise intervention strategies.

data.name: Pharmacotherapy
data.description: Pharmacotherapy is the treatment of health conditions by using pharmaceutical products (drugs) as medication. It refers to the use of pharmaceutical agents, such as medications or drugs, to treat medical conditions, diseases, or disorders in patients. It involves the administration of specific drugs to alleviate symptoms, manage conditions, or cure illnesses. Pharmacotherapy can encompass various forms of drug delivery, including oral medications, injections, infusions, topical applications, and more.

data.name: Risk Factors
data.description: Risk factors are determinants associated with an increased risk of a disease. Risk factors can be genetic or an aspect of personal behavior, lifestyle or environmental exposure.

data.name: Herpes Virus
data.description: Herpesvirus is an infectious agent belonging to the virus family Herpesviridae that causes latent and lytic infections in a wide range of animals and humans. There are 8 herpesvirus types currently known to infect humans, including Herpes simplex viruses, varicella-zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus and human cytomegalovirus.

data.name: Nanoscale Devices
data.description: Nanoscale devices are devices that are one hundred to ten thousand times smaller than human cells and that can manipulate matter on atomic or molecular scales. Examples of nanoscale devices are synthetic molecular motors such as rotaxanes, graphene-based transistors and nanoelectromechanical oscillators.

data.name: NK Cells
data.description: NK (natural killer) cells are a population of lymphocytes with both innate and adaptive immune features. They produce cytotoxic molecules and can eliminate infected cells or cancer cells.

data.name: Reverse Breeding
data.description: Reverse breeding is a plant breeding technique that involves the creation of genetically engineered plants with a set of specific genetic alterations. It is called "reverse breeding" because it is the opposite of traditional breeding methods, where desired traits are introduced into plants through crossbreeding.

data.name: Soil Microbiology
data.description: Soil microbiology is the scientific discipline that is concerned with the study of all biological aspects of the microorganisms (bacteria, archaea, viruses, fungi, parasites and protozoa) that exist in the soil environment. This is a subdiscipline of environmental microbiology.

data.name: Model Vertebrates
data.description: Model vertebrates are extensively studied non-human vertebrates (species with a notochord, or vertebral column) chosen for the ease of investigating particular biological phenomena in areas such as development, physiology or disease. Research on model vertebrates provides insights that are relevant to other organisms, often including humans.

data.name: Parasitic Plant
data.description: A parasitic plant is a type of plant that obtains nutrients and water from other plants or hosts. Unlike typical plants that rely on photosynthesis to produce their own food, parasitic plants have evolved to exploit the resources of other plants in order to survive.

data.name: Electronic Materials
data.description: Electronic materials are materials studied and used mainly for their electrical properties. The electric response of materials largely stems from the dynamics of electrons, and their interplay with atoms and molecules. A material can be classified as a conductor, semiconductor or insulator according to its response to an external electric field.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials
Solids. Solid state chemistry (Inorganic and organic)
Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Oral Conditions
data.description: Oral health refers to the health of the teeth, gums, and the entire oral-facial system that allows us to smile, speak, and chew. Some of the most common diseases that impact our oral health include cavities (tooth decay), gum (periodontal) disease, and oral cancer. Oral conditions are frequently considered separate from other chronic conditions, but these are actually inter-related. Poor oral health is associated with other chronic diseases such as diabetes and heart disease. Oral disease also is associated with risk behaviors such as using tobacco and consuming sugary foods and beverages.

data.name: Parathyroid Glands
data.description: The parathyroid glands are two pairs of small oval-shaped glands located in the front and the base of the neck, adjacent to the two lobes of the thyroid gland. They secrete parathyroid hormone, which regulates calcium, phosphorous and magnesium levels.

data.name: Plant Ecology
data.description: Plant Ecology is the branch of ecology that focuses on the relationships between plants and their environment, including interactions with other organisms, climate, soil, and physical factors. It examines how plant species adapt to their habitats, the distribution and abundance of plant communities, and the dynamics of ecosystems. Key areas of study within plant ecology include plant physiology, population dynamics, community structure, and the impact of environmental changes on plant life. This field is essential for understanding biodiversity, ecosystem services, and the effects of human activities on natural habitats.

subjects.term: Plant ecology, plants characteristic of specific environments

data.name: Bayesian Inference
data.description: Bayesian inference is a statistical method of inductive reasoning based on the reassessment of competing hypotheses in the presence of new evidence. Conceptually similar to the scientific method itself, formal Bayesian techniques are increasingly used in Artificial Intelligence and Brain models for decision-making under uncertainty.

data.name: Pregnancy Outcome
data.description: Pregnancy outcome is the final result of a fertilization event. Types of pregnancy outcomes include live birth (full term or preterm birth), stillbirth, spontaneous abortion, and induced abortion.

data.name: Surgical Orthopedics
data.description: Orthopedic surgery, also known as orthopedics, is a branch of surgery dealing with the musculoskeletal system. Orthopedic surgeons use various surgical and non-surgical procedures such a hip replacement surgery and spinal fusion to treat all problems relating to one's bones and joints.

data.name: Politics and Religion
data.description: Politics and Religion examines the interactions between religious beliefs, institutions, and political systems, exploring how religion influences political behavior, policy, and governance.

data.name: Immunotherapy
data.description: Immunotherapy is the treatment of disease by inducing, enhancing or suppressing an immune response. Activation immunotherapies induce or amplify an immune response and are used in vaccines and as cancer immunotherapies. Suppression immunotherapies reduce or suppress an immune response and are used to prevent graft rejection and treat autoimmunity and allergy.

data.name: Population Screening
data.description: Population screening is the process of assessing the prevalence of a particular trait in the entire population or in a subgroup of the population. Genetic testing or other means are used to determine the presence of biomarkers or genetic characteristics.

data.name: Microbiota
data.description: The microbiota is a collective term for the micro-organisms that live in or on the human body. Specific clusters of microbiota are found on the skin or in the gastrointestinal tract, mouth, vagina and eyes.

data.name: Psychiatric Disorder
data.description: Psychiatric disorders are a heterogeneous group of mental disorders, manifesting as unusual mental or behavioural patterns that cause distress or disability to the individual.

data.name: Geochemistry
data.description: Geochemistry is the study of the chemical composition of the Earth and other planets, and the chemical processes that affect them.

data.name: Fungus-like Organism
data.description: A fungus-like organism, also known as a fungus-like microorganism or fungus-like protist, refers to a group of organisms that share some characteristics with fungi but are classified separately due to genetic and structural differences. These organisms exhibit features similar to both fungi and protists.

data.name: Adenovirus
data.description: Adenoviruses are infectious agents that replicate in humans and many animals, often causing no, or only mild, symptoms. Owing to their large genome size and overall stability, members of this virus family are used as viral vectors, for example in vaccines or cancer therapy.

data.name: Cell Self-Renewal
data.description: Self-renewal is the process of giving rise to indefinitely more cells of the same cell type. All stem cells have the capacity to self-renew by dividing.

data.name: Astrobiology
data.description: Astrobiology makes use of molecular biology, biophysics, biochemistry, chemistry, astronomy, physical cosmology, exoplanetology and geology to investigate the possibility of life on other worlds and help recognize biospheres that might be different from that on Earth.

data.name: Blood-Brain Barrier
data.description: The blood–brain barrier acts as a strict control point for what can enter the brain, and is created by tight junctions between endothelial cells lining blood vessels, astroyctic endfeet and a basement membrane. The ability to cross the blood–brain barrier must be considered for drugs administered peripherally, but whose target lies inside the brain.

data.name: Clinical Trials
data.description: A clinical trial involves the study of the safety, efficacy and/or dosage regimen of a therapeutic intervention (such as a drug) in humans selected according to predetermined criteria of eligibility (such as a defined severity of a specific disease), who are observed for predefined evidence of favourable and unfavourable effects.

data.name: Metal-organic Frameworks
data.description: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are a class of crystalline materials that consist of coordination bonds between transition-metal cations and multidentate organic linkers. The structure of MOFs is characterized by an open framework that can be porous (porous materials). MOFs can be used for gas storage, purification and separation, as well catalysis and sensing applications.

data.name: Metabolomics
data.description: Metabolomics refers to the systematic identification and quantification of the small molecule metabolic products (the metabolome) of a biological system (cell, tissue, organ, biological fluid, or organism) at a specific point in time. Mass spectrometry and NMR spectroscopy are the techniques most often used for metabolome profiling.

data.name: Drug Regulation
data.description: Drug regulation is the control of drug use by international agreement and/or by regulatory authorities such as the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the Japanese Pharmaceutical and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA). This includes regulations concerned with the development, approval, manufacturing and marketing of drugs.

data.name: Economic Geology
data.description: Economic geology is the study of Earth materials that can be used for economic or industrial processes.

data.name: Time-domain Astronomy
data.description: Time domain astronomy is the study of how astronomical objects, especially those beyond the Solar System, change with time. This may be due to movement or changes in the object itself. Common targets included are supernovae, novas, flare stars, blazars and active galactic nuclei.

data.name: Brain Mapping
data.description: Brain mapping is a set of neuroscience techniques predicated on the mapping of (biological) quantities or properties onto spatial representations of the (human or non-human) brain resulting in maps.

data.name: Islets of Langerhans
data.description: The islets of Langerhans are the regions of the pancreas that contain cells that produce hormones. There are five types of cells in the islets of Langerhans: beta cells secrete insulin; alpha cells secrete glucagon; PP cells secrete pancreatic polypeptide; delta cells secrete somatostatin; and epsilon cells secrete ghrelin.

data.name: Cell-nanoparticle Interaction
data.description: Particle-cell interactions are interactions resulting from the physical and chemical contact of nanoparticles with biological cells. Nanoparticle–cell interactions play an important role in the targeted delivery of therapeutics to a tissue and in nanotoxicology.

data.name: German
data.description: German refers to the language spoken primarily in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and other German-speaking regions. It is a West Germanic language and is one of the most widely spoken languages in Europe.

data.name: Inhibition
data.description: Inhibition in the nervous system occurs when a neuron or circuit is rendered less likely to generate an action potential. It generally involves the release of an inhibitory neurotransmitter such as GABA, which acts to hyperpolarize a neuron and thus increase the threshold for depolarization and action potential generation.

data.name: Plant Breeding
data.description: Plant breeding is the production of plants by selective mating or hybridization. It is the traditional mechanism for producing new varieties of plants for horticulture and agriculture.

data.name: Infection
data.description: Infection is the invasion by and multiplication of 'foreign' microorganisms that can cause pathological conditions or diseases in the host organism.

data.name: Meiosis
data.description: Meiosis is the generation of germ cells (eggs and sperm). In meiosis, DNA replication is followed by two division cycles: meiosis I, which segregates homologous chromosomes and meiosis II, which segregates sister chromatids. Thus, four daughter cells are generated that each contains one homologue of each chromosome.

data.name: Metal Oxides
data.description: Metal oxides are solid chemical compounds that contain a metal cation and an oxide anion.

data.name: Pattern Recognition Receptors
data.description: Pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) are expressed by cells in the body in order to sense molecules that are associated with infection or tissue damage. They are important for activating the immune system.

data.name: Thyroid Gland
data.description: The thyroid gland is a butterfly-shaped endocrine gland located in the neck underneath the cartilage tissue that forms the Adam's apple. By producing hormones, such as tri-iodothyronine (T3), tetraiodothyronine (T4) and calcitonin, the thyroid gland regulates a number of functions, for example the metabolic rate of cells and blood calcium levels.

data.name: Air Microbiology
data.description: Air microbiology is a scientific discipline that concerns the microorganisms, including bacteria, archaea, fungi and viruses, in the atmospheric air. It is a subdiscipline of environmental microbiology.

data.name: Literary Diction
data.description: Diction is a writer's or speaker's distinctive vocabulary choices and style of expression in a literary work, poem or story. In its common meaning, it is the distinctiveness of speech.

data.name: Arabic
data.description: Arabic is a Semitic language belonging to the Afro-Asiatic language family. It is primarily spoken in the Arab world, which spans across the Middle East and North Africa. Arabic is one of the world's major languages, Arabic is known for its unique alphabet, written from right to left, and its complex grammatical structure.

data.name: Pain Management
data.description: Pain management refers to a therapy that is directed at ameliorating pain and suffering and improving health-related quality of life in patients with pain. It includes analgaesic, anxiolytic and non-pharmacological treatments.

data.name: Earth Core Processes
data.description: Core processes describe the transfer of heat and material between the Earth’s solid inner core and molten outer core and the exchange of heat across the core-mantle boundary, as well as the convection in the outer core that generates the geomagnetic field.

data.name: Information Theory
data.description: Information theory is the scientific study of the quantification, storage, and communication of information.  Applications range from data telecommunications to evolution, brain science and cosmology. This scientific field is at the intersection of probability theory, statistics, computer science, statistical mechanics, information engineering, and electrical engineering.

data.name: Literacy
data.description: Literacy in its broadest sense describes "particular ways of thinking about and doing reading and writing" with the purpose of understanding or expressing thoughts or ideas in written form in some specific context of use.

subjects.term: EDUCATION / Teaching Methods & Materials / Reading & Phonics

data.name: Systematic Botany
data.description: Concerned with the range and diversity of organisms and their relationships, particularly as determined by their evolutionary history

data.name: Partial Differential Equations on Manifolds
data.description: A manifold is a mathematical space that locally resembles Euclidean space but may have a more complex global structure. PDEs on manifolds are used to describe and analyze various physical, geometric, and differential geometric phenomena that occur on these curved spaces. The formulation of PDEs on manifolds takes into account the geometric properties of the manifold, such as its curvature and metric, which are essential for understanding the behavior of solutions.

data.name: Placebo Effect
data.description: The placebo effect is the beneficial outcome caused by a treatment that is not attributable to the pharmacological properties of the treament itself. This effect occurs if, for example, individuals taking pills with no active pharmacological agent have improved health outcomes compared with those taking no pills.

data.name: Green Criminology
data.description: Green criminology is a specialized subfield within criminology that focuses on the study of environmental crimes, harms, and conflicts. It examines the criminal and harmful behaviors that have an impact on the environment, including illegal activities related to pollution, wildlife trafficking, illegal logging, hazardous waste disposal, and other forms of ecological destruction.

data.name: Musculoskeletal Models
data.description: Musculoskeletal models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of human musculoskeletal development, function or disease. For example, rodents have been used to study musculoskeletal disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis.

data.name: Economic Geography
data.description: Economic geography is the subfield of human geography which studies economic activity and factors affecting them. It can also be considered a subfield or method in economics.[1] There are four branches of economic geography.

data.name: Forensic Medicine
data.description: The branch of medicine dealing with the application of medical knowledge to establish facts in civil or criminal legal cases, such as an investigation into the cause and time of a suspicious death.

subjects.term: Forensic medicine. Medical jurisprudence. Legal medicine

data.name: Gender and ICT
data.description: Gender and ICT refers to the study of the relationship between gender and information and communication technologies, exploring the ways in which these technologies affect and are affected by gender roles, relationships, and inequalities. This area of research investigates topics such as digital access, digital literacy, technological innovation, and online gender-based harassment.

synonyms: Technologies affect and are affected by gender roles

data.name: Fungi
data.description: Fungi are organisms that are grouped in a distinct kingdom within the eukaryotes. This kingdom includes diverse organisms ranging from microorganisms such as yeasts or moulds to large multicellular mushrooms.

data.name: Pollen
data.description: Pollen is the powder produced by the male sex organs of seed plants which contains the microgametophytes, which in turn produce the male gametes. Pollen grains have a hard coat that protects the sperm cells during their movement to the female sex organs in order to effect fertilization.

data.name: Myelin biology and repair
data.description: Myelin biology and repair refers to the science of myelin physiology, manufacture, and how myelin damage in either the peripheral or central nervous systems can be repaired. Myelin – produced by Schwann cells in the periphery and oligodendrocytes in the CNS – is defective in diseases such as multiple sclerosis, and many myelin repair strategies aim to mitigate this damage.

data.name: Immunoprecipitation
data.description: Immunoprecipitation is a method for isolating a target molecule from a solution or cell lysate using an antibody that recognizes it. In the most common version, binding of antibody to a peptide antigen forms an aggregate (including any binding partners or complexes) that precipitates and can be concentrated by centrifugation.

data.name: Dental Diseases
data.description: People typically use the term “dental problems” to refer to conditions that affect oral health. Dental problems include cavities, tooth erosion, gum infections, and gum diseases.

data.name: Ca2+ imaging
data.description: Calcium (Ca2+) imaging is a method for visualizing the local concentration of calcium in cells or tissues. It relies on fluorescent indicators, including small chemical indicators and genetically encoded calcium indicators (GECIs), that change spectral properties upon binding calcium.

data.name: Dental Public Health
data.description: Dental public health is defined as “the science and art of preventing and controlling dental diseases and promoting dental health through organized community efforts.”

data.name: Special Emergency Medicine
data.description: Special Emergency Medicine is the medical speciality concerned with the care of illnesses or injuries requiring advanced expertise in a defined clinical field, such as cardiac, neurological, pediatric, toxicological, or trauma emergencies.

data.name: Pharmacogenetics
data.description: Pharmacogenetics examines how variation in a single gene or a small set of genes influences an individual’s response to a drug, pharmaceutical agent, or other xenobiotic. It focuses on specific genetic variants that alter drug metabolism, efficacy, or the risk of adverse effects. The field identifies gene–drug relationships that can inform individualized treatment decisions.

data.name: Reproductive Disorders
data.description: Reproductive disorders are diseases involving the reproductive system, including reproductive tract infections, congenital abnormalities, cancers of the reproductive system and sexual dysfunction.

data.name: Single-molecule Fluorescence
data.description: Single-molecule fluorescence experiments involve the study of individual fluorescent molecules, and can provide information that would be hidden in measurements involving a large number of molecules. Techniques for probing single-molecule fluorescence include total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy (TIRF microscopy).

data.name: Geodesy
