data.description: Geodesy is the study of accurately measuring and understanding Earth's geometric shape, orientation in space and gravitational field. The field also incorporates studies of how these properties change over time and equivalent measurements for other planets.

subjects.term: Geographical information systems, geodata and remote sensing

data.name: Feminist Anthropology
data.description: Feminist anthropology is a subfield of anthropology that emerged in the late 20th century and is characterized by its focus on gender and the exploration of women's roles, experiences, and contributions in different societies and cultures. It seeks to address historical imbalances and biases in traditional anthropological research that often neglected or marginalized the study of women and their perspectives.

data.name: Marine Chemistry
data.description: Marine chemistry is the study of the chemical composition and chemical processes of the world’s oceans. Some of the key processes studied are the cycling of: inorganic and organic carbon; nutrients, such as nitrogen and phosphorus; and trace elements, such as iron.

data.name: Immunogenetics
data.description: Immunogenetics is the study of the genetic basis of the immune response. It includes the study of normal immunological pathways and the identification of genetic variations that result in immune defects, which may result in the identification of new therapeutic targets for immune diseases.

data.name: Computational Neuroscience
data.description: Computational neuroscience includes both the study of the information processing functions of the nervous system, and the use of digital computers to study the nervous system. It is an interdisciplinary science that links the diverse fields of neuroscience, cognitive science and psychology, electrical engineering, computer science, physics and mathematics. Computational neuroscience is the field of study in which mathematical tools and theories are used to investigate brain function. It can also incorporate diverse approaches from electrical engineering, computer science and physics in order to understand how the nervous system processes information.

data.name: Biological Databases
data.description: Biological databases are libraries of life sciences information, collected from scientific experiments, published literature, high-throughput experiment technology, and computational analysis.

data.name: Fistula Creation
data.description: An arteriovenous fistula creation is a surgical procedure performed by a vascular surgeon to create a connection between an artery and a vein. The fistula is usually placed on the forearm or upper arm; however, it may also be placed on the leg.

data.name: Agroecology
data.description: Agroecology is the study of the ecology of terrestrial agricultural systems. It includes both the effects of agricultural practices such as pesticide use on non-domesticated species, and the effect of the ecological environment on crop and livestock yields.

subjects.term: Ecology of environments made by humans

data.name: Socioeconomic Scenarios
data.description: Socioeconomic scenarios are plausible representations of the future based on coherent, and internally consistent, assumptions about the evolution of key social and economic drivers. Examples of these drivers are economic growth, technological development and population. They are not intended to be predictive, but are designed to explore the implications of different futures.

data.name: Membrane Potential
data.description: The membrane potential of a neuron refers to the relative difference of ionic (electric) charge across a membrane. It is created by differential ion concentrations, maintained by ion channels and ion transporters, and for most neurons, the resting membrane potential is around -70 mV. Changes in membrane potential are associated with depolarization and hyperpolarization.

data.name: Crystallography and Scattering Methods
data.description: Crystallography is the experimental science of determining the arrangement of atoms in crystalline solids.

data.name: Feeding Behaviour
data.description: Feeding behaviour refers to the set of actions and processes through which organisms obtain, select, and consume food. It includes activities such as foraging, hunting, grazing, and scavenging. Feeding behaviour is influenced by factors such as nutritional needs, environmental conditions, and physiological mechanisms (e.g., hunger and metabolism), and can vary across species depending on ecological context and diet.

data.name: Health Policy
data.description: Health policy is the set of decisions and plans, developed by governmental or nongovernmental agencies, designed to promote specific health-care objectives. Policies can be directed at individuals, physicians, pharmaceutical companies, or health-care systems. Examples include tobacco control policies and those designed to promote equal opportunites to access care.

data.name: Carbohydrate Chemistry
data.description: Carbohydrate chemistry is the branch of organic chemistry that focuses on the study of carbohydrates, which are a group of biomolecules composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms. Carbohydrates play crucial roles in living organisms, serving as a major source of energy, structural components, and cell signaling molecules.

data.name: Nucleic Acid Therapeutics
data.description: Nucleic acid therapeutics are based on nucleic acids or closely related chemical compounds. They include antisense oligonucleotides, aptamers and small interfering RNAs, and are typically considered in cases where specific inhibition of the function of a particular gene involved in disease is thought to be therapeutically desirable.

data.name: Internal Combustion Engines
data.description: Heat engine where the combustion of a fuel occurs with an oxidizer in a combustion chamber that is an integral part of the working fluid flow circuit. In particular Diesel and Otto Engines. Turbomachines are a separate concept.

data.name: Metabolic Disease
data.description: Metabolic disorders occur when the body's usual metabolic processes are disrupted. These diseases can be congenital or acquired, for example, diabetes and phenylketonuria.

data.name: Automotive Infrastructure and Services
data.description: Automotive Infrastructure and Services refer to the supporting framework, facilities, and services that enable the operation, maintenance, and development of vehicles and transportation systems. This includes the physical infrastructure like roads, highways, charging stations, and parking facilities, as well as the services and technologies that enhance the driving experience and vehicle performance.

data.name: ESCRT
data.description: The ESCRT (endosomal complexes required for transport) complexes are cytoplasmic proteins that are involved in membrane budding or bending events, such as multivesicular body biogenesis, the abscission step of cell division, and viral budding. There are four ESCRT complexes (ESCRT-0, -I, -II, and -III).

synonyms: Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport Machinery
Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport
Endosomal Sorting Complexes Required for Transport
Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport I

data.name: Obstetrics
data.description: The branch of medical science that deals with problems and difficulties of pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period. To be distinguished from midwifery which emphasizes the normalcy of pregnancy while acknowledging the vulnerability associated with the reproductive process.

data.name: Bioethics
data.description: Bioethics is the study of ethical, social, and legal issues that arise in biomedicine and biomedical research.

data.name: Data Acquisition
data.description: Data acquisition is the process of converting measurements, such as temperature, pressure, relative humidity, light, resistance, current, power, speed and vibration, into digital numeric values that can be manipulated by a computer. During data acquisition physical measurements are converted into a voltage that is in turn transformed into a binary number by a digital-to-analog converter.

data.name: Innate Immune Cells
data.description: Innate immune cells are white blood cells that mediate innate immunity and include basophils, dendritic cells, eosinophils, Langerhans cells, mast cells, monocytes and macrophages, neutrophils and NK cells.

data.name: Immunological Models
data.description: Immunological models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of the human immune system to study its development and function in health and disease. The most common are transgenic or genetic mouse models with altered immunity.

data.name: Environmental Economics
data.description: Environmental economics is the study of the economics of ecological and environmental issues. It focuses on the monetary value of ecosystems and the costs and benefits of environmental policies.

subjects.term: Land, recreational and wilderness areas, energy
Environmental policy and economic development. Sustainable development

data.name: Quantitative Criminology
data.description: Quantitative criminology is a subfield of criminology that utilizes quantitative research methods and statistical analysis to examine patterns, trends, and relationships related to crime and criminal behavior. It involves the collection and analysis of numerical data, such as crime rates, offender characteristics, and factors associated with criminal activities, to gain insights and make empirical assessments within the field of criminology.

data.name: Neurological Models
data.description: Neurological models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of human neurological development, function or disease. For example, induced pluripotent stem cells derived from patients with neurological disease, and genetic and transgenic animal models allow the study of neuronal activity and dysfunction.

data.name: Medical Genomics
data.description: Medical genomics is the application and integration of genomic and other data - including functional genomics, genome structure, genome-scale population genetics, epigenomics, proteomics, systems analysis and pharmacogenomics - to better understand the genetic bases of drug response and disease.

data.name: Interpreting
data.description: Interpreting refers to the oral conversion of spoken language from one language to another in real-time. Interpreters play a crucial role in facilitating communication between individuals or groups who do not share a common language.

data.name: Astronomical Optics
data.description: Astronomical optics is a branch of optics that focuses on the design, construction, and use of optical instruments for observing and studying celestial objects. It involves the application of optical principles and technologies to develop telescopes, lenses, mirrors, and other optical systems used in astronomy.

data.name: Optogenetics
data.description: Optogenetics is a method that uses light to modulate molecular events in a targeted manner in living cells or organisms. It relies on the use of genetically-encoded proteins that change conformation in the presence of light to alter cell behaviour, for example, by changing the membrane voltage potential of excitable cells.

data.name: Plant Cell Death
data.description: Plant cell death is the intracellular program of events resulting in the termination of a plant cell's life processes. Forms of plant cell death include necrosis, apoptosis and autophagy.

data.name: Working Memory
data.description: Working memory is the active and robust retention of multiple bits of information over the time-scale of a few seconds. It is distinguished from short-term memory by the involvement of executive or attentional control that makes the information flexible yet resistant to interference.

data.name: Biodiversity
data.description: Biodiversity is the variation in living forms and can be measured in ways that include the number of species, functional variety of species, evenness of species distribution or genetic diversity. Biodiversity science investigates levels of biodiversity, its functional effects, and how and why it changes over time.

data.name: Democracy
data.description: Democracy is a form of government in which the people have the authority to deliberate and decide legislation, or to choose governing officials to do so.

data.name: Dentine
data.description: Dentine is a calcified tissue of the body and, along with enamel, cementum, and pulp, is one of the four major components of teeth.

synonyms: Hard dense bony tissue forming the bulk of a tooth

data.name: Dental Business
data.description: Dental business  means the development, manufacture, marketing and sale of Dental products as well as the managment of a dental practice.

data.name: Invadopodia
data.description: Invadopodia are dynamic actin-rich membrane protrusions that degrade the extracellular matrix through the local deposition of proteases and are involved in cell invasion. Invadopodia are found on cancer cells and are similar to the podosomes of normal cells.

data.name: Radiation Dosimetry and Radiation Protection
data.description: Dosimetry measure, calculates, and assesses the exposure of individuals and the environment to ionizing radiation. It encompasses the development and application of dosimetric techniques to quantify radiation doses received by biological tissues, ensuring that exposure levels remain within safe limits to prevent harmful effects. Radiation protection tires to minimize radiation risks in medical, industrial, and research settings. Key components include the use of dosimeters, which are devices that measure radiation exposure, and the establishment of guidelines and standards for radiation safety, aimed at safeguarding public health and the environment.

data.name: Chronic Inflammation
data.description: Chronic inflammation refers to a prolonged inflammatory response that involves a progressive change in the type of cells present at the site of inflammation. It is characterized by the simultaneous destruction and repair of the tissue from the inflammatory process. It can follow an acute form of inflammation or be a prolonged low-grade form.

data.name: General Anesthesia
data.description: General anaesthesia is a state of controlled unconsciousness. During a general anaesthetic, medicines are used to send you to sleep, so you're unaware of surgery and do not move or feel pain while it's carried out.

data.name: Crossbreeding
data.description: Crossbreeding, also known as outbreeding, is the process of mating individuals from different breeds, populations, or species to produce offspring with desirable traits or characteristics. It involves combining the genetic material from two distinct parent lines to create a new genetic combination in the offspring. Crossbreeding is commonly employed in agriculture, animal breeding, and plant breeding to improve various traits, such as productivity, disease resistance, adaptability, and overall performance.

data.name: Soft Lithography
data.description: Soft lithography refers to printing and moulding techniques to produce microstructures or nanostructures from elastomeric polymer such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The techniques are flexible and inexpensive.

data.name: Engineering Ethics
data.description: Engineering ethics is a branch of applied ethics that focuses on the ethical considerations, values, and responsibilities of engineers in their professional practice. It involves examining the moral dilemmas and decision-making processes that engineers encounter in designing, developing, and implementing technological solutions.

data.name: Inflammasome
data.description: The inflammasome is a multiprotein intracellular complex that detects pathogenic microorganisms and sterile stressors, and that activates the highly pro-inflammatory cytokines interleukin-1b (IL-1b) and IL-18. Inflammasomes also induce a form of cell death termed pyroptosis. Dysregulation of inflammasomes is associated with a number of autoinflammatory syndromes and autoimmune diseases.

data.name: Optical Spectroscopy
data.description: Optical spectroscopy encompasses a wide variety of techniques used to study how matter interacts with light. Optical spectroscopy techniques are used in physics, astronomy, chemistry, biology, and associated research fields.

subjects.term: Properties of materials and nondestructive testing

data.name: Financial Crises
data.description: A financial crisis is any of a broad variety of situations in which some financial assets suddenly lose a large part of their nominal value.

subjects.term: Economic and financial crises and disasters

data.name: Ectoderm
data.description: The ectoderm is the outermost layer of cells in very early vertebrate and insect embryos. It is one of the three primary germ cell layers and gives rise to the epidermis and nervous system.

data.name: Preventive Dentistry
data.description: Preventive dentistry is the practice of caring for your teeth to keep them healthy. This helps to avoid cavities, gum disease, enamel wear, and more.

data.name: Antibody Isolation and Purification
data.description: Antibody isolation and purification is the concentration of an antibody or antibodies that recognize a specific target molecule and the removal of non-specific antibodies and contaminants. Pure isolated antibodies tend to have greater activity and are less likely to cross-react with non-target molecules than impure mixtures.

data.name: Aldosterone
data.description: Aldosterone is a hormone produced in the adrenal gland. This steroid molecule, derived from cholesterol, promotes retention of sodium and water and lowers the levels of potassium in the blood through many mechanisms, including action on the mineralocorticoid receptors in the kidneys. It plays a central role in the regulation of blood pressure.

data.name: Paleoecology
data.description: Palaeoecology is the study of past ecosystems using palaeontological methods. Fossil data are used to reconstruct interactions between different species and between species and their environment.

subjects.term: Paleoecology and fossils of specific environment

data.name: Dental Conditions
data.description: Conditions that effect the teeth, number of teeth and structure of teeth

data.name: Membrane Fusion
data.description: Membrane fusion involves the merging of two separate membranes into a single contiguous membrane. This process is often catalysed by SNARE proteins and is involved in exocytosis, autophagy, membrane trafficking and organelle homeostasis.

data.name: Tumour Vaccines
data.description: A tumour vaccine is an agent used for cancer therapy or cancer prevention that elicits an immune response and induces protective immunity against specific molecules (antigens) expressed on tumour cells. There are currently no vaccines that can prevent cancer from developing, but some therapeutic tumour vaccines have shown promise in patients with selected cancers.

data.name: Rehabilitation Psychology
data.description: Rehabilitation psychology is a field of study that focuses on promoting the psychological well-being, functional independence, and quality of life of individuals with disabilities or chronic health conditions. It involves understanding the impact of physical, cognitive, emotional, and social limitations on individuals' functioning and developing interventions to enhance their adjustment, coping skills, and overall rehabilitation outcomes. Rehabilitation psychologists work collaboratively with individuals, their families, and healthcare professionals to facilitate the recovery process, improve functioning, and optimize participation in daily activities and society.

data.name: Urinary Tract
data.description: Urinary tract is the term used to describe the series of structures involved in the production, storage and excretion of urine. The urinary tract encompasses the kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra.

data.name: Pedology
data.description: Study of soil in its natural setting

data.name: Neural Progenitors
data.description: Neural progenitor cells are lineage-committed descendants of neural stem cells that can self-renew to a limited extent and generate multiple neural cell types, including various neurons and glia, but not non-neural cells.

data.name: Nutrition Disorder
data.description: Nutrition disorders are diseases that occur when a person's dietary intake does not contain the right amount of nutrients for healthy functioning, or when a person cannot correctly absorb nutrients from food. Nutrition disorders can be caused by undernutrition, overnutrition or an incorrect balance of nutrients.

data.name: Disease-free Survival
data.description: Disease-free survival is a concept used to describe the period after a successful treatment during which there are no signs and symptoms of the disease that was treated. This concept is commonly used in cancer therapy and other situations where no definitive cure is available.

data.name: Digital Sociology
data.description: Digital Sociology is the study of the relationship between digital technologies, social processes, and human behavior. This field explores topics such as the impact of the internet and social media on social interactions, the digital divide, online privacy, and the role of digital technologies in shaping social institutions, identities, and inequalities.

data.name: Model Prokaryotes
data.description: Model prokaryotes are extensively studied prokaryotes (bacteria and archaea) chosen as tools for molecular biology or biotechnology, for their role as disease agents, or for the ease of investigating particular biological phenomena.

data.name: Cell Wall
data.description: The plant cell wall is a complex matrix of linked polysaccharides such as cellulose and pectin, forming a thick semi-permeable rigid barrier outside the plasma membrane. It physically protects and constrains the cell, and its exact composition is highly variable depending on the species.

data.name: Phagocytosis
data.description: Phagocytosis is a specialised form of endocytosis in which a cell engulfs solid particles from the extracellular space. Microorganisms, dead or dying cells, and cell debris can be engulfed by phagocytosis. Once internalised, the engulfed particles are contained within a phagosome, which then fuses with the lysosomes for degradation.

data.name: Structure And Bonding
data.description: Structure and bonding refer to the arrangement of atoms and the forces that hold them together in molecules or solid materials. It encompasses the study of how atoms form chemical bonds and the resulting molecular or solid-state structures.

data.name: Laboratory Astrophysics
data.description: Laboratory Astrophysics uses laboratory experiments based on condensation, irradiation-induced processing, and spectroscopy of cosmic dust grains and molecules to investigate some of the key astrophysical processes in the interstellar medium and circumstellar environments.

data.name: Interstellar Medium
data.description: The interstellar medium is the matter and radiation that exists in the space between the star systems in a galaxy. This matter includes gas in ionic, atomic, and molecular form, as well as dust and cosmic rays. It fills interstellar space and blends smoothly into the surrounding intergalactic space.

data.name: Cadherins
data.description: Cadherins are transmembrane proteins that contain calcium-binding domains, termed 'cadherin repeats' in their extracellular regions. As the major constituents of adherens junctions, cadherins of adjacent cells mediate intercellular adhesion by interacting with each other, and by associating with specialized protein complexes linked to the actin cytoskeleton through their intracellular regions.

data.name: tRNAs
data.description: Transfer RNAs (tRNAs) are a type of non-coding ribonucleic acid (ncRNA) that carry specific amino acids and recognize unique messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences. The pairing of a tRNA to its compatible mRNA sequence within the ribosome is the basis for the translation of RNA into protein.

data.name: Signalling Gradients
data.description: A signalling gradient is a progressive increase or decrease in the levels of a signalling molecule across a tissue or cell, usually arising as a result of the diffusion of soluble signalling molecules from their sources. Gradients of signalling molecules are involved in processes including tissue patterning, chemotaxis and axon guidance

data.name: Caveolae
data.description: Caveolae are lipid-rich craters in the plasma membrane with roles in exocytosis, endocytosis and signal transduction. Caveolae are formed by caveolin oligomers stabilised by cytoplasmic cavin proteins. On internalisation, caveolae can fuse with early endosomes, and then be recycled back to the plasma membrane or targeted to multivesicular bodies for degradation.

data.name: Synaptic Plasticity
data.description: Synaptic plasticity is the biological process by which specific patterns of synaptic activity result in changes in synaptic strength and is thought to contribute to learning and memory. Both pre-synaptic and post-synaptic mechanisms can contribute to the expression of synaptic plasticity.

data.name: Adaptive Radiation
data.description: Adaptive radiation is the process by which a single lineage undergoes multiple speciation events to fill divergent ecological niches. This results in a cluster of phenotypically distinct, related species and often occurs after a physical disturbance or extinction event opens up new niches for exploitation.

data.name: Dynamic Combinatorial Chemistry
data.description: Dynamic combinatorial chemistry is an approach to molecular design in which building blocks combine through reversible chemical reactions to form libraries of complex structures. These dynamic combinatorial libraries are responsive to external influence (biomolecules, for example), which alter the relative thermodynamic stabilities of members of the library and can shift product distributions.

data.name: Orthodontics
data.description: Orthodontics is a specialist branch of dentistry. The term "orthodontics" can be broken down into two Greek words - "orthos" meaning straight or correct and "dontics" meaning teeth. Orthodontics therefore describes the practice of straightening misaligned teeth or malocclusions.

data.name: Boreal Ecology
data.description: Boreal ecology is the study of ecosystems in the subarctic (boreal) zone of the Northern hemisphere. These areas are dominated by coniferous forest, generally have permafrost soils, and occur below the Arctic tundra latitudes.

data.name: Transformation Optics
data.description: Transformation optics is a technique that simplifies the modelling of optical devices by altering the coordinate system, warping space to control the trajectories of light rays. The mathematical tool has proved particularly useful in the development of metamaterials.

data.name: Gene Regulatory Networks
data.description: A gene regulatory network is a set of genes, or parts of genes, that interact with each other to control a specific cell function. Gene regulatory networks are important in development, differentiation and responding to environmental cues.

data.name: Peptide
data.description: Peptides are amino acid polymers. They are generally much smaller than proteins and don't have sufficient activity on their own  they generally represent a small portion of a full protein. They may also be signaling molecules that act through interaction with specific receptors, as in peptide hormones and cytokines.

data.name: Cardiac Device Therapy
data.description: Cardiac device therapy is the use of devices in the treatment of patients with arrhythmias or heart failure. Commonly used devices include implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, devices for cardiac resynchronization therapy, and ventricular assist devices.

data.name: Enzymes
data.description: Enzymes catalyze nearly all of the chemical reactions that occur in biological systems. Enzymes are generally proteins but also include catalytic DNA and catalytic RNA. As effective biological catalysts, enzymes work by lowering a reaction's activation energy barrier, thereby increasing the rate of the reaction. They also improve the specificity of the reactions.

data.name: Cytogenetics
data.description: Cytogenetics is the study of chromosomal structure, location and function in cells. It includes the study of chromosome number and appearance (karyotyping), the physical location of genes on chromosomes, and chromosomal behaviour in processes such as cell division.

data.name: Antibody fragment therapy
data.description: Antibody fragment therapies are a type of biologic. They are typically fragments of monoclonal antibodies selected to bind to a particular protein (often a cell-surface protein), and produced using recombinant DNA technology.

data.name: Nucleus
data.description: The nucleus is the double membrane limited structure within an eukaryotic cell that contains the chromosomes, and where the DNA is replicated or transcribed into RNA. The membrane is perforated by nuclear pores within the double-membrane to allow exchanges between the nucleus and the cytosplasm.

data.name: Personality
data.description: Personality refers to the unique pattern of thoughts, feelings, and behaviors that characterize an individual and distinguish them from others. It encompasses a wide range of psychological traits and characteristics that are relatively enduring over time and across different situations. These traits may include aspects such as emotional stability, sociability, openness to experience, conscientiousness, and agreeableness, among others. Personality can be studied and measured through various psychological tools and assessments, and it plays a crucial role in shaping an individual's behavior, relationships, and overall well-being.

subjects.term: Psychology: the self, ego, identity, personality

data.name: Transporters in the Nervous System
data.description: Transporters in the nervous system are proteins that span the plasma membrane and are involved in movement of ions and molecules across the membrane. They include neurotransmitter transporters, which move neurotransmitters or their metabolites from the extracellular space into a neuron, and vesicular transporters, which are involved in filling synaptic vesicles.

data.name: Neural Ageing
data.description: Neural ageing is the process by which neural cells in the brain and peripheral nervous system deteriorate structurally and functionally over time. It is associated with a decline in sensory, motor and cognitive functions of the brain.

data.name: Synthetic Organisms
data.description: Synthetic organisms are organisms for which a substantial portion of the genome or the entire genome has been designed or engineered.

data.name: Radiation Oncology
data.description: Radiotherapy, or radiation therapy, is the clinical use of high energy rays (ionizing radiation) to induce DNA damage in all exposed cells to ultimately kill cancer cells or prevent cancer growth. Radiotherapy may be used to eradicate some cancers, to reduce recurrence or as palliative treatment.

data.name: Shakespeare
data.description: William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet and actor.

data.name: Organic Farming
data.description: Organic farming is an agricultural practice that emphasizes the use of natural and sustainable methods to cultivate crops and raise livestock. It aims to minimize the use of synthetic chemicals, pesticides, genetically modified organisms (GMOs), and other artificial inputs. Instead, organic farming relies on ecological processes, biodiversity, and organic inputs to maintain soil fertility, promote healthy plant growth, and ensure animal welfare.

data.name: Genomic Instability
data.description: Chromosome instability describes the increased probability of acquiring chromosomal aberrations due to defects in processes such as DNA repair, replication or chromosome segregation.

data.name: Precambrian Geology
data.description: Precambrian geology is the study of solid Earth and environmental processes that occurred during the Precambrian supereon.

data.name: Coordination Chemistry
data.description: Coordination chemistry is the study of compounds that have a central atom (often metallic) surrounded by molecules or anions, known as ligands. The ligands are attached to the central atom by dative bonds, also known as coordinate bonds, in which both electrons in the bond are supplied by the same atom on the ligand.

data.name: Signal Transduction
data.description: Transformative Signal Processing is the transmission of information with a modification, so that the new form of information may be exploited by downstream devices, as in sound converted to nerve impulses from ear to neurons. The scientific study of signal processing implicates information theory and is key to telecommunications or biology.

data.name: Cajal Bodies
data.description: Cajal bodies are regions within the nucleus that are enriched in proteins and RNAs involved in mRNA processing. They are the main sites for the assembly of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs).

data.name: Quiescence
data.description: Quiescence is the reversible state of a cell in which it does not divide but retains the ability to re-enter cell proliferation. Some adult stem cells are maintained in a quiescent state and can be rapidly activated when stimulated, for example by injury to the tissue in which they reside.

data.name: Care Systems and Practices
data.description: Care Systems and Practices is a field that investigates the organization, provision, and quality of care for individuals and groups, such as children, the elderly, and people with disabilities. This includes examining formal care systems like healthcare, social services, and long-term care, as well as informal care provided by families and communities.

data.name: Austronesian Languages
data.description: Austronesian languages refer to a language family that spans a vast region of the world, including Southeast Asia, Oceania, and parts of East Africa. example such as Malay/Indonesian, Javanese, Filipino/Tagalog, Malagasy, Maori, Hawaiian, etc.

data.name: Podosomes
data.description: Podosomes are dynamic actin-rich cellular protrusions that degrade the extracellular matrix through local proteolysis. Podosomes are involved in the motile function of normal cells, for example osteoclasts and certain immune cells. Invadopodia are related structures found on cancer cells.

data.name: Tonsils
data.description: Tonsils are clusters of lymphoid tissues located around the throat that help to fight infections. They can become swollen and enlarged as a result of infection and may need to be surgically removed.

data.name: Juries and Criminal Trials
data.description: Juries and Criminal Trials is the study of the role of jurors and the jury system in the administration of criminal justice. This area of research explores topics such as jury selection, jury decision-making, the impact of evidence and persuasion on jury verdicts, and the effectiveness of juries in providing fair and impartial trials.

data.name: Acute Inflammation
data.description: Acute inflammation is a short-term process occurring in response to tissue injury, usually appearing within minutes or hours. It is characterized by five cardinal signs: pain, redness, immobility (loss of function), swelling and heat.

data.name: Inhibition-excitation Balance
data.description: Inhibiton–excitation balance (E–I balance) is a form of homeostatic plasticity that helps to maintain neuronal activity within a narrow, safe range. It refers to the relative degree of excitatory and inhibitory drive in a neural circuit, and is established during development and is maintained in the mature nervous system.

synonyms: Balance of inhibitory and excitatory activity

data.name: Flow Cytometry
data.description: Flow cytometry is a technology for assaying labelled cells suspended in fluid and passed through a detector. The labels are usually fluorescent and used for counting and sorting the cells in a signal dependent manner, but other labels and detection methods can also be used. Imaging flow cytometers can take a fluorescence image of each cell.

data.name: Disease Genetics
data.description: Disease genetics, of human, animal and plant diseases, investigates the consequences of pathogenic (host) genetic variants as the major causes of heritable disorders (monogenic diseases) as well as the consequences of genome variation in the population to the variable predisposition of the individual to complex diseases with infectious or environmental causes.

data.name: Immunoblotting
data.description: Immunoblotting is an in vitro technique for detecting specific proteins using antibodies. Protein mixtures are transferred to a filter membrane either directly or after separation by electrophoresis, then probed with antibodies that are either labelled (e.g. with fluorophore or an enzyme) or bound by a labelled secondary antibody for detection.

data.name: Dental Psychology
data.description: Dental Psychology examines the contributions of the behavioral sciences to the practice of dentistry, drawing subject matter from a wide range of disciplines that include psychology, sociology, education, anthropology, economics, epidemiology, health services, and public health.

data.name: Ordinary Differential Equations
data.description: In mathematics, an ordinary differential equation (ODE) is a differential equation containing one or more functions of one independent variable and its derivatives. The term ordinary is used in contrast with the term partial differential equation which may be with respect to more than one independent variable.

data.name: Planting Field Trials
data.description: Field trials in plant biotechnology are designed to test promising new plants in a situation similar to the actual growing conditions by farmers, such as unpredictable light and temperature, the presence of unknown microbes and animals in the soil, and competing weeds.

data.name: Superconducting Devices
data.description: Superconducting devices are electronic devices that harness the zero-resistance properties of superconductors. Superconducting devices are used for highly sensitive optical sensors, detectors of magnetic fields and low-noise amplifiers. Superconducting circuits are one possible type of qubit, the building blocks of quantum computers.

data.name: Voting
data.description: Voting is when a group of people decide something by saying what they want. It can be for electing a leader or representative, passing a law, and other things. When people are done voting, the votes are counted (often by machines) and the winner is determined.

subjects.term: POLITICAL SCIENCE / Political Process / Campaigns & Elections

data.name: Literature Mining
data.description: Literature mining is a specialised data mining method that is used to extract information (facts or data) from text, such as the scientific literature. Literature mining can generate new hypotheses by systematically scrutinising huge numbers of abstracts, or full text versions, of scientific publications.

data.name: Seed Distribution
data.description: Seed distribution refers to the process by which seeds are dispersed from their parent plants to new locations where they can germinate and grow into new plants. This process is crucial for the reproduction and survival of plant species, as it affects genetic diversity, population dynamics, and ecosystem health. Seed distribution can occur through various mechanisms, including abiotic factors such as wind and water, and biotic factors such as animals and humans. Wind-dispersed seeds are often lightweight and equipped with structures like wings or tufts that allow them to travel long distances. Water-dispersed seeds may float and be carried by currents to new areas. Animal-mediated seed dispersal involves animals consuming fruits and excreting seeds in different locations, which can enhance seed germination and establishment. Human activities, such as agriculture and landscaping, also play a significant role in seed distribution, often introducing non-native species to new environments. Understanding seed distribution is essential for conservation efforts, habitat restoration, and managing invasive species, as it influences plant community structure and ecosystem functioning.

data.name: Crime Prevention
data.description: Crime prevention is a field of study that focuses on strategies, interventions, and policies aimed at reducing and deterring criminal behavior within communities and societies. It involves understanding the causes and risk factors of crime, as well as identifying effective measures to prevent criminal acts and promote public safety.

data.name: Cell Culture
data.description: Cell culture is a method for growing or maintaining cells in vitro under controlled conditions. Primary cell cultures refer to dispersed cells that are cultured directly from tissues and have limited lifespan, whereas cell lines refer to immortalized cells that can be cultured indefinitely.

data.name: Disability Studies
data.description: Disability Studies is an interdisciplinary field that studies the meaning, nature and consequence of disability. Disability is understood as a social construct, as opposed to impairment of a person's mind or body.

subjects.term: People with disabilities and illnesses, gifted people

data.name: Respiratory Tract Diseases
data.description: Respiratory tract diseases are illnesses that affect components of the respiratory system, including the nasal passages, the bronchi and the lungs. They range from acute infections, such as pneumonia and bronchitis, to chronic conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

data.name: Body Patterning
data.description: Body patterning defines the processes occurring during early animal development that determine the animal's basic body plan and direct morphogenesis. Body patterning ensures that the correct cell types and consequently body parts will develop at the correct relative positions of the body.

data.name: Semiconductor Lasers
data.description: Semiconductor lasers use the optical properties of semiconducting materials to produce coherent light. Electrons and their positive-charge counterpart called holes are injected into an optically active region where they combine together and generate photons. Reflection of light from semiconductor–air or semiconductor–semiconductor interfaces proved the necessary optical feedback.

data.name: Evolution of Language
data.description: Evolution of language is the gradual change in human language over time. It involves the origin and divergence of languages and language families, and can be considered analogous to biological evolution, although it does not necessarily occur through the same mechanisms.

data.name: Comparative Sociology
data.description: Comparative sociology involves comparison of the social processes between nation states, or across different types of society (for example capitalist and socialist). There are two main approaches to comparative sociology: some seek similarity across different countries and cultures whereas others seek variance.

data.name: Salt
data.description: Salt is any ionic compound containing a metallic cation and non-metallic anion; the most common example being sodium chloride. The presence of high levels of salt in an environment, for example as a result of drought, is a major stressor of plants.

data.name: Diffusion Process
data.description: Diffusion is the passive movement of molecules or particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration

data.name: Computational Social Sciences
data.description: Computational social science refers to the academic sub-disciplines concerned with computational approaches used to model, simulate, and analyze social phenomena. It focuses on investigating social and behavioral relationships and interactions through social simulation, modeling, network analysis, and media analysis.Social Networks aim to analyze the structure of whole social entities as well as a variety of theories explaining the patterns observed in these structures. The study of these structures uses social network analysis to identify local and global patterns, locate influential entities, and examine network dynamics.

subjects.term: Computer applications in the social and behavioural sciences
Soziologie/Methoden der empirischen und qualitativen Sozialforschung

data.name: Periodontics
data.description: Periodontics is a dental specialty. The word “periodontics” comes from two Greek words: “peri,” which means “around” and “odont,” which means “tooth.” So, the field of periodontics treats conditions that affect the tissues “around your teeth,” such as bone loss, gum recession and periodontal (gum) disease.

data.name: Embodiment
data.description: Embodiment is the concept that our physical bodies significantly shape and influence our experiences, thoughts, and behaviors. This interdisciplinary field involves the study of the relationship between the body and the mind in various domains such as psychology, philosophy, and anthropology.

data.name: Stochastic Integrals
data.description: Stochastic Integrals discusses one area of diffusion processes: the differential and integral calculus based upon the Brownian motion. The book reviews Gaussian families, construction of the Brownian motion, the simplest properties of the Brownian motion, Martingale inequality, and the law of the iterated logarithm

data.name: Chromosome abnormality
data.description: Chromosome abnormality is the condition in a cell or organism where the number of chromosomes or the structure of any chromosome differs from the normal karyotype. When the variant genotype is not associated with abnormal phenotypes (traits), chromosomal abnormalities are referred to as karyotype variation or structural genome variation.

data.name: Cell Proliferation
data.description: Cell proliferation is the process that results in an increase of the number of cells, and is defined by the balance between cell divisions and cell loss through cell death or differentiation. Cell proliferation is increased in tumours.

data.name: X-Ray Spectroscopy
data.description: X-ray spectroscopy is a general term for several spectroscopic techniques for characterization of materials by using x-ray excitation

data.name: Spermatogenesis
data.description: Spermatogenesis is the development of the mature male germ cells called sperm cells or spermatozoa. Primordial germ cells, the founder cells of the germ line, develop through several immature stages by undergoing mitosis, meiosis and differentiation into the haploid spermatozoa, which carry only one set of chromosomes.

data.name: Small Intestine
data.description: The small intestine is located between the stomach and the large intestine and is composed of the duodenum, jejunum and ileum. The small intestine is the site of chemical digestion and absorption of nutrients and minerals from food.

data.name: Geomorphology
data.description: Geomorphology is the study of landforms and landscapes on Earth and other planets, and the processes that shape them. This discipline is primarily concerned with the erosion and deposition of rock and sediments by wind and water, but also includes the creation of topography through tectonics.

data.name: SNARE
data.description: SNARE (Soluble NSF Attachment Protein Receptor) proteins mediate membrane fusion events, such as vesicle fusion and exocytosis. Prior to membrane fusion, SNARE complexes exist in a trans-SNARE conformation on opposing membranes. Fusion results in the formation of cis-SNARE complexes on the same membrane.

synonyms: Soluble N ethylmaleimide Sensitive Factor Attachment Protein Receptor

data.name: Conformity
data.description: Conformity in the field of psychology refers to the tendency of individuals to adjust their thoughts, beliefs, and behaviors to match the standards and expectations of a particular group or society. It involves changing one's attitudes or actions to align with the majority opinion or social norms.

data.name: Skin Diseases
data.description: Skin diseases are pathologic conditions that affect the body's surfaces (also called the integument), including skin, hair, nails and associated glands. They can involve all layers of the skin and have numerous aetiologies such as infections, tumours or inflammation.

data.name: Theatre in Education
data.description: Theatre in education is the use of theatre for purposes beyond entertainment. It involves trained actors/educators performing theatre for students or communities, with the intention of changing knowledge, attitudes and behaviour.

data.name: Energy Access
data.description: Energy access is defined by the physical availability of electricity and modern energy carriers and improved end-use devices such as cook stoves (clean cooking).

data.name: Stem-cell Niche
data.description: A stem-cell niche is an area of a tissue that provides a specific microenvironment, in which stem cells are present in an undifferentiated and self-renewable state. Cells of the stem-cell niche interact with the stem cells to maintain them or promote their differentiation.

data.name: Romanic Literature
data.description: Romantic literature is marked by six primary characteristics: celebration of nature, focus on the individual and spirituality, celebration of isolation and melancholy, interest in the common man, idealization of women, and personification and pathetic fallacy.

data.name: Sustainable Growth
data.description: Sustainable economic growth means maintaining growth without creating economic problems or complications. It's the practise of supporting long-term economic growth without depleting resources.

subjects.term: Economic policy, economic development, economic growth
Economic development. Development economics. Economic growth

data.name: Adaptive Optics
data.description: Adaptive optics is a branch of optics and photonics that uses light-controlling components to actively correct distortion in an incoming image. These distortions can occur when light from an astronomical object passes through the Earth’s atmosphere, for example.

data.name: Topological Material
data.description: A topological material (e.g. insulator) is a material with non-trivial symmetry-protected topological order that behaves as an insulator in its interior but whose surface contains conducting states, meaning that electrons can only move along the surface of the material.

data.name: Matrix Theory
data.description: In mathematics, a matrix (plural: matrices) is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions, arranged in rows and columns

data.name: Transplantation Tolerance
data.description: Transplantation tolerance is a state in which the immune system of the recipient of a tissue or organ transplantation does not attack the transplanted tissue. Transplantation tolerance is induced by immunosuppression, and prevents rejection of the transplant.

data.name: Stochastic Modelling
data.description: "Stochastic" means being or having a random variable. Stochastic modelling is the development of mathematical models for non-deterministic physical systems, which can adopt many possible behaviours starting from any given initial condition. Monte-Carlo simulations, for example, consist of exploring the various possible states of a complex probabilistic system. A stochastic model is a tool for estimating probability distributions of potential outcomes by allowing for random variation in one or more inputs over time. through random sampling of initial conditions and repeated computer simulations.

data.name: Nematode
data.description: A nematode is a type of roundworm belonging to the phylum Nematoda. Nematodes are slender, unsegmented worms with a cylindrical body shape. They can be found in various environments, including soil, freshwater, and marine habitats. Nematodes are incredibly diverse and can be free-living or parasitic, with some species causing diseases in plants, animals, and humans.

data.name: Allotransplantation
data.description: Allotransplantation is the transplantation of an organ or tissue from one individual to another of the same species with a different genotype. The transplant is called an allograft. This is distinct from a xenograft, which is an organ or tissue that is transplanted from one species to another.

data.name: Antisense Elements
data.description: Antisense elements are single-stranded nucleic acid sequences that are complementary to a target RNA or DNA and may be used to label or inactivate the target by hybridization.

data.name: Nucleoskeleton
data.description: The nucleoskeleton, also referred to as nuclear matrix, is the filamentous component of the nucleus not solubilized during extraction with high salt buffers. The nucleoskeleton is akin to a scaffold with which other components of the nucleus (proteins, RNA, DNA) can interact to fix their positions within the nucleus.

data.name: Mid-infrared Photonics
data.description: Mid-infrared photonics is the practical application of electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength between two and approximately twenty micrometres. This region includes a number of so-called water windows: wavelengths of light that can propagate through the Earth’s atmosphere without being absorbed by water molecules. It is also highly relevant in spectroscopy.

data.name: Corporate Social Responsibility
data.description: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is a field of management research that examines the ways in which organizations can contribute to the well-being of society beyond their economic or financial objectives. CSR involves a company taking responsibility for its impact on society and the environment, and seeking to make a positive difference through its operations, products, services, and philanthropy.

subjects.term: Social responsibility of business. Social entrepreneurship

data.name: Infectious-Disease Diagnostics
data.description: Infectious-disease diagnostics is the procedure by which the causative agent of an infectious disease is identified and often characterized. It can be based solely on clinical presentation or more rigorous diagnostic tests, such as culturing of the infectious agent, microscopy, biochemical screens and molecular methods.

data.name: Probabilistic Methods
data.description: The probabilistic method is a remarkable technique for proving the existence of combinatorial objects with specified properties. It is based on probability theory but, surprisingly, it can be used for proving theorems that have nothing to do with probability.

data.name: Solid-phase Microextraction
data.description: Solid-phase microextraction (SPME) is a technique for separating mixtures of compounds without the use of solvents. SPME uses a fibre coated with a polymer or sorbent extracting phase that extracts chemical compounds from liquid or gas phases. It is often used for sample clean up prior to using other analytical methods.

data.name: Oral History
data.description: Oral history is the collection and study of historical information about individuals, families, important events, or everyday life using audiotapes, videotapes, or transcriptions of planned interviews. These interviews are conducted with people who participated in or observed past events and whose memories and perceptions of these are to be preserved as an aural record for future generations.

data.name: Food Studies
data.description: Food science is the study of the physical, biological (including microbiological) and chemical makeup of food. Food studies is an interdisciplinary field of study that examines various aspects of food, including its production, consumption, culture, history, sustainability, nutrition, and impact on society. It encompasses a wide range of disciplines, including anthropology, sociology, geography, history, nutrition, public health, environmental studies, and agriculture.

data.name: Genome-wide Analysis of Gene Expression
data.description: Genome-wide analysis of gene expression is the study of transcription at a genomic scale, also known as transcriptomics. Typically relying on data from microarrays or high throughput sequencing, it can determine what genes or transcript isoforms are enriched in a particular cell or tissue type, condition, disease or phenotype.

data.name: Recidivism
data.description: Recidivism refers to the tendency or likelihood of an individual who has previously engaged in criminal behavior to reoffend or commit another crime after completing their sentence or intervention program. It focuses on studying the patterns, factors, and dynamics associated with repeated criminal behavior.

data.name: Particle Astrophysics
data.description: Particle astrophysics, is a branch of particle physics that studies elementary particles of astronomical origin and their relation to astrophysics and cosmology.

data.name: Oculomotor system
data.description: The oculomotor system consists of interconnected regions throughout the central nervous system that interact to control various eye movements. It includes different brainstem nuclei, the superior colliculus of the midbrain, and various regions throughout the cerebral cortex.

data.name: Prison Policy
data.description: Prison policy focuses on the examination and analysis of policies and practices related to the operation, management, and reform of prisons and correctional institutions. It involves studying various aspects such as sentencing, prison conditions, rehabilitation programs, parole systems, and the overall goals and effectiveness of incarceration.

data.name: Osteoblasts
data.description: Osteoblasts are one of the three cell types found in vertebrate bones. Osteoblasts synthesise the bone collagen matrix of the bone and also participate in matrix mineralisation, which provides strength. When osteoblasts are trapped into the matrix, they become osteocytes. While it is formed by osteoblasts, the bond matrix is degraded by osteoclasts.

data.name: Therapeutic Endoscopy
data.description: Therapeutic endoscopy is the medical term for an endoscopic procedure during which treatment is carried out via the endoscope. It normally occurs after a diagnostic endoscopy.

data.name: Critical Theory
data.description: Critical Theory is a philosophical method and tradition that has its origins in Marx and Marxisms, especially of the Frankfurt School theorists.

data.name: Forensic Psychiatry
data.description: Is a branch of psychiatry deling with the assessment and treatment of offenders in prisons, secure hospitals and the community with mental health problems. It requires a sophisticated understanding of the links between mental health and the law.

data.name: Neuroendocrinology
data.description: The field of neuroendocrinology covers the anatomical and functional interactions between the nervous system and the endocrine system.

data.name: Chondrocytes
data.description: Chondrocytes are the sole cells found in the lacunae of the cartilage, a connective tissue with flexible property found in various regions of the mammalian bodies, including joints, nose and ear. They synthesise the collagen, proteoglycans and elastin fibres that make up the cartilage.

data.name: Water Microbiology
data.description: Water microbiology is the scientific discipline that is concerned with the study of all biological aspects of the microorganisms (bacteria, archaea, viruses, fungi, parasites and protozoa) that exist in water. This is also known as marine microbiology, which is a subdiscipline of environmental microbiology.

data.name: Motor Protein Regulation
data.description: Motor protein regulation is the process by which molecular motors moving along cytoskeletal filaments are regulated, enabling them to perform multiple functions in the cell. The mechanisms governing this regulation are preserved across structurally diverse protein families.

data.name: Comparative Genomics
data.description: Phylogenomics involves the reconstruction of evolutionary relationships by comparing sequences of whole genomes or portions of genomes..Comparative genomics deals with the processes of evolution via the alignment and analysis of genes and genomes of living or extinct organisms related by varying degrees of evolutionary divergence from a common ancestor. Comparisons are usually made pairwise with reference to a third genome 'outgroup' or by examination of pairs of paired sequences and summarized in phylogenetic trees.

data.name: Heat Stress
data.description: Heat stress is defined as an increase in temperature sufficient to cause irreversible damage to plant function and development. Plants can be damaged by either high day or night temperatures, and by high air or soil temperatures.

data.name: Religion and Sustainability
data.description: Religion and Sustainability refers to the intersection of religious beliefs, values, and practices with environmental sustainability and ecological stewardship. It involves exploring how different religious traditions and spiritual worldviews address environmental issues, promote responsible use of natural resources, and advocate for ecological balance.

data.name: Alphaviruses
data.description: Alphaviruses are infectious agents that replicate in humans and many animals; this viral genus includes Chikungunya virus, Semliki Forest virus and Sindbis virus. Alphaviruses are transmitted by arthropods, mainly mosquitoes, and thus are arboviruses.

data.name: Intrinsic Excitability
data.description: Intrinsic excitability is the electrical excitability of a particular neuron. It is determined by the number and distribution of ion channels and receptors that contribute the electrical properties and depolarization potential of the neuron.

data.name: Dermatological Therapy
data.description: The treatment of all skin diseases and conditions, including various surgical procedures, pharmaceutical treatments and other therapies

data.name: Kidney
data.description: The kidney is the organ that filters blood and removes excess fluid and waste products, which are excreted in the urine. The kidney also has a role in the regulation of ion concentrations and blood pressure.

data.name: Interference Microscopy
data.description: Interference microscopy is an optical microscopy technique that uses interference between two white-light illumination beams or rays to generate an image with enhanced contrast.

data.name: ELISPOT
data.description: The enzyme-linked immunosorbent spot (ELISPOT) assay is a sensitive method to count cells of a specific type by capturing molecules that they secrete on an immunosorbent surface and detecting them with the ELISA method. It is commonly used to count immune cells based on the secretion of cytokines.

data.name: Area Studies
data.description: Area studies are interdisciplinary fields of research and scholarship pertaining to particular geographical, national/federal, or cultural regions.

data.name: Consanguinity
data.description: Consanguinity is the property of having a recent common ancestor with another individual. The genetic distance between two individuals can be expressed in meioses (the number of times the shared genome is halved by the generation of ova or sperm) or by the coefficient of relationship (r).

data.name: Cell Growth
data.description: Cell growth usually refers to cell proliferation, the increase in cell numbers that occurs through repeated cell division. Cell growth can also refer to the enlargement of cell volume, which can take place in the absence of cell division.

data.name: Flowering
data.description: Flowering is a major developmental transition in plants, from the vegetative to the reproductive state, during which the plants structurally acquires reproductive competence by producing inflorescences. The timing of this change is influenced by endogenous and environmental signals such as hormones, day length and temperature.

data.name: Criminal Justice
data.description: Criminal justice is the system of practices, institutions, and policies involved in maintaining social control, deterring crime, and sanctioning those who violate laws, including law enforcement, the courts, and correctional facilities.

data.name: Digital Ethics
data.description: It  is a field of study that focuses on the ethical considerations, values, and responsibilities arising from digital technologies, online interactions, and the use of the internet. It involves examining the moral dilemmas and ethical challenges that arise in the digital realm, including issues related to privacy, security, online behavior, and the impact of technology on individuals and society.

data.name: Atomic Cluster Collisions
data.description: Atomic cluster collisions make use of photonic, electronic, heavy particle and atomic collisions to study structures, properties and dynamics of complex nuclear, atomic, molecular, cluster, nanoscopic and biological systems.

data.name: Endocytosis
data.description: Endocytosis is the internalisation of extracellular material. Endocytic pathways include clathrin-dependent endocytosis, caveolae-dependent endocytosis, macropinocytosis and phagocytosis. Endosomes that are generated by endocytosis can be recycled back to the plasma membrane, targeted to another subcellular location, or sent to multivesicular bodies for degradation.

data.name: Multilinear Algebra
data.description: In mathematics, multilinear algebra extends the methods of linear algebra, it builds on the concepts of p-vectors and multivectors with Grassmann algebra

data.name: Theoretical Astrophysics
data.description: It employs theoretical models, computational simulations, and mathematical methods to study and understand the physical processes, phenomena, and structures occurring in the universe. It combines principles from physics and astronomy to develop theoretical frameworks that explain and predict the behavior of celestial objects and systems

data.name: Climate System Modelling
data.description: Climate system modelling is the scientific practice of numerically simulating the Earth’s climate system to understand past, present, and future climate behaviour

data.name: Dental Radiology
data.description: Dental radiology is a branch of dentistry concerned with the use of radiant energy (such as X-rays and other high-energy radiation) or radioactive material in the diagnosis and treatment of dental and oral diseases. Dental radiographs assist in detecting hidden painful pathology, estimating the severity of dental conditions, assessing treatment options, providing intraoperative guidance, and also serve to monitor success of prior treatments.

data.name: Comparative Genomic Hybridization
data.description: Comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) is a method for detecting regional variation in DNA copy number between a test and a control genomic sample. It is used to find the location of large changes including deletions, duplications and amplifications.

data.name: Science Policy
data.description: Science policy is concerned with the allocation of resources for the conduct of science towards the goal of best serving the public interest.

subjects.term: POLITICAL SCIENCE / Public Policy / Science & Technology Policy

data.name: Pharmacodynamics
data.description: Pharmacodynamics (PD) is an area of pharmacology concerned with the relationship between a drug’s concentration at the site of action and the resulting effect, as well as the measurement of that relationship within an individual or group. Factors influencing a drug’s pharmacodynamics include the concentration of the drug target and the signalling pathways downstream.

data.name: Animal Disease Models
data.description: Animal disease models are non-human animals bearing pathologies that share features with a human disease. Disease models can either exist naturally or be induced artificially and are used for studying human disease with an experimental system.

data.name: Rural Geography
data.description: Studies agriculture, land use, population, communities, and settlement patterns in rural areas.

data.name: Tendons
data.description: Tendons are tough, inelastic bands of connective tissue formed of a dense, highly organized matrix of parallel collagen fibres that is maintained by resident tenocytes. Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones and other structures, and serve to transmit and absorb force.

data.name: Cellular Motility
data.description: Cellular motility is the spontaneous movement of a cell from one location to another by consumption of energy. The term encompasses several types of motion, including swimming, crawling, gliding and swarming.

data.name: Gothic Fiction
data.description: Gothic fiction, sometimes called Gothic horror in the 20th century, is a loose literary aesthetic of fear and haunting.

data.name: Paleogenetics
data.description: Paleogenetics, also known as ancient DNA (aDNA) analysis or ancient genomics, is a field of research that involves the study of genetic material obtained from ancient or historical human and non-human remains. It focuses on extracting and analyzing DNA from preserved biological samples to gain insights into genetic variation, evolutionary processes, population dynamics, and human migration patterns throughout history.

data.name: Emotion
data.description: Emotion in the field of psychology refers to a complex psychological and physiological state that involves subjective experiences, physiological arousal, and behavioral expressions. Emotions are multifaceted responses to internal or external stimuli and play a crucial role in motivation, decision-making, and social interactions.

data.name: Spine Regulation and Structure
data.description: Spine regulation is the biological process by which the structure or function of a dendritic spine is modulated by factors such as neuronal excitation. The structure of dendritic spines is highly variable; however, a typical spine consists of a spine head that may be mushroom- or cup-shaped and a thinner neck region.

data.name: Gerodontics
data.description: The branch of dentistry that deals with the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases and problems specific to the aged

data.name: Sequencing
data.description: Sequencing refers to the techniques used to determine the primary structure of an unbranched biopolymer (DNA, RNA, protein, carbohydrate) resulting in a symbolic linear depiction of the monomeric subunits which summarizes much of the atomic-level structure of the molecule.

data.name: Historical Geography
data.description: Historical geography is the branch of geography that studies the ways in which geographic phenomena have changed over time. It is a synthesizing discipline which shares both topical and methodological similarities with history, anthropology, ecology, geology, environmental studies, literary studies, and other fields

data.name: Reasoning
data.description: Reasoning in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive process of using logical and critical thinking to draw conclusions, make judgments, and solve problems. It involves the ability to analyze information, apply rules and principles, and reach valid and sound conclusions.

data.name: Novel
data.description: a fictitious prose narrative of book length, typically representing character and action with some degree of realism.

data.name: Giant Planet
data.description: Giant planets are large planets, typically 10 or more times the mass of Earth, made predominantly of liquid or gas, notably hydrogen and helium. There are four giants in the solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

data.name: Small RNAs
data.description: Small RNAs are a type of non-coding RNA (ncRNA) molecule that are 50–250 nucleotides in length. They are often involved in regulating the translation of target RNAs through RNA–RNA interactions.

data.name: Microwave Photonics
data.description: Microwave photonics is the practical application of electromagnetic waves with a wavelength between one millimetre and one meter. Microwaves are important for communications, and systems for detecting microwaves are crucial for astronomy. The term also includes high-frequency electronic systems.

data.name: Polariton
data.description: Polaritons are hybrid particles made up of a photon strongly coupled to an electric dipole. Examples of such a dipole include an electron–hole pair in a semiconductor, which forms an exciton polariton, and the oscillating electrons at the surface of a metal, which creates a surface-plasmon polariton.

data.name: Asteroids, Comets and Kuiper belt
data.description: Asteroids, comets and Kuiper belt are bodies smaller than planets that orbit the sun. Asteroids are composed of metals and rock, whereas comets also contain ice and dust. The Kuiper belt is a collection of such bodies that orbits at the edge of the solar system.

data.name: Religion and Gender
data.description: Sex differences in religion can be classified as either "internal" or "external". Internal religious issues are studied from the perspective of a given religion, and might include religious beliefs and practices about the roles and rights of men and women in government, education and worship; beliefs about the sex or gender of deities and religious figures; and beliefs about the origin and meaning of human gender. External religious issues can be broadly defined as an examination of a given religion from an outsider's perspective, including possible clashes between religious leaders and laity; and the influence of, and differences between, religious perspectives on social issues.

data.name: Microbiome
data.description: The microbiome comprises all of the genetic material within a microbiota (the entire collection of microorganisms in a specific niche, such as the human gut). This can also be referred to as the metagenome of the microbiota.

data.name: Basolateral Polarity
data.description: Basolateral polarity is a type of cell polarity specific to epithelial cells, referring to a specialised basolateral membrane oriented away from the lumen of internal cavities or the outside of the body, opposite a specialised apical membrane which faces the lumen. The two domains are often physically separated by adherens junctions complexes.

data.name: Nutrition Therapy
data.description: Nutrition therapy is the treatment of a medical condition, for example diabetes mellitus, through changes in diet, by adjusting quantity, quality and methods of nutrient intake. In the USA, medical nutrition therapy has a legal definition and is provided by a registered dietitian.

data.name: Learning Process
data.description: The learning process, in the field of psychology, refers to the acquisition, retention, and application of knowledge or skills through various cognitive and behavioral processes. It involves the encoding and storage of information, as well as the retrieval and utilization of that information when needed.

data.name: Cognitive Control
data.description: Cognitive control is the process by which goals or plans influence behaviour. Also called executive control, this process can inhibit automatic responses and influence working memory. Cognitive control supports flexible, adaptive responses and complex goal-directed thought. Some disorders, such as schizophrenia and ADHD, are associated with impairments of executive function.

data.name: Genetic Counseling
data.description: Genetic counselling is an educational process that aims to inform and advise patients and relatives at risk of a genetic condition about the nature of the disorder, the probability of developing it and the risk of passing it on to future generations. Individuals can then make informed decisions about available testing, health management, treatment, and family planning options.

data.name: Cancer Stem Cells
data.description: Cancer stem cells are rare immortal cells within a tumour that can both self-renew by dividing and give rise to many cell types that constitute the tumour, and can therefore form tumours. Such cells have been found in various types of human tumours and might be attractive targets for cancer treatment.

data.name: Turbomachines
data.description: Describes machines that transfer energy between a rotor and a fluid, including both turbines and compressors. While a turbine transfers energy from a fluid to a rotor, a compressor transfers energy from a rotor to a fluid

data.name: Biolegalities
data.description: Biolegalities explore the legal and ethical implications of biotechnological advancements, including issues related to genetic engineering, bioethics, and the regulation of biological research and applications.

data.name: Sepsis
data.description: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition that is caused by an excessive immune response to an infection, most commonly a bacterial infection. Sepsis can lead to multi-organ failure and death.

data.name: Expertise
data.description: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

data.name: RNA probes
data.description: RNA probes are stretches of single-stranded RNA used to detect the presence of complementary nucleic acid sequences (target sequences) by hybridization. RNA probes are usually labelled, for example with radioisotopes, epitopes, biotin or fluorophores to enable their detection.

data.name: Prosthetic Dentistry
data.description: Prosthodontics is the replacement of missing parts of teeth, bone, gums, or facial structures. Most general dentists perform some prosthodontic procedures, but a prosthodontist specializes in prosthodontics, having completed 3 or more years of postdoctoral education in one or more phases of this specialty.

data.name: Motor Proteins
data.description: Motor proteins are a class of proteins that play a crucial role in cellular transport and movement. These proteins generate force and enable the movement of various cellular components, such as organelles, vesicles, and chromosomes, within cells.

data.name: Viral Membrane Fusion
data.description: Viral membrane fusion is the process by which enveloped viruses enter host cells. It involves the merging (fusion) of the virus membrane with the host cell membrane or at an intracellular location following virus uptake by endocytosis. Fusion is mediated by transmembrane proteins that are anchored on the virus surface.

data.name: Cytokinesis
data.description: Cytokinesis occurs after nuclear division and is the process that divides the cytoplasm to give rise to two new cells, each with one set of chromosomes. Cytokinesis begins with the contraction of the cell equator and ends with severing the remaining connection between the daughter cells.

data.name: State Crime
data.description: State crime refers to illegal or unethical actions committed by governments, government officials, or state institutions, which violate human rights, international law, or domestic laws. State crimes can involve a wide range of offenses, such as torture, genocide, war crimes, corruption, and political repression.

data.name: Science Fiction
data.description: fiction based on imagined future scientific or technological advances and major social or environmental changes, frequently portraying space or time travel and life on other planets.

data.name: Early Universe
