data.description: After the Big Bang, the universe was like a hot soup of particles (i.e. protons, neutrons, and electrons). When the universe started cooling, the protons and neutrons began combining into ionized atoms of hydrogen (and eventually some helium).

data.name: Phylogeny
data.description: A phylogeny is a hypothetical reconstruction of the evolutionary relationships of a group of organisms or a set of sequences (nucleotide or amino acid). Phylogenies are often represented graphically in the form of a 'tree' and enable scientists to find new relationships between organisms.

data.name: Oncogenesis
data.description: Oncogenesis is the process through which healthy cells become transformed into cancer cells. It is characterized by a series of genetic and cellular changes, including oncogene activation, that lead the cell to divide in an uncontrolled manner.

data.name: Religion and Population Studies
data.description: Religion and Population Studies is an interdisciplinary field that examines the relationship between religion and demographic trends, population dynamics, and socio-cultural factors. It involves the study of how religious beliefs, practices, and institutions influence population behavior and demographic patterns, and how demographic changes, in turn, impact religious communities and practices.

data.name: Crime Fiction
data.description: Crime fiction, detective story, murder mystery, mystery novel, and police novel are terms used to describe narratives that centre on criminal acts and especially on the investigation, either by an amateur or a professional detective, of a serious crime, generally a murder.

data.name: Combinatorial Geometry
data.description: Combinatorial geometry studies combinatorial properties and constructive methods of discrete geometric objects and focuses on the combinatorial properties of these objects, such as how they intersect one another, or how they may be arranged to cover a larger object

data.name: Biosocial Criminology
data.description: Biosocial criminology is a subfield within criminology that seeks to understand criminal behavior by examining the interplay between biological, genetic, and environmental factors. It combines insights from biology, genetics, neuroscience, psychology, and sociology to provide a comprehensive understanding of the complex causes of criminal behavior.

data.name: Ethnicity in Education
data.description: Ethnicity in Education is the study of the role of ethnicity in educational systems, policies, and practices. This field examines how ethnic identities and relations influence educational access, achievement, and experiences and explores strategies for addressing ethnic inequality and fostering cultural diversity and inclusivity in education.

data.name: Galaxies and Clusters
data.description: Galaxies are a gravitationally bound system of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter. Galaxies range in size from dwarfs with just a few hundred million stars to giants with one hundred trillion stars, each orbiting its galaxy's center of mass. They Galaxies are categorized according to their visual morphology as elliptical, spiral, or irregular and commonly they are gravitationally organized into groups, clusters, and superclusters.

data.name: Gastrointestinal System Model
data.description: Gastrointestinal models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of the human digestive system to study its function in digestion and disease. They include animal models such as mouse genetic models of bowel disease and in vitro chemical systems that recapitulate digestion and can include intestinal epithelium and gut microbes..The human gastrointestinal system principally refers to the stomach and intestine, but can encompass the entire gastrointestinal tract, including all structures and organs from the mouth to the anus. The gastrointestinal system has a vital role in digestion, which is under hormonal control, to obtain nutrients for the body and eliminate waste.

data.name: Concept Formation
data.description: Concept formation in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive process of creating mental representations or concepts based on shared features or attributes of objects, events, or ideas. It involves the ability to identify commonalities and develop abstract representations that allow for generalization and categorization.

data.name: Navigation
data.description: Navigation is the process by which an animal or individual establishes its present location and plans a route to a future destination within its environment.

data.name: Biosurface
data.description: Biosurfaces are synthetic surfaces that are coated with biological materials and/or are designed to have a specific biological function or application. They are important in areas such as sensing and the detection of diseases.

data.name: Classical Conditioning
data.description: Classical conditioning, in the field of psychology, is a type of learning in which an organism learns to associate a neutral stimulus with a meaningful stimulus, leading to a conditioned response. Through repeated pairings of the neutral stimulus with the meaningful stimulus, the neutral stimulus alone can elicit a response similar to the meaningful stimulus.

data.name: Immunosurveillance
data.description: Immunosurveillance is a term used to describe the processes by which cells of the immune system look for and recognise foreign pathogens, such as bacteria and viruses, or pre-cancerous and cancerous cells in the body.

data.name: Ethology
data.description: Ethology or Animal behaviour is the scientific study of the behaviour of animals. The discipline covers study under experimental conditions, behaviourism, or natural conditions, ethology.

data.name: History of Dentistry
data.description: The historical development of the dental profession, dental techniques and treatments.

data.name: Lamination
data.description: Lamination is the biological process by which cells are arranged in layers within a tissue during development. Laminated structures in the nervous system include the cerebral cortex, retina and hippocampus. During nervous system development, the molecular mechanisms governing cell specification, migration and axon guidance contribute to the process of lamination.

data.name: Symbiosis
data.description: Symbiosis refers to the partnership (usually long-term) that is established between two or more organisms. In microbiology, symbiotic relationships are often established between a microorganism and its host, and the partnership can be mutualistic or parasitic.

data.name: Stomata
data.description: Stomata are minute openings found in the epidermis of leaves, stems and other plant organs. Stomata allow gases such as carbon dioxide, water vapour and oxygen to diffuse into and out of the internal tissues of the plant.

data.name: Faith, Spirituality and Business
data.description: Faith and spirituality research as a field of management research refers to the study of the impact of faith and spirituality on organizational behavior, performance, and outcomes. This research field is concerned with exploring how individuals' beliefs, values, and spirituality can influence their behavior, motivation, and decision-making processes in the workplace.  This area of research aims to examine how organizations can integrate faith and spirituality into their management practices to improve employee well-being, organizational culture, and overall performance. It also seeks to understand how employees' spiritual and religious practices can impact their engagement, job satisfaction, and overall performance.  Overall, faith and spirituality research in management aims to provide insights into the role of religion and spirituality in the workplace and how organizations can leverage these beliefs and values to create a positive and supportive work environment.

data.name: Pituitary Gland
data.description: The pituitary gland is an endocrine gland located downstream of the hypothalamus at the base of the brain, which is composed of an anterior, an intermediate and a posterior lobe. It secretes pivotal hormones such as growth hormone, TSH, ACTH and prolactin, which regulate functions including growth, thyroid function and blood pressure.

data.name: Inbreeding
data.description: Inbreeding is the mating of individuals or organisms that are genetically closely related, resulting in increased homozygosity and consequently an increase in the occurrence of recessive traits. This can lead to inbreeding depression: reduced biological fitness of the population. Inbreeding is also used as a technique in selective breeding to identify and establish new and desirable traits.

data.name: Apoptosis
data.description: Apoptosis is a mechanism of programmed cell death and is essential for development and homeostasis. Cell stress stimulates pro-apoptotic signalling pathways that activate caspase proteases and cause mitochondrial dysfunction. Apoptotic cells undergo characteristic changes in cell morphology, including cell rounding, plasma membrane blebbing and nuclear fragmentation.

data.name: Archaeal Genetics
data.description: Archaeal genetics is the scientific study of the genes, consisting of hereditary units, of Archaea, a domain of organisms that comprise single, nucleus-free cells, distinct from bacteria and eukaryotes.

data.name: Corporate Communication
data.description: Corporate communication research is a subfield of business and management research that examines how organizations communicate with their various stakeholders, including employees, customers, investors, and the general public. It involves the study of communication strategies and practices that organizations use to achieve their goals, as well as the effects of these communication activities on the attitudes and behaviors of stakeholders. The research topics within corporate communication research may include: Analysis of communication channels used by organizations to reach their stakeholders Evaluation of the effectiveness of different communication strategies and practices Examination of the impact of organizational communication on stakeholders' attitudes and behaviors Investigation of the role of communication in organizational change and crisis management Study of the relationship between corporate communication and organizational reputation and image Analysis of the ethical dimensions of organizational communication Corporate communication research can inform business and management practices by providing insights into effective communication strategies that can help organizations achieve their goals and maintain positive relationships with their stakeholders. Additionally, research in this area can inform public policy and regulatory efforts aimed at promoting ethical and effective corporate communication practices.

subjects.term: Communication in management. Communication in organizations. Communication of information

data.name: Child and Adolescence Psychology
data.description: Child and Adolescent Psychology is a specialized field within psychology that focuses on the study of psychological development and behavior during childhood and adolescence. It examines the cognitive, emotional, social, and physical aspects of development from infancy through adolescence.

data.name: Ultrafast Lasers
data.description: Ultrafast lasers are lasers that produce short pulses of light, typically less than one picosecond. These devices often rely on techniques such as mode locking to create a train of pulses. Ultrafast lasers are an important probe of electron dynamics in atoms and molecules.

data.name: Perception
data.description: Perception, in the field of psychology, refers to the process of interpreting and making sense of sensory information received from the environment. It involves the organization, identification, and interpretation of sensory stimuli, allowing individuals to form mental representations of the world around them.

data.name: Physiotherapy
data.description: Physiotherapy is a health profession as well as a treatment method that focuses on the science of movement and helps people to restore, maintain and maximize their physical strength, function, motion and overall well-being by addressing the underlying physical issues. Physiotherapy aims at preventing injury and disability, managing acute and chronic conditions, Improving and maintaining optimal physical performance, Rehabilitating injury and the effects of disease or disability and Educating patients to prevent re-occurrence of an injury. For these purposes, Physiotherapy applies a variety of techniques, such as manual manipulation, electrical nerve stimulation, acupuncture, functional testing or provision of assistive, adaptive, supportive and protective devices and equipment.

data.name: Stress Fibres
data.description: Stress fibres are contractile bundles of actin filaments and myosin, which can attach to focal adhesions and function in cell adhesion, migration and mechanotransduction. Different types of stress fibres include ventral and dorsal stress fibres, transverse arcs and the perinuclear actin cap.

data.name: Partial Differential Equations
data.description: In mathematics, a partial differential equation (PDE) is a differential equation that contains beforehand unknown multivariable functions and their partial derivatives. PDEs are used to formulate problems involving functions of several variables, and are either solved by hand, or used to create a computer model.

data.name: Large Intestine
data.description: The large intestine is the final part of the lower gastrointestinal tract and includes the caecum, appendix, colon, rectum and anal canal. The large intestine's function is to finish digestion of food, extracting water, salt and nutrients from solid waste and excreting indigestible matter from the body via the anus.

data.name: History of Chemistry
data.description: The history of chemistry is rich, evolving from early discussions on the nature of matter in ancient Egypt and Greece, through to the emergence of alchemy, the development of the periodic table and quantum chemistry.

data.name: Biogerontology
data.description: Biogerontology is the study of the biological basis of ageing and age-related diseases. It represents the step in research which aims primarily at achieving healthy old age accompanied by improved longevity.

data.name: Information and Communication, Circuits
data.description: Information and Communication Circuits are electronic circuits designed to process and transmit information or signals in communication systems. Information and Communication Circuits are essential components of communication systems, including telecommunications networks, wireless systems, satellite communication, computer networks, and many other applications.

data.name: Reflexes
data.description: Reflexes are involuntary or automatic movements that are often elicited in response to a stimulus. Reflexes can be evoked to various mechanical, visual/vestibular, auditory and other types of stimuli.

data.name: Energy Supply and Demand
data.description: Energy supply is the delivery of fuels or transformed fuels to point of consumption while energy demand is the term used to describe the consumption of energy by human activity. Both together drive the energy system and influence the total amount of energy used and are often looked at together in scientific studies.

data.name: Propagation, Transmission, Absorption
data.description: The act or process of propagating, especially the process by which a disturbance, such as the motion of electromagnetic or sound waves, is transmitted through a medium such as air or water. The process of absorption depends on the nucleus, electrons and the level of vibration. The transmission depends on the transparency of the object where the ray of light falls. Reflection takes place when the angle of incidence stands equal to the angle of reflection in real-time.

data.name: Supramolecular Assembly
data.description: Supramolecular assembly is the formation of a well-defined complex of molecules held together by noncovalent bonds. It is usually used to describe large groups of molecules that form sphere-, rod- or sheet-like species.

data.name: Peripheral Nervous System
data.description: The peripheral nervous system is the part of the nervous system outside the brain and spinal cord. It consists of nerves that carry information between the central nervous system and the extremities of the body.

data.name: Ichthyology
data.description: Ichthyology is the branch of zoology devoted to the study of fish, including: bony fish, Osteichthyes; cartilaginous fish, Chondrichthyes; and jawless fish, Agnatha. The discipline can include the biology, taxonomy and conservation of fish, as well as husbandry and commercial fisheries.

data.name: Fertilization
data.description: Fertilization is the fusion of two haploid gametes, during the process of sexual reproduction, to initiate the development of a new diploid organism with mixed genetical heritage. In flowering plants, the pollen grain germinates once it reaches the carpel, and develops a tube that will reach and fuse with the ovule.

data.name: Laser Applications
data.description: Laser is an optical device that generates intense beam of coherent monochromatic light by stimulated emission of radiation.  Laser light is different from an ordinary light. It has various unique properties such as coherence, monochromacity, directionality, and high intensity. Because of these unique properties, lasers are used in various applications.  The most significant applications of lasers include:  Lasers in medicine Lasers in communications Lasers in industries Lasers in science and technology Lasers in military

data.name: Autobiographical Memory
data.description: Autobiographical memory, in the field of psychology, refers to the collection of memories that are personally significant and relevant to one's own life. It encompasses the recollection of past events, experiences, and knowledge that are associated with oneself and contribute to the sense of identity and self-awareness. Autobiographical memory includes both episodic memories (specific events) and semantic memories (general knowledge), allowing individuals to construct a narrative of their lives.

data.name: Virus Structures
data.description: Virus structures are the physical components of a virus particle, including its genome and structural proteins.

data.name: Historical Anthropology
data.description: Historical anthropology is a historiographical movement which applies methodologies and objectives from social and cultural anthropology to the study of historical societies.

data.name: Long non-coding RNAs
data.description: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNA) are a type of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) that exceed 200 nucleotides in length. lncRNAs are a relatively abundant component of the mammalian transcriptome and have been implicated in several cellular functions, including the regulation of gene transcription through the recruitment of chromatin-modifying enzymes.

data.name: Machine Translation
data.description: Machine translation refers to the automated process of translating text or speech from one language to another using computer algorithms and models. It aims to enable communication and understanding between people who speak different languages.

data.name: Chinese Politics
data.description: Chinese Politics is a sub-discipline within political science that focuses on the political system of the the People's Republic of China, transnational and strategic relations with other countries, as well as political developments within China.

data.name: General Emergency Medicine
data.description: General Emergency Medicine encompasses the non‑specialized emergency care of patients with acute conditions or injuries that do not require subspecialty expertise. It includes initial evaluation, stabilization, and management of common, undifferentiated, or multisystem emergencies.

data.name: Lamellipodia
data.description: The lamellipodium is the actin-rich foremost region of the leading edge of a migrating cell. This highly dynamic structure promotes cell migration through protrusion formation driven by actin polymerisation at the plasma membrane.

data.name: Genetic Models
data.description: Genetic models are biological systems which allow the study of genetic phenomena. For example, certain pure-bred dog varieties may serve as a model for investigating genetic bottlenecks.

data.name: Soil and Rock Mechanics
data.description: The subject soil and rock mechanics is the theoretical and applied science of the mechanical behavior of soils and rocks and their application.

data.name: Reconstructive Surgery
data.description: Reconstruction is the process of surgically rebuilding damaged tissue. This procedure restores the original form and function to tissues damaged through traumatic events such as motor vehicle accidents or substantial burns. Reconstruction can also restore form and function to tissue damaged through a surgery performed to treat another disease.

data.name: Riboswitches
data.description: A riboswitch is a regulatory segment within a messenger RNA (mRNA) that binds to specific metabolites and modifies the expression of the riboswitch-containing mRNA’s protein product. Riboswitches are used by bacteria to maintain specific levels of a given metabolite, by regulating the expression of the protein responsible for its accumulation.

data.name: Ecosystems
data.description: Ecosystem ecology is the combined study of the physical and biological components of ecosystems. It focuses on how matter and energy flow through both organisms and the abiotic components of the environment.

subjects.term: Nature conservation. Landscape protection. Biodiversity conservation. Endangered species and ecosystems (General). Habitat conservation. Ecosystem management. Conservation biology

data.name: Discrete Mathematics in Computer Science
data.description: Discrete mathematics plays a fundamental role in computer science. It provides the theoretical foundation and mathematical tools necessary for analyzing and solving problems in various areas of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, cryptography, logic, and computer networks

data.name: RNA quality control
data.description: RNA quality control is the active process by which ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules are monitored for integrity. The RNA quality control machinery directs the degradation of compromised RNA molecules.

data.name: Thymus Hormone
data.description: Thymus hormones are hormones produced by the thymus. They are generally small proteins, which regulate the development and selection of an immune-competent repertoire of T cells, and stimulate antibody production by B cells. They are important for immune system development and function and also the development of other tissues.

data.name: Forestry
data.description: Forestry is the study and practice of the cultivation and management of woodlands. Forests provide goods and services such as timber, recreation and carbon sequestration.

subjects.term: Forestry and silviculture: practice and techniques

data.name: British Politics
data.description: British politics is the study of the political institutions, actors, and decision‑making processes of the United Kingdom, including its constitutional framework, parties, and systems of governance.

data.name: Astronomical Instrumentation
data.description: Astronomical instrumentation refers to the development of new technologies devoted to increase the understanding of the universe.

data.name: Psychopharmacology
data.description: Psychopharmacology is the scientific study of the effects drugs have on mood, sensation, thinking, and behavior. It is distinguished from neuropsychopharmacology, which emphasizes the correlation between drug-induced changes in the functioning of cells in the nervous system and changes in consciousness and behavior.

subjects.term: Drugs acting on the nervous system. Neuropsychopharmacology

data.name: Multivariate Analysis
data.description: involves evaluating multiple variables (more than two) to identify any possible association among them

data.name: Stochastic Networks
data.description: The analysis of stochastic networks and their applications includes modelling, stability analysis, control, performance analysis and design of stochastic networks. Such analysis requires the bringing together of ideas and methodologies from a range of mathematical disciplines, including applied probability, stochastic processes, operational research, combinatorics and graph theory. Stochastic networks are networks that vary over time with non-binary vertices that represent a probability for a link between two nodes. Statistical approaches or computer simulations are often necessary to explore how such networks evolve, adapt or respond to external intervention

data.name: Protozoa and Algae
data.description: Protozoa are a diverse group of single-celled eukaryotic microorganisms. They belong to the Kingdom Protista and are found in various aquatic and terrestrial environments. Algae are a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. They can be found in aquatic environments such as freshwater and marine habitats, as well as in soil and other moist environments.

data.name: Lineage Tracking
data.description: Lineage tracking methods follow the position and behaviour of cells and their descendents over time. Cells are typically labelled and/or imaged in real time or at frequent time intervals to determine their lineage.

data.name: Patterning
data.description: A pattern is a regularity in the world, man-made design, or abstract ideas. As such, the elements of a pattern repeat in a predictable manner. A geometric pattern is a kind of pattern formed of geometric shapes and typically repeated like a wallpaper design. Geometric patterning is the study of such patterns (mathematics Springer).Patterning describes the processes by which the plan for later development of a plant is laid down. It involves the early establishment of 'prepatterns' of 'morphogens' which form a complex signalling network, which in turn determines further differentiation (Nature)

data.name: Digital Culture
data.description: Digital culture is the relationship between people and the use of technology. It describes how digital media and technology have shaped our everyday lives and interactions with society, people and work.

data.name: Abdominal Surgery
data.description: Surgery of gastrointestinal and endocrine organs like tract, liver, pancreas and endocrine organs, including very specialized procedures.

data.name: Algorithm Analysis and Problem Complexity
data.description: Analysis of algorithms is the determination of the amount of time and space resources required to execute it. While The complexity of a problem is the infimum of the complexities of the algorithms that may solve the problem, including unknown algorithms.

data.name: Thermoelectrics
data.description: Thermoelectrics are materials that can generate electricity from the application of a temperature gradient, or vice versa, through the thermoelectric effect. By exploiting this coupling between thermal and electrical properties, thermoelectric devices can be made that carry heat from a cold to a hot side (refrigeration) or that generate electricity from heat flows.

Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Filopodia
data.description: Filopodia (singular: filopodium) are thin protrusions with a core of parallel bundles of actin filaments that extend from the plasma membrane and explore the cell's surroundings. Filopodia can be found at the leading edge of migrating cells.

data.name: Sexual Offending
data.description: Sexual offending within criminology refers to the study of crimes involving sexual acts that are non-consensual, exploitative, or otherwise violate the laws and norms related to sexual behavior. It examines the causes, patterns, consequences, and prevention of sexual offenses, as well as the treatment and management of offenders.

data.name: Licensing
data.description: Licensing refers to the legal process of granting permission to use an intellectual property (IP) asset such as a patent, trademark, or copyright to a third party in exchange for compensation, usually in the form of royalties or fees. Licensing is an important field of research and practice within technology commercialization because it enables companies to monetize their inventions and innovations while avoiding the costs and risks associated with manufacturing and distribution. The core topics of licensing as a field of research and practice within technology commercialization include: Intellectual Property Law: Licensing is a legal process, and thus a fundamental understanding of intellectual property law is essential for practitioners in this field. This includes knowledge of the different types of IP assets, the requirements for obtaining and maintaining them, and the legal frameworks that govern their use and enforcement.  Negotiation and Contracting: Licensing agreements involve complex negotiations and contractual agreements between the licensor and the licensee. Practitioners must be skilled in drafting and negotiating these agreements, as well as understanding the key terms and provisions that are critical to the success of the licensing deal. Technology Assessment: Before licensing a technology, it is important to assess its commercial viability and potential market demand. Practitioners must be able to evaluate the technology's potential market size, competitive landscape, and potential applications to determine whether it is a viable candidate for licensing. Market Analysis: To successfully license a technology, practitioners must have a deep understanding of the market and the competitive landscape. This includes conducting market research, identifying potential licensees, and developing a licensing strategy that aligns with the company's overall business goals. Intellectual Property Valuation: Determining the value of an IP asset is critical in negotiating licensing agreements. Practitioners must be able to accurately assess the value of the IP asset, taking into account factors such as the strength of the patent, the size of the market, and the potential revenue streams. Compliance and Enforcement: Once a licensing agreement is in place, it is important to ensure that both parties comply with the terms of the agreement. Practitioners must be able to monitor and enforce compliance, and take legal action when necessary to protect the licensor's rights and interests. Overall, licensing is a complex field that requires a deep understanding of intellectual property law, negotiation and contracting, technology assessment, market analysis, intellectual property valuation, and compliance and enforcement.

data.name: Cell Cycle Checkpoint
data.description: Checkpoints or cell cycle checkpoints are transition points in the cell cycle that can be negatively regulated. Checkpoints ensure that the cell only divides if conditions are favourable, and that the events take place in the correct order, for example that mitosis does not happen until DNA replication is complete.

data.name: Soil Chemistry
data.description: Study of the chemical characteristics of soil

data.name: Paediatric Urology
data.description: Paediatric Urology is the Surgical Specialty that deals with problems with the genitourinary system in children.

data.name: Organizational Learning
data.description: Organizational learning is a field of research that focuses on how organizations acquire, process, and use knowledge to improve their performance and achieve their goals. It involves studying the ways in which organizations learn from their experiences, both positive and negative, and how they use this knowledge to adapt to changing environments, innovate, and improve their practices and processes. The main topics within organizational learning include: Knowledge acquisition: This refers to how organizations gather and collect knowledge from various sources, such as employees, customers, suppliers, and competitors. This involves understanding the mechanisms and processes of knowledge creation, transfer, and sharing. Knowledge transfer and sharing: This refers to the ways in which organizations share knowledge within and across different units or departments. It involves studying the communication, collaboration, and coordination processes that facilitate knowledge transfer and sharing. Learning processes: This refers to the cognitive and behavioral processes that individuals and groups use to acquire and use knowledge. This involves studying how individuals and groups process information, make decisions, and learn from their experiences. Organizational culture and climate: This refers to the shared values, norms, beliefs, and practices that shape the learning environment within an organization. It involves studying how the organizational culture and climate can facilitate or inhibit learning. Innovation and creativity: This refers to the ways in which organizations use their knowledge to innovate and create new products, services, and processes. It involves studying the mechanisms and processes of innovation, such as idea generation, experimentation, and implementation. Performance improvement: This refers to the ways in which organizations use their knowledge to improve their performance and achieve their goals. It involves studying the mechanisms and processes of performance improvement, such as benchmarking, continuous improvement, and knowledge management.

data.name: Manufacturing Organization
data.description: Manufacturing organization that produce physical goods. It's easy to see the operations management process at work in these types of organizations because raw materials are turned into recognizable physical products.

data.name: Myosin
data.description: Myosins are a large family of cytoskeletal motor proteins that bind actin and use the energy of ATP hydrolysis to perform diverse functions such as cell motility and contractility, cytokinesis, intracellular trafficking and muscle contraction.

data.name: Conservation Genomics
data.description: Conservation genomics is the application of genomic analysis to the preservation of the viability of populations and the biodiversity of living organisms. Genomic methods can be used to argue species identity, degree of hybridization, genetic diversity, demographic history and effective population size.

data.name: Multivesicular Bodies
data.description: Multivesicular bodies (MVBs) are a specialised subset of endosomes that contain membrane-bound intraluminal vesicles. These vesicles form by budding into the lumen of the MVB. The content of MVBs can be degraded, via fusion with lysosomes, or released into the extracellular space, via fusion with the plasma membrane.

data.name: Infectious-Disease Epidemiology
data.description: The study of the incidence and spread of infectious diseases in populations over time. Host, pathogen and environmental factors are monitored to determine the dynamics of infection, the ultimate goal of which is to devise intervention strategies. Molecular methods, such as phylogenomics, can be used to accurately track pathogens.

data.name: Local Anesthesia
data.description: Local anesthesia is any technique to induce the absence of sensation in a specific part of the body, generally for the aim of inducing local analgesia, i.e. local insensitivity to pain, although other local senses may be affected as well. It allows patients to undergo surgical and dental procedures with reduced pain and distress. In many situations, such as cesarean section, it is safer and therefore superior to general anesthesia.

data.name: Logistics
data.description: Logistics is a critical part of supply chain management that involves the planning, implementation, and control of the movement and storage of goods, services, and related information between the point of origin and the point of consumption. In the context of management research, logistics involves the study of various strategies, techniques, and technologies that are used to ensure the efficient and effective flow of goods and services through the supply chain.  Logistics research may involve analyzing different transportation modes, such as air, sea, rail, or road, and evaluating the benefits and drawbacks of each for specific types of goods and services. It may also involve examining various distribution strategies, such as centralized, decentralized, or hybrid systems, and assessing the impact of these strategies on delivery times, inventory costs, and customer satisfaction.  Other areas of logistics research may include inventory management, warehouse design and operations, packaging and labeling, and reverse logistics, which involves the management of returned goods and waste. Overall, logistics research seeks to identify best practices and innovative solutions for optimizing the supply chain and improving organizational performance.

data.name: Digital Society
data.description: Digital Society adresses all aspects of the transformation of societies that are a direct or indirect consequence of digitalisation, in particular how we interact, work, and communicate.

subjects.term: Computers and civilization. Social aspects of computers
Digital and information technologies: social and ethical aspects

data.name: Discourse
data.description: Discourse is the study of language in use and broader social practices, examining how spoken and written texts are structured, produced, and interpreted in various contexts. It includes the analysis of communication beyond the sentence level, addressing aspects such as power relations, ideology, and identity.

data.name: Neural Induction
data.description: Neural induction refers to the process during embryonic development where a group of cells becomes committed to forming neural tissue, specifically the neural plate and subsequently the neural tube. Neural induction is a crucial step in the formation of the central nervous system (CNS).

data.name: Meteoritics
data.description: Meteoritics is the study of meteorites — solid parts of asteroids or comets that have landed on another celestial body, notably (but not limited to) the Earth. Measuring the composition of meteorites provides vital information about the formation of astronomical bodies that are otherwise impossible to study.

data.name: Chemotherapy
data.description: Chemotherapy is a treatment used to kill cancer cells. It involves taking one or more of a type of drug that interferes with the DNA of fast-growing cells. These drugs are subdivided into specific classes such as alkylating agents, antimetabolites, anthracyclines and topoisomerase inhibitors.

data.name: Enzyme Mechanisms
data.description: Enzyme mechanisms are the chemical transformations, and the steps within them, generated by enzymatic action on substrates. The mechanism of enzyme catalysis is similar in principle to other types of chemical catalysis, for instance by involving a combination of several different types of catalysis. Determining enzyme mechanisms includes determining their kinetic and thermodynamic properties.

data.name: Dental Pharmacology
data.description: Dental pharmacology is the study of drugs used to treat conditions of the oral cavity. Some of these drugs include antibiotics, analgesics, anti-inflammatory drugs and anti-periodontitis agents.

data.name: Cell Type Diversity
data.description: Cell type diversity refers to the range of different cell types that comprise a tissue or organism. Cell type diversity arises during the development of the nervous system as a result of the acts of cell intrinsic and extrinsic factors controlling cell fate determination.

data.name: Stratigraphy
data.description: Stratigraphy is the study of stratified rocks.

data.name: US Politics
data.description: US politics refers to the political entities and processes which comprise government at all levels and all branches, including the Presidency, Congress, and the judicial system in the United States of America.

data.name: Metabolic Pathways
data.description: Metabolic pathways are enzyme-mediated biochemical reactions that lead to biosynthesis (anabolism) or breakdown (catabolism) of natural product small molecules within a cell or tissue. The glycolysis and Krebs cycle metabolic pathways, in aerobic respiration, produce precursors of various important cellular molecules such as the primary metabolite ATP; other metabolic pathways produce secondary metabolites.

subjects.term: General biochemistry of plants and animals

data.name: Necroptosis
data.description: Necroptosis is a form of programmed necrosis. Necroptotic stimuli promote the interaction of the RIP1 and RIP3 kinases under conditions in which caspase-8 is not active. This RIP1/RIP3 complex, known as complex IIb, mediates necroptosis.

data.name: Restriction Factors
data.description: Restriction factors are anti-viral proteins that are produced in the host and counteract or 'restrict' viral replication. These proteins are considered a first line of defence against viruses.

data.name: Mesenchymal Migration
data.description: Mesenchymal cell migration is a motility mode characterised by cell polarisation to form a leading edge that extends actin-rich protrusions, such as lamellipodia, leading to adhesive interactions with the substratum and proteolytic extracellular matrix remodelling, followed by retraction of the contractile cell rear to achieve cellular movement.

data.name: Osteocytes
data.description: Osteocytes are mature bone cells that originate from osteoblasts once they become fully embedded in the mineralised matrix. Their primary role is to act as mechanosensors and regulators of bone turnover, detecting mechanical strain and coordinating the activity of osteoblasts and osteoclasts through signalling pathways.

data.name: Investments and Securities
data.description: The Investments and Securities industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the analysis, management, and trading of financial instruments such as stocks, bonds, options, and other securities. The field encompasses a wide range of topics, including portfolio management, risk management, financial analysis, asset pricing, trading strategies, and market microstructure. It involves understanding the behavior of financial markets and the factors that influence their movements, as well as developing models and tools to help investors make informed decisions about their investments. Research in this field often involves the use of quantitative methods and may draw upon insights from economics, finance, and mathematics.

data.name: Brain Stimulation
data.description: Brain stimulation refers to techniques and methods used to directly modulate the activity of the brain. These techniques involve applying electrical or magnetic fields to specific areas of the brain, resulting in changes in neural activity and influencing brain function. Brain stimulation has both therapeutic and research applications and has shown potential in treating various neurological and psychiatric conditions.

data.name: Catalytic Materials
data.description: Catalytic materials are those solids that allow the chemical reaction to occur efficiently and cost-effectively

data.name: Parasitism
data.description: Parasitism is a type of relationship between two species where one species, the parasite, benefits at the expense of the other, the host. When parasites cause disease in their host they are referred to as pathogens.

data.name: Pharmacokinetics
data.description: Pharmacokinetics is an area of pharmacology concerned with the time course of absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (collectively ADME) of drugs from biological systems in order to understand the effect of the drug, or of the organism, on the drug's impact. Pharmacokinetic parameters can also include toxicology and a drug’s liberation from its medicinal formulation.

data.name: Environmental Policy
data.description: Studies the commitment of an organization or government to the laws, regulations, and other policy mechanisms concerning environmental issues.

subjects.term: POLITICAL SCIENCE / Public Policy / Environmental Policy

data.name: Power Law
data.description: A power law is a special mathematical relationship between two quantities in which one quantity varies as a power of the other. Numerous examples of power laws occur in nature, for example, the frequency of any word in a language is inversely proportional to its ranking in a frequency table.

data.name: Action Potential Generation
data.description: Action potential generation is the process by which a neuron rapidly depolarizes from a negative resting potential to a more positive potential, and is achieved by influx of cations (sodium ions or calcium ions) through ion channels. It occurs at the action potential initiation zone region of the soma, and is propagated along the axon to downstream targets.

data.name: Coastal Sciences
data.description: Coastal Science is an interdisciplinary approach that includes geomorphology, ecology, engineering, technology, oceanography, and human activities as they relate to coasts.

data.name: Glial Biology
data.description: The study of the molecular and cellular biology of glial cells, for example, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, Schwann cells and microglia.

data.name: Abiotic
data.description: Abiotic factors are non-living chemical and physical elements in the environment, which affect individual organisms as well as ecosystems. Examples are UV, IR and visible light, radiation, temperature, wind, humidity, water, pH, heavy metals, atmospheric gases, soil chemicals, and, more generally, climate.

data.name: Regional Anesthesia
data.description: Regional anesthesia is a type of pain management for surgery that numbs a large part of the body, such as from the waist down. A temporary loss of feeling or awareness in a part of the body, such as an arm or a leg, caused by special drugs or other substances called anesthetics. The patient stays awake but has no feeling in the part of the body treated with the anesthetic.

data.name: Solid-State Lasers
data.description: Solid-state lasers are lasers made from crystalline materials. The very first laser used ruby as a solid-state active region in 1960, and there are now hundreds of known alternatives. The most common approach however is to introduce rare-earth atoms into a crystalline lattice – titanium-doped sapphire, for example.

synonyms: Neodymium Doped Yttrium Aluminum Garnet Lasers

data.name: Motor Protein Function
data.description: Motor proteins are molecular motors that use ATP hydrolysis to move along cytoskeletal filaments within the cell. They fulfil many functions within biological systems, including controlling the sliding of filaments in muscle contraction and mediating intracellular transport along biopolymer filament tracks.

data.name: Iron
data.description: Iron (Fe, atomic number 26) is a redox-active transition metal element found in living systems as Fe2+ or Fe3+ ions. It is rarely found free in biology, but is bound to proteins such as ferritin or haem, to form metalloproteins such as haemoglobin, which is responsible for the transport of oxygen in the blood.

data.name: Queueing Theory
data.description: Queueing theory is a field of management research and practice that focuses on the study of waiting lines, or queues, and the mathematical models used to analyze them. The goal of queueing theory is to understand the behavior of queues, how to design systems that minimize wait times and improve efficiency, and how to make informed decisions regarding system improvements and resource allocation.  Queueing theory considers various factors that impact queue performance, such as the arrival rate of customers or requests, the service rate of the system, the number of servers or service points available, and the behavior of customers while they wait. By analyzing these factors, queueing theory provides managers and analysts with the tools to optimize system performance, identify bottlenecks, and evaluate system trade-offs.  Queueing theory has broad applications in many fields, including telecommunications, transportation, healthcare, finance, and manufacturing. It is used to design call centers, hospitals, factories, and other systems that require efficient resource utilization and customer service. In addition, queueing theory is also used to study the behavior of customers and employees, providing insights into their decision-making processes and the factors that influence their behavior.

data.name: Centromeres
data.description: Centromeres are regions of linear chromosomes at which the two chromatids are joined. They are the sites of attachment of the mitotic spindle, which is necessary for chromosome segregation during cell division.

data.name: Retromer
data.description: The retromer is a protein complex containing sorting nexin (Snx) and vacuolar protein sorting (Vps) components. It has an essential role in recycling cargo molecules from endosomes to the trans-Golgi network, and mediates certain endosome-to-plasma membrane recycling events.

data.name: Entomology
data.description: Entomology is a branch of zoology concerned with the study of insects. The discipline can include the biology and control of insects, as well as their ecology and impact on animal, plant and human health.

data.name: Free-Electron Lasers
data.description: Free-electron lasers create coherent light by constantly accelerating a beam of electrons. Free-electron lasers are particularly useful because they can produce radiation with a short-wavelength, down to just a few tenths of a nanometre. Thus, it is hoped they will become an important tool for atom-level material characterization.

data.name: Foundations of Physics and Cosmology
data.description: This is the branch of physics which together with cosmology deals with foundational issues such as the nature of space and time, the nature of heat and of energy, the concept of irreversibility and probability, the nature of matter and measurement in quantum theory, renormalization, etc.

synonyms: Grundlegende Fragen der Physik und Kosmologie

data.name: Recombinant Vaccine
data.description: A recombinant vaccine is a vaccine produced through recombinant DNA technology. This involves inserting the DNA encoding an antigen (such as a bacterial surface protein) that stimulates an immune response into bacterial or mammalian cells, expressing the antigen in these cells and then purifying it from them.

data.name: Model Invertebrates
data.description: Model invertebrates are extensively studied animal species that lack a vertebral column and are chosen for the ease of investigating particular biological phenomena. Research on model invertebrates provides biological insights relevant to other organisms in many areas including genetics, development, biochemistry, evolution, disease, neurobiology and behaviour.

data.name: Quantum Cascade Lasers
data.description: Quantum cascade lasers are made up of many thin layers of semiconductor. An injected electron makes a small energy transition as it moves from one layer to the next, emitting light on each cascade. Because the energy steps are small, quantum cascade lasers can produce long-wavelength mid-infrared or terahertz radiation.

data.name: Melatonin
data.description: Melatonin is an endocrine hormone with a monoamine alkaloid structure, produced from the amino acid tryptophan. Melatonin is generated by the pineal gland in mammals. Melatonin is involved in entrainment of plant and animal circadian clocks via its action on melatonin receptors, expressed abundantly in the central nervous system, and through its direct antioxidant activity.

data.name: Edaphology
data.description: Study of soil in relation to soil-dependent uses.

data.name: Optical Cloaking
data.description: Manipulating the paths traversed by light through a novel optical material, rendering objects seemingly invisible.

data.name: Conservation Biology
data.description: Conservation biology or Conservation Ecology is a mission-oriented science that focuses on how to protect and restore biodiversity, or the diversity of life on Earth. Like medical research, conservation biology deals with issues where quick action is critical and the consequences of failure are great. To preserve biodiversity, scientists must answer three general questions. First, how is the diversity of life distributed around the planet? Second, what threats does this diversity face? Third, what can people do to reduce or eliminate these threats and, when possible, restore biological diversity and ecosystem health?

subjects.term: Nature conservation. Landscape protection. Biodiversity conservation. Endangered species and ecosystems (General)

data.name: Autophagosomes
data.description: Autophagosomes are double-membraned vesicles that contain cellular material slated to be degraded by autophagy. An isolation membrane or phagophore forms near autophagic cargo and expands until it encloses the cargo. Autophagosome formation depends on the activity of a type III PI3K lipid kinase.

data.name: Physical Oceanography
data.description: Physical oceanography is the study of the physics of marine systems. It includes the distribution of temperature and salinity, water mass formation and movement, ocean currents, interior and surface mixing, energy inputs and dissipation, surface and internal waves, and surface and internal tides.

data.name: Body, Aerodynamics, Design
data.description: Aerodynamic shape optimization, or aerodynamic design optimization consists in maximizing the performance of a given body (such as an airfoil or wing) by changing its shape.

data.name: Spinal Cord Injury
data.description: A spinal cord injury consists of damage to the spinal cord that results from external trauma including accidents, falls and sports-related injuries, rather than a degenerative disease. The effects of a spinal cord injury widely vary from no effect, to pain, or to complete loss of spinal cord function.

data.name: Astrophysical Plasma
data.description: Astrophysical plasma is plasma outside of the solar system. The plasma is made by electrically-charged particles that are susceptible to influences by local electromagnetic fields. E.g. strong fields generated by stars, and weak fields which exist in star forming regions, in interstellar space, and in intergalactic space.

data.name: Sports Ethics
data.description: Sports Ethics deals with any type of ethical issue, questions or problem in the context of Sport and attempts to suggest sensible courses of actions in order to alleviate or regulate these problems and establish ethical standards. Ethical issues in Sports commonly concern performance enhancing drugs (doping), Gender Discrimination, Fair Play, Responsibility for the performance, Fan Behaviour, Diversity or Protection of athletes health and safety.

subjects.term: Ethics of recreation, leisure, public performances, communication
Relation to ethics. Fair play. Sportsmanship

data.name: Limnology
data.description: Limnology is the study of inland freshwaters, both standing bodies, such as lakes, and running waters, like rivers. It encompasses the biology, geology, physics, chemistry and climatology of these water systems, and may also cover wetland conservation and ecosystem services.

data.name: Terrestrial Ecology
data.description: Terrestrial ecology is the study of how land-based organisms interact with each other and their environment.

data.name: Macroecology
data.description: Macroecology is the study of broad scale ecological patterns and processes. The focus is rarely on single communities and ecosystems, and instead looks at principles that apply more broadly such as metabolic scaling, extinction risk and diversity gradients.

data.name: Pollination
data.description: Pollination is the process of transferring pollen from the anther to the stigma of flowering plants. Pollination results in the stimulation of pollen to produce pollen tubes.

data.name: Herbivory
data.description: Herbivores are organisms that are anatomically and physiologically adapted to eat plants, algae and photosynthetic bacteria. Adaptations for a herbivorous diet include the four-chambered stomach of ruminants, and the specialist grinding teeth of cattle, sheep and goats.

data.name: Cell Fate
data.description: The fate of a cell describes its future identity, or the identity of its daughter cells, before it is actually phenotypically detectable through differentiation or division. Cell fate can be determined by endogenous developmental factors, interaction with adjacent cells, or external long-distance signals such as morphogens and hormones.

data.name: Structure and Properties of Clusters
data.description: Clusters are aggregates of atoms, molecules, or ions that are bound together by intermolecular or interatomic forces. They can exist as discrete entities with a specific number of constituent particles, and their structure and properties can vary depending on the size and composition of the cluster. Some key aspects of the structure and properties of clusters Geometrical Structure, Size and Composition, Surface and Core, Thermal Stability, Magnetic and Magnetic Resonance Properties

data.name: Fluorescence Microscopy
data.description: Fluorescence microscopy is a powerful imaging technique that utilizes fluorescent probes or dyes to visualize specific structures or molecules within biological samples. It allows researchers to observe and study cellular processes, protein localization, molecular interactions, and various biological phenomena with high sensitivity and specificity.

data.name: Recombinant Peptide Therapy
data.description: A recombinant peptide therapy is produced through recombinant DNA technology. This involves inserting the DNA encoding the peptide into bacterial or mammalian cells, expressing the peptide in these cells and then purifying it from them.

data.name: Reward
data.description: Reward is an appealing or appetitive concept that can be applied to an object or a situation, which positively reinforces a response, satisfies a motive or intent, or signals pleasure.

data.name: Bose-Einstein Condensate
data.description: Bose-Einstein condensate is a state of matter of a dilute gas of bosons cooled to temperatures close to absolute zero. Under such conditions, a large fraction of bosons occupy the lowest quantum state, at which point microscopic quantum phenomena, particularly wavefunction interference, become apparent macroscopically.

subjects.term: Quantum physics (quantum mechanics & quantum field theory)
Quantum physics (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory)

data.name: Chemotaxis
data.description: Chemotaxis is the directional movement of cells in response to a chemical stimulus gradient.

data.name: Mechanotransduction
data.description: Mechanotransduction refers to the processes through which cells sense and respond to mechanical stimuli by converting them to biochemical signals that elicit specific cellular responses.

data.name: Slavic Literature
data.description: Slavic literature refers to the literary works produced by Slavic-speaking peoples, who primarily reside in Central, Eastern, and Southeastern Europe. Slavic literature encompasses a diverse range of languages, including Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Czech, Slovak, Bulgarian, Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian, and others.

data.name: Crystal Engineering
data.description: Crystal engineering is the design of molecular solids with specific physical and chemical properties through an understanding and manipulation of intermolecular interactions. Engineering strategies typically rely on hydrogen bonding and coordination bonds, but can also use other interactions, such as halogen bonds and pi-pi interactions.

data.name: Small GTPases
data.description: Small GTPases are a large family of monomeric proteins that bind and hydrolyse GTP to GDP. Small GTPases activate downstream effectors when bound to GTP. Their activity is controlled by GTPase activating proteins, guanine nucleotide exchange factors, and GDP dissociation inhibitors. Small GTPases have many cellular functions.

data.name: Consciousness
data.description: Consciousness is the state of being aware of oneself and the environment. It is associated with wakefulness, responsiveness and arousal. Consciousness is typically measured by verbal reports about experience. Related areas of interest are those functions that are thought to operate without consciousness, such as blindsight and subliminal perception.

data.name: Numerical Simulation
data.description: A numerical simulation is a calculation that is run on a computer following a program that implements a mathematical model for a physical system. Numerical simulations are required to study the behaviour of systems whose mathematical models are too complex to provide analytical solutions, as in most nonlinear systems.

data.name: Quantum Theory
data.description: Quantum theory is the theoretical basis of modern physics that explains the nature and behavior of matter and energy on the atomic and subatomic level.

data.name: Protein Engineering
data.description: Protein engineering is the conception and production of unnatural polypeptides, often through modification of amino acid sequences that are found in nature. Synthetic protein structures and functions can now be designed entirely on a computer or produced through directed evolution in the laboratory.

data.name: Probability and Statistics in Computer Science
data.description: Probability and Statistics for Computer Science treats the most common discrete and continuous distributions, showing how they find use in decision and estimation problems, and constructs computer algorithms for generating observations from the various distributions.

synonyms: Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung und Statistik in der Informatik

data.name: Centrosome
data.description: The centrosome is the major microtubule-organising centre of the cell and consists of two centrioles surrounded by pericentriolar material. The centrosome is duplicated during the cell cycle and in mitosis the two centrosomes form the poles of the mitotic spindle, which segregates the chromosomes into two daughter cells.

data.name: Plant Embryogenesis
data.description: Plant embryogenesis is the process by which plant embryos form and develop. During embryogenesis the basic body plan of the plant is established, primary plant tissue types are differentiated, and food reserves are accumulated that will ultimately be used by the germinating seedling following a period of dormancy.

data.name: Artificial Photosynthesis
data.description: Artificial photosynthesis is a chemical process that biomimics the natural process of photosynthesis to convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and oxygen. The term artificial photosynthesis is commonly used to refer to any scheme for capturing and storing the energy from sunlight in the chemical bonds of a fuel (a solar fuel). Photocatalytic water splitting converts water into hydrogen and oxygen and is a major research topic of artificial photosynthesis. Light-driven carbon dioxide reduction is another process studied that replicates natural carbon fixation.  Research on this topic includes the design and assembly of devices for the direct production of solar fuels, photoelectrochemistry and its application in fuel cells, and the engineering of enzymes and photoautotrophic microorganisms for microbial biofuel and biohydrogen production from sunlight.  -- Copied from Wikipedia

data.name: Plant Hybridization
data.description: Plant hybridization is the process of crossbreeding between genetically dissimilar parents to produce a hybrid. It frequently results in polyploid offspring.

data.name: High-throughput Cell Screening
data.description: High-throughput screening methods provide efficient measurement of the effects of agents or conditions in biological or chemical assays. These methods often require robotics, imaging and computation to increase the scale and speed of assays.

data.name: Realism
data.description: Realism, in the context of literature and art, refers to an artistic movement that emerged in the 19th century as a reaction against romanticism. Realism aims to depict the world as it is, presenting a truthful and objective representation of everyday life, social conditions, and human experiences. Realism in literature often focuses on ordinary people and their struggles, portraying their lives with attention to detail, accuracy, and psychological depth.

data.name: Macrophages
data.description: Blood monocytes that enter damaged tissues from the circulation differentiate into macrophages. These specialised phagocytic cells recognise, engulf and degrade cellular debris and pathogens and can survive several months. They function both in innate and adaptative immunity and are also essential for wound healing processes.

data.name: Archaeal Biology
data.description: Archaeal biology is a scientific discipline that concerns the biology of archaea, a domain of organisms consisting of single, nucleus-free cells, distinct from bacteria and eukaryotes.

data.name: Political Science of Religion
data.description: Religious Political Science may involve, but are not limited to, those concerning freedom of religion, applications of religious law, and the right to religious education.

data.name: DNA methylation
data.description: DNA methylation is the covalent addition of methyl groups to DNA bases, typically the cytosine of CpG dinucleotides. It is catalyzed by methyltransferase enzymes using a S-adenosyl methionine donor and can lead to mitotic propagation of the modified sequence with consequences for the binding of regulatory proteins such as transcription factors.

data.name: English
data.description: English is a West Germanic language that originated in England and is now one of the most widely spoken languages in the world. It serves as a lingua franca in many parts of the globe and has a significant impact on various aspects of society, including business, education, and popular culture.

data.name: Magnetic Tweezers
data.description: Magnetic tweezers are devices used for studying mechanical properties of single molecules, such as force and torque. A single molecule is tethered to a surface at one end and attached to a magnetic bead at the other; the bead is manipulated via external magnets.

data.name: Water Industry and Water Technology
data.description: The water industry provides drinking water and wastewater services (including sewage treatment) to residential, commercial, and industrial sectors of the economy.  Water treatment/ Water technologies are an essential line of defence to remove contaminants and bacteria before the delivery of clean, potable water supplies for consumption.

data.name: Membrane Permeation and Transport
data.description: Membrane transport is the means by which small molecules and biopolymers permeate a cell membrane. Membranes are lipid bilayers exhibiting selective permeability, meaning that they are permeable to some substances and not to others. Membrane transport is mediated by membrane-transport proteins.

data.name: Biooceanography
data.description: Biooceanography is the study of marine organisms and their interactions with their environment. It includes the ecology and biogeochemistry of marine plants, animals and microbes.

data.name: Gene Silencing
data.description: Gene silencing describes the epigenetic regulation of a gene, at the level of transcription or translation, to prevent gene expression. Mechanisms include DNA methylation, histone modification and RNAi. Methods to silence genes are exploited by researchers to study gene function, and for the development of therapeutics for diseases including cancer, infectious diseases and neurodegenerative disorders.

data.name: Protein Structure Predictions
data.description: Protein structure predictions are bioinformatic analyses that produce predicted protein structures automatically using the protein amino acid sequence. Protein structures are important because structural features can shed light on biological functions.

data.name: Stem Cell Biotechnology
data.description: Stem cell biotechnology is a field of biotechnology that develops tools and therapeutics through modification and engineering of stem cells. Stem cell biotechnology is important in regenerative medicine.

data.name: Glial Development
data.description: Glial development is the biological process by which glial cells – which comprise most of the non-neuronal cells present in the nervous system and include oligodendrocytes, astrocytes and Schwann cells – are produced during development. Glial development encompasses the entire developmental trajectory of glial cells—from their origin, lineage specification, migration, differentiation, maturation, to acquisition of functional roles, including the processes that contribute to glial development, proliferation, differentiation and migration.

data.name: Colorectal Surgery
data.description: Colorectal surgery is the management of conditions of the colon, rectum, and anus.

subjects.term: Lower sigmoid, rectum, and anal region

data.name: Translation Studies
data.description: Translation studies is an interdisciplinary field that focuses on the theory, practice, and analysis of translation and interpreting. It involves the examination of various aspects of translation, including the process, strategies, cultural considerations, and the impact of translation on language and communication.

data.name: Supercontinuum Generation
data.description: Supercontinuum generation is a combination of nonlinear optical effects that spectrally broaden an initially nearly monochromatic laser beam. This can be achieved, for example, by sending a short intense burst of light along a photonic-crystal optical fibre. Supercontinuum generation is used to provide intense sources of white light.

data.name: Computational Geometry
data.description: Computational geometry is a branch of computer science devoted to the study of algorithms which can be stated in terms of geometry

data.name: Self Incompatability
data.description: Self-incompatibility is the mechanisms adopted by a plant to prevent self-fertilization and thus encourage outcrossing. Self-incompatibility can be achieved either by preventing self-pollination or by ensuring that self-pollen does not successfully achieve fertilization.

data.name: Transport Receptors
data.description: Transport receptors are soluble proteins that mediate the nuclear export or import of proteins across the nuclear envelope. Transport receptors are characterised as either exportins or importins, depending on the direction of transport.

data.name: Long-term Memory
data.description: Long-term memory is information encoded in the brain on the time-scale of years. It consists of explicit (declarative) memories that are consciously reportable and depend heavily on the medial temporal lobe and hippocampus and implicit (procedural) memories that are unconscious and depend on the basal ganglia and cerebellum.

data.name: Biophysical Economics
data.description: Biophysical economics is the study of the ways and means by which human societies procure and use energy and other biological and physical resources to produce, distribute, consume and exchange goods and services, while generating various types of waste and environmental impacts.

data.name: Microarrays
data.description: A microarray is a set of samples, for example DNA, RNA or proteins, arranged on a solid substrate or chip, such as a glass slide or silicon film, that is used in high throughput experiments. Microarrays enable multiple simultaneous measurements to be made in one experiment.

data.name: Focal Adhesion
data.description: Focal adhesion is a type of adhesive contact between the cell and extracellular matrix through the interaction of the transmembrane proteins integrins with their extracellular ligands, and intracellular multiprotein assemblies connected to the actin cytoskeleton. Focal adhesions anchor the cell to the substratum and can mediate both mechanical and biochemical signalling.

data.name: Kinesin
data.description: Kinesins are a large superfamily of cytoskeletal motor protein that hydrolyse ATP to move along microtubules and perform diverse functions in intracellular trafficking and cell division.

data.name: Software Management
data.description: Software Management is a field of business and management research and practice that focuses on managing the development, delivery, and maintenance of software products and services. It encompasses the coordination of software development teams, the allocation of resources, and the creation of processes and methodologies for software development.  Major topics within the field of Software Management include:  Software Development Methodologies: These are frameworks used to manage the development of software projects. Examples include Agile, Waterfall, and DevOps.  Project Management: This involves the planning, organizing, and managing of resources to achieve specific software development goals within a given time frame and budget.  Software Testing: This involves the process of evaluating software products or services to ensure they meet quality standards and user requirements.  Software Maintenance: This involves the ongoing process of updating and improving existing software products or services to ensure they remain functional and relevant.  Software Metrics and Measurements: This involves the use of quantitative data to measure and track the progress of software development projects and assess their success.  Software Quality Assurance: This involves the process of ensuring that software products or services meet established quality standards and requirements.  Risk Management: This involves identifying, assessing, and managing risks that could impact the success of software development projects.  Software Architecture: This involves the design and organization of software components and systems to ensure they are scalable, maintainable, and meet user requirements.  Team Management: This involves managing software development teams to ensure they are effective and efficient in achieving project goals.

subjects.term: COMPUTERS / Software Development & Engineering / Project Management

data.name: Fibre Lasers
data.description: Fibre lasers are lasers made from thin strands of a light-guiding glass. Atomic or molecular impurities introduced into the fibre when it is formed provide the optically active component, and the optical feedback required for stimulated emission can be created by patterning part of the fibre so it acts as a mirror.

data.name: Nomograms
data.description: A nomogram is a graphical analogue computation device. A set of n scales, one for each variable in an equation, are arranged according to the equation. The nomogram can be used to determine the value of unknown variable if the values of n-1 variables are known.

data.name: Historical Geology
data.description: Historical geology uses the principles and techniques of geology to reconstruct and understand the geological history of Earth.

data.name: Islamic Finance
data.description: Islamic finance is a type of financing activities that must comply with Sharia (Islamic Law). The concept can also refer to the investments that are permissible under Sharia. The common practices of Islamic finance and banking came into existence along with the foundation of Islam.

data.name: Metrology
data.description: Metrology is concerned with the establishment of units of measurement, the development of new measurement methods, the realisation of measurement standards, and the transfer of traceability from these standards to users in a society.

data.name: Interventional Cardiology
data.description: Interventional cardiology is the use of intravascular, catheter-based techniques in the treatment of patients with cardiovascular disease.

data.name: Forensic Dentistry
data.description: Forensic dentistry or forensic odontology is the application of dental knowledge to those criminal and civil laws that are enforced by police agencies in a criminal justice system. Forensic dentists are involved in assisting investigative agencies to identify recovered human remains in addition to the identification of whole or fragmented bodies; forensic dentists may also be asked to assist in determining age, race, occupation, previous dental history and socioeconomic status of unidentified human beings.

data.name: Information Studies
data.description: Information studies is a multidisciplinary field that explores how people create, collect, organize, and access information. It encompasses areas such as library science, data science, information management, and information technology.

data.name: Potassium
data.description: Potassium (K, atomic number 19) is an alkali metal and its ions (K+) are necessary for the function of all living cells. Potassium is important in hyperpolarization of membranes during nerve transmission and in regulating a cell's osmotic balance. Potassium is transported across membranes by potassium channels and the ion pump Na+/K+-ATPase.

data.name: Synaptogenesis
data.description: Synaptic development is the biological process by which a synapse between two neurons forms. The membranes of the two neurons become closely apposed and this is accompanied by presynaptic differentiation, during which synaptic vesicles gather close to the active zone, and postsynaptic differentiation, including the clustering of neurotransmitter receptors.

data.name: Inner Planet
data.description: Inner planets are the four planets closest to the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. They are collectively characterized by a solid surface and small size relative to the outer gas giants.

data.name: Nucleolus
data.description: The nucleolus is a region within the nucleus that primarily functions as the site for the transcription of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) genes, the processing of precursor rRNAs into mature components of ribosomes, and the initial steps of ribosome assembly.

data.name: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
data.description: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a technique that detects the chemical environment of atomic nuclei by the absorption of radio-frequency electromagnetic radiation when in the presence of a high magnetic field. NMR is used in chemistry and related fields for high-resolution molecular structure determination and the study of molecular dynamics.

data.name: Stem-cell Therapies
data.description: Stem cell therapies are a type of cell therapy in which the cells used are either stem cells (as in the case of bone marrow transplantation) or are derived from stem cells, as is this case with some stem cell therapies that are currently being investigated for their therapeutic potential in areas such as regenerative medicine.

data.name: Hydraulic Engineering
data.description: Concerned with the flow and conveyance of fluids, principally water and sewage. Includes the design of bridges, dams, channels, canals, and levees.

data.name: Theoretical and Statistical Ecology
