data.description: Theoretical ecology is the scientific discipline devoted to the study of ecological systems using theoretical methods such as simple conceptual models, mathematical models, computational simulations, and advanced data analysis. Statistical ecology deals with the development of new methodologies for analyzing ecological data.

data.name: Dermatological Diagnoses
data.description: The application of medical techniques to define skin disease in humans

data.name: Plant Cytoskeleton
data.description: The plant cytoskeleton is the network of protein filaments, microtubules, and interconnecting filamentous bridges that give shape, structure and organization to the cytoplasm of the plant cell.

data.name: Birdsong
data.description: Birdsong is a communicative process between birds associated with courtship and mating. Birdsong is considered to be distinct from bird calls, which are shorter than birdsong and attributed with alarms or maintaining contact with a flock.

data.name: Creativity
data.description: Creativity in the field of psychology refers to the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas, solutions, or products. It involves the generation of unique and original insights, the ability to think divergently, and the capacity to engage in imaginative and flexible thinking.

data.name: Intermediate Filaments
data.description: Intermediate filaments are a type of cytoskeletal filaments characterised by their intermediate diameter compared to actin filaments and microtubules. Different types of intermediate filaments are composed by a variety of proteins, including keratins, lamins and vimentin, and may be involved in cell adhesion and maintenance of cellular and nuclear shape.

data.name: Plant Transporters
data.description: Plant transporters are molecules, frequently proteins, specialized for transporting water, food, wastes and other materials within plants.

data.name: Oligonucleotide Probes
data.description: Oligonucleotide probes are short stretches of single-stranded DNA or RNA used to detect the presence of complementary nucleic acid sequences (target sequences) by hybridization. Oligonucleotide probes are usually labelled, for example with radioisotopes, epitopes, biotin or fluorophores to enable their detection.

data.name: Immunosuppression
data.description: Immunosuppression is the deliberate prevention or reduction of an immune response. It can result from the administration of immunosuppressive agents or from the deliberate depletion of immune cells, as well as from malnutrition, cancers and certain chronic infections such as HIV. An unwanted side-effect of immunosuppression is immunodeficiency.

data.name: Tokamaks
data.description: Tokamaks are devices that use a powerful magnetic field to confine a hot plasma in the shape of a torus. The tokamak is one of several types of magnetic confinement devices being developed to produce controlled thermonuclear fusion power and it is the leading candidate for a practical fusion reactor.

data.name: RNA editing
data.description: RNA editing is the process by which ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules are enzymatically modified post synthesis on specific nucleosides. Examples of RNA editing include pseudouridylation (the isomerization of uridine residues) and deamination (removal of an amine group from cytidine to give rise to uridine, or C-to-U editing).

data.name: Sodium
data.description: Sodium (Na, atomic number 11) is an alkali metal that exists in living systems as Na+ ions. In physiology, it regulates blood volume, blood pressure, osmotic equilibrium and cellular pH. Sodium is transported though membranes to and from the extracellular fluid via sodium channels and the sodium-potassium pump.

data.name: Limb Development
data.description: Limb development is the process by which a limb forms in the vertebrate embryo. Early in limb development, outgrowths called the limb buds form on the flanks of the embryo, and these develop into mature limbs by the coordinated processes of pattern formation, cell proliferation, differentiation and morphogenesis.

data.name: RNA folding
data.description: RNA folding is the process by which a linear ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecule acquires secondary structure through intra-molecular interactions. The folded domains of RNA molecules are often the sites of specific interactions with proteins in forming RNA–protein (ribonucleoprotein) complexes.

data.name: SAXS
data.description: Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) is a small-angle scattering (SAS) technique whereby the scattering of X-rays upon interaction with a material or biological molecule in solution is monitored. A SAXS pattern can be used to interpret molecular structure.

data.name: Linear Logic
data.description: Linear logic is a substructural logic proposed by Jean-Yves Girard as a refinement of classical and intuitionistic logic, joining the dualities of the former with many of the constructive properties of the latter.

data.name: Development Geography
data.description: Studies on the spatial patterns of human development, and the causes and consequences of changes. Development geography is measured by e.g. economic, political, and social factors.

data.name: Game Theory
data.description: Game theory is the study of mathematical models of strategic interaction between rational decision-makers. It has applications in all fields of social science, as well as in logic and computer science. Originally, it addressed zero-sum games, in which one person's gains result in losses for the other participants. Today, game theory applies to a wide range of behavioral relations, and is now an umbrella term for the science of logical decision making in humans, animals, and computers

data.name: Tiling
data.description: Tiling in geometry is the study of the covering of a plane using one or more geometric shapes, called tiles, with no overlaps and no gaps. In mathematics, tessellations/tilings can be generalized to higher dimensions and a variety of geometries. Mathematicians use many technical terms when discussing tilings

data.name: Disaster
data.description: A disaster is a serious problem occurring over a period of time that causes widespread human, material, economic or environmental loss which exceeds the ability of the affected community or society to cope using its own resources

subjects.term: Social impact of disasters / accidents (natural or man-made)

data.name: Insect Hormone
data.description: Insect hormones are generated and used by insects to regulate physiological, developmental and behavioural events. Insect hormones can be produced by epithelial glands – for example, juvenile hormones or the steroid hormones ecdysteroids – or by neurosecretory cells, as for the neuropeptide hormones such as prothoracicotropic hormone. Insect hormones have been used commercially to control insect populations.

data.name: Shoot Apical Meristem
data.description: Shoot apical meristem is the region in the growing shoot containing meristematic cells. The shoot apical meristem contains multipotent stem cells and produces primordia that develop into all the above ground organs of a plant.

data.name: Humanistic Anthropology
data.description: “Humanistic anthropology involves the recognition that professional inquiry takes places in a context of human value. The humanistic orientation is particularly concerned with the personal, ethical, and political choices facing humans.”

data.name: Stellar Evolution
data.description: Stellar evolution is the process by which a star changes over the course of time. Depending on the mass of the star, its lifetime can range from a few million years for the most massive to trillions of years for the least massive, which is considerably longer than the age of the universe. All stars are born from collapsing clouds of gas and dust, often called nebulae or molecular clouds. Over the course of millions of years, these protostars settle down into a state of equilibrium, becoming what is known as a main-sequence star.

data.name: State of Health
data.description: Illness: is the response of person to disease, which is based on the person's perception…… symptom.  Wellness (health): is a status in which individual is capable of meeting the minimum physical, psychological and social requirements of appropriate functioning.

data.name: Thoracic Surgery
data.description: Thoracic surgery focuses on treating conditions of the body's thorax (chest) area, including the esophagus, lungs, mediastinum (the area between the lungs), trachea, and diaphragm. Thoracic surgeons treat the following conditions: Chest wall tumors. Emphysema, pulmonary fibrosis, and other end-stage lung-diseases.

data.name: Restoration Ecology
data.description: Restoration ecology is the scientific study supporting the practice of ecological restoration, which is the practice of renewing and restoring degraded, damaged, or destroyed ecosystems and habitats in the environment by active human intervention and action.

data.name: Mining and Exploration
data.description: Mining and exploration are two distinct yet interconnected processes involved in the extraction and discovery of mineral resources from the Earth's crust.

data.name: Desmosomes
data.description: Desmosomes are multiprotein complexes that mediate cell-cell adhesion by anchoring intermediate filaments to the plasma membrane. The intercellular adhesive units of desmosomes are the desmoglein and desmocolin members of the cadherin superfamily, which recruit a variety of intracellular proteins to form the intermediate-filament-tethering desmosomal plaque.

data.name: Biochemical Engineering
data.description: Biochemical engineering is a field of study with roots stemming from chemical engineering and biological engineering. It involves the study of how basic raw materials are converted to the finished products by means of rigorous processes.

data.name: Applications of AFM
data.description: Applications of atomic force microscopy (AFM) include biochemistry applications (imaging the structure of biological molecules, cellular components, cells or tissues), chemistry, materials science and nanotechnology applications (imaging of polymers, nanostructures or other materials) and physics and biophysics applications (measuring forces between the AFM tip and the sample surface).

data.name: RNA decay
data.description: RNA decay is the process by which ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules are enzymatically degraded. RNA decay is a regulated event and serves to control levels of particular RNA molecules. A specific example is nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD), a process that eliminates transcripts containing premature stop codons.

data.name: Risk Theory
data.description: In actuarial science and applied probability risk theory or ruin theory (sometimes collective risk theory) uses mathematical models to describe an insurer's vulnerability to insolvency/ruin. In such models key quantities of interest are the probability of ruin, distribution of surplus immediately prior to ruin and deficit at time of ruin

data.name: Migration and Health
data.description: Migration and Health describes the overall condition (physical, mental, and social well-being) of an individual or a population who are on the move from one place to another with the intention to settle.

data.name: Trauma Psychology
data.description: Trauma is a physiological wound, which can be penetrating or nonpenetrating, caused directly or indirectly by external physical force.

data.name: Kinetochores
data.description: Kinetochores are large protein complexes that assemble at the centromere of a chromosome, and function to connect the chromosome to microtubules in the mitotic spindle.

data.name: Climate Change Ecology
data.description: Climate-change ecology is the study of the effects of anthropogenic climate change on any aspect of ecology. It includes the effects of altered temperature and precipitation on the distribution, abundance, behaviour and physiology of populations and communities.

data.name: Fiscal Policy
data.description: Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and tax policies to influence economic conditions, especially macroeconomic conditions. These include aggregate demand for goods and services, employment, inflation, and economic growth. Fiscal policy is one of the two main tools used by the government to influence the economy. The other is monetary policy.

data.name: Occupational Health Psychology
data.description: Occupational health psychology is a field that focuses on the application of psychological principles and research to improve the health, safety, and well-being of workers in the workplace. It examines the interaction between work and psychological factors, such as stress, job satisfaction, and work-life balance, and their impact on physical and mental health outcomes.

data.name: Energy Security
data.description: Energy security is the association between national security and the availability of natural resources for energy consumption. Access to afforable energy has become essential to the functioning of modern societies and economies.

subjects.term: Energy industries. Energy policy. Fuel trade

data.name: Hate Studies
data.description: Hate crime focuses on the study of criminal offenses committed against individuals or groups based on their perceived race, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or other protected characteristics. Hate crimes are motivated by bias, prejudice, or hatred towards a particular group, and they have significant social and psychological impacts on both victims and communities.

data.name: Technopolitics
data.description: Technopolitics (uncountable) Politics that relates to, or is driven by, modern technology.

data.name: Chinese
data.description: Chinese refers to the Sinitic language family, which includes various dialects and regional varieties spoken primarily in China. Key aspects of Chinese Mandarin Chinese, Cantonese, Written Chinese.  Chinese is one of the most widely spoken languages in the world and has a rich history and cultural significance.

data.name: Bone
data.description: Bone is a mineralized connective tissue from which bones, the main component of the vertebrate skeleton, are formed. Bone tissue is composed of cells, namely osteoblasts, osteoclasts and osteocytes, and an extracellular matrix comprising inorganic hydroxyapatite crystals and organic collagen.

data.name: Pattern Recognition Receptors in Plants
data.description: Pattern recognition receptors are a family of cell surface receptors that bind conserved molecular structures present in pathogens. They play important roles in defence by mediating cellular responses to pathogens.

data.name: Bone Calcium Homeostasis
data.description: Calcium, the most abundant mineral in the body, and vitamin D, a group of fat-soluble secosteroids crucial to calcium homeostasis, are essential for the mineralization of bone matrix. Extracellular calcium concentrations are controlled by parathyroid hormone, which stimulates the release of calcium from bones, and vitamin D, which promotes intestinal calcium absorption.

data.name: Climate-Change Adaptation
data.description: Climate-change adaptation encompasses a broad range of human policies and activities primarily intended to reduce the risks posed by climate change. It includes both realised and expected risks.

data.name: Space Weather
data.description: Space weather refers to the environmental conditions and events occurring in the space surrounding Earth, particularly the Sun-Earth system, that can affect technological systems and human activities. It is driven by various dynamic processes on the Sun, solar wind, magnetic fields, and interactions with the Earth's magnetosphere and atmosphere. Space weather phenomena can have significant impacts on satellite operations, communication systems, power grids, aviation, and other technological infrastructure.

data.name: Sub-wavelength Optics
data.description: Sub-wavelength optics is the study of light on a spatial scale smaller than its wavelength. Conventionally, the minimum length scale on which a beam of light can operate is equal to half its wavelength. However, by coupling light to matter, photonic effects can be realised on a much smaller spatial scale.

data.name: Motor Protein Structure
data.description: Motor protein structure describes the structure of molecular motors capable of moving along a cytoskeletal filament. In many cases, motor proteins transport cargo in a particular direction along the filament, and this directionality is associated with both protein and filament structure.

data.name: Plant Polarity
data.description: Plant polarity refers to the asymmetric distribution of cellular components along a particular axis within a cell, and is essential for processes such as intercellular communication, cell division, cell morphogenesis and differentiation. Polarised cells are involved in the patterning of plant tissues and organs, and therefore contribute to the overall shape of the plant.

data.name: Geriatric Psychiatry
data.description: Geriatric psychiatry emphasizes the biological and psychological aspects of normal aging, the psychiatric effect of acute and chronic physical illness, and the biological and psychosocial aspects of the pathology of primary psychiatric disturbances of older age. Geriatric psychiatrists focus on prevention, evaluation, diagnosis and treatment of mental and emotional disorders in the elderly and improvement of psychiatric care for healthy and ill elderly patients.

data.name: Aurora
data.description: An aurora, also commonly known as polar lights, northern lights, or southern lights, is a natural light display in Earth's sky, predominantly seen in high-latitude regions. Auroras display dynamic patterns of brilliant lights that appear as curtains, rays, spirals, or dynamic flickers covering the entire sky.

data.name: Clinical Microbiology
data.description: Clinical microbiology is a branch of microbiology that focuses on the study of microorganisms and their impact on human health. It involves the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of infectious diseases through the identification and characterization of pathogenic microorganisms. Clinical microbiologists work in medical laboratories, where they utilize a range of techniques to isolate, culture, and identify microorganisms found in patient samples.

data.name: Ethical, Legal, and Social Aspects of Genetics
data.description: Genetics and Society analyzes the social, ethical, and legal implications of genetic research and technologies, examining issues such as genetic privacy, discrimination, and the impact of genetic information on individuals and communities.

data.name: Internet Studies
data.description: Internet studies is an interdisciplinary field studying the social, psychological, pedagogical, political, technical, cultural, artistic, and other dimensions of the Internet and associated information and communication technologies.

data.name: British and Irish Literature
data.description: Literature originating from the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man, the Channel Islands and Ireland.

synonyms: Literature from the United Kingdom and Ireland

data.name: Supramolecular Cages
data.description: Supramolecular cages, also known as molecular cages or host-guest complexes, are three-dimensional structures formed by the self-assembly of smaller molecules or building blocks. These cages have an enclosed space or cavity that can encapsulate guest molecules, providing a controlled and protective environment for them.

data.name: Lithography
data.description: Lithography is the process of transferring a pattern onto a surface. In optical lithography, a physical mask covers a light sensitive film as it is exposed to (usually ultraviolet) radiation. Electron lithography instead draws the pattern by scanning a beam of electrons. A solution then develops the exposed film.

data.name: Membrane Fission
data.description: Membrane fission involves the splitting of a single, contiguous membrane into two parts. This process requires energy and is involved in cell division, endocytosis, transport carrier formation, budding, and division of membrane-bound organelles.

data.name: Microtubules
data.description: Microtubules are cylindrical polymers composed of alpha and beta tubulin. They are a major component of the cytoskeleton and mediate crucial cellular functions including formation of the mitotic spindle that segregates chromosomes during cell division and intracellular trafficking.

data.name: Peroxisomes
data.description: Peroxisomes are cytoplasmic organelles that catalyse the breakdown of very long chain fatty acids through beta-oxidation. Peroxisomes also have an important role in generating and degrading reactive oxygen species.

data.name: Surface Assembly
data.description: Surface assembly describes the processes by which a disordered system of discrete atomic or molecular components forms an organized structure or pattern on a surface. Understanding the molecular structure and properties of these patterns and why they arise underpins this field, which often requires the use of surface-specific techniques such as scanning probe microscopy.

data.name: Physical Properties of Materials
data.description: Physical properties refer to properties that can be observed or measured without changing the composition of the material. Examples include colour, hardness and smell and freezing, melting and boiling points

data.name: Enterprise Architecture
data.description: Enterprise Architecture (EA) is a field of business and management research and practice that focuses on the design and implementation of a coherent and integrated set of business and IT capabilities that support an organization's goals and objectives. It involves the development of a comprehensive understanding of an organization's current and desired states, and the identification of the gaps and opportunities for improvement.  The following are major topics within the field of Enterprise Architecture:  Business Architecture: Business Architecture defines the organization's business strategy, goals, processes, and organizational structure. It aims to provide a clear understanding of the organization's operations and how they can be optimized.  Information Architecture: Information Architecture defines the organization's information strategy, including the data, information, and knowledge assets required to support the business processes. It ensures that information is available, secure, and usable by the organization's stakeholders.  Application Architecture: Application Architecture focuses on the design and implementation of software applications that support the organization's business processes. It includes the development of application standards, guidelines, and best practices.  Technology Architecture: Technology Architecture defines the organization's technology strategy, including the hardware, software, and network infrastructure required to support the business processes. It ensures that the technology is aligned with the organization's goals and objectives.  Governance: Governance refers to the establishment of policies, standards, and procedures to ensure that the Enterprise Architecture is consistent with the organization's goals and objectives. It ensures that the organization's resources are used effectively and efficiently.  Change Management: Change Management refers to the process of managing the changes to the Enterprise Architecture. It involves the development of a plan to manage the implementation of new systems, applications, or processes, and the communication of the changes to stakeholders.  Risk Management: Risk Management involves identifying, assessing, and managing risks associated with the implementation of the Enterprise Architecture. It ensures that the organization's assets are protected and that the risks are managed effectively.  Overall, the goal of Enterprise Architecture is to provide a holistic and integrated view of the organization, its processes, and its resources.

data.name: HTLV
data.description: HTLV (human T-cell lymphotropic virus) is an infectious agent belonging to the virus family Retroviridae that is spread through contact with bodily fluids and causes a persistent infection in humans. It is associated with a number of pathologies, including adult T-cell leukaemia.

data.name: Hepatitis B Virus
data.description: Hepatitis B virus is an infectious agent that causes hepatitis B, a type of liver inflammation in humans. A vaccine exists against this virus species.

data.name: Cell Invasion
data.description: Cell invasion is related to cell migration, and defines the ability of cells to become motile and to navigate through the extracellular matrix within a tissue or to infiltrate neighbouring tissues. Cancer cells that become invasive may disseminate to secondary sites and form metastases.

data.name: Seed Development
data.description: Seed development is the process by which seeds are formed from the end of fertilization to the production of a mature seed body.

data.name: Mitochondria
data.description: Mitochondria are cytoplasmic organelles found in most eukaryotic cells. They are formed from an outer membrane, a highly invaginated inner membrane containing cristae, and a matrix. Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, and also have a central role in apoptosis.

data.name: Neural Patterning
data.description: Neural patterning is the biological process by which cells in the developing nervous system acquire distinct identities according to their specific spatial positions. Neural patterning is controlled by the combinatorial actions of signalling gradients along the dorso–ventral, antero–posterior and left–right axis of the developing nervous system.

data.name: Autologous Transplantation
data.description: Autologous transplantation is a procedure in which an individual's own tissue is used to replace their damaged tissue. The removed tissue can be used immediately at a different site. Alternatively, the tissue can be removed, the individual or the tissue can be treated, and the tissue can then be replaced, for example cell transplantation.

data.name: Underground Engineering and Tunnel Construction
data.description: Underground construction refers to the construction of underground tunnels, shafts, chambers, and passageways, it is also sometimes used to describe the portion of traditional construction that takes place below grade. The method of tunnel construction depends on such factors as the ground conditions, the ground water conditions, the length and diameter of the tunnel drive, the depth of the tunnel, the logistics of supporting the tunnel excavation, the final use and shape of the tunnel and appropriate risk management. Tunnel construction is a subset of underground construction. Underground construction and tunnel engineering is truly an interdisciplinary practice, involving knowledge and skills primarily in civil engineering, geological engineering and mining engineering and, to a lesser extent, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, geophysics, geology and others.

data.name: Algorithmic Complexity
data.description: Algorithmic complexity is concerned about how fast or slow particular algorithm performs. We define complexity as a numerical function T(n) - time versus the input size n. We want to define time taken by an algorithm without depending on the implementation details.

data.name: Optical processing and Holography
data.description: In general, holography is the storage of the phase and amplitude information of a wavefront. It is usually used as an approach to create three-dimensional (3D) images of objects through interference between a wavefront diffracted and a coherent reference beam.

data.name: Trafficking
data.description: Trafficking refers to the illegal trade and transportation of goods, services, or individuals, often involving exploitation and coercion. It is commonly associated with activities such as human trafficking, drug trafficking, arms trafficking, and trafficking in wildlife.

data.name: Continuum Biomechanics
data.description: Continuum biomechanics is a field of study that applies principles of mechanics to analyze the mechanical behavior of biological tissues and systems at various scales. It focuses on understanding how biological materials and structures deform, respond to loads, and interact with their environment. Continuum biomechanics considers biological materials as continuous and deformable bodies, treating them as a continuum rather than individual discrete elements. It is particularly relevant in areas such as tissue mechanics, organ function, and biomechanical modeling.

data.name: Chromatin Immunoprecipitation
data.description: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) is a technique for identifying DNA sequences associated with specific proteins in vivo. The association of DNA fragments with a binding protein, such as a transcription factor or modified histone, can be assessed by sequencing, microarrays or PCR after precipitation with an antibody that recognizes the protein.

data.name: Planet Formation
data.description: The nebular hypothesis is the most widely accepted model in the field of cosmogony to explain the formation and evolution of the Solar System (as well as other planetary systems). It suggests the Solar System is formed from gas and dust orbiting the Sun which clumped up together to form the planets.

data.name: Viral Host Response
data.description: The viral host response is the process by which a host interacts with and responds to viruses that it encounters. It includes various mechanisms, such as immune mechanisms that are elicited in an attempt to eliminate the virus or halt its growth.

data.name: Nanochemistry
data.description: Nanochemistry is the combination of chemistry and nano science; it can be characterized by concepts of size, shape, self-assembly, defects and bio-nano. Nano-construct synthesis is dependent on how the surface, size and shape will lead to self-assembly of the building blocks into the functional structures.

data.name: Leaf Development
data.description: Leaf development describes the coordinated morphogenesis process by which a leaf is formed, and grows to become a mature photosynthetic organ. It starts from the initiation of a primordium in the shoot meristem, and ends with the fully structured leaf, composed of several cell types such as trichomes, guard cells, epidermal and mesophyll layers, and vascular cells.

data.name: Gastrointestinal Hormones
data.description: Gastrointestinal hormones are hormones produced from specialized endocrine cells of the stomach, pancreas and small intestine, which are secreted directly into the bloodstream. Here, they promote the physical process of food digestion, detect harmful substances and generate responses that protect against harmful substances. Examples of gastrointestinal hormones are ghrelin, amylin and glucagon-like peptides 1 and 2.

data.name: Bisphosphonates
data.description: Bisphosphonates are a class of drugs, structurally similar to pyrophosphate, that inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption by binding with high affinity to the hydroxyapatite crystals of bone mineral. Bisphosphonates are used in the therapy of a range of metabolic bone diseases, notably osteoporosis, and as bone-imaging agents.

data.name: Proteolysis in Plants
data.description: Proteolysis in plants refers to the cleavage of proteins into smaller peptides or amino acids by plant proteases. This can occur both inter- and intracellularly.

data.name: Bone Quality and Biomechanics
data.description: Bone quality and mechanics is a concept used to describe physical features of bone. They can be quantified with bone density, the amount of mineral matter per unit of volume, and the trabecular bone score, a measure of bone microarchitecture. These scores can be used to predict the risk of fractures and osteoporosis.

data.name: Development Policy
data.description: Development policy encompasses all political, economic and social measures to help improve living conditions in developing countries in a sustainable way.

data.name: Infection control in dentistry
data.description: Infection control procedures are actions taken in oral health care settings to prevent the spread of disease. Specific recommendations for dental office infection control ensure the safety of patients and dental staff.

data.name: Italian
data.description: Italian is a Romance language spoken primarily in Italy, San Marino, Vatican City, and parts of Switzerland and Slovenia. It is one of the major languages of the world and has a rich cultural heritage, particularly in the fields of art, literature, music, and cuisine. Italian evolved from Vulgar Latin and has been influenced by various regional dialects. Standard Italian, known as Italiano standard or lingua italiana, is based on the Tuscan dialect, particularly the variety spoken in Florence.

data.name: Bionanoelectronics
data.description: Bionanoelectronics is an interdisciplinary field concerned with systems that interface biological matter with synthetic biocompatible nanomaterials for use in electronic components. Examples of bionanoelectronic systems are biosensors, drug-delivery devices and neural circuits.

data.name: Regeneration
data.description: Regeneration is the process by which lost or damaged tissues, organs or limbs are re-formed from the remaining tissue. During regeneration, adult stem cells and/or progenitor cells differentiate to replace the missing tissue, although in some instances differentiated cells can also participate in the regeneration by proliferation or transdifferentiation.

data.name: Drought
data.description: Drought is a prolonged period of water deficit. For plants, it represents a severe abiotic stress to which they have to adapt, and it can lead to considerable economical losses in worldwide crop agriculture.

data.name: Stomach
data.description: The stomach, which is located in the abdomen between the oesophagus and the duodenum, is composed of four parts: the cardia, fundus, body and pylorus. It is responsible for food digestion and release of enzymes, and acts to protect the intestine from harmful organisms.

data.name: Food Security
data.description: Food security is the availability of food in a country (or geography) and the ability of individuals within that country (geography) to access, afford, and source adequate foodstuffs.

data.name: Coordination Polymer
data.description: Coordination polymers are materials composed of metal ions linked by ligands that form an extended array. The arrays can extend in one, two or three dimensions.

data.name: Media Research
data.description: Media research involves the study of media's impact on social, physical, and psychological aspects of people's lives. It involves the study of information related to mass communication. Newspapers, magazines, radio broadcasts, and television are examples of mass media.

data.name: Ionic Liquids
data.description: Ionic liquids are salts with melting points below 100 oC and are therefore liquids at lower temperatures than other salts. The materials can have useful physical properties, such as low or non-volatility, and are often used as solvents and electrolytes.

data.name: Confocal Microscopy
data.description: Confocal microscopy is an optical imaging technique that scans a focused point of light around a sample to reconstruct an image in a point-by-point manner. A pinhole is used in the detection path to reject out-of-focus light and increase resolution and contrast compared to wide field illumination. The technique is particularly useful for three-dimensional imaging.

data.name: Econometrics
data.description: Econometrics is the application of statistical and mathematical methods to economic data. It aims to quantify economic relationships, test economic theories, and forecast future economic trends. By using statistical tools, econometrics helps in making informed decisions and policies based on empirical data. It combines economic theory, mathematics, and statistical inference to analyze economic phenomena.

data.name: Genetic Testing
data.description: Genetic testing involves the detection of specific alleles, mutations, genotypes or karyotypes that are associated with heritable traits, diseases or predispositions to disease for the individual or their descendants. Genetic testing may also be used as a method for the determination of parentage or ancestry.

data.name: Bioanalytical Chemistry
data.description: Bioanalytical chemistry is a subdiscipline of analytical chemistry that involves the separation, detection, identification and quantification of biological samples in different settings. It often involves the study of molecules such as proteins, peptides, DNA and drugs.

data.name: UV-Visible Spectroscopy
data.description: UV spectroscopy or UV–visible spectrophotometry refers to absorption spectroscopy or reflectance spectroscopy in part of the ultraviolet and the full, adjacent visible regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. or in simple terms it is a quantitative technique used to measure how much a chemical substance absorbs light.

data.name: Transgenic Plants
data.description: Transgenic plants are plants into which one or more genes from another species have been introduced into the genome, using genetic engineering processes. Techniques include the biolistic method, in which a heavy metal is coated with plasmid DNA is shot into cells, and Agrobacterium tumefaciens mediated transformation.

data.name: Financial Engineering
data.description: Financial engineering is a multidisciplinary field that applies mathematical and quantitative methods to design, develop, and analyze financial products, instruments, and strategies. In research and practice, financial engineering involves a range of activities and tasks, including:  Design and development of financial products: The design and development of financial products such as derivatives, options, and futures contracts, which can be used to manage financial risk or to achieve specific investment objectives.  Risk management: The identification, assessment, and management of financial risks associated with various financial products and strategies, including credit risk, market risk, and operational risk.  Quantitative analysis: The use of mathematical and statistical models to analyze financial data and to develop strategies for managing financial risk.  Optimization of financial strategies: The development and optimization of financial strategies such as portfolio management, asset allocation, and hedging strategies, to achieve specific financial objectives such as maximizing returns or minimizing risk.  Pricing and valuation: The development of pricing and valuation models for financial products, to ensure that they are priced accurately and fairly.  Overall, the goal of financial engineering is to create innovative financial products and strategies that meet the needs of investors and financial institutions, while managing financial risk and achieving specific financial objectives. In practice, financial engineering is used by a range of financial institutions and organizations, including banks, hedge funds, insurance companies, and pension funds.

data.name: Fuel Cells
data.description: A fuel cell is a device that generates electric energy through electrochemical reactions between an oxidizing agent and a fuel – a material that stores energy in chemical form. Both species are not stored in the fuel cell but must be supplied from external sources.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Doubled Haploids
data.description: Doubled haploids (DH) are plants that have been artificially produced to possess a complete set of homozygous chromosomes through a process called haploid doubling. Haploid doubling involves inducing a doubling of the chromosome number in a haploid cell, resulting in a plant with a complete diploid genome. Doubled haploids are useful in plant breeding and genetic research because they can bypass several generations of traditional breeding by generating completely homozygous lines in a single step.

data.name: Ectopic Hormone
data.description: Ectopic hormones are hormones produced by tumours derived from tissues that are not normally engaged in the production of that hormone. Ectopic hormone production is generally considered inappropriate and detrimental as the hormones can dysregulate various metabolic functions that are reliant on the hormone.

data.name: Dynein
data.description: Dynein is a minus-end-directed microtubule motor protein, which transports a variety of intracellular cargo by hydrolysing ATP to power its movement along microtubule tracks. Axonemal dyneins are found cilia and flagella, whereas cytoplasmic dynein is found in all animal cells.

data.name: Water Quality and Water Pollution
data.description: Water quality refers to the physical, chemical, and biological characteristics of water, which determine its suitability for various uses, such as drinking, recreational activities, agriculture, and industrial processes. When water has high quality, it is safe for human consumption and supports a healthy aquatic ecosystem. However, water pollution occurs when harmful substances are introduced into water bodies, degrading the water quality and posing risks to human health and the environment.

data.name: Tight Junctions
data.description: Tight junctions are a type of cell-cell junction found in epithelia that forms a barrier that is impermeable to the majority of soluble molecules between the two sides of the epithelium. Major components of tight junctions are claudin and occludin proteins.

data.name: Patenting
data.description: Patenting is a field of management research and practice that focuses on the strategic use of patents to commercialize technology. This field encompasses a range of topics related to the identification, acquisition, management, and enforcement of patents in order to create value for a firm.  Core topics within the field of patenting include:  Patent strategy: This topic focuses on developing a patent strategy that aligns with a firm's overall business goals. It involves understanding the competitive landscape and identifying areas where patents can be used to create a competitive advantage.  Patent acquisition: This topic deals with the process of acquiring patents either through internal development or external sources, such as licensing or purchasing patents from other firms. It includes assessing the value of patents and negotiating licensing or acquisition agreements.  Patent portfolio management: This topic involves managing a firm's patent portfolio to maximize its value. It includes identifying and prioritizing patents for commercialization, monitoring the patent landscape for potential infringement, and assessing the potential value of new patents.  Patent litigation: This topic deals with the legal aspects of enforcing patents, such as filing lawsuits against infringers or defending against infringement claims. It includes assessing the likelihood of success in litigation and the potential costs and benefits of pursuing legal action.  Patent licensing: This topic involves negotiating licensing agreements with other firms to commercialize patented technology. It includes assessing the value of the licensed technology, negotiating licensing terms, and monitoring compliance with the licensing agreement.  Overall, patenting is a critical field for firms looking to commercialize technology, and understanding its core topics is essential for success in this area.

data.name: World Regional Geography
data.description: World regional geography explores how the world is divided into distinct regions based on shared cultural, environmental, political, and economic characteristics. Typical areas are continents, countries and regions.

data.name: Market Intelligence
data.description: Market Intelligence is a field of management research that involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting information about the market, customers, competitors, and industry trends to support strategic decision-making. Market intelligence provides businesses with a comprehensive understanding of their market, which can help them identify new opportunities, mitigate risks, and gain a competitive advantage.  Market intelligence is a systematic and ongoing process that involves collecting and analyzing data from a variety of sources, including market research reports, customer surveys, industry publications, and competitor analysis. This information is then used to develop insights and recommendations that guide business strategy and inform decision-making across a range of functions, including product development, marketing, sales, and operations.  The ultimate goal of market intelligence is to provide businesses with a deep understanding of their market and customers, allowing them to make informed decisions that lead to long-term success and profitability. By staying on top of market trends and changes, businesses can adapt quickly to changing conditions and maintain a competitive edge in their industry

data.name: Remote Sensing and Photogrammetry
data.description: Remote sensing collects data in the form of light and color. By detecting different wavelengths of light radiation, it can generate maps. Instead of measuring wavelengths of radiation, on the other hand, photogrammetry uses imagery to measure coordinates in space. Photogrammetry is the science and technology of obtaining reliable information about physical objects and the environment through the process of recording, measuring and interpreting photographic images and patterns of electromagnetic radiant imagery and other phenomena.

Geographical information systems, geodata and remote sensing

data.name: Religion and Ethics
data.description: Religious believers who make ethical judgements solely on the basis of their religious beliefs see the two as indistinguishable. So some Christians see the wrongness of divorce as consisting in its offence against God’s law. While some people see their religious and ethical duties as compatible and even co-extensive. For example, some people see adultery as wrong because it is forbidden by God’s law and because it involves deceiving marriage partners.

data.name: Ferromagnetism
data.description: Ferromagnetism is a form of magnetic ordering in which the intrinsic magnetic dipole moment, or spin, of electrons on each crystal-lattice site all align in the same direction. It is the phenomenon that gives materials such as iron, cobalt and nickel their magnetic properties.

data.name: Instructional Design
data.description: Instructional design is a field of study that focuses on the systematic process of creating effective and efficient instructional materials and learning experiences. It involves the application of learning theories, educational psychology, and pedagogical principles to design and develop instructional materials, courses, and programs.

data.name: Whole Genome Amplification
data.description: Whole genome amplification is a method for generating many copies of an entire genome for downstream applications such as sequencing when starting material is limited.

data.name: Gender and STS
data.description: Gender and STS (Science, Technology, and Society) examines how gender influences and is influenced by scientific and technological developments, exploring issues of equity, representation, and impact.

data.name: Oral Medicine
data.description: Oral medicine is concerned with clinical diagnosis and non-surgical management of non-dental pathologies affecting the orofacial region (the mouth and the lower face).

data.name: Stem-Cell Differentiation
data.description: Stem-cell differentiation is the process by which a more specialised cell is formed from a stem cell, leading to loss of some of the stem cell's developmental potential. Stem-cell differentiation occurs during development of an organism to produce new specialised cells, and also in adults to replenish cells that are lost.

data.name: Mechanobiology
data.description: focuses on how physical forces and changes in the mechanical properties of cells and tissues contribute to development, cell differentiation, physiology, and disease

data.name: Personalized Medicine
data.description: Personalized medicine is a therapeutic approach involving the use of an individual's genetic and epigenetic information to tailor drug therapy or preventive care.

data.name: Totipotent Stem Cells
data.description: Totipotent stem cells are cells that have the capacity to self-renew by dividing and to develop into the three primary germ cell layers of the early embryo and into extra-embryonic tissues such as the placenta. A fertilised egg is a totipotent stem cell and as such can develop into any specialised cell found in the organism.

data.name: Pathogens
data.description: Pathogens are infectious agents, such as a bacterium, virus, fungus or parasite, that cause disease when they colonize a host organism.

data.name: Cartilage
data.description: Cartilage is a semi-rigid, avascular connective tissue composed of chondrocytes loosely embedded in an extracellular matrix of collagen fibres, proteoglycans and other, noncollagenous proteins. The three main forms of cartilage are hyaline cartilage, fibrocartilage and elastic cartilage.

data.name: Cilia
data.description: Cilia are outgrowths of the plasma membrane of eukaryotic cells that contain a specialised cytoskeleton. Motile cilia are present on multiciliated cells and use this cytoskeleton to move fluid, whereas non-motile, or primary, cilia have a different cytoskeleton and participate in signalling between cells.

data.name: Lymph Node
data.description: Lymph nodes are small organs that are distributed throughout the body and drain lymph fluid from the tissues. Immune cells reside in lymph nodes and survey the lymph for signs of infection. If a tissue is infected, immune cells in the draining lymph node become activated and proliferate.

data.name: Quantitative Geology
data.description: Quantitative geology uses statistical, mathematical, and computing techniques.

data.name: Quality Control, Reliability, Safety and Risk
data.description: Quality control is a set of methods for maintaining standards in production lines or in a process. Quality control can be applied to methods, equipment, processes or products and usually involves spot tests or products or procedures to ensure that standards are maintained.

data.name: Motor Protein Tracks
data.description: Motor protein tracks are the cytoskeletal filaments, including actin and microtubules, on which motor proteins move. In many cases, motor proteins transport cargo in a particular direction along the filament, and this directionality is associated with both protein and filament structure.

data.name: Medical Imaging
data.description: Medical imaging is the technique and process of imaging the interior of a body for clinical analysis and medical intervention, as well as visual representation of the function of some organs or tissues (physiology). Medical imaging seeks to reveal internal structures hidden by the skin and bones, as well as to diagnose and treat disease. Medical imaging also establishes a database of normal anatomy and physiology to make it possible to identify abnormalities.  (Although imaging of removed organs and tissues can be performed for medical reasons, such procedures are usually considered part of pathology instead of medical imaging.)

data.name: Childhood Studies
data.description: Childhood studies or children's studies (CS) or Critical Childhood Studies is a multidisciplinary field that seeks to understand the experience of childhood, both historically and in the contemporary world. CS views childhood as "a complex social phenomenon"[1] with an emphasis on children's agency as social actors, and acknowledges that childhood is socially constructed as the concept of childhood is not universal.

data.name: Group Level Phenomena
data.description: Group-level phenomena in the field of psychology refer to the behaviors, attitudes, and dynamics that emerge within groups or collectives of individuals. It focuses on understanding how individuals' thoughts, emotions, and behaviors are influenced by the group context and how groups function as a whole.

data.name: Marker Assisted Selection
data.description: An indirect selection process where a trait of interest is selected based on a marker (morphological, biochemical or DNA/RNA variation) linked to a trait of interest (e.g. productivity, disease resistance, abiotic stress tolerance, and quality), rather than on the trait itself.

data.name: Oral Pathology
data.description: Oral pathology is the study, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases in the teeth, gums, bones, joints, glands, skin, and muscles around your mouth. The American Dental Education Association states that Oral Pathologists require 37 months of advanced education on average to become experts in this field.

data.name: Coevolution
data.description: Coevolution is the process by which two or more species evolve in tandem by exerting selection pressures on each other. Examples of coevolutionary systems include host and parasites, predators and prey, and mutualistic or symbiotic interactions.

data.name: Research Methods in Education
data.description: Research methods in education refer to the various techniques and approaches used to gather data, analyze information, and generate knowledge in the field of education. These methods enable researchers to investigate educational phenomena, answer research questions, and contribute to the understanding and improvement of education.

data.name: Indo-Iranian Languages
data.description: Indo-Iranian languages are a major branch of the Indo-European language family. They are primarily spoken in the Indian subcontinent, Iran, Afghanistan, and Tajikistan. This branch is further divided into two main groups: Indo-Aryan and Iranian languages. Indo-Aryan languages include Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, Gujarati, Marathi, and Nepali. Iranian languages include  Persian (Farsi), Pashto, Kurdish, Balochi, Tajik, and several other languages.

data.name: Energy Economics
data.description: Energy economics studies human utilization of energy resources and the consequences of that utilization.

synonyms: Wirtschaft der natürlichen Ressourcen und Energie

subjects.term: Energy industries. Energy policy. Fuel trade

data.name: Collision Processes Involving Bio-macromolecules
data.description: The interactions and events that occur when large biological molecules, such as proteins, nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), polysaccharides, and other complex biomolecules, come into contact with each other or with other molecules in their environment. These collisions can lead to various biochemical and biophysical processes that play critical roles in biological systems.

data.name: CRISPR-Cas systems
data.description: CRISPR-Cas systems are prokaryotic immune systems that confer resistance to foreign genetic elements such as plasmids and phages. CRISPR-Cas systems have been exploited for targeted genome editing.

data.name: Quantum Computing
data.description: Quantum computing is computing using quantum-mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement. The relative device is called quantum computer.

subjects.term: Quantum physics (quantum mechanics & quantum field theory)
Quantum physics (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory)

data.name: Glial Progenitors
data.description: Glial progenitors are cells that are capable of dividing a limited number of times and have the capacity to differentiate into a restricted repertoire of glial cell types.

data.name: Plant Stem Cell
data.description: Plant stem cells are innately undifferentiated cells located in the meristems of plant. They serve as the origin of plant vitality, as they maintain themselves while providing a steady supply of precursor cells to form differentiated tissues and organs in the plant.

data.name: Knowledge and Innovation
data.description: Knowledge and Innovation has, as its objective, that of contributing through its basic and applied research to the generation of new knowledge on contemporary societies and the transformations taking place within them.

data.name: Vernalization
data.description: Vernalization refers to the acceleration of flowering that occurs following prolonged exposure of seeds or young seedlings to low temperatures. Plants that are vernalized do not flower immediately upon exposure to higher temperatures, but often weeks later.

data.name: Archaeal Genomics
data.description: Archaeal genomics is a scientific discipline that concerns the genome, encompassing the entire hereditary information, of Archaea, a domain of organisms consisting of single, nucleus-free cells, distinct from bacteria and eukaryotes.

data.name: Data Integration
data.description: Data integration is the process of combining data generated using a variety of different research methods in order to enable detection of underlying themes and, in computational biology and bioinformatics, biological principles. Data integration is important in biology owing to the large and different 'omics' datasets now available.

data.name: Corrosion
data.description: Corrosion is the deterioration of a material as a result of its chemical reaction with oxidizing agents that are present in its environment.

data.name: Classics and Classicism
data.description: The following of ancient Greek or Roman principles and style in art and literature, especially from the Renaissance to the 18th century. Generally refers to a high regard for a classical period.

data.name: European Union Politics
data.description: Politics of the European Union

data.name: Cohesion
data.description: Cohesion is a molecular phenomenon that refers to the force that holds together sister chromatids, which are identical copies of a chromosome, during cell division. This process is primarily mediated by the cohesin protein complex, which encircles the chromatids and maintains their attachment until the appropriate stage of mitosis. The regulated dissolution of cohesin allows for the precise separation of chromatids into daughter cells, ensuring accurate genetic distribution. Cohesion is crucial for maintaining genomic stability and is tightly controlled to prevent errors during cell division.

data.name: Semantic Memory
data.description: Semantic memory, in the field of psychology, refers to a long-term memory system responsible for storing and retrieving general knowledge and concepts about the world, including facts, meanings, and relationships between words and concepts. It represents our understanding of language, objects, people, and abstract ideas, and it is essential for comprehension, communication, and problem-solving.

data.name: Silicon Photonics
data.description: Silicon photonics is the study of the optical properties of the group-IV semiconductor and the design and fabrication of devices for generating, manipulating and detecting light. Silicon is prevalent in photodetectors, solar cells in particular. However, its indirect band structure means that it is not a natural creator of light.

data.name: Neonatology
data.description: Neonatology is a subspecialty of pediatrics that consists of the medical care of newborn infants, especially the ill or premature newborn.

data.name: Bone Metastases
data.description: Bone metastases are cancers that have spread (metastasized) from other tissues in the body through the blood or lymphatic systems to the bone marrow. Bone metastases form the main type of bone cancer and, in descending order of frequency, originate from: breast, prostate, lung, colon, stomach, bladder, uterus, rectum, thyroid and kidney.

data.name: Substructural Logics
data.description: In logic, a substructural logic is a logic lacking one of the usual structural rules (e.g. of classical and intuitionistic logic), such as weakening, contraction, exchange or associativity. Two of the more significant substructural logics are relevance logic and linear logic.

data.name: Religion and Society
data.description: Religion ideally serves several functions. It gives meaning and purpose to life, reinforces social unity and stability, serves as an agent of social control, promotes psychological and physical well-being, and may motivate people to work for positive social change.

data.name: Trauma Surgery
data.description: Trauma surgery is a surgical specialty that utilizes both operative and non-operative management to treat traumatic injuries, typically in an acute setting. Trauma surgeons generally complete residency training in general surgery and often fellowship training in trauma or surgical critical care.

data.name: Respiratory Management
data.description: Airway management is the practice of evaluating, planning, and using a wide array of medical procedures and devices for the purpose of maintaining or restoring a safe, effective pathway for oxygenation and ventilation. These procedures are indicated in patients with airway obstruction, respiratory failure.

data.name: Religion and Sport
data.description: Sport is often used as a metaphor for religious striving; Sporting events evoke passionate commitment similar to that of religious festivals; Religion and sport are symbolic systems that emphasize similar values and goals, including transcendence of limited personal desires in favor of nonmaterial achievements or experiences and an emphasis on cooperation and personal sacrifice for the good of the group

data.name: Restorative Dentistry
data.description: Restorative dentistry focuses on repairing or replacing damaged or missing teeth. These procedures help improve oral health and function. Common dental restorations include crowns, bridges and implants.

data.name: Genetic Modification
data.description: Genetic engineering, also called genetic modification or genetic manipulation, is the direct manipulation of an organism's genes using biotechnology. It is a set of technologies used to change the genetic makeup of cells, including the transfer of genes within and across species boundaries to produce improved or novel organisms.

data.name: Circadian Rhythms in Plants
data.description: Circadian rhythms are observable biological oscillations that occur with a 24-hour periodicity. They are based on an endogenous transcriptional clock, which itself is reinforced by environmental cues such as variations in light and temperature.

data.name: Cultural Sociology
data.description: the sociological study of the historical processes involved in cultural phenomena (such as art, philosophy, and religion)

data.name: Environmental Impact
data.description: Defined as any change to the environment, caused by development, industry or infrastructure, or by the release of certain substances in the environment.

data.name: Rings and Moons
data.description: Rings and moons are natural features commonly associated with planets and some other celestial bodies in the solar system. Rings are made up of various materials, including ice particles, rocks, dust, and debris.  Rings are typically formed by the gravitational interactions between a celestial body and its orbiting moons or other objects. Moons are natural satellites that orbit around planets, dwarf planets, asteroids, or other celestial bodies.  Moons can have diverse compositions, including rocky, icy, or a combination of both materials.

data.name: DNA Damage Checkpoints
data.description: A DNA damage checkpoint is a pause in the cell cycle that is induced in response to DNA damage to ensure that the damage is repaired before cell division resumes. Proteins that accumulate at the damage site typically activate the checkpoint and halt cell growth at the G1/S or G2/M boundaries.

data.name: Predictive Medicine
data.description: Predictive medicine is a branch of medicine that aims to identify patients at risk of developing a disease, thereby enabling either prevention or early treatment of that disease. Either single or more commonly multiple analyses are used to identify markers of future disposition to a disease.

data.name: Numerical Cognition
data.description: Numerical cognition in the field of psychology refers to the study of how individuals perceive, process, and understand numerical information. It involves the cognitive processes and mechanisms underlying numerical representation, calculation, estimation, and problem-solving.

data.name: Social and Cultural Geography
data.description: Studies the cultural landscapes which are determined by societies developing out of their local landscapes, and those landscaped being shaped on the the other hand by the societies located there. Social/Cultural geography is a complex research field that encloses a variety of subfields such as political and gender studies, anthropology, and sociology.

data.name: Bioeconomies
data.description: Bioeconomy refers to an economic system that is based on the sustainable utilization of biological resources, including renewable resources from land and sea, as well as waste and byproducts, to produce food, energy, and industrial goods. It encompasses a wide range of sectors including agriculture, forestry, fisheries, biotechnology, and more.

data.name: Social Robotics
data.description: The field of social robotics concentrates on the development and design of robots which interact socially with humans, but sociality between robots (e.g., in multirobot systems) is not part of the field.

data.name: Viral Pathogenesis
data.description: Viral pathogenesis is the process by which viruses infect and cause disease in a host.

data.name: Polymer Synthesis
data.description: Polymer synthesis, also called polymerization, is the process by which monomers (small molecules) are covalently bonded to form a (usually long) polymer chain or network.

data.name: Scandinavian Languages
data.description: Scandinavian languages refer to a group of closely related languages spoken in the Scandinavian region of Northern Europe. These languages belong to the North Germanic branch of the Germanic language family and share many similarities in terms of grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation. some main Scandinavian languages: Danish, Norwegian, Swedish, Icelandic, Faroese.

data.name: Fracture Repair
data.description: Fracture repair is the complex physiological process by which bone tissue heals following fracture, involving characteristic phases of inflammation, bony callus formation and bone remodelling.

data.name: Development Aid
data.description: Development aid is a type of foreign/international/overseas aid given by governments and other agencies to support the economic, environmental, social, and political development of developing countries.

data.name: Reading
data.description: Reading is the process of deriving meaning from complex symbols. It involves decoding letters and recognizing words, as well as fluency in understanding sentences and larger units of language.

data.name: Academic Spin-Offs
data.description: Academic spin-offs refer to new ventures that are created to commercialize technologies, products, or services developed in universities or research institutions. These ventures are typically founded by academic researchers or entrepreneurs who have a strong knowledge of the technology and market opportunities for their innovation.  The field of academic spin-offs encompasses a range of research and practice areas, including:  Technology transfer: This involves the transfer of knowledge, intellectual property, and technology from universities or research institutions to new ventures. It includes issues such as patenting, licensing, and protecting intellectual property.  Entrepreneurship: This includes the skills and competencies required to start and grow a new venture. It includes topics such as business planning, fundraising, and marketing.  Innovation management: This involves the processes and strategies for managing innovation within a new venture. It includes topics such as product development, market research, and project management.  Financing and funding: This involves the sources of funding and financing available for academic spin-offs. It includes topics such as venture capital, angel investing, and crowdfunding.  Legal and regulatory issues: This involves the legal and regulatory frameworks that impact academic spin-offs. It includes topics such as corporate governance, securities regulations, and tax laws.  Overall, the field of academic spin-offs is interdisciplinary, encompassing business, technology, law, and policy. It is an important area of research and practice, as it provides a pathway for bringing new technologies and innovations to market, creating jobs, and driving economic growth.

data.name: Actin
data.description: Actin is a globular protein that is a major constituent of the cellular cytoskeleton. Actin can exist in monomeric form as G-actin (globular actin) or can form filaments (F-actin, filamentous actin) and mediates multiple cellular functions, including cell migration, contractility and cytokinesis.

data.name: Light-sheet Microscopy
data.description: Light-sheet microscopy uses a thin plane of light to illuminate a sample orthogonally to the detection objective such that the axial resolution of the microscope is determined wholly or partly by the thickness of the light sheet. It allows fast volumetric imaging with reduced sample irradiation compared to conventional light microscopy methods.

data.name: Soil Physics
data.description: Study of soil physical properties and processes

data.name: Apicobasal Polarity
data.description: Apicobasal polarity is a type of cell polarity specific to epithelial cells, referring to a specialised apical membrane facing the outside of the body or lumen of internal cavities, and a specialised basolateral membrane localised at the opposite side, away from the lumen. The two domains are often physically separated by adherens junctions complexes.

data.name: RNA transport
data.description: RNA transport is the process by which ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules are actively transported from one location within the cell to another. Examples include the export of RNAs from the nucleus to the cytoplasm through the nuclear pores, and the microtubule-assisted movement of specific RNAs along nerve fibres (axons).

data.name: DNA probes
data.description: DNA probes are stretches of single-stranded DNA used to detect the presence of complementary nucleic acid sequences (target sequences) by hybridization. DNA probes are usually labelled, for example with radioisotopes, epitopes, biotin or fluorophores to enable their detection.

data.name: Borders and Migration
data.description: Borders and migration in criminology refers to the study of crime, criminal behavior, and related issues in the context of borders, immigration, and the movement of people across national boundaries. It examines the social, economic, and legal factors that influence migration patterns, as well as the criminal activities and challenges that arise in the process. Here are five synonyms for borders and migration:

data.name: Spintronics
data.description: Spintronics is the use of a fundamental property of particles known as spin for information processing. In many ways, spintronics is analogous to electronics, which instead uses the electrical charge on an electron. Carrying information in both the charge and spin of an electron potentially offers devices with a greater diversity of functionality.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Nuclear Astrophysics
data.description: Nuclear astrophysics aims to understand the origin of the chemical elements and the energy generation in stars.It is an interdisciplinary branch of physics involving stellar modeling, measurement and theoretical estimation of nuclear reaction rates, physical cosmology and cosmochemistry, gamma ray, optical and X-ray astronomy.

data.name: Pollen Tube
data.description: The pollen tube is a growth from a pollen grain down into the flower style which allows two sperm cells to pass, one to the ovum within the ovule, and the other to the central cell of the ovule. This process is called double fertilization

data.name: Dental Anthropology
data.description: Dental Anthropology provides a view into biological, ecological and cultural aspects like individuality, human behavior, living conditions, and environments by analysing teeth and denture. Teeth are used to separate fossil hominids, demonstrate trends in hominid dentition, reflect individual and group patterns of demography, biological relationships in the context of affinity and kinship, aspects of diet and cultural adaptation, and supply information on dental health, art, cult, and custom in fossil and archeological series.

data.name: Arenaviruses
data.description: Arenaviruses are infectious agents that infect rodents and sometimes humans. This virus family is divided into Old and New World viruses, and includes lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus, Lassa virus and Junin virus.

data.name: Cognitive Ageing
data.description: Cognitive ageing is the decline in cognitive processing that occurs as people get older. Age-related impairments in reasoning, memory and processing speed can arise during adulthood and progress into the elder years.

data.name: Polar Geography
data.description: The polar regions, also called the frigid zones or polar zones, of Earth are Earth's polar ice caps, the regions of the planet that surround its geographical poles (the North and South Poles), lying within the polar circles. These high latitudes are dominated by floating sea ice covering much of the Arctic Ocean in the north, and by the Antarctic ice sheet on the continent of Antarctica and the Southern Ocean in the south.

data.name: War Crime
data.description: War crimes focus on the study of criminal acts committed during armed conflicts or war. War crimes are defined as serious violations of international humanitarian law, including the Geneva Conventions and other international treaties. These crimes occur during both international and non-international armed conflicts and involve acts such as deliberate targeting of civilians, torture, sexual violence, unlawful killings, forced displacement, and the destruction of civilian infrastructure.

synonyms: Violations of the laws of war

data.name: Recombinant Protein Therapy
data.description: A recombinant protein therapy is produced through recombinant DNA technology, which involves inserting the DNA encoding the protein into bacterial or mammalian cells, expressing the protein in these cells and then purifying it from them. Many biologics, such as monoclonal antibodies, are recombinant protein therapies.

data.name: Hebrew
data.description: Hebrew is a Semitic language and belongs to the Canaanite subgroup within the Afro-Asiatic language family. It is primarily spoken in Israel and is the official language of the country. Hebrew has a rich history and is considered one of the world's oldest continuously spoken languages.

data.name: Structural Geology
data.description: Structural geology is the study of the deformation of the surface and subsurface of the Earth and other planetary bodies. This deformation reflects past changes in local and regional stress and strain, and can be used to reconstruct past crustal movements and dynamics.

data.name: Peptide Nucleic Acid Oligo
data.description: Peptide nucleic acids are synthetic polymers that mimic the structure of DNA or RNA. PNAs are used in various molecular biology techniques involving specific recognition of a complementary DNA or RNA strand and have been investigated as the basis for diagnostics and antisense therapies.

data.name: Household Finance
data.description: The household finance industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the financial behavior of households, including their borrowing, saving, investment, and insurance decisions. The research in this field is concerned with understanding the factors that influence households' financial decisions and the consequences of those decisions for their financial well-being. This includes examining the impact of financial literacy and education, income and wealth, demographic factors, and social and cultural factors on household financial behavior. The household finance industry is interdisciplinary, drawing on insights from economics, psychology, sociology, and other fields to better understand the complex financial decisions made by households.

data.name: Materials Mechanics
data.description: Materials Mechanics, also known as Mechanics of Materials or Solid Mechanics, is a branch of engineering and applied mechanics that deals with the behavior of solid materials under various loading and deformation conditions. It focuses on understanding how materials respond to external forces and stresses, as well as how they deform, bend, and break.

data.name: Histology
data.description: Histology is the branch of biology that focuses on the microscopic structure of tissues and cells. It involves the study of the organization, composition, and function of biological tissues, which are groups of cells that work together to perform specific functions in organisms. Histology employs various techniques, including tissue fixation, embedding, sectioning, and staining, to prepare samples for examination under a microscope. This field is essential for understanding the normal structure and function of tissues, as well as the pathological changes that occur in diseases. Histology is widely used in medical research, diagnostics, and education, providing critical insights into cellular processes, tissue development, and the effects of diseases on tissue architecture.

data.name: Applied Ecology
data.description: Applied ecology is a sub-field within ecology that considers the application of the science of ecology to real-world questions. It is also described as a scientific field that focuses on the application of concepts, theories, models, or methods of fundamental ecology to environmental problems.

data.name: Fruiting
data.description: Fruiting is a developmental process that starts after fertilization, and modifies flower organs, mostly the ovary and surrounding tissues, to create a new slowly maturing structure called a fruit. It is generally energy-rich and will help disperse and protect the embryo-containing seed, and nourish it during germination.

data.name: Cell Therapy
data.description: A cell therapy is a medicinal product containing cells, and is typically injected into a patient. Examples include bone marrow transplants (also known as haematopoietic stem cell transplantation) and mesenchymal stem cell therapies.

data.name: Hepatitis C Virus
data.description: Hepatitis C virus is an infectious agent that causes hepatitis C, a type of liver inflammation in humans. This virus species leads to chronic infection and severe complications such as liver cirrhosis or cancer more often than some of the other hepatitis viruses.

data.name: Central Nervous System
