data.description: The central nervous system is the part of the nervous system that consists of the brain, spinal cord and cranial nerves

data.name: Technoscience
data.description: In common usage, technoscience refers to the entire long-standing global human activity of technology combined with the relatively recent scientific method that occurred primarily in Europe during the 17th and 18th centuries. Technoscience is the study of how humans interact with technology using the scientific method.

data.name: Urban Geography
data.description: incl. megacities, cities, towns

data.name: Fantasy Fiction
data.description: Fantasy is a genre of speculative fiction involving magical elements, typically set in a fictional universe and sometimes inspired by mythology and folklore.

data.name: Dark Energy and Dark Matter
data.description: The dark energy is an unknown form of energy which is hypothesized to permeate all of space, tending to accelerate the expansion of the universe. Two proposed forms for dark energy are the cosmological constant, representing a constant energy density filling space homogeneously, and scalar fields such as quintessence or moduli, dynamic quantities whose energy density can vary in time and space.Dark matter is a hypothetical form of matter that is thought to account for approximately 85% of the matter in the universe, and about a quarter of its total energy density. The majority of dark matter is thought to be non-baryonic in nature, possibly being composed of some as-yet undiscovered subatomic particles.

data.name: Magnetic Materials
data.description: Magnetic materials are materials studied and used mainly for their magnetic properties. The magnetic response of a materials is largely determined by the magnetic dipole moment associated with the intrinsic angular momentum, or spin, of its electrons. A material’s response to an applied magnetic field can be characterized as diamagnetic, paramagnetic, ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic.

subjects.term: Solids. Solid state chemistry (Inorganic and organic)
Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Laser Material Processing
data.description: Laser material processing uses high-intensity light beams in material fabrication. This can include cutting, engraving, drilling or welding metals. It can also include cleaning materials with lasers. Health and safety issues associated with using these techniques are an important consideration.

data.name: Antibody Generation
data.description: Antibody generation is the production of antibodies from cells or animals in sufficient quantity to be used as an experimental or therapeutic reagent. Polyclonal antibody mixtures are generated by injecting an animal with an agent that elicits an immune response, and monoclonal antibodies are generated from immortal immune cell lines.

data.name: Secretion
data.description: Secretion involves the release of proteins and other macromolecules by a cell. In eukaryotic cells, proteins synthesised at the ER are transported to the Golgi, where they are packaged into vesicles, transported to the plasma membrane and released via exocytosis. Bacterial secretion systems are essential for infection of host cells.

data.name: Interference and Diffraction
data.description: Interference refers to the phenomenon where two waves of the same kind overlap to produce a resultant wave of greater, lower, or the same amplitude. Diffraction is defined as the bending of a wave around the corners of an obstacle or aperture.

data.name: Nuclear Envelope
data.description: The nuclear envelope is a structure that surrounds and defines the nucleus and separates it from the cytoplasm. It is comprised of inner and outer membranes separated by the perinuclear space, and contains specialized nuclear pore structures that permit communication and transport between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

data.name: Terrorism
data.description: Terrorism refers to the use of violence, intimidation, or the threat of violence to create fear and panic in a population, typically for political, religious, or ideological purposes. It is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon with diverse motivations, methods, and actors involved.

data.name: Probation
data.description: Probation focuses on the study and practice of community-based correctional strategies aimed at rehabilitating and supervising individuals who have been convicted of crimes but have been given a suspended sentence or released on probation instead of serving time in prison. Probation involves monitoring and supporting offenders in the community, helping them reintegrate into society, and reducing the likelihood of reoffending.

data.name: Epithelial-mesenchymal Transition
data.description: The epithelial–mesenchymal transition is the process by which polarised epithelial cells that are connected via adhesion lose their characteristics and acquire migratory and invasive properties characteristic of a mesenchymal cell. This occurs during developmental processes such as neural tube formation, and when metastasis is initiated in cancer.

data.name: Violence and Crime
data.description: It examines the various forms of violence, including interpersonal violence, domestic violence, sexual violence, homicide, and collective violence such as riots or terrorism, and it encompasses a wide range of criminal acts, from property offenses like theft and burglary to offenses against persons like assault, robbery, and murder. Researchers in this area investigate the individual, social, and environmental factors that contribute to the occurrence of violent and criminal behaviors, and analyze the impact of violence and crime on victims, offenders, communities, and society as a whole.

data.name: Skin Models
data.description: Skin models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of human skin physiology, function or disease. They include in vitro methods, ex vivo skin cultures and animal models, especially mice and fish.

data.name: Diagnostic Devices
data.description: Diagnostic devices are devices used to identify the nature or cause of a certain phenomenon, usually related to a medical condition. Examples of diagnostic devices are magnetic resonance imaging apparatuses, temperature sensors or pacemakers.

data.name: Change Blindness
data.description: Change blindness is a perceptual phenomenon that refers to the failure to notice significant changes in a visual scene, even when those changes are quite obvious. It occurs when a person is unable to detect changes in an object or scene that would typically be easily noticeable. Change blindness highlights the limitations of our visual perception and our tendency to miss changes in our environment.

data.name: Gender and Sexuality
data.description: Gender and sexuality are two distinct but interconnected concepts that play significant roles in shaping individual identities, social structures, and cultural norms. Gender refers to the social, cultural, and behavioral characteristics, roles, expectations, and identities that a given society associates with individuals based on their perceived sex.  Sexuality refers to an individual's sexual orientation, attractions, and experiences. It encompasses who a person is emotionally, romantically, and sexually attracted to.

data.name: Exocytosis
data.description: Exocytosis is the process by which cytoplasmic secretory vesicles fuse with the cellular membrane, releasing contents to the extracellular space.

data.name: Chemistry Policy
data.description: "Chemistry policy" refers to the set of guidelines, regulations, and decisions made by governments, organizations, and international bodies to address various aspects of chemistry's impact on society, the environment, and human health. These policies aim to ensure the safe and responsible use of chemicals, promote scientific research and innovation, and mitigate potential risks associated with chemical substances.

data.name: Polarization
data.description: Polarization (also polarisation) is a property of transverse waves which specifies the geometrical orientation of the oscillations. In a transverse wave, the direction of the oscillation is perpendicular to the direction of motion of the wave.

data.name: High-Field Lasers
data.description: High-field lasers are lasers that can create intense electric fields. The high fields are often achieved by concentrating the optical energy into a very short temporal pulse. This has led to the development of terawatt and petawatt lasers, which are important probes of matter under extreme conditions.

data.name: Pathology
data.description: Pathology is the precise study of the causes and consequences of a disease. The two major components of pathology are anatomical studies of structure and function at levels ranging from the whole organism to the subcellular level, and laboratory techniques and procedures to analyse bodily fluids.

data.name: Pollution Remediation
data.description: Pollution remediation is the removal of pollutants, including chemical substances and/or energy, that are judged to be having a negative impact on the environment. Frequent targets of remediation include: soils, sediments and watercourses.

data.name: Optical Sensor
data.description: Optical sensors are a broad class of device for detecting light intensity. This can be just a simple component for notifying when ambient light levels rise above or fall below a prescribed level, or a highly sensitive device for detecting single photons. Most optical sensors produce an electrical output.

data.name: Hardware and Infrastructure
data.description: Hardware comprises the physical parts of a computer that can be touched, and infrastructure comprises the physical hardware used to connect computers to other computers and users.

data.name: Behavioral Medicine
data.description: Behavioral Medicine is a multidisciplinary field that combines principles and knowledge from psychology, medicine, and behavioral sciences to understand the complex relationship between behavior and health. It focuses on the application of behavioral and psychological principles to prevent and treat illness, promote health, and enhance well-being. Behavioral Medicine recognizes that human behavior plays a crucial role in the development, maintenance, and treatment of various physical and mental health conditions. It integrates psychological interventions, behavior change strategies, and lifestyle modifications with medical treatments to optimize health outcomes and improve quality of life.

subjects.term: Medicine and disease in relation to psychology

data.name: Business Process Management
data.description: Business Process Management (BPM) is a discipline within the field of management and information technology that focuses on designing, modeling, executing, monitoring, and optimizing business processes. BPM seeks to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of business operations by aligning them with the strategic goals of an organization. Major topics within BPM include: Process modeling: This involves documenting and representing business processes using diagrams and other visual aids. Process modeling helps stakeholders to understand the flow of activities, inputs, and outputs in a process, and to identify potential bottlenecks and inefficiencies. Process automation: This involves using technology to automate routine or repetitive tasks within a process. Process automation can help to reduce errors, improve consistency, and free up human resources to focus on more complex or strategic activities. Process optimization: This involves identifying areas for improvement within a process and implementing changes to streamline and improve its performance. Process optimization can help to reduce costs, increase customer satisfaction, and improve overall business performance. Process monitoring: This involves tracking the performance of a process over time, using metrics and other indicators to identify trends and areas for improvement. Process monitoring can help to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and other issues that may be affecting the performance of a process. Process governance: This involves establishing policies, procedures, and guidelines for the management of business processes within an organization. Process governance helps to ensure that processes are consistent, compliant, and aligned with the strategic goals of the organization. Process innovation: This involves exploring new and innovative ways to design, execute, and manage business processes. Process innovation can help to drive business growth, create competitive advantage, and improve overall organizational performance.

data.name: Neuronal Cell Fate and Cell Lineage
data.description: A cell’s lineage describes the developmental history of a cell from its birth until its final division and differentiation into a particular cell type, which is known as its cell fate. Cell fate is determined by the actions of numerous cell intrinsic and extrinsic factors.

data.name: Goethe
data.description: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749-1832) was a German writer, poet, playwright, and philosopher. He is considered one of the most prominent figures in German literature and a key representative of the Weimar Classicism movement. Goethe's works span various genres, including poetry, drama, fiction, and non-fiction, and his contributions have had a lasting impact on literature and cultural discourse.

synonyms: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's literary works

data.name: Supramolecular Polymers
data.description: Supramolecular polymers are polymers in which the monomers are linked through non-covalent interactions such as coordination bonds, pi-pi interactions or hydrogen bonds.

data.name: Maternal and Child Health
data.description: Maternal and child health (MCH) care is the health service provided to mothers (women in their child bearing age) and children. The targets for MCH are all women in their reproductive age groups, i.e., 15 - 49 years of age, children, school age population and adolescents.

data.name: Energy Management
data.description: Energy management covers studies on planning and operation of energy production and energy consumption units. This includes resource conservation, and cost savings, while the users have permanent access to the energy they need.

data.name: French
data.description: French is a Romance language and is one of the major languages of the world. It is primarily spoken in France, but it is also an official language in many countries and regions, including Canada (particularly in Quebec), Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Monaco, and several nations in Africa and the Caribbean. Standard French, also known as Metropolitan French, is based on the dialect of the Île-de-France region, which includes Paris

data.name: Corpus Linguistics
data.description: Corpus linguistics is the study of language as a language is expressed in its text corpus (plural corpora), its body of "real world" text. Corpus linguistics proposes that reliable language analysis is more feasible with corpora collected in the field in its natural context ("realia"), and with minimal experimental interference.

data.name: Dosage compensation
data.description: Dosage compensation is a process that balances expression of sex-linked and autosomal genes in the heterogametic sex. For example, one X chromosome in XX female mammals is randomly inactivated in every cell, and gene transcription levels from the X chromosome of XO or XY male Drosophila is elevated to approximately equal the output of two sex chromosomes in XX females.

data.name: Pharynx
data.description: The pharynx, composed of the nasopharynx, oropharynx and hypopharynx, is part of the digestive and respiratory systems. It conducts food to the oesophagus, as well as air to the larynx and lungs. The pharynx is located in the throat, posterior to the nasal cavity, oral cavity and larynx.

data.name: Helium Droplets
data.description: Helium droplets are large helium clusters that are capable of picking up individual atoms and molecules and act as nano-reactors for the synthesis of unique nanoparticles.

data.name: Alternative Splicing
data.description: Alternative splicing is a process that enables a messenger RNA (mRNA) to direct synthesis of different protein variants (isoforms) that may have different cellular functions or properties. It occurs by rearranging the pattern of intron and exon elements that are joined by splicing to alter the mRNA coding sequence.

data.name: Neuronal Differentiation
data.description: Neuronal differentiation refers to the process by which undifferentiated or immature precursor cells, known as neuroblasts or neural stem cells, develop into mature and specialized neurons. This process involves a series of cellular and molecular events that lead to the acquisition of neuronal characteristics and functions.

data.name: Reaction Kinetics
data.description: Reaction kinetics describes rate dynamics in chemical and biological systems. It allows for the experimental determination of reaction rates, from which rate constants may be estimated, in order to better understand biological systems modelled by reaction–diffusion processes.

data.name: Victorian Literature
data.description: Literary works written during the reign of Queen Victoria, from 1837 to 1901. Poets and novelists during the Victorian era began to reflect on realities such as factory work, the plight of the lower class, and the treatment of women and children.

data.name: Paediatric Research
data.description: Research that is directly related to diseases, disorders, and other conditions in children, including pediatric pharmacology.

data.name: Outdoor Education
data.description: Outdoor Education is an experiential learning approach that uses outdoor and natural settings to facilitate personal and social development, environmental awareness, and the acquisition of technical and practical skills. This field explores the theory, methods, and evaluation of outdoor education programs, as well as their role in fostering holistic and lifelong learning.

data.name: Dental Ethics
data.description: A system of principles governing dental practice; a moral obligation to render the best possible quality of dental service to the patient and to maintain an honest relationship with other members of the profession and society at large.

data.name: Community Well-Being
data.description: Community wellbeing is the combination of social, economic, environmental, cultural, and political conditions identified by individuals and their communities as essential for them to flourish and fulfill their potential.”

data.name: Hydrogen Bonding
data.description: Hydrogen bonding is a type of intermolecular bonding that occurs when a hydrogen atom is attracted to an electronegative atom, such as oxygen, nitrogen, or fluorine, in a neighboring molecule. It is a relatively strong and important interaction in chemistry, influencing the properties and behavior of many compounds and systems.

data.name: Innovation and Medicine
data.description: Innovation and Medicine is a field of study that examines the processes, practices, and implications of medical innovations, exploring the social, ethical, and technological aspects of medical advancements and their impact on healthcare delivery and patient outcomes.

data.name: Ciliogenesis
data.description: Ciliogenesis is the process by which cilia - slender outgrowths on a cell's surface in eukaryotes - form. Motile cilia have a beating motion and serve to move fluids, whereas non-motile, or primary, cilia receive signals from other cells or fluids.

data.name: Microengraving
data.description: Microengraving is a method that uses high-density arrays to probe the secretory behaviour of thousands of individual cells. It employs elastomeric nanolitre wells to trap single living cells and their secreted molecules, followed by serial probing of the molecules with labelled antibodies that are imaged for detection.

data.name: General Relativity
data.description: General relativity describes gravitation in a geometrical framework generalizing special relativity and classical mechanics. This term includes theoretical studies of gravity, experimental studies of gravitational waves and observational studies of gravitational lensing, as well as tests of general relativity and laboratory experiments.

data.name: Natural Remedies
data.description: Substances/Remedies of claimed medical value derived directly from plants or other natural sources.

data.name: Statistical Mechanics
data.description: A mathematical framework that applies probability theory and statistics to large assemblies of microscopic entities in order to derive macroscopic properties (temperature, pressure, entropy, magnetization) from microscopic laws of motion.

data.name: Sexual Medicine
data.description: The branch of medicine concerning the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disorders of sexual function

data.name: Neuro-vascular Interaction
data.description: Neuro–vascular interactions are the interactions between blood vessels in the brain and their adjacent neurons, and are regulated by complex interactions between endothelial cells, pericytes, fibroblasts, neurons and glia. They regulate blood flow and provide vital support for brain development and neuronal function. Defective neuro–vascular function is associated with a variety of neurological disorders.

data.name: Material Culture
data.description: Material culture refers to the physical objects and artifacts that are created, used, and valued by a particular society or group of people. These objects are tangible and can include a wide range of items, such as tools, clothing, buildings, art, religious symbols, technology, household items, and more. Material culture is an essential aspect of anthropology and archaeology as it provides valuable insights into the beliefs, values, social structures, and everyday life of past and present societies.

data.name: Vacuole
data.description: A vacuole is a membrane-bound organelle found in plant and fungal cells. Vacuoles have a variety of cellular functions, including storage, sequestration and structural support. Vacuoles also have important roles in autophagy and degradation of cellular contents.

data.name: Cardiovascular Physiology
data.description: Cardiovascular biology is the study of the mechanisms of cardiovascular physiology and pathophysiology.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Life Sciences / Anatomy & Physiology (see also Life Sciences / Human Anatomy & Physiology)

data.name: Structural Anthropology
data.description: Structural Anthropology is a branch of anthropology that analyzes human culture and society in terms of underlying structures, such as myths, kinship systems, and rituals. It seeks to identify universal patterns and principles that govern human behavior and cultural expression, drawing on structuralist theory and methodology.

data.name: Ecotoxicology
data.description: Ecotoxicology is an interdisciplinary field that draws from knowledge and techniques in the fields of ecology and toxicology to study the effects of toxic chemical or biological agents on biological organisms at the population, community or ecosystem level.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Chemistry / Environmental (see also Environmental Science)

data.name: Fungal Genes
data.description: A fungal gene is a functional hereditary unit of fungi, a DNA sequence corresponding to protein-coding sequence or functional RNA.

data.name: Nuclear Waste
data.description: Radioactive waste is a type of hazardous waste that contains radioactive material. Radioactive waste is a result of many activities, including nuclear medicine, nuclear research, nuclear power generation, nuclear decommissioning, rare-earth mining, and nuclear weapons reprocessing.

data.name: Chemistry Publishing
data.description: Chemistry publishing and communication is the creation and dissemination of information that covers the discipline of chemistry. This topic covers, for example, editorial and publication processes (such as peer review), discussion of how information should be presented, methods of sharing data and the evolution of publishing as a business.

data.name: X-ray Crystallography
data.description: X-ray crystallography is a technique that uses X-ray diffraction patterns to determine high-resolution, three-dimensional structures of molecules such as proteins, small organic molecules, and materials. The substance of interest must be in crystalline form, which typically requires testing various crystallization conditions.

data.name: Amoeboid Migration
data.description: Amoeboid migration is a mode of rapid motility that is driven by actin-rich pseudopods, hydrostatically-generated blebs and a highly-contractile uropod, and is characterized by weak or absent adhesion to the substratum and little or no extracellular matrix proteolysis. The Dictyostelium amoeba, and lymphocytes, leukocytes, dendritic and cancer cells exhibit amoeboid motility.

data.name: Head and Neck Surgery
data.description: Otorhinolaryngology (/oʊtoʊˌraɪnoʊˌlærɪnˈɡɒlədʒi/ oh-toh-RY-noh-LARR-in-GOL-ə-jee, abbreviated ORL and also known as otolaryngology, otolaryngology – head and neck surgery (ORL–H&N or OHNS), or ear, nose, and throat (ENT) is a surgical subspeciality within medicine that deals with the surgical and medical management of conditions of the head and neck.

data.name: Computational Astrophysics
data.description: Computational astrophysics refers to the methods and computing tools developed and used in astrophysics research. Well-established areas of astrophysics employing computational methods include magnetohydrodynamics, astrophysical radiative transfer, stellar and galactic dynamics, and astrophysical fluid dynamics. A recently developed field is numerical relativity.

data.name: Russian and Post-Soviet Politics
data.description: Russian and Post-Soviet Politics is were political organizations and governmental bodies of the former Russian Empire, primarily associated with the Russian Revolution, which gave the name to the latter state of the Soviet Union.

data.name: Bodies and Technology
data.description: Bodies and Technology examines the interactions between human bodies and technological advancements, exploring how technology influences physical capabilities, identity, and societal norms.

data.name: Sports Biomechanics
data.description: Sports Biomachanics refers to the description, detailed analysis and assessment of human movement during sport activities. Sport Biomachanics applies the laws of machanics to sport movements in order to explain how and why the human body moves in the way that it does and how the athletes body interacts with sports equipment and the environment during movement. Sport Biomachanics helps to gain unterstanding of athlete performance, as well as to minimise risk of injury, and increase performance. It usually includes detailed quantitative analysis of athletes movements by means of measurement, mathematical modelunf or computer simulation.

data.name: Polymerization
data.description: A polymerization mechanism is the sequence of elementary chemical reactions by which polymerization – the process of converting monomer molecules into a polymer – proceeds.

data.name: Scanning Probe Microscopy
data.description: Scanning probe microscopy images a sample by scanning a physical probe just above the surface. A variety of different probes and detection modalities can be used to generate either a topological map of the surface or to detect and image some other electromagnetic, physical or molecular characteristic.

data.name: Quantum Optomechanics
data.description: Quantum optomechanics relates to the enhancement of radiation pressure interaction between light (photons) and matter using optical resonators (cavities). Cavity optomechanics are based on well established concepts and technology like quantum information, Bell inequalities and laser.

data.name: Transdifferentiation
data.description: Transdifferentiation is the conversion of a cell type present in one tissue or organ into a cell type from another tissue or organ without going through a pluripotent cell state. Transdifferentiation between some cell types can occur naturally in response to injury and can be induced experimentally.

data.name: DNA adducts
data.description: DNA adducts are a form of DNA damage caused by covalent attachment of a chemical moiety to DNA. Adducts that are not removed by the cell can cause mutations that may give rise to cancer. They are frequently used as biomarkers for chemical hazard exposure or cancer therapy efficacy.

data.name: Protein Trafficking in Plants
data.description: Protein trafficking in plants involves moving plant proteins from one cellular compartment to another. This involves various sorting and transport mechanisms such as gated transport, protein translocation, and vesicular transport.

data.name: Surface Spectroscopy
data.description: Surface spectroscopy involves the use of surface-sensitive spectroscopic techniques to analyse samples. These techniques include X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, Auger electron spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy and sum frequency generation spectroscopy.

data.name: Terrestrial Pollution
data.description: Soil contamination, soil pollution, or land pollution as a part of land degradation is caused by the presence of xenobiotic chemicals or other alteration in the natural soil environment. It is typically caused by industrial activity, agricultural chemicals or improper disposal of waste.

data.name: Laser Cooling
data.description: Laser cooling refers to a number of techniques in which atomic and molecular samples are cooled down to near absolute zero. The most common method is Doppler cooling but also sisyphus cooling, resolved sideband cooling, Raman sideband cooling, cavity mediated cooling, electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) cooling, belong to these techniques.

subjects.term: Quantum physics (quantum mechanics & quantum field theory)
Radiation and absorption. Laws of cooling
Quantum physics (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory)

data.name: Total Internal Reflection Microscopy
data.description: Total internal reflection microscopy is a light microscopy technique that relies on total internal reflection of illumination light to generate an evanescent wave that extends less than 200 nm from the microscope coverslip. This allows selective excitation of fluorophores immediately adjacent to the coverslip or monitoring of the distance between the coverslip and a microscopic sphere.

data.name: Atom Optics
data.description: Atom optics is the study of the wave-like properties of beams of atoms. Wave–particle duality — a central principle of quantum mechanics — implies that effects traditionally associated with waves, such as interference and diffraction, can also be observed with an individual particle.

data.name: Administrative Justice
data.description: Administrative justice is the branch of law that requires public institutions and officials (as well as private institutions performing public functions) to adhere to due process principles when making administrative decisions, or taking administrative actions.

subjects.term: Administration of justice. Organization of the judiciary

data.name: Photobiology
data.description: Photobiology is the study of the effects of ultraviolet, visible and infrared radiation on living organisms. It includes topics such as photosynthesis, vision, bioluminescence, circadian rhythms and photodynamic therapy. [the study of the effects of light on living organisms.]

data.name: Physical Examination
data.description: A physical examination is the systematic inspection of the body of a patient for signs and symptoms of disease or abnormality. A physical examination can be performed as part of a general medical examination, or prompted by a medical event.

data.name: Powertrain
data.description: Comprises the main components that generate power and deliver that power to the road surface, water, or air to propel a vehicle.

data.name: Integrated Optics
data.description: Integrated optics is a system of light-controlling components combined into a single device. The ultimate aim is to create miniature optical circuits similar to the silicon chips that have revolutionized the electronics industry. The advantage of the optical approach however is that data can be processed at much higher speeds.

data.name: Chromosome Segregation
data.description: Chromosome segregation occurs in mitosis and is the process by which the mitotic spindle separates the duplicated chromosomes into daughter cells.

data.name: Optical Frequency Combs
data.description: Optical frequency combs are specialized lasers that act like a ruler for light. They measure exact frequencies of light — from the invisible infrared and ultraviolet to visible red, yellow, green and blue light — quickly and accurately. These Nobel Prize-winning devices fill an important technological gap.

data.name: Communication and Replication
data.description: Communication is the transfer of data between data sources and data sinks, and replication is the copying of data from one server to another. Communication and replication are important in database maintenance and preservation of data.

data.name: Information Processing
data.description: Information processing in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive processes involved in receiving, encoding, storing, retrieving, and using information. It involves the way our mind perceives, organizes, and makes sense of incoming information from the environment.

data.name: Environmental Geography
data.description: Environmental geography is the branch of geography that describes the spatial aspects of interactions between humans and the natural world.

data.name: Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence
data.description: The philosophy of artificial intelligence is a branch of the philosophy of technology that explores artificial intelligence and its implications for knowledge and understanding of intelligence, ethics, consciousness, epistemology, and free will.

subjects.term: Digital and information technologies: social and ethical aspects

data.name: Happiness Economics
data.description: Happiness economics is the formal academic study of the relationship between individual satisfaction and economic issues such as employment and wealth.

data.name: Excitability
data.description: Excitability is a property of a cell, allowing it to respond to stimulation by rapid changes in membrane potential produced by ion fluxes across the plasma membrane. This is most commonly associated with neurons, but more recently astrocytes have also been shown to exhibit ‘cellular excitability’, resulting from changes in calcium ion concentration in the cytosol.

data.name: Clinical Epigenetics
data.description: Clinical epigenetics is the application of molecular biology techniques detecting alterations in DNA methylation or histone modification to diagnose or study disorders characterized by heritable defects in the expression of a gene or genome. Applications include Rett syndrome, disorders of imprinting, uniparental inheritance of chromosomes and chromosome segments, and somatic epigenetic anomalies in cancers.

data.name: Body-Technology Studies
data.description: Body-Technology Studies is an interdisciplinary area of research that investigates the complex interrelationship between human societies, cultures, and technological advancements. This field explores the social, ethical, and philosophical implications of technologies, including the impact on human values, well-being, and the future of humanity.

data.name: Discourse Analysis
data.description: Discourse analysis is the research approach within the field of linguistics that focuses on the study of language in use, particularly how language is used to construct meaning, represent social interactions, and shape social reality. It involves the systematic analysis of spoken or written language data to uncover underlying linguistic patterns, textual structures, textual organization, pragmatic features and functions of discourse.

data.name: Neuronal Migration
data.description: Neuronal migration refers to the process by which newly formed neurons move from their site of origin to their final destination in the developing nervous system. It is a critical process during brain development that establishes the proper positioning and layering of neurons, forming the intricate neural circuits and structures.

data.name: Foundation Engineering
data.description: Application of soil mechanics and rock mechanics  in the design of foundation elements of structures.

data.name: Epigenetic Memory
data.description: The epigenetic memory of a cell defines the set of modifications to the cell's deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) that do not alter the DNA sequence, and have been inherited from the cell from which it descends. Such modifications can alter gene expression and therefore the properties and behaviour of the cell.

data.name: Genetic Circuit Engineering
data.description: Genetic circuit engineering is the synthesis of unnatural DNA segments encoding protein or RNA molecules that control each other's levels. Genetic circuit engineering is the bottom-up, local approach to synthetic biology; to be distinguished from top-down, global genomic engineering.

data.name: Anthropology of Work
data.description: The study of human work and labor practices within societies. It examines the cultural, social, economic, and historical aspects of work, including the organization of labor, division of tasks, and the meaning and significance of work in different cultural contexts.

data.name: Ligaments
data.description: Ligaments are tough, somewhat flexible bands of avascular connective tissue, usually white, composed of fibroblasts within an extracellular matrix of parallel collagen fibres and elastin fibres. Ligaments serve to connect bones to other bones at the articular extremities, whereby they stabilize joints and enable or restrict movement.

data.name: Mullerian mimicry
data.description: Mullerian mimicry is a phenomenon in which two or more harmful species have evolved to become phenotypically similar. This increases their protection from potential predators whose learned avoidance behaviour will be more strongly reinforced.

data.name: Enamel
data.description: Tooth enamel is one of the four major tissues that make up the tooth in humans and many other animals. Enamel is the hardest substance in the human body and contains the highest percentage of minerals (at 96%) with water and organic material composing the rest.

data.name: Mens' Studies
data.description: Men's studies is an academic field devoted to topics concerning men, masculinity, gender, culture, politics and sexuality.

data.name: Cardiovascular Models
data.description: Cardiovascular models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of human cardiovascular development, function or disease. They can include experimental, genetic or transgenic systems in animals such as the rat, mouse, pig, rabbit and zebrafish.

data.name: Marxist Anthropology
data.description: Also known as Anthropology of Marxism or Marxist-oriented Anthropology, is a theoretical approach within the field of anthropology that applies Marxist principles and perspectives to the study of societies and cultures. It draws on the ideas and critiques of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, focusing on social class, political economy, and historical materialism to understand human societies and cultural practices.

data.name: Palaeoceanography
data.description: Palaeoceanography is the study of past changes in ocean conditions including temperature, salinity, redox state, productivity, circulation, and ecology. These variables are typically reconstructed through analyses of the geochemistry, microfossil composition, and organic contents of ancient marine sediments that have either been exposed on land or collected through seafloor drilling.

data.name: Reactivity of Clusters
data.description: In the context of chemistry and materials science, the reactivity of clusters refers to how these small groups of atoms or molecules interact with other substances or their environment. Clusters typically consist of a few to several hundred atoms, and their properties can differ significantly from those of individual atoms or bulk materials. Understanding the reactivity of clusters is crucial for exploring their potential applications in catalysis, nanotechnology, and other fields.

data.name: Early Solar System
data.description: The formation of the Solar System began about 4.6 billion years ago with the gravitational collapse of a small part of a giant molecular cloud. Most of the collapsing mass collected in the center, forming the Sun, while the rest flattened into a protoplanetary disk out of which the planets, moons, asteroids, and other small Solar System bodies formed.

data.name: Nervous Motor System
data.description: The nervous motor system, also known as the motor nervous system, is a component of the peripheral nervous system (PNS) that controls voluntary and involuntary movements of the body. It is responsible for transmitting signals from the central nervous system (CNS) to the muscles, enabling them to contract and generate movement.

data.name: Cardiac Surgery
data.description: Cardiac surgery is surgery on the heart and the large blood vessels in the chest performed by cardiac surgeons and the perioperative management of these patients

data.name: Probabilistic Data Networks
data.description: Probabilistic data networks represent sets of uncertain data whose behaviour cannot exactly be predicted. The likeliness of any version of the network being true is associated with a probability.

data.name: Urogenital Models
data.description: Urogenital models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of human urogenital development, function or disease. They include animal models of gonad development and urogenital disease.

data.name: Welfare
data.description: The term welfare refers to a range of government programs that provide financial or other aid to individuals or groups who cannot support themselves. Welfare programs are typically funded by taxpayers and allow people to cope with financial stress during rough periods of their lives.

subjects.term: POLITICAL SCIENCE / Public Policy / Social Services & Welfare

data.name: Virulence
data.description: Virulence refers to the relative ability of a microorganism to cause disease.

data.name: Noise Control
data.description: Noise control studies strategies to reduce noise pollution or to reduce the impact of that noise outdoors and indoors.

data.name: Stress and Resilience
data.description: Stress and resilience refers to the individual's ability to withstand and adapt to ongoing stressors and adverse events.

data.name: Batesian Mimicry
data.description: Batesian mimicry is a phenomenon in which non-harmful species have evolved to mimic the appearance of a species that is harmful to potential predators. The Batesian mimics therefore benefit from the predator's learned avoidance behaviour.

data.name: Phase-contrast Microscopy
data.description: Phase contrast microscopy is a white-light optical microscopy technique that relies on sample-induced phase changes in illumination light to generate images with more information than provided by sample-induced intensity changes. Phase information is mixed with intensity information in conventional phase-contrast microscopy, whereas quantitative phase-contrast microscopy displays only the phase information.

data.name: Medical and Health Technologies
data.description: Health technology is defined as the "application of organized knowledge and skills in the form of devices, medicines, vaccines, procedures, and systems developed to solve a health problem and improve quality of lives". This includes pharmaceuticals, devices, procedures, and organizational systems used in the healthcare industry, as well as any technology, including medical devices, IT systems, algorithms, artificial intelligence (AI), cloud and blockchain, designed to support healthcare organizations.

subjects.term: Auxiliary techniques and procedures; apparatus, equipment, materials

data.name: Development Theory
data.description: Development theory is a collection of theories about how desirable change in society is best achieved. Such theories draw on a variety of social science disciplines and approaches.

data.name: Metagenomics
data.description: Metagenomics is the study of the metagenome, the collective genome of microorganisms from an environmental sample, to provide information on the microbial diversity and ecology of a specific environment. Shotgun metagenomics refers to the approach of shearing DNA extracted from the environmental sample and sequencing the small fragments.

data.name: Herpetology
data.description: Herpetology is the branch of zoology concerned with the study of amphibians (including frogs, toads, salamanders, newts and the gymnophiona) and reptiles (including snakes, lizards, amphisbaenids, turtles, terrapins, tortoises, crocodilians and the tuataras). The discipline can include the biology, ecology, behaviour, taxonomy and husbandry of these organisms.

data.name: Animal Breeding
data.description: Animal breeding is the process of selective mating of animals with desirable genetic traits, to maintain or enhance these traits in future generations. For livestock, this involves estimation of the genetic value of individuals for traits including growth rate and yield of products such as eggs, milk or meat.

data.name: Planetary Surface
data.description: A planetary surface is where the solid or liquid material of certain types of astronomical objects contacts the atmosphere or outer space.

data.name: Halogen Bonding
data.description: Halogen bonding is the attractive, non-covalent interaction that can form between an electrophilic region of a halogen atom in a molecule and a nucleophilic region of a molecule. The bonding can be exploited in areas such as supramolecular chemistry, crystal engineering and the fabrication of liquid crystals.

data.name: Plant Cell Cycle
data.description: Plant Cell Cycle is the complex series of events which take place in plant cells between the end of one cycle of division and the end of the next. The process involves growth of a plant cell and subsequent division into daughter cells.

data.name: Saliva
data.description: Saliva (commonly referred to as spit) is an extracellular fluid produced and secreted by salivary glands in the mouth. In humans, saliva is around 99% water, plus electrolytes, mucus, white blood cells, epithelial cells (from which DNA can be extracted), enzymes (such as lipase and amylase), antimicrobial agents (such as secretory IgA, and lysozymes)

data.name: Nanofabrication and Nanopatterning
data.description: Nanofabrication and nanopatterning are fields of study in which methods are developed to manufacture nanomaterials, or pattern materials on a nanometre scale (i.e., below 100 nm in at least one dimension). Nanolithography is a common method used in nanopatterning.

data.name: Super-Resolution Microscopy
data.description: Super-resolution microscopy includes a variety of microscopy techniques that increase the resolving ability of a light microscope well beyond the classical limits dictated by the diffraction barrier.

data.name: Adverse Effects
data.description: Adverse effects are the unintended outcomes, caused by a medical intervention, that have a negative impact on an individual's health or well-being. Common adverse effects include nausea, headaches, and tiredness. Investigators in clinical trials often distinguish between serious adverse events and those that do not substantially affect the individual's well-being.

data.name: Interlocked Molecules
data.description: Interlocked molecules are molecular architectures formed from two or more components that are linked together mechanically; the entangled components are not connected through covalent bonds but cannot be separated without breaking a covalent bond. Examples of interlocked molecules include catenanes and rotaxanes.

data.name: Social Cognition
data.description: Social cognition, in the field of psychology, refers to the cognitive processes and mental representations that underlie our understanding of social information and guide our social interactions. It involves how individuals perceive, process, interpret, and remember social cues, such as emotions, attitudes, beliefs, intentions, and social norms, to make sense of others' behavior and make informed social judgments.

data.name: Process Chemistry
data.description: Process chemistry involves the development and optimization of production processes for chemical compounds, and the scaling up of laboratory reactions, particularly in the pharmaceutical sector.

data.name: Chemistry Education
data.description: Chemistry education (or chemical education) is the study of teaching and learning chemistry. It is one subset of STEM education or discipline-based education research (DBER).

subjects.term: EDUCATION / Teaching Methods & Materials / Science & Technology

data.name: Immune Cell Isolation
data.description: Immune cell isolation refers to methods that enable the enrichment of immune cell subsets using antibody-mediated recognition of specific cell surface antigens, followed by sorting or separation with techniques such as flow cytometry, density centrifugation or magnetic isolation.

data.name: Global Health
data.description: Global health is the health of the populations in the worldwide context;[1] it has been defined as "the area of study, research, and practice that places a priority on improving health and achieving equity in health for all people worldwide"

data.name: Biological Therapy
data.description: Biological therapy is a type of therapeutic treatment. The agents used for biological therapy are designed to specifically target a biological phenomenon, gene, protein, or group of genes or proteins thought to be involved in the disease.

data.name: Biological Metamorphosis
data.description: Biological metamorphosis is the process of profound physical changes that occur in some non-mammalian animal species during development from immature to adult form. Examples include the metamorphoses of tadpoles to frogs and caterpillars to butterflies.

data.name: Transmission Light Microscopy
data.description: Transmission light microscopy is any optical microscopy technique that relies on detection of light from the opposite side of the sample that was illuminated.

data.name: Machine Tools
data.description: A machine tool is a machine for handling or machining metal or other rigid materials, usually by cutting, boring, grinding, shearing, or other forms of deformations. Machine tools employ some sort of tool that does the cutting or shaping. All machine tools have some means of constraining the workpiece and provide a guided movement of the parts of the machine.

data.name: High-Energy Astrophysics
data.description: High Energy Astrophysics explores energetic events in the Universe with energies extending from the far UV through the keV X-rays and into the Y-ray band. Scientific investigations of objects range from the Sun to distant active galactic nuclei. Research includes studies of the largest scales through wide area surveys.

data.name: Pancreas
data.description: The pancreas is a large gland in the abdomen. It secretes pancreatic juices into the small intestine to digest food, and secretes insulin into the bloodstream to regulate glucose levels. The pancreas is both an endocrine gland (releasing juices directly into the bloodstream) and an exocrine gland (releasing juices into ducts).

data.name: Homologous Recombination
data.description: Homologous recombination is the exchange of DNA strands of similar or identical nucleotide sequence. It can be used to direct error-free repair of double-strand DNA breaks and generates sequence variation in gametes during meiosis.

data.name: Forensic Archaeology
data.description: Forensic archaeology is a specialized branch of archaeology that applies archaeological methods, techniques, and principles to the investigation of legal and criminal cases. It involves the scientific recovery, documentation, and analysis of physical evidence and human remains within the context of a crime scene or legal investigation.

data.name: Water Treatment
data.description: Water treatment is any process that improves the quality of water to make it more acceptable for a specific end-use. This may be drinking, industrial water supply, irrigation, river flow maintenance, water recreation and many other uses, including used water being safely returned to the environment.

data.name: Cell Transplantation
data.description: Cell transplantation is a procedure in which cells, often stem cells or cells that can be induced to become pluripotent stem cells, are transferred to a site where the tissue is damaged or diseased. The transfer can occur within an individual (autologous transplantation), between individuals, or between species. Cells can be treated before implantation.

data.name: Special Dermatology
data.description: Specialized dermatology refers to the subspecialties within the field of dermatology that focus on specific areas or conditions related to the skin, hair, nails, and mucous membranes.

data.name: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
data.description: Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy (EPR), also called electron spin resonance (ESR), is a technique used to study chemical species with unpaired electrons. EPR spectroscopy plays an important role in the understanding of organic and inorganic radicals, transition metal complexes, and some biomolecules

data.name: Assisted Reproductive Techniques
data.description: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) is used to treat infertility. It includes fertility treatments that handle both eggs and sperm. It works by removing eggs from the ovaries. The eggs are then mixed with sperm to make embryos.

data.name: Social Inequality
data.description: Social inequality is the condition of unequal access to the benefits and rights of society. In a purely equal society, every citizen is equally able to contribute to the overall wellbeing of that society, and they are equally able to benefit from their membership within that society.

subjects.term: SOCIAL SCIENCE / Social Classes & Economic Disparity

data.name: Corporate Crime
data.description: Corporate crime focuses on the study of illegal or unethical behavior committed by corporations or individuals within corporate settings. It examines white-collar crimes such as fraud, embezzlement, bribery, insider trading, environmental violations, and other offenses committed for financial gain or to benefit the corporation.

data.name: Air Pollution and Air Quality
data.description: Air Pollution, Atmospheric Protection or Air Quality Control

data.name: Superconductivity
data.description: Superconductivity is a set of physical properties observed in certain materials, superconductors, where electrical resistance vanishes and magnetic flux fields are expelled from the material. Superconductors conduct direct current (DC) electricity without energy loss when they are cooled below a critical temperature (referred to as Tc).

subjects.term: Condensed matter physics (liquid state & solid state physics)
TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Historical Sociology
data.description: Historical sociology is a branch of sociology that examines social structures, processes, and institutions from a historical perspective, using both historical data and sociological theories to better understand how societies evolve and change over time.

data.name: Palaeoclimate
data.description: Palaeoclimate is the reconstruction and study of past climate states on Earth and other planets. Climate parameters such as precipitation, temperature, wind strength, and patterns of interannual climate variability are frequently estimated from proxies in ice and sediment cores, tree rings, cave deposits and historical records. These are assessed in numerical models.

data.name: Neurotrophic Factors
data.description: Neurotrophic factors are molecules that enhance the growth and survival potential of neurons. They play important roles in both development, where they can act as guidance cues for developing neurons, and in the mature nervous system, where they are involved in neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity and the formation of long-lasting memories.

data.name: Genome Informatics
data.description: Genome informatics is the field in which computer and statistical techniques are applied to derive biological information from genome sequences. Genome informatics includes methods to analyse DNA sequence information and to predict protein sequence and structure.

data.name: Endoderm
data.description: The endoderm is the innermost layer of cells in very early vertebrate and insect embryos. It is one of the three primary germ cell layers and gives rise to epithelial tissue lining some organs, including the digestive, urinary and respiratory tracts.

data.name: Phyllotaxis
data.description: Phyllotaxis refers to the arrangement of leaves on a plant stem. Basic patterns include the alternate, opposite, whorled or spiral spacing of leaves.

data.name: Tourism Studies
data.description: Tourism Studies treats its study and research area as a whole, where physical, economic, social and cultural aspects of tourism, tourist markets, and destinations are the main corner-stones of learning.

data.name: Acupuncture
data.description: Acupuncture is a form of alternative medicine and a component of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in which thin needles are inserted into the body. Acupuncture is a pseudoscience the theories and practices of TCM are not based on scientific knowledge, and it has been characterized as quackery.

subjects.term: Cupping. Acupuncture. Artificial hyperemia. Mustard plasters
Complementary, integrated and alternative medicine and therapies

data.name: Flooding
data.description: Flooding is an exceptional or seasonal overflow of water that submerges land and saturates soil. It generally represents a type of abiotic stress for plants, leading to oxygen and energy deprivation, and impeding proper root respiration. Nevertheless, some important plants such as deepwater rice are adapted to cyclical flood.

data.name: Magnetospheric Physics
data.description: Magnetospheric physics is the study of the magnetic fields surrounding the Earth and other bodies in the solar system.

data.name: Menopause
data.description: Menopause is the permanent cessation of menstrual cycles. Natural menopause is caused by ageing-related loss of ovarian function; by contrast, iatrogenic menopause occurs due to medical interventions such as removal of the ovaries. Menopause can cause symptoms such as hot flushes and it increases the risk for certain diseases such as osteoporosis.

data.name: Existentialism
data.description: Existentialism is a philosophical movement that emerged in the 19th and 20th centuries, primarily in Europe. It focuses on the individual's existence, freedom, and the subjective experience of life. Existentialism addresses fundamental questions about human existence, meaning, and the nature of reality. Some key aspects and themes commonly associated with existentialism include Existence Precedes Essence, Authenticity and Freedom, Anxiety and Dread

data.name: Judgment
data.description: Judgment in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive process of evaluating, forming opinions, and making decisions based on available information and personal experiences. It involves weighing evidence, considering alternatives, and arriving at a conclusion or belief.

data.name: Laser Dynamics
data.description: The temporal evolution of quantities such as the optical power and gain in a laser.

data.name: Oesophagus
data.description: The oesophagus is a muscular tube that connects the pharynx to the stomach, enabling the passage of food and liquids. It is part of the upper gastrointestinal tract and runs through the middle of the chest cavity.

data.name: Skeleton
data.description: The skeleton is a rigid framework of bones that forms the supporting structure of the musculoskeletal system, and also functions in movement, haematopoiesis and endocrine regulation. Skeletal bones are connected at the joints by ligaments, and are attached to skeletal muscles by tendons.

data.name: Ion channels in the Nervous System
data.description: Ion channels in the nervous system refers to the study of ion channels – proteins allowing charged particles to cross membranes – found in neurons and glia, where they are involved in maintaining the electrochemical gradients that allow neurons to produce action potentials and neurons and glia to release and recycle neurotransmitters.

data.name: Transient Astrophysical Phenomena
data.description: Transient astrophysical phenomena are events or phenomena in astronomy that occur over a relatively short duration of time, ranging from milliseconds to months or even years. These phenomena are often characterized by sudden changes in brightness, energy output, or other observable properties

data.name: Cementum
data.description: Cementum is a specialized calcified substance covering the root of a tooth. The cementum is the part of the periodontium that attaches the teeth to the alveolar bone by anchoring the periodontal ligament.

data.name: Experimental Models of Disease
data.description: Experimental models of disease are used to investigate processes thought to be involved in human diseases, and to evaluate and select drug candidates that affect these processes to support their progression into clinical trials. They typically involve animals in which processes that are considered to be sufficiently similar to those in human disease are either induced or naturally occur.

synonyms: Experimental Models of Disease Disease models

data.name: Magnesium
data.description: Magnesium (Mg, atomic number 12) is an alkaline earth metal that exists in living systems as Mg2+ ions. Various metalloproteins require magnesium for their function and these are involved in glycolysis and nucleic acid biochemistry. Magnesium can be bound directly or indirectly in metalloproteins or directly to ATP for ATP-dependent reactions.

data.name: Optical interferometry
data.description: Optical interferometry is a method of measuring distance changes with a precision down to sub nanometer scale. By use of imaging techniques the acquisition of surface profiles is also possible. The profile is derived from the relative or absolute phase of the reflected light for each profile point.

data.name: Luminescence Spectroscopy
data.description: Spectroscopic techniques based on luminescence, the spontaneous emission of light by a substance not resulting from heat; Luminescence can be caused by chemical reactions, electrical energy, subatomic motions or stress on a crystal.

data.name: Complications in Anesthesia
data.description: Since a needle is being utilized, the risks of bleeding, hematoma formation, bruising at the injection site, and infection are all possible. Nerve damage from direct needle contact or secondarily to hematoma or infection can also occur. This type of anesthesia, while very safe, is the type most likely to cause side effects and to carry risks. Most side effects are minor and temporary, such as nausea, vomiting, chills, confusion for a few days, and a sore throat caused by a breathing tube.

data.name: Targeted Therapies
data.description: A targeted therapy is one that has been developed to affect a specific target, such as an enzyme or receptor. Targeted therapies can either block or increase the function of their target in order to treat a given disease; in this case, cancer.

data.name: Receptor Pharmacology
data.description: Receptor pharmacology is the study of the interactions of receptors with drugs/pharmaceuticals and other xenobiotics. A basic tenet of receptor pharmacology is that a drug’s effect is directly proportional to the number of occupied receptors. Also, the duration of the drug effect is related to the association and dissociation rates of the drug–receptor complex.

data.name: Water Policy
data.description: Water resource policy, sometimes called water resource management or water management, encompasses the policy-making processes and legislation that affect the collection, preparation, use, disposal, and protection of water resources.

data.name: Mandibular Muscles
data.description: The muscles of mastication are a group of muscles responsible for the chewing movement of the mandible at the temporomandibular (TMJ) joint, they enhance the process of eating, they assist in grinding food, and also function to approximate the teeth.

data.name: Fullerenes
data.description: Fullerene is an allotrope of carbon in the form of a hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube, and many other shapes. Fullerenes are similar in structure to graphite. Nanostructures made by fullerene (buckyballs and buckytubes) are the subject of intense research, both for their chemistry and for their technological applications, especially in materials science, electronics, and nanotechnology.

data.name: Plant Regeneration
data.description: Plant regeneration refers to the process by which plants can restore lost or damaged tissues, organs, or entire individuals through various biological mechanisms. This phenomenon can occur naturally or be induced artificially through techniques such as tissue culture, cuttings, or grafting. In nature, regeneration can involve the growth of new shoots, roots, or leaves from existing plant structures, allowing for recovery from injury, environmental stress, or herbivory. Key factors influencing plant regeneration include the type of plant species, the extent of damage, environmental conditions, and the presence of specific hormones like auxins and cytokinins. Understanding plant regeneration is crucial for applications in agriculture, horticulture, and conservation, as it can enhance crop yields, restore ecosystems, and support biodiversity.

data.name: Calcium
data.description: Calcium (Ca, atomic number 20) is an abundant alkaline earth metal which exists in living systems as Ca2+ ions. Mobilization of calcium stores within cells is important for physiological processes, including oocyte activation during fertilization. Calcium is also involved in multiple cellular signalling pathways, including synaptic transmission in nerve cells and cell motility.

data.name: Neurohistology
data.description: Neurohistology is the study of the microscopic structure and organization of nervous tissue, including the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves. It involves the examination of neural cells, their components, and the connections between them at a cellular and tissue level. Neurohistology encompasses various techniques and methods used to analyze and visualize nervous tissue, such as staining, sectioning, and microscopy.

data.name: Problem Solving
data.description: Problem solving in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive process of finding solutions to complex or challenging problems. It involves identifying the problem, generating possible solutions, evaluating their effectiveness, and implementing the most appropriate solution.

data.name: Biotic
data.description: Biotic components are the living organisms present in an ecosystem, such as bacteria, fungi, plants and animals, and elements produced by them. A biotic factor is any living component that interacts with another organism and affects it in some way.

data.name: General Dermatology
data.description: This area of dermatology helps patients with various skin diseases or ailments that are affecting their quality of life or health.

data.name: Homeostasis
data.description: Homeostasis is the result of variables being regulated such that the internal environment remains stable and fairly constant even though the external environment varies. For example, in humans, the pH of blood and the internal temperature are kept reasonably constant.

data.name: Language and Gender
data.description: The study within sociolinguistics and feminist linguistics that examines the ways in which language reflects and influences gender identity, gender roles, and social norms. It investigates how language is used by individuals and within communities to express and construct gender identities, as well as how gender-related factors influence language use and communication patterns.

data.name: Fluorescent Proteins
data.description: Fluorescent proteins are proteins that absorb light and re-emit it at a longer wavelength. They can be genetically encoded as fusions to other proteins to act as labels.

data.name: Andrology
data.description: The branch of medicine concerned with the anatomy, functions, and disorders (such as infertility or impotence) of the male reproductive system

subjects.term: Diseases and functional disorders of the genital organs (General and male). Andrology

data.name: Pediatric Allergology
data.description: Treating and managing allergic diseases in infants, children, adolescents, and young adults.

data.name: Tissue Culture
data.description: Tissue culture is a method for growing or maintaining tissue in vitro under controlled conditions. The tissue is taken directly from an organism for culture without first dissociating cells.

data.name: Nuclear Pore Complex
data.description: The nuclear pore complex mediates the selective exchange of components, including RNA, ribosomal proteins, signalling molecules and lipids between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. It is one of the largest protein complexes in the cells. Small molecules diffuse through them while larger molecules are recognised by specific components called nucleoporins to be transported through the pores.

data.name: Queer Studies
data.description: Queer studies, sexual diversity studies, or LGBT studies is the study of issues relating to sexual orientation and gender identity usually focusing on lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, gender dysphoria, asexual, queer, questioning, intersex people and cultures.

data.name: Integrin Signalling
data.description: Integrin signalling refers to the signal transduction pathways in which integrins at the cell surface respond to mechanical or biochemical stimuli in the extracellular matrix and transmit this information intracellularly to elicit appropriate responses. Integrin signalling is involved in processes including cell migration, proliferation and regulation of cellular shape.

data.name: Financial Crime
data.description: Financial crime refers to a category of criminal activities that involve fraudulent or illegal actions primarily motivated by financial gain. These activities typically target financial systems, institutions, or individuals, aiming to deceive, manipulate, or misappropriate financial resources for personal or organizational benefit.

data.name: Secularism
data.description: Secularism means the separation of religion from political, economic, social and cultural aspects of life, religion being treated as a purely personal matter. The term “Secular” means being “separate” from religion or having no religious basis.

data.name: Cancer Epigenetics
data.description: Cancer epigenetics is the study of somatically heritable changes to molecular processes that influence the flow of information between the DNA of cancer cells and their gene expression patterns. This includes comparative (tumour cell versus normal cell) investigation of nuclear organization, DNA methylation, histone modification and the consequences of genetic mutations in genes encoding epigenetic regulators.

data.name: Politics and Gender
data.description: Politics and Gender examines the influence of gender on political behavior, representation, and policy-making, as well as the impact of political structures on gender equality and identity.

data.name: Proteome Informatics
data.description: The proteome is the entire complement of proteins that is or can be expressed by a cell, tissue, or organism. Proteome informatics is a set of bioinformatic methods (i.e. methods for collecting and analysing complex datasets) that can be used to analyse the outputs of experiments that determine the proteome of a cell, tissue, organ or organism.

data.name: Sexuality Studies
data.description: Sexuality Studies provides students with knowledge about the processes and variations in sexual functions and reproduction, intimate relationships, sexual and gender role development and behavior, and the social, cultural, historical, and moral contexts of sex and love.

data.name: Transport Vesicle
data.description: Transport carriers are membrane-bound vesicles that contain cargo destined for another cellular destination. Transport carriers bud from cellular membranes and undergo membrane trafficking to reach their target.

data.name: Religion and Popular Science
data.description: Science and religion are closely interconnected in the scientific study of religion, which can be traced back to seventeenth-century natural histories of religion. Natural historians attempted to provide naturalistic explanations for human behavior and culture, including religion and morality.

data.name: Quantum Hall Effect
data.description: Quantum Hall is the quantum-level version of the Hall effect: a voltage produced as electrons flow through a magnetic field. In two-dimensional materials and at low temperatures the quantum mechanical nature of this phenomenon is evident as a series of steps in the Hall voltage with increasing applied magnetic field.

data.name: Planetary Interior
data.description: The structure of a planetary interior and its dynamics control heat transfer within a planet through advected mantle material, heat conducted through the lithosphere, and volcanism.

data.name: Chloroplasts
data.description: Chloroplasts are specialized organelles where photosynthesis occurs, in a highly structured network of membranes, composed of stacked thylakoids interconnected by lamellae. They possess their own DNA and are able to divide. According to the endosymbiotic theory, they originate from engulfed cyanobacteria.

data.name: Japanese
data.description: Japanese refers to the language spoken primarily in Japan. It is a member of the Japonic language family and is known for its unique writing systems, including a combination of Chinese characters (kanji), two syllabaries (hiragana and katakana), and a phonetic script (romaji).

data.name: Lamella
data.description: The lamella is a region at the leading edge of migrating cells that is located behind the dynamic lamellipodium region and contributes to cell migration. The lamella contains an actin fibre network coupled to myosin contractility that contributes to cell migration.

data.name: Biological Fluorescence
data.description: Fluorescence is used in biology as a non-destructive way of analysing biological molecules, even at low concentrations, by means of the molecule’s intrinsic fluorescence, or by attaching it with a fluorophore. Fluorescence is also employed in Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) to detect biopolymer interactions and conformational changes.

data.name: Mineral Resources
data.description: Mineral Resources are a concentration or occurrence of material of intrinsic economic interest in or on the earth's crust in such form, quality and quantity that there are reasonable prospects for eventual economic extraction.

data.name: Transgenic Organisms
data.description: Transgenic organisms are organisms that have undergone heritable genetic changes by transformation with foreign DNA.

data.name: Functional Clustering
data.description: Functional clustering is a computational technique that groups samples, for instance proteins, into clusters with similar functions. Clustering is the first step in forming a network of functions, and can help to identify new connections between, for example, different proteins in a cell.

data.name: Cryospheric Science
data.description: Cryospheric science is the interdisciplinary study of permafrost, snow and ice, primarily on the surface of the Earth, but also on other planets and moons. The cryosphere is an integral part of the climate system, and is investigated with techniques from geophysics, meteorology and hydrology.

data.name: Exoplanet
data.description: Exoplanets are the celestial bodies orbiting stars other than our Sun. Their small size makes them difficult to detect from Earth, particularly as they appear much dimmer than their parent stars. So indirect methods are employed, such as observing changes in starlight as a result of the exoplanet and its motion.

data.name: Food Nanotechnology
data.description: Food nanotechnology is a branch of nanotechnology concerned with the application of nanotechnology to food or food packaging so as to extend the life or safety of food, to detect harmful bacteria, or to produce stronger flavours.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Food Science / Chemistry & Biotechnology

data.name: Laser Spectroscopy
data.description: Methods of laser spectroscopy are often used for detecting the composition of materials, often including quantitative measurements of concentrations.

data.name: Gene Ontology
data.description: The Gene Ontology (GO) project is a bioinformatics initiative that provides an ontology (shared vocabulary) of defined terms to represent specific gene product properties. The use of controlled terms from the GO means that computers can be used to analyse relationships between gene products, which in turn can reveal previously unknown functions.

data.name: Chemical Process Engineering
data.description: Chemical Process Engineering deals with the design, optimization, and operation of industrial chemical processes. It focuses on the practical implementation of chemical transformations in manufacturing environments, emphasizing efficiency, scalability, and troubleshooting of production systems.

data.name: Multimessenger Astronomy
data.description: Multi-messenger astronomy is astronomy based on the coordinated observation and interpretation of disparate "messenger" signals. The four extrasolar messengers are electromagnetic radiation, gravitational waves, neutrinos, and cosmic rays. They are created by different astrophysical processes, and thus reveal different information about their sources.

data.name: Plant Morphogenesis
data.description: Plant morphogenesis concerns the origin and development of the physical form and external structure of plants.

data.name: Preterm Birth
data.description: Preterm is defined as babies born alive before 37 weeks of pregnancy are completed. There are sub-categories of preterm birth, based on gestational age: extremely preterm (less than 28 weeks) very preterm (28 to less than 32 weeks) moderate to late preterm (32 to 37 weeks).

data.name: Planetary Atmosphere
data.description: Planetary atmospheres function as reservoirs for mixing and rapidly distributing elements that have a volatile phase.

data.name: Mitotic Spindle
