data.description: The mitotic spindle is the microtubule-based bipolar structure that segregates the chromosomes in mitosis. The poles of the mitotic spindle are made up of centrosomes and the chromosomes are lined up at the spindle equator to ensure their correct bi-orientation and segregation.

data.name: ADAS, Connectivity, E/E
data.description: ADAS focuses on driver assistance and safety features, Connectivity enables vehicles to connect to external networks and services, and E/E encompasses the electrical and electronic systems that control various functions in modern vehicles.

data.name: Postcolonial STS
data.description: Postcolonial Science and Technology Studies (STS) critically analyzes the production, distribution, and consequences of scientific knowledge and technology in the context of historical colonialism and its aftermath. This interdisciplinary field explores the intertwined relationship between power, culture, and technology and seeks to decolonize the discourse on knowledge production.

data.name: Structural Mechanics
data.description: Structural mechanics is the branch of continuum mechanics that studies the behavior of solid materials, especially their motion and deformation under the action of forces, temperature changes, phase changes, and other external or internal agents. It is important for both engineering and physics aspects of materials science.

data.name: Electronic Structure Calculations
data.description: Electronic structure calculations use quantum chemistry computer programs to solve the equations describing the quantum mechanical motion of a molecular system.

data.name: Data-driven Science, Modeling and Theory Building
data.description: Data-driven Science is an interdisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from data in various forms. It employs several techniques and theories drawn from many fields within the context of mathematics, statistics, information science, and computer science.

data.name: Fat Metabolism
data.description: Fat metabolism is the biochemical processes that break down dietary fats into fatty acids and glycerol for energy production, storage in adipose tissue, or conversion into other molecules (e.g., ketone bodies); regulated by hormones such as insulin and glucagon.

data.name: Reprogramming
data.description: Cell reprogramming is the process of reverting mature, specialised cells into induced pluripotent stem cells. Reprogramming also refers to the erasure and re-establishment of epigenetic marks during mammalian germ cell development.

data.name: Genetic Imprinting
data.description: Imprinting is epigenetic marking of a locus on the basis of its parental origin, which can result in differential expression of the paternal and maternal alleles in specific tissues or developmental stages. These epigenetic marks are established in the germline and can be maintained through mitotic divisions.

data.name: Energy and Society
data.description: Studies the interaction of issues related to energy (including supply and demand, ethics, economic effects, etc.) with the society in a holistic way.

data.name: Haplotypes
data.description: A haplotype is the genetic makeup of an individual with respect to combinations of alleles that are closely linked and tend to be inherited together. This may be one locus, several loci, or an entire chromosome.

data.name: Russian
data.description: Russian is an East Slavic language spoken primarily in Russia, as well as in other countries that were formerly part of the Soviet Union, such as Ukraine, Belarus, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan. It is one of the most widely spoken Slavic languages and one of the official languages of the United Nations. Russian belongs to the Indo-European language family and shares similarities with other Slavic languages such as Ukrainian, Polish, and Bulgarian.

data.name: Mechanical Properties of Materials
data.description: Mechanical properties are physical properties that a material exhibits upon the application of forces. Examples of mechanical properties are the modulus of elasticity, tensile strength, elongation, hardness and fatigue limit.

data.name: Combinatorial Libraries
data.description: Combinatorial libraries are collections of molecules generated through the combination of different building blocks or subunits. These libraries allow for the rapid and efficient exploration of a vast chemical space, enabling the discovery and optimization of novel compounds with desired properties. Combinatorial chemistry techniques have revolutionized drug discovery, materials science, and other fields by providing a diverse set of molecules for screening and analysis.

data.name: Viral Genetics
data.description: Viral genetics is the study of the mechanisms of heritable information in viruses, including genome structure, replication and genetic change. Disease causing viruses are of particular interest, however geneticists also use viruses to help understand fundamental mechanisms of molecular genetics.

data.name: Membrane Curvature
data.description: Membrane curvature is the deflection of cellular membranes. The generation of membrane curvature is essential for cellular processes such as cell division, and endocytosis and exocytosis. Membrane curvature can be induced by protein association with the membrane or by changes in local membrane lipid concentration.

data.name: Anaesthetic
data.description: An anesthetic or anaesthetic is a drug used to induce anesthesia ⁠— ⁠in other words, to result in a temporary loss of sensation or awareness.

data.name: Museum Anthropology
data.description: Museum anthropology, also known as anthropological museology or ethnographic museum studies, is a subfield of anthropology that focuses on the study of museums and their roles in preserving, representing, and interpreting human cultures and societies. It involves the examination of museums as institutions and the way they collect, exhibit, and engage with cultural artifacts and ethnographic materials.

data.name: Procedures in Anesthesiology
data.description: General anesthesia is an anesthetic used to induce unconsciousness during surgery. The medicine is either inhaled through a breathing mask or tube, or given through an intravenous (IV) line. A breathing tube may be inserted into the windpipe to maintain proper breathing during surgery.

data.name: Biochemical Assay
data.description: A biochemical assay is an analytical in vitro procedure used to detect, quantify and/or study the binding or activity of a biological molecule, such as an enzyme.

data.name: Language Processing
data.description: Language processing in the field of psychology refers to the cognitive and neural processes involved in the comprehension, production, and use of language. It encompasses various aspects such as phonological processing, syntactic processing, semantic processing, and pragmatic processing, which collectively contribute to our ability to understand and communicate through language.

subjects.term: Psychological principles, language acquisition, speech perception

data.name: Episodic Memory
data.description: Episodic memory, in the field of psychology, refers to the type of long-term memory that involves the encoding, storage, and retrieval of personal experiences and specific events that are tied to a particular time and place. It allows individuals to remember specific details and contextual information about past events, such as autobiographical memories. Episodic memory plays a crucial role in our ability to recall personal narratives, remember specific life events, and mentally time travel to the past.

data.name: Axon and Dendritic Guidance
data.description: Axon and dendritic guidance is the biological process by which growing axons and dendrites orient and navigate to their targets during the development of the nervous system. Axon and dendritic guidance determines synaptic connectivity and is regulated by fixed or diffusible extracellular molecules as well as factors intrinsic to the neuron.

data.name: Respiratory System Models
data.description: Respiratory system models are experimental systems that recreate aspects of human respiratory system development, function or disease. Animal models such as dog, rodent and pig can be used to study infectious and genetic respiratory illnesses.

data.name: Marxist Sociology
data.description: Marxist Sociology applies the theories of Karl Marx to analyze social structures, focusing on class relations, economic systems, and the impact of capitalism on society.

data.name: Extracellular Matrix
data.description: The extracellular matrix is a complex network of material such as proteins and polysaccharides that are secreted locally by cells and remain closely associated with them to provide structural, adhesive and biochemical signalling support.

data.name: Light Stress
data.description: Light stress refers to the detrimental effect that exposure to insufficient or excess levels of light can have on plant function and development. Whereas exposure to insufficient light limits photosynthetic activity, exposure to excess light energy can damage the photosynthetic apparatus.

data.name: Forensic Anthropology
data.description: Forensic anthropology is a subfield of forensic science that applies principles and methods of biological anthropology to analyze human skeletal remains in the context of legal investigations. It involves the identification, examination, and interpretation of skeletal and anatomical evidence to establish the identity, age, sex, ancestry, stature, and potential cause of death of individuals. Forensic anthropologists also play a crucial role in the recovery and analysis of human remains in forensic contexts, such as crime scenes or mass disasters.

data.name: Molecular Deformation Dynamics
data.description: Deformation dynamics describes the effect of forces and torques on the shape of a molecule, for instance on biopolymers, such as polynucleotides, polypeptides or polysaccharides.

synonyms: Structural Deformation at the Molecular Level

data.name: Hand Surgery
data.description: Hand surgery deals with both surgical and non-surgical treatment of conditions and problems that may take place in the hand or upper extremity (commonly from the tip of the hand to the shoulder) including injury and infection. Hand surgery may be practiced by post graduates of orthopedic surgery and plastic surgery.

data.name: Transhumanism
data.description: Transhumanism is a class of philosophies that seek to guide us towards a posthuman condition. Transhumanism shares many elements of humanism, including a respect for reason and science, a commitment to progress, and a valuing of human (or transhuman) existence in this life.

data.name: Slang and Jargon
data.description: Slang and jargon are two distinct types of language varieties that are used in specific social or professional contexts. Slang refers to informal, non-standard language that is commonly used in casual or colloquial speech. It is often associated with particular social groups, subcultures, or communities. while Jargon refers to specialized vocabulary, terminology, or technical language used within a specific profession, industry, or field of study. It is often characterized by its precision, efficiency, and specificity

data.name: Industrial Pollution Prevention
data.description: Pollution whose source originates directly from industry is known as industrial pollution. Pollution Prevention means eliminating or reducing the amount and toxicity of potentially harmful substances at their sources, prior to generation, treatment, off-site recycling or disposal.

data.name: Computational Fluid Dynamics
data.description: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is a science that, with the help of digital computers, produces quantitative predictions of fluid-flow phenomena based on the conservation laws (conservation of mass, momentum, and energy) governing fluid motion.

data.name: German Politics
data.description: Germany is a democratic and federal parliamentary republic, where federal legislative power is vested in the Bundestag (the parliament of Germany) and the Bundesrat (the representative body of the Länder, Germany's regional states).

data.name: Dental Pulp
data.description: The dental pulp is a mass of connective tissue that resides within the center of the tooth, directly beneath the layer of dentin.

data.name: Osteoimmunology
data.description: Osteoimmunology is the study of how the immune and skeletal systems interact.

data.name: Bioconjugate Chemistry
data.description: Bioconjugate chemistry is the study of linking one molecule to another by chemical or biological means. The resulting complexes will typically be formed from at least one biomolecule, though they can also be purely synthetic molecules with a biological application..Conjugated polymers are organic macromolecules that are characterized by a backbone chain of alternating double- and single-bonds. Their overlapping p-orbitals create a system of delocalised π-electrons, which can result in interesting and useful optical and electronic properties.

data.name: Child Abuse and Neglect
data.description: This is a transdisciplinary field covering all aspects of child protection, rights, and public health, social welfare and humanitarian aid directed to the protection of children from exploitation, abuse, mistreatment, in any sphere of life.

data.name: Dengue Virus
data.description: Dengue virus is an infectious agent that causes the tropical disease dengue fever in humans. This virus species is transmitted by mosquitoes (arthropods) and thus is an arbovirus.

data.name: Effectors in Plant Pathology
data.description: Effectors are proteins expressed by plant pathogens to aid infection of specific plant species. These molecules can alter plant processes and are central to understanding the complicated interplay between plants and their pathogens.

data.name: Digital Religion
data.description: Digital Religion is the practice of religion in the digital world, and the academic study of such religious practice. Now digital religion is a modern field sub-category stemming out of digital culture. In the mid-1990s, "cyber-religion" was a term that arose to describe the interface between religion and virtual reality technologies. Most scholars started documenting how religious groups moved worship online and how religious rituals were performed.

data.name: Data Publication and Archiving
data.description: Data publication is the process of making information, particularly data generated from research, available to all. Data archiving is the long term storage of such data and methods. In science, publishing and archiving data is important to preserve scientific information for future research.

data.name: Physics of Proteins in Health and Disease
data.description: The physical principles and properties of proteins contribute to their functioning in biological systems, as well as how disruptions in these physical processes can lead to various health conditions and diseases.

synonyms: Biophysical Aspects of Health and Disease
Protein Biophysics in Health and Pathology
Physical Mechanisms of Health and Disease at the Protein Level
Protein Physics in Health and Disease

data.name: Clusters and Nanostructures on Surfaces
data.description: Clusters and nanostructures on surfaces refer to the arrangement and aggregation of atoms or molecules on the surface of a material at the nanoscale. The term "nanostructures" generally refers to structures with dimensions on the order of nanometers , while "clusters" specifically refer to small groups of atoms or molecules.

data.name: Narcotic
data.description: A narcotic refers to a drug that produces analgesic (pain-relieving) effects, induces drowsiness or sleep, and can cause dependence or addiction when used chronically. Narcotics are often prescribed for the management of severe pain but also have a high potential for abuse.

data.name: Conservative Orthopedics
data.description: Conservative orthopaedics as primary treatment. We aim to offer conservative treatment primarily, which is the successful mode of treatment in most cases. Conservative treatment includes physiotherapy, medication, infiltrations, bandages, shock wave therapy, acupuncture treatment and other pain management options.

data.name: Diamond
data.description: Diamond is a highly prized and renowned gemstone known for its exceptional hardness, brilliance, and clarity. It is composed of carbon atoms arranged in a crystal lattice structure, making it a form of carbon allotrope. Diamonds are formed deep within the Earth's mantle under high pressure and temperature conditions and are brought to the surface through volcanic eruptions.

data.name: Gender, Sexuality and Law
data.description: This subject area explores the intersections of gender, sexuality, and legal institutions. It examines how laws and legal practices impact the experiences, rights, and identities of individuals based on gender and sexual orientation and how these factors shape legal theory and policy.

data.name: Ethnicity, Class, Gender and Crime
data.description: This subfield explores the intersectionality of race, social class, gender, and their influence on crime and criminal justice. It recognizes that individuals experience crime and justice differently based on their race, socioeconomic status, and gender, and seeks to understand the complex dynamics and inequalities that exist within these intersections.

data.name: German Literature
data.description: German literature refers to the body of literary works written in the German language or by German-speaking authors. It encompasses a rich and diverse tradition that spans many centuries and includes various genres and styles. German literature has made significant contributions to world literature, with renowned authors and works that have had a profound impact on literary movements and cultural discourse.

data.name: Non-model Organisms
data.description: Non-model organisms are organisms that have not been selected by the research community for extensive study either for historic reasons, or because they lack the features that make model organisms easy to investigate (e.g. they cannot grow in the laboratory, have a long life cycle, low fecundity or poor genetics).

data.name: Language Acquisition and Development
data.description: Language acquisition is the ability to understand a language, using it to communicate with others.   Language acquisition and language development can be understood as synonymous

data.name: Microbe
data.description: Microbes are single or multicellular microscopic organisms. Plant-microbe interactions can bring benefit or harm to plants. For instance, mycorrhizal fungi can supply plants with nutrients, whereas fungal, bacterial and viral pathogens can impair plant function.

data.name: Conflict and War
data.description: War is an intense armed conflict between states, governments, societies, or paramilitary groups such as mercenaries, insurgents, and militias. It is generally characterized by extreme violence, destruction and mortality, using regular or irregular military forces.

data.name: Social Movements
data.description: A social movement is a loosely organized effort by a large group of people to achieve a particular goal, typically a social or political one.  This may be to carry out a social change, or to resist or undo one.  It is a type of group action and may involve individuals, organizations or both.

data.name: Human-Computer Studies
data.description: "Human-Computer Studies" typically refer to interdisciplinary fields of study that examine the interaction and relationship between humans and computers, including aspects of design, usability, interface development, and more.

data.name: Learning Theory
data.description: Learning theory as a field of study encompasses the systematic examination, analysis, and exploration of the processes, principles, and mechanisms underlying human learning. It involves the study of how individuals acquire, process, retain, and apply knowledge and skills across different domains and contexts. Learning theory as a field draws from various disciplines, including psychology, education, neuroscience, and cognitive science, to develop and refine theories, models, and frameworks that explain the nature of learning and inform educational practices. Researchers in this field investigate factors that influence learning, such as motivation, cognition, environment, and social interactions, and strive to identify effective instructional strategies, interventions, and approaches that optimize learning outcomes.

data.name: Traditional Chinese Medicine
data.description: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) is an alternative medical practice drawn from traditional medicine in China.

data.name: Nuclear Speckles
data.description: Nuclear speckles are structures that can be observed by immunofluorescence microscopy as a punctate pattern within the nucleus of mammalian cells. Nuclear speckles are dynamic and their composition can change over time, but they are generally enriched in pre-mRNA splicing factors and co-localize with actively transcribed chromatin regions.

data.name: Telomeres
data.description: Telomeres are the ends of linear chromosomes. Telomeric DNA is bound by specialized proteins that prevent it from being targeted by DNA damage repair pathways, and is maintained by the enzyme telomerase.

data.name: X-Ray Scattering
data.description: X-ray scattering is a technique used to study the structure and properties of materials at the atomic and molecular levels. It involves the interaction of X-rays with a sample, leading to the scattering of X-rays in different directions. By analyzing the scattering pattern, valuable information about the atomic arrangement, crystal structure, and other properties of the material can be obtained.  Two main types of X-ray scattering techniques: X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Small-Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS).

data.name: Ribosome
data.description: The ribosome is a large assembly of proteins and ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs) that functions to translate messenger RNAs (mRNAs) into proteins. The ribosome catalyzes the assembly of amino acids into peptide chains of defined sequence, as dictated by the interaction of amino-acid-carrying transport RNAs (tRNAs) with complementary sequences in the ribosome-bound mRNA.

data.name: Shape Analysis
data.description: The study that deals with the mathematical representation, comparison, and manipulation of shapes or geometrical objects. It involves developing techniques to extract meaningful information from shapes, quantify their similarities or differences, and perform various operations based on shape-related attributes.

data.name: Religious Pluralism
data.description: Religious pluralism is the state of being where every individual in a religiously diverse society has the rights, freedoms, and safety to worship, or not, according to their conscience.

data.name: Ab Initio Calculations
data.description: Ab initio calculations are computations of electronic orbitals with no other hypotheses than Coulomb interactions between all electrons and nuclei with electrons obeying Fermi statistics with the Pauli exclusion principle.

data.name: Dental Trauma
data.description: Dental trauma refers to trauma (injury) to the teeth and/or periodontium (gums, periodontal ligament, alveolar bone), and nearby soft tissues such as the lips, tongue, etc.

data.name: Science Ethics
data.description: Science ethics, also known as research ethics or scientific ethics, is a branch of applied ethics that focuses on the ethical considerations and responsibilities arising in scientific research and the practice of science. It involves the examination of moral principles, values, and guidelines that guide scientific inquiry, publication, and the interaction between science and society.

data.name: Banking
data.description: The banking industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on financial institutions that provide various banking services to individuals, businesses, and governments. It includes the study of banking operations, financial management, risk management, corporate governance, regulations, and innovations in the banking sector. Some of the key topics in banking industry research include the impact of technology on banking, financial regulation and compliance, financial risk management, asset and liability management, investment banking, retail banking, and financial inclusion. The banking industry is a critical component of the global economy, and research in this field can provide insights into economic growth, financial stability, and sustainable development.

data.name: Volcanology
data.description: Volcanology is the study of the generation and movement of molten rock on Earth and other planetary bodies, primarily through volcanoes and volcanic eruptions. This encompasses the generation of magma, its geochemistry and movement through the Earth’s crust, the physics of volcanic eruptions and hazards including ash clouds and pyroclastic flows.

data.name: Fossil Fuel
data.description: A fossil fuel is a hydrocarbon-containing material such as coal, oil, and natural gas, formed naturally in the Earth's crust from the remains of dead plants and animals that is extracted and burned as a fuel. Fossil fuels may be burned to provide heat for use directly, to power engines, or to generate electricity.

data.name: Photovoltaics
data.description: Solar energy and photovoltaic technology is the study of using light from the sun as a source of energy, and the design and fabrication of devices for harnessing this potential. This involves collecting solar radiation for converting to both electricity and heat. Solar energy is carbon-free and renewable.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Power Resources / Alternative & Renewable
Generation of electricity from solar radiation
Photovoltaic power generation. Photovoltaic power systems

data.name: Renewable Energy
data.description: Renewable energy is energy that comes from sources that are readily replenishable on short-timescales. Examples of these are solar radiation, wind, and biomass.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Power Resources / Alternative & Renewable
Alternative and renewable energy sources and technology

data.name: Palliative Care
data.description: Palliative care is the set of medical interventions to alleviate symptoms, most frequently pain, associated with a medical condition. The main goal of palliative care is to reduce and prevent patient suffering. Unlike therapeutics, palliative care does not aim to cure the underlying disease. Palliative care is an interdisciplinary medical caregiving  approach that improves the quality of life of patients and their families facing the problems associated with life-threatening illness, through the prevention and relief of suffering by means of early identification and impeccable assessment and treatment of pain and other problems, physical, psychosocial, and spiritual.

data.name: Industrial Psychology
data.description: Industrial psychology, also known as industrial-organizational psychology or I-O psychology, is a field of psychology that focuses on understanding and improving human behavior in the workplace. It applies psychological principles and research methods to address issues related to personnel selection, employee training and development, organizational effectiveness, and work environment. Industrial psychology aims to enhance employee well-being, productivity, and job satisfaction while optimizing organizational performance and efficiency.

data.name: Market Psychology
data.description: Market psychology, also known as investor psychology or financial psychology, refers to the study of how psychological factors influence financial markets, investment decisions, and market behavior. It explores the role of emotions, cognitive biases, and social influences in shaping market trends, investor sentiment, and the overall functioning of financial markets.

data.name: Mental Training
data.description: The term Mental Training is used to describe a variety of psychological methods, which aim at facilitating and improving performance, resilience, self-awareness, confidence or well-being by optimising social and communicative skills, cognitive skills or motivational and emotional processes.   In Sport Psychology, the narrow definition of Mental Training specifies it as training procedures for optimising the regulation of movement by conciously and repeatedly envisioning movement tasks or actions. Mental Training may also include techniques to regulate emotion (anger, fear, stress), motivation (will, achievement motivation) or perception (focus, concentration) and strengthen the athletes confidence in his or her capability. This may also include techniques that focus on coach-athlete or team interaction. Besides the long term systematic application of mental training, it is also used situationally in competition preparation or evaluation.

data.name: Metacognition
data.description: Metacognition in the field of psychology refers to the ability to think about and have awareness of one's own cognitive processes. It involves reflecting on and monitoring one's thoughts, knowledge, and strategies, as well as regulating and adapting one's cognitive activities to enhance learning and problem-solving.

data.name: Neuropsychology
data.description: A branch of psychology examining how cognition and behavior are related to the brain and the rest of the nervous system. Often focuses on how injuries affect cognitive and behavioral functions.

data.name: Attention Deficit Disorder
data.description: Attention deficit disorder (ADD), as a field of study in psychology, focuses on understanding the nature, causes, and treatment of attention deficits that significantly impact individuals' daily functioning. It involves examining the cognitive, behavioral, and emotional aspects of attention difficulties, as well as exploring the factors that contribute to the development and persistence of attention deficits. Researchers and clinicians in the field of ADD aim to identify effective strategies and interventions to help individuals with attention deficits improve their attentional control, academic performance, and overall well-being.

data.name: Substance Abuse Disorder
data.description: Substance abuse addiction, also known as substance use disorder, is a field of study in psychology that focuses on understanding and addressing the patterns of excessive and harmful use of substances such as drugs or alcohol. It involves examining the psychological, social, and biological factors contributing to the development and maintenance of addiction, as well as developing effective prevention, intervention, and treatment strategies. The field of substance abuse addiction seeks to understand the underlying mechanisms, risk factors, and consequences associated with substance abuse, and to promote recovery and overall well-being.

data.name: Psychotic Disorder
data.description: Psychotic Disorder, as a field of study in psychology, focuses on understanding and treating severe mental illnesses characterized by significant disturbances in thinking, perception, and behavior. Researchers and clinicians in this field investigate the causes, symptoms, and treatment options for psychotic disorders, such as schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder. They examine biological, psychological, and social factors that contribute to the development and progression of these disorders, and work towards developing effective interventions to alleviate symptoms and improve overall functioning.

data.name: Panic Disorder
data.description: Panic Disorder, as a field of study in psychology, focuses on the examination and treatment of a type of anxiety disorder characterized by recurrent and unexpected panic attacks. Researchers and clinicians in this field explore the etiology, risk factors, and underlying mechanisms of panic disorder, including biological, psychological, and environmental factors. They investigate the cognitive and physiological processes involved in panic attacks, assess the impact of panic disorder on daily functioning and well-being, and develop effective interventions for symptom management and recovery.

data.name: Agoraphobia
data.description: Agoraphobia, in the context of psychology, refers to a specific anxiety disorder characterized by an intense fear or anxiety about being in situations or places where escape might be difficult or help may not be readily available in the event of a panic attack or other distressing symptoms. Individuals with agoraphobia often avoid or feel significant distress in places such as open spaces, crowded areas, public transportation, or places outside their comfort zone. Agoraphobia is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding the causes, symptoms, assessment, and treatment of this particular anxiety disorder.

data.name: Social Phobia
data.description: Social phobia, also known as social anxiety disorder, is a psychological condition characterized by intense fear and anxiety in social situations. Individuals with social phobia often experience excessive self-consciousness and a fear of being judged or humiliated by others. This fear can significantly impact their ability to engage in social interactions and can lead to avoidance behaviors. The field of study that examines social phobia and its related aspects is known as social psychology.

data.name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
data.description: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding and addressing the psychological and emotional impact of traumatic experiences. It involves the exploration of the symptoms, causes, and treatment of PTSD, which can occur following exposure to a traumatic event such as war, natural disasters, accidents, or personal assault. Researchers and practitioners in this field aim to better understand the complex nature of PTSD, its effects on individuals, and develop effective interventions to promote healing and recovery.

data.name: Somatoform Disorder
data.description: Somatoform Disorder is a field of study in psychology that involves the investigation and understanding of a group of mental disorders characterized by physical symptoms that cannot be fully explained by a medical condition or other physiological factors. Individuals with somatoform disorders often experience distress and impairment due to their physical symptoms, which are believed to be influenced primarily by psychological factors.

data.name: Eating Disorder
data.description: Eating disorders, as a field of study in psychology, involves the examination of abnormal eating behaviors and their psychological underpinnings. Researchers and clinicians in this field investigate the complex interplay between biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors that contribute to the development and maintenance of eating disorders. They study various types of eating disorders such as anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge eating disorder, aiming to understand the underlying mechanisms, risk factors, and treatment approaches associated with these conditions. The field of eating disorders encompasses research, assessment, and interventions to support individuals struggling with disordered eating patterns and promote their recovery.

data.name: Sexual Disorder
data.description: Sexual disorders refer to a range of conditions that affect an individual's ability to experience sexual arousal, desire, or function in a way that is satisfactory to them. These disorders can have a significant impact on an individual's quality of life and relationships. The field of study that focuses on the diagnosis, assessment, and treatment of sexual disorders is known as sexual psychology.

data.name: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
data.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is a widely used therapeutic approach within the field of psychology that focuses on the connections between thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. It is based on the idea that our thoughts and beliefs influence our feelings and behaviors, and by identifying and modifying negative or maladaptive thought patterns, individuals can experience positive changes in their emotions and behaviors. CBT combines cognitive restructuring techniques to address faulty thinking patterns with behavioral techniques to promote behavioral change and improve overall well-being.

data.name: Operant Conditioning
data.description: Operant conditioning, in the field of psychology, is a form of learning in which behavior is influenced by its consequences. It involves the use of reinforcements (rewards or punishments) to strengthen or weaken a specific behavior, thereby shaping and modifying behavior over time.

data.name: Social Learning
data.description: Social learning, in the field of psychology, refers to the process by which individuals acquire new behaviors, attitudes, or knowledge through observation, imitation, and interaction with others in their social environment. It emphasizes the role of social interactions and modeling in shaping behavior and cognitive processes.

data.name: Achievement Motivation
data.description: Achievement motivation refers to the psychological drive or desire to accomplish and succeed in challenging tasks, activities, or goals. It is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding the factors that influence individuals' motivation to achieve success, excel in their endeavors, and attain desired outcomes. Achievement motivation encompasses various cognitive, emotional, and behavioral processes that contribute to goal-directed behavior and the pursuit of excellence. Researchers in this field explore topics such as goal setting, self-evaluation, self-regulation, persistence, and the impact of achievement motivation on academic, occupational, and personal achievement. The study of achievement motivation aims to enhance our understanding of the complex factors that drive individuals to strive for success and the ways in which motivation can be fostered and optimized.

data.name: Extrinsic Motivation
data.description: Extrinsic motivation refers to the drive or desire to engage in activities or pursue goals that are influenced by external rewards, outcomes, or incentives. It is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding the factors that motivate individuals based on external factors such as tangible rewards, social approval, or avoidance of punishment. Extrinsic motivation is often contrasted with intrinsic motivation, which involves engaging in activities for the inherent satisfaction and enjoyment they provide.

data.name: Intrinsic Motivation
data.description: Intrinsic motivation refers to the inherent drive or desire to engage in activities or pursue goals for their own sake, driven by internal rewards and personal satisfaction. It is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding the factors that motivate individuals based on internal factors such as curiosity, interest, and the enjoyment derived from the activity itself. Intrinsic motivation is often characterized by a sense of autonomy, competence, and relatedness, where individuals engage in activities because they find them meaningful, enjoyable, or personally fulfilling.

data.name: Power Motivation
data.description: Power motivation, also known as need for power, refers to an individual's psychological drive or desire to have an impact, influence others, and control or exercise authority over one's environment. It is a field of study within psychology that focuses on understanding the motivational factors underlying the pursuit of power and the impact of power motivation on behavior, cognition, and social interactions. Power motivation can manifest in different ways, such as seeking leadership roles, striving for control and dominance, or exerting influence over others to achieve personal or group goals.

data.name: Group Coaching
data.description: Group coaching is a type of coaching that involves working with a group of individuals who share a common goal or interest. In this approach, a coach facilitates a group session in which each participant has the opportunity to share their experiences, insights, and challenges related to the group's focus. The coach supports the group by providing structure, guidance, and feedback to help members achieve their individual and collective goals.

data.name: Individual Coaching
data.description: Coaching is a field within Human Resources Management that focuses on developing and enhancing the skills and performance of employees through one-on-one interactions with a coach. The coach provides guidance, support, and feedback to help individuals improve their job performance, achieve their career goals, and reach their full potential.  In coaching, the coach and employee work together to identify areas for improvement and set goals for development. The coach may use a variety of techniques, such as questioning, active listening, and role-playing, to help the employee gain new insights and develop new skills.  Coaching is often used in conjunction with other Human Resources Management initiatives, such as performance management, talent development, and leadership development. Coaching can be provided by internal coaches within an organization, or by external coaches who are hired on a contract basis.

data.name: Intervision
data.description: Intervision is a form of professional development that involves a group of peers within a specific field or profession coming together to engage in collaborative learning, sharing of experiences and knowledge, reflection, and feedback. In coaching, intervision is a way for coaches to work together to improve their skills and competencies by examining and discussing their own coaching practices and receiving feedback from other coaches.

data.name: Team Coaching
data.description: Team coaching and management is a field within human resource management that focuses on improving team performance through coaching and training interventions. It involves using coaching techniques to identify and develop team members' strengths and areas for improvement, as well as improving communication and collaboration within the team.  Topics within team coaching and management may include:  Team building Group dynamics Conflict resolution Communication skills Leadership development Performance management Organizational culture Change management Research in this field may explore the impact of team coaching and management on team performance, as well as the effectiveness of different coaching techniques and interventions. It may also examine the role of team coaching and management in promoting employee engagement, retention, and job satisfaction.

subjects.term: BUSINESS & ECONOMICS / Human Resources & Personnel Management

data.name: Leadership Psychology
data.description: Leadership psychology is a field of management research that focuses on understanding the psychological processes that underlie effective leadership. It seeks to identify the personality traits, cognitive abilities, and behavioral patterns that are associated with successful leadership, as well as the situational factors that influence leadership effectiveness.  Leadership psychology draws on a range of theories and research methods from psychology, sociology, and other social sciences to examine how leaders motivate and inspire others, build trust and loyalty, and navigate complex social dynamics. It also investigates the impact of leadership on organizational culture, employee satisfaction, and overall performance.  Research in leadership psychology has practical implications for management practice, as it can help organizations identify and develop effective leaders, as well as design training and development programs to improve leadership skills at all levels of the organization. It also informs policies and practices that promote ethical leadership, diversity and inclusion, and employee well-being.

data.name: Organizational Climate
data.description: Organizational climate refers to the collective perceptions, attitudes, and experiences of employees within an organization. It represents the prevailing atmosphere, culture, and work environment that shape employee behavior, attitudes, and performance. It encompasses factors such as leadership style, communication patterns, teamwork, and organizational policies and practices.

data.name: Organizational Development
data.description: Organizational development (OD) is a field of management research that focuses on improving organizational effectiveness and employee well-being through planned interventions in the organization's processes and structures. OD aims to enhance the organization's ability to adapt to change and achieve its goals by fostering a culture of continuous learning, innovation, and collaboration.  Some major topics within the field of organizational development include: Change management: The process of managing and implementing organizational changes to improve performance, increase efficiency, and enhance the organization's competitive advantage. Leadership development: The process of developing leadership skills and abilities within the organization to enable leaders to inspire, motivate, and guide employees to achieve organizational goals. Team building: The process of developing high-performing teams by promoting communication, collaboration, and mutual accountability among team members. Performance management: The process of setting goals, measuring performance, providing feedback, and improving employee performance to achieve organizational objectives. Talent management: The process of attracting, retaining, and developing employees with the skills and abilities needed to achieve organizational goals. Diversity, equity, and inclusion: The process of creating a more inclusive and diverse workplace culture that values and respects the differences among employees and promotes equitable treatment and opportunities for all. Organizational culture: The shared values, beliefs, and practices that shape the way people behave within an organization, and the impact of culture on employee engagement, motivation, and performance. Employee engagement: The degree to which employees are committed to their work and the organization, and the impact of engagement on employee satisfaction, productivity, and retention. Organizational learning: The process of creating a learning organization that encourages continuous learning and knowledge sharing to improve organizational performance and innovation. Organizational design: The process of designing the organizational structure, processes, and systems to support the organization's goals and strategies.

data.name: Performance Assessment
data.description: Performance assessment in the field of psychology refers to the systematic evaluation of an individual's skills, knowledge, abilities, and behaviors in relation to predetermined criteria or standards. It involves the collection and analysis of data to assess an individual's performance in various domains, such as academic, professional, or personal settings.

data.name: Performance Development
data.description: Performance development and management is a field within Human Resource Management that involves the continuous process of improving employees' skills, knowledge, and performance to meet organizational goals. It includes identifying the skills and behaviors required for successful job performance, developing and implementing training programs, and evaluating employee performance. The main topics within performance development and management include: Performance appraisal: This involves the systematic evaluation of employees' job performance against predetermined performance standards and goals. Performance feedback: This involves providing employees with information about their performance and ways to improve. Performance improvement plans: This involves creating plans for employees who are not meeting performance standards, outlining the steps they need to take to improve. Training and development: This involves identifying training needs and developing training programs to improve employees' skills and knowledge. Goal setting: This involves setting specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) goals that align with the organization's objectives. Coaching and mentoring: This involves providing employees with guidance and support to help them develop their skills and achieve their goals. Succession planning: This involves identifying and developing employees who have the potential to take on leadership roles within the organization. Overall, performance development and management is essential for improving employee performance, increasing employee engagement, and achieving organizational goals.

data.name: Personnel Development
data.description: Personnel development in the field of psychology refers to the intentional and systematic process of enhancing the knowledge, skills, abilities, and attitudes of individuals within an organization. It involves identifying and addressing developmental needs, providing training and learning opportunities, and supporting the growth and career advancement of personnel.

data.name: Personnel Marketing
data.description: Personnel marketing, also known as employer branding, is a field of research and practice within human resources management that focuses on creating and maintaining an attractive image of an organization to attract and retain employees. It involves strategies and activities aimed at promoting the organization as an employer of choice, creating a positive employer brand image, and differentiating it from competitors in the job market. Some of the topics within personnel marketing include: Employer branding: developing and promoting an organization's image as an attractive employer. Talent attraction and recruitment: strategies and activities aimed at attracting the best candidates for open positions. Employee retention: strategies and activities aimed at retaining high-performing and valuable employees. Employee value proposition (EVP): a set of rewards, benefits, and opportunities that an employer offers to its employees in exchange for their skills, capabilities, and contributions. Candidate experience: the sum of all interactions that a job candidate has with an organization during the recruitment process. Social media and online presence: using social media and other digital platforms to enhance the organization's employer brand and attract candidates. Diversity, equity, and inclusion: creating a workplace culture that is inclusive and values diversity. Overall, personnel marketing aims to create a positive and compelling employer brand that attracts and retains talented employees, thereby contributing to the organization's success.

data.name: Personnel Selection
data.description: Personnel selection is the process of evaluating job candidates and making decisions about who to hire for a particular job. It is a crucial part of human resource management and involves various methods and techniques to assess the knowledge, skills, and abilities of candidates. The main goal of personnel selection is to identify the most qualified candidate for a job while ensuring fairness and objectivity in the selection process. Topics within personnel selection include: Job analysis: This involves identifying the knowledge, skills, and abilities required for a specific job and developing job descriptions. Recruitment: This involves attracting a pool of qualified candidates for a job through various sources such as job postings, social media, and employee referrals. Screening: This involves reviewing resumes, conducting initial phone interviews, and assessing whether candidates meet the minimum requirements for the job. Selection tests: These can include cognitive ability tests, personality tests, and job simulation exercises to assess a candidate's knowledge, skills, and abilities. Interviews: These can be structured or unstructured and can involve behavioral questions or situational questions to assess a candidate's fit for the job. Background checks: These involve verifying a candidate's education, work history, and other relevant information. Decision making: This involves evaluating all the information gathered during the selection process and making a decision about which candidate to hire. In research, personnel selection is a well-studied area of organizational psychology and human resource management. Researchers investigate the effectiveness of different selection methods and techniques, the fairness and validity of selection processes, and the impact of personnel selection on employee outcomes such as job satisfaction and performance.

data.name: Cognitive Dissonance
data.description: Cognitive dissonance, in the field of psychology, refers to the psychological discomfort or tension that arises from holding conflicting beliefs, attitudes, or values, or from engaging in behaviors that contradict one's beliefs or self-image. When individuals experience cognitive dissonance, they are motivated to reduce the discomfort by altering their beliefs, attitudes, or behaviors to restore consistency.

data.name: Milgram Experiment
data.description: The Milgram Experiment, conducted by social psychologist Stanley Milgram in the 1960s, aimed to examine the willingness of individuals to obey authority figures, even when their actions may harm others. The study involved participants acting as "teachers" who were instructed to administer electric shocks to a "learner" whenever they answered a question incorrectly. In reality, the shocks were fake, and the learner was an actor. The experiment revealed the significant influence of authority and situational factors on human behavior. It demonstrated that a considerable number of participants were willing to administer potentially harmful shocks to others simply because they were instructed to do so by an authority figure. The findings raised ethical concerns regarding the well-being of participants and the power of authority in shaping human behavior.

data.name: Attribution Theory
data.description: Attribution theory is a field of psychology that examines how individuals explain the causes of behavior, both their own behavior and the behavior of others. It focuses on the cognitive processes involved in making attributions and understanding the underlying reasons and motivations behind actions. Attribution theory explores how people assign causal explanations to events and behaviors, and how these attributions influence emotions, judgments, and interpersonal interactions.

data.name: Political Ethics
data.description: Political ethics is the practice of making moral judgements about political action and political agents.

data.name: Public Accounting
data.description: Public accounting refers to a business or individual who helps a range of clients, from individuals to corporations, prepare financial documents. Certified public accountants, or CPAs, act as a third party to review the financials of a company for public disclosure.

data.name: Organization Theory
data.description: Organizational theory refers to a series of interrelated concepts that involve the sociological study of the structures and operations of formal social organizations. Organizational theory also seeks to explain how interrelated units of organization either connect or do not connect with each other.

data.name: Privatisation
data.description: Privatization refers to the transfer of government service or assets to the private sector. The assets owned by the government may be sold to the private sector or statutory restrictions on competition between publicly and privately owned enterprises may be lifted.

data.name: Lobbying
data.description: Lobbying” means communicating with any official in the legislative or executive branch for the purpose of attempting to influence legislative or administrative action or a ballot issue.

data.name: Performance Management
data.description: Performance management is an ongoing process of communication between a supervisor and an employee that occurs throughout the year, in support of accomplishing the strategic objectives of the organization.

data.name: Global Governance
data.description: Global governance refers to the complex of institutions, mechanisms, relationships, and processes between and among states, nonstate actors, markets, citizens, and organizations that articulate collective interests on the global plane, establish rights and obligations, and mediate differences.

data.name: Civil Service/Bureaucracy
data.description: The civil service is a collective term for a sector of government composed mainly of career civil servants hired rather than appointed or elected, whose institutional tenure typically survives transitions of political leadership. The term bureaucracy refers to a complex organization that has multilayered systems and processes. The systems and processes that are put in place effectively make decision-making slow. They are designed to maintain uniformity and control within the organization.

data.name: Non-Profit Organisations
data.description: A nonprofit organization (NPO) or non-profit organization, also known as a non-business entity, or nonprofit institution, is a legal entity organized and operated for a collective, public or social benefit, in contrary with an entity that operates as a business aiming to generate a profit for its owners.

data.name: Discourse Research
data.description: Discourse research is a research approach in sociology that focuses on analyzing language use and communication practices to understand how meaning is constructed and power relations are enacted within social contexts. It examines the ways in which language, both written and spoken, shapes and is shaped by social structures, identities, and cultural norms.

data.name: Federalism
data.description: Federalism is a combined and compound mode of government that combines a general government (the central or "federal" government) with regional governments (provincial, state, cantonal, territorial, or other sub-unit governments) in a single political system, dividing the powers between the two.

data.name: Party Research
data.description: Party Research studies political parties, their organization, behavior, and role in the political system, including their impact on elections, governance, and public policy.

data.name: Third Sector Research
data.description: The third sector includes charities, social enterprises and volunteer groups, and aims to deliver essential services, help to improve people's well-being and contributes to economic growth.

data.name: History of Political Thought
data.description: History of Political Thought examines the development and evolution of political ideas, theories, and philosophies throughout history, exploring their impact on political systems and societies.

data.name: Constructivism Theory in Political Science
data.description: Constructivism Theory in Political Science posits that international relations and political outcomes are shaped by social constructs, such as identities, norms, and beliefs, rather than solely by material factors.

data.name: Transcultural Comparative Political Theory
data.description: Transcultural Comparative Political Theory examines political ideas and theories across different cultures, comparing and contrasting them to understand diverse political thought and practices.

data.name: Cyber Politics
data.description: How politicians and political parties use the internet/online spaces for various activities including election campaigns, keeping in touch with constituents, and forging alliances with other groups or individuals. The internet may also enable small groups with limited resources to participate in the political process.

subjects.term: POLITICAL SCIENCE / Political Process / Media & Internet
Media studies: internet, digital media and society

data.name: Citizenship
data.description: Citizenship is an allegiance of a person to a state. Each state determines the conditions under which it will recognize persons as citizens, and the conditions under which that status will be withdrawn.

data.name: String Theory
data.description: String theory is a theoretical framework in which the point-like particles of particle physics are replaced by one-dimensional objects called strings. It is a theory of quantum gravity.

subjects.term: Quantum physics (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory)

data.name: Social Economy
data.description: The term 'social economy' refers to all business activities that are not only driven by a strong social mission but also intended to be economically viable.

data.name: Social Area
data.description: Social Area Analysis is a field of study within social work that focuses on examining and understanding the social dynamics, structures, and characteristics of specific geographic areas or communities. It involves analyzing various aspects of the community, such as its demographics, resources, social interactions, and community development. Social area analysis helps social workers gain insights into the unique challenges, strengths, and needs of communities, which can inform the design and implementation of effective social interventions.

data.name: Critical Social Work
data.description: Critical social work is a field of study within social work that focuses on challenging and addressing structural inequalities, power imbalances, and social injustices. It aims to promote social change, advocate for marginalized populations, and advance social justice through a critical examination of social systems, policies, and practices.

data.name: Domestic and Sexual Violence
data.description: Domestic and sexual violence is a subfield of social work that focuses on addressing and preventing interpersonal violence within the context of intimate relationships and sexual encounters. It involves providing support, advocacy, and interventions for individuals and communities affected by domestic and sexual violence, as well as working towards creating social change to eliminate such violence.

subjects.term: Family violence. Domestic violence. Conjugal violence
Sexual practices outside of social norms. Paraphilias

data.name: Social Work and Gender
data.description: Social work and gender is a field of study within social work that focuses on understanding and addressing the ways in which gender influences social structures, relationships, and individual experiences. It involves promoting gender equality, challenging gender-based discrimination and oppression, and supporting individuals, families, and communities in achieving gender justice and empowerment.

data.name: Social Work and Migration
data.description: Social work and migration is a field of study within social work that focuses on understanding and addressing the unique challenges and needs of individuals, families, and communities affected by migration. It involves providing support, advocacy, and interventions to promote the well-being and social inclusion of migrants, refugees, and displaced populations.

data.name: Sport Physiology
data.description: Sport physiology is the study of how exercise alters the function and structure of the body (physical and biomechanical), by applying concepts from the medical fields of Anatomy (the study of basic bodily structure and the interrelationships between various body parts) and Physiology (the study of the processes or functions of living things, or the study of body functions) to a context of sports and exercise. It is primarily the study of how the body adapts physiologically to the acute or short term stress of exercise, and the chronic or long term stress of physical training, but also specifically focuses at the athletes training and enhancing athlete performance within a specific sport.

data.name: Sport Career
data.description: Sport Career primarily  refers to the career of an athlete, but might also refer to the occupational career of a person working in a wider context of sport. A career or professional career is the personal career of a person in his or her professional life. While the term career is generally understood to designate a change in qualification and income and is therefore related to social and economic upwards mobility, Sport Careers are similarly linked to the accumulation of accomplishments in sports and accompanying opportunities.

data.name: Fitness and Exercise Culture
data.description: Fitness and Exercise Culture refers to the cultural and social factors and effects of fitness and physical exercise and is concerned with the ways in which people attribute meaning to sports activities through shared and culturally prescribed interpretative patterns.  It covers sports as a mass phenomenon and generally recognised and commerzialised types of sport, as well as communities of less popular and/or special and distinctive types of sport. This includes Lifestyle-, Health- and aesthetic aspects.

data.name: Sports Nutrition
data.description: Sports Nutrition is an interdisciplinary field of study concerned with the understanding of the body's use of nutrients during athletic competition (and the need for nutritional supplements), as well as the practical use of proper nutrition and dietary supplements to enhance athletic performance. Works in the field of Sports Nutrition commonly apply knowledge nutrition science, dietology, biochemistry, exercise physiology, cell and molecular biology. For instance, studies in Sports Nutrition focus on the different types and quantities of fluids and food taken by an athlete, and also deals with the consumption of nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, supplements and organic substances that include carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

data.name: Fitness
data.description: Fitness is generally understood as physical and also mental well-being. Altough being a vague concept without any measurable determinants, there are different factors contributing to overall fitness. In medicine, fitness refers to the physical, mental and emotional general condition of a person in relation to the performance demands placed on them from outside. From this perspective, fitness is affected by physical performance potential, intelligence, emotional stability, state of the immune system, reproducibility and Adaptability in case of lack of resources.

data.name: Disability Sport
data.description: Disability Sport refers to the aim to guarantee full participation of disabled persons (including physical and intellectual disabilities) into sport life, as practising sport not only covers the therapeutic and medical intentions generally defined as treatment, but also the social and educational aspects. Accordingly, disability sports or parasports, are sports played by persons with a disability (physical, mental, permanent and temporary). As many disabled sports are based on existing able bodied sports, modified to meet the needs of persons with a disability, they are sometimes referred to as adapted/adaptive sports.

data.name: Sport Orthopaedics
data.description: Sport Orthopaedics is a medical subspecialty of Orthopedics and Sports medicine. It focuses on the investigation, preservation, restoration and health care in general pertaining structures of the musculoskeletal system affected by athletic activity. Activities of Sport Othopedics include diagnosis of your injury or disorder, Treatment with medication, exercise, surgery or other treatment plans, rehabilitation through exercises or physical therapy to restore movement, strength and function, as well as prevention of injury or deceleration of progressing diseases.

data.name: Modernism
data.description: Modernism refers to a cultural and intellectual movement that emerged in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is characterized by a break from traditional forms and conventions, embracing innovation, experimentation, and a critical examination of established norms and beliefs. Modernism can be observed in various fields such as art, literature, architecture, music, and philosophy.

data.name: Postmodern Literature
data.description: Postmodern literature refers to a literary movement that emerged in the mid-20th century as a response and departure from the principles of modernism. It is characterized by a playful, self-reflexive, and fragmented narrative style that often challenges traditional notions of authorship, meaning, and reality. Postmodern literature often incorporates elements of intertextuality, metafiction, irony, and cultural references.

data.name: Individual Sport
data.description: Individual Sport is any sport which is practiced either by a single person (e.g. running) or by two opposing individuals (e.g. tennis). Competition in individual sports is also characterised by competing individuals rather than competing in teams. This allows athletes to aim for personal goals and has various effects on training strategies, tactics and the overall significance and prominence of individual athletes in individual sports.

data.name: Team Sport
data.description: Team sport includes any sport where individuals are organized into opposing teams of two or more members interacting directly and simultaneously in competition to win. The team members act together toward a shared objective and usually fulfill different roles and take positions with specific tasks and functions during a game. Examples of team sports are soccer, basketball, baseball, rugby or hockey.

data.name: Cell Cycle Analysis
data.description: Cell cycle analysis is a scientific method used to study and quantify the different phases of the cell cycle in a population of cells. The cell cycle refers to the series of events that occur in a cell, leading to its growth, division, and duplication of genetic material. By analyzing the cell cycle, researchers can gain insights into cell proliferation, cell cycle regulation, and the effects of various treatments or conditions on cell division.

data.name: Behavioral Methods
data.description: Behavioural methods are methods used to study the neural, molecular, genetic or physiological mechanisms that underlie behaviour in humans or other animals (the field of behavioural neuroscience), or methods used to study the psychology of behaviour.

subjects.term: Auxiliary techniques and procedures; apparatus, equipment, procedures
Methods of research. Technique. Experimental biology

data.name: Epigenomics
data.description: Epigenomics is the systematic analysis of epigenetics at the genome level, ie. the global state of gene expression not attributable to mutational changes in the underlying DNA genome. An organism has multiple, cell type-specific, epigenomes comprising epigenetic marks such as DNA methylation, histone modification and specifically positioned nucleosomes.

data.name: Children, Youth and Media
data.description: Multidisciplinary perspectives on a wide range of research topics, addressing children and youth from infancy to young adulthood, whether framed in terms of child and adolescent psychosocial development, critical constructions of ‘youth’, cultural analyses of childhood in diverse settings, media effects or media design issues.

data.name: Communication of Non-Profit Organizations
data.description: Nonprofit communications encompasses a wide range of tools that organizations can use to get their message across.

data.name: Mixed Methods
data.description: Mixed methods in sociology refer to research approaches that integrate both quantitative and qualitative methods to gain a comprehensive understanding of social phenomena. Rather than relying solely on one type of data, mixed methods research combines numerical data and statistical analysis with qualitative data and interpretive analysis.

data.name: Sociological Quantitative Methods
data.description: Sociological quantitative methods are research techniques that analyze numerical data in order to understand social patterns, relationships, and trends. It encompasses methods such as surveys, experiments, and statistical analysis.

data.name: Sociological Qualitative Methods
data.description: Sociological qualitative methods refer to a range of research approaches used in sociology to gather and analyze qualitative data for the purpose of understanding social phenomena. These methods emphasize the collection of non-numerical, in-depth, and descriptive data to explore social processes, meanings, and experiences.

data.name: Sociology of Work
data.description: Denotes social relations, behaviors, experiences and normative codes around work and working lives of people in society. The sociology of work cross-cuts discussions on gender, age, ethnicity, education, race, migration and globalization.

subjects.term: Industrial sociology. Social conditions of labor

data.name: Sociology of Political Insitutions
data.description: Political institutions can be defined as entities within a society that create, enforce, and make laws.  For example, the court system is a political institution, so is a head of state or head of government.  Political parties and unions are also considered political institutions.

data.name: Research on Associations
data.description: Associations are groups of persons banded together for a specific purpose.

data.name: Societal Psychology
data.description: Societal Psychology is a branch of psychology that studies the impact of socio-cultural and political factors on individual and group behavior. This field seeks to understand how broader societal contexts shape cognition, emotion, and motivation, as well as how psychological processes influence the development of social structures and cultural norms.

data.name: Sociology of Architecture
data.description: Sociology of architecture is the sociological study of the built environment and the role and occupation of architects in modern societies.

data.name: Sociology of the Financial Market
data.description: Sociology of the Financial Market is a subfield of sociology that examines the social structures, interactions, and institutions within financial markets to understand how market participants and organizations influence economic transactions and outcomes. This field explores the relationships between social and economic factors in the functioning of financial markets and the impacts of financial events on society at large.

data.name: Convention Theory
data.description: Convention theory is a sociological framework that examines how social norms, conventions, and institutions shape individual and collective behavior, focusing on the social coordination of actions, the formation of expectations, and the evaluation of performance in various social contexts.

data.name: Sociology of Literature
data.description: The sociology of literature is an interdisciplinary subfield of the sociology of culture. It examines the relationship between literature and society by studying the social production of literature and its social implications. It analyses how literature reflects, influences, and is influenced by social structures, cultural norms, historical contexts, and the collective consciousness of a given society. This subfield of sociology explores how literary works, such as novels, poems, plays, and other forms of creative expression, can serve as a mirror of societal values, beliefs, and conflicts, while also shaping public discourse and contributing to social change. Scholars in this area may investigate topics such as the role of literature in constructing identities, representations of social issues, the reception and interpretation of literary texts by different social groups, and the impact of literary movements on social thought and movements.

data.name: Sociology of Music
data.description: Sociology of Music is a subfield of sociology that examines the social and cultural aspects of music, including the production, consumption, and distribution of music and the ways in which music shapes and is shaped by society. Key areas of study include the role of music in identity formation, social interaction, and political expression.

data.name: Sociology of Film
data.description: Sociology of Film is a branch of sociology that explores the social, cultural, and political dimensions of film-making and film consumption. This includes the study of the film industry, production techniques, audience reception, and the representation of social issues and identities in cinema.

data.name: Sociology of Consumption
data.description: Sociology of Consumption is a subfield of sociology that investigates the social and cultural aspects of consumer behavior, the meanings attached to goods and services, and the relationship between consumption patterns and social organization. This field examines the role of consumption in shaping social identities, values, and relationships, as well as the implications of consumer culture for sustainability, well-being, and social inequality.

data.name: Rural Sociology
data.description: Rural sociology is a field of sociology traditionally associated with the study of social structure and conflict in rural areas.

data.name: Sociology of Migration
data.description: The sociology of immigration involves the sociological analysis of immigration, particularly with respect to race and ethnicity, social structure, and political policy. Important concepts include assimilation, enculturation, marginalization, multiculturalism, postcolonialism, transnationalism and social cohesion.

data.name: Lymphatic Vessels
data.description: Lymphatic vessels are thin, tubular structures with valve-like openings that collect lymph from the tissues and transport it throughout the body. Afferent lymphatics deliver lymph from tissues into lymph nodes, whereas efferent lymphatics bring the filtered lymph away from the lymph node. Lymphocytes also circulate via the lymphatic vessels.

data.name: Utilitarianism
data.description: Collection of normative theories advocating for actions that maximize utility and well-being for all (or as many as possible) persons these actions concern.

data.name: Deontological Approaches
data.description: Deontology is a set of normative theories that suggest morality of an action should be based on whether that action itself is right or wrong under a series of rules.

data.name: Mathematical Logic in Philosophy
data.description: Mathematical logic, also known as symbolic logic or formal logic, plays a crucial role in philosophy as a tool for rigorous analysis and investigation of philosophical concepts and arguments. It is a branch of logic that uses mathematical methods and symbolic notation to study formal systems of reasoning.

data.name: Humanism
data.description: Humanism is a philosophical and ethical approach that emphasizes the inherent value and worth of human beings, their dignity, and their potential for personal growth and fulfillment. Humanism places the focus on human reason, ethics, and the value of human experience in understanding and shaping the world. It encompasses a range of perspectives and variations, including secular humanism and religious humanism.

data.name: Indigenous Education
