data.description: Indigenous education refers to the education of Indigenous peoples, which involves recognizing and valuing their cultural, linguistic, and traditional knowledge systems. It aims to address historical injustices, promote self-determination, and support the educational success and well-being of Indigenous students.

data.name: Multicultural Education
data.description: Multicultural education refers to an approach to education that recognizes and values the diversity of cultures, languages, backgrounds, and perspectives within a society. It aims to create inclusive and equitable learning environments that promote understanding, respect, and appreciation for cultural differences.

data.name: Citizenship Education
data.description: Citizenship education, also known as civic education or civic engagement, refers to the process of equipping individuals with the knowledge, skills, and values necessary to actively participate in their communities, societies, and the broader world as informed and responsible citizens. It aims to foster an understanding of democratic principles, human rights, social justice, and civic responsibilities.

data.name: Environmental Ecojustice
data.description: Environmental justice is the fair treatment and meaningful involvement of all people, regardless of race, color, national origin, or income, with respect to the development, implementation, and enforcement of environmental laws, regulations, and policies.

data.name: eLearning
data.description: eLearning, also known as electronic learning or online learning, refers to the use of digital technologies to deliver educational content and facilitate learning experiences. It involves the use of electronic devices, internet connectivity, and various digital tools and platforms to deliver educational materials, interact with instructors and peers, and complete learning activities.

data.name: Baroque
data.description: Baroque is an artistic and cultural style that emerged in Europe during the 17th century, flourishing until the mid-18th century. It is characterized by grandeur, ornate details, dramatic expression, and a sense of movement. The Baroque style is found in various art forms, including architecture, painting, sculpture, music, literature, and theater.

data.name: Literature of the Enlightenment
data.description: The Literature of Enlightenment refers to the body of writing produced during the Enlightenment that championed reason, critical inquiry, and the questioning of traditional authority. It includes philosophical, political, and literary works that sought to promote individual freedom, scientific thinking, and social reform.

data.name: Baltic Literature
data.description: Baltic literature refers to the body of literature produced in the Baltic states, which include Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. Baltic literature encompasses works written in the native languages of these countries, namely Estonian, Latvian, and Lithuanian, as well as literature produced by Baltic authors in other languages. Baltic literature holds a rich and diverse cultural heritage, often shaped by historical, social, and political contexts.

data.name: Life Writing
data.description: This genre encompasses autobiography, biography and other accounts of personal experience and memory, such as memoir, diaries, letters, testimonies, personal essays and digital forms like blogs and email.

data.name: Epic
data.description: In literature, an epic is a genre of narrative poetry that typically tells a long and grandiose story of heroic deeds and adventures. Epics often focus on the actions of legendary or mythological heroes, exploring themes of courage, heroism, honor, and the struggle between good and evil.

data.name: Short Story
data.description: a story with a fully developed theme but significantly shorter and less elaborate than a novel.

data.name: Mathematical Teaching Skills
data.description: Mathematics provides an effective way of building mental discipline and encourages logical reasoning and mental rigor. In addition, mathematical knowledge plays a crucial role in understanding the contents of other school subjects such as science, social studies, and even music and art. Mathematics teaching is the act of imparting mathematical knowledge, methods, calculations, computational techniques etc by someone( teacher) to another. It may be formal in an educational setting or informal. Mathematics is a fundamental part of human thought and logic, and integral to attempts at understanding the world and ourselves.

data.name: Bilingualism
data.description: The ability to speak and understand two languages fluently. Bilingual individuals are proficient in two languages and can effectively communicate, comprehend, read, and write in both languages.

data.name: Spanish
data.description: Spanish, also known as Español, is a Romance language spoken primarily in Spain and throughout many countries in Latin America. Spanish originated from Vulgar Latin and shares similarities with other Romance languages, such as Italian, French, and Portuguese. Standard Spanish, known as "Español estándar" or "Castilian Spanish," is based on the variety spoken in the central region of Spain, particularly around Madrid.

data.name: Portuguese
data.description: Portuguese is a Romance language spoken primarily in Portugal, Brazil, and several other countries and regions around the world. Portuguese evolved from Vulgar Latin and shares similarities with other Romance languages such as Spanish, Italian, and French. However, it has its own distinct features, vocabulary, and pronunciation.

data.name: Morphology
data.description: In linguistics, morphology is the study of words, how they are formed, and their relationship to other words in the same language. It analyzes the structure of words and parts of words such as stems, root words, prefixes, and suffixes. Morphology also looks at parts of speech, intonation and stress, and the ways context can change a word's pronunciation and meaning.

data.name: Polish
data.description: Polish is a West Slavic language spoken primarily in Poland, where it is the official language. Polish belongs to the Indo-European language family and shares similarities with other Slavic languages such as Czech, Slovak, and Russian. Polish uses the Latin alphabet with additional diacritical marks to represent specific sounds.

data.name: Hungarian
data.description: Hungarian is a Uralic language spoken primarily in Hungary and by Hungarian communities in neighboring countries. It is not related to the Indo-European language family that includes most European languages. Hungarian is unique in its linguistic structure and has no close linguistic relatives.  It also has a rich vocabulary, influenced by various languages throughout its history, including Turkic, Slavic, German, and Latin.

data.name: Syntax
data.description: In linguistics, syntax is the study of how words and morphemes combine to form larger units such as phrases and sentences.

data.name: Language Disorders
data.description: Language disorders, also known as communication disorders, refer to conditions or impairments that affect an individual's ability to understand, produce, or use language effectively.

data.name: Latin
data.description: Latin is an ancient Indo-European language that was spoken by the Romans and used as the lingua franca throughout the Roman Empire. It is no longer a spoken language in its classical form, but it has had a profound influence on the development of many modern languages(such as Italian, Spanish, French, Portuguese).

data.name: Dialectology
data.description: The analysis and description of regional or social varieties of a language, including their phonological, morphological, syntactic, and lexical features. Dialectologists investigate the distribution, boundaries, and characteristics of dialects within a particular language or language family.

data.name: Language and Youth
data.description: The language practices, patterns, and variations among young people. It examines how language is used by and with youth, and how youth language reflects their identities, social interactions, and cultural affiliations. Language and youth research sheds light on the unique linguistic features, trends, and dynamics of language use in youth communities.

data.name: Technical Languages
data.description: The specialized terminology and language used within a particular field or domain. It consists of words, phrases, and concepts that are specific to a specific profession, industry, or area of expertise. Technical language is designed to communicate precise and specific information effectively within a particular field, often involving complex and specialized knowledge. such as Medical Terminology, Scientific Terminology, Computer Programming Languages

data.name: Variation Linguistics
data.description: Variation linguistics, also known as sociolinguistic variation, is a subfield of linguistics that focuses on the systematic study of language variation and its social, cultural, and contextual factors. It investigates how language varies across different speakers, regions, social groups, and situations, and explores the underlying factors that influence this variation.

data.name: Food Production
data.description: Food production is the process of converting raw materials into finished food products. The finished food or converted food items are used either in homes or food processing industries. Food is vital for the human body to continue its basic life processes, providing energy and nutrition. Food production provides a stable source of employment, plays an important role in local economies, contributes to innovation in the food system, responds to increased demand for exports, contributes to food affordability, addresses consumer demand.

data.name: Media Philosophy
data.description: Media philosophy, also known as philosophy of media or philosophy of communication, is an interdisciplinary field that explores the philosophical aspects of media, technology, and communication. It investigates the nature, role, and impact of media in society, as well as the philosophical implications of media technologies and their relationship with human experience, knowledge, and culture.

data.name: Humour
data.description: The quality or ability to provoke amusement, laughter, or enjoyment. It involves the use of wit, irony, wordplay, or comedic elements to create a sense of amusement or entertainment. Humour is a subjective and cultural phenomenon, as what may be funny to one person or in one culture may not be funny to another.

data.name: Feminism and Feminist Theory
data.description: Feminist theory, also known as feminism, is the belief in the full economic, political, and social equality of the genders.

data.name: Transcendentalism
data.description: Transcendentalism is a philosophical and literary movement that emerged in the United States during the mid-19th century. It was influenced by various intellectual and cultural trends, including Romanticism, Unitarianism, and German Idealism. Transcendentalists sought to explore the relationship between individual spirituality, nature, and the divine, emphasizing the inherent goodness of both humanity and the natural world. In other words, idea that individuals can transcend or go beyond the physical and material world through intuition, insight, and spiritual experience.

data.name: Computational Cosmology
data.description: "Computational Cosmology” is the modeling of structure formation in the Universe by means of numerical simulations. These simulations can be considered as the only “experiment” to verify theories of the origin and evolution of the Universe.

data.name: Heliospheric Physics
data.description: Heliophysics (from the prefix "helio", from Attic Greek hḗlios, meaning Sun, and the noun "physics": the science of matter and energy and their interactions) is the physics of the Sun and its connection with the Solar System.

data.name: LED
data.description: LEDs (light emitting diodes) convert an electrical current into light using spontaneous emission in optically active semiconductors.

data.name: Bioinspired Robotics
data.description: Bioinspired robotics, also known as biomimetic or biologically inspired robotics, is a field of robotics that draws inspiration from biological systems and organisms to design and develop robotic systems. Researchers in this field aim to replicate the functional principles, structures, and behaviors found in nature to create robots that can perform tasks more efficiently, adapt to diverse environments, and interact with the natural world.

data.name: Biomedical Micro Devices
data.description: Devices operating at the microscale for biomedical applications including electronic or mechanical functions

data.name: Wearable Technology
data.description: Wearable technology is any kind of electronic device designed to be worn on the user's body.

data.name: Computational Solid Mechanics
data.description: It  focuses on using computational methods, numerical analysis, and computer simulations to study and solve problems related to the behavior and performance of solid materials and structures. It involves the application of mathematical models, algorithms, and computer programming to analyze the mechanical response and deformation of solids under various loading and boundary conditions.

data.name: Mechanics of Solid and Soft Tissue
data.description: The mechanics of solid and soft tissue is a field of study that focuses on understanding the mechanical behavior and properties of biological tissues, including both rigid (solid) and deformable (soft) materials. It involves the application of principles from mechanics, materials science, and engineering to investigate how tissues respond to external forces and deformations.

synonyms: Mechanik für Weichteilgewebe und festes Gewebe

data.name: Ornithology
data.description: Ornithology is the branch of zoology that focuses on the study of birds, encompassing their physiology, behavior, ecology, evolution, and conservation. This scientific discipline involves the observation and analysis of avian species, their habitats, migration patterns, reproductive strategies, and interactions with ecosystems. Ornithologists employ various research methods, including field studies, laboratory experiments, and the use of technology such as bird banding and tracking devices, to gather data and enhance understanding of bird life. The field plays a crucial role in biodiversity conservation, as birds are key indicators of environmental health and are often affected by habitat loss, climate change, and human activities. Ornithology also intersects with other scientific fields, such as ecology, conservation biology, and environmental science, contributing to a holistic understanding of avian species and their roles in the natural world.

data.name: Malacology
data.description: Malacology is the study of molluscs, a large and spectacularly diverse group of soft-bodied, invertebrate animals.

data.name: Mammalogy
data.description: Mammalogy is the study of mammals – a class of vertebrates with characteristics such as homeothermic metabolism, fur, four-chambered hearts, and complex nervous systems.

data.name: Primatology
data.description: Primatology is the scientific study of non-human primates, including their behavior, biology, evolution, and conservation. This interdisciplinary field encompasses various aspects of primate life, such as social structures, communication, cognition, and ecological roles. Primatologists employ methods from anthropology, biology, psychology, and ecology to understand the complexities of primate species, which range from lemurs and monkeys to apes and humans' closest relatives. The research in primatology not only aims to enhance our understanding of primate species but also addresses critical issues related to their conservation and the impact of human activities on their habitats. By studying primates, scientists gain insights into evolutionary processes, social dynamics, and the origins of human behavior.

data.name: Animal Agriculture
data.description: Animal Agriculture is the branch of agriculture concerned with animals that are raised for meat, fibre, milk, or other products. It includes day-to-day care, selective breeding, and the raising of livestock.

data.name: Animal Anatomy
data.description: Animal Histology, Animal Morphology.  Animal anatomy is the study of the structure of animals, including the internal structure of organs, muscles, bones, and other tissues.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Life Sciences / Anatomy & Physiology (see also Life Sciences / Human Anatomy & Physiology)

data.name: Veterinary Epidemiology
data.description: Veterinary epidemiology is a branch of epidemiology that focuses on the study of diseases and health-related issues in animal populations. It involves the investigation of the occurrence, distribution, and determinants of diseases among animals, as well as the development of strategies to prevent and control these diseases. Veterinary epidemiology plays a crucial role in animal health management, public health, and the understanding of disease dynamics in various animal species.

data.name: Fish and Wildlife Biology
data.description: Fish and wildlife biology, also known as fish and wildlife management or fisheries and wildlife science, is a field of study that focuses on the biology, ecology, conservation, and management of fish and wildlife species and their habitats. It involves understanding the life histories, behavior, population dynamics, and ecological interactions of various species, as well as the application of scientific principles to ensure their conservation and sustainable use.

data.name: .NET
data.description: Software development framework from Microsoft, part of Visual Studio. .NET is a free, open-source, cross-platform framework developed by Microsoft that serves as a platform for building and running a wide range of applications.

subjects.term: Software development in specific programming languages

data.name: Windows
data.description: Proprietary client and server operating system from Microsoft with desktop. "Windows" refers to the Microsoft Windows operating system, which is a family of operating systems developed and marketed by Microsoft Corporation. Windows is one of the most widely used and recognizable operating systems in the world, providing a graphical user interface (GUI) and support for various applications and hardware devices.

subjects.term: Software development for specific operating systems

data.name: Industry 4.0
data.description: Industrial subset of the fourth industrial revolution, smart manufacturing, smart factory, industrial internet of things, sensor data collection and processing

data.name: Smart Infrastructure
data.description: Intelligent interconnection of energy systems, buildings and industry platforms incl. the control thereof by collecting and processing the generated data

data.name: IT Security Awareness
data.description: Knowledge and attitude regarding IT security aspects. The level of understanding and consciousness that individuals and organizations have about potential security threats and best practices to protect information technology (IT) systems and data. It involves educating users and employees about the importance of cybersecurity and fostering a security-conscious culture within an organization. IT Security Awareness aims to promote responsible behaviors and actions to mitigate risks and prevent security breaches.

data.name: Dangerous Chemical Goods
data.description: Dangerous Chemical Goods are substances that when transported are a risk to health, safety, property or the environment.

data.name: Penology
data.description: Penology refers to the study of punishment and correctional systems as a means of controlling and preventing crime. It involves examining the theories, practices, and institutions involved in the management of offenders, their treatment, and the overall goal of maintaining social order.

data.name: Complex Fluids
data.description: Complex fluids are mixtures that have a coexistence between two phases: solid–liquid (suspensions or solutions of macromolecules such as polymers), solid–gas (granular), liquid–gas (foams) or liquid–liquid (emulsions). They exhibit unusual mechanical responses to applied stress or strain due to the geometrical constraints that the phase coexistence imposes. The mechanical response includes transitions between solid-like and fluid-like behavior as well as fluctuations. Their mechanical properties can be attributed to characteristics such as high disorder, caging, and clustering on multiple length scales.

data.name: Canadian Politics
data.description: The politics of Canada function within a framework of parliamentary democracy and a federal system of parliamentary government with strong democratic traditions.[1] Canada is a constitutional monarchy, in which the monarch is head of state. In practice, the executive powers are directed by the Cabinet, a committee of ministers of the Crown responsible to the elected House of Commons of Canada and chosen and headed by the Prime Minister of Canada.

data.name: Interpersonal Communication
data.description: Interpersonal Communication is the study of direct, often face-to-face or small-group interactions, focusing on relational processes, nonverbal behavior, emotional expression, and the co-construction of meaning between individuals.

data.name: Earth and Environmental Modelling
data.description: Earth and Environmental Modelling refers to the use of mathematical models and simulations to understand and predict natural processes and systems on Earth. These models help analyze environmental changes and make informed decisions for environmental protection and resource management.

data.name: Educational Inequality
data.description: Critical Race Theory in Education is an interdisciplinary framework that examines how race and racism influence educational systems, policies, and practices

subjects.term: SOCIAL SCIENCE / Social Classes & Economic Disparity
Educational equalization. Right to education. Compensatory education

data.name: Adolescent Medicine
data.description: Adolescent Medicine is a specialized field of healthcare focused on the physical, mental, and emotional well-being of individuals during the adolescent years (typically ages 10-19) and young adulthood, encompassing a wide range of health concerns and promoting healthy transitions into adulthood.

subjects.term: Paediatric medicine / child and adolescent medicine

data.name: Screen Music and Sound
data.description: Screen Music and Sound means the composition of sound and music for screen-based media like TV, film, and video games.

data.name: Postcolonial Studies
data.description: Postcolonial Studies is an academic field that examines the effects of colonialism on cultures and societies. It looks at the lasting impacts of colonization, such as cultural identity, power dynamics, and economic disparities, and how these legacies continue to shape the world today. This field challenges Eurocentric narratives and highlights the voices and experiences of previously colonized peoples. It's about understanding and addressing historical injustices and their ongoing repercussions.

data.name: Sociology of Everyday Life
data.description: Sociology of everyday life zeroes in on the mundane, daily activities and interactions that shape human experience. It's all about the routines, habits, and social norms that occur without much notice but profoundly influence our existence. From a casual chat with a neighbor to how we navigate public spaces, this branch of sociology digs into what makes the ordinary so significant.

data.name: Animal Sociology
data.description: Animal sociology studies the social behaviors, interactions, and structures within animal species. It looks at how animals form communities, communicate, establish hierarchies, and cooperate or compete.

data.name: Media Economics
data.description: Economic aspects of the media system, especially from a communication science perspective: media economics is thus not limited to the consideration of economic aspects of the media system, but also considers the consequences of economization for the entire communication and information system of a society

data.name: Rehabilitation Medicine
data.description: Physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R), also known as physiatry or rehabilitation medicine, is a branch of medicine aiming to enhance and restore functional ability and quality of life to those with physical impairments or disabilities affecting the brain, spinal cord, nerves, bones, joints, ligaments, muscles, and tendons.

data.name: Aesthetic Surgery
data.description: Aesthetic Surgery is a component of Plastic Surgery which applies surgical procedure to improve someone’s appearance.

data.name: Audiovisual Translation
data.description: Definition	Audiovisual translation is a specialized branch of translation which deals with the transfer of multimodal and multimedial texts into another language and/or culture.

data.name: Child and Adolescence Psychiatry
data.description: A branch of psychiatry that focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental disorders in children, adolescents, and their families.

subjects.term: Mental disorders of children and adolescents. Child psychiatry. Child mental health services

data.name: Floriculture
data.description: Floriculture is the branch of horticulture that focuses on the cultivation, breeding, and marketing of flowering and ornamental plants. This field encompasses a wide range of activities including the production of cut flowers, potted plants, bedding plants, and landscape plants, as well as the design and maintenance of floral arrangements and gardens. Floriculture plays a significant role in the agricultural economy and contributes to environmental beautification and biodiversity.

data.name: Gum Disease
data.description: Gum Disease, also known as periodontal disease, encompasses conditions affecting the gums and supporting structures of the teeth, including gingivitis and periodontitis, leading to tooth loss if untreated.

data.name: Haematological Cancer
data.description: Haematological malignancies are the types of cancer affecting blood, bone marrow and lymph nodes. They are referred to as leukaemia, lymphoma and myeloma depending on the type of cell affected. The three types of malignancies are connected through the immune system and, generally, a disease affecting one will also affect the others.

data.name: Vascular Diseases
data.description: Vascular diseases are pathological conditions affecting any of the blood vessels.

data.name: Bacterial Physiology
data.description: Bacterial physiology is a scientific discipline that concerns the life-supporting functions and processes of bacteria, which allow bacterial cells to grow and reproduce.

data.name: Neural Tube Defects
data.description: Neural tube defects result from a failure in closing of the neural tube during gastrulation, which causes congenital malformations of the spinal cord and brain. Open neural tube defects result in exposure of the brain and/or spinal cord at birth and include anencephaly, encephaloceles, hydranencephaly, iniencephaly, schizencephaly and spina bifida.

data.name: Fibromyalgia
data.description: Fibromyalgia is a rheumatic disorder characterized by chronic widespread pain, allodynia and fatigue, thought to arise from a combination of psychological, genetic, neurobiological and environmental factors.

data.name: Lipofuscin
data.description: Lipofuscin is similar to ceroid and is a type of lipochrome (deposit of lipid-rich pigment) that appears in histological examination of tissues, especially from older organisms and particularly from the eye where it can indicate macular degeneration. Lipofuscin is thought to be a product of oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids and is correlated with membrane damage.

data.name: Interspersed repetitive sequences
data.description: Interspersed repetitive sequences are identical or nearly identical DNA sequences that are scattered throughout the genome, as a result of transposition or retrotransposition events. One example is the Alu element, a sequence 300 bp that belongs to the short interspersed elements (SINE) family and is found in the genome of primates, with >1 million copies in the human genome.

data.name: Monocytes and Macrophages
data.description: Monocytes and macrophages are myeloid cells that have important innate immune functions. Macrophages reside in tissues and respond to infection by producing inflammatory mediators and engulfing bacteria. Monocytes are recruited to inflamed tissues and can produce inflammatory mediators or differentiate into macrophages. Both cells types can also promote tissue repair.

data.name: Data and Information Visualization
data.description: Data and information visualization is the practice of designing graphic or visual representations of otherwise difficult-to-understand information. It helps to understand, communicate and explore a certain field of expertise or study or other structures or correlations. It is not primarily used for imaging scientific findings, but to facilitate the comprehension and communication of these findings.

data.name: RNA Nanotechnology
data.description: RNA nanotechnology is a branch of nanotechnology concerned with the design, study and application of synthetic structures based on RNA. RNA nanotechnology takes advantage of the physical and chemical properties of RNA rather than the genetic information it carries.

data.name: Gonadal Disorders
data.description: Gonadal disorders affect the ovaries and testes. Examples include hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovary syndrome.

data.name: Epigenetics Analysis
data.description: Epigenetics analysis is the study of heritable changes that are distinct from changes in DNA sequence. Epigenetic changes include covalent modifications to the DNA bases or histone proteins that make up chromatin; they can be influenced by the environment and transmitted through DNA replication.

data.name: Somatosensory System
data.description: The somatosensory system consists of the peripheral receptors and neural pathways through which the nervous system detects and processes information about touch (mechanoception), pain (nociception), temperature (thermoception) and the position and movement of parts of the body (proprioception).

data.name: Arrhythmias
data.description: Arrhythmias are conditions in which electrical impulses are abnormally conducted through the heart, resulting in an altered heart beat (muscle contraction) rhythm. These alterations to heart beat rhythm can include changes in heart rate, irregularity of heart beats, or fibrillation of the heart muscle.

data.name: Bioethers
data.description: Bioethers, also known as oxygenated biofuels or simply ethers, are a type of biofuel that contains oxygen in its molecular structure. These compounds are derived from renewable feedstocks and are used as an alternative to conventional fossil fuels. Bioethers can be blended with gasoline or diesel fuel to enhance combustion and reduce emissions.

data.name: Neurogenic Bladder
data.description: Neurogenic bladder is loss of bladder control caused by neurological disorders, such as neural tube defects, spinal cord diseases and injury. Symptoms include urinary incontinence, renal damage and recurrent urinary tract infection.

synonyms: Neurogenic Dysfunction of the Urinary Bladder

data.name: Proteins
data.description: Proteins are biopolymers of amino acids (polypeptides), joined by peptide bonds, that are generated by ribosomes. The amino acid sequence, encoded by its gene, determines a protein's structure and function. Newly synthesized proteins can be modified by post-translational modification, altering its protein folding, stability and activity. Proteins often associate into protein-protein interaction networks for function.

data.name: Dendritic Cells
data.description: Dendritic cells (DCs) are professional antigen-presenting cells located in the skin, mucosa and lymphoid tissues. Their main function is to process antigens and present them to T cells to promote immunity to foreign antigens and tolerance to self antigens. They also secrete cytokines to regulate immune responses.

data.name: Osteopontin
data.description: Osteopontin is an acidic phosphoprotein produced by osteoblasts and other cell types. Osteopontin is an extracellular protein that has a cell-adhesion sequence (RGD) that mediates its interaction with integrins and extracellular matrix components. It has functions in biomineralization of bone, chemotaxis, apoptosis and cell activation in immunity.

data.name: Parasite Development
data.description: Parasite development is the study of all the different stages that a parasite undergoes during its life cycle, including the various changes in physiology, metabolism and physical form.

data.name: Eye Cancer
data.description: Eye cancer is an uncommon tumour that can affect the outer parts of the eye (like the eyelid) or the inside of the eyeball (intraocular cancer). The most common intraocular cancers in adults are melanoma and lymphoma, whereas the most common in children is retinoblastoma, which starts in cells of the retina.

data.name: Dictyostelium discoideum
data.description: Dictyostelium discoideum is a forest floor-dwelling amoeboid protozoan (slime mould) that serves as a model organism for studying cell biology, differentiation, chemotaxis and cell-cell interaction. Individual Dictyostelium cells grow independently but interact and assemble under starvation to form an organized multicellular organism.

data.name: Complement Cascade
data.description: The complement cascade is a biochemical process in the blood that helps or 'complements' cells of the immune system to eliminate invading pathogens. When activated by one of three pathways, a cascade of serial cleavage events results in a marked amplification of the immune response and formation of the cell-killing membrane attack complex.

data.name: Fanconi Syndrome
data.description: Fanconi syndrome is a hereditary or acquired disease of the renal proximal tubules, without primary involvement of kidney glomeruli, and is characterized by the tubular wasting of nutrients and salts, which are released into the urine. Clinical features include hypokalaemia, acidosis, hypercalciuria and proteinuria.

synonyms: Neonatal De Toni Debre Fanconi Syndrome

data.name: Marine Biology
data.description: Marine biology is the study of life in the oceans and brackish waters, which ranges from archaea and bacteria to marine mammals, and includes organisms such as corals that affect the shape of the seafloor. This may also include human modifications to ocean biology, such as fisheries or the effects of overfishing.

data.name: Acute Coronary Syndromes
data.description: Acute coronary syndromes are sudden episodes of reduced or no blood flow - and therefore oxygen delivery - to part of the heart, usually as a result of narrowing or blockage of an artery. The lack of oxygenation of the heart muscle, known as myocardial ischaemia, results in death of heart tissue.

data.name: Movement Disorders
data.description: Movement disorders are a group of neurological syndromes in which the hallmark symptom is paucity of movement, excessive and/or involuntary movement or tremor. Movement disorders can be neurodegenerative, such as Parkinson's disease and Huntington's disease, but they can also be induced by medication, infection, inflammation or trauma.

data.name: Autoimmune Diseases
data.description: Autoimmune diseases are a pathophysiological state wherein immune responses are directed against, and damage, the body's own tissues (autoimmunity). Common examples of autoimmune disease include type 1 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis and psoriasis.

data.name: Inflammatory Diseases
data.description: Inflammatory diseases include a vast array of disorders and conditions that are characterized by inflammation. Examples include allergy, asthma, autoimmune diseases, coeliac disease, glomerulonephritis, hepatitis, inflammatory bowel disease, preperfusion injury and transplant rejection.

data.name: Preventive Medicine
data.description: Preventive medicine is a type of medical treatment focused on disease prevention. This strategy could be particularly useful to treat individuals with risk factors for a disease. Strategies used include patient education, lifestyle modification, and therapeutics.

data.name: Motility Disorders
data.description: Motility disorders are characterized by abnormal movements of the gastrointestinal tract, causing the abnormal transit, slow or fast, of contents in the absence of mucosal disease or obstruction. Motility disorders can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract. Examples of motility disorders include achalasia, gastroparesis, intestinal pseudo-obstruction and faecal incontinence.

data.name: Intestinal diseases
data.description: Intestinal diseases are those that affect any segment of the intestine (small or large intestine), from the duodenum to the rectum. The term encompasses acute or chronic conditions and covers a wide range of diseases including constipation, diverticular disease and irritable bowel syndrome.

data.name: Digestive Signs and Symptoms
data.description: Digestive signs and symptoms is a term that refers to gastrointestinal manifestations of diseases. The underlying diseases are usually gastrointestinal, but can be diseases that primarily affect organs outside the gastrointestinal system.

data.name: Solitons
data.description: Solitons are waves with just a single crest. They result when a wave’s natural tendency to spread as it propagates is cancelled out by an inherently nonlinear phenomenon known as self-focusing. This means that solitons can travel a long distance whilst maintaining their same shape.

data.name: Retrovirus
data.description: A retrovirus is an infectious agent belonging to the RNA virus family Retroviridae. These viruses encode a reverse transcriptase enzyme that converts the RNA genome into DNA during the retroviral life cycle, which then becomes integrated into the host genome.

data.name: Genetic Hybridization
data.description: Genetic hybridization is the process of interbreeding individuals from genetically distinct populations to produce a hybrid. A genetic hybrid would therefore carry two different alleles of the same gene.

data.name: Cryoelectron Tomography
data.description: Cryo-electron tomography (also cryo-ET or electron cryotomography) is a technique where an electron microscope is used to record a series of two-dimensional images as a biological sample held at cryogenic temperatures is tilted. Using computational methods, the two-dimensional images can be aligned to yield a three-dimensional (tomographic) reconstruction of the sample.

data.name: Lipopeptides
data.description: Lipopeptides are peptides modified covalently by at least one lipid molecule. Lipopeptides expressed on the surface of bacterial cells can act as pathogen-associated molecular patterns that are recognized by the host immune system. They may also be used as antibiotics.

data.name: Literature and Media
data.description: Literature and Media examines the relationship between literary texts and various forms of media, including film, television, and digital media, exploring how they influence and interact with each other.

data.name: Muscle Stem Cells
data.description: Muscle stem cells are adult stem cells, present in skeletal muscle tissue, which can self-renew and are capable of giving rise to skeletal muscle cells. These stem cells are activated in response to muscle injury to regenerate damaged muscle tissue.

data.name: Neurotransmitters
data.description: Neurotransmitters are biological molecules that are secreted by neurons and that alter the behaviour of their target neurons or effector cells.

data.name: Electrocardiography
data.description: Electrocardiography (EKG or ECG) is a form of diagnostic testing used to monitor the electrical activity of the heart over time via electrodes placed on the skin of the chest. The method can identify aberrant activity caused by heart conditions such as murmurs or myocardial infarction (heart attack).

data.name: Gene Expression Profiling
data.description: Gene expression profiling is the determination of the pattern of genes expressed, at the level of transcription, under specific circumstances or in a specific cell to give a global picture of cellular function. Techniques to measure this include DNA microarrays which measure the relative activity of previously identified target genes, or sequencing technologies that allow profiling of all active genes.

data.name: Literature and the Environment
data.description: Literature and the Environment explores how literary texts represent and engage with environmental issues, including themes of nature, ecology, and human impact on the natural world.

data.name: Heart Tumor
data.description: Heart Tumor refers to an abnormal growth in the heart, which can be benign or malignant, and may affect the heart's function and require medical or surgical intervention.

data.name: Lacrimal apparatus diseases
data.description: Lacrimal apparatus diseases refer to conditions affecting the lacrimal system, which is responsible for tear production and drainage, leading to issues such as dry eye or excessive tearing.

data.name: X-ray Tomography
data.description: X-ray tomography, or X-ray computed tomography, is a method for generating 3-dimensional imaged volumes from 2-dimensional X-ray image slices. X-ray imaging is based on the differential absorption or scattering of an X-ray source to reveal the internal attributes of a structure or specimen; it is commonly used in medical imaging.

data.name: Bacterial Pathogenesis
data.description: Bacterial pathogenesis is the process by which bacteria infect and cause disease in a host. Not all bacteria are pathogens and have the ability for pathogenesis (also known as virulence).

data.name: Antimicrobial Responses
data.description: Antimicrobial responses refer to any host process triggered by the exposure to a microorganism that results in a change in state, activity or viability of the microorganism – for example, movement, secretion, enzyme production or gene expression.

data.name: Empathy
data.description: Empathy is a social process by which a person has an understanding and awareness of another's emotions and/or behaviour, and can often lead to a person experiencing the same emotions. It differs from sympathy, which involves concern for others without sharing the same emotions as them.

data.name: Heritable Quantitative Trait
data.description: A heritable quantitative trait is a quantitative trait whose variation is demonstrably influenced by genetic differences, meaning that part of its phenotypic variance is transmitted from parents to offspring.

data.name: Stomach Diseases
data.description: Stomach diseases are any diseases that affect the normal functioning of the stomach. Stomach diseases include stomach cancer, gastritis, peptic ulcers, gastroparesis. Many stomach diseases are associated with infection, such as with Helicobacter pylori. Common symptoms are nausea, bloating, diarrhoea and abdominal pain.

data.name: Ulcers
data.description: Ulcers are a breach in the mucosa or membrane of any organ in the body. They affect the normal functioning of the organ and are commonly found in the stomach, mouth and on the surface of genitals.

data.name: Genetic Variation
data.description: Genetic variation describes the genotypic and phenotypic differences between individuals in a population, and between populations. This variation arises through genetic mutation and is important as it provides the diversity within and between populations required for natural selection.

data.name: Gastrointestinal Cancer
data.description: Gastrointestinal cancer refers to malignant conditions of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract and other organs involved in digestion, including the oesophagus, stomach, biliary system, pancreas, small intestine, large intestine, rectum and anus. The symptoms relate to the organ affected and can include obstruction, abnormal bleeding and other associated problems.

data.name: Connective Tissue Diseases
data.description: Connective tissue diseases are a heterogeneous group of autoimmune disorders that affect any of the body's connective tissues. These disorders can be inherited or acquired, and can present with a wide range of systemic inflammatory and immunological features.

data.name: Hamartoma
data.description: A hamartoma is a benign, focal malformation that resembles a neoplasm in the tissue of its origin. It is composed of tissue elements normally found at that site, that grow in a disorganized mass. They occur in many different parts of the body.

data.name: Gene Expression Analysis
data.description: Gene expression analysis is the study of gene products by imaging, amplification, probe hybridization or sequencing-based detection methods.

subjects.term: Auxiliary techniques and procedures; apparatus, equipment, procedures
Methods of research. Technique. Experimental biology

data.name: Skeletal Muscle
data.description: Skeletal muscle is a subtype of muscle formed of bundles of elongated, cylindrical, multinucleate muscle fibres arranged in a striated pattern. Skeletal muscle is attached to the skeleton by tendons, and maintains the position of bones and has a role in their movement through voluntary contraction.

data.name: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy
data.description: Near-infrared spectroscopy is a form of non-invasive imaging that applies near-infrared radiation (wavelengths 780 nm to 3,000 nm) to chemicals or biological subjects to measure differential absorption. It can measure tissue oxygenation in blood including blood flow changes in the brain cortex for cognitive psychology research.

data.name: Autoimmunity
data.description: Autoimmunity is a process by which the immune system reacts against the body's own tissues. Chronic and/or excessive autoimmune responses can result in autoimmune diseases.

data.name: Transmission Electron Microscopy
data.description: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) is a powerful imaging technique that uses a focused beam of electrons transmitted through an ultra-thin specimen to produce highly magnified images of its internal structure. Unlike light microscopy, TEM achieves resolutions down to the atomic scale, allowing researchers to study fine details such as crystal structures, morphology, and chemical composition of materials.

data.name: Genetic Engineering
data.description: Genetic engineering is a process that uses laboratory-based technologies to alter the DNA makeup of an organism. This may involve changing a single base pair (A-T or C-G), deleting a region of DNA or adding a new segment of DNA.

data.name: Vaccines
data.description: Vaccines are a clinical product that is composed of live or dead material from an infectious agent – bacterium, virus, fungus or parasite – that elicit protective immunity against the pathogen when administered. These substances are used to prevent the spread of infectious diseases.

data.name: Cartilage Development
data.description: Cartilage development is the formation of cartilage by specialised cells called chondrocytes. These secrete large amounts of the cartilage extracellular matrix, which contains collagen and proteoglycans. Cartilage has limited repair capacity once damaged.

data.name: Marburg Virus
data.description: Marburg virus is an infectious agent belonging to the virus family Filoviridae, which also includes the Ebolavirus genus, and causes a rare and severe type of haemorrhagic fever in humans and non-human primates. Owing to their high morbidity and mortality, filoviruses are classified as category A priority pathogens.

data.name: Thermodynamics
data.description: Thermodynamics is the mathematical analysis of energy relationships. It is a scientific discipline concerned with heat and temperature and their relation to energy and work. It deals with the bulk macroscopic properties of a system, rather than those of the microscopic constituents.

data.name: Immunological Deficiency Syndromes
data.description: Immunological deficiency syndromes are diseases or conditions in which there is a loss of or defect in a component of the immune system. Patients with these syndromes have an increased susceptibility to infections and to developing certain cancers. These syndromes include primary immune deficiency diseases, such as severe combined immunodeficiency, and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).

data.name: Forgetting
data.description: Forgetting refers to the loss of, or inability to access, information stored in memory. This may occur through a passive process by which the original memory trace is degraded, or by an active process by which new memories interfere with the retrieval of old ones.

data.name: Environmental Law
data.description: Environmental law refers to a system of legal principles, regulations, and statutes that aim to protect and manage the natural environment and address environmental issues. It encompasses a wide range of legal frameworks at international, national, regional, and local levels, governing various aspects of environmental protection, conservation, and sustainable development. Environmental law encompasses both public and private law and involves the interaction between legal, social, economic, and scientific considerations.

subjects.term: Environment, transport and planning law: general

data.name: Translesion Synthesis
data.description: Translesion synthesis can bypass a replication block caused by various DNA damage. Specialised translesion synthesis DNA polymerases can replicate DNA over such lesions to resume publication but the enzymes are error prone.

data.name: Aspergillus Nidulans
data.description: Aspergillus nidulans is a filamentous soil fungus in the phylum Ascomcyetes. It is a fungal model system used to study cell biology and molecular genetics including recombination and DNA repair, and can form sexual spores by meiosis, enabling genetic crosses; its sexual form or teleomorph is known as Emericella nidulans.

data.name: Blood Flow
data.description: Circulation is the movement of blood through the cardiovascular system, resulting in the distribution of nutrients, oxygen and other products of metabolism throughout the body.

data.name: Glomerular Diseases
data.description: Glomerular diseases encompass a wide spectrum of conditions, characterized by injury to the glomeruli, resulting in the incorrect filtering of blood and excretion of waste products. Causes include environmental and genetic factors, such as drug toxicity and infection, as well as other diseases, including diabetes and lupus.

data.name: Gastrulation
data.description: Gastrulation is the process during which the early sphere-like embryo of most animals is dramatically re-organised by the inward migration of cells on the outside of the embryo. During gastrulation, the three primary germ cell layers that will give rise to specific tissues and organs are formed.

data.name: Biological Microscopy
data.description: Biological microscopy refers to the use of microscopes for studying biological samples or to study the structure, function, and behavior of biological specimens at different scales, ranging from cells to tissues and beyond.

data.name: Chemoprevention
data.description: Chemoprevention involves the use of chemical compounds or biologics to prevent or delay the development of a specific disease. For example, chemoprevention approaches are currently used in oncology to reduce the risk of cancer returning following surgery (known as secondary chemoprevention).

data.name: Hypertension
data.description: Hypertension is high blood pressure. It is generally defined in adults as systolic blood pressure greater than or equal to 140mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure greater than or equal to 90mmHg. Rarely associated with obvious symptoms, hypertension can result in heart disease, vascular disease, stroke and/or chronic kidney disease

data.name: Developmental Neurogenesis
data.description: Developmental neurogenesis is the formation of functional, mature neurons from neural stem cells during development of an organism. Understanding developmental neurogenesis helps in the understanding of congenital neurological disorders.

data.name: Breast Cancer
data.description: Breast cancer is caused by the development of malignant cells in the breast. The malignant cells originate in the lining of the milk glands or ducts of the breast (ductal epithelium). Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, but it can also appear in men.

data.name: Lipopolysaccharides
data.description: Lipopolysaccharides are lipids that are covalently modified with polysaccharides, consisting generally of three parts: a repetitive glycan polymer (an O-lipid), the polysaccharide component and Lipid A (two glucosamine groups with attached fatty acids), and often containing one phosphate on each glucosamine. Lipopolysaccharides function in Gram-negative bacterial membranes and are endotoxins released by bacterial lysis.

data.name: Prognostic Markers
data.description: Prognostic markers are biological characteristics that are objectively measured and evaluated to predict the course of a disease or a response to a therapeutic intervention among patients with the same characteristic. Examples include the presence of a particular gene variant, patterns of gene expression or levels of a particular protein in body fluids.

data.name: Blood Urea Nitrogen
data.description: Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) is a diagnostic procedure that measures the amount of nitrogen in the blood that is derived from urea. BUN is used as a measure of kidney function.

data.name: Indigenous Studies
data.description: Indigeneity refers to the inherent and original connection of certain groups of people, known as Indigenous peoples or First Nations, to a specific territory, land, or region. It encompasses their unique cultural, social, spiritual, and economic relationships with the land, as well as their distinct languages, traditions, and ways of life that have developed over generations. Indigeneity recognizes the historical continuity of these communities and their sustained presence prior to the colonization and establishment of modern nation-states. The concept also acknowledges the challenges and struggles Indigenous peoples have faced in maintaining their identities, rights, and autonomy in the face of historical injustices, marginalization, and attempts at assimilation.

subjects.term: Ethnographies of special categories of peoples

data.name: Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
data.description: Tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy(TERS) is a variant of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy that combines scanning probe microscopy with Raman spectroscopy.

data.name: Coagulation Disorders
data.description: Coagulation disorders, also known as bleeding disorders or clotting disorders, are a group of conditions characterized by abnormalities in the blood clotting process. The blood clotting, or coagulation, process is crucial for preventing excessive bleeding and promoting wound healing. Coagulation disorders can be inherited or acquired and can result in abnormal bleeding or excessive clotting.

data.name: Infectious Diseases
data.description: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogenic microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, parasites or fungi, that infect a host organism and can be spread, directly or indirectly, from one organism to another. An infectiologist manages nosocomial (healthcare-acquired) or community-acquired infections.

data.name: Ethnohistory
data.description: In the context of criminology, ethnohistory can provide insights into the historical roots of criminal behavior, the impact of colonization and systemic oppression, and the dynamics of power and resistance within marginalized communities.

data.name: Cellular Noise
data.description: Cellular noise is a generic term designating random fluctuations in the rates of biochemical reactions, which can cause non-deterministic heterogeneity among genetically identical cells. Such fluctuations can either be detrimental to the accuracy of biological function or favourable to the sensitivity or adaptability of biological processes.

data.name: Energy Conservation
data.description: Energy conservation is the effort made to reduce the consumption of energy by using less of an energy service. This can be achieved either by using energy more efficiently or by reducing the amount of service used.

data.name: Optic nerve diseases
data.description: Optic nerve diseases refer to conditions affecting the optic nerve, which transmits visual information from the eye to the brain, leading to vision impairment or loss.

data.name: Climate-Change Policy
data.description: Climate-change policy encompasses policies formulated specifically to tackle climate change and can be local, national or international in scope. These broadly fall into two categories; those designed to minimise the extent of climate change – climate change mitigation – and those intended to minimise risks and seize upon new opportunities – climate change adaptation.

subjects.term: POLITICAL SCIENCE / Public Policy / Environmental Policy

data.name: Hydrogen Storage
data.description: Hydrogen storage is a key enabling technology for the advancement of hydrogen and fuel cell technologies in applications including stationary power, portable power, and transportation.

data.name: Medicinal Chemistry
data.description: Medicinal chemistry deals with the design, optimization and development of chemical compounds for use as drugs. It is inherently a multidisciplinary topic — beginning with the synthesis of potential drugs followed by studies investigating their interactions with biological targets to understand the medicinal effects of the drug, its metabolism and side-effects.

data.name: Compound Screening
data.description: Compound screening, also known as high-throughput screening (HTS), is a process used in drug discovery and other fields to rapidly evaluate large numbers of chemical compounds for their biological activity or potential therapeutic effects. It involves the systematic testing of diverse compounds against specific targets or assays to identify promising candidates for further study or development.

data.name: Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
data.description: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are pluripotent stem cells generated from adult cells by reprogramming. iPSCs have the same properties as embryonic stem cells, and therefore self-renew and can differentiate into all cell types of the body except for cells in extra-embryonic tissues such as the placenta.

synonyms: Fibroblast Derived Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells

data.name: Auditory System
data.description: The auditory system is the sensory system for hearing. It consists of the outer ear (the auricle and auditory canal), the middle ear (the tympanic membrane, malleus, incus and stapes), the inner ear (consisting of the cochlea and vestibular organs), the auditory nerve, the auditory cortex and other brain areas involved in sound processing.

data.name: Post-translational Modifications
data.description: Post-translational modifications are modifications that occur on a protein, catalysed by enzymes, after its translation by ribosomes is complete. Post-translational modification generally refers to the addition of a functional group covalently to a protein as in phosphorylation and neddylation, but also refers to proteolytic processing and folding processes necessary for a protein to mature functionally.

data.name: Gliogenesis
data.description: Gliogenesis is the developmental process by which glial cells – astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, Schwann cells, microglia – are generated. It includes the production of glial progenitor cells and their differentiation into mature glia.

data.name: Urological Cancer
data.description: Urological cancer refers to a group of cancers that originate in the urinary system and male reproductive organs. The urinary system includes the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra, while the male reproductive organs consist of the prostate gland, testicles, and related structures.

data.name: Immunization
data.description: Immunization is the deliberation stimulation of the host's immune system to protect the host from a disease. Active immunization involves the administration of an immunogen to render the host more responsive to a subsequent encounter. Passive immunization involves the transfer of immune components, such as antibodies or lymphocytes, or of immune-cell-producing tissues.

data.name: Atmospheric Optics
data.description: Atmospheric optics is a branch of optics and photonics that studies how light behaves in the Earth’s atmosphere. This can include both understanding naturally occurring effects involving sunlight and the propagation and distortion of electromagnetic signals through air.

data.name: RNA Interference
data.description: RNAi (RNA interference) is a biological process in which RNA molecules (microRNA (miRNA) and small interfering RNA (siRNA)) inhibit gene expression, typically by binding to messenger RNA (mRNA) and triggering its degradation. The process is exploited by researchers to knock down gene expression in cell culture and in vivo in model organisms.

data.name: Head and Neck Cancer
data.description: Head and neck cancer comprises a group of biologically similar cancers that start in the lip, oral cavity (mouth), nasal cavity (inside the nose), paranasal sinuses, pharynx and larynx. Most head and neck cancers are squamous cell carcinomas that originate from the epithelium of these regions.

data.name: Atmospheric Chemistry
data.description: Atmospheric chemistry is the study of the components of planetary atmospheres, particularly that of the Earth. It specifically looks at the composition of planetary atmospheres and the reactions and interactions that drive these dynamic and diverse systems. The topic encompasses lab-based studies, field measurements and also their modelling.

data.name: Endoscopy
data.description: Endoscopy is an optical imaging technique that uses a rigid or flexible small diameter light guide inserted into an organ, cavity or tissue for light delivery and collection.

data.name: Lab-on-a-Chip
data.description: A lab-on-a-chip is a class of device that integrates and automates multiple laboratory techniques into a system that fits on a chip up to a maximum of a few square centimetres in size. By manipulating reagents on the microscale effects such as rapid heating and mixing can be exploited. It also allows waste and exposure to dangerous chemicals to be minimized.

data.name: Megakaryocytes
data.description: Megakaryocytes are large, multinucleated cells found in the bone marrow that are responsible for the production of platelets (thrombocytes), which are essential for blood clotting. These cells originate from hematopoietic stem cells and undergo a process called endomitosis, where they replicate their DNA without cell division, resulting in a large cell with multiple nuclei. Once mature, megakaryocytes extend cytoplasmic projections called proplatelets into the bloodstream, which fragment into individual platelets. Megakaryocytes play a crucial role in hemostasis, the process that prevents excessive bleeding, and are also involved in various physiological and pathological processes, including inflammation and immune responses.

data.name: Continuing professional development in dentistry
data.description: Continuing professional development in dentistry involves ongoing education and training for dental professionals to maintain and enhance their knowledge, skills, and competencies throughout their careers.

data.name: Skin Cancer
data.description: Skin cancer can involve melanocytes, leading to melanoma, but there are other non-melanoma skin cancers. These include basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma and, less commonly, Merkel cell carcinoma, Kaposi's sarcoma and T-cell lymphoma of the skin.

data.name: Bacterial Transcription
data.description: Bacterial transcription is the process by which bacteria transcribe genetic information encoded in their genome into messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) molecules. mRNA is then used as a template for the production of bacterial proteins.

data.name: Forming
data.description: Forming is a manufacturing process that involves shaping materials, typically metals or plastics, into desired forms through mechanical deformation.

data.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
data.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is defined as a progressive loss of renal function that lasts for more than 3 months, and is classified according to the degree of kidney damage - measured by the level of proteinuria - and the decline in glomerular filtration rate. The most severe form is end-stage renal disease.

data.name: Genomic Engineering
data.description: Genomic engineering is the synthetic assembly of complete chromosomal DNA that is more or less derived from natural genomic sequences. Genomic engineering is the top-down, global approach to synthetic biology; to be distinguished from bottom-up, local genetic circuit engineering.

data.name: Protein sequence analyses
data.description: Protein sequence analyses are experimental methods that determine the amino acid sequence of a protein or of parts of a protein (peptide, oligopeptide). The amino acid sequence of a protein can be used in bioinformatic analyses to predict protein structure and possible functions.

data.name: Thyroid Diseases
data.description: Thyroid diseases are characterized by hyperfunction (hyperthyroidism), hypofunction (hypothyoidism) or inflammation (thyroiditis) of the thyroid gland or the presence of thyroid nodules, which can be benign or cancerous. All of these disorders can result in an enlarged thyroid gland that causes swelling of the neck, a so-called goiter.

data.name: Hypocretin
data.description: Hypocretin (also known as orexin) is a neuropeptide hormone produced in the hypothalamus that exerts important influences over sleep, arousal, appetite and energy expenditure. Defective hypocretin signalling is associated with narcolepsy.

data.name: Streptococcus mutans
data.description: Streptococcus mutans is a type of bacteria commonly found in the human oral cavity, known for its role in the development of dental caries by producing acid that demineralizes tooth enamel.

data.name: Innate Lymphoid Cells
data.description: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) are immune cells that belong to the lymphoid lineage but do not express antigen-specific receptors. These cells have important functions in innate immune responses to infectious microorganisms and in the regulation of homeostasis and inflammation.

data.name: Amalgam
data.description: Amalgam is a dental filling material composed of a mixture of metals, including mercury, silver, tin, and copper, used to restore decayed teeth due to its durability and strength.

data.name: Genome Evolution
data.description: Genome evolution is the process by which a genome changes in structure over time, through mutation, horizontal gene transfer, and sexual reproduction. The study of genome evolution involves multiple fields including structural analysis of the genome, genomic parasites, gene and ancient genome duplications, polyploidy, and comparative genomics.

data.name: Transcranial magnetic stimulation
data.description: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is a method to noninvasively stimulate neurons in the brain and induce immediate or long term changes in activity. Stimulation is mediated by electromagnetic induction of weak electric current in neurons using an electromagnetic coil over the head.

data.name: Astrophysical magnetic fields
data.description: Magnetic fields are produced by electrical currents that are generated by various astrophysical objects. The study of magnetic fields seeks to understand their origin, as well as the acceleration of charged particles in such fields, and includes numerical simulations and observational studies of magnetism in astrophysical environments.

data.name: Huntington's Disease
data.description: Huntington's disease is a hereditary neurodegenerative disorder caused by an autosomal dominant mutation. The hallmark symptom of Huntington's disease is the presence of progressive chorea (abnormal involuntary movements), which is accompanied by psychiatric symptoms and cognitive decline.

data.name: Vesicle Trafficking
data.description: Vesicle trafficking is the biological process by which vesicles, including synaptic vesicles, transport materials between different cellular compartments and between a cell and its environment. In the process of synaptic transmission, vesicle trafficking refers to the formation, intracellular movement and exocyotosis and endocytosis of synaptic vesicles.

data.name: Lipidomics
data.description: Lipidomics is the study of the structure and function of the complete set of lipids (the lipidome) produced in a given cell or organism as well as their interactions with other lipids, proteins and metabolites. Lipid profiles or fatty acid profiles can be determined using diverse methods including thin layer chromatography, liquid chromatography, gas chromatography. Identification of the lipids or fatty acids is typically done by NMR or mass spectrometry.

data.name: Leukocytes
data.description: Leukocytes are the white blood cells of the immune system that protect our tissues from infection and other forms of damage. Leukocytes can be sub-classed as cells of the innate immune system (for example, macrophages, neutrophils and dendritic cells) or of the adaptive immune system (for example, B cells and T cells).

data.name: Visual System
data.description: The visual system is the part of the central nervous system that is required for visual perception: receiving, processing and interpreting visual information to build a representation of the visual environment. It consists of the eye, retina, fibres that conduct visual information to the thalamus, the superior colliculus and parts of the cerebral cortex.

data.name: Diabetes
data.description: Diabetes describes a group of metabolic diseases characterized by high blood sugar levels. Diabetes can be caused by the pancreas not producing insulin (type 1 diabetes) or by insulin resistance (cells do not respond to insulin; type 2 diabetes).

subjects.term: Diabetes mellitus and other disorders of the pancreatic internal secretion

data.name: Dyslipidaemias
data.description: Dyslipidaemias are diseases characterized by abnormal levels of lipids in the blood. These lipids can include cholesterol, triglycerides and high density lipoprotein. Hypercholesterolaemia and hyperlipoproteinaemia are examples of dyslipidaemias.

data.name: Multicellular systems
data.description: Multicellular systems are living organisms that are composed of numerous interacting cells. In synthetic biology, multicellularity allows some degree of modularity in the combination of elementary functions performed by separate cells.

data.name: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion and Women in Business
data.description: Diversity Management is a field of research and practice that focuses on promoting diversity and inclusion in the workplace. It involves recognizing and valuing differences in individuals based on their race, gender, age, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, and other dimensions of diversity. Diversity management aims to create an inclusive workplace culture where all employees feel valued, respected, and supported, and where they can contribute their unique perspectives and experiences to the organization's success.  As a field of research, diversity management investigates the factors that influence diversity in the workplace, such as hiring practices, leadership styles, and organizational culture. It explores the impact of diversity on organizational outcomes such as performance, innovation, and employee well-being. Research in this field also examines strategies for managing diversity, such as diversity training programs, mentorship and sponsorship initiatives, and employee resource groups.  Women in Business is a field of research and practice that focuses on advancing women's leadership and career development in business and management. It seeks to address the barriers that women face in the workplace and promote gender equality in leadership positions. Women in Business aims to create a more diverse and inclusive workplace where women have equal opportunities to advance and succeed.  As a field of research, Women in Business investigates the factors that contribute to gender inequality in the workplace, such as unconscious bias, stereotypes, and systemic barriers. It explores strategies for promoting gender equality and advancing women's leadership, such as mentorship and sponsorship programs, flexible work arrangements, and inclusive leadership practices. Research in this field also examines the impact of women's leadership on organizational outcomes, such as performance, innovation, and employee engagement.  As a field of practice, Women in Business involves implementing programs and initiatives that support women's leadership and career development, such as leadership development programs, networking events, and advocacy campaigns. It also involves creating a supportive organizational culture that values diversity and inclusion and fosters the advancement of women in the workplace.

synonyms: Diversity Management und Frauen in der Wirtschaft

subjects.term: BUSINESS & ECONOMICS / Human Resources & Personnel Management
Minorities. Diversity in the workplace. Multiculturalism

data.name: Testicular Cancer
data.description: Testicular cancer is a cancer that starts in the testis. The majority (95%) of testicular cancers are germ cell tumours. Treatment for testicular cancer is highly effective, with 5-year overall survival rates approaching 100% for localized disease.

data.name: Bacterial Host Response
data.description: The bacterial host response is the process by which the host interacts with, and responds to, bacteria that colonize or infect it. This includes defense mechanisms such as the immune response.

data.name: Adaptive Immunity
data.description: Adaptive immunity is the protection of a host organism from a pathogen or toxin. It is mediated by B cells and T cells, and is characterized by immunological memory. Adaptive immunity is highly specific to a given antigen and is highly adaptable.

data.name: Zea mays
data.description: Zea mays, known as maize or corn, is a plant in the grass family (Poaceae) cultivated for its seeds which are eaten as a human staple crop and used in animal feed. Many varieties are grown and used to study genetics, development, domestication and biotechnology.

data.name: Adult Neurogenesis
data.description: Adult neurogenesis is the formation of functional, mature neurons from neural stem cells in specific brain regions in adults. In these regions, new neurons are generated throughout life and integrated into established neuronal circuits.

data.name: Cellular Imaging
data.description: Cellular imaging encompasses the techniques that allow the detection and analysis of cellular organelles and macromolecules. Cellular imaging observations are obtained using light-based or electron-based microscopes and often request further analysis with computer based programming.

data.name: Postharvest Physiology
data.description: Postharvest Physiology is the branch of agricultural science that studies the biological and biochemical processes that occur in fruits, vegetables, and other crops after they have been harvested. This field focuses on understanding how these processes affect the quality, shelf life, and safety of produce during storage, transportation, and marketing. Key areas of research include respiration, ripening, senescence, and the effects of environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, and ethylene exposure. By applying knowledge from postharvest physiology, scientists and agricultural professionals aim to develop methods to minimize spoilage, enhance nutritional value, and maintain the sensory qualities of harvested crops, ultimately improving food security and reducing waste.

data.name: Bioremediation
data.description: Bioremediation is a process that uses living organisms, mostly microorganisms and plants, to degrade and reduce or detoxify waste products and pollutants.

subjects.term: Pollution control technology and industrial sanitation engineering

data.name: Non-photochemical Quenching
data.description: Non-photochemical quenching is a protective mechanism that plants employ to dissipate excess light energy. Plants often absorb more light energy than they can process in photosynthesis, and the quenching of singlet excited chlorophylls - non-photochemical quenching - leads to the harmless dissipation of this excess energy as heat.

data.name: Perovskites
data.description: Perovskite is a naturally occurring mineral of calcium titanate with a chemical formula of CaTiO3.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Gastrointestinal Bleeding
data.description: Gastrointestinal bleeding is any form of bleeding (haemorrhage) observed in any section of the digestive tract, typically classified as bleeding in either the upper or lower gastrointestinal tract. The degree of bleeding can vary from barely detectable (microscopic) to severe and life-threatening; blood can appear in stool or vomit.

data.name: Liver
data.description: The liver is a large, glandular, vital organ - divided into two main lobes - with a major role in metabolism, detoxification and production of chemicals necessary for digestion. The liver is largely comprised of hepatocytes, but Kupffer cells, endothelial cells and hepatic stellate cells are also present.

data.name: Proteolysis
data.description: Proteolysis is the enzymatic process by which proteins are degraded into their component polypeptide or amino acid parts. This generally occurs through protease-mediated hydrolysis of peptide bonds, but can also occur through non-enzymatic methods such as by action of mineral acids and heat.

data.name: Chromatography
data.description: Chromatography is a technique used to separate mixtures of chemical compounds or biomolecules based on differences in their relative affinities for mobile (gas or liquid) and stationary (solid or liquid) phases. Chromatography is used for both preparative and analytical purposes and can be performed in column or planar format.

data.name: Machine Learning
data.description: Machine learning (ML) is the scientific study of algorithms and statistical models that computer systems use to progressively improve their performance on a specific task. Machine learning algorithms build a mathematical model of sample data, known as "training data", in order to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed to perform the task. The study of mathematical optimization delivers methods, theory and application domains to the field of machine learning. In its application across business problems, machine learning is also referred to as predictive analytics
