data.name: Anal Diseases
data.description: Anal diseases are diseases that affect the anus, which is the final segment of the large intestine. Anal diseases include haemorrhoids, fissures, abscesses and cancer.

data.name: Viral Tracing
data.description: Viral tracing is a method that uses viral movement between cells as a label to determine the cells' connectivity. Viruses are most commonly used as tracers to define neural circuitry.

data.name: Epilepsy
data.description: Epilepsy refers to a group of neurological disorders of varying aetiology, characterized by recurrent brain dysfunction that result from sudden excessive and disordered neuronal discharge. These episodes can manifest as epileptic seizures, but they can also occur with subtle or no behavioural signs.

data.name: Oesophageal Diseases
data.description: Oesophageal diseases are diseases that affect the oesophagus. Oesophageal diseases include Barrett's oesophagus, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and oesophageal cancer.

data.name: Brassinosteroid
data.description: Brassinosteroids are a group of plant steroid hormones that regulate growth and development, structurally similar to cholesterol-derived animal steroid hormones and insect ecdysteroids. They are involved in cell expansion, biotic and abiotic stress tolerance, vascular differentiation, pollen tube formation, and other important processes during the life of the plant.

data.name: Protein Translocation
data.description: Protein translocation is a process by which proteins move between cellular compartments. Short amino-acid sequences within a protein, known as signal peptides or signal sequences, can direct its localisation, although translocation also occurs in the absence of these signal sequences. Protein translocation can occur co-translationally or post-translationally.

data.name: Vasculitis Syndromes
data.description: Vasculitis sydromes are a group of autoimmune disorders characterized by inflammation of the blood vessels, either primary or secondary to another condition. The different vasculitis syndromes are classified by the size of blood vessel predominantly affected.

data.name: Neurospora crassa
data.description: Neurospora crassa, a bread mould, is a filamentous ascoymcete fungus used as a model for studying genetics, biochemistry, circadian rhythm and meiosis. It is easy to culture and is haploid with a short diploid stage prior to meiosis.

data.name: Endodontic Instruments
data.description: Endodontic instruments are all hand-held and rotary specialized tools used in root canal therapy to clean, shape, and fill the root canals, including files, reamers, and irrigating solutions.

data.name: Bacterial Techniques and Applications
data.description: Bacterial techniques and applications refer to the various methods and uses of bacteria in different fields, including medicine, industry, agriculture, and environmental science. Bacteria have been extensively studied and manipulated for their unique properties and capabilities.

data.name: Peritoneal Dialysis
data.description: Peritoneal dialysis is a procedure to remove waste products from the blood, such as creatinine and urea, which are insufficiently removed by the kidneys in patients with renal failure. The dialysis fluid is introduced into and removed from the peritoneal cavity, and the peritoneum is used as the dialysis membrane.

data.name: Viral Vectors
data.description: Viral vectors are used for the delivery of genetical material into cells. Because viruses have a natural ability to efficiently deliver their genome into host cells, they are an ideal tool for gene transfer and are often used by molecular biologists to deliver therapeutic genes.

data.name: Granulocytes
data.description: Granulocytes are cells of the innate immune system that are characterized by granules in their cytoplasm. The three main types of granulocytes are neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils.

data.name: Quantum Information
data.description: Quantum information is problem solving and data processing using a quantum system as the information carrier, rather than binary ‘1’s and ‘0’s used in conventional computation. Quantum information systems could be able to transmit data that is fundamentally secure and solve problems that are beyond the power of modern computers.

subjects.term: Quantum physics (quantum mechanics & quantum field theory)
Quantum physics (quantum mechanics and quantum field theory)

data.name: Infrared Spectroscopy
data.description: Infrared spectroscopy (IR spectroscopy) is an optical technique that detects molecular bond vibrations and rotations upon absorption of infrared light. Because different chemical functional groups absorb IR light at different frequencies, IR spectroscopy can be used for chemical structure analysis, chemical fingerprinting and chemical imaging.

data.name: Xenopus
data.description: Xenopus is a genus of African aquatic frogs. Xenopus laevis, the African clawed frog, is a model organism for embryonic development, toxicology, neurobiology and cell biology.

data.name: Embryonic Stem Cells
data.description: Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent cells isolated from the inner cell mass of a blastocyst, the early mammalian embryo that implants into the uterus. Embryonic stem cells self-renew by dividing and can differentiate into any specialised cell of the body, but not extra-embryonic tissues such as the placenta.

data.name: Biliary Tract Disease
data.description: Biliary tract disease describes any disease that affects the biliary tract - the gall bladder, bile ducts and accompanying structures. Examples include primary sclerosing cholangitis, secondary sclerosing cholangitis and biliary atresia.

data.name: Cleft lip and palate
data.description: Cleft lip and palate are congenital deformities where the upper lip and/or the roof of the mouth (palate) do not fully form, requiring surgical intervention and multidisciplinary care.

data.name: Criticality
data.description: Criticality is the state in which a material behaves like water at pressures and temperatures above the critical point, where it turns from liquid to gas without change in density. Critical phenomena such as ferromagnetism or percolation present universal properties over large scales also found in biology and sociology.

data.name: Western Blot
data.description: The western blot is a method for detecting the presence and size of specific proteins. Proteins are first separated according to size or other physical properties by gel electrophoresis, then transferred to a membrane (blotted) before a detection step that uses labelled antibody to recognize the protein of interest.

data.name: Electrophoresis
data.description: Electrophoresis is the process by which large charged molecules travel through a medium under a uniform electric field. The most common implementation, gel electrophoresis, is a method used to separate nucleic acids by length or proteins by size, conformation and charge based on their migration through a porous matrix.

data.name: Synaptic Vesicle Endocytosis
data.description: Synaptic vesicle endocytosis is the biological process by which the plasma membrane at the pre-synaptic axon terminal invaginates to create membrane-bound synaptic vesicles. This process enables the neuron to recover and recycle the membrane that is added to the plasma membrane during synaptic vesicle exocytosis.

data.name: Psychosis
data.description: Psychosis is a mental state in which the individual's cognitive judgment and contact with reality are disturbed. Hallmark symptoms of psychosis include hallucinations and delusions. Psychosis can result from a psychiatric disorder, such as schizophrenia, but it can also be caused by substance abuse, a brain tumour or neurodegenerative disease.

data.name: Population Dynamics
data.description: Population dynamics is the branch of life sciences that studies the size and age composition of populations as dynamical systems, and the biological and environmental processes driving them. It is the study of how and why populations change in size and structure over time. Important factors in population dynamics include rates of reproduction, death and migration. Population dynamics has traditionally been the dominant branch of mathematical biology

data.name: Bacterial Genomics
data.description: Bacterial genomics is a scientific discipline that concerns the genome, encompassing the entire hereditary information, of bacteria. Bacterial genomics can, for example, be used to study bacterial evolution or outbreaks of bacterial infections.

data.name: Oomycetes
data.description: They include some of the most destructive plant pathogens including the genus Phytophthora, which includes the causal agents of potato late blight and sudden oak death. Particular species of oomycetes are responsible for root rot.

data.name: Adaptive clinical trial
data.description: An adaptive clinical trial is designed to allow modifications after its initiation without undermining its statistical validity and integrity. Adaptive clinical trials based on Bayesian statistical methods are common.

data.name: Gynaecological Cancer
data.description: Gynaecological cancers are tumours located in the female reproductive system, and they include ovarian, uterine (or endometrial), cervical, vulval and vaginal cancer.

data.name: Demyelinating Diseases
data.description: Demyelinating diseases are a group of disorders of the nervous system that involve loss of the myelin sheath that normally surrounds the neurons. Demyelinating diseases can affect both the central nervous system and peripheral nervous system.

data.name: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
data.description: Obsessive compulsive disorder is a psychiatric disease that is characterized by anxiety, fear and repetitive behaviour. Possible symptoms are excessive cleaning, repeated checking or hoarding.

data.name: Wind Energy
data.description: Wind power or wind energy describes the process by which the wind is used to generate mechanical power or electricity. This mechanical power can be used for specific tasks (such as grinding grain or pumping water) or a generator can convert this mechanical power into electricity.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Power Resources / Alternative & Renewable

data.name: Nanofluidics
data.description: Nanofluidics is the study and manipulation of fluids confined within nanostructures. The fluid dynamics of substances on the nanoscale differs significantly from the fluid dynamics of substances on longer length scales.

data.name: Fatigue
data.description: Fatigue is extreme tiredness that can manifest as physical weakness or mental exhaustion. It is characterized by decreased energy, motivation and difficulty concentrating.

data.name: Bone Development
data.description: Bone development is the formation and growth of bones. New bone is formed by the action of specialised cells called osteoblasts and osteoclasts, either by directly laying down bone tissue into connective tissue or forming it from cartilage, such as during growth in length of long bones.

data.name: Sleep Deprivation
data.description: Sleep deprivation is a state that arises when an organism has less sleep than is optimal, and is followed by a 'rebound' in slow-wave sleep when the opportunity arises. This can be induced experimentally or environmentally (such as shift work), but is also associated with neurological and psychiatric disorders such as dementia, in which normal sleep patterns are disrupted.

data.name: Molecular Machines and Motors
data.description: Molecular motors, also called molecular machines, are either natural or synthetic molecules that convert chemical energy into mechanical forces and motion. An example of a biological motor is the protein kinesin, which uses the hydrolysis of adenosine triphosphate to move along microtubule filaments.

data.name: Antenna Complex
data.description: The antenna complex is a light-harvesting membrane-associated aggregate of proteins and photosensitive pigments such as chlorophyll and carotenoids. They are situated inside the chloroplasts of photosynthetic organisms, capture the energy from light, and transfer it to the reaction centre where chemical reactions take place.

data.name: Mesothelioma
data.description: Mesothelioma is a rare and aggressive cancer deriving by uncontrolled growth of mesothelial cells and is most commonly caused by exposure to asbestos. The most common site for mesothelioma is the pleura (outer lining of the lungs), but it can also arise in the abdominal (peritoneum) or cardiac cavity (pericardium).

data.name: Nanocomposites
data.description: Nanocomposites are solid materials that have multiple phase domains and at least one of these domains has a nanoscale structure. The materials can have novel chemical and physical properties that depend on the morphology and interfacial characteristics of the component materials.

data.name: Five Factor Model
data.description: The Five Factor Model (FFM), also known as the Big Five personality traits, is a widely accepted framework in psychology that organizes human personality into five broad dimensions: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism (commonly referred to as OCEAN). Each of these dimensions is thought to reflect a basic and relatively stable aspect of personality, and research has consistently shown that individuals can be placed somewhere along each of these five dimensions, resulting in a unique profile that describes their overall personality. The FFM is commonly used in research, clinical practice, and personal development as a tool for understanding and measuring personality.

data.name: NOD-like Receptors
data.description: NOD-like receptors (NLRs) are a group of pattern recognition receptors that are expressed in the cell cytosol. They can sense molecules that are associated with infection (for example, bacterial peptidoglycans) and induce inflammatory immune responses that help clear the infection.

data.name: Lung Cancer
data.description: Lung cancer arises in tissues of the lung, usually in the cells lining air passages. The two main types are small-cell lung cancer and non-small-cell lung cancer, according to the shape of cells under a microscope. The most common symptoms are coughing, shortness of breath and chest pains.

data.name: Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders
data.description: Functional gastrointestinal disorders are a range of disorders of the gastrointestinal tract for which there are no structural or biochemical abnormalities that can be found to explain the symptoms. Examples include irritable bowel syndrome and functional dyspepsia.

data.name: Pancreatic Disease
data.description: Pancreatic disease is disease that affects the pancreas. Pancreatic diseases include pancreatitis - acute, chronic or autoimmune - and pancreatic cancer.

data.name: Parathyroid Diseases
data.description: Parathyroid diseases are disorders of parathyroid gland function, resulting in abnormally high (primary hyperparathyroidism) or low (primary hypoparathyroidism) levels of calcium and parathyroid hormone. Secondary hyperparathyroidism is characterized by normal calcium but high parathyroid hormone levels, whereas pseudohypoparathyroidism is associated with low calcium and high parathyroid hormone levels.

data.name: Dental Caries
data.description: Dental Caries, commonly known as cavities, are areas of tooth decay caused by bacterial activity that demineralizes the tooth enamel and dentin, leading to structural damage.

data.name: Two-dimensional Materials
data.description: Two-dimensional materials are substances with a thickness of a few nanometres or less. Electrons in these materials are free to move in the two-dimensional plane, but their restricted motion in the third direction is governed by quantum mechanics. Prominent examples include quantum wells and graphene.

subjects.term: Condensed matter physics (liquid state & solid state physics)
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Cardiomyopathies
data.description: Cardiomyopathies are diseases of the heart muscle. This group of pathological conditions includes dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, and left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy. They can be hereditary or acquired conditions.

data.name: Toxin-induced Nephropathy
data.description: Toxin-induced nephropathy is used to describe any kidney damage that is known to be caused by exposure to a nephrotoxin, usually through ingestion. A nephrotoxin can be defined as any chemical that induces damage to the kidney, and includes some antibiotics and chemotherapies.

data.name: Corneal diseases
data.description: Corneal diseases refer to medical conditions affecting the cornea, the transparent front part of the eye, which can lead to vision impairment and require medical or surgical treatment.

data.name: Tetrahymena thermophila
data.description: Tetrahymena thermophila is a freshwater unicellular ciliated protozoan that serves as a model organism for molecular biology. It features unusual genomic and nuclear structure.

data.name: Interstitial Disease
data.description: Interstitial disease is defined as a disorder that primarily affects the connective tissues of an organ.

data.name: Dementia
data.description: Dementia is a syndrome that involves severe loss of cognitive abilities as a result of disease or injury. Dementia caused by traumatic brain injury is often static, whereas dementia caused by neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer's disease, is usually progressive and can eventually be fatal.

subjects.term: Alzheimer’s, dementia, Parkinson’s disease and other neurodegenerative diseases

data.name: Pain
data.description: Pain is an unpleasant sensory and emotional experience. Acute nociceptive pain is induced by noxious stimuli, and is often a result of an intense or potentially damaging stimulus.

data.name: Lipid Peroxides
data.description: Lipid peroxides are oxidative degradation products of lipids, generated by a free radical chain reaction. Because of their abundance of reactive hydrogens, polyunsaturated fatty acids are highly susceptible to lipid peroxidation, which compromises the integrity and function of the cell membrane in which they reside.

data.name: Dynamical Systems
data.description: Dynamical systems describe an ensemble of particles whose state varies over time and thus obeys differential equations involving time derivatives. In order to make a prediction about the system’s future behavior, an analytical solution of such equations or their integration over time through computer simulation is realized..In mathematics dynamical systems refer to dynamical systems theory, an area of mathematics used to describe the behavior of the complex dynamical systems, usually by employing differential equations or difference equations. This theory deals with the long-term qualitative behavior of dynamical systems, and studies the nature of, and when possible the solutions of, the equations of motion of systems that are often primarily mechanical or otherwise physical in nature, such as planetary orbits and the behaviour of electronic circuits, as well as systems that arise in biology, economics, and elsewhere. Much of modern research is focused on the study of chaotic systems

data.name: Protein Databases
data.description: A protein database is one or more datasets about proteins, which could include a protein's amino acid sequence, conformation, structure, and features such as active sites. Protein databases are compiled by the translation of DNA sequences from different gene databases and include structural information. They are an important resource because proteins mediate most biological functions.

data.name: siRNAs
data.description: siRNAs (small interfering RNAs) are double-stranded RNA molecules 20–25 bases in length with 2 nucleotide overhangs that are produced through the enzymatic cleavage of longer precursor RNAs by the ribonuclease Dicer. siRNAs can limit the expression of specific genes by targeting their RNA for destruction through the RNA interference (RNAi) pathway.

data.name: Diffraction
data.description: Diffraction involves the scattering of particles/waves from a material. This affords structural information about the material or can be used as an effect to select, for example, certain wavelengths from a source.  The phenomena by which X-rays are reflected from the atoms in a crystalline solid is called diffraction.

data.name: Erectile dysfunction
data.description: Erectile dysfunction is the inability to achieve a penile erection sufficient for sexual intercourse. It can be physical or psychological in origin, and can have a profound effect on quality of life.

data.name: Carbohydrates
data.description: Carbohydrates (also known as sugars) are molecules consisting of a basic unit, usually a six-membered ring, containing carbon and oxygen, either alone (monosaccharides) or joined together (disaccharides, oligosaccharides, or polysaccharides). They have various biological functions, including energy storage, protein modification and regulation, and act as structural components of cell membranes.

data.name: Predictive Markers
data.description: Predictive markers indicate the likely response to a specific therapy, identifying whether a patient is expected to benefit from, be resistant to, or be harmed by a particular treatment.

data.name: Clinical Trial Design
data.description: Clinical trial design is a key aspect of the successful conduct of clinical trials. It involves deciding parameters such as the number of patients, the length of the trial, the comparator arm (in the case of randomized controlled trials) using information on current treatments, the anticipated effect of the therapeutic intervention being studied and applying biostatistics methods.

data.name: Mucositis
data.description: Mucositis is the inflammation and ulceration of the mucous membranes lining the digestive tract, commonly occurring as a side effect of chemotherapy or radiation therapy.

data.name: Sickle Cell Disease
data.description: Sickle cell disease is an autosomal recessive blood disorder that can lead to anaemia. It is caused by a mutation in the haemoglobin gene, which leads to deformation of red blood cells. Deformed red blood cells can obstruct small vessels and they are prone to destruction.

data.name: Neuropathic pain
data.description: Neuropathic pain is caused by disorders of, or damage to, the nervous system. The affected nerves can induce the sensation of pain in the brain. Neuropathic pain is often associated with the sensation of burning, coldness, "pins and needles", numbness or itching.

data.name: Auxin
data.description: Auxin is one of the major five plant hormones, mostly present natively as free or conjugated indole-acetic acid (IAA), a tryptophan derivative. Polar auxin transport is tightly regulated, and the hormone has a cardinal role in almost all important processes of a plant's life cycle, such as shoot and root growth, development, cell expansion and division, flowering, fruit maturing, organ patterning, and stress responses.

data.name: Scanning Electron Microscopy
data.description: Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) is an imaging technique that uses a focused beam of electrons to scan the surface of a specimen, producing high-resolution images of its topography and composition.

data.name: Hamster
data.description: Hamsters are burrowing rodents of the Cricetidae family used in biomedical research. Hamster cell lines are used in research and in the industrial production of recombinant proteins.

data.name: Caries Risk Assessment
data.description: Caries Risk Assessment involves evaluating a patient's likelihood of developing dental caries based on factors such as oral hygiene, diet, fluoride exposure, and medical history.

data.name: Learning Algorithms
data.description: A learning algorithm is a mathematical framework or procedure that calculates the best output given a particular set of data. It does this by updating the calculation based on the difference between the actual and desired output. These algorithms are typically concerned with representation and generalization of the input data.

data.name: Liver Diseases
data.description: Liver diseases are any diseases that affect the functioning of the liver. Liver diseases can be inherited (such as Wilson disease and alpha 1-antitrypsin deficiency) or acquired (for example hepatitis and liver cancer).

data.name: Photosystem II
data.description: Photosystem II is a multi-subunit protein embedded within the thylakoid membrane of chloroplasts, and the first protein complex involved in the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis. The protein complex uses light energy to oxidise two molecules of water to molecular oxygen, liberating four electrons and four hydrogen ions in the process.

synonyms: Photosystem II Reaction Center Complex D2 Protein

data.name: Ecological Network
data.description: Ecological networks are representations of the interactions that occur between species within a community. The interactions include competition, mutualism and predation, and network properties of particular interest include stability and structure.

data.name: Standardization
data.description: Standardization is the sociological process of reducing diversity in existing custom devices or practices, according to norms acceptable to a larger community of citizens, engineers or scientists. Standardization may facilitate technology transfers, enhance consistency or safety, and produce economies of scale.

data.name: Attention
data.description: Attention, in the field of psychology, refers to the cognitive process of selectively focusing awareness on specific stimuli or information while filtering out or ignoring irrelevant or distracting stimuli. It involves the allocation of cognitive resources to enhance perception, processing, and engagement with the target stimuli.

data.name: Psychophysics
data.description: Psychophysics is a field of methodology within psychology concerned with studying the sensation of stimuli. Psychophysics methods typically record the effect of systematic modulation of stimuli on a subject’s perception.

data.name: Guidelines and Law in Dentistry
data.description: Guidelines and Law in Dentistry involve the regulations, ethical standards, and legal requirements governing dental practice, ensuring patient safety and professional accountability.

data.name: Bone Marrow Transplantation
data.description: Bone marrow transplantation is the transference of bone marrow from one human or animal to another for a variety of purposes. Bone marrow transplantation can be used to treat certain blood disorders such as leukemia or immunodeficiency, but can also have serious complications such as graft-versus-host disease.

data.name: Glycolipids
data.description: Glycolipids are glycoconjugates of lipids that are generally found on the extracellular face of eukaryotic cellular membranes, and function to maintain stability of the membrane and to facilitate cell-cell interactions. Glycolipids can also act as receptors for viruses and other pathogens to enter cells. Gangliosides and cerebrosides that form glycosphingolipids (carbohydrate + sphingolipid) are two classes of glycolipids.

data.name: Voltage Clamp
data.description: Voltage clamp is a particular type of intracellular recording in which the membrane voltage potential of the cell is clamped at a desired value and the current crossing the membrane is measured.

data.name: Literature and Childhood
data.description: Literature and Childhood examines how literary texts depict childhood, including themes of innocence, growth, and education, as well as the representation of children in literature.

data.name: Nanophotonics and Plasmonics
data.description: Nanophotonics and plasmonics is the study of light at the nanometre-scale. Light can only be focused to a spot roughly half its wavelength in size (a few hundred nanometres for visible light). This limit can be surpassed by coupling light to electrons at the surface of a metal and creating surface plasmons.

data.name: DNA mismatch repair
data.description: DNA mismatch repair is a process that removes and replaces nucleotides that are erroneously inserted during DNA replication. Non-complementary bases on the newly synthesized DNA strand are recognized and excised, often with surrounding bases, to generate a gap that is repaired by copying the undamaged DNA strand.

data.name: ELISA
data.description: The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) is a sensitive method to quantify or test for the presence of antigen or ligand. Enzyme-linked antibodies (or ligand binding proteins) are used to bind an analyte on a solid substrate, and convert a colourless reporter molecule to a coloured or luminescent product for detection.

data.name: Spinocerebellar Ataxia
data.description: Spinocerebellar ataxia refers to a group of genetic, progressive neurodegenerative disorders of the spine and the cerebellum that can affect balance, coordination and speech.

data.name: Obstructive nephropathy
data.description: Obstructive nephropathy is defined as renal dysfunction resulting from obstruction of the urinary tract. The disease is characterized by inflammation, tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis.

data.name: Neural Stem Cells
data.description: Neural stem cells are multipotent adult stem cells present in the adult central nervous system that can self-renew, and give rise to new neurons and supporting cells called glial cells. Activation of neural stem cells or their transplantation into areas of central nervous system injury can lead to regeneration in animal models.

data.name: Cat
data.description: The domestic cat, Felis catus, is a small feline mammal used in the study of disease and behaviour. Over 250 hereditary diseases are shared between cats and humans, as well as some infectious diseases such as acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).

data.name: Fluoridation
data.description: Fluoridation is the addition of fluoride to public water supplies to prevent dental caries and improve oral health in the population.

data.name: Mouse
data.description: The house mouse, Mus musculus, is a small rodent and a classic vertebrate model organism for basic and biomedical research. It is attractive due to the existence of many well-characterized strains, the ability to make transgenics and to perform gene targeting by homologous recombination.

data.name: Arboriculture
data.description: Study of, and the selection, plant, care, and removal of, individual trees, shrubs, vines, and other perennial woody plants.

data.name: Lotus Japonicus
data.description: Lotus japonicus is a self-fertilzing plant in the legume family (Fabaceae) with a rapid life cycle, that serves as a model organism for the study of bacterial symbiosis for nitrogen fixation.

data.name: Electroencephalography
data.description: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a method for monitoring electrical activity in the brain. It uses electrodes placed on or below the scalp to record activity with coarse spatial but high temporal resolution. EEG can be used in cognitive research or to diagnose conditions such as epilepsy and sleep disorders.

data.name: Tooth Wear
data.description: Tooth Wear refers to the loss of tooth structure due to mechanical actions such as abrasion, attrition, and erosion, which can affect dental function and aesthetics.

data.name: Fungal Host Response
data.description: The fungal host response is the process by which the host interacts with and responds to fungi that colonize or infect it. This includes defense mechanisms such as the immune response.

data.name: Endocrine Reproductive Disorders
data.description: Endocrine reproductive disorders are disorders that affect the reproductive endocrine system and often result in fertility problems. Examples include ovarian insufficiency and polycystic ovary syndrome in women and low testosterone in men.

data.name: Ureter
data.description: A ureter is one of a pair of muscle-lined epithelial tubes that connect the kidneys to the bladder, enabling the flow of urine. Ureters can be adversely affected by cancer and urinary tract obstruction.

data.name: Malnutrition
data.description: Malnutrition is a condition that develops when a person's dietary intake does not contain the right amount of nutrients for healthy functioning, or when a person cannot correctly absorb nutrients from food. The term malnutrition includes undernutrition, overnutrition or an incorrect balance of nutrients.

data.name: Infertility
data.description: Infertility is the inability to conceive a child after a certain period of time, the length of which varies by country. The term can also refer to women who are unable to carry a pregnancy to term. Infertility has many different causes, including polycystic ovary syndrome and low sperm quality.

data.name: Platelets
data.description: Platelets are small, non-nucleated cells that are derived from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow. Platelets circulate in the blood, sense damage to a blood vessel and accumulate at these sites, where they initiate blood clotting.

data.name: Systems Analysis
data.description: Systems analysis is the study of a complex system’s interacting parts, while keeping a eye on their function in the integrated whole. Systems analysis is often called upon to evaluate the safety of complex systems that have grown haphazardly, as when computers and the internet faced the Y2K problem.

data.name: Asymmetric Catalysis
data.description: Asymmetric catalysis is a type of catalysis in which a chiral catalyst directs the formation of a chiral compound such that formation of one particular stereoisomer is favoured. Since the catalyst is not consumed in this process it may be used in a substoichiometric quantity – potentially improving efficiency and avoiding waste.

data.name: Ion Channels
data.description: Ion channels are integral membrane protein assemblies that modulate the flow of ions into and out of a cell or organelle, leading to generation of electrical signals. Opening (gating) of ion channels can occur upon stimulation with ligands such as second messengers, voltage, temperature and mechanical stress. The directionality of channels is dictated by the electrochemical gradient.

data.name: Peripheral Neuropathies
data.description: Peripheral neuropathies are a group of diseases that cause acute and/or chronic impairment or damage to the nerves belonging to the peripheral nervous system, such as motor nerves or sensory nerves.

data.name: Stereochemistry
data.description: Stereochemistry is the scientific concept that describes the relationship between chemical compounds which have the same molecular formula and identical functional groups but with different three dimensional arrangements of atoms. These molecules are known as stereoisomers and can have very different properties from one another, particularly when interacting with biological systems.

data.name: Astrophysical Dust
data.description: Astrophysical dust is dust which exists in outer space. It can be further distinguished by its astronomical location: intergalactic dust, interstellar dust, interplanetary dust and circumplanetary dust.

data.name: Gutta percha
data.description: Gutta percha is a material derived from the latex of certain trees, commonly used in endodontics to fill and seal root canals after cleaning and shaping.

data.name: Acute Kidney Injury
data.description: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a rapid deterioration in kidney function that occurs within 48 hours of an initiating event and is associated with an absolute increase in serum creatinine of  ≥ 26.4 µmol/l. Main causes of AKI include sepsis, ischaemia-reperfusion injury and nephrotoxins. Symptoms include fatigue, loss of appetite, headache, nausea and vomiting.

data.name: Time-lapse Imaging
data.description: Time-lapse imaging is a technique whereby serial images are taken at regular time points to capture the dynamics of what is being observed. Recorded images can be played back at different speeds to aid analysis.

data.name: Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy
data.description: Continuous renal replacement therapy is a procedure in which patients with acute renal failure are dialysed slowly over 24 hours. The procedure is particularly well suited to intensive care settings where critically ill patients might be intolerant to traditional intermittent haemodialysis.

data.name: Spike-timing-dependent Plasticity
data.description: Spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) is a process by which synaptic transmission is enhanced or depressed. In STDP, the precise relative timing of presynaptic and postsynaptic action potentials determines the strength of synaptic potentiation or depression.

data.name: Acute Inflammatory Arthritis
data.description: Acute inflammatory arthritis is an umbrella term that describes a group of disorders characterized by joint inflammation involving the immune system and sudden, painful onset.

data.name: Carbon-13 NMR
data.description: Carbon-13 NMR is the application of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to carbon and allows the identification of  carbon atoms in an organic molecule. NMR carbon-13 and 1H-NMR structural analysis of small molecules, proteins, nucleic acids analytical data are used in the characterisation of molecules.

data.name: Occlusion
data.description: Occlusion refers to the process of closure or blockage of a passage, opening, or space. It can involve the physical obstruction of a pathway, the contact or alignment of opposing surfaces, or the closure of a body part or structure.

data.name: Neurulation
data.description: Neurulation is the process in which the neural plate, a flat structure of ectodermal tissue in the vertebrate embryo, folds to form the neural tube, a hollow tube that gives rise to the brain and spinal cord. Certain congenital defects of the central nervous system such as spina bifida result from failure of the neural tube to close during neurulation.

data.name: Dyslexia
data.description: Dyslexia is a disorder characterized by an impaired ability to comprehend written and printed words or phrases despite intact vision. It can be developmental or acquired, but in either case it interferes with academic achievement or with activities of daily living that require reading skills.

data.name: Immobilized Enzymes
data.description: Immobilized enzymes are enzymes that have been attached, either through adsorption or crosslinking, to a solid support for experimentation or industrial purposes; for example, generating large quantities of products through biosynthesis. The inert, water-insoluble calcium alginate, as well as water-soluble matrices, can serve as the immobilization substrate.

data.name: Nucleotide excision repair
data.description: Nucleotide excision repair is a process that repairs damage to one strand of the DNA, particularly from UV irradiation, which distorts the DNA helix. The DNA flanking the damage site is cleaved to generate a single-stranded gap that is repaired by copying the undamaged strand to restore an intact helix.

data.name: Fever
data.description: Fever is defined as an increase in body temperature above the normal range, which can be caused by a wide range of conditions, including infection, inflammation or cancer. Treatment depends on severity.

data.name: Fluid- and Aerodynamics
data.description: Fluid dynamics is the study of the motion of liquids, gases and plasmas. Flow is dependent on the intrinsic properties of the matter itself, such as compressibility, viscosity and density. Example systems are a liquid flowing through a pipe or capillary, air moving across an aeroplane wing, and plasma motion in a stars magnetic field.

data.name: Microsatellite instability
data.description: Microsatellite instability is genetic instability in short nucleotide repeats (microsatellites) due to a high mutation rate as a result of abnormal DNA mismatch repair. Rather than correcting errors that occur spontaneously during DNA replication, cells with impaired mismatch repair accumulate these errors. These sequences are not preserved faithfully through DNA replication and novel microsatellites are created.

data.name: Thrombotic Microangiopathies
data.description: Thrombotic microangiopathies are a group of diseases caused by thrombosis in the microvasculature, they most frequently affect the brain and kidneys. Two prominent causes are thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura and haemolytic uremic syndrome.

data.name: Adrenal gland diseases
data.description: Adrenal gland diseases are disorders characterized by hyperfunction or hypofunction of the adrenal glands, resulting in either high levels or low levels of the hormones produced by the adrenal glands. Examples include pheochromocytoma and Addison disease.

data.name: Endocrine Cancer
data.description: Endocrine cancers are a mixed group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation of the hormone-producing glands of the endocrine system. These include the thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid and pituitary glands.

data.name: Brain Injuries
data.description: Brain injuries refer to a heterogeneous group of injuries that damage the brain. Common forms of brain injury include traumatic brain injury and stroke.

data.name: Obesity
data.description: Obesity is a condition in which excess fat has accumulated in the body, such that it can have an adverse effect on health. Obesity is defined as a body mass index (BMI) of greater than 30 kg/m2.

data.name: Fluorescence Spectroscopy
data.description: Fluorescence spectroscopy is the measurement of the fluorescence response of an excited sample.

data.name: Measles Virus
data.description: An infectious agent belonging to the virus family Paramyxoviridae that causes an infection of the respiratory system that is characterized by a maculopapular rash on the skin. The infection mostly occurs in children but is preventable by vaccination.

data.name: Genotyping and haplotyping
data.description: Genotyping and haplotyping are forms of genetic analysis that determine DNA sequence at sites of variation in a diploid (genotyping) or haploid (haplotyping) genomic complement. Haplotyping determines the specific combination of polymorphisms (sequence variants) along a chromosome that are inherited in blocks.

data.name: Quantitative Trait
data.description: A quantitative trait is a measurable phenotype that depends on the cumulative actions of many genes and the environment. These traits can vary among individuals, over a range, to produce a continuous distribution of phenotypes. Examples include height, weight and blood pressure.

data.name: Urinary Incontinence
data.description: Urinary incontinence is the involuntary leakage of urine from the bladder. It can be caused by increased bladder pressure, nerve damage, muscular dysfunction or medication.

data.name: Metabolic Bone Disease
data.description: Metabolic bone disease describes a diverse group of disorders of bone metabolism, most commonly caused by abnormalities of minerals (such as calcium or phosphorous) or vitamin D.

data.name: Stochastic Ordinary Differential Equations
data.description: Stochastic differential equations involve a “noisy” process. This means there is a random component to how the state of a system evolves over time. Ordinary differential equations, on the other hand, are deterministic; no random evolution is present.

data.name: Signal, Speech, Image and Video Processing
data.description: Signal, speech, image, and video processing is the field that analyzes, transforms, and interprets digital signals—from raw sensor data to human communication—using mathematical and computational methods to extract information, enhance quality, enable recognition, and support intelligent decision‑making.

data.name: Phospholipids
data.description: Phospholipids are lipids that generally consisting of three components: a diglyceride, a phosphate group and another organic molecule for instances choline to create phosphatidylcholine. Phospholipids are a major component of all cellular membranes and can form bilayers.

data.name: Sphingolipids
data.description: Sphingolipids are lipids with a sphingoid base backbone, bearing its own hydrocarbon chain, an amine group and two hydroxyl groups. The amine group is bonded to a fatty acid of varying length and one of the hydroxyl groups may be functionalized to a phosphate or carbohydrate. Sphingolipids are involved in signal transduction across membranes.

data.name: Autism Spectrum Disorders
data.description: Autism spectrum disorders are a group of neurodevelopmental disorders that are characterized by impaired social interaction and communication skills, and are often accompanied by other behavioural symptoms such as repetitive or stereotyped behaviour and abnormal sensory processing. Individual symptoms and cognitive functioning vary across the autism spectrum disorders.

data.name: Respiratory Distress Syndrome
data.description: Respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) is a condition commonly seen in premature infants, characterized by difficulty breathing due to insufficient surfactant in the lungs.

data.name: Locus coeruleus
data.description: The locus coeruleus is a nucleus in the pons that plays important roles in homeostasis, arousal and sleep, memory and emotions. Neurons of the locus coeruleus project to numerous brain areas including the spinal cord, cerebellum, hypothalamus, the thalamic relay nuclei, the amygdala, the basal telencephalon, and the cortex.

data.name: Urinary Tract Infection
data.description: A urinary tract infection is any microbial invasion that results in an inflammatory response in the epithelium of the urinary tract.

data.name: Photosystem I
data.description: Photosystem I is a multi-subunit protein complex embedded within the thylakoid membrane of chloroplasts, and the second protein complex involved in the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis. The protein complex uses light energy to drive the transfer of electrons across the thylakoid membrane, and the reduction of NADP to NADPH.

data.name: Skin Stem Cells
data.description: Skin stem cells are multipotent adult stem cells present in the adult skin, which can self-renew and differentiate into different cell lineages of the skin. Skin stem cells are active during skin renewal, which occurs throughout life, and in skin repair after injury.

data.name: Vision disorders
data.description: Vision disorders refer to a range of conditions that impair visual function, including refractive errors, cataracts, glaucoma, and retinal diseases, affecting one's ability to see clearly.

data.name: Dental Implant
data.description: A Dental Implant is a surgical component placed into the jawbone to support a dental prosthesis, such as a crown, bridge, or denture, providing a permanent solution for missing teeth.

data.name: Fluoride varnish
data.description: Fluoride varnish is a topical fluoride treatment applied to the teeth to prevent dental caries and strengthen tooth enamel.

data.name: Diffusion Processes and Stochastic Analysis on Manifolds
data.description: In mathematics, stochastic analysis on manifolds or stochastic differential geometry is the study of stochastic analysis over smooth manifolds. It is therefore a synthesis of stochastic analysis and differential geometry.  Stochastic analysis on manifolds investigates stochastic processes on non-linear state spaces or manifolds.  Brownian motion is defined to be the diffusion process generated by the Laplace-Beltrami operator can be constructed as the solution to a non-canoncial stochastic differential equation on a Riemannian manifold.

data.name: Fungal Pathogenesis
data.description: Fungal pathogenesis is the process by which fungi infect and cause disease in a host. Not all fungi are pathogens and have the ability for pathogenesis, also known as virulence.

data.name: Uniparental disomy
data.description: Uniparental disomy (UPD) occurs when both copies of a chromosome, or of part of a chromosome, are derived from a single parent. When these chromosomes are different, due to a meiosis stage I error, this is uniparental heterodisomy. When these chromosomes are identical, due to a meiosis stage II error, this is uniparental isodisomy.

data.name: Short-term potentiation
data.description: Short-term potentiation (STP) is the biological process by which synaptic transmission is transiently enhanced, usually as a result of an increase in synaptic vesicle release probability. Paired pulse facilitation is a well-known form of STP.

data.name: Bone Cancer
data.description: Bone cancer is characterized by uncontrolled growth of cells of the bone. Primary bone cancer (that arises directly in the bone), is relatively rare. Different types of bone tissue give rise to different types of primary bone cancer: osteosarcoma develops from cells that form the bone and Ewing sarcoma develops from immature nerve tissue within the bone.

data.name: Medaka
data.description: The medaka, Oryzias latipes (also known as Japanese rice fish), is a small fish with a rapid life cycle that is used as a model organism for the study of many biological subjects including behaviour, ecology, reproduction and development.

data.name: Auger Spectroscopy
data.description: It is a form of electron spectroscopy that relies on the Auger effect, based on the analysis of energetic electrons emitted from an excited atom after a series of internal relaxation events.

data.name: Sustainability
data.description: Sustainability is essentially the ability to endure, for example by exploiting resources in a way that does not deplete their future availability or unduly damage the wider environment. This concept has been incorporated in the idea of sustainable development.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Environmental Science (see also Chemistry / Environmental)

data.name: Antirrhinum
data.description: Antirrhinum is a genus of flowering plants commonly known as snapdragons. The perennial Antirrhinum majus is a model organism for plant developmental biology, particularly for the study of floral morphology and genetics.

data.name: Urban Economics
data.description: Urban Economics studies the economic functions and development of cities, focusing on issues such as land use, housing, transportation, and urban policy.

data.name: Carbon Nanotubes
data.description: Carbon nanotubes are cylindrical nanostructures composed of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice, derived from rolled-up sheets of graphene. They exhibit exceptional mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and thermal stability, making them valuable in fields like electronics, materials science, and nanomedicine.

data.name: CNS Cancer
data.description: CNS cancer is a type of cancer that forms in the central nervous system. It includes brain stem glioma, craniopharyngioma, medulloblastoma and meningioma.

data.name: Neurological Manifestations
data.description: Neurological manifestations refer to neurological signs and symptoms that are caused by a disease or injury that is not primarily neurological.

data.name: White Matter Disease
data.description: White matter disease refers to a group of heterogeneous disorders that involve degeneration of the white matter of the brain.

synonyms: Childhood Ataxia with Diffuse Central Nervous System Hypomyelination

data.name: Topological Insulator
data.description: Topological insulators are materials that are insulating in their interior but can support the flow of electrons on their surface. The underlying cause is time-reversal symmetry: their physics is independent of whether time is flowing backward or forward. These surface states are robust, maintained even in the presence of surface defects.

data.name: Olfactory System
data.description: The olfactory system is the sensory system that is responsible for the sense of smell (olfaction). It receives, processes and interprets odour information.

data.name: Lactobacilli
data.description: Lactobacilli are a genus of bacteria that are part of the normal oral and gut microbiota, known for their role in fermenting carbohydrates and producing lactic acid.

data.name: Epispadias
data.description: Epispadias is a congenital malformation of the penis in which the urethral opening is on the dorsum. It can also develop in females when the urethra develops too far anteriorly.

synonyms: Congenital disorders of male genital organs

data.name: Radiography
data.description: Radiography is the use of X-rays or gamma rays to examine non-uniformly composed material; images are recorded on a sensitized surface, such as photographic film or a digital detector. Medical radiography includes examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes, such as detecting fractures or a bowel obstruction.

data.name: Viral Reservoirs
data.description: Viral reservoirs refer to populations of viruses that persist in a host organism or environment, often in a dormant or low-activity state, allowing them to evade the host's immune response and antiviral treatments. These reservoirs can be found in various biological systems, including human tissues, animal hosts, or environmental sources, and play a crucial role in the transmission and re-emergence of viral infections. For example, in the context of HIV, viral reservoirs are cells where the virus remains hidden despite antiretroviral therapy, posing challenges for complete eradication. Understanding viral reservoirs is essential for developing effective strategies for disease control, vaccine design, and therapeutic interventions.

data.name: Chemical Modification
data.description: Chemical modification describes the modification, addition or removal, through chemical reaction, of any of a variety of macromolecules, including proteins and nucleic acids. It refers to the use of chemical reagents in vitro rather than to post-translational modification of biological molecules during biosynthesis in vivo.

data.name: Bacterial Synthetic Biology
data.description: Bacterial synthetic biology is a scientific discipline that deals with the synthesis of part, or the whole, of bacteria that do not exist in nature in this form. It uses engineering and molecular biology tools.

data.name: Atmospheric Dynamics
data.description: Atmospheric dynamics encompasses all physical processes within atmospheres, including global and regional-scale circulation, convection, tropical and extratropical cyclones, and interannual variability. Information about atmospheric dynamics informs both short range weather forecasting and projections for medium to long term climate change.

data.name: Bacteriophages
data.description: Bacteriophages are infectious agents that comprise viruses that infect bacteria. Bacteriophages are widespread, abundant and very diverse.

data.name: Neurovascular Disorders
data.description: Neurovascular disorders are a group of pathological conditions that result from infarction, ischaemic or haemorrhagic stroke of the brain or the spinal cord.

data.name: Saccades
data.description: A saccade is a biological process by which a rapid, small eye movement is made as the eye changes focus from one point to another within the visual field. Saccades generally are made towards stationary objects, but sometimes occur when the eyes need to catch up to a quickly moving target.

data.name: Aesthetic Dentistry
data.description: Aesthetic Dentistry focuses on improving the appearance of teeth, gums, and smiles through various cosmetic procedures, including whitening, veneers, and orthodontics.

data.name: Viral Transmission
data.description: Viral transmission is the process by which viruses spread between hosts. It includes spread to members of the same host species or spread to different species in the case of viruses that can cross species barriers.

data.name: Germ Cell Tumours
data.description: Germ cell tumours form from reproductive cells and can be cancerous or noncancerous. When cancerous, they normally develop as cancer of the testicles in men or of the ovaries in women. Germ cell tumours can be given different names according to their characteristics; for example, yolk-sac tumours, germinomas, embryonal carcinomas, teratomas and immature teratomas.

data.name: Archaeal Genes
data.description: An archaeal gene is a DNA sequence corresponding to protein-coding sequence or functional RNA, either from a cultured archaeon or inferred by phylogenetic clustering to originate in an archaeon. Due to similarity in operon organization and gene expression between archaea and bacteria, the definition of a novel genome sequence as archaean requires multiple sequence comparisons.

data.name: Genome assembly algorithms
data.description: Genome assembly algorithms are sets of well defined procedures for reconstructing DNA sequences from large numbers of shorter DNA sequence fragments. Fragments are aligned against one another and overlapping sections are identified and merged.

data.name: Zebrafish
data.description: Zebrafish (Danio rerio) is a small freshwater fish that is an extensively studied vertebrate model organism. It can be bred rapidly in large numbers, is amenable to genetics, and has a clear embryo, making it attractive to study vertebrate development, physiology and disease.

data.name: Diagnostic Markers
data.description: Diagnostic markers are biological parameters that aid the diagnosis of diseases. Examples include the presence of particular genetic variants and the levels of particular proteins in body fluids.

data.name: Porous Media
data.description: Porous Media refers to materials containing pores (voids) through which fluids can flow, studied in fields such as geology, hydrology, and materials science.

data.name: Blotting
data.description: Blotting is a technique for detecting nucleic acids or proteins by transferring them to a filter membrane. Molecules may be added directly to the membrane or separated by gel electrophoresis before transfer. Blotted nucleic acids are identified using labelled probes, whereas specific proteins are identified by immunodetection.

data.name: Nutritional Supplements
data.description: Nutritional supplements are any dietary supplement that is intended to provide nutrients that may otherwise not be consumed in sufficient quantities; for example, vitamins, minerals, proteins, amino acids or other nutritional substances. Products are usually ingested in capsule, tablet or liquid form.

data.name: Nephrons
data.description: The nephrons are the structures of the kidney that filter the blood and reabsorb water and other molecules. Each nephron consists of a tubule and a glomerulus.

data.name: Phosphorus metabolism disorders
data.description: Phosphorus metabolism disorders are the result of abnormal serum phosphate levels. These abnormal levels are caused by defects in the intake, excretion and cellular utilization of phosphate. Hypophosphataemia is a low blood level of phosphate, whereas hyperphosphataemia describes high levels of phosphate in the blood.

data.name: Replisome
data.description: The replisome is a large protein complex that carries out DNA replication, starting at the replication origin. It contains several enzymatic activities, such as helicase, primase and DNA polymerase and creates a replication fork to duplicate both the leading and lagging strand.

data.name: Transport Geography
data.description: Transport geography or transportation geography is a branch of geography that investigates the movement and connections between people, goods and information on the Earth's surface.

data.name: Rotavirus
data.description: Rotavirus is an infectious agent belonging to the virus family Reoviridae, which are important human and veterinary gastrointestinal pathogens. These viruses, particularly rotavirus A, are a leading cause of severe dehydrating diarrhoea (commonly known as 'stomach flu') in infants and young children.

data.name: Gustatory System
data.description: The gustatory system is the sensory system responsible for the perception of taste and flavour. In humans, the gustatory system is comprised of taste cells in the mouth (which sense the five taste modalities: salty, sweet, bitter, sour and umami), several cranial nerves, and the gustatory cortex.

synonyms: System for sense of taste and flavour

data.name: Antimicrobials
data.description: Antibiotics are substances that inhibit the growth of microbes such as bacteria, microscopic fungi or protozoans.

data.name: Prostatic diseases
data.description: Prostatic diseases are benign or malignant disorders that affect the prostate. The most common prostatic diseases are prostatitis, benign prostatic hyperplasia and prostate cancer.

data.name: Oxidoreductases
data.description: Oxidoreductases are enzymes that catalyze transfer of electrons from a donor (reductant) to an acceptor (oxidant) molecule, generally using nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADP) or nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) as cofactors. The name of the oxidoreductase generally takes the form of '[acceptor name] dehydrogenase'.

data.name: Intestinal stem cells
data.description: Intestinal stem cells are multipotent adult stem cells, which in mammals reside in the base of the crypts of the adult intestine. Intestinal stem cells continuously self-renew by dividing and differentiate into the specialised cells of the intestinal epithelium, which renews throughout life.

data.name: Biodiesel
data.description: Biodiesel is a renewable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional diesel fuel that is produced from renewable resources, primarily vegetable oils and animal fats. It is a type of biofuel that can be used in diesel engines without requiring any engine modifications.

data.name: Schizophrenia
data.description: Schizophrenia is a severe and debilitating psychiatric disorder that involves psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions, accompanied with regressive behaviour.

data.name: Ileum
data.description: The ileum is the final and narrowest part of the small intestine, continuing from the jejunum to the caecum of the large intestine, separated by the ileocoecal valve. Absorption of vitamin B12, bile salts and any digestive products or nutrients not absorbed by the jejunum occurs in the ileum.

data.name: Solid Biofuels
data.description: Solid biofuels are a type of renewable energy derived from organic materials in solid form. These materials are commonly of biological origin, such as wood, agricultural residues, grasses, and other biomass sources. Solid biofuels are used for heating, electricity generation, and other energy applications. They are considered a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels and contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

data.name: Bladder
data.description: The bladder is a muscular sac located in the pelvis that stores urine until it is excreted from the body through the urethra. Urine produced in the kidneys flows into the bladder via the ureters.

data.name: Meteorology
data.description: Meteorology is the scientific study of the atmosphere that focuses on weather processes and forecasting.

data.name: Hypothalamus
data.description: The hypothalamus is a brain area located below the thalamus. It consists of several nuclei with distinct functions, many of which involve regulation of the autonomic nervous system.

data.name: Phase I Trials
data.description: Phase I trials are conducted to provide initial indications about the safety of therapeutic interventions and, in the case of drugs, their pharmacodynamic and, pharmacokinetic properties. They involve a small number of subjects (typically 20 to 100), who are often healthy volunteers. In some areas, such as oncology, however, they may involve patients with the disease intended to be treated by the intervention, and so can also provide initial indications of therapeutic activity.

data.name: Mineral Trioxide Aggregate
data.description: Mineral Trioxide Aggregate (MTA) is a dental material used for root-end filling, pulp capping, and repair of root perforations, known for its biocompatibility and sealing ability.

data.name: Burning mouth syndrome
data.description: Burning mouth syndrome is a chronic condition characterized by a burning sensation in the mouth without an identifiable cause, often accompanied by dryness, altered taste, and discomfort.

data.name: Genetic Databases
data.description: A genetic database is one or more sets of genetic data (genes, gene products, variants, phenotypes) stored together with software to enable users to retrieve genetic data, add genetic data and extract information from the data. Genetic databases are repositories of organised data that are a resource for understanding how organisms function.

data.name: Panoramic Radiography
data.description: A panoramic radiograph is a panoramic scanning dental X-ray of the upper and lower jaw.

data.name: Wakefulness
data.description: Wakefulness is a state of arousal in which there is a conscious monitoring of the environment and there is potential for efficient responsiveness to external stimuli or threats. It is in contrast to the state of sleep in which there is reduced responsiveness to environmental stimuli.

data.name: Circadian regulation
data.description: Circadian regulation is the control of the cyclic variation of physiological processes over a 24 hour cycle. The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) in the brain is understood to be the 'master regulator' or 'central pacemaker' of circadian rhythms, and circadian oscillations of so called 'clock genes' in the SCN in turn influence other processes in a circadian manner.

data.name: Thermophotovoltaics
data.description: Thermophotovoltaics (TPV) is the direct conversion of radiant heat into electricity through the photovoltaic (PV) effect [1–4]. Photons radiated by a high temperature body (or emitter) are directed toward a closely spaced infrared-sensitive PV cell (or TPV cell) that subsequently produces electricity

data.name: Macular degeneration
data.description: Macular degeneration usually refers to the age-related degenerative changes in the retina that can result in loss of central vision. It is caused by abnormal blood vessel growth (a condition referred to as 'wet' macular degeneration) or atrophy and accumulation of debris ('dry' macular degeneration), both of which damage the macula.

data.name: Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies
data.description: The idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are a heterogeneous group of connective tissue diseases of unknown aetiology characterized by chronic inflammation of skeletal muscle, or myositis. The main types of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are polymyositis, dermatomyositis and inclusion-body myositis.

data.name: Literature and Disability Studies
data.description: Literature and Disability Studies explore the representation and experiences of disability in literary texts, examining how literature reflects, challenges, and shapes societal attitudes toward disability.

data.name: Transferases
data.description: Transferases are enzymes that catalyse the transfer of a functional group from a donor molecule, often a coenzyme, to an acceptor molecule. These include methyltransferases and formyltransferases for transferring single-carbon groups, methyl (CH3) and formyl (CHO) groups respectively, and transaldolases for transferring a three carbon ketol group.

data.name: Leukopoiesis
data.description: Leukopoiesis is the process through which leukocytes are generated from haematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow. The two major forms of leukopoiesis are myelopoiesis and lymphopoiesis. Myelopoiesis generates cells of the innate immune system, whereas lymphopoiesis gives rise to the cells of the adaptive immune system.

data.name: Pulp conservation
data.description: Pulp conservation in dentistry refers to treatment approaches aimed at preserving the vitality of the dental pulp, the innermost part of the tooth, often through minimally invasive procedures.

data.name: Antibody Therapy
data.description: Antibody therapy is a biologic treatment using monoclonal antibodies designed to target specific proteins, often on cell surfaces, and are produced using recombinant DNA technology. This therapy helps the immune system recognize and combat diseases like cancer, autoimmune disorders, and infections by binding to particular targets.

data.name: Oral Herpes
data.description: Oral Herpes is an infection caused by the herpes simplex virus, characterized by painful blisters and sores around the mouth and lips.

data.name: Renal Fibrosis
data.description: Renal Fibrosis is the formation of scar tissue in the kidneys, often resulting from chronic kidney disease or injury, leading to impaired kidney function and potential kidney failure.

data.name: Viral Evolution
data.description: Viral evolution refers to the heritable genetic changes that a virus accumulates during its life time, which can arise from adaptations in response to environmental changes or the immune response of the host. Because of their short generation times and large population sizes, viruses can evolve rapidly.

data.name: Targeted Gene Repair
data.description: Targeted gene repair is a technique used to correct a mutation at a specific site in an episome or chromosome. It uses synthetic oligonucleotides together with the cell's inherent DNA repair system to direct single base pair changes.

data.name: Nerve Conduction Studies
data.description: Nerve conduction studies are tests used to evaluate the electrical conduction in the motor nerves and sensory nerves. Nerve conduction studies are commonly used to evaluate and diagnose disorders that involve weakness or paraesthesia, numbness or unusual tingling or burning sensation.

data.name: Fungal Ecology
data.description: Fungal ecology is the scientific study of fungi and the ecosystem they are part of. It includes the interactions of fungi with their environment and with the organisms they share it with.

data.name: Neurotoxicity Syndromes
data.description: Neurotoxicity syndromes are neurological disorders that result from exposure to neurotoxic substances, such as pharmaceutical agents, pesticides, solvents, heavy metals, radiation or naturally occurring neurotoxic substances such as bacterial toxins.

data.name: Graft-versus-host Disease
data.description: Graft-versus-host disease is a potentially serious complication in a recipient of an allograft (usually a haematopoietic stem cell transplant) that arises from the attack of recipient tissues (such as the skin, liver or gut) by donor-derived T cells.

data.name: Spondyloarthritis
data.description: Spondyloarthritis is the name given to a group of phenotypically diverse chronic rheumatic diseases characterized by inflammatory spinal pain or synovitis, peripheral arthritis, enthesopathy, sacroiliitis, the absence of rheumatoid factor and a degree of heritability.

data.name: Gonads
data.description: Gonads are glands that produce gametes. The female gonads are the ovaries and the male gonads are the testes.

data.name: Organic LEDs
data.description: Organic LEDs are light emitting diodes (LEDs) that use polymers or small organic molecules as their optically active element. Development of organic LEDs is driven in particular by its potential as a display technology. Organic LEDs can be fabricated on flexible substrates, unlike their rigid inorganic counterparts.

data.name: DNA Synthesis
data.description: DNA synthesis is the biological process by which a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) molecule is created. In the cell, each of the two strands of the DNA molecule acts as a template for the synthesis of a complementary strand.

data.name: Duodenum
data.description: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine and begins after the stomach. The duodenum is the shortest part of the small intestine and is where most digestion takes place. Stomach emptying is regulated by the duodenum, via hormonal pathways.

data.name: Haematopoietic Cell Growth Factor
data.description: Haematopoietic cell growth factors are proteins that regulate growth and differentiation of red and white blood cells – haematopoietic cells. These include the cytokine SCF (stem cell factor), involved in proliferation and self-renewal of haematopoietic cells, as well as erythropoietin and colony-stimulating factors (CSFs), which stimulate the production of erythrocyte, granulocyte and macrophage blood cell lineages.

data.name: Retinal diseases
data.description: Retinal diseases encompass a range of conditions affecting the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, which can lead to vision loss and include disorders such as macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy.

data.name: Circular Dichroism Spectroscopy
data.description: Circular dichroism is the difference in the absorption of left- and right-handed circularly polarized light that occurs when a molecule contains one or more chiral, light-absorbing groups. It is used as a spectroscopic technique to study chiral molecules, particularly for analyzing the secondary structure of macromolecules such as proteins.

data.name: Pexophagy
data.description: Pexophagy is a type of macroautophagy that selectively degrades perioxisomes. Double-membraned autophagosomes enclose perioxisomes, and then fuse with lysosomes for degradation.

data.name: Long-term potentiation
data.description: Long-term potentiation (LTP ) is the biological process by which certain types of synaptic stimulation – such as prolonged high frequency input – result in a long-lasting increase in the strength of synaptic transmission. It is thought that the mechanisms underlying LTP, together with those underlying long-term depression, may contribute to synaptic plasticity during learning.

data.name: Digital Privacy
data.description: Digital privacy is the ability to protect information about an individual or group. Related concepts include human, societal, and economic aspects of information security privacy; privacy-preserving data mining and information retrieval, and related usability tradeoffs; differential privacy and other cryptography and information security approaches to defining and quantifying privacy loss; legal frameworks such as GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) in the context of information privacy and data protection; privacy-preserving authentication; privacy-enhancing technologies and privacy by design; and end-to-end security and encryption.

data.name: Biostatistics
data.description: Biostatistics is the application of statistical methods in studies in life and health sciences, and encompasses the design of experiments, the collection of data from them, and the analysis and interpretation of data. The data come from a wide range of sources, including genomic studies, experiments with cells and organisms, and clinical trials.

data.name: Periapical Radiographs
data.description: Periapical radiographs are probably the most familiar, with images of a few teeth at a time captured on small film cards inserted in the mouth.

data.name: Bacterial Development
data.description: Bacterial development is a process that allows bacteria to develop into different cellular states; for example, the formation of spores or the establishment of competence.

data.name: DNA Restriction-Modification Enzymes
data.description: DNA restriction-modification enzymes are enzymes involved in DNA restriction modification. They include DNA restriction endonucleases (restriction enzymes) and their companion modification methylase restriction enzymes, DNA methyltransferases and related proteins, which are generally found together in a multi-protein complex. DNA restriction-modification systems in bacteria protect cells against parasitic infection.

data.name: Biomethanol
data.description: Biomethanol, also known as renewable methanol or bio-based methanol, is a type of methanol that is produced from renewable feedstocks rather than traditional fossil fuels. Methanol is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CH3OH, and it serves as an important industrial chemical and fuel.

data.name: Heart Failure
data.description: Heart failure is a pathological condition in which the heart is unable to pump enough blood to the rest of the body, because it is either unable to fill with a sufficient volume of blood or unable to generate sufficient force to pump out enough blood; it is not a condition in which the heart has stopped pumping.

data.name: Molecularly Targeted Therapy
data.description: A molecularly targeted therapy is designed to specifically modulate the function of a protein or other cellular component linked to a particular disease; for example, specific inhibitors of protein kinase involved in cell proliferation are used to treat some cancers. Such therapies may often be used with companion diagnostics to identify patients that are most likely to respond favourably.

data.name: Paediatric Rheumatic Diseases
data.description: Paediatric rheumatic diseases is an umbrella term that encompasses the spectrum of musculoskeletal, arthritic and connective tissue disorders with onset in childhood.

data.name: Dental treatment planning
data.description: Dental treatment planning involves the systematic assessment and organization of dental care for a patient, including diagnosis, prognosis, and the development of a comprehensive treatment strategy.

data.name: Optical Biological Imaging
data.description: Optical imaging includes a variety of imaging techniques that rely on illumination light in the ultraviolet, visible and infrared regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. The term typically excludes classical microscopy techniques in favour of larger scale imaging methods that rely on the detection of ballistic or diffusive photons, or the photoacoustic effect.

data.name: Genetic Association Study
data.description: A genetic association study aims to test whether a given sequence, such as a region of a chromosome, a haplotype, a gene, or an allele, has involvement in controlling the phenotype of a specific trait, metabolic pathway, or disease. This usually involves comparing genotypes from two groups of individuals (often diseased subjects and healthy controls).

data.name: Phase II trials
data.description: Phase II trials are conducted to provide evidence of the effectiveness of a therapeutic intervention in patients and to determine the optimal treatment regimen (for example, dosing schedule) for investigation in Phase III trials, and also provide further information on safety. They typically involve 100-300 patients with the disease intended to be treated by the intervention.

data.name: RNA splicing
data.description: RNA splicing is a modification of the nascent pre-messenger RNA (pre-mRNA) transcript in which introns are removed and exons are joined prior to translation. For many eukaryotic introns, splicing is done in a series of reactions which are catalyzed by the spliceosome, a complex of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) and associated proteins, but there are also self-splicing introns.

data.name: Sexual Dimorphism
data.description: Sexual dimorphism consists of phenotypic distinctions between one sex and another. These distinctions can include physiological and behavioural differences.

data.name: Dental Anxiety and Phobia
