data.description: Dental Anxiety and Phobia refer to the fear and apprehension associated with dental visits and procedures, which can lead to avoidance of dental care and negatively impact oral health.

data.name: Open Reading Frames
data.description: Open reading frames (ORFs) are parts of a reading frame that contain no stop codons. A reading frame is a sequence of nucleotide triplets that are read as codons specifying amino acids; a single strand of DNA sequence has three possible reading frames. Long ORFs may indicate candidate protein coding regions in a DNA sequence.

data.name: Fungal Physiology
data.description: Fungal physiology is a scientific discipline that concerns the life-supporting functions and processes of fungi that allow fungal organisms to grow and reproduce.

data.name: Oligodontia
data.description: Oligodontia is a dental condition characterized by the congenital absence of six or more teeth, excluding the third molars, often requiring specialized dental treatment.

data.name: Protein Design
data.description: Protein design (or protein engineering) is a technique by which proteins with enhanced or novel functional properties are created. Proteins can be engineered by rational design, which typically uses computational tools to identify useful mutations, or by directed evolution, which uses random mutagenesis coupled with a selection process to identify desired variants.

data.name: Gene Targeting
data.description: Gene targeting is the process of altering a specific sequence or gene at its location in a genome. Potential modifications include deletion, insertion or replacement of endogenous sequence with alternative sequences. Targeting can be achieved by homologous recombination in some organisms (notably, mice), or with site-directed genome editing nucleases.

data.name: Osteonecrosis of the jaw
data.description: Osteonecrosis of the jaw is a severe condition characterized by the death of jawbone tissue, often associated with the use of bisphosphonates or other medications, leading to pain and exposed bone.

data.name: 3-D Image Reconstruction
data.description: 3D reconstruction is the process of generating a computer model of the 3D (3-dimensional) appearance of an object from a set of two-dimensional images. It is common in computer vision. In medicine, for example, it uses serial sections generated by computed tomography (CT), electron microscopy or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

data.name: Lymphopoiesis
data.description: Lymphopoiesis is the process in which lymphocytes (B cells, T cells and NK cells) develop from progenitor cells. B cell lymphopoiesis is completed in the bone marrow, whereas T cell lymphopoiesis occurs in the thymus.

data.name: Ferroelectrics and Multiferroics
data.description: Ferroelectrics and multiferroics are a class of materials that exhibit switching of their physical properties under an external influence. Ferroelectrics demonstrate a switchable electric polarization when an electric field is applied. Multiferroics exhibit a similar ‘ferroic’ behaviour in two or more of their (usually electric, magnetic or elastic) properties. + Ferroelectricity is a characteristic of certain materials that have a spontaneous electric polarization that can be reversed by the application of an external electric field.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Lipid-storage Diseases
data.description: Lipid-storage diseases are a group of disorders characterized by excessive accumulation of lipids due to inherited abnormalities in lipid metabolism. Excessive lipid deposition eventually causes damage to the cells and tissues, resulting in neurodegeneration and often also heart, liver, spleen and kidney problems.

data.name: RNA Sequencing
data.description: RNA sequencing refers to techniques used to determine the sequence of RNA molecules. It includes high-throughput shotgun sequencing of cDNA molecules obtained by reverse transcription from RNA, and next-generation sequencing technologies to sequence the RNA molecules within a biological sample in an effort to determine the primary sequence and relative abundance of each RNA molecule.

data.name: Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
data.description: Stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) generalize partial differential equations via random force terms and coefficients

data.name: Rectum
data.description: The rectum is part of the large intestine and is placed between the sigmoid colon and the anal canal. It stores stools before excretion via the anus. Rectal problems are common and include haemorrhoids, abscesses, incontinence and cancer.

data.name: Computer Ethics
data.description: Computer ethics, also known as cyberethics, is a branch of applied ethics that focuses on the ethical issues and dilemmas arising from the use of computers, digital technologies, and information systems. It deals with the moral principles and guidelines that govern the behavior and actions of individuals and organizations in the digital realm. Computer ethics address a wide range of ethical concerns related to privacy, security, data protection, intellectual property, digital rights, and the impact of technology on society as a whole.

subjects.term: Digital and information technologies: social and ethical aspects

data.name: Pheromone
data.description: A pheromone is a chemical substance that is secreted or excreted by an organism into the environment, which evokes physiological and/or social responses in one or more organisms of the same species. Perception of these chemical signals may be by olfaction or by contact.

data.name: Multistability
data.description: Multistability is the characteristic of a system that presents two or more mutually exclusive stable states. Bistable systems, for example, enable the implementation of logic gates, and therefore computation.

data.name: Oral-health-related Quality of Life
data.description: Oral-health-related Quality of Life refers to the impact of oral health on an individual's overall well-being, including physical, psychological, and social aspects of life.

data.name: Erythropoiesis
data.description: Erythropoiesis is the process by which red blood cells (erythrocytes) are produced. During human foetal development, erythropoiesis first occurs in the yolk sac, then in the foetal liver and then, in the third trimester and after birth, in the bone marrow.

synonyms: Process of Red Blood cells production

data.name: Cystic Fibrosis
data.description: Cystic fibrosis is a genetic disorder driven by CFTR mutations that affects the exocrine glands. Manifesting with excessively viscous mucus production, patients typically experience obstruction of passageways (e.g., pancreatic and bile ducts, intestines, and bronchi). Lung disease is responsible for the majority of morbidity in patients.

data.name: Mammary stem cells
data.description: Mammary stem cells are multipotent adult stem cells that reside in the mammary gland, can self-renew by dividing and can differentiate into all specialised mammary epithelial cells. Mammary stem cells drive the development of the mammary gland during puberty and are responsible for its expansion during pregnancy.

data.name: Fungal Genomics
data.description: Fungal genomics is a scientific discipline that concerns the genome, encompassing the entire hereditary information, of fungi. Fungal genomics can, for example, be used to study fungal evolution or outbreaks of fungal infections.

data.name: Osteoarthritis
data.description: The term osteoarthritis refers to a group of disorders that result in the primarily mechanically induced structural and functional failure of synovial joints.

data.name: Evolvability
data.description: Evolvability is the degree to which a biological system can evolve into a diversity of adaptive solutions to future environments. Two organisms with the same phenotype and fitness in a current environment may differ in their evolvability, owing to differences in the cryptic evolutionary potential of their genomes.

data.name: Thrombocytopaenic Purpura
data.description: Thrombocytopaenic purpura is a condition that leads to a reduction in the number of platelets, which are important for blood clotting. In most patients, the disease is thought to be caused by the immune system.

data.name: Sensors
data.description: Sensors are devices that detect and quantify physical aspects of the world around us. The measurement can either be read directly or converted to a signal for processing by electrical, hydraulic or pneumatic systems. Sensors can quantify everything from temperature, light intensity and mechanical stress to salinity, heart rate and blood pressure.

data.name: Membrane Lipids
data.description: Membrane lipids are lipids involved in forming the structure of biological membranes - both the cell membrane and intracellular membranes - and in membrane function, namely compartmentalization of biological processes. Membrane lipids consist primarily of phospholipids, glycolipids and cholesterol, which can be arranged in bilayers and organized with integral and peripheral membrane proteins to generate functioning membranes.

data.name: Autonomic Nervous System
data.description: The autonomic nervous system is the part of the peripheral nervous system that controls visceral functions such as heart rate, respiratory rate and digestion. It consists of enteric, parasympathetic and sympathetic nervous systems and is regulated by the central nervous system, but functions largely autonomously, without conscious control.

data.name: Antimicrobial Therapy
data.description: An antimicrobial therapy kills or inhibits the growth of microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, or protozoans. Therapies that kill microorganisms are called microbiocidal therapies and therapies that only inhibit the growth of microorganisms are called microbiostatic therapies.

data.name: Polycystic kidney disease
data.description: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is a genetic disorder whereby a large number of cysts develop primarily within the kidneys, but also in other organs. PKD can be autosomal dominant (one mutated gene required to develop the disease) or autosomal recessive (mutated genes are inherited from both parents leading to disease).

data.name: Sequence Annotation
data.description: Sequence annotation is the process of marking specific features in a DNA, RNA or protein sequence with descriptive information about structure or function.

data.name: Graph Theory
data.description: In mathematics, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects. A graph in this context is made up of vertices, nodes, or points which are connected by edges, arcs, or lines

data.name: Vertigo
data.description: Vertigo is a sensation of spinning or dizziness, often caused by inner ear problems or neurological conditions, affecting balance and spatial orientation.

data.name: Embryonic Induction
data.description: Embryonic induction describes the embryonic process in which one group of cells, the inducing tissue, directs the development of another group of cells, the responding tissue. Induction directs the development of various tissues and organs in most animal embryos; for example, the eye lens and the heart.

data.name: Forest Ecology
data.description: Forest ecology is the study of all aspects of the ecology of wooded areas, including rainforest, deciduous and evergreen, temperate and boreal forest. It includes the community ecology of the trees and other plant and non-plant species, as well as ecosystem processes and conservation.

data.name: Pharmacogenomics
data.description: Pharmacogenomics studies how the entire genome and its regulatory networks influence drug response, drug development, and therapeutic strategies. It integrates genomics, transcriptomics, and systems biology to understand multi‑gene and genome‑wide patterns affecting drug metabolism, efficacy, and toxicity, with the broader goal of improving and personalizing drug therapy.

data.name: Impaired Function
data.description: Disability is an umbrella term that encompasses congenital and acquired impairments to body function or structure, activity limitations and participation restrictions. A disability can be physical, cognitive, mental, sensory, emotional, developmental, or some combination of these.

data.name: Network Models
data.description: Network models are a computer architecture, implementable in either hardware or software, meant to simulate biological populations of interconnected neurons. These models, also known as perceptrons or multilayer connectionist models, process information based on the pattern and strength of the connections among the neuron-like units that compose them.

data.name: Replay
data.description: Replay is the process of watching a video or sound recording more than once. Replay is often used in studies of animal behaviour where individual aspects of the behaviour need to be measured or monitored.

data.name: Bacterial Genetics
data.description: Bacterial genetics is the study of the mechanisms of heritable information in bacteria, their chromosomes, plasmids, transposons and phages. Techniques that have enabled this discipline are culture in defined media, replica plating, mutagenesis, transformation, conjugation and transduction.

data.name: Spanish Literature
data.description: Spanish literature generally refers to literature written in the Spanish language within the territory that presently constitutes the Kingdom of Spain.

data.name: Depression
data.description: Depression refers to a state of low mood that can be accompanied with loss of interest in activities that the individual normally perceived as pleasurable, altered appetite and sleep/wake balance. Its severe form, major depression is classified as a mood disorder.

data.name: Solution-state NMR
data.description: Solution-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is the classical NMR spectroscopy approach used for molecular structure determination, where the experimental sample is studied while in solution.

data.name: Plaque
data.description: Plaque is a sticky film of bacteria that forms on teeth and gums, contributing to dental caries and periodontal disease if not regularly removed through oral hygiene practices.

data.name: Myelopoiesis
data.description: myelopoiesis in the broadest sense of the term is the production of bone marrow and of all cells that arise from it, namely, all blood cells.[1] In a narrower sense, myelopoiesis also refers specifically to the regulated formation of myeloid leukocytes (myelocytes), including eosinophilic granulocytes, basophilic granulocytes, neutrophilic granulocytes, and monocytes

data.name: Gas Separation
data.description: Gas separation refers to the process of separating individual gases or gas mixtures into their constituent components. This separation is achieved based on the differences in physical or chemical properties of the gases, such as molecular size, polarity, solubility, or diffusivity. Gas separation techniques are widely used in various industries and applications, including gas purification, air separation, gas processing, and environmental protection.

data.name: Oils
data.description: Oils in biological systems are lipids that are in liquid form at room temperature. Usually triglycerides, oils are made from glycerol and fatty acids.

data.name: Dental Anaesthesia
data.description: Dental anaesthesia refers to the use of anesthetic agents to induce loss of sensation in the oral region, enabling pain-free dental procedures.

data.name: Ribophagy
data.description: Ribophagy is a type of macroautophagy that selectively degrades ribosomes or ribosome-RNA complexes. Double-membraned autophagosomes enclose ribosomes, and then fuse with lysosomes for degradation.

data.name: Colon
data.description: The colon is the final part of the digestive tract. In mammals, the colon is made up of the ascending colon, the transverse colon, the descending colon and the sigmoid colon, which continues into the rectum. The colon's function is to extract water and salt from solid waste before excretion.

data.name: Antibiotic prophylaxis in dentistry
data.description: Antibiotic prophylaxis in dentistry involves the use of antibiotics before dental procedures to prevent bacterial infections, particularly in patients at high risk for endocarditis or other complications.

data.name: Catalyst Synthesis
data.description: Catalyst synthesis is the process of fabricating catalytic materials. It aims to optimize factors such as the catalyst activity, selectivity, stability and cost.

subjects.term: Conditions and laws of chemical reactions

data.name: Pox Virus
data.description: Pox virus is an infectious agent belonging to the virus family Poxviridae that can infect humans and animals. The most well-known human disease caused by these viruses, smallpox, has been eradicated.

data.name: ADHD
data.description: ADHD, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, is a neurodevelopmental disorder that involves problems with attention, concentration and/or increased activity levels, resulting in problems with school, work and social situations. Individuals with ADHD also often experience trouble with impulse control.

data.name: Olericulture
data.description: Olericulture is the branch of horticulture that focuses on the cultivation, production, and management of vegetable crops. It encompasses the study of various aspects of vegetable farming, including soil preparation, planting techniques, pest and disease management, irrigation, and harvesting. Olericulture aims to optimize the growth and yield of edible plants, ensuring they are nutritious, high-quality, and economically viable. This field also addresses the environmental impacts of vegetable production and promotes sustainable practices to enhance food security and support local economies. Olericulture plays a crucial role in agriculture by contributing to the diversity of food systems and providing essential nutrients to populations worldwide.

data.name: Gender Geography
data.description: Gender geography seeks to analyze how gendered social processes are linked to space, place, and scale. In this discussion, gender is defined as a social construct mediated by various axes of power that include race, class, ethnicity, and sexuality.

data.name: Combination Drug Therapy
data.description: A combination therapy is a therapeutic intervention in which more than one therapy is administered to the patient. Examples of combination therapy include treatment regimens that involve administering several separate pills, each containing a particular drug, or single pills that contain several drugs.

data.name: Bacterial Structural Biology
data.description: Bacterial structural biology is a scientific discipline that concerns the structure of bacterial macromolecules, especially proteins and nucleic acids. Such studies are used to understand the function and properties of components of the bacterial cell.

data.name: Neuroendocrine diseases
data.description: Neuroendocrine diseases are disorders that affect the interaction between the nervous system and the endocrine system. Examples of diseases of neuroendocrine origin include diabetes insipidus, Kallman syndrome, and neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), which are neoplasms that arise from cells of the endocrine and nervous systems.

data.name: Heterogeneous Catalysis
data.description: Heterogeneous catalysis involves a system in which the catalyst, reactants and products exist in two or more phases. Commonly, the catalyst is a solid material and the reactants are in a solution/liquid or gas phase.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Non-homologous-end joining
data.description: Non-homologous-end joining is the repair of double-strand DNA breaks by direct ligation of the broken ends. No homology is required to promote the end-joining reaction, but it is more error prone than recombination-based repair.

data.name: Slow-wave Sleep
data.description: Slow-wave sleep (SWS) refers to phase 3 sleep, which is the deepest phase of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, and is characterized by delta waves (measured by EEG). Dreaming and sleepwalking can occur during SWS. SWS is thought to be important for memory consolidation.

data.name: Reproductive Signs and Symptoms
data.description: Reproductive signs and symptoms are signs and symptoms associated with diseases of the reproductive system. For example, men with testicular cancer are likely to have one or more lumps in either or both testes and could experience lower abdominal pain.

data.name: Eye manifestations
data.description: Eye manifestations refer to ocular symptoms that result from a primarily non-ocular disorder or injury.

data.name: Enzyme Catalysis
data.description: Enzyme catalysis refers to the process by which enzymes facilitate and accelerate chemical reactions in living organisms. Enzymes are protein molecules that act as catalysts, meaning they increase the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed or permanently altered in the process.

data.name: Waxes
data.description: Waxes are lipids composed of esters between fatty acids and fatty alcohols. Waxes are water-insoluble, but soluble in organic, non-polar solvents. Waxes can be found in biological systems, for instance as beeswax and as epicuticular waxes in plants. Biological waxes are generally mixtures so are softer and melt more readily than the pure components.

data.name: Nanowires
data.description: Nanowires are structures with a width and depth of a few nanometres or less, but a much longer length. Electrons in these materials are free to travel along the wire, but their motion in the other two directions is governed by quantum mechanics, radically altering the properties of the material.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Phase IV trials
data.description: Phase IV trials are studies of therapeutic interventions following their market approval and are typically conducted to obtain additional data about the safety and effectiveness of the intervention; for example in broader patient populations than were studied in the Phase III trials that provided the basis for regulatory approval.

data.name: Guinea pig
data.description: The domesticated guinea pig, Cavia porcellus, is a rodent used in biomedical research including the study of bacterial infection.

data.name: Astrocyte
data.description: Astrocytes are the largest and most prevalent type of glial cell in the central nervous system. Astrocytes contribute to formation of the blood–brain barrier, participate in the maintenance of extracellular ionic and chemical homeostasis, are involved in the response to injury, and affect neuronal development and plasticity.

data.name: Fungal Evolution
data.description: Fungal evolution refers to the heritable genetic changes that a fungus accumulates during its life time, which can arise from adaptations in response to environmental changes or the immune response of the host. Because of their short generation times and large population sizes, fungi can evolve rapidly.

data.name: Biocatalysis
data.description: Biocatalysis is the chemical process through which enzymes or other biological catalysts perform reactions between organic components. Biocatalysis has been used widely in the pharmaceutical industry to make small molecule drugs.

data.name: Machining
data.description: Machining is a manufacturing process that involves shaping materials, typically metals, by removing material using tools such as lathes, mills, and drills.

data.name: Pruritus
data.description: Pruritus, commonly known as itching, is an uncomfortable sensation that provokes the desire to scratch, often associated with skin conditions or systemic diseases.

data.name: Musculoskeletal Abnormalities
data.description: Musculoskeletal abnormalities are congenital malformations or deformities of the musculoskeletal system that occur in isolation or as part of a syndrome.

data.name: Biliary Tract
data.description: The biliary tract is the anatomical term for the organs and ducts (the gall bladder, bile ducts and accompanying structures) involved in the secretion, collection, storage and transportation of bile into the duodenum.

data.name: Growth disorders
data.description: Growth disorders are disorders that affect the patient's height, weight and sexual development. These disorders are typically the result of atypical levels of growth hormone and patients can have either slow or fast growth. Examples include acromegaly and achondroplasia.

data.name: Parasite Biology
data.description: Parasite biology is the study of all biological aspects of parasites and parasitic diseases, including the structure, growth, development, genetics, ecology and evolution of these organisms.

data.name: Gestalt Psychology
data.description: Gestalt perception, in the field of psychology, refers to the theory and study of how humans perceive and interpret visual stimuli as organized wholes, rather than individual parts. It emphasizes the role of perception in organizing and structuring sensory information into meaningful patterns and configurations.

data.name: Refractive errors
data.description: Refractive errors are vision problems caused by the improper focusing of light on the retina, leading to conditions such as myopia (nearsightedness), hyperopia (farsightedness), and astigmatism.

data.name: Morality
data.description: Morality is a social process by which a person deems thoughts, intentions, choices or actions as either good (or right) or bad (or wrong). It can be based on a personal and/or a population's code of conduct or values.

data.name: Saccharomyces Cerevisiae
data.description: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, commonly known as baker's or brewer's yeast, is a unicellular fungus and a classic model organism used extensively for research in genetics and molecular biology. It is also used for the industrial production of some biopharmaceuticals.

data.name: Root canal treatment
data.description: Root canal treatment is a dental procedure to remove infected or damaged pulp from the interior of a tooth, followed by cleaning, shaping, and filling the root canals to save the tooth.

data.name: Phase Transition and Critical Phenomena
data.description: Phase transitions and critical phenomena are the changes of a system from one regime or state to another exhibiting very different properties, and the unusual effects that occur on the boundary between them. A change in the state of matter, such as from a solid to a liquid, is a classic example. + Phase transitions and critical phenomena are usual events associated with an enormous variety of physical systems (simple fluids and mixtures of fluids, magnetic materials, metallic alloys, ferroelectric materials, superfluids and superconductors, liquid crystals, etc.).Phase Transitions commonly describe transitions between solid, liquid, and gaseous states of matter, as well as plasma.Critical phenomena include scaling relations among different quantities, power-law divergences of some quantities described by critical exponents, universality, fractal behaviour, and ergodicity breaking.

subjects.term: Condensed matter physics (liquid state & solid state physics)
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Oral Manifestations
data.description: Oral manifestations are symptoms or conditions in the mouth that can occur as a result of diseases affecting other organs.

data.name: Mechanobiological Cell Signaling
data.description: Cell signalling is the mechanism by which stimuli are transmitted via a signalling cascade to effector molecules that orchestrate the appropriate response. Types of cell signalling pathways include checkpoint signalling, lipid signalling, growth signalling, nutrient signalling, insulin signalling, stress signalling, morphogen signalling, Hippo signalling, TOR signalling and integrin signalling.

data.name: Rubber Dam
data.description: A Rubber Dam is a dental tool used to isolate the operative site from the rest of the mouth, improving visibility and preventing contamination during dental procedures.

data.name: Phytomyxea
data.description: Some slime molds in Phytomyxea cause important diseases, including club root in cabbage and its relatives and powdery scab in potatoes. These are caused by species of Plasmodiophora and Spongospora, respectively.

data.name: TOR Signalling
data.description: TOR (target of rapamycin) signalling is a cell signalling pathway. TOR and its mammalian ortholog mTOR are serine-threonine kinases that sense growth factor, nutrient or oxygen status and promote appropriate changes in cell growth and proliferation, cell survival, and protein synthesis. TOR signalling has key roles in cancer and autophagy.

data.name: Joining
data.description: Joining refers to the processes and techniques used to connect materials, such as welding, soldering, and adhesive bonding, in manufacturing and construction.

data.name: Male Factor Infertility
data.description: Male factor infertility is the failure of a couple to conceive owing to a male-related factor. Male factor infertility can be caused by semen abnormalities (detected on semen analysis) or sexual dysfunction.

data.name: Rat
data.description: The rat is a medium-sized rodent from the genus Rattus. Rattus norvegicus (brown rat) is a model vertebrate reared in the laboratory for studying subjects such as genetics, physiology, disease and the effects of drugs.

data.name: Tropical Ecology
data.description: Tropical ecology is the study of all aspects of the ecology of tropical areas, which are those found approximately 23.5 degrees either side of the Equator. Notable tropical ecosystems include the rainforests of Amazonia, Africa and South East Asia, savannah grasslands and coral reefs.

data.name: Anxiety
data.description: Anxiety is characterized by excessive uneasiness, apprehension or dread. It can be generalized or be directed towards specific, usually imagined or exaggerated threat.

data.name: Vestibuloocular reflex
data.description: The vestibuloocular reflex (VOR) is a compensatory process by which the eyes move in the opposite direction to that of the head, stabilizing the retinal image of a visual target. The VOR is driven primarily by the vestibular system.

data.name: Neuromuscular disease
data.description: Neuromuscular disease refers to a group of heterogeneous disorders that impair the function of motor nerves, muscles or neuromuscular junctions. Symptoms can include muscle pain, weakness or atrophy, fasciculations or spasms, hypertonia and hypotonia.

data.name: Oenology
data.description: Oenology is the scientific discipline concerned with the production, chemistry, microbiology, and quality evaluation of wine. It focuses on the processes involved in transforming grapes into wine, including fermentation, maturation, stabilization, and sensory assessment.

data.name: Tumour-necrosis factor
data.description: Tumour-necrosis factors are cytokines that are secreted by immune cell such as monocytes and lymphocytes. Tumour-necrosis factors can cause cell death or T cell activation and proliferation by binding to their receptors as a homotrimer or heterotrimer.

data.name: Nephrosclerosis
data.description: Nephrosclerosis is defined as hardening of the small arteries and arterioles of the kidney. This process is normally associated with hypertension and can lead to renal ischaemia.

data.name: Acid, Base, Fluid, Electrolyte Disorders
data.description: The kidneys are responsible for maintaining the balance of acids, bases, fluids and electrolytes in the body, avoiding significant fluctuations that can lead to life-threatening conditions. Acid, base, fluid and electrolyte disorders occur in renal failure as a consequence of declining glomerular filtration rate.

data.name: Salivary Gland Diseases
data.description: Salivary Gland Diseases refer to conditions affecting the salivary glands, such as infections, blockages, and tumors, which can lead to symptoms like dry mouth, pain, and swelling.

data.name: DNA Nanomachines
data.description: DNA nanomachines are nanorobots made entirely or partially of DNA. DNA nanomachines can switch between defined molecular conformations and can be used as sensing, computing, actuating or therapeutic nanodevices.

data.name: Immunoediting
data.description: Immunoediting is a term used to describe the evolution of tumours such that the tumour cells are no longer effectively recognised and killed by the immune system.

data.name: Disorders of Consciousness
data.description: Disorders of consciousness refer to medical conditions that impair the individual's ability for self-awareness and interaction with the environmental stimuli.

data.name: Nanoparticles
data.description: Nanoparticles are particles that exist on a nanometre scale (i.e., below 100 nm in at least one dimension). They can possess physical properties such as uniformity, conductance or special optical properties that make them desirable in materials science and biology.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Surface Plasmon Resonance
data.description: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) spectroscopy is a technique to detect biomolecular binding interactions. In SPR, one molecular partner is immobilized on a metallic film. Light excites surface plasmons in the metal; when the binding partner binds to the immobilized molecule, this causes a detectable change in the surface plasmon signal.

data.name: Neutron Scattering
data.description: Neutron scattering, the irregular dispersal of free neutrons by matter, can refer to either the naturally occurring physical process itself or to the man-made experimental techniques that use the natural process for investigating materials. In simple terms Neutron scattering involves creating a beam of neutrons, passing that beam through a sample, and noting where (and possibly when) neutrons scattered from the sample hit a detector.

data.name: Organic-inorganic Nanostructures
data.description: An organic-inorganic nanostructure is a nanoscale structure (that is, a structure with single units sized between 1 and 1000 nanometres) composed of an intimate combination of inorganic and organic components. As such, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are an example of an organic-inorganic nanostructure.

data.name: Minimal intervention dentistry
data.description: Minimal intervention dentistry focuses on the prevention and early detection of dental diseases, employing conservative treatment methods to preserve as much natural tooth structure as possible.

data.name: Reverse engineering
data.description: Reverse engineering is an attempt to analyse how an unknown machine, natural or artificial, was designed to achieve its visible function. When such a machine is sufficiently modular, as with a TV set or an insect, reverse engineering can be achieved through perturbation of each of its parts in turn.

data.name: Oligodendrocyte
data.description: Oligodendrocytes are a type of large glial cell found in the central nervous system. Oligodendrocytes produce the myelin sheath insulating neuronal axons (analogous to Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system), although some oligodendrocytes (called satellite oligodendrocytes) are not involved in myelination.

data.name: Climate Change Management
data.description: Holistic and integrated way of managing climate change, including mitigation, adaptation, and risk management.

data.name: Osteoclasts
data.description: Osteoclasts are one of the three cell types found in vertebrate bones. While osteoblasts are responsible for the mineralised matrix production, osteoclasts carry out its resorption. The activity of osteoclasts and osteoblasts ensures the equilibrium in bone content, and is controlled partly by osteocytes.

data.name: Political Geography
data.description: Political geography is concerned with the study of both the spatially uneven outcomes of political processes and the ways in which political processes are themselves affected by spatial structures.

data.name: Immunoproliferative Disorders
data.description: Immunoproliferative disorders are a specific subgroup of immunological disorders characterized by abnormal proliferation of immune cells (e.g., lymphoproliferative diseases).

data.name: Inhibitory RNA techniques
data.description: Inhibitory RNA techniques are methods that use engineered RNA molecules to inhibit gene expression. Various approaches, including the expression or injection of microRNA, short inhibiting RNA, double-stranded or antisense RNA (e.g. morpholino oligomers), work via mechanisms that include transcript cleavage, sequestration and the inhibition of protein translation.

data.name: Neural Encoding
data.description: Neural encoding is the study of how neurons represent information with electrical activity (action potentials) at the level of individual cells or in networks of neurons. Studies of neural encoding aim to characterize the relationship between sensory stimuli or behavioural output and neural signals.

data.name: Somatic system
data.description: The somatic system refers to the part of the peripheral nervous system that is responsible for somatosensory function; that is, voluntary control of movement and sensing external stimuli. The somatic nervous system innervates skeletal muscles and sensory organs, and carries and integrates motor and sensory information.

data.name: Microfinance
data.description:
Microfinance refers to the financial services provided to low-income individuals or groups who are typically excluded from traditional banking. Most microfinance institutions focus on offering credit in the form of small working capital loans, sometimes called microloans or microcredit. However, many also provide insurance and money transfers, and regulated microfinance banks provide savings accounts.

Microfinance aims to improve financial services access for marginalized groups, especially women and the rural poor, to promote self-sufficiency.

data.name: Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
data.description: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy or surface-enhanced Raman scattering is a surface-sensitive technique that enhances Raman scattering by molecules adsorbed on rough metal surfaces or by nanostructures such as plasmonic-magnetic silica nanotubes

data.name: Drosophila
data.description: Drosophila is a genus of two-winged flies commonly known as fruit flies that are used in evolutionary and developmental studies. D. melanogaster is an important model organism for the study of genetics and development.

data.name: SARS Virus
data.description: SARS virus is an infectious agent belonging to the virus family Coronaviridae, which causes severe respiratory illnesses in humans and animals. SARS (severe acute respiratory syndrome) coronavirus (CoV) is a novel member of this family that causes acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), which is associated with high mortality rates.

data.name: Tobacco
data.description: Tobacco (Nicotiana tabacum) is a flowering plant in the nightshade family (Solonaceae) cultivated as a crop. Its leaves, which contain the stimulant nicotine, are dried and consumed primarily by smoking or chewing. The plant is a model organism for plant molecular biology.

data.name: Hydrocephalus
data.description: Hydrocephalus refers to the medical condition in which an excessive amount of cerebrospinal fluid accumulates within the cranium. It often results in enlarged cerebral ventricles and increased intracranial pressure, which can be fatal.

data.name: miRNAs
data.description: micro RNAs (miRNAs) are a type of non-coding RNA (ncRNA), ~21–24 nucleotides in length, that function in the post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression. Typically miRNAs interact with specific mRNAs through complementary base-pairing to influence the translation or stability of the target mRNA molecule.

data.name: Hepatocyte Growth Factor
data.description: Hepatocyte growth factor is a protein secreted by mesenchymal stem cells that regulates cell growth, cell motility and morphogenesis of epithelial cells, endothelial cells, and haematopoietic stem cells, through its receptor, c-Met. Signalling downstream of c-Met leads to cell identity changes that take place during organ development, angiogenesis and other morphogenesis processes.

data.name: Quantum Dots
data.description: Quantum dots are crystals of a fluorescent semiconductor material with a diameter of as few as 10 to 100 atoms (2-10 nm). They are used as labels for imaging molecules because of their very narrow fluorescence spectra, brightness and resistance to photobleaching.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Caries Sealants
data.description: Caries Sealants are protective coatings applied to the chewing surfaces of teeth to prevent dental caries (cavities) by sealing out food particles and bacteria.

data.name: Nutrigenomics
data.description: Nutrigenomics is the study of the effects of food and food constituents on gene expression, and how genetic variations affect the nutritional environment. It focuses on understanding the interaction between nutrients and other dietary bioactives with the genome at the molecular level, to understand how specific nutrients or dietary regimes may affect human health.

data.name: Piwi RNAs
data.description: Piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) are a large class of small non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), 26–31 nucleotides in length, that interact with piwi-domain-containing proteins. piRNAs function in the germline to silence genetic elements such as retrotransposons and in RNA silencing as components of the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC).

data.name: Food Web
data.description: Food webs are ecological networks of consumption interactions, including the relationships between different trophic levels such as primary producers, herbivores, predators and decomposers. Key areas of the study of food webs are their stability and how energy and nutrients flow through them.

data.name: Antibiotics in Dentistry
data.description: Antibiotics in Dentistry are used to treat and prevent bacterial infections in the oral cavity, particularly in cases of severe dental infections, abscesses, and post-surgical prophylaxis.

data.name: Cone-beam Computed Tomography
data.description: Cone beam computed tomography (or CBCT, also referred to as C-arm CT, cone beam volume CT, flat panel CT or Digital Volume Tomography (DVT)) is a medical imaging technique consisting of X-ray computed tomography where the X-rays are divergent, forming a cone

data.name: Homogeneous Catalysis
data.description: Homogeneous catalysis is a type of catalysis in which the catalyst operates in the same phase as the reactants — usually dissolved in a solvent. Mechanistic studies of homogeneous catalysts are generally easier than those of heterogeneous catalysts, which aids optimization.

data.name: Addiction
data.description: Addiction involves loss of control over use of a substance, often in the presence of physiological and psychological dependence on a substance and compulsion to continue seeking and using the substance despite possible negative consequences.

data.name: Protein Sequencing
data.description: Protein sequencing refers to methods for determining the amino acid sequence of proteins (or peptides) and analysis of the sequence, for example to infer protein conformation. Techniques include mass spectrometry and the Edman degradation reaction as well as prediction of the protein sequence from the encoding DNA or mRNA sequence.

data.name: Single-channel recording
data.description: Single-channel recording is a single-molecule technique that measures the activity of a single membrane channel, usually by means of a patch pipette.

data.name: Catalytic Mechanism
data.description: A catalytic mechanism is the sequence of elementary reactions by which a catalytic reaction proceeds.

data.name: RNAi Therapy
data.description: RNAi Therapy involves the use of RNA interference (RNAi) technology to silence specific genes, offering potential treatments for various genetic disorders and diseases.

data.name: Turf Management
data.description: Turf management is the science and practice of maintaining and cultivating turfgrass, which is the grass grown for lawns, sports fields, golf courses, and other recreational areas. This field encompasses a variety of activities including soil preparation, seeding, fertilization, irrigation, pest control, and mowing, all aimed at promoting healthy grass growth and aesthetic appeal. Turf management integrates principles from agronomy, horticulture, and environmental science to optimize turf health, resilience, and sustainability. Effective turf management practices consider factors such as grass species selection, climate conditions, soil type, and intended use of the turf area, ensuring that the turf can withstand wear and environmental stresses while providing functional and visual benefits.

data.name: Italian Literature
data.description: Italian literature is written in the Italian language, particularly within Italy. It may also refer to literature written by Italians or in other languages spoken in Italy, often languages that are closely related to modern Italian, including regional varieties and vernacular dialects.

data.name: Conjunctival Diseases
data.description: Conjunctival Diseases refer to medical conditions affecting the conjunctiva, the thin membrane covering the white part of the eye and the inner eyelids, such as conjunctivitis and pterygium.

data.name: Prostate
data.description: The prostate is a secretory gland situated in the pelvis of males; it sits underneath the bladder and surrounds the urethra. Fluid produced by the prostate is the main component of semen.

data.name: Base excision repair
data.description: Base excision repair is a process that removes and replaces damaged or misincorporated bases in one strand of the DNA that may generate mutations if left unrepaired. The damaged base is modified and excised to create a single-stranded DNA break that is repaired to regenerate an intact helix.

data.name: Phytoplasma
data.description: Phytoplasmas are specialized bacteria that belong to the class Mollicutes. They are obligate plant pathogens, meaning they can only survive and reproduce within plant cells. Phytoplasmas are responsible for causing diseases known as phytoplasma diseases or yellows diseases in a wide range of plants, including agricultural crops, ornamental plants, and trees.

synonyms: Aster yellows phytoplasma (specific phytoplasma strain causing a widespread disease)
Candidatus Phytoplasma (followed by the specific strain name)

data.name: Genetic Mapping
data.description: Genetic mapping is the process of determining the order of and relative distance between genetic markers (specific sequences or heritable elements that generate a phenotype) on a chromosome based on their pattern of inheritance. Genetic mapping in bacteria relies on chromosome transfer between cells.

data.name: Patch Clamp
data.description: Patch clamp is a type of intracellular recording that relies on attaching a flat open tip glass pipette to the outer membrane of a single cell by means of suction and then recording the activity of ion channels in the membrane.

data.name: Phase 0 trials
data.description: Phase 0 trials are conducted to obtain preliminary data on the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of an investigational therapeutic. They involve the administration of single subtherapeutic doses (often called microdoses) of the therapeutic to a small number of subjects (typically 10 to 15).

data.name: Ocular Hypertension
data.description: Ocular Hypertension is a condition characterized by higher-than-normal intraocular pressure without detectable damage to the optic nerve or vision loss, which can be a risk factor for glaucoma.

data.name: Respiratory Signs and Symptoms
data.description: Respiratory signs and symptoms are the physical manifestations of diseases in the lungs or respiratory tract. These can be caused by respiratory tract diseases, such as pneumonia or pulmonary fibrosis, or can be secondary to other diseases, particularly cardiovascular diseases. Examples include shortness of breath, sneezing and wheezing.

data.name: Brainstem
data.description: The brainstem is a part of the brain that connects the cerebrum with the spinal cord. It comprises the mesencenphalon or midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata, and contributes to motor and sensory innervation, cardiovascular and respiratory control, and consciousness.

data.name: Neurodegeneration
data.description: Neurodegeneration refers to the progressive atrophy and loss of function of neurons, which is present in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease.

data.name: Renal Calculi
data.description: Renal culculi are commonly known as kidney stones and consist of usually crystalline deposits that accumulate in the kidney. These deposits vary in size, and most contain calcium oxalate.

data.name: Literature, Science and Medicine Studies
data.description: Literature, Science and Medicine Studies explore the intersections between literary texts, scientific knowledge, and medical practices, analyzing how literature reflects and influences scientific and medical discourses.

data.name: Spinal Cord Diseases
data.description: Spinal cord diseases are a heterogeneous group of conditions that cause damage or dysfunction of the spinal cord. They include infections, inflammatory disorders, vascular diseases and disorders that affect the meninges or perimeningeal spaces that surround the spinal cord.

data.name: Computational Methods for Stochastic Equations
data.description: Computational Methods for Stochastic Equations refer to a set of numerical techniques and algorithms used to solve and analyze mathematical equations that involve randomness or uncertainty, typically in the form of stochastic processes or random variables. Stochastic equations are mathematical models used to describe systems or processes that exhibit random behavior.

synonyms: Monte Carlo Methods for Stochastic Equations

data.name: Heart Stem Cells
data.description: Heart stem or progenitor cells are multipotent cells residing in the adult mammalian heart that are capable of self-renewing and generating coronary vessels and heart muscle cells called cardiomyocytes. Heart stem cells can contribute to new cardiomyocyte formation following experimental myocardial infarction in mice.

data.name: Nanopores
data.description: Nanopores are nanoscale pores in electrically insulating materials used to study the physical properties of biomolecules by measuring changes in current as individual molecules transit. Nanopore arrays are constructed from channel proteins in lipid membranes or from pores patterned in synthetic materials, and can sequence DNA or characterize protein folding.

data.name: Nanometrology
data.description: Nanometrology is a branch of metrology concerned with measurements at the nanoscale. It develops both new measurement techniques and standards. Some of the most common techniques used in nanometrology are atomic force microscopy, electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction.

data.name: Spiroplasma
data.description: Spiroplasma is a genus of bacteria belonging to the class Mollicutes. They are helical or spiral-shaped prokaryotes, known for their unique twisting or corkscrew appearance. Spiroplasma species are typically found in various environments, including plants, arthropods (such as insects and ticks), and other animals.

data.name: Materials Fatigue
data.description: Fatigue (of a material) is the process of progressive localized plastic deformation occurring in a material subjected to cyclic stresses and strains at high stress concentration locations that may culminate in cracks or complete fracture after a sufficient number of fluctuations.

subjects.term: Properties of materials and nondestructive testing

data.name: Valvular Disease
data.description: Valvular disease is a pathological condition affecting one or more of the heart valves.

data.name: Jejunum
data.description: The jejunum is the second part of the small intestine, between the duodenum and ileum sections. The main function of the jejunum is absorption of nutrients that have undergone enzymatic digestion in the duodenum.

data.name: Cardiovascular Genetics
data.description: Cardiovascular genetics is the study of the genetic mechanisms of cardiovascular physiology and pathophysiology.

data.name: Cysts
data.description: A cyst is a closed cluster of cells forming a sac that is surrounded by a membrane. The cells in this membrane are different in appearance and behaviour from the surrounding cells in that location. Cysts contain air, fluids, or semi-solid material and they can be formed from normal, abnormal, non-neoplastic or neoplastic tissues.

data.name: Glycomics
data.description: Glycomics is a subset of the field of glycobiology that aims to identify the structure and function of the complete set of glycans (the glycome) produced in a given cell or organism and identify all the genes that encode glycoproteins.

data.name: Dystonia
data.description: Dystonia refers to a movement disorder characterized by abnormal posture or movements, caused by involuntary muscle contractions or cramps.

data.name: Crop Waste
data.description: Crop waste, also known as agricultural or crop residues, refers to the parts of crops that are left behind after the primary harvest of the main crop or commodity. These are the non-edible parts of plants that remain unused after the harvest and are often considered as byproducts of agricultural production. Crop waste can include various plant materials such as stems, leaves, husks, shells, and other parts that are not part of the primary harvested product.

data.name: Cross-Coupling Reaction
data.description: Cross-coupling reactions are those in which two different starting materials, each of which is usually endowed with an activating group, are reacted together with the aid of a metal catalyst. The result is the loss of the two activating groups and the formation of a new covalent bond between the remaining fragments.

data.name: Dental post graduate education
data.description: Dental post graduate education refers to advanced training programs for dentists, including residencies, fellowships, and specialty certifications, aimed at enhancing clinical skills and knowledge.

data.name: Embryonic Germ Cells
data.description: Embryonic germ cells are pluripotent stem cells derived from the early embryo that have the potential to differentiate into gametes, which are the reproductive cells in sexually reproducing organisms. In animals, these gametes include sperm cells in males and egg cells (ova) in females. Germ cells are crucial for sexual reproduction as they carry genetic information to the next generation.

data.name: Resorption
data.description: Resorption in dentistry refers to the process by which the body breaks down and absorbs bone or tooth structure, which can occur due to trauma, infection, or orthodontic treatment.

data.name: Genetic Linkage
data.description: A genetic linkage study is a family-based method used to map a trait to a genomic location by demonstrating co-segregation of the disease with genetic markers of known chromosomal location; locations identified are more likely to contain a causal genetic variant. This technique is particularly useful for the identification of genes that are inherited in a Mendelian fashion.

data.name: Rubisco
data.description: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco) is a copper-containing enzyme involved in the first major step of carbon fixation. It is the central enzyme of photosynthesis and probably the most abundant protein on Earth.

data.name: Biofortification
data.description: Biofortification is the process of increasing the nutritional value of crops through conventional breeding or genetic modification to address micronutrient deficiencies in populations.

data.name: Glial stem cells
data.description: Glial stem cells are self-renewing cells that have the capacity to produce some or all forms of glia.

data.name: REM sleep
data.description: REM sleep (random eye movement sleep) is the fourth stage of sleep in which the eyes can be seen to be moving rapidly behind the eyelids. It is associated with increased brain activity and dreaming, but decreased muscle tone.

data.name: Chemical Process Reliability
data.description: The reliability of a chemical analytical method is a composite property of the method. This composite property may be resolved into four more elementary properties which may be designated as (1) specificity, (2) accuracy, (3) precision, and (4) sensitivity.

data.name: Haematopoietic Stem Cells
data.description: Haematopoietic stem cells are progenitor cells that have the ability to both generate all types of blood cells, including those of the myeloid and lymphoid lineages, and to replace themselves. In adults, they mainly reside in the bone marrow.

data.name: Polyhydroxyalkanoates
data.description: Polyhydroxyalkanoates are linear polyesters generated by fermentation of sugars or lipids. They are generally made and used by bacteria to store energy and commercially to make bioplastics. Formation of polyhydroxyalkanoates from hydroxy fatty acids of short (3-5 carbons) or medium (6-14 carbons) chain length is catalysed by the polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) synthase enzymes.

data.name: Gastroenteritis
data.description: Gastroenteritis is inflammation of any section of the gastrointestinal tract, from the oesophagus to the rectum. This inflammation can be caused by a number of factors, including genetics, infection, hypersensitivity, drugs and cancer. Depending on the location and cause, symptoms can include diarrhoea, vomiting and abdominal pain.

data.name: Electromyography
data.description: Electromyography (EMG) is a method to record the electrical activity of skeletal muscle. It uses a thin needle electrode inserted into the muscle through the skin and can be used to diagnose neurological and other disorders that affect muscle function.

data.name: Social Work and Community Development
data.description: Studies processes that help to develop local communities; it is a very much practice-orientated or applied discipline, based on sustainable development, economics, equality, social justice, resilience, and the work of social insitutions.

subjects.term: POLITICAL SCIENCE / Public Policy / Social Policy

data.name: Dental patient management
data.description: Dental patient management encompasses the strategies and practices used by dental professionals to effectively care for and communicate with patients, ensuring positive treatment outcomes and patient satisfaction.

data.name: Hypoxia
data.description: Hypoxia is a condition in which insufficient levels of oxygen are supplied to one or more tissues in the body.

data.name: Oncostatin M
data.description: Oncostatin M is a secreted cytokine, and is related to leukaemia inhibitory factor. Oncostatin M functions in differentiation and development of various cell lineages, cell proliferation, and haematopoiesis. The transmembrane receptor for Oncostatin M on responding cells is a heterodimer between the glycoprotein gp130 and either CD118/LIFR or OSMR.

data.name: Eye abnormalities
data.description: Eye abnormalities refer to any deviations from the normal structure or function of the eye, which can affect vision and overall ocular health.

data.name: Energy Metabolism
data.description: Energy metabolism is the process of generating energy (ATP) from nutrients. Metabolism comprises a series of interconnected pathways that can function in the presence or absence of oxygen. Aerobic metabolism converts one glucose molecule into 30-32 ATP molecules. Fermentation or anaerobic metabolism is less efficient than aerobic metabolism.

data.name: Habituation
data.description: Habituation occurs upon repeated presentation of stimulus such that the innate physiological or behavioural response to that stimulus is gradually diminished.

data.name: Hydroenergy
data.description: Hydroenergy/Hydropower, or hydroelectric power, is a renewable source of energy that generates power by using a dam or diversion structure to alter the natural flow of a river or other body of water.

data.name: Holoenzymes
data.description: Holoenzymes are the active forms of enzymes. Enzymes that require a cofactor but are not bound by one are called apoenzymes. Holoenzymes represent the apoenzyme bound to its necessary cofactors or prosthetic groups.

data.name: Semen analysis
data.description: Semen analysis is the term used for the laboratory techniques and procedures that are performed to measure sperm parameters, including number, motility, morphology and viability. Semen analysis is commonly performed to assess male factor infertility.

data.name: Fissure seal
data.description: Fissure seal refers to the application of a protective coating to the grooves and pits of teeth, particularly molars, to prevent dental caries by sealing out food particles and bacteria.

data.name: Embryonal Neoplasms
data.description: Embryonal neoplasms are tumours formed from a mass of rapidly growing cells that begin in embryonic (fetal) tissue and express one or more embryo-exclusive genes. They account for 2-3 % of germ cell tumours. They can be benign or malignant. The disease type does not include neoplasms located in an embryo or foetus.

data.name: Strigolactone
data.description: Strigolactones are a class of plant hormones that stimulate branching in plants and the growth of symbiotic arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in the soil. They also impede shoot branching and trigger the germination of parasitic plant seeds.

data.name: Vitiligo
data.description: Vitiligo is a skin disease that is characterized by loss of pigmentation caused by death or dysfunction of melanocytes, which are pigment producing cells. Autoimmune processes, oxidative stress, genetic factors and environmental triggers all have been implicated in the pathogenesis of the disease.

data.name: Ascomycetes
data.description: Ascomycota is a phylum of the kingdom Fungi that, together with the Basidiomycota, forms the subkingdom Dikarya. Its members are commonly known as the sac fungi or ascomycetes.

data.name: Lymphokine
data.description: Lymphokines are cytokines produced by T cells (lymphocytes) of the immune system. Lymphokines act to attract additional immune cells to mount an immune response, for instance in stimulating B cells to generate antibodies against the invading pathogen.

data.name: Macroautophagy
data.description: Macroautophagy is a process in which cellular contents are degraded by lysosomes or vacuoles and recycled. Double-membraned structures called autophagosomes enclose cellular material and then fuse with lysosomes. Non-selective macroautophagy is stimulated by starvation. Organelle-specific macroautophagy processes such as mitophagy, pexophagy and ribophagy remove damaged organelles.

data.name: Schwann cell
data.description: Schwann cells are glial cells in the peripheral nervous system that produce the myelin sheath around neuronal axons, facilitating rapid signal transmission.

data.name: Ceroid
data.description: Ceroid is a lipid pigment that is easily stained by Sudan dyes, similar to lipofuscin. It accumulates in numerous pathological conditions such as in cirrhotic livers and in lysosomal disorders affecting the central nervous system that manifest as severe neurodegeneration.

data.name: Solid-state NMR
data.description: Solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) spectroscopy is a variant of the NMR spectroscopy technique used for molecular structure determination, where the experimental sample is contained in media with little or no mobility (such as, a crystalline or powder state, membrane-bound system or aligned solution).

data.name: Caecum
data.description: The caecum is a pouch that forms the beginning of the large intestine. It is separated from the ascending colon by the cecocolic junction and from the small intestine by the ileocecal valve. The appendix is a vermiform process connected to the caecum, from which it develops.

data.name: Targeted Resequencing
data.description: Targeted resequencing is a method that aims to identify causative mutations within discrete genomic loci in populations by isolating and sequencing genomic regions of interest from a sample library. It is one of the fastest growing applications for next-generation sequencing technologies.

data.name: Metabolic Syndrome
data.description: Metabolic syndrome is a disorder of energy use and storage. This syndrome is characterized by central obesity, dyslipidaemia, raised blood pressure and high blood sugar levels. Patients with metabolic syndrome are at increased risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

data.name: Urban Ethnography
data.description: Urban ethnography is a qualitative research method that involves the in-depth study and observation of social phenomena within urban contexts. It focuses on understanding the social interactions, behaviors, and cultural dynamics within urban communities, with a specific emphasis on the impact of urban environments on crime, deviance, and social control.

data.name: Hereditary eye disease
data.description: Hereditary eye disease refers to genetic conditions that affect the eyes and vision, passed down from parents to offspring, including disorders such as retinitis pigmentosa and congenital cataracts.

data.name: Cancer Immunotherapy
data.description: Cancer immunotherapy is a therapy used to treat cancer patients that involves or uses components of the immune system. Some cancer immunotherapies consist of antibodies that bind to, and inhibit the function of, proteins expressed by cancer cells. Other cancer immunotherapies include vaccines and T cell infusions.

data.name: Nuclear Medicine
data.description: Nuclear medicine is a specialized area of radiology that uses very small amounts of radioactive materials, or radiopharmaceuticals, to examine organ function and structure. Nuclear medicine imaging is a combination of many different disciplines. These include chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer technology, and medicine. This branch of radiology is often used to help diagnose and treat abnormalities very early in the progression of a disease, such as thyroid cancer.

subjects.term: Medical physics. Medical radiology. Nuclear medicine

data.name: Zebra finch
data.description: The zebra finch (Taeniopygia guttata) is a small songbird from the perching-bird order (Passeriformes) that is used as a model organism for the study of subjects including song production, evolution, neurobiology, learning and behaviour.

data.name: Caenorhabditis elegans
data.description: Caenorhabditis elegans is a species of soil-dwelling nematode (roundworm) used as a model organism in molecular genetics and developmental biology. It is predominantly hermaphroditic (can self-fertilize) and it is transparent, allowing the position and fate of every cell in the body to be mapped.

data.name: Bisphosphonates in dentistry
data.description: Bisphosphonates in dentistry are medications used to treat bone diseases that can impact dental health, such as osteoporosis, but may also be associated with risks like osteonecrosis of the jaw.

data.name: Dental clinical teaching
data.description: Dental clinical teaching involves the instruction and training of dental students in clinical settings, providing hands-on experience in diagnosing and treating patients under supervision.

data.name: Forestry Management
data.description: Forestry management is the process of planning and implementing practices for the stewardship and use of forests and other wooded land to meet specific environmental, economic, social and cultural objectives. It deals with the overall administrative, economic, legal, social, technical and scientific aspects related to natural and planted forests.

data.name: DNA Nanostructures
data.description: DNA nanostructures are nanoscale structures made of DNA, which acts both as a structural and functional element. DNA nanostructures can serve as scaffolds for the formation of more complex structures.

data.name: Composite Resin
data.description: Composite Resin is a tooth-colored material used in dentistry for restorative procedures, such as fillings and veneers, known for its aesthetic appeal and durability.

data.name: Periodontitis
data.description: Periodontitis is a severe gum infection that damages the soft tissue and destroys the bone supporting the teeth, leading to tooth loss if not treated, and is associated with systemic health issues.

data.name: Oral analgesics
data.description: Oral analgesics are medications taken by mouth to relieve pain, commonly used in dentistry to manage pain associated with dental procedures and conditions.

data.name: Warfarin in dentistry
data.description: Warfarin in dentistry involves managing dental treatment for patients taking warfarin, an anticoagulant medication, to prevent excessive bleeding and ensure safe dental procedures.

data.name: Acne vulgaris
data.description: Acne vulgaris is skin disease that is characterized by excessive oil production, blackheads, whiteheads, pustules and scarring. It is very common during puberty but it can persist or occur later as well. Genetic, hormonal and infectious factors underlie its pathogenesis.

data.name: Epistasis
data.description: Epistasis refers to the interaction between genes at different loci, where the expression of one gene is influenced or suppressed by one or more other genes.

data.name: Health Economics
data.description: Health economics is a branch of economics concerned with issues related to efficiency, effectiveness, value and behavior in the production and consumption of health and healthcare.

subjects.term: Medical economics. Economics of medical care

data.name: Complexity
data.description: Complexity is the property of a system whose behaviour as a whole emerges as distinct from the simple sum of its individual behaviours. The understanding of complex systems is therefore beyond the linear algebra of classic reductionism and requires either statistical methods or computer simulations

data.name: Proteomics
data.description: Proteomics refers to the study of proteomes, but is also used to describe the techniques used to determine the entire set of proteins of an organism or system, such as protein purification and mass spectrometry.

data.name: Hyperdontia
data.description: Hyperdontia is a dental condition characterized by the presence of extra teeth beyond the normal number, which can cause crowding and alignment issues.

data.name: CRISPR-Cas9 Genome Editing
data.description: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing exploits the CRISPR-Cas system to modify a genome in a targeted manner. Guided by RNA, the Cas9 endonuclease breaks DNA at a target sequence. Imprecise repair of the double strand break can result in insertion or deletion mutations, while repair pathways can be engineered to introduce specific point mutations or insertions.

data.name: Stochastic Integral Equations
data.description: Stochastic Integral Equations are a type of mathematical equations that involve both stochastic processes and integrals. These equations combine the concepts of stochastic calculus and integral equations, providing a framework to study dynamic systems subject to random influences.

data.name: Protein Purification
data.description: Protein purification is a technique by which a single protein type is isolated from a complex mixture such as a cell lysate. It can refer to purification of a native protein from a biological sample or of a recombinant protein using one of a variety of chemical, physical or biological methods.

data.name: Cellular Circadian Rhythms
data.description: Circadian rhythms are 24-hour cycles determining periodicity in various physiological processes, including nervous system activity and hormone production, which influences sleeping and feeding patterns. These rhythms are regulated by endogenous networks of gene activity and can be modulated by changes in the environment, such as sunlight and temperature.

data.name: Dental Pulp Necrosis
data.description: Pulp necrosis is a clinical diagnostic category indicating the death of cells and tissues in the pulp chamber of a tooth with or without bacterial invasion. It is often the end result of many cases of dental trauma, caries and irreversible pulpitis.

data.name: Combinatorics
data.description: Combinatorics is a branch of mathematics that deals with counting, arranging, and selecting objects or elements within a finite set. Combinatorics encompasses a wide range of concepts and techniques for solving problems related to arrangements, permutations, combinations, and more.

data.name: Schizosaccharomyces pombe
data.description: Schizosaccharomyces pombe, or fission yeast, is a unicellular fungus and a model organism used to study subjects including cell cycle control, DNA replication and genome integrity.

data.name: Aneuploidy
data.description: Aneuploidy is the observation of an abnormal number of chromosomes per cell, differing from the normal karyotype (somatic number 2n, or n in gametes) by loss or gain of pairs of chromosomes, whole chromosomes or chromosome fragments. Chromosome missegregation in mitosis or meiosis can produce aneuploid cells or organisms respectively.

data.name: French Literature
data.description: French literature generally speaking, is literature written in the French language, particularly by citizens of France; it may also refer to literature written by people living in France who speak traditional languages of France other than French.

data.name: Aphthous Stomatitis
data.description: Aphthous Stomatitis, commonly known as canker sores, is a condition characterized by the recurrent formation of small, painful ulcers in the mouth, with an unclear etiology.

data.name: Extracellular Recording
data.description: Extracellular recording is an electrophysiology technique that uses an electrode inserted into living tissue to measure electrical activity coming from adjacent cells, usually neurons.

data.name: Eyelid diseases
data.description: Eyelid diseases refer to medical conditions affecting the eyelids, such as blepharitis, ptosis, and chalazion, which can cause discomfort, vision problems, and cosmetic concerns.

data.name: Protein Enrichment
data.description: Protein enrichment is a technique by which proteins of a particular type in a biological sample are concentrated for further analysis and identification. Enrichment is used to help concentrate low-abundance proteins to improve their downstream analysis.

data.name: Non-bonded Restorations
data.description: Non-bonded restorations in dentistry refer to dental restorations that do not rely on adhesive bonding to the tooth structure, such as certain types of crowns and bridges.

data.name: Business Analytics
data.description: Business analytics is the process of transforming data into insights to improve business decisions. Data management, data visualization, predictive modeling, data mining, forecasting simulation, and optimization are some of the tools used to create insights from data.

subjects.term: COMPUTERS / Business & Productivity Software / Business Intelligence

data.name: Fear Conditioning
data.description: Fear conditioning is a type of classical conditioning that involves pairing an aversive stimulus (such as an electric shock) with either a neutral context (such as a location) or stimulus (such as a tone). This results in the expression of a fear response in the presence of the context or stimulus alone.

data.name: Digital Radiography in Dentistry
data.description: Digital radiography refers to x-ray imaging. It uses digital x-ray sensors to produced enhanced computer images of your dental structure. Digital radio graphs near Scars dale are used to detect, monitor, diagnose and treat dental issues. The dental images used can be acquired through different methods.

data.name: Amelogenesis Imperfecta
data.description: Amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) is a congenital disorder which presents with a rare abnormal formation of the enamel or external layer of the crown of teeth, unrelated to any systemic or generalized conditions.

data.name: Fatty Acids
data.description: Fatty acids are organic acids with at least one carboxyl (-C(=O)OH, -COOH or -CO2H) group and a long carbon chain that can be joined by double bonds, as in unsaturated fatty acids, or single bonds, as in saturated fatty acids. Fatty acids are generally derived from triglycerides and phospholipids. Dietary fats are generally fatty acids.

data.name: Primary Herpetic Gingivostomatitis
data.description: Primary Herpetic Gingivostomatitis is an initial infection caused by the herpes simplex virus, characterized by painful sores and inflammation of the gums and oral mucosa, commonly seen in children.

data.name: C3 Photosynthesis
data.description: C3 photosynthesis is the major of the three metabolic pathways for carbon fixation by plants. This process uses the enzyme RuBisCO in relatively inefficient conditions, to fix CO2 from the air and obtain the 3-carbon organic intermediate molecule 3-phosphoglycerate. C3 photosynthetic plants possess a specific leaf structure, and are not adapted to non-optimal conditions.

data.name: Molecular Electronics
data.description: Molecular electronics is the use of molecules as the primary building block for electronic circuitry. A molecular approach, it is hoped, will enable the construction of much smaller circuits than is currently possible using the more conventional semiconductors such as silicon. The motion of the electrons in such devices is inherently governed by quantum mechanics. + Molecular electronics is the study and application of molecular building blocks for the fabrication of electronic components.

subjects.term: TECHNOLOGY & ENGINEERING / Materials Science / Electronic Materials
Condensed matter physics (liquid state and solid state physics)

data.name: Bacillus subtilis
data.description: Bacillus subtilis is a rod-shaped, flagellated Gram-positive soil bacterium used as a model for endospore formation and differentiation.

data.name: Syngas
data.description: Syngas, short for "synthesis gas," is a versatile mixture of gases primarily composed of hydrogen (H2) and carbon monoxide (CO). It is produced through various chemical processes, such as gasification or steam reforming, from carbon-rich feedstocks like coal, natural gas, biomass, or even waste materials. Syngas can be used as an intermediate product for producing a wide range of valuable fuels and chemicals.

data.name: Communication skills in dentistry
data.description: Communication skills in dentistry refer to the abilities required by dental professionals to effectively interact with patients, colleagues, and other stakeholders, ensuring clear and compassionate communication.

data.name: Biogeochemistry
