data.description: Biogeochemistry is the study of how chemical elements flow through living systems and their physical environments. It investigates the factors that influence cycles of key elements such as carbon, nitrogen and phosphorous.

subjects.term: SCIENCE / Chemistry / Environmental (see also Environmental Science)

data.name: Renal Artery Stenosis
data.description: Renal artery stenosis is a narrowing or blockage of the renal artery to one or both kidneys. It is most often associated with atherosclerosis and can lead to hypertension.

data.name: Cancer of Unknown Primary
data.description: Cancer of unknown primary occurs when cancer cells are found in the body, but the place where the cells first started growing (the origin or primary site) cannot be determined. Also called cancer of unknown primary origin or CUP.

data.name: Isoenzymes
data.description: Isoenzymes are closely related variants of the same enzyme with the same catalytic function, but with different amino acid sequences due to being encoded by different alleles of the same gene. Isoenzymes generally differ in their kinetic and/or thermodynamic properties.

data.name: Magnetic Devices
data.description: Magnetic devices are components for creating, manipulating or detecting magnetic fields. This can include magnetic memories, magnetometers and devices for magneto-optics. Magnetism can also play a central role in spintronic devices.

data.name: Tetrode recording
data.description: Tetrode recording is an electrophysiology technique that uses a particular type of electrode containing four small electrodes to make extracellular recordings in the brain.

data.name: Gene amplification
data.description: Gene amplification is an increase in the number of copies of a gene without a proportional increase in other genes. This can result from duplication of a region of DNA that contains a gene through errors in DNA replication and repair machinery as well as through fortuitous capture by selfish genetic elements.

data.name: Multihormonal system disorders
data.description: Multihormonal system disorders occur as a result of defects in the production or action of more than one hormone.

data.name: Dyspnoe
data.description: Dyspnoe, or dyspnea, is a medical term for shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, which can be a symptom of various underlying health conditions.

data.name: Porous Materials
data.description: Porous materials are materials with pores (cavities, channels or interstices). The characteristics of a porous material vary depending on the size, arrangement and shape of the pores, as well as the porosity (the ratio of the total pore volume relative to the apparent volume of the material) and composition of the material itself.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Pericardial Diseases
data.description: Pericardial Diseases refer to medical conditions affecting the pericardium, the sac surrounding the heart, which can lead to inflammation, fluid accumulation, and other cardiac complications.

data.name: Brain
data.description: The brain is the part of the central nervous system that is contained within the skull. It is responsible for executive and cognitive functions and regulates the functioning of the other parts of the nervous system.

data.name: Dental Sedation
data.description: Dental Sedation involves the use of sedative medications to help patients relax and reduce anxiety during dental procedures, ensuring a more comfortable experience.

data.name: Interleukin
data.description: Interleukins are cytokines produced and secreted mainly by CD3+ and CD4+ T lymphocytes. Interleukins promote development and differentiation of natural killer cells, T and B lymphocytes and haematopoietic stem cells. Interleukins are involved in systemic inflammation and immune system modulation, so play important roles in fighting cancer, infectious disease and other diseases.

data.name: Literature and Economics
data.description: Literature and Economics explores the representation of economic themes, such as wealth, poverty, labor, and capitalism, in literary texts, analyzing how literature reflects and critiques economic systems.

data.name: Anus
data.description: The anus continues from the rectum via the anal canal and is the final segment of the large intestine, functioning as the external outlet of the gastrointestinal tract, through which faecal matter is expelled. Defecation is controlled by the internal and external anal sphincters, which surround the top and bottom of the anus.

data.name: Superior colliculus
data.description: The superior colliculus is one of the anterior pair of round eminences of the midbrain that contribute to visual function, including the generation of eye movements. In non-mammalian vertebrates, this structure is referred to as the optic tectum.

data.name: Chromosome conformation capture-based methods
data.description: Chromosome conformation capture (3C)-based methods reveal chromosome organization within the nucleus by determining the physical proximity of pairs of points along chromatin. They preserve chromatin interactions by cross-linking followed by fragmentation, ligation and sequencing of interacting regions. Genome organization affects processes such as transcription, repair and DNA replication.

data.name: Parasite Physiology
data.description: Parasite physiology is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the mechanisms and processes that enable parasites to grow and reproduce.

data.name: RIG-I-like Receptors
data.description: RIG-I-like receptors (retinoic acid-inducible gene I-like receptors, RLRs) are a family of molecules that are expressed inside cells in order to sense viruses. They recognise double-stranded RNA molecules that are produced by certain viruses and can induce antiviral immune responses.

data.name: Fungal Genetics
data.description: Fungal genetics is the study of the mechanisms of heritable information in fungi. Yeasts and filamentous fungi are extensively used as model organisms for eukaryotic genetic research, including cell cycle regulation, chromatin structure, genetic recombination and gene regulation.

data.name: Catalytic DNA
data.description: Catalytic DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) are single-stranded DNA molecules with enzyme activity, for instance in cleaving RNA. Binding of catalytic DNA to its RNA targets is generally by Watson-Crick base pairing. Catalytic DNA can also target proteins and DNA with a range of outcomes, for instance as a peroxidase. Non-natural catalytic DNA molecules have been designed or discovered.

data.name: Dysbiosis
data.description: Dysbiosis is the condition of having imbalances in the microbial communities either in or on the body. Dysbiosis is associated with many diseases, such as inflammatory bowel disease and chronic fatigue syndrome.

data.name: Landscape and Regional Planning
data.description: Landscape and Regional Planning involves the design and organization of land use and infrastructure in urban, suburban, and rural areas to promote sustainable development and improve quality of life.

data.name: Skin Manifestations
data.description: Skin manifestations are cutaneous signs, symptoms, or physiological changes that arise as a consequence of systemic diseases, infections, or other non‑dermatological conditions.

data.name: Xerostomia
data.description: Xerostomia, or dry mouth, is a condition characterized by reduced saliva production, leading to difficulties in speaking, chewing, swallowing, and an increased risk of dental caries and infections.

data.name: Sleep Disorders
data.description: Sleep disorders are a group of conditions in which the normal sleep pattern or sleep behaviours are disturbed. Primary sleep disorders include insomnia, hypersomnia, obstructive sleep apnoea and parasomnias (abnormal sleep behaviours, such as sleepwalking and rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder).

data.name: Climate Change Mitigation
data.description: Climate-change mitigation encompasses policies and activities intended to reduce the greenhouse gas forcing of the climate system. Key intervention points include: the reduction of greenhouse gas sources, for example by reducing deforestation; emissions, for instance low carbon energy generation; and enhancing greenhouse gas sinks, for example by changes in land use.

data.name: Autocrine Motility Factor
data.description: Autocrine motility factor (AMF) is a substance secreted by a cell that acts via surface receptors on the same cell to regulate cell motility pathways by signalling through the GTPase Rho to the actin cytoskeleton, and through PI3 kinase. When derived from tumours, AMF can enhance cell migration, leading to tumour metastasis.

data.name: Bone Marrow Cells
data.description: Bone marrow cells are the cells contained within the bone marrow. These include stromal cells, which are not directly involved in haematopoiesis (adipocytes, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, osteoblasts, osteoclasts and macrophages), and haematopoietic stem cells, which are responsible for the production of blood cells such as leukocytes, erythrocytes and platelets.

data.name: Modularity
data.description: Modularity is the characteristic of a system whose components can be separated or integrated without a change in their own properties or those of the rest of the system. A system lacks modularity when a tweak to one of its components affects the functioning of others.

data.name: Legal Geography
data.description: Studies focuses on law/legal systems considering a spatial connection, and how social and cultural systems affect it.

data.name: Parasite Genomics
data.description: Parasite genomics is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the genetic material (genome) of parasites, primarily using sequencing, bioinformatics and computational tools. The ultimate goal of which is to understand the diversity, functional roles and evolution of all genes encoded by the parasite.

data.name: DNA Sequencing
data.description: DNA sequencing is any chemical, enzymatic or technological procedure for determining the linear order of nucleotide bases in DNA. Sanger sequencing by replicative synthesis in the presence of dideoxy nucleotide chain terminator monomers has now given way to 'next generation' sequencing by short parallel read technologies. The term often applies to the entire sequence determination pipeline including post-sequencing software analysis.

data.name: Chimaerism
data.description: Chimaerism is the occurrence in an organism of two or more genetically distinct cell populations derived from more than one individual. For example, in mouse genetics, embryonic stem cells may be aggregated with an 8-cell embryo to form a mouse from both cell types.

data.name: Oedema
data.description: Oedema is the medical term for soft-tissue swelling that results from the abnormal accumulation of interstitial fluid. Oedema can be generalized or organ-specific.

data.name: Landscape Ecology
data.description: Landscape ecology is the study of the pattern and interaction between ecosystems within a region of interest, and the way the interactions affect ecological processes, especially the unique effects of spatial heterogeneity on these interactions.

data.name: Wood Science and Technology
data.description: The study of the science and technology of wood and other lignocellulosic materials.

data.name: Mitophagy
data.description: Mitophagy is a form of macroautophagy that selectively degrades damaged mitochondria. Double-membraned autophagosomes enclose whole mitochondria, or selectively target the damaged areas. Autophagosomes then fuse with lysosomes for degradation.

data.name: Intracellular Recording
data.description: Intracellular recording is an electrophysiology technique that uses a microelectrode inserted into a single cell, usually a neuron, to measure its electrical activity.

data.name: Genetic translocation
data.description: Genetic translocation is the process of exchange of genetic material between chromosomes. A balanced translocation results in no gain or loss of material, while an unbalanced translocation may result in trisomy or monosomy of a particular chromosome segment.

data.name: Density Functional Theory
data.description: Density functional theory (DFT) is a computational quantum mechanical modelling method used in physics, chemistry and materials science to investigate the electronic structure of many-body systems, in particular atoms, molecules, and the condensed phases. // Density functional theory is computational technique used to predict the properties of molecules and bulk materials. It is a method for investigating the electronic structure of many-body systems and is based on a determination of a given system’s electron density rather than its wavefunction.

data.name: Spectrophotometry
data.description: Spectrophotometry is a method that measures the amount of light that a sample or object absorbs or reflects as a functional of wavelength using an instrument known as a spectrophotometer.

data.name: Lifestyle Modification
data.description: Lifestyle modification involves altering long-term habits, typically of eating or physical activity, and maintaining the new behaviour for months or years. Lifestyle modification can be used to treat a range of diseases, including obesity.

data.name: Parasite Genetics
data.description: Parasite genetics is the study of the genetic material of parasites, including the distribution, function and evolution of genes and genomes.

data.name: Fixed Prosthodontics
data.description: Fixed Prosthodontics is a branch of dentistry focused on the design and placement of permanent dental prostheses, such as crowns, bridges, and implants, to restore function and aesthetics.

data.name: Research Standards
data.description: Standards in research refer to a specified level of quality or achievement. For example, in medical research, reporting standards have been drawn up to ensure authors of publications report everything necessary for a full understanding and replication of published research. Standards can also include agreed nomenclature or identifiers.

data.name: Temporomandibular Disorders
data.description: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) are conditions affecting the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) and surrounding muscles, leading to pain, dysfunction, and difficulty in jaw movement.

data.name: Sexual Dysfunction
data.description: The term 'sexual dysfunction' describes a range of functional disorders of the reproductive system. Types of sexual dysfunction include erectile dysfunction (impotence), premature ejaculation and female sexual arousal disorder.

data.name: Pre-diabetes
data.description: Prediabetes is a metabolic disorder that is considered a precursor for the development of diabetes mellitus. It is characterized by higher than normal blood glucose levels that have not yet reached diabetic levels.

data.name: Fats
data.description: Fats are lipid small molecules generated by esterification between fatty acids and glycerol to generate a triglyceride. Fats are soluble in organic solvents, but insoluble in water. They can be either solid or liquid, though references to fats generally imply the solid unsaturated forms, containing carbon double bonds, rather than unsaturated forms.

data.name: Fluorosis
data.description: Fluorosis is a condition caused by excessive intake of fluoride during tooth development, leading to changes in the appearance of tooth enamel, ranging from mild discoloration to severe pitting.

data.name: Photocatalysis
data.description: Photocatalysis is a type of catalysis that results in the modification of the rate of a photoreaction - a chemical reaction that involves the absorption of light by one or more reacting species - by adding substances (catalysts) that participate in the chemical reaction without being consumed.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Sarcoma
data.description: A sarcoma is a cancer that arises from uncontrolled cell growth in tissues of mesodermal origins, such as connective tissue, bone, cartilage, fat or muscle. There are around 100 different subtypes of sarcoma that can be classified into three broad groups: soft tissue sarcoma; primary bone sarcoma; and gastro-intestinal stromal tumours.

data.name: Heart Development
data.description: Heart development, also known as cardiogenesis, is the complex biological process through which the heart forms and matures from embryonic structures. This process begins in the early stages of embryonic development, typically around the third week of gestation in humans, and involves a series of tightly regulated events including cell differentiation, migration, and morphogenesis. Key stages of heart development include the formation of the heart tube, looping of the heart tube to establish the basic heart structure, and the septation of the heart chambers to create a four-chambered organ. Various signaling pathways, such as the Wnt, Notch, and BMP pathways, play crucial roles in regulating these processes. Additionally, genetic factors and environmental influences can impact heart development, leading to congenital heart defects if abnormalities occur. Understanding heart development is essential for advancing medical knowledge related to cardiovascular health, congenital heart disease, and regenerative medicine.

data.name: Polysaccharide Sequencing
data.description: Polysaccharide sequencing refers to the determination of the sequence of polysaccharides. This is more complex than sequencing some other biopolymers as although many polysaccharides are linear, many also have branches. Additionally there are many monosaccharides which can each be bonded in different ways by different enzymes. Techniques for determining polysaccharide structures include NMR spectroscopy and methylation analysis.

data.name: Evoked potentials
data.description: Evoked potentials are the electrical responses of the nervous system that result from sensory or motor stimulation. The term is often used in the context of responses of the central nervous system that are indicative of sensory processing and cognitive function.

data.name: Tobacco cessation in dentistry
data.description: Tobacco cessation in dentistry involves strategies and interventions provided by dental professionals to help patients quit smoking and other tobacco use, improving overall oral and systemic health.

data.name: Thrombopoiesis
data.description: Thrombopoiesis is the process through which thrombocytes are generated. Thrombocytes are cells that are important for blood clotting. In mammals, thromobocytes are known as platelets.

data.name: Urethra
data.description: The urethra is the tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body during urination. In men, the urethra also transports semen during ejaculation.

data.name: Isomerases
data.description: Isomerases are enzymes that catalyze the isomerization of a molecule. This process involves the change in bond connectivity or spatial arrangements within a single substrate molecule, generating a product with the same chemical formula described as an isomer.

data.name: Origin Firing
data.description: Origin firing is the initiation of DNA replication that takes place at specialised start sites, or replication origins, where the DNA first has to be opened up and unwound, before DNA synthesis machinery is loaded to start replication. Not all replication origins are fired at the same time

data.name: Medicago Truncatula
data.description: Medicago trunculata, or barrel clover, is a small annual plant in the legume family (Fabaceae) that serves as a model organism for the study of symbiosis with nitrogen-fixing bacteria and fungi due to its simple genome, rapid life cycle and ease of genetic manipulation.

data.name: Bacterial Evolution
data.description: Bacterial evolution is the process of heritable change in populations of bacteria over multiple generations. It occurs through mechanisms including natural selection and genetic drift, and can result in adaptations to environmental change or host immunity. Because of their short generation times and large population sizes, bacteria can evolve rapidly.

data.name: Glass-ionomer cement
data.description: Glass-ionomer cement is a dental restorative material made from a mixture of glass and an organic acid, used for fillings and luting due to its adhesive properties and fluoride release.

data.name: Paediatric Neurological Disorders
data.description: Paediatric neurological disorders refer to those disorders of the nervous system that affect children.

synonyms: Paediatric Neurological Disorder. Central nervous system. nervous system. central nervous system.

data.name: Removable prosthodontics
data.description: Removable prosthodontics is a branch of dentistry focused on the design, creation, and fitting of removable dental appliances, such as dentures and partial dentures, to replace missing teeth.

data.name: Atomic Force Microscopy
data.description: Atomic force microscopy (AFM), a form of scanning probe microscopy, is a technique where a cantilever with a sharp tip is systematically scanned across a sample (biological or material) surface to produce a nanometre-resolution topographic map. AFM can also be used to measure forces between the tip and sample.

data.name: Financial Econometrics
data.description: Financial econometrics is the application of statistical methods to financial market data. Financial econometrics is a branch of financial economics, in the field of economics. Areas of study include capital markets, financial institutions, corporate finance and corporate governance. Topics often revolve around asset valuation of individual stocks, bonds, derivatives, currencies and other financial instruments.

data.name: Dynamic Networks
data.description: Dynamic networks are networks that vary over time; their vertices are often not binary and instead represent a probability for having a link between two nodes. Statistical approaches or computer simulations are often necessary to explore how such networks evolve, adapt or respond to external intervention.

data.name: Hypodontia
data.description: Hypodontia is a dental condition characterized by the congenital absence of one or more teeth, excluding the third molars, often requiring orthodontic or prosthetic treatment.

data.name: Next-generation Sequencing
data.description: Next-generation sequencing refers to non-Sanger-based high-throughput DNA sequencing technologies. Millions or billions of DNA strands can be sequenced in parallel, yielding substantially more throughput and minimizing the need for the fragment-cloning methods that are often used in Sanger sequencing of genomes.

data.name: NEMS
data.description: NEMS, or nanoelectromechanical systems, are devices in which the physical motion of a nanometre-scale structure is controlled by an electronic circuit, or vice versa. NEMS make particularly sensitive sensors, of chemicals and acceleration, for example. NEMS also offer the possibility of observing quantum effects in systems much larger than few-atom ensembles.

data.name: Nutrition and Diet in Dentistry
data.description: Nutrition and Diet in Dentistry examines the relationship between dietary habits and oral health, focusing on how nutrition impacts dental diseases and the role of diet in preventive dental care.

data.name: Circadian Mechanisms
data.description: Circadian mechanisms control the rhythmic cycles of physiological processes that occur over 24 hours. Circadian mechanisms are controlled mainly by the suprachiasmatic nucleus, in which cyclic oscillations in 'clock genes' regulate ion fluxes, hormone levels and variations in neural activity over a 24 hour cycle.

data.name: DNA Repair Enzymes
data.description: DNA repair enzymes are enzymes that recognize and correct physical damage in DNA, caused by exposure to radiation, UV light or reactive oxygen species. The correction of DNA damage alleviates loss of genetic information, generation of double-strand breaks, and DNA crosslinkages. DNA repair enzymes recognize DNA damage or a nearby site, or enable repair.

data.name: Marine Microbiology
data.description: Marine microbiology is the study of the microorganisms (bacteria, archaea, viruses and microbial eukaryotes) in the marine environment, including their biodiversity, ecology and biogeochemistry. The use of metagenomics has been fundamental in revealing the abundance and composition of marine microbial ecosystems.

data.name: Encephalopathy
data.description: Encephalopathy is a syndrome that involves global brain dysfunction. Encephalopathies have varying aetiologies: causes include for example ischaemic or traumatic brain injury, infectious agents, toxins, autoimmune attack or neurodegeneration.

data.name: Data Structures
data.description: Data structures are fundamental concepts in computer science that define the organization and storage of data in a computer's memory or storage devices. They provide a systematic way to manage and manipulate data efficiently, enabling various algorithms and operations to be performed effectively. Different data structures are designed to suit specific types of data and the operations that need to be performed on them.

data.name: Gap Junctions
data.description: Gap junctions are intercellular channels that allow small molecules and electrical current to passively diffuse between adjacent cells. They are found in neurons and glia throughout the nervous system and are the main structural element of electrical synapses.

data.name: Metathesis Reaction
data.description: Metathesis reactions are chemical reactions in which two hydrocarbons (alkanes, alkenes or alkynes) are converted to two new hydrocarbons by the exchange of carbon–carbon single, double or triple bonds. These are usually catalyzed by a metal catalyst.

data.name: Haemodialysis
data.description: Haemodialysis is an extracorporeal procedure to remove waste products from the blood, such as creatinine and urea, which are insufficiently removed by the kidneys in patients with renal failure. During the procedure, patients' blood is withdrawn and cleansed by filtration through a series of membranes before being returned to the patient.

data.name: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
data.description: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is a unicellular freshwater green alga that is amenable to genetic studies and can be grown in the laboratory. It has a chloroplast, two flagella and an eye spot and is used to study phenomena such as photosynthesis, flagellar locomotion and light sensing.

data.name: Ear manifestations
data.description: Ear manifestations refer to symptoms and conditions affecting the ear, which can be indicative of various underlying health issues, including infections, hearing loss, and balance disorders.

data.name: Halitosis
data.description: Halitosis, commonly known as bad breath, is an unpleasant odor emanating from the mouth, often caused by poor oral hygiene, dental issues, or systemic conditions.

data.name: Fungal Systems Biology
data.description: Fungal systems biology is the scientific study of the functions and properties of fungi in an integrative, systematic way, based on the analysis and modelling of large data sets. Fungal systems biology is, for example, used to build networks of fungal metabolism.

data.name: Metabolic Engineering
data.description: Metabolic engineering is the use of genetic engineering to modify the metabolism of an organism. It can involve the optimization of existing biochemical pathways or the introduction of pathway components, most commonly in bacteria, yeast or plants, with the goal of high-yield production of specific metabolites for medicine or biotechnology.

data.name: Sea Anemone
data.description: Sea anemones are Cnidarians (related to jellyfish and corals) in the order Actiniaria that exist mainly as polyps (an anchored tubular body with a single oral opening surrounded by tentacles). Nematostella vectensis grows in the laboratory and is used as a model to study evolutionary and developmental biology.

data.name: Cryoelectron Microscopy
data.description: Cryoelectron microscopy is a method for imaging frozen-hydrated specimens at cryogenic temperatures by electron microscopy. Specimens remain in their native state without the need for dyes or fixatives, allowing the study of fine cellular structures, viruses and protein complexes at molecular resolution.

data.name: Cough
data.description: Cough is a reflex action to clear the airways of mucus, irritants, or foreign particles, which can be a symptom of various respiratory conditions or other underlying health issues.

data.name: Ion Pumps
data.description: Ion pumps are assemblies of integral membrane proteins, like ion channels, that modulate ion transport into and out of a cell or organelle, leading to generation of electrical signals. Ion pumps, however, work against their concentration gradient, so require energy input, but the energy can also be derived from the concentration gradient of another ion.

data.name: Non-REM sleep
data.description: Non-REM sleep refers to the stages of sleep in which there is little or no random eye movements (REM), that is, stages 1–3 of sleep. During these phases, muscle tone is retained and dreaming is rare; stage 3, the deepest sleep stage, has been associated with memory consolidation.

data.name: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
data.description: Oral and maxillofacial surgery is a surgical specialty focusing on reconstructive surgery of the face, facial trauma surgery, the oral cavity, head and neck, mouth, and jaws, as well as facial cosmetic surgery/facial plastic surgery including cleft lip and cleft palate surgery.

data.name: HIPPO Signalling
data.description: Hippo signalling is a cell signalling pathway that controls organ size. Activation of Hippo results in a series of phosphorylation events that culminate in the phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention of a downstream transcriptional coactivator, terminating expression of Hippo-regulated genes. Hippo signalling has an important role in development and cancer.

data.name: Gingivitis
data.description: Gingivitis is the inflammation of the gums, usually caused by plaque buildup, leading to redness, swelling, and bleeding, and is reversible with proper oral hygiene.

data.name: Alcohol Misuse in Dental Patients
data.description: Alcohol Misuse in Dental Patients refers to the excessive consumption of alcohol and its impact on oral health, including increased risk of dental diseases and complications during dental treatment.

data.name: Ligases
data.description: Ligases are enzymes that catalyze the formation of chemical bonds, for instance C-O, C-N, C-S bonds, between two macromolecules, such as proteins or peptides, usually with accompanying hydrolysis of a pyrophosphate bond from adenosine triphosphate (ATP) or another high-energy donor.

data.name: Orofacial pain
data.description: Orofacial pain refers to pain perceived in the face and mouth, which can arise from dental, musculoskeletal, neurological, or psychological sources.

data.name: Climate-Change Impacts
data.description: Climate-change impacts are the consequences of climate change – both expected and realised – for natural and human systems. Climate impacts research is typically interdisciplinary and frequently involves the construction of climate impact models. Some key research themes include: ecology, water resources, agriculture, human heath, the economy and built infrastructure.

data.name: Literature and Mobility
data.description: Literature and Mobility explores themes of movement, travel, migration, and displacement in literary texts, examining how these experiences shape identities and narratives.

data.name: Synechocystis
data.description: Synechocystis is a genus of freshwater cyanobacteria that is easy to transform with foreign DNA and is especially used in the study photosynthesis.

data.name: Transforming Growth Factor Beta
data.description: Transforming growth factor beta (TGFβ) is a cytokine that is secreted by various cell types, including macrophages, and functions in cell growth, cell differentiation, apoptosis and cellular homeostasis by binding to its receptor, the TGFβ type II receptor. Multiple signalling pathways lie downstream of the receptor, including the SMAD transcription factors and cell-cycle proteins.

data.name: Parasite Host Response
data.description: The parasite host response is the process by which a host interacts with and responds to parasites that it encounters. It includes various mechanisms, including immune mechanisms that are elicited in an attempt to eliminate the parasite or halt its growth.

data.name: Astrophysical disks
data.description: Astrophysical disks are rotationally-supported disks of gas and dust. They are found in a range of astrophysical objects, from small protoplanetary systems and accreting X-ray binaries, to massive disks surrounding actively accreting supermassive black holes in the centre of galaxies.

data.name: Biopolymers
data.description: Biopolymers are polymers synthesized by living organisms. Biopolymers can be polynucleotides (such as the nucleic acids DNA and RNA), polypeptides (that is, proteins) or polysaccharides (that is, polymeric carbohydrates).These consist of long chains made of repeating, covalently bonded units, such as nucleotides, amino acids or monosaccharides..Biopolymers are covalently bonded linear structures produced by living organisms, including polynucleotides, like RNA and DNA; polypeptides, from which proteins are formed; and polysaccharides, comprising carbohydrates. Biopolymers in vivo refers to these polymers when they are studied in the cells of whole living organisms.

data.name: Green Diesel
data.description: "Green diesel" refers to a type of environmentally friendly diesel fuel that is produced using renewable feedstocks or advanced synthetic processes. It is designed to reduce the carbon footprint and emissions associated with conventional diesel fuels. Two main categories of green diesel are Renewable Diesel and Synthetic Diesel Fuel

data.name: Energy Justice
data.description: Energy justice applies justice principles to energy policy and security, its production and systems, energy consumption through the society, and energy activism, and is strongly related to sustainable living and mitigation of climate change.

data.name: Tree Biology
data.description: The study of tree structure and function, and the relationship between them. Or  Tree biology is the study of the biological processes and characteristics of trees, which are woody plants typically characterized by a single main stem or trunk and numerous branches. It is a specialized branch of plant biology that focuses on the unique aspects of tree growth, development, and functioning.

data.name: Dog
data.description: The domestic dog, Canis familiaris, is a canid mammal that has been bred to produce a large number of varieties with diverse characteristics, enabling the study of breeding and the genetics underlying many traits and diseases.

data.name: Biogas
data.description: Biogas is a renewable energy source that is produced through the anaerobic digestion or fermentation of organic materials, such as agricultural waste, animal manure, sewage sludge, food scraps, and other organic matter. It is a mixture of gases, primarily consisting of methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2), along with smaller amounts of other gases such as hydrogen (H2), nitrogen (N2), and traces of volatile organic compounds.

data.name: Neural Decoding
data.description: Neural decoding is the study of what information is available in the electrical activity (action potentials) of individual cells or networks of neurons. Studies of neural decoding aim to identify what stimulus, event, or desired output elicits a particular pattern of neural activity.

data.name: Fugu
data.description: Fugu (also known as Takifugu), commonly referred to as pufferfish, is a genus of fish belonging to the family Tetraodontidae, notable for their ability to inflate their bodies and for containing potent toxins, particularly tetrodotoxin. The species Fugu rubripes, also known as the Japanese pufferfish, is significant in scientific research due to its relatively small genome and has been a model organism in genomic and evolutionary studies. Its genome was one of the first among vertebrates to be sequenced, providing insights into vertebrate evolution and genetics. Fugu is also culturally important in Japanese cuisine, where it is prepared as a delicacy, requiring specialized training to serve safely due to its toxic properties.

data.name: Medical Geography
data.description: Medical geography focuses on patterns of disease and death—of how diseases spread, for example, and how variations in morbidity and mortality rates reflect local environments—and on geographies of health care provision.

data.name: Research Ethics
data.description: Research ethics, also known as scientific ethics or scholarly ethics, refers to the ethical considerations and responsibilities that guide the conduct of research. It involves the examination of moral principles, values, and guidelines that ensure the protection of participants, the integrity of the research process, and the responsible dissemination of research findings.

data.name: Cytokinin
data.description: Cytokinins are one of the classical five plant hormones and are adenine derivatives. Together with auxin, they play an important role in several plant processes such as cell division and differentiation, apical dominance, morphogenesis, and leaf senescence.

data.name: C4 Photosynthesis
data.description: C4 photosynthesis is an evolved metabolic mechanism for plant carbon fixation, in which atmospheric CO2 is first incorporated into a 4-carbon intermediate, which is then shuttled to specialized internal cells. This biochemical and anatomical adaptation allows for a more efficient photosynthetic process compared to C3 photosynthesis, especially in non-optimal conditions.

data.name: Calcium and Phosphate Metabolic Disorders
data.description: Calcium and phosphate metabolic disorders are disorders that are characterized by abnormalities in the processing of calcium or phosphate. These disorders can affect the absorption, transport, storage and use of these minerals. Examples include hypocalcaemia and hyperphosphataemia.

data.name: Latino and Latina Sociology
data.description: Latino and Latina Sociology is the study of the social, economic, political, and cultural experiences of Latino and Latina communities, both within and beyond the United States. This field examines topics such as migration, identity formation, social stratification, and the roles that race, ethnicity, gender, and class play in the lives of Latinos and Latinas.

data.name: Gibberellins
data.description: Gibberellins are one of the classical five plant hormones and are diterpenoid weak acids. They are involved in several biological processes in plants such as starch hydrolysis during germination, fruit maturation, and stem elongation. Gibberellin mutants played a key role during the Green Revolution thanks to their sturdier semi-dwarf stature allowing increased yield.

data.name: Pink porcelain
data.description: Pink porcelain in dentistry refers to a type of dental ceramic material used for aesthetic restorations, designed to mimic the natural color of gum tissue.

data.name: Bladder Disease
data.description: Bladder disease is an umbrella term used to describe pathological conditions that affect the structure or function of the bladder. Bladder diseases include conditions related to inflammation, infection and urinary incontinence.

data.name: Sensory Processing
data.description: Sensory processing refers to the way our nervous system receives, interprets, and responds to sensory information from our environment. It involves the brain's ability to organize and make sense of sensory input from various sensory modalities, such as sight, hearing, touch, taste, and smell. Sensory processing is crucial for our daily functioning, as it helps us navigate and interact with the world around us.

data.name: Kinases
data.description: Kinases are enzymes that catalyze the addition of a phosphate group (PO43-) to substrates, usually proteins. The phosphate generally comes from adenosine triphosphate (ATP). Kinases and phosphatases, which remove phosphate groups, are involved in nearly all signal transduction processes, often with cascades of phosphorylation events.

data.name: Channelopathies
data.description: Channelopathies are a group of disorders that are caused by dysfunction of ion channels. Channelopathies can disrupt neuronal or muscle function, including heart function, and can affect the brain, resulting in seizures. Channelopathies can result from a mutation or autoimmune attack on an ion channel.

data.name: Literature, Gender and Sexuality
data.description: Literature, Gender and Sexuality examines how literary works portray and interrogate issues related to gender identities, sexual orientations, and the social constructions of gender and sexuality.

data.name: Hormonal Therapies
data.description: Hormonal therapies use hormones or hormone antagonists in medical treatment. For example, hormone replacement therapy can be used to alleviate the symptoms of the menopause and growth hormone is given to people with growth hormone deficiency.

data.name: Literature and Class
data.description: Literature and Class explores how literary texts represent and critique social class structures, economic inequalities, and class-based identities and struggles.

data.name: Neuroradiology
data.description: Neuroradiology, Neuroimaging or Brain Imaging. Brain imaging refers to the usually non-invasive or minimally invasive techniques that enable imaging the structure or function of the brain. Brain imaging techniques take advantage of X-rays, radioactive labelling, magnetic fields induced by the brain's electric activity, or optical absorption or paramagnetic properties of haemoglobin.

data.name: Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
data.description: Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) is a powerful imaging technique used to visualize and manipulate individual atoms on a surface with extremely high resolution. It operates based on the principle of quantum tunneling, a phenomenon in quantum mechanics where electrons can pass through energy barriers that classical physics would consider insurmountable.

data.name: Primary Immunodeficiency Disorders
data.description: Primary immunodeficiency disorders are a set of syndromes that arise from defects in the immune system. Most are diagnosed in young children, and patients are generally characterized by increased susceptibility to infections.

data.name: Proteases
data.description: Proteases are enzymes that catalyse hydrolysis of the peptide and isopeptide bonds that join amino acids within proteins (known as proteolysis). Proteases can also remove protein post-translational modifications. Exopeptidases remove the terminal amino acids from the protein chain and endopeptidases attack an internal peptide bond, as in trypsin, chymotrypsin, pepsin, elastase and papain.

data.name: Geographic Tongue
data.description: Geographic Tongue is a benign condition characterized by map-like red patches on the tongue's surface, which can change shape and location, often causing sensitivity or discomfort.

data.name: Photoacoustics
data.description: Photoacoustics is the study of vibrations induced in matter by light. Laser light causes localised heating when it is absorbed by a surface. This in turn makes the target area expand and sends a pressure wave through the rest of the material. This effect enables imaging of opaque systems, particularly biological samples.

data.name: Data Analytics
data.description: Data analytics is the science of analyzing raw data to make conclusions about that information. Many of the techniques and processes of data analytics have been automated into mechanical processes and algorithms that work over raw data for human consumption.

data.name: Dental Biofilms
data.description: Dental Biofilms are structured communities of bacteria adhering to the surfaces of the teeth and gums, contributing to dental caries and periodontal diseases if not properly managed.

data.name: Central Nervous System Infections
data.description: Central nervous system infections include bacterial and aseptic (typically viral) meningitis, viral and autoimmune encephalitis and myelitis, which targets the spinal cord.

data.name: Lens diseases
data.description: Lens diseases refer to medical conditions affecting the lens of the eye, such as cataracts, which can impair vision and require medical or surgical intervention.

data.name: System Robustness
data.description: Robustness is the property of a system whose behaviour is relatively insensitive to perturbations either in its environment or in its components. There is often a trade-off between robustness and adaptability.

data.name: Nephritis
data.description: Nephritis is defined as inflammation of the kidney and may involve the glomeruli, tubules or interstitium.

data.name: Surface Coating
data.description: Coating refers to the application of a layer of material to the surface of an object, typically to protect, decorate, or enhance its properties.

data.name: Pressure Chemistry
data.description: Pressure chemistry is a field of chemistry that focuses on studying chemical reactions and materials under high-pressure conditions. It involves subjecting substances to elevated pressures, often above atmospheric pressure, to induce unique and sometimes unexpected chemical transformations.

data.name: Paediatric Cancer
data.description: Paediatric cancers are malignancies that occur in young children.The most common childhood cancers are leukaemia and brain tumors, such as gliomas.

subjects.term: Paediatric medicine / child and adolescent medicine

data.name: Synaptic Vesicle Exocytosis
data.description: Synaptic vesicle exocytosis is the biological process by which a synaptic vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane of the pre-synaptic axon terminal and releases its contents into the synaptic cleft. Before exocytosis, neurotransmitter-filled synaptic vesicles are docked at the plasma membrane and primed: exocytosis is triggered by calcium influx.

data.name: Fatty Alcohols
data.description: Fatty alcohols are lipid small molecules that consist of a terminal hydroxyl (OH) group and a long carbon chain. They are the reduced forms of fatty acids in which the carboxylic acid has been reduced to give a primary alcohol. They are derived from natural fats and oils and can sometimes be unsaturated or branched.

data.name: Sensation
data.description: Sensation, in the field of psychology, refers to the process by which sensory organs detect and receive stimuli from the environment and transmit them to the brain. It involves the initial registration of sensory information through the senses, such as vision, hearing, taste, touch, and smell.

data.name: Stochastic Learning and Adaptive Control
data.description: Stochastic learning refers to a family of machine learning algorithms by following the theory and principles of stochastic optimization, which have achieved great successes for solving large-scale machine learning tasks in practice.Stochastic learning is closely related to online learning. Adaptive control is the control method used by a controller which must adapt to a controlled system with parameters which vary, or are initially uncertain.

data.name: Tooth brushing
data.description: Tooth brushing is a fundamental oral hygiene practice involving the use of a toothbrush and toothpaste to clean teeth, remove plaque, and prevent dental diseases.

data.name: Mesenchymal Stem Cells
data.description: Mesenchymal stem cells are multipotent adult stem cells that are present in multiple tissues, including umbilical cord, bone marrow and fat tissue. Mesenchymal stem cells can self-renew by dividing and can differentiate into multiple tissues including bone, cartilage, muscle and fat cells, and connective tissue.

data.name: Biophysical Models
data.description: A biophysical model is a simulation of a biological system using mathematical formalizations of the physical properties of that system. Such models can be used to predict the influence of biological and physical factors on complex systems.

data.name: Parasite Evolution
data.description: Parasite evolution refers to the heritable genetic changes that a parasite accumulates during its life time, which can arise from adaptations in response to environmental changes or the immune response of the host. Because of their short generation times and large population sizes, parasites can evolve rapidly.

data.name: Uveal Diseases
data.description: Uveal diseases refer to medical conditions affecting the uvea, the middle layer of the eye, which can lead to inflammation, vision loss, and other ocular complications.

data.name: Toll-like Receptors
data.description: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are a family of pattern recognition receptors that recognize conserved structures that are associated with infection or tissue damage. Activation of TLRs promotes inflammatory responses.

data.name: Origin Selection
data.description: Each time the DNA is replicated, only a subset of replication origins are used, and origin usage also changes during development. How the selection of origins is achieved is not clear but may involve chromatin structure and availability of replication initiation proteins

data.name: Rhesus Macaque
data.description: The rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta) is an Asian Old World monkey used in biomedical research due to its closeness to humans and to the ease of rearing the animal in captivity.

data.name: Angiogenesis
data.description: Angiogenesis is the formation and remodelling of new blood vessels from pre‑existing ones. It occurs normally in processes such as wound healing and embryonic development, but is also active in diseases such as tumour growth and diabetic eye disease.

data.name: PCR-based Techniques
data.description: PCR-based techniques are methods that rely on the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to amplify stretches of DNA by creating many identical or near-identical copies. For example, PCR amplification can be used to isolate the sequence at a specific location in the genome (genotyping).

data.name: Xylitol
data.description: Xylitol is a sugar alcohol used as a sweetener, known for its dental benefits, including reducing the risk of tooth decay by inhibiting the growth of cavity-causing bacteria.

data.name: Extended skills training in dentistry
data.description: Extended skills training in dentistry involves additional education and practice for dental professionals to acquire advanced competencies in specialized areas of dental care.

data.name: Pulpitis
data.description: Pulpitis is the inflammation of the dental pulp, the innermost part of the tooth containing nerves and blood vessels, often caused by dental caries or trauma, leading to pain and sensitivity.

data.name: Arabidopsis Thaliana
data.description: Arabidopsis thaliana is a small annual flowering plant in the mustard family (Brassicaceae). Its small genome size, rapid life cycle, large seed production, ease of genetic transformation and ability to grow in the laboratory make it a model organism for the study of plant genetics, physiology, biochemistry and development.

data.name: X-Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy
data.description: X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), also known as Electron Spectroscopy for Chemical Analysis (ESCA), is a surface-sensitive analytical technique used to determine the elemental composition and chemical state of materials. It provides valuable information about the electronic structure and bonding within a sample.

data.name: Visual Sociology
data.description: Visual sociology refers to the use of visual methods and approaches in the field of sociology to study and understand social phenomena. It involves using visual materials, such as photographs, videos, films, and other visual media, as both data and analytical tools.

data.name: Cardiac Regeneration
data.description: Cardiac regeneration is the repair or replacement of heart tissue.

data.name: Bioluminescence Imaging
data.description: Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) is a technology that uses light emitted by enzyme-catalyzed reactions to report activity at the molecular level. Bioluminescent reporters require a small chemical substrate for non-invasive imaging in cell biology and small animal studies. BLI does not require incident light like fluorescence or phosphorescence, avoiding phototoxicity.

data.name: Mutagenesis
data.description: Mutagenesis is the process of generating a genetic mutation. This may occur spontaneously or be induced by mutagens. Researchers also use a number of techniques to create mutations, including transposon mutagenesis to generate random gene knockouts, and site-directed mutagenesis, which utilises the polymerase chain reaction to introduce specific mutations.

data.name: Antagomir and RNA Sponge
data.description: Antagomirs and RNA sponges are both agents that are used to silence microRNAs. Antagomirs are chemically modified oligonucleotides that bind specifically to particular microRNAs and sponge RNAs are small synthetic RNAs that bind to multiple microRNAs that have the same sequence in their ‘seed region’.

data.name: Gingival recession
data.description: Gingival recession is the process in which the gum tissue pulls back from the tooth, exposing the root surface, which can lead to sensitivity, increased risk of decay, and aesthetic concerns.

data.name: Lymphoproliferative Disorders
data.description: Lymphoproliferative disorders are medical conditions in which excessive numbers of lymphocytes are produced. Lymphoproliferative disorders can be caused by inherited immunodeficiency syndromes or may arise following viral infection or treatment with immunosuppressant drugs.

data.name: Recombinases
data.description: Recombinases are enzymes that catalyse site-specific recombination events within DNA; for example, genetic recombination during meiosis in which recombination serves to generate new combinations of alleles on chromosomes. DNA recombination events involve DNA breakage, strand exchange between homologous segments and rejoining of the DNA by DNA ligases. Recombinases also function in recombinational DNA repair.

data.name: Biochemical Network
data.description: Biochemical networks are abstract graphs in which biological molecules such as enzymes or metabolites are represented by nodes, which are connected when two molecules interact physically or functionally. Such models allow one to make complex predictions about cellular functions that would not be accessible from single-molecule studies.

data.name: Transcriptional regulatory elements
data.description: Transcriptional regulatory elements are nucleotide sequences of a gene that are involved in regulation of genetic transcription. These include the promoter, plus response elements, activator and enhancer sequences for binding of transcription factors to aid RNA polymerase binding and promote expression, and operator or silencer sequences to which repressor proteins bind to block RNA polymerase attachment and prevent expression.

data.name: Stochastic Differential Equations
data.description: A stochastic differential equation (SDE) is a differential equation in which one or more of the terms is a stochastic process, resulting in a solution which is also a stochastic process.

data.name: Rice
data.description: Rice (Oryza sativa) is a plant in the grass family (Poaceae) cultivated for its seed which is eaten as a staple cereal grain.

data.name: Pseudomonas fluorescens
data.description: Pseudomonas fluorescens is a Gram-negative bacterium found in soil and water that harbours multiple flagella and secretes the fluorescent pigment pyoverdin. It also produces the antibiotic mupirocin and protects some plant roots from parasitic fungi or nematodes.

data.name: Mitochondrial genome
data.description: The mitochondrial genome is the full genetic complement of a mitochondrion. Mitochondrial DNA is only a small portion of the total DNA of a eukaryotic cell and in most species is solely inherited from the mother. In humans mitochondrial DNA contains approximately 16,600 base pairs encoding 37 genes.

data.name: Peri-implantitis
data.description: Peri-implantitis is an inflammatory condition affecting the tissues around dental implants, leading to bone loss and potential implant failure if not managed appropriately.

data.name: Oral Hygiene
data.description: Oral Hygiene refers to the practices and habits that maintain the cleanliness and health of the mouth, teeth, and gums, including brushing, flossing, and regular dental check-ups.

data.name: Inorganic LEDs
data.description: Inorganic LEDs are light-emitting diodes (LEDs) made from a crystalline semiconductor. The optical emission wavelength can be selected by varying material composition. Example active regions include germanium, gallium arsenide, gallium nitride and indium phosphide. Inorganic LEDS are prized for their low power consumption and are rapidly replacing conventional incandescent light bulbs.

data.name: Ocular motility disorders
data.description: Ocular motility disorders refer to conditions that affect the movement of the eyes, leading to issues such as double vision, misalignment, or difficulty tracking objects.

data.name: Gene Duplication
data.description: Gene duplication is a genetic event where a segment of DNA containing a gene is duplicated, resulting in multiple copies of that gene, which can lead to genetic variation and evolution.

data.name: Nanosensors
data.description: Nanosensors are chemical or mechanical sensors that can be used to detect the presence of chemical species and nanoparticles, or monitor physical parameters such as temperature, on the nanoscale. They also find use in medical diagnostic applications.

data.name: Fungal Biology
data.description: Fungal biology is the scientific discipline that concerns the biology of fungi, which include unicellular microorganisms as well as large multicellular organisms. Fungal biology is sometimes called mycology, a term that was coined by botanists when it was still assumed that fungi were plants.

data.name: Glycerides
data.description: Glycerides are generated when glycerol is modified at one (monoglycerides), two (diglycerides) or all three (triglycerides or fats) of its hydroxyl (OH) functional groups by esterification with a fatty acid.

data.name: Virus-host Interaction
data.description: Virus–host interactions are the viral and host processes that occur during viral infection, which enable both partners to respond to each other.

data.name: Biobricks
data.description: Biobricks is a trademark term for man-made DNA sequences encoding elementary modules that may be combined to produce more complex synthetic biological systems. The long-term goal of the Biobricks Foundation is to offer an open-source library of standardized genetic components.

data.name: Social Behavior
data.description: Social Behavior encompasses the actions and interactions of individuals within a society, including cooperation, competition, communication, and social norms.

data.name: Basidiomycetes
data.description: Basidiomycetes is a major group of fungi that includes a diverse range of organisms commonly known as the "club fungi." They are characterized by the presence of reproductive structures called basidia, which produce and release spores. Basidiomycetes play important ecological roles as decomposers, mycorrhizal symbionts, and plant pathogens. They also have economic significance as a source of edible mushrooms, as well as producers of medicinal compounds and industrial enzymes.

data.name: Mosaicism
data.description: Mosaicism is the occurrence in an organism of two or more genetically distinct cell populations derived from the same individual. In human genetics, the consequences of aneuploidy or gene mutation can be less severe if the affected individual also contains some normal cells.

data.name: Calcium-based cement
data.description: Calcium-based cement in dentistry is a material used for various dental procedures, such as root canal treatments and pulp capping, known for its biocompatibility and ability to promote healing.

data.name: Phase III trials
data.description: Phase III trials are conducted to provide stronger evidence of the effectiveness and safety of a therapeutic intervention and typically form a key part of applications to regulatory authorities to grant market approval. They usually involve 500-3000 or more patients and compare the therapeutic intervention with the current standard of care for patients with the disease intended to be treated.

data.name: Jasmonic Acid
data.description: Jasmonic acids are a class of lipidic plant hormones, synthesized from linolenic acid present in the chloroplast membrane. They are involved in development, abiotic stress responses and plant-microbes interactions in defence and symbiosis. Derivates such as methyl-jasmonate are volatile and participate in long range signalling between plants.

data.name: Monokine
data.description: Monokines are cytokines produced mainly by monocytes and macrophages for function in the immune system. Monokines can function as chemoattractants for guiding neutrophil migration.

data.name: Fragile Sites
data.description: Fragile sites are chromosomal regions that are susceptible to gaps or breaks. Common fragile sites occur in all individuals, are thought to be sensitive to replication stress due to chromosome structure, and are often re-arranged in cancer. Rare fragile sites are caused by nucleotide repeats and are inherited.

data.name: Fixed Appliances
data.description: Fixed Appliances in orthodontics are devices attached to the teeth, such as braces, used to correct dental alignment and bite issues over an extended period.

data.name: Paediatric kidney disease
data.description: Paediatric kidney disease is any type of kidney disease that occurs in patients aged 18 years or under.

data.name: Dental Epidemiology
data.description: Dental Epidemiology is the study of the distribution and determinants of dental diseases and conditions in populations, aiming to inform public health policies and preventive strategies.

data.name: Oral Candidiasis
data.description: Oral Candidiasis, also known as oral thrush, is a fungal infection caused by Candida species, characterized by white patches on the tongue and inner cheeks, often occurring in immunocompromised individuals.

data.name: Spinal Cord
data.description: The spinal cord is a bundle of nerves and supporting tissue that extends from the brain. It has an essential role in conducting motor and sensory information from and to the brain, as well as in regulating certain reflexes.

data.name: Smooth pursuit
data.description: Smooth pursuit is a process by which a slowly moving object is visually tracked with a continuous eye movement. It generally cannot occur without a moving visual target.

data.name: Urological Manifestations
data.description: Urological manifestations are complications of non-urological diseases or medications that affect the urinary tract or male genitals.

data.name: Multienzyme Complexes
data.description: Multienzyme complexes are stable assemblies of more than one enzyme, generally involved in sequential catalytic transformations. These are distinct from a multienzyme polypeptide, in which multiple catalytic domains are found in a single polypeptide chain. Fatty-acyl-CoA Synthase is an example of six enzymes that assemble in a barrel shape to generate fatty acids.

data.name: Congenital Heart Defects
data.description: Congenital heart defects are abnormal structural conditions of the heart, and/or large blood vessels, that are present at birth. Symptoms might not be apparent until later in life.

data.name: DNA Computing and Cryptography
data.description: DNA computing is a branch of biomolecular computing concerned with the use of DNA as a carrier of information to make arithmetic and logic operations..DNA computing is the use of nucleotides and their pairing properties in DNA double-helices as the alphabet and basic rules of a programming language. The chemical nature of DNA thus considered as both hardware and software provides a direct interface for the digital control of nanoscale physical or biological systems.

data.name: Bacterial Toxins
data.description: Bacterial toxins are toxic substances that are produced and released by bacteria to target other bacterial or host cells. Bacteria often have antitoxins to avoid the deleterious effects of toxins.

data.name: Urinalysis
data.description: Urinalysis is the examination of urine using laboratory techniques and procedures. The composition of urine can provide information regarding hydration status, infection, kidney function, hormones and urogenital diseases.

data.name: Stalled Forks
data.description: Replication fork stalling occurs if the replication proteins, or replisome, encounter problems. Stalled forks activate checkpoint signalling and therefore pause replication.

data.name: Logic Gates
data.description: A logic gate is a device performing an elementary Boolean function, producing a logical 0 or 1 output depending on one or several such logical inputs. Implemented with either electronic, optic, mechanical or even biological devices, logic gates can be composed into physical models of all conceivable algorithms or computation.

data.name: Craniofacial Orthodontics
data.description: Craniofacial orthodontics is a specialized field of orthodontics focusing on the diagnosis and treatment of dental and skeletal abnormalities in the craniofacial region, often involving interdisciplinary care.

data.name: Literature and Space
data.description: Literature and Space explores how literary works depict and conceptualize physical, social, and metaphorical spaces, including landscapes, urban environments, and imaginary worlds.

data.name: Vasopressin
data.description: Vasopression is a peptide hormone synthesized in the hypothalamus and secreted by the posterior pituitary gland (or neurohypophysis). It contributes to the maintenance of homeostasis in the body, as well as the neuromodulation of social interactions, including sexual behaviour and bonding.

data.name: Sterols
data.description: Sterols are amphipathic lipids based on the steroid ring structure but with a polar hydroxyl (OH group) on one of the 6-membered rings. Sterols are also known as steroid alcohols, an example of which is cholesterol. They are generated in living systems from acetyl-coA by the HMG-CoA reductase pathway.

data.name: Literature and Animal Studies
data.description: Literature and Animal Studies examine the representation and significance of animals in literary texts, exploring themes of human-animal relationships, ethics, and animal rights.

data.name: Pomology
data.description: Pomology is the branch of botany that focuses on the study and cultivation of fruit-bearing plants. It encompasses the science of fruit production, including the breeding, genetics, physiology, and management of fruit crops. Pomologists analyze various factors affecting fruit quality, yield, and disease resistance, and they work to improve fruit varieties through selective breeding and genetic modification. This field also involves the study of the environmental conditions necessary for optimal fruit growth, such as soil composition, climate, and pest management. Pomology plays a crucial role in agriculture and food production, contributing to the development of sustainable practices and enhancing the nutritional value of fruits for human consumption.

data.name: Hypospadias
data.description: Hypospadias is a congenital condition in males in which the opening of the urethra is on the underside of the penis.

data.name: Regulatory Networks
data.description: In biology, regulatory networks are sets of macromolecules, mostly proteins and RNAs, that interact to control the level of expression of various genes in a given genome. The main players in regulatory networks are DNA-binding proteins, also called transcription factors as they modulate the first step in gene expression.

data.name: Organocatalysis
data.description: Organocatalysis is a type of catalysis where the catalyst in the chemical reaction is an organic (non-metallic) compound. The catalysts operate both through the transient formation of covalent bonds, such as in enamine and imminium catalysis, as well as through non-covalent interactions, such as in hydrogen bonding catalysis.

data.name: Dental Lasers
data.description: Dental Lasers are advanced tools used in various dental procedures, such as cavity preparation, soft tissue surgery, and teeth whitening, offering precision and reduced healing times.

data.name: Bacterial Secretion
data.description: Bacterial secretion is the process by which bacteria release substances to their surroundings, including other cells. Bacteria achieve this using dedicated secretion systems that transport molecules - such as factors involved in bacterial pathogenesism, so called effectors - across the cell wall.

data.name: Labor Movements
data.description: The labour movement or labor movement[a] consists of two main wings: the trade union movement (British English) or labor union movement (American English) on the one hand, and the political labour movement on the other.

data.name: Micro-optics
data.description: Micro-optics are optical systems that are between a few micrometres and a millimetre in size. This includes small lenses or arrays of lenses, or optical fibres with a microscale core diameter. Such small optical components are important for integrated optics.

data.name: Skill-mix in dentistry
data.description: Skill-mix in dentistry refers to the strategic allocation and utilization of different dental professionals, such as dentists, hygienists, and dental nurses, to optimize patient care and practice efficiency.

data.name: Organizing materials with DNA
data.description: Organizing materials with DNA involves using DNA molecules as a template or scaffold to arrange and assemble other materials at the nanoscale, often for applications in nanotechnology and biotechnology.

data.name: Microbial Biooceanography
data.description: Microbial oceanography is the study of the biology, biogeochemistry and ecology of marine microbes, including phytoplankton and zooplankton, it studies how microorganisms influence—and are influenced by—oceanic processes. There is a particular focus on diversity patterns and the interaction between biological processes and physical ones such as nutrient flow and climate.

data.name: Technological Infrastructures
data.description: Technology infrastructure refers to the components that make the operation and management of enterprise IT services and IT environments possible. This infrastructure includes all hardware, software, networks, and facilities companies use to create, test, deliver, control, and support IT services.

data.name: Pupil disorders
data.description: Pupil disorders refer to abnormalities in the size, shape, or reactivity of the pupils, which can indicate underlying neurological or ocular conditions.

data.name: Solar Thermal Energy
data.description: Solar thermal energy (STE) is a form of energy and a technology for harnessing solar energy to generate thermal energy for use in industry, and in the residential and commercial sectors.

data.name: Dental Biomaterials
data.description: Dental Biomaterials are materials used in dentistry to repair, replace, or enhance dental tissues, including composites, ceramics, metals, and polymers.

data.name: Bruxism
data.description: Bruxism is the involuntary grinding or clenching of teeth, often occurring during sleep, which can lead to tooth wear, jaw pain, and other dental issues.

data.name: Protein-Ligand Interactions
data.description: Protein-ligand interactions refer to the specific interactions between a protein molecule and a small molecule known as a ligand. These interactions play a crucial role in various biological processes, including enzyme catalysis, signal transduction, drug action, and molecular recognition.

data.name: Object Recognition
data.description: Object recognition, in the field of psychology, refers to the cognitive process by which individuals perceive, identify, and categorize objects based on their sensory information and stored knowledge. It involves the ability to extract relevant features, match them to stored representations, and assign meaning to the recognized objects.

data.name: Dental foundation training
data.description: Dental foundation training is a postgraduate program for newly qualified dentists, providing supervised clinical experience and professional development to ensure competence in general dental practice.

data.name: Enteric neuropathies
data.description: Enteric neuropathies are degenerative diseases characterized by degradation of the nerves and muscles in the digestive system. The gut stops functioning as a result of this degradation.

synonyms: Degenerative neuromuscular condition of the digestive system

data.name: Bioalcohols
data.description: Bioalcohols are alcohols produced from biological sources, such as plants or algae, used as renewable fuels or chemical feedstocks, including ethanol and butanol.

data.name: Resonance Raman Spectroscopy
data.description: Resonance Raman spectroscopy is a Raman spectroscopy technique in which the incident photon energy is close in energy to an electronic transition of a compound or material under examination.

data.name: Catalytic RNA
data.description: Catalytic RNA (ribonucleic acid) are RNA molecules that have enzyme activity. The classic example is the hammerhead ribozyme. Catalytic RNAs are involved in a number of biological processes, including RNA processing and protein synthesis. Discovery of catalytic RNA contributed to the hypothesis of an 'RNA world', describing the origin of life as starting from RNA.

data.name: Urinary tract obstruction
data.description: Urinary tract obstruction is a blockage of the urinary tract that prevents the flow of urine, leading to pain, urinary tract infection and renal damage. Causes of urinary tract obstruction include calculi, stricture and cancer.

data.name: Impression taking
data.description: Impression taking in dentistry is the process of creating a negative replica of a patient's teeth and oral tissues, used for diagnostic and treatment planning purposes.

data.name: Housing and Built Environments
data.description: Housing and Built Environments study the design, construction, and management of residential and urban spaces, focusing on how these environments impact human living conditions and societal development.

data.name: Nanocrystallography
data.description: Nanocrystallography (serial femtosecond crystallography) is a protein X-ray crystallography technique that uses femtosecond pulses from an X-ray free-electron laser to collect diffraction snapshots from a stream of single nano-sized crystals of a macromolecule, in order to solve a high-resolution three-dimensional macromolecular structure.

data.name: Molecular Fluctuations
data.description: Molecular fluctuations are random changes of molecular parameters such as conformation or concentration. In living cells, molecular fluctuations are a source of heterogeneity among cells sharing a common genetic background.

data.name: Emergence
data.description: Emergence is the arising of rich and coherent macroscopic structures from numerous repetitions of simple elementary interactions among large numbers of microscopic particles. An emergent system is characterized by a property of wholeness that is not contained in its generative rules.

data.name: Bonded restorations
data.description: Bonded restorations in dentistry involve the use of adhesive materials to repair and restore damaged teeth, enhancing their function and appearance.

data.name: Electrocatalysis
data.description: Electrocatalysis is a type of catalysis that results in the modification of the rate of an electrochemical reaction occurring on an electrode surface. The relative electrocatalytic properties of a group of materials at a given temperature and concentration are not necessarily constant, and may vary according to the different dependence of rates on electrical potential.

subjects.term: Engineering applications of electronic, magnetic, optical materials

data.name: Scleral diseases
data.description: Scleral diseases refer to medical conditions affecting the sclera, the white outer layer of the eyeball, which can lead to inflammation, degeneration, or other ocular complications.

data.name: Hydrolases
data.description: Hydrolases are enzymes that catalyze the cleavage of a covalent bond using water. Types of hydrolase include esterases, such as phosphatases, that act on ester bonds, and proteases or peptidases that act on amide bonds in peptides.

data.name: Oscillators
data.description: Oscillators are physical systems whose evolution over time varies repeatedly around a central state of equilibrium. Oscillating cycles that are more or less periodic are found in all sectors of science, from quantum physics to cell biology, sociology or cosmology.

data.name: Bacterial Systems Biology
data.description: Bacterial systems biology is the scientific study of the functions and properties of bacteria in an integrative, systematic way, based on the analysis and modelling of large data sets. Systems biology is, for example, used to build networks of bacterial metabolism.

data.name: Ocular Ischemic Syndrome
data.description: Ocular Ischemic Syndrome is a condition characterized by reduced blood flow to the eye, leading to vision problems and potential blindness.

data.name: Literature and Human Rights
data.description: Literature and Human Rights explores the intersection of literary works and human rights issues, examining how literature reflects, critiques, and influences the understanding and advocacy of human rights.

data.name: Fluorescence Imaging
data.description: Fluorescence imaging is the visualization of fluorescent dyes or proteins as labels for molecular processes or structures. It enables a wide range of experimental observations including the location and dynamics of gene expression, protein expression and molecular interactions in cells and tissues.

data.name: Chaperone-mediated Autophagy
data.description: Chaperone-mediated autophagy is a type of autophagy in which individual cytosolic proteins are selectively targeted to the lysosome for degradation. Substrate proteins are recognised by a cytoplasmic chaperone protein that sends them to the lysosome membrane for subsequent import and degradation. Chaperone-mediated autophagy occurs without the formation of autophagosomes.

data.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
data.description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a disease of the respiratory tract that is characterized narrowing of the small airways and destruction of lung tissue. This leads to poor airflow, shortness of breath, cough and frequent exacerbations, which are often due to infections. Smoking is the most common aetiologic factor.

data.name: Vitreous detachment
